# magnum internal API

Exported surface of every package under `internal/`. The package sections below are generated verbatim from `go doc -all ./internal/<pkg>` by `make api-doc`; only the text above the generated marker is hand-written (it is kept on regeneration). Run `make api-doc` whenever an exported signature or doc comment changes. `go doc ./internal/<pkg> <Symbol>` prints a single symbol.

Module: `github.com/zhuravel/magnum` (Go 1.27). Import paths are `github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/<pkg>`. Every package is implemented.

## Cross-cutting conventions

- Every subprocess goes through `execx.Runner` (`Real`, `Fake`, `DryRun`). Commands that change state set `Cmd.Mutates = true`, so `--dry-run` only prints them. Packages that run subprocesses take a runner: `gitx`, `github`, `identity`, `launchd`, `reveal`, `slots`, `inventory`, `agents`, `pipeline`, `cleanup`, `notify` (osascript). `execx.Real` refuses a missing `Cmd.Dir` with a `working directory` error (code -1) before starting the process.
- `mysqlx` (database/sql), `herdr` (Unix socket) and `identity.App`'s REST calls (net/http) do not use execx, so `execx.DryRun` does not stop them. Under `daemon --dry-run` the engine therefore never calls `agents`, `pipeline.RunRound`, `notify` toasts/`Sidebar` or identity refresh, and writes no tab-bar file; `slots` and `cleanup` have their own dry-run flags (`slots.Deps.DryRun`, `cleanup.Options.DryRun`), and `app.New` opens a private `VACUUM INTO` copy of `state/magnum.db`.
- One `app.App` per process wires every layer (`app.New(cfg, layout, app.Options{...})`, then `engine.FromApp(a)` for the daemon). Non-daemon commands pass `Options.Logger`, otherwise the App logs to `state/logs/daemon.log`.
- Commands: `cli` exports only `Main` and `Context`. Every command is a cobra command built per call by `newRoot` from its own `new*Cmd(c)` constructor in its own file (unexported helpers carry a per-group prefix: `act*`, `insp*`/`status*`/`doctor*`, `daemon*`); `magnum --help` lists them by group and README.md summarizes their flags. `status --watch`, `pick`, `cleanup` and `watch` run a `tui` screen when stdin and stdout are terminals (`tui.IsTerminal`) and keep their plain-text output anywhere else and with `--json`; the cli adapts its own types into the screen's structs, and actions run after the screen exits (pick) or capture their output (the dashboard).
- CLI and daemon hand-off: mutating commands call `store.EnqueueRequest(engine.Req*, payload)` and then `engine.KickDaemon(layout)` (pid 0 = no daemon). In-process slot or cleanup work takes `engine.AcquireLock(layout.Lock())`; `held == true` means a daemon runs, so send a request instead (`slots provision|repair|adopt` → `engine.ReqProvision|ReqRepair|ReqAdopt`, `magnum open` of a parked PR → `engine.ReqOpen`). Never probe the lock.
- Per-PR repositories: the main clone is whatever `(*gitx.Client).FindClone` finds under the watch's `clone_root` (`<name>`, `<owner>-<name>`, `<owner>_<name>`, else any directory whose origin is the repository; folders without `.git` are never handed to git). The engine records it in `repos.clone_path`; per-PR worktrees live next to it at `<clone>__worktrees/pr-N` (`slots.PRWorktreePath`).
- Logs: the daemon writes and rotates `state/logs/daemon.log`; the LaunchAgent's stdout/stderr go to `state/logs/launchd.log` (`launchd.LogPath`).
- Secrets: pass free text through `execx.Redact` before logging it or storing it in events. Session env (`sessions.env_json`) holds only non-secret values.
- Timestamps written to SQLite must go through `store.FormatTime` (fixed-width, so text order is time order).
- Each package has its own sentinel errors; match them with `errors.Is`: `store.ErrNotFound`/`ErrConflict`, `github.ErrNotFound`/`ErrUnauthorized`/`ErrForbidden`/`ErrRateLimited`, `gitx.ErrNoSuchRef`/`ErrNoMergeBase`, `mysqlx.ErrGuard`/`ErrNotFound`, `herdr.ErrUnavailable`/`ErrTimeout`, plus the `Err*` values of `slots`, `agents`, `pipeline` and `cleanup` listed below.
- GitHub logins: GraphQL returns `talkable`, REST and config use `talkable[bot]`. Compare with `github.SameLogin`.
- Run rows: `agents` moves runs pending → submitted/working/failed/abandoned and submitted/working → ended; `pipeline` owns ended → verified/failed and the `codex_review` run; the engine closes out stale runs of a PR before each new round. A submitted run is observed, never re-sent.
- Completion signal: the engine calls `agents.ObserveSnapshot` exactly once per tick (each call counts one idle tick); `pipeline` only reads run and session rows.
- Magnum's herdr agents are named `mg-…` (`inventory.AgentPrefix`); `slots.Guard` ignores panes recorded in live sessions.
- Pool database drop guard: `Prefix` = the common start of `pool.databases` before `{` (`talkable_`), `AllowRegexp` = `slot_name` with `{n}` as `[0-9]+` (`^review[0-9]+$`). One helper derives it, `slots.DropGuard(pool)`, used by `slots`, `inventory` and `cleanup`.
- Event subjects (audit log): `pr:<owner>/<name>#<N>` (engine, pipeline), `pr:<store id>` (cleanup), `slot:<name>` and `slot:<name>:…` (slots, cleanup), `slot:<owner>/<name>#<N>` (per-PR slots), `slug:<slug>`, `path:<dir>`, `tool:<codex|claude>`, `identity:<name>`, `pool:<repo>`, `repo:<owner/name>`, `request:<id>`. `magnum logs <ref>` matches every PR form.
- kv keys read by `magnum status`/`doctor`: `daemon.paused|paused_reason|paused_until|started_at|last_tick|last_poll|last_reconcile|pid`, `<codex|claude>.paused_until|paused_reason|paused_detail|backoff`, `identity.<name>.check|error|tick_error|token_expiry`, `watch.<owner>.paused`, `gh.remaining|limit|reset|poll_paused_until`, `herdr.up`, plus per-PR `pr.<id>.simplify|fresh|dry_run`. Their names are `store.KV*` constants and functions, shared by the engine (which keeps its older `engine.KV*` aliases) and `cli`; never spell them as literals.
- Review pipeline: `config.Config.Roles` (`[[role]]`) and `Kinds` (`[kinds.<name>]`) define the agents of a round; read them through `RolesFor`, `JudgeFor`, `RoleByNameOrAlias`, `Stages` and `KindSpec`, never by hard-coded role names. Prompt templates live in the top-level `prompts/` directory (package `github.com/zhuravel/magnum/prompts` embeds the defaults); `Config.ResolvePrompt` reads `[pipeline] prompts_dir` first. `prompts/README.md` documents the variables.

## agenthooks

```text
package agenthooks // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/agenthooks"

Package agenthooks carries an agent's own hook events (a Claude Code or Codex
Stop, StopFailure, PermissionRequest, SessionStart, SessionEnd, Interrupt or
UserPromptSubmit) from a magnum pane to the daemon that started the pane.
The hook script (hooks/magnum-agent-hook.sh, Script) runs `magnum hook-event
<agent> <event>`, which reads the hook's payload (ReadPayload), keeps a few of
its fields (Parse) and sends one Unix datagram (Send) to the socket the pane's
env names (EnvSocket). The daemon's Listener reads it (Serve) and hands it on.

An event is a hint, never the source of truth: the daemon reads herdr,
the transcript or the rollout again before it acts, and polling stays the floor.
An agent in the pane has the env and can send any datagram, so a forged event
costs no more than an early look.

The package uses the standard library alone (no config, no registry, no other
package of magnum's), so the hook's process stays light.

CONSTANTS

const (
	AgentClaude = "claude"
	AgentCodex  = "codex"
)
    The agents that send events (Event.Agent, the hook script's first argument).

const (
	NameStop              = "stop"               // the agent ended its turn
	NameStopFailure       = "stop_failure"       // Claude: the turn ended on an API error (Event.Error)
	NamePermissionRequest = "permission_request" // the agent waits on an approval now
	NameSessionStart      = "session_start"      // the session's id and transcript (Event.Source: startup, resume, ...)
	NameSessionEnd        = "session_end"        // Claude: the session ended
	NameInterrupt         = "interrupt"          // Codex: the turn was cut
	NameUserPromptSubmit  = "user_prompt_submit" // a prompt was submitted: a turn begins (the prompt itself is never kept)
)
    The events (Event.Name, the hook script's second argument).

const (
	// EnvSocket is the socket of the daemon that started the pane; without
	// it the hook script exits at once.
	EnvSocket = "MAGNUM_HOOK_SOCKET"
	// EnvBin is the magnum binary the hook script runs.
	EnvBin = "MAGNUM_HOOK_BIN"
	// EnvPane is herdr's id of the pane (Event.Pane).
	EnvPane = "HERDR_PANE_ID"
	// EnvAgent is magnum's own key of the pane (Event.PaneKey): the name
	// of the agent magnum starts there (its session row's agent_name),
	// which needs no herdr.
	EnvAgent = "MAGNUM_AGENT"
	// EnvCodexThread is the Codex thread the hook runs in
	// (Event.CodexThread): a helper's differs from its session's id.
	EnvCodexThread = "CODEX_THREAD_ID"
)
    The env of a magnum pane, and the agents' own env the parser reads.

const (
	// MaxDatagram bounds an event's datagram: 2 KiB, macOS's
	// net.local.dgram.maxdgram.
	MaxDatagram = 2 << 10
	// SendTimeout bounds Send.
	SendTimeout = 200 * time.Millisecond
	// MaxPayload bounds how much of the hook's stdin ReadPayload reads.
	MaxPayload = 64 << 10
	// ReadTimeout bounds ReadPayload.
	ReadTimeout = 100 * time.Millisecond
	// HookBound bounds `magnum hook-event` as a whole: Claude does not
	// enforce a timeout on an async hook.
	HookBound = 300 * time.Millisecond
	// SocketPathLimit is the length at which a Unix socket's path is too
	// long: sun_path holds 104 bytes on macOS, its terminating NUL
	// included.
	SocketPathLimit = 104
)
    The transport's bounds.

const (
	// ScriptVersion is the version of the embedded script. It changes only
	// with the script's file: the hooks' command lines stay the same forever
	// (Codex keys its trust on them), so an upgrade asks for no new trust.
	ScriptVersion = 1
	// ScriptMarker begins the line that marks a file as magnum's own.
	ScriptMarker = "# managed by magnum"
)
    The hook script's header (hooks/magnum-agent-hook.sh, embedded as
    magnum.AgentHookScript): ScriptMarker, "# MAGNUM_HOOK_ID=<agent>" and "#
    MAGNUM_HOOK_VERSION=<n>".

const PingName = "ping"
    PingName is the event `magnum doctor` sends a daemon's hook socket to see
    that it takes datagrams. No hook sends it, and every receiver drops it:
    Serve hands on only the events above.

const Version = 1
    Version is the Event's V. The fields are additive under it: a later field
    never changes the meaning of an older one, so a daemon reads an event with a
    field it does not know as the event it knows.


FUNCTIONS

func ReadPayload(r io.Reader) []byte
    ReadPayload reads the hook's payload from r (its stdin): at most MaxPayload
    bytes, and only what came within ReadTimeout. An agent that keeps its end of
    stdin open costs the hook ReadTimeout, no more; what was read by then is the
    payload (Parse keeps the fields before a cut).

func Script(template []byte, agent string) ([]byte, error)
    Script is the hook script template (magnum.AgentHookScript) made for agent:
    its MAGNUM_HOOK_ID names it. An agent that sends no events, and a template
    without the placeholder, are errors.

func ScriptHeader(b []byte) (agent string, version int, managed bool)
    ScriptHeader reads a hook script's header from b (its first few KiB):
    the agent it was made for, its version, and whether a line begins with
    ScriptMarker (magnum's own file, which the install may overwrite). A file
    without the marker reports no agent and version 0.

func Send(path string, ev Event) error
    Send sends ev as one datagram (at most MaxDatagram bytes; a V of 0 goes as
    Version) to the socket at path, within SendTimeout. It never waits for a
    daemon that is not there: a missing socket (ENOENT) and one nobody reads
    (ECONNREFUSED) fail at once.


TYPES

type Event struct {
	V     int    `json:"v"`     // Version
	Agent string `json:"agent"` // AgentClaude or AgentCodex
	Name  string `json:"name"`  // NameStop, ...
	// SessionID is the agent's session id, TranscriptPath its transcript
	// (Claude) or rollout (Codex) as the agent names it, TurnID the turn
	// (Codex), Source what started the session (startup, resume, clear,
	// compact), Error the API error a StopFailure ended on (rate_limit,
	// overloaded, authentication_failed, billing_error, ...), ToolName the
	// tool a permission request is for, AgentID the subagent the event is
	// from (Claude; empty for the session's own).
	SessionID      string `json:"session_id,omitempty"`
	TranscriptPath string `json:"transcript_path,omitempty"`
	TurnID         string `json:"turn_id,omitempty"`
	Source         string `json:"source,omitempty"`
	Error          string `json:"error,omitempty"`
	ToolName       string `json:"tool_name,omitempty"`
	AgentID        string `json:"agent_id,omitempty"`
	// Pane is the pane's HERDR_PANE_ID, PaneKey its MAGNUM_AGENT, CodexThread
	// its CODEX_THREAD_ID. An event names a pane, a pane key or both.
	Pane        string `json:"pane"`
	PaneKey     string `json:"pane_key,omitempty"`
	CodexThread string `json:"codex_thread,omitempty"`
	// Background is how many background tasks a Claude Stop reports still
	// running.
	Background int `json:"background,omitempty"`
}
    Event is one hook event, encoded as JSON with lower-case snake keys. It
    never has a field for the agent's last message, a prompt or a tool's input:
    they carry PR text.

func Parse(agent, name string, payload []byte, getenv func(string) string) (Event, error)
    Parse builds the Event of hook event name of agent from its payload
    (the JSON the agent wrote to the hook's stdin, ReadPayload) and its env
    (getenv: EnvPane, EnvAgent, EnvCodexThread). It keeps only session_id,
    transcript_path, turn_id, source, error, tool_name, agent_id and the
    number of background_tasks; every other field (the last assistant message,
    a prompt, a tool's input, the cwd) is dropped unread. A payload cut short
    or that is no JSON keeps the fields read before the break; a value of
    another type than its field's is no value. An id that is too long or holds
    a character no id has (a space, a quote, a backslash, <, >, &, anything
    outside printable ASCII) is left out whole, the free text (the path,
    the error, the tool, the source) loses its control characters and is cut,
    and the event always fits one datagram (fit). An unknown agent or event,
    and a hook in a pane that names neither a valid HERDR_PANE_ID nor a valid
    MAGNUM_AGENT, are errors: there is nothing to send.

type Listener struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Listener reads the events sent to one socket (Listen, Serve).

func Listen(path string, log *slog.Logger) (*Listener, error)
    Listen opens the datagram socket at path for Serve. The caller holds the
    daemon lock, so no other daemon serves path: the socket's directory is
    made (or made again) the user's alone (0700), a socket a daemon left there
    (it stopped, or it was killed) is removed first, and the new one is 0600.
    A path of SocketPathLimit bytes or more, and a file at path that is no
    socket (which is never removed), are errors. log receives Serve's lines (nil
    = none).

func (l *Listener) Close() error
    Close closes the socket (Serve returns). Its file stays: the next Listen
    removes it, and a hook that sends to it meanwhile fails at once.

func (l *Listener) Path() string
    Path is the socket's path.

func (l *Listener) Serve(ctx context.Context, handle func(Event))
    Serve reads the socket until ctx ends, then closes it, and hands each
    event to handle, one at a time, on Serve's goroutine. It drops a datagram
    over MaxDatagram, one that is no JSON object, of another V than Version,
    or without an agent or an event this version knows, one that names neither
    a pane nor a pane key, and a pane's events past its rate (rateBurst at once,
    then one per rateEvery, and all panes' past globalBurst, then one per
    globalEvery; an event without a pane counts against its pane key's).
    The ids of an event it hands on are ids (as Parse makes them; a pane or key
    that is none is left out) and its free text is cut, since anyone with the
    pane's env can send one. Each event it hands on logs one debug line with its
    name, its pane (paneForLog) and its key (keyForLog), never another field.
    A handler that panics costs its event, not the listener.

```

## agents

```text
package agents // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/agents"

Package agents runs magnum's review agents inside herdr: one workspace per PR
with a pane per configured role (config.Role: the judge plus reviewers such as
claude-review, the codex-review shell and claude-simplify), agent start (fresh
or resumed) on any configured kind (config.Kind: codex, claude, droid, omp,
...), prompts, per-tick completion tracking, pane-output health classification,
login preflight, quit, park and crash recovery.

Durable state lives in the store's sessions and runs rows; herdr is only
observed. Prompts are rendered from the configured prompt files (see
RenderPrompt and Manager.RolePrompt); PR titles and bodies are never
interpolated into them.

Agent CLIs are often launched through the user's zsh wrapper functions (herdr
types the agent command into the pane's shell), so magnum passes only the args
Kind.Argv builds; a kind's args are appended only when it is not a wrapper (see
Manager.Wrapper).

CONSTANTS

const (
	KindCodex  = config.KindCodex
	KindClaude = config.KindClaude
	KindDroid  = config.KindDroid
	KindOMP    = config.KindOMP
	KindShell  = config.KindShell // sessions.agent_kind of a shell role's pane
)
    Agent kinds (herdr agent.start --kind, sessions.agent_kind) of the built-in
    kinds; any [kinds.<name>] is a kind too.

const (
	AgentStartTimeout   = 120 * time.Second // agent.start timeout_ms
	PromptAckTimeout    = 60 * time.Second  // agent.prompt --wait --until working|blocked
	IdleShellTimeout    = 60 * time.Second  // a fresh pane's shell (oh-my-zsh + mise) must be idle by then
	QuitIdleTimeout     = 10 * time.Second  // after a quit's keys (two ctrl+c, or one and the exit keys; again after a hard quit's exit keys) the pane must be a shell again
	PreflightTimeout    = 30 * time.Second
	WrapperProbeTimeout = 20 * time.Second
)
    Timeouts used against herdr and the CLIs.

const (
	// CodexPromptSettle is how long a Codex session's screen must show its
	// composer with no startup dialog before its first prompt goes out:
	// Codex may draw its composer and show its hooks review a moment later
	// (the tests' fake shows it 2 s after the composer), and a dialog that
	// comes while the wait runs is answered and the wait starts again.
	CodexPromptSettle = 3 * time.Second
	// CodexReadyTimeout bounds that wait: a screen magnum cannot read, or
	// one that shows neither the composer nor a dialog it knows, gets the
	// prompt after it as before (logged), and the check after the prompt
	// (codexPromptTaken) still looks for a dialog that ate it.
	CodexReadyTimeout = 30 * time.Second
	// PromptTakenWait bounds the check that Codex took a first prompt herdr
	// did not see it take (agent_prompt_stalled).
	PromptTakenWait = 10 * time.Second
)
const (
	EventFirstPromptUnready = "agents.first_prompt_unready"
	EventFirstPromptStalled = "agents.first_prompt_stalled"
)
    EventFirstPromptUnready is recorded (warn, the PR's subject) when a
    Codex session's first prompt goes out after CodexReadyTimeout of a
    screen that never showed the composer with no startup dialog, and
    EventFirstPromptStalled when herdr saw no turn start from a first prompt
    and the check that Codex took it found neither a sign it did nor a dialog
    that ate it (the run is observed as before). Twice on 2026-10-23 the cause
    was unknown, so each carries what the screen showed then (data: role, run,
    agent, pane, screen: screenTail's lines; Codex's start screen, never PR
    text).

const (
	// CompactTimeout bounds Compact's wait for the compaction turn to end.
	CompactTimeout = 10 * time.Minute
)
    Compaction timing.

const (
	EventHooksTrusted  = "agents.hooks_trusted"
	EventHooksDeclined = "agents.hooks_declined"
)
    Event kinds recorded each time magnum answers a hooks review.

const (
	// DefaultModelLimitCooldown is used when daemon.model_limit_cooldown is
	// unset (zero).
	DefaultModelLimitCooldown = 5 * time.Hour
	// SwitchModelTimeout bounds the wait for an agent to be idle again after
	// the switch command.
	SwitchModelTimeout = 30 * time.Second
)
    Model switching timing.

const (
	EventModelSwitched = "agent.model_switched" // data: session, role, from, to, reason
	EventModelLimited  = "kind.model_limited"   // data: kind, model, until
	EventRebound       = "agent.rebound"        // data: session, role, agent, pane (Submit, see rebindLost)
)
    Event kinds of per-model limits, and of a lost session made live again.

const (
	SwitchLimitHit = "model_limit"   // the model hit its limit during a run
	SwitchLimited  = "model_limited" // the model was already limited (before a prompt, or at start)
	SwitchExpired  = "limit_expired" // the role's model is no longer limited: back to it
)
    SwitchModel reasons (EventModelSwitched's reason).

const (
	// NotesReadFile is the frozen copy of the notes in a round's (or a fix
	// job's) report directory.
	NotesReadFile = "notes-read.md"
	// NotesPartMax bounds a part: whole lines of at most this many bytes,
	// newlines counted, or a piece of one longer line.
	NotesPartMax = 16 << 10
)
    The roles read the repository notes in parts. Codex 0.162.1 keeps at most
    10,000 tokens of one command's output by default and drops the middle
    (its exec tool's default request, under the policy the codex kind's
    tool_output_limit raises), and Claude Code's Read refuses a file above about
    25,000 tokens: whole, the 97 KB notes reached the Codex judges cut in 94 of
    103 reads, their middle (pitfalls, decisions) gone. So a round copies the
    live file into its report directory before its first prompt (FreezeNotes;
    judges rewrite the live file about 20 times a day, so line ranges of the
    live file would shift between two reads), and its prompts give the copy
    as parts of at most NotesPartMax bytes, one command each (SplitNotes);
    the judge re-reads the live file in parts, under the notes lock, before it
    merges (NotesRereadLine).

const (

	// NotesHarnessMax bounds the harness entries a judge prompt lists.
	NotesHarnessMax = 40
)
    Repository notes (engine.NotesPath) are rewritten by the judge of every
    round of a repository, and rounds of different PRs of one repository run at
    the same time. Three judges once rewrote the same file within four minutes,
    each from the text it had read half an hour earlier, and the result
    named one of six harness scripts. So the judge takes a lock for its
    read-merge-write: a directory created with mkdir (atomic, and it outlives
    the shell command that made it, which an flock would not: the judge reads,
    merges and writes in separate tool calls), waited for at most three minutes
    and taken over when older than ten (its judge died holding it).

const (
	EventSessionParkBegin  = "pr.session_park_begin"
	EventSessionParked     = "pr.session_parked"
	EventSessionParkFailed = "pr.session_park_failed"
)
    The events of one session's early park (ParkSessions), info each, with the
    role, the session, its pane and agent: its begin, its end as parked (ok) and
    its failure (fail, with the cause). The engine's pr.parked sums the park up,
    and its pr.park_failed warns once per cause.

const (
	// EventPromptDenied: magnum answered No to an agent's permission prompt.
	EventPromptDenied = "agent.prompt_denied"
	// EventPromptDeniedLimit: a run reached MaxPromptDenies; magnum stopped
	// answering and the agent stays blocked for the human.
	EventPromptDeniedLimit = "agent.prompt_denied_limit"
	// EventDenyContinued: an agent that went idle after a deny was sent its
	// kind's after_deny_prompt (see continueAfterDeny).
	EventDenyContinued = "agent.deny_continued"
)
    Permission-prompt events, recorded on the PR subject
    ("pr:<owner>/<name>#<N>").

const (
	// ReadinessResetDB is a [[pool]] reset_db command, run first when the
	// slot's databases carry another schema than the checkout's: it loads
	// the PR's schema into them.
	ReadinessResetDB = "reset_db"
	ReadinessPrepare = "prepare" // a [[repo]]/[[pool]] prepare command
	ReadinessReady   = "ready"   // a [[repo]]/[[pool]] ready probe (exit 0 = ready)
	ReadinessRuby    = "ruby"    // the built-in check that the login shell runs the Ruby the checkout pins
)
    Readiness check kinds (ReadinessCheck.Kind).

const (
	ReadinessOK      = "ok"
	ReadinessFailed  = "failed"  // a non-zero exit, a failed start, or (ruby) the wrong version
	ReadinessTimeout = "timeout" // the readiness budget (ready_timeout) ran out while it ran
	ReadinessSkipped = "skipped" // not run: the budget was spent, or the round was cancelled
)
    Readiness check statuses (ReadinessCheck.Status).

const (
	// RecoverIDAfter is how long after its start a live Codex session that
	// herdr gave no id gets it from its rollout; it is tried again at each
	// observation until it has one.
	RecoverIDAfter = time.Minute
	// RecoverIDWindow is how far a rollout's start (its session_meta's
	// timestamp) may be from the session's start to be its rollout.
	RecoverIDWindow = 2 * time.Minute
	// RecoverIDHeads bounds the rollouts one recovery reads the first line
	// of, newest first by name.
	RecoverIDHeads = 300
)
const (
	CodexHookMissing  = "missing"  // no SessionStart hook names HerdrSessionHook
	CodexHookDisabled = "disabled" // every such hook's [hooks.state] entry has enabled = false
	CodexHookPlace    = "place"    // a hook before it has no timeout, or one over CodexHookMaxTimeout
	CodexHookTrust    = "trust"    // its place has no [hooks.state] entry with a trusted_hash
)
    The checks herdr's Codex session hook can fail (CodexHookProblem.Check).

const (
	// EventShellStopBegin (warn) is recorded before StopShell's first
	// signal to an own run: the role, the pane, the run, the process group
	// (pgid) and the job it captured (tree: pid, pgid and name of each, never
	// argv).
	EventShellStopBegin = "pr.shell_stop_begin"
	// EventShellStopped (info): the step that stopped it (term, kill,
	// replace: the pane replaced, close: the pane closed without a
	// replacement, exited: it ended before a signal) and the seconds it
	// took.
	EventShellStopped = "pr.shell_stopped"
	// EventShellStopFailed (warn): the cause, not_own (nothing more was
	// sent: the command is not proven an own run, or herdr shows another one
	// now), signal (a signal was refused, the process table could not be
	// read, or a captured process outlived every step) or close (the pane
	// would not close).
	EventShellStopFailed = "pr.shell_stop_failed"
	// EventShellMoveBegin (warn), EventShellMoved (info) and
	// EventShellMoveFailed (warn, the cause split or registry): RunShell
	// moves a shell role to a new pane, as something that is no run of
	// magnum's keeps its pane busy; the busy pane gets nothing.
	EventShellMoveBegin  = "pr.shell_move_begin"
	EventShellMoved      = "pr.shell_moved"
	EventShellMoveFailed = "pr.shell_move_failed"
)
    Events of StopShell and of RunShell's move to a new pane, on the PR.

const (
	PhaseOwnPass    = "own_pass"   // the judge's own pass, while the reviewers work
	PhaseCandidates = "candidates" // the judge judges the reviewers' reports against its own pass
)
    Judge phases of JudgeData.Phase.

const (
	ModeInitial  = config.PromptInitial  // the role's first run for the PR
	ModeRereview = config.PromptRereview // a new head after the role's earlier run
	ModeRestart  = config.PromptRestart  // a push cut the role's turn short; the round restarted on the new head
)
    Prompt modes of RoleData.Mode.

const (
	// TrustWindow: the fallback answers a trust dialog only this soon after
	// the agent started (it is a first-launch dialog), and only before the
	// session was ever prompted.
	TrustWindow = 90 * time.Second
	// TrustReadyTimeout bounds the wait for the agent to be idle after the
	// dialog was answered.
	TrustReadyTimeout = 60 * time.Second
)
    Trust-dialog fallback timing.

const CodexCyberPolicy = "cyber_policy"
    CodexCyberPolicy is the codex_error_info of Codex's cybersecurity refusal
    ("This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk").

const CodexForgetStaleStep = "if `codex` asks nothing, run `magnum hooks install codex --forget-stale`"
    CodexForgetStaleStep is the way out of a record Codex will never replace (it
    trusts the rewritten hook as it is, so it asks nothing): status, doctor and
    the hold's texts name it.

const CodexHookMaxTimeout = 10
    CodexHookMaxTimeout is the longest timeout, in seconds, a SessionStart hook
    that runs before herdr's may have for herdr's hook's place to pass: herdr's
    own hook has 10 s, and Codex gives a hook without a timeout up to 600 s.

const CodexSourceSubagent = "subagent"
    CodexSourceSubagent is the Source of a Codex subagent's rollout,
    whose session_meta source is an object naming the subagent ({"subagent":
    "review"}, {"subagent": {"thread_spawn": ...}}).

const CompactCommand = "/compact"
    CompactCommand is what Compact types into the agent's pane: Claude Code's
    /compact, which replaces the conversation so far with its summary.

const CompletionGap = 3 * time.Second
    CompletionGap is how long after the first idle|done reading of a streak
    the reading that ends the turn may come at the earliest: the review daemon
    observes every few seconds (its observe clock), and two readings a second
    apart would let a status that flickers idle for a moment end the turn.
    Readings farther apart (the tick's, the factory's at 10 s) meet it on the
    second, as before.

const CompletionIdleTicks = 2
    CompletionIdleTicks is how many consecutive idle|done observations end a
    turn. The pipeline ends a judge's turn sooner, once its result file holds a
    final status; the agent's work after that is still the run's (turnTail).

const EventBackgroundWait = "agent.background_wait"
    EventBackgroundWait is recorded once per run when background work holds an
    idle claude agent's run open (data: role, run, tasks).

const EventClaudeProjectDeclined = "agents.claude_project_declined"
    EventClaudeProjectDeclined is recorded (subject "pr:<owner>/<name>#<N>")
    each time a Claude session of the PR starts with the user's settings only
    because the PR changes .claude/, .mcp.json, a CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md or
    AGENTS.md; for its data's residue, the checkout's files there differ though
    the PR's commits do not change them (ProjectNote.Residue).

const EventCodexProjectDeclined = "agents.codex_project_declined"
    EventCodexProjectDeclined is recorded (subject "pr:<owner>/<name>#<N>")
    each time a Codex session of the PR starts without the PR's changes to the
    project config Codex loads from the checkout: with the checkout untrusted
    because the PR changes .codex/, or with no AGENTS.md when it changes only
    those; for its data's residue, the checkout's files there differ though the
    PR's commits do not change them (ProjectNote.Residue).

const EventDefaultModelRestored = "agent.default_model_restored"
    EventDefaultModelRestored is recorded when SwitchModel put the Claude
    settings' default model back (data: session, role, file, model, found;
    model and found are null when the key was absent).

const EventHerdrIDsReused = "agents.herdr_ids_reused"
    EventHerdrIDsReused is recorded (info, the PR's subject) when retired
    sessions of the PR record herdr ids that are no longer theirs: their herdr
    ids are dropped and nothing of theirs is closed. One event per reason (data:
    reason; sessions, the rows; panes and workspaces, the ids dropped):
    "other_pr", live sessions of other PRs use them now; "another_agent",
    herdr shows another agent in the pane (or in the workspace) they record;
    "outside_checkout", herdr shows a pane without their agent that works
    outside their checkout there. It names ids, never a pane's text or
    directory.

const EventHookStateDiffers = "agent.hook_state_differs"
    EventHookStateDiffers is recorded (info, on the PR) once per session and
    pair of states, when herdr's status and the hooks' state agree again after
    they disagreed for longer than the observe interval (hookObserveEvery),
    or the pass can no longer compare them: data role, session, kind, hook,
    herdr, by (what last moved the hooks' state: an event's name, "transcript"
    or "rollout") and seconds, from the later of the two changes to the last
    pass that saw them differ. No PR text.

const EventHooksTrustUnsaved = "agents.hooks_trust_unsaved"
    EventHooksTrustUnsaved is recorded (warn, subject tool:<kind>) when magnum
    trusted a Codex hooks review and a hook whose place had no trust entry
    in Codex's config.toml before still has none, once per hooks.json (data:
    role, agent, pane, places: those hooks' places, hooks: the hooks.json
    fingerprint). A toast says the same (Deps.Toast).

const EventHumanActive = "agent.human_active"
    EventHumanActive is recorded on the PR when an ObsHumanActive begins its
    cooldown (Observation.CooldownUntil; data: role, until).

const EventLaunchCleared = "pr.launch_cleared"
    EventLaunchCleared is recorded (warn) when magnum closed the pane of a
    launch that never came up which held a role's agent name (clearDeadLaunch);
    it names the role, the agent, the pane, its replacement and the CLI's own
    last error line there (paneError), never the TUI's text.

const EventPanesClosed = "pr.panes_closed"
    EventPanesClosed is recorded (info) when CloseRetiredPanes closed panes:
    how many, and which roles they served. Of a lost session's pane the close
    reads the CLI's own last error line first (paneError), which the agent.lost
    event does not carry and the pane takes with it: the event's last_lines maps
    each such role to its line, and the message repeats them.

const EventParkForced = "pr.park_forced"
    EventParkForced is recorded when a hard park (ParkHard) closed the pane
    of an agent that was still its pane's foreground process after ctrl+c and
    its kind's exit keys; it names the role, the pane and the cause, never the
    pane's text.

const EventPromptRetried = "agents.prompt_retried"
    EventPromptRetried is recorded (warn, the PR's subject) each time magnum
    sends a Codex session's first prompt again because a startup dialog ate it
    (data: role, run, agent, pane, dialog).

const EventSessionID = "agent.session_id"
    EventSessionID is recorded (info, the PR's subject) when the observer
    records a Codex session's id from its rollout because herdr's session hook
    gave none (data: role, session, session_id, source).

const EventSessionIDMissing = "agents.session_id_missing"
    EventSessionIDMissing is recorded (warn, subject tool:<kind>) once per kind
    and Manager when a session's first turn ends without a session id from herdr
    (see sessionIDMissing).

const EventTrustDialogAnswered = "agents.trust_dialog_answered"
    EventTrustDialogAnswered is the event kind recorded (subject
    "pr:<owner>/<name>#<N>") each time a trust dialog is answered.

const EvidenceFile = "evidence.json"
    EvidenceFile is the file the judge writes what it examined to,
    in the report directory next to its result file (JudgeData.EvidenceFile),
    and the name of the PR's merged evidence map above the per-head directories
    (JudgeData.EvidenceMap).

const FallbackPromptName = "model-fallback.md"
    FallbackPromptName is the prompt file the continuation after a model switch
    renders (with FallbackData).

const HealthLines = 80
    HealthLines is how much pane output CheckHealth classifies.

const HerdrSessionHook = "herdr-agent-state.sh"
    HerdrSessionHook is the script herdr's Codex SessionStart hook runs;
    a hook whose command names it is herdr's.

const JudgeNoResult = "the judge stopped without posting a review or writing its result"
    JudgeNoResult begins the error of the judge's runs of a round that ended
    without the judge's result, also after a nudge (the pipeline's verdict):
    the judge may still post that round's review, which the next round on the
    head adopts (the engine's late_result.go, the pipeline's findUnverified).
    Its session at work after such a round is someone typing, as any agent at
    work with no magnum prompt in flight.

const LostGrace = 15 * time.Second
    LostGrace keeps an observe tick from judging a session lost from a snapshot
    that may predate its agent: a session whose started_at, agent_status_at or
    live mark (StartAgent, a rebind in Submit) is after, or within LostGrace
    before, the snapshot's capture time is left for the next tick. A round once
    failed on a judge marked lost in the second it started: the tick's snapshot
    was taken before StartAgent made the session live.

const MaxImportHops = 5
    MaxImportHops is how many hops of imports magnum follows from an instruction
    file: Claude Code's four, and one more, so an off-by-one in either reading
    errs toward a target.

const MaxPromptDenies = 10
    MaxPromptDenies caps the permission prompts magnum denies, plus the
    after-deny continuations it sends, per run: an agent that keeps asking is
    misbehaving and is left blocked.

const MaxReset = 24 * time.Hour
    MaxReset caps a usage-limit reset read from pane text: the text may quote
    or fake a far-off date, so a pause never lasts longer than this from one
    reading (a longer limit is simply hit again).

const OriginQueued = "queued"
    OriginQueued is the Origin of a prompt typed while the agent worked
    (ClaudeQueuedTurns).

const OwnFindingsFile = "judge-own.md"
    OwnFindingsFile is the file the judge's own pass writes in the round's
    report directory (JudgeData.OwnFindings): its findings, their proofs and the
    checks it ran.

const PostRepliesFile = "replies.json"
    PostRepliesFile is the file the judge of a reply round writes its thread
    replies to for `magnum post-review --replies` (JudgeData.RepliesFile).

const PostReviewFile = "review.json"
    PostReviewFile is the file the judge writes its review to for
    `magnum post-review`, in the report directory next to its result file
    (JudgeData.ReviewFile).

const RolloutGrowth = 90 * time.Second
    RolloutGrowth is how recently a Codex session's rollout must have been
    written for a turn without a task_complete since its prompt to count as
    still working while herdr reports the agent idle or done.

const SessionIDBlind = "no session id: judges are never resumed, and a helper's Codex refusal is not seen"
    SessionIDBlind says what goes blind without a Codex session id: resumable
    never resumes the judge and TurnError cannot read the rollout, which the
    pipeline's check for a helper's refusal reads.

const SessionIDFromHook = "hook"
    SessionIDFromHook is EventSessionID's source of an id an agent's
    SessionStart hook gave (Wake).

const SessionIDFromRollout = "rollout"
    SessionIDFromRollout is EventSessionID's source of an id read from the
    session's Codex rollout.

const SessionIDWindow = 24 * time.Hour
    SessionIDWindow is how far back doctor and the daemon read the session ids
    of a kind's sessions (RecentSessionIDs).

const ShellStatusUnknown = -1
    ShellStatusUnknown is RunShell's status when the done marker carried no exit
    status (a full-line template that echoes the bare marker).

const TitleAttempts = 5
    TitleAttempts caps the rename attempts per session row (one generation;
    a restart creates a new row and a fresh budget).

const UnknownModel = "default"
    UnknownModel names the model of a session whose model magnum does not
    know (a role without model whose CLI default never named itself in a limit
    message).


VARIABLES

var (
	// ErrBlocked: the agent waits on an approval/trust dialog (herdr
	// agent_blocked, or the prompt ack came back blocked). The CLIs'
	// first-launch folder-trust dialogs are answered Yes (EnsureTrust
	// prevents them; AnswerTrustDialog is the fallback); a permission prompt
	// during a run is answered No by the observer when the role's, else the
	// kind's, on_permission_prompt is "deny"; nothing is ever approved otherwise.
	ErrBlocked = errors.New("agent blocked")
	// ErrStalled: herdr accepted the text but the agent never started working
	// (agent_prompt_stalled). The run is left submitted, never re-sent.
	ErrStalled = errors.New("agent prompt stalled")
	// ErrNotTaken: a Codex session never took its first prompt: a startup
	// dialog (the hooks review, the folder access) ate it, and again after
	// magnum answered the dialog and sent the prompt once more (Submit,
	// codexRetry). The run is failed: "Codex did not take the prompt (a
	// startup dialog ate it)".
	ErrNotTaken = errors.New("a startup dialog ate it")
	// ErrTimeout: herdr's own timeout or a client deadline.
	ErrTimeout = errors.New("agent timed out")
	// ErrLoginRequired: Preflight found the CLI logged out.
	ErrLoginRequired = errors.New("agent login required")
	// ErrBusy: an agent is working/blocked, a shell runs a command, or a run is
	// in flight, so the requested change (park, quit, move, shell command) waits.
	ErrBusy = errors.New("agent busy")
	// ErrHumanActive: a human typed into the session within daemon.human_cooldown.
	ErrHumanActive = errors.New("human active in agent pane")
	// ErrNoSession: the role has no live session (EnsureWorkspace/StartAgent first).
	ErrNoSession = errors.New("no live agent session")
	// ErrNotAgent: the role is a shell role (kind "shell", e.g. codex-review),
	// whose pane has no agent.
	ErrNotAgent = errors.New("role has no agent")
	// ErrUnknownTemplate: a prompt name exists neither in pipeline.prompts_dir
	// nor among the embedded defaults (the same sentinel as
	// config.ErrPromptNotFound).
	ErrUnknownTemplate = config.ErrPromptNotFound
)
    Sentinel errors; match with errors.Is.

var ErrHerdrUnread = errors.New("herdr cannot say what the shell panes run")
    ErrHerdrUnread is ClearShellPanes' answer when herdr cannot say what the
    PR's shell panes in the checkout run: no hold of a command, only a look that
    could not be made, which the caller tries again.

var ErrNoModelSwitch = errors.New("agent kind cannot switch models")
    ErrNoModelSwitch: the session's kind has no switch_model command.

var ErrNotOwn = errors.New("not magnum's own run")
    ErrNotOwn is StopShell's and InterruptShell's answer when the command a
    shell role's pane runs is not proven the run's own (ownShell): they sent
    nothing (more).

var ErrShellHold = errors.New("a command keeps a shell pane in the checkout busy")
    ErrShellHold is what a ShellHoldError is: a command keeps a shell pane in
    the checkout busy, so nothing may switch it.

var ErrUnsafeBaseRef = errors.New("base branch name has characters magnum does not pass to a shell")
    ErrUnsafeBaseRef means a judge or reviewer prompt's base ref is not a
    branch name gitx.ShellSafeRef passes. The prompts put it, unquoted, into git
    commands the agent runs; the error never quotes it.

var ErrUnsafeHeadRef = errors.New("head branch name has characters magnum does not pass to a shell")
    ErrUnsafeHeadRef means the fix prompt's branch (RoleData.HeadRef) is not
    a branch name gitx.ShellSafeRef passes: the prompt puts it, unquoted,
    into the push the fixer runs. The error never quotes it.


FUNCTIONS

func AgentName(repo string, number int, role Role) string
    AgentName is the herdr agent name of a PR role: "mg-<N>-<role>-<hash>" (e.g.
    mg-11920-codex-judge-1a2b3c), where repo is "owner/name" and hash is the
    first 6 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its lower-cased form. herdr agent names
    are global, so the hash keeps the same PR number of two repositories apart.
    The role is sanitized (lowercase, other characters than [a-z0-9_-]
    become "-") and trimmed when the name would exceed 32 characters;
    the hash of a trimmed role covers the role's full name too, so the name
    stays unique per (owner, repo, number, role) and always matches herdr's
    ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$.

func CodexFileName(home, file string) string
    CodexFileName names file of the Codex home home for a message that must
    not name a pane env value: "~/.codex/<file>" for the default home, else
    "$CODEX_HOME/<file>".

func CodexHookHomes(cfg *config.Config, home func(config.Role) string) (homes []string, users map[string][]string)
    CodexHookHomes are the Codex homes herdr's session hook is checked in
    (CodexSessionHomes). None unless the codex kind's session ids come from
    herdr (session_source "herdr"); a shell role's `codex review` needs no id.

func CodexHookName(typ, command string) string
    CodexHookName names a hook of a hooks.json as magnum's messages do
    (codexHookName): the last path element of its program, or of the script
    an interpreter runs ("bash ~/.codex/herdr-agent-state.sh session" is
    herdr-agent-state.sh), cleaned for the terminal; its type for a hook that
    runs no command.

func CodexSessionHomes(cfg *config.Config, home func(config.Role) string) (homes []string, users map[string][]string)
    CodexSessionHomes are the Codex homes the session roles of the codex
    kind read, in the roles' order, with the roles that read each (home:
    the Manager's CodexHome; "" for one unknown): where Codex shows its startup
    dialogs, the hooks review among them. A shell role's `codex review` shows
    none.

func CodexTrustEntries(home string, places []string) []string
    CodexTrustEntries are those of places of the Codex home home's hooks.json
    whose [hooks.state] entry has a trusted_hash: what a record would hold.

func CommandAnchor(marker string) string
    CommandAnchor is text that only the pane's echo of a shell line built with
    marker contains (the done printf's format, which the output shows with a
    number instead): pane text after it is the command's output.

func CopyModelLimits(ctx context.Context, from, to *store.Store, kind string, now time.Time) error
    CopyModelLimits copies kind's limits that end after now from registry from
    into registry to, keeping the later end of a model both hold, with the CLI's
    default model as a limit message named it (KVKindCLIModel) when to has none:
    a pane job seeds its scratch registry with what rounds and earlier jobs
    recorded in the live one, so its launch (StartAgent, LaunchModel) skips
    a model they found limited. The limits read are copied even when another
    cannot be read; that one is the error.

func CountWorking(agents []herdr.AgentInfo, kind string) int
    CountWorking counts agents of kind (codex, claude, ...) whose status is
    working, magnum's or not (daemon.max_total_working_codex gate).

func DBLockLine(magnum, checkout, role string) string
    DBLockLine is the command prefix a role runs each command that
    touches the checkout's databases with (JudgeData.DBLockCommand and
    RoleData.DBLockCommand, `db_lock` in the judge's <magnum> block): `magnum
    db-lock` (the daemon's binary, else magnum on PATH) with the checkout and
    the role, each shell-quoted, ending in `--`; the role appends its command.
    The roles of a round run at the same time on one slot, whose databases
    they share; the lock makes them take turns. An empty checkout is left out
    (db-lock then takes the git work tree it runs in), and so is an empty role.

func DoneMarker(runID string) string
    DoneMarker is the line a shell role's line prints when its command finished,
    followed by the command's exit status ("<marker> 0").

func ExactTarget(p string) string
    ExactTarget is the target an import of the directory p gives: p alone,
    with a slash at its end (MatchTarget). Claude Code loads no directory an
    import names, nor anything under it, so a change there is none; a commit
    that makes p a file or a link, or a path on the way to it a link, is,
    which a match of the path against the target the other way round finds.

func FixReplyLine(magnum string) string
    FixReplyLine is the line the fixer posts each of its replies through
    (RoleData.FixReplyCommand): `magnum fix-reply` of the daemon's binary
    (else magnum on PATH), shell-quoted; the fixer adds `--comment <id>` or
    `--issue` and passes the reply on stdin. The command signs the reply with
    postreview.FixReplyMarker, by which magnum tells the fixer's replies from
    the author's own.

func FixSyncLine(magnum, checkout, from, branch, base string) string
    FixSyncLine is the line the fixer runs when GitHub rejects its push
    because the branch moved (RoleData.FixSyncCommand): `magnum fix-sync` of
    the daemon's binary (else magnum on PATH) with the fixer's checkout (the
    slot's path, so the line replays there wherever the fixer's shell stands,
    as DBLockLine's does; "" leaves it out, and the command takes the git work
    tree it runs in), the run's start head (from), the PR's branch and its base
    branch, each shell-quoted. The command replays the fixer's commits onto the
    branch's new tip when the branch gained only merges of the base, and changes
    nothing otherwise.

func ForgetStaleCodexTrust(home string) (int, error)
    ForgetStaleCodexTrust removes every record of the Codex home home's
    hooks.json and says how many it removed: a place magnum recorded that Codex
    will never trust anew (it trusts the hook as it is) then reads trusted
    again. Without a records directory there is none.

func HasOwnCodexTrust(home string, hook OwnCodexHook) bool
    HasOwnCodexTrust is TakeOwnCodexTrust that forgets nothing: a dry run's
    look.

func HasSessionID(s store.Session) bool
    HasSessionID reports whether session s has its CLI's session id.

func HookSessionOf(live []store.Session, ev agenthooks.Event) (store.Session, bool)
    HookSessionOf is the session of live (starting and live rows) whose
    pane sent hook event ev: by its pane key (agenthooks.Event.PaneKey,
    the pane's MAGNUM_AGENT: the row's agent_name, which needs no herdr), else,
    for an event without the key (a pane made before it, an older hook-event) or
    one whose key no row's agent has (a row whose name a failed rename cleared),
    by its herdr pane (HERDR_PANE_ID); the newest row when two match. false when
    none does.

func HooksReviewShown(text string) bool
    HooksReviewShown reports whether text, a pane's visible screen,
    shows Codex's startup hooks review live at its bottom (detectHooksDialog):
    a session that shows it eats its next prompt until someone answers it.

func ImportPaths(text string, limit int) (paths []string, more bool)
    ImportPaths are the paths text imports (@path), each once, in order,
    at most limit of them (more reports that text has more, or more readings
    than ImportPaths compares in time linear in it), read wider than Claude
    Code reads them so that magnum errs toward a target. Claude Code 2.1 matches
    `(?:^|\s)@((?:[^\s\\]|\\ )+)` in each text token marked (without GFM) gives,
    but in code spans and fenced blocks, and in an HTML block that starts with
    a comment, with its comments taken out; it cuts the path at its first #,
    makes "\ " a space and trims it. ImportPaths reads an @ where a text token
    may start or after a blank (the text's start, a blank, or a mark an inline
    token starts or ends with: > ) ] [ * _ ` or an escaped one; not ( " or a
    letter), in code too, up to the first blank a backslash does not escape
    (JS's \s: U+FEFF is one, U+0085 is not). It gives that token as it is and
    as Claude's pattern ends it (at a backslash no space follows), each without
    its #fragment too, and, since a text token ends where another begins,
    the path up to each mark that may begin or end an emphasis, a code span,
    a link's text, an image or inline HTML (* _ ` < [ ] and ![; an underscore
    inside a word is none, so @app_config gives no app), each with and without
    the punctuation that may end a sentence after it and an escaped space at its
    end. It reads on after such a mark for a further @, reads the text after a
    YAML frontmatter on its own (Claude strips one before it lexes the rest,
    so an @ right after the closing --- imports), and each text again with \[
    and \] made brackets (marked makes them so in a link's text before it lexes
    it, so a path there goes on through them: linkTextUnescaped). It reads each
    again with its HTML comments taken out, where a cut starts a path too,
    and each HTML block that starts with a comment on its own, so taken out,
    as Claude does (readCommentBlocks). A home (~) or an absolute path is left
    out: no commit's tree holds it, and Claude loads a file outside its working
    directory only once the user approves the project's external imports,
    which magnum never does.

func JoinCodexHookProblems(problems []CodexHookProblem) string
    JoinCodexHookProblems says problems in one sentence without its final
    period: the first in full, each other after "; it" ("herdr's Codex session
    hook runs after ...; it has no trust entry ...").

func KVHooksTrustUnsaved(kind string) string
    KVHooksTrustUnsaved is the kv key holding the fingerprint of the
    hooks.json whose unsaved trust magnum last told the operator about
    (EventHooksTrustUnsaved): "kind.<kind>.hooks_trust_unsaved". A hooks.json
    with another fingerprint is told about again.

func KVKindCLIModel(kind string) string
    KVKindCLIModel is the kv key holding the CLI's own default model of
    kind (what a session runs when neither its role's model nor the kind's
    default_model is set), as a limit message of such a session named it.

func KVModelLimited(kind, model string) string
    KVModelLimited is the kv key holding when kind's limit on model ends
    (store.FormatTime): "kind.<kind>.model_limited.<model>".

func KVModelLimitedAt(kind, model string) string
    KVModelLimitedAt is the kv key holding when kind's last limit on model was
    first recorded and when it ends, "<at> <until>" (both store.FormatTime):
    "kind.<kind>.model_limited_at.<model>". Unlike KVModelLimited it outlives
    the limit, so RecordModelLimit knows a model that hits its limit again soon
    after the last one ended.

func KVModelLimits(kind string) string
    KVModelLimits is the kv key listing (comma-separated) the models of kind
    that have a KVModelLimited row, so status can find them.

func KVSessionModel(sessionID int64) string
    KVSessionModel is the kv key holding the model magnum switched a session row
    to (absent while the session runs its role's model).

func KindName(kind string) string
    KindName is an agent kind as a sentence names it: "Codex" for codex,
    "Claude" for claude ("The agent" for none).

func LaunchModel(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, cfg *config.Config, role config.Role, now time.Time) (model string, fallback, none bool)
    LaunchModel is the model a fresh launch of role starts on over registry st,
    as StartAgent picks it (startModel) for a Manager over st: role.Model
    while the model the role's sessions run (Config.RoleModel, else the CLI's
    default as a limit message named it, KVKindCLIModel) is not limited,
    else the first of the role's fallback models (the role's, else its kind's)
    that is not, and fallback reports that substitution. none reports a limited
    model with nothing to start on instead: the list is empty or used up,
    or the kind cannot pick a model (no model args, no switch_model); model is
    then role.Model. A pane job asks it before it starts again on a fallback.
    Limits that cannot be read give role.Model, neither a fallback nor none.

func LooseFold(s string) string
    LooseFold is s as a key two names share that a case-insensitive filesystem
    may open as one: its ASCII letters in lower case; a rune outside ASCII whose
    case partner is ASCII (ſ, the Kelvin sign, ı, İ) as that letter, ß, ẞ and
    the Latin ligatures (ﬁ) as the letters they fold to, the Greek question mark
    and varia as the ASCII marks they decompose to; the code points HFS+ ignores
    left out; any other rune as its simple case fold (the smallest of its orbit:
    Ж and ж alike). Names with other keys may still be one where both are
    outside ASCII (a decomposed é and a composed one: Go's standard library has
    no Unicode normalization), never where one is ASCII (MayFold).

func MagnumCommand(text string, cmds map[string]bool) bool
    MagnumCommand reports whether text, a user turn, is Claude Code's record of
    one of cmds (MagnumCommands).

func MagnumCommands(cfg *config.Config) map[string]bool
    MagnumCommands are the slash commands magnum types into an agent's pane
    outside any prompt, by name ("/model"): Compact's CompactCommand, and for
    every kind of cfg its switch_model and rename commands and the word its
    exit_keys type. They are the one list both sides of the factory's measure
    read: what the factory records of its panes, and the baseline of what the
    operator typed before it, drop their records (MagnumCommand), so a person's
    command of one of these names is dropped on both sides alike.

func MayFold(a, b string) bool
    MayFold reports whether a case-insensitive filesystem may open a for b,
    two names of one path element of which at least one has a byte outside
    ASCII. magnum does not model the filesystem's fold of two such names (APFS
    decomposes é, folds Ж to ж, ß to ss; HFS+ ignores some code points), so two
    names outside ASCII always may. One outside ASCII and one in it may only
    when each rune of the first outside ASCII folds into ASCII or is ignored
    (LooseFold: ſ, the Kelvin sign, ı, İ, ß, ẞ, the Latin ligatures, the two
    Greek marks that decompose to ASCII; every other rune folds to one outside
    ASCII, or decomposes to a letter and a mark outside it, under every such
    filesystem) and the folds are equal: José is never Jose, 日本.md never abc.md.
    False for two ASCII names (asciiEqualFold decides those).

func NewRunID(now time.Time) string
    NewRunID is a run id: "r-<UTC yyyymmddThhmmss>-<6 random hex digits>",
    sortable by creation second. The judge's review carries it as its magnum:run
    marker, and a review with the marker posted by another login is an identity
    leak, so the random part keeps outsiders from guessing it.

func NoteDeclinedProjects(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, prID int64, head string, kinds []string, jd *JudgeData)
    NoteDeclinedProjects sets the judge's ProjectChecks from the PR's records
    of head (the round's), which each launch of those CLIs writes, for the
    kinds among the round's roles only (kinds: their agent kinds, the judge's
    included), in projectKinds' order: a record names the kind's last launch on
    the head, which may be a session the round did not run (a reviewer paused,
    or left out of the round).

func NotesFiles(notesPath string) (dir, lock string)
    NotesFiles returns the harness directory and the lock of the repository
    notes file notesPath: the same path without ".md", and that with ".lock"
    (engine.NotesDir and engine.NotesLockPath). Both are "" for "".

func NotesHarness(dir string) (names []string, more int)
    NotesHarness is NotesHarnessLogged without a log.

func NotesHarnessLogged(dir string, log execx.Logger) (names []string, more int)
    NotesHarnessLogged lists the harness directory dir for a judge prompt
    (JudgeData.NotesHarness): entry names sorted, a directory with a trailing
    "/", at most NotesHarnessMax, and how many more there are. A name with
    anything but letters, digits and "._@+-" is never listed: it counts under
    more, and log (optional) gets one line with how many such names there are,
    never the names. The archive of retired notes lines (notes.ArchiveName) is
    no script and is left out: the judge reads it only where the notes name it.
    A missing or unreadable directory lists nothing.

func NotesLockLine(lock string) string
    NotesLockLine is the shell line a judge runs to take the notes lock (a
    directory): it prints "notes locked" once it holds it, or "notes busy" after
    three minutes. A lock older than ten minutes is removed first.

func NotesRereadLine(path string) string
    NotesRereadLine is the shell line that prints, for the notes file path as
    it is when it runs, the commands of its parts, as SplitNotes gives them (awk
    under LC_ALL=C, so lengths are bytes). The judge runs it under the notes
    lock, before it merges its lessons into the live file, which the round's
    frozen copy can be older than.

func NotesUnlockLine(lock string) string
    NotesUnlockLine is the shell line that releases the notes lock.

func OwnCodexTrustCount(home string) int
    OwnCodexTrustCount is how many memories of magnum's own trust the Codex home
    home's hooks.json has.

func PaneErrorOf(msg string) string
    PaneErrorOf is the pane's error line a refused prompt's error carries (a
    run's error: Prompt appends paneError's line after "; the pane shows: "),
    as pr.launch_cleared's last_line carries it; "" when it carries none.

func PostRepliesLine(d JudgeData) string
    PostRepliesLine is the shell line the judge of a reply round runs to answer
    in its threads instead of posting a review (JudgeData.PostRepliesCommand,
    `post_replies`): the post_review line with --replies and the replies file in
    place of --review.

func PostReviewLine(d JudgeData) string
    PostReviewLine is the shell line the judge runs to post its review
    (JudgeData.PostReviewCommand, `post_review` in the <magnum> block):
    `magnum post-review` with the run's facts as flags, each value shell-quoted.
    --gh-config-dir only for an identity with its own gh config; --dry-run in
    a dry run; --no-findings-event, the round's no-findings event, from the
    value the prompt's no_findings_event shows (d.NoFindingsEvent), so the two
    never disagree and post-review refuses an APPROVE the round cannot post;
    --local-base (the base the blind replay's diff starts at) in a blind one,
    so the tool reads nothing from GitHub.

func ProjectBase(pr store.PR, repo store.Repo, base string) string
    ProjectBase is what a session of pr compares the checkout's project config
    with (checkoutProject): base, the PR's base ref or its merge base with the
    head, when the PR is based on the repository's default branch (or names
    no base), else origin/<default branch>. The team's config is the default
    branch's: a stacked PR's base branch is another PR's head, whose own
    .claude/ or .codex/ changes nobody reviewed, and compared with origin/<that
    branch> once it is fresh (the operator's fetch, a fix's: a pool slot
    fetches only the pool's base) they would load as the team's, hooks and all,
    outside the sandbox. Against the default branch they count as the PR's,
    and the session leaves them out. The engine's reload check compares a new
    head with the same base, so what that head brings from the PR's base branch
    counts there too.

func ProjectLinks(ctx context.Context, kind, dir string) (targets []string, partial bool)
    ProjectLinks are the targets, relative to the checkout dir's root, of the
    links among kind's paths at its root and under its project directories,
    and under a directory such a link leads to, and the files the instruction
    files there import (addImports; a directory one names as ExactTarget,
    that path alone), as the disk has them (onDisk: what a session in dir loaded
    through them), sorted; partial reports that the walk stopped at maxLinkWalk
    steps, or as ctx ended, so one may be missing. None for a kind magnum does
    not compare.

func ProjectPaths(kind string) []string
    ProjectPaths are the paths, relative to the checkout's root, that kind
    loads its project config from (claude: .claude, .mcp.json and CLAUDE.md,
    CLAUDE.local.md and AGENTS.md at the root and, as gitx.AnyDir globs,
    in any directory, .claude/ and what lies under it too: anyDirSpecs),
    for a comparison limited to them (gitx.Client.ChangedUnder, whose answer
    ProjectTouched reads); nil for a kind magnum does not compare.

func ProjectRule(kind string) (paths, effect, docs, docsEffect string, servers bool)
    ProjectRule describes for `magnum roles --kinds` the project config of
    kind magnum compares with the PR's merge base, e.g. ".codex/, AGENTS.md or
    AGENTS.override.md", what a session of a PR that changes it runs with (the
    kind's project_untrust), e.g. "the checkout untrusted for the session",
    the instruction files among them and what a session of a PR that changes
    only those runs with (the kind's project_docs_off; "" for a kind without
    such args), and whether project_mcp applies (that config declares MCP
    servers magnum turns off by name); paths is "" for a kind whose project
    config magnum does not compare.

func ProjectSentences(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, prID int64, head string) string
    ProjectSentences is what the board's card says of the PR's head: one
    sentence per CLI whose sessions of that head ran without the PR's project
    configuration, in projectKinds' order, naming the files and how ("Codex ran
    without the PR's AGENTS.md changes (its sessions loaded no AGENTS.md)";
    for a record of residue, "Claude ran without the checkout's .claude/ files,
    which the PR's commits do not change (…)": projectCheckOf); "" when none
    did.

func ProjectTouched(kind string, paths []string) bool
    ProjectTouched reports whether paths (a PR's changed files, relative to
    the repository root) name the project config kind loads from the checkout:
    a file at or under one of its paths, or of the name of a path in any
    directory, or under a directory of such a name (a .claude/ below the
    root), in any case (pathOf: macOS opens .Claude/settings.json for
    .claude/settings.json). A kind magnum does not compare touches nothing.

func PushLine(magnum, checkout, base string) string
    PushLine is the line a fixer App pushes with (FixPromptInput.PushCommand):
    `magnum push` of the daemon's binary (else magnum on PATH) with the
    fixer's checkout (the slot's path, so the line pushes from there wherever
    the fixer's shell stands, as DBLockLine's does; "" leaves it out, and the
    command takes the git work tree it runs in) and the PR's base as the cycle
    reads it (--base, which wins over the pane's MAGNUM_BASE_BRANCH, set when
    the pane was made; "" leaves it out), each shell-quoted. The command reads
    the PR's branch and repository from the pane's env and pushes HEAD there
    alone, with a lease, as the App.

func PushLineCI(magnum, checkout, base string) string
    PushLineCI is PushLine for a CI fix's push (the engine's CI fix mode):
    with --ci, which refuses a change to CI config.

func RecentSessionIDs(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, kind string, now time.Time, wait time.Duration) ([]store.Session, error)
    RecentSessionIDs are the sessions of agent kind kind started within
    SessionIDWindow before now whose session id tells whether herdr's hook
    gives ids, newest first: those that ran an agent (magnum prompted them),
    were not resumed (a resumed session takes the id it resumes) and started
    at least wait before now (herdr's hook reports the id at the start of a
    session's first turn). It only reads.

func RecordModelLimit(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, kind, model string, reset *time.Time, cooldown time.Duration, now time.Time) (time.Time, error)
    RecordModelLimit records in registry st that model of kind hit its own limit
    at now and returns when the limit ends: at reset when the limit message
    named one after now, else after cooldown (DefaultModelLimitCooldown when 0
    or less), never earlier than an end already recorded for the model (a report
    while the limit lasts is no repeat). A model whose last limit ended less
    than MaxReset before now hit it again within the day: without a named reset
    its limit lasts at least twice the last one's span, capped at MaxReset,
    so a weekly window costs at most one probe of the model a day; a longer
    cooldown stays as it is. It is what NoteModelLimit writes for a session,
    for a caller without one (a pane job records its limit in the live registry
    with it) and over any registry. Ended limits leave the index with their
    rows. A limit that cannot be read is the error, before anything is written;
    a failure after the limit's row was written (the repeat record, an ended
    row) leaves the limit recorded.

func RecordOldCodexTrust(home string, places []string, dry bool) (int, error)
    RecordOldCodexTrust records, as RecordStaleCodexTrust does, the trust
    entries at places (magnum's entries in the Codex home home's hooks.json)
    that no record covers yet, and says how many it recorded (with dry,
    how many it would). It is the operator's word (`magnum hooks install codex
    --assume-untrusted`) for entries an install made before magnum recorded
    the trust an append landed on: no file tells those old entries from the
    operator's Trust all.

func RecordStaleCodexTrust(home string, places []string) error
    RecordStaleCodexTrust records, for each of places (as Codex keys its trust:
    "stop:1:0") of the Codex home home's hooks.json, the trusted_hash its
    [hooks.state] entry has now: magnum rewrites its hook there in its place,
    or puts its hook at a place whose entry a hook that once stood there left
    (Codex never removes an entry), and ReadCodexHooksTrust counts the place
    untrusted while its entry keeps that hash. A place without a trust entry,
    or with one without a hash, needs no record (it reads untrusted
    anyway). hooks.json need not exist yet. Without a records directory
    (SetStaleCodexTrustDir) it records nothing and says so.

func RelatedStackLine(below, above []int) string
    RelatedStackLine is JudgeData.RelatedStack, and the round.related event's
    words for the stacks: "#751 stacked below this PR; #753 above it", either
    half alone ("#753 stacked above this PR"); "" without either.

func RememberOwnCodexTrust(home string, hooks []OwnCodexHook) error
    RememberOwnCodexTrust remembers, for each of hooks (magnum's own, which
    an uninstall is about to remove from the Codex home home's hooks.json),
    the trusted_hash at its place when the place reads trusted (it has a hash,
    and no stale record holds that hash): Codex keeps the entry after the hook
    goes, so an install that later puts the identical hook back at that place
    finds magnum's own valid trust there, which TakeOwnCodexTrust tells apart
    from a hook's that once stood there. A place with no trust, or a stale one,
    is not remembered. Without a records directory it remembers nothing.

func RenderPrompt(p config.Prompt, data any) (string, error)
    RenderPrompt executes a resolved prompt template
    (config.Config.ResolvePrompt or RolePrompt) with data: JudgeData for the
    judge's prompts, RoleData for every other session role and ShellData for
    a shell role's full-line template (values or pointers). Prompts are Go
    text/template files, a judge prompt parsed with the partials file whose
    blocks it includes (config.Prompt.Shared); a field the template needs
    but data lacks is an error. JudgeData is completed first: its Reports
    (see Report), the notes fields NotesPath implies (NotesDir, NotesLock
    and the lock commands; see NotesFiles) and the derived command lines;
    RoleData's DBLockCommand too. A judge or role prompt whose base ref, or a
    fix prompt whose head ref, a shell would read is refused (ErrUnsafeBaseRef,
    ErrUnsafeHeadRef). ShellData values are shell-quoted when needed (see
    ShellLine; use it to build a shell role's line). Trailing newlines are
    trimmed: a prompt or typed command must not end with one (a shell line would
    submit an extra empty command).

func ReportMarker(runID string) string
    ReportMarker is the line a role's report starts with to say which run wrote
    it (`<!-- magnum:run=<runID> -->`, an HTML comment Markdown does not show):
    report paths are per head, not per run, so a reviewer that kept working
    after its run ended can write where a later run on the same head looks.
    The reviewer prompts ask for it (RoleData.RunID), and a shell role's line
    with capture "stdout" prints it before the output it tees into the report
    (ShellLine).

func ReportRun(report []byte) (runID string, rest []byte)
    ReportRun reads the run a report's ReportMarker names, on its first line
    that is not blank (a byte-order mark aside), and returns the report after
    that line; a report whose first line is no marker returns "" and itself.

func SameModel(a, b string) bool
    SameModel reports whether two model names mean the same model as limit
    messages and configs spell them: equal ignoring case, or one is a word of
    the other ("opus" and "claude-opus-4-5"). "" means UnknownModel.

func SetStaleCodexTrustDir(dir string)
    SetStaleCodexTrustDir sets the directory of magnum's records of Codex
    trust entries that a rewrite of its own hooks left stale (under magnum's
    state directory). The CLI sets it once at its start, for every command
    and the daemons it runs; "" (the default, and a test binary's) keeps none,
    and ReadCodexHooksTrust then reads Codex's files alone.

func ShellDBLockLine(magnum, checkout, role, run string) string
    ShellDBLockLine is DBLockLine with `--run <run>` before the `--`: the line
    a shell role's command runs through (ShellData.DBLockCommand). The run id is
    magnum's run token: StopShell signals a command in a shell role's pane only
    when its db-lock names a run of that PR and role (runToken). An empty run is
    left out, as DBLockLine leaves it.

func ShellLine(role config.Role, d ShellData) (string, error)
    ShellLine builds the one-line command typed into a shell role's pane (see
    RunShell). With role.Command set (the role's command template overridable by
    d.Command) the line is

        [printf '\033]0;%s\007' <Title>; DISABLE_AUTO_TITLE=true; ]set -o pipefail; [{ printf '<ReportMarker(RunID)>\n'; ]<command> <args...>[; } | tee <ReportPath>]; printf '\n<Marker> %d\n' "$?"

    where <command> is the command template executed with d (every value
    shell-quoted, e.g. `{{.DBLockCommand}} codex review --base {{.BaseSHA}}`),
    the args (role.Args, or d.Args) are shell-quoted and appended, and the
    braces and the tee are there only for capture "stdout" (ReportPath is then
    required): the report starts with the run's ReportMarker, then the command's
    output. The optional prefix sets the pane's terminal title (OSC 0),
    which herdr's sidebar shows, and stops oh-my-zsh from resetting it after the
    command (its title hooks honour DISABLE_AUTO_TITLE at run time). pipefail
    makes the status the command's, not tee's; the final printf puts the marker
    on a line of its own (also after output without a trailing newline) followed
    by that status, which RunShell returns (config.Role.StatusOK judges it).
    With role.Prompt set instead, that full-line .sh template (d.Template,
    else the embedded default of that name) is rendered with d and must contain
    the marker (prompts/codex-review.sh shows the same ending). Marker must
    match [A-Za-z0-9._-]+; trailing newlines are trimmed.

func SlashCommand(text string) (name string, ok bool)
    SlashCommand is the slash command a user turn of a Claude Code transcript
    records, with its slash ("/model"): Claude Code files a slash command typed
    into the pane as a record of tags (<command-name>/model</command-name>,
    <command-message>, <command-args>), in no fixed order. ok is false for any
    other text.

func StaleCodexTrustCount(home string) int
    StaleCodexTrustCount is how many records the Codex home home's hooks.json
    has (ForgetStaleCodexTrust's count, removing nothing).

func TaggedAgentName(tag string, repo string, number int, role Role) string
    TaggedAgentName is AgentName for agents started under a tag (Deps.Tag,
    "eval" for magnum eval): the tag joins the hashed key, so a replay of a PR
    never shares, adopts or collides with the agents of the PR's own rounds.
    An empty tag is AgentName.

func TaggedPaneLabel(tag string, number int, r Role) string
    TaggedPaneLabel is the herdr pane name for a role under a tag (Deps.Tag):
    "PR #N <role>", e.g. "PR #729 codex-judge" (TaggedTitle without a repo).

func TaggedTitle(tag, repo string, number int, role Role) string
    TaggedTitle is Title under a tag (Deps.Tag): "eval PR #729 codex-judge -
    talkable". An empty tag is Title.

func TakeOwnCodexTrust(home string, hook OwnCodexHook) bool
    TakeOwnCodexTrust reports whether the trust entry at hook's place in
    the Codex home home is magnum's own, remembered at an uninstall for
    the identical hook (RememberOwnCodexTrust) and still with that hash:
    an install appending that hook there then records no stale trust. The memory
    is forgotten either way: it serves one install.

func Title(repo string, number int, role Role) string
    Title is the terminal title of a PR role's pane, which herdr's agents
    sidebar shows (terminal_title_stripped): "PR #<N> <role> - <repo>", e.g.
    "PR #729 codex-judge - talkable", "PR #729 claude-review - talkable". repo
    is the name part of "owner/name" (or a bare name); without one the title is
    the pane label "PR #<N> <role>".

    A kind with name args gets it at launch (claude --name, see StartAgent),
    a kind with only a rename command through that command typed while it works
    (codex /rename, see nameAgent), and a shell role from the OSC 0 prefix of
    its command line (ShellData.Title). A Manager's agents take agentTitle,
    with Deps.Tag and Deps.OwnerName's owner in place of "PR #<N>".

func UnderTarget(f, t string) bool
    UnderTarget reports whether f may be the link target t or lie under it
    (MatchTarget: Under or MaybeUnder): a name magnum cannot fold counts,
    so the session and the reload check err toward the config.


TYPES

type CodexHook struct {
	// Name is the last path element of its program (of the script an
	// interpreter such as bash runs), cleaned for the terminal; its type for
	// a hook that runs no command.
	Name string
	// Timeout is its timeout in seconds; 0 = none.
	Timeout int
}
    CodexHook is one hook of a Codex hooks.json, as messages name it.

type CodexHookAt struct {
	// Place is its [hooks.state] key without the hooks.json path:
	// "<event>:<group>:<index>" ("pre_tool_use:1:0").
	Place string
	CodexHook
	// Stale: its place has a trust entry, but of the hook before magnum
	// rewrote it there (RecordStaleCodexTrust), which Codex no longer
	// accepts.
	Stale bool
}
    CodexHookAt is one hook of a hooks.json at its place.

type CodexHookProblem struct {
	Check string // CodexHookMissing, CodexHookDisabled, CodexHookPlace or CodexHookTrust
	// Text says what is wrong in one sentence without its final period.
	Text string
}
```
