    CodexHookProblem is one check herdr's Codex session hook fails
    (CodexSessionHook.Problems).

type CodexHooksTrust struct {
	HooksFile  string // <home>/hooks.json
	ConfigFile string // <home>/config.toml
	// Hooks counts the hooks of HooksFile, of the events Codex runs.
	Hooks int
	// Untrusted are those whose place has no [hooks.state] entry with a
	// trusted_hash, by Codex's event order, then group and index. A hook
	// changed in place keeps its entry, whose hash is then another
	// command's: magnum cannot tell (Codex hashes its own normal form).
	Untrusted []CodexHookAt
	// Fingerprint is HooksFile's (its path and content, hashed), by which
	// the daemon and the check after a "Trust all" tell the operator once.
	Fingerprint string
}
    CodexHooksTrust is what a Codex home says of the trust of the hooks of
    its hooks.json (ReadCodexHooksTrust). Codex shows its hooks review when a
    session starts while a hook's place has no trust entry, and a prompt typed
    into the review is lost.

func ReadCodexHooksTrust(home string) (t CodexHooksTrust, ok bool, err error)
    ReadCodexHooksTrust reads which hooks of the Codex home home's hooks.json
    have no trust entry: every hook of every event Codex runs (codexHookEvents),
    in every group, whose place has no [hooks.state] entry with a trusted_hash
    in config.toml (keyed by the hooks.json path, as written or with its
    symlinks resolved; an entry without a hash trusts nothing), and every one
    whose entry keeps the hash magnum recorded when it rewrote the hook there
    (RecordStaleCodexTrust: Stale). ok is false when there is nothing to judge:
    home unknown or no hooks.json there. A missing config.toml or [hooks.state]
    table trusts nothing. err names a file that cannot be read or decoded,
    without the decoder's message. It never writes Codex's files; it removes
    a record of magnum's whose entry's hash changed, or whose entry or hook is
    gone.

func (t CodexHooksTrust) UntrustedPlaces() string
    UntrustedPlaces names the hooks of t without a trust entry and their places:
    "moshi-hook at session_start:1:0, Bartender NotchBar at pre_tool_use:0:0".

func (t CodexHooksTrust) UntrustedSentence(hooksFile string) string
    UntrustedSentence says how many hooks of t have no trust entry, or one
    Codex no longer accepts (Stale), naming hooksFile as given: "2 hooks in
    ~/.codex/hooks.json have no trust entry"; with a stale one it adds the way
    out when Codex asks nothing (CodexForgetStaleStep); "" when every hook is
    trusted.

type CodexSessionHook struct {
	HooksFile  string // <home>/hooks.json
	ConfigFile string // <home>/config.toml
	// Found: a SessionStart hook of HooksFile names HerdrSessionHook.
	Found bool
	// Disabled are the keys of the [hooks.state] entries that set enabled =
	// false on each such hook, when every one of them has such an entry;
	// nil when one of them runs (its entry enables it, or it has none).
	Disabled []string
	// Group and Index are the place of herdr's hook that runs, when one
	// does (the first whose place has a trust entry, else the first not
	// disabled): its group among HooksFile's SessionStart groups and its
	// index in that group. Place is its [hooks.state] key without the
	// hooks.json path ("session_start:<group>:<index>").
	Group, Index int
	Place        string
	// Before are the SessionStart hooks before it, in Codex's order, but
	// those their entries disable.
	Before []CodexHook
	// Trusted: config.toml has a [hooks.state] entry with a trusted_hash for
	// its place. Whether that hash is of this command magnum cannot tell
	// (Codex hashes its own normal form of the hook).
	Trusted bool
	// Version is the HERDR_INTEGRATION_VERSION its script's header names
	// ("" = unknown: no such line, or no script where its command says).
	Version string
}
    CodexSessionHook is what a Codex home says of herdr's SessionStart hook
    (ReadCodexSessionHook).

func ReadCodexSessionHook(home string) (h CodexSessionHook, ok bool, err error)
    ReadCodexSessionHook reads herdr's SessionStart hook in the Codex home home:
    whether a SessionStart hook of its hooks.json names HerdrSessionHook,
    whether config.toml's [hooks.state] entry of each such hook (keyed by the
    hooks.json path, as written or with its symlinks resolved) sets enabled
    = false, and, of the one that runs, its place, the hooks before it,
    its trust entry and its script's integration version. ok is false when
    there is nothing to judge: home unknown or no hooks.json there (herdr not
    installed is another check). A missing config.toml, [hooks.state] table or
    entry disables nothing and trusts nothing. err names a file that cannot be
    read or decoded, without the decoder's message, which may quote the file.
    It only reads.

func (h CodexSessionHook) Problems(hooksFile, configFile string) []CodexHookProblem
    Problems are the checks herdr's hook fails, naming the files as
    hooksFile and configFile say (doctor shows their paths; a daemon message
    CodexFileName's, since a Codex home may be a pane env value): the hook is
    missing, or disabled, or else its place (a hook before it can hold it up:
    no timeout, or one over CodexHookMaxTimeout) and its trust (its place has no
    trust entry, so Codex asks the operator to review the hooks before it runs
    it). None when it passes.

type Deps struct {
	Herdr  Herdr
	Store  *store.Store
	Runner execx.Runner // wrapper probe and preflight (read-only commands)
	Config *config.Config
	Layout paths.Layout
	Clock  func() time.Time // nil = time.Now
	// Sleep waits between polls (quit, trust-dialog readiness); nil = a
	// timer honouring ctx.
	Sleep func(ctx context.Context, d time.Duration) error

	// CodexConfig and ClaudeConfig are the CLI config files EnsureTrust
	// edits; "" = the CLIs' defaults ($CODEX_HOME/config.toml or
	// ~/.codex/config.toml; $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.claude.json or
	// ~/.claude.json). A test binary never falls back to the defaults.
	CodexConfig  string
	ClaudeConfig string
	// ClaudeSettings is the Claude Code settings file whose default model
	// SwitchModel restores after a /model switch; "" = the CLI's default
	// ($CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json or ~/.claude/settings.json). A test
	// binary never falls back to the defaults.
	ClaudeSettings string
	// ClaudeDir is Claude Code's config directory, whose projects/ holds
	// the session transcripts the observer reads for background work (see
	// backgroundWait); "" = $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, else ~/.claude. A session
	// whose pane env sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR uses that. A test binary never
	// falls back to the defaults.
	ClaudeDir string
	// CodexHome is the Codex home whose sessions/ holds the rollouts
	// TurnError reads a turn's error from; "" = $CODEX_HOME, else ~/.codex.
	// A session whose pane env sets CODEX_HOME uses that. A test binary
	// never falls back to the defaults.
	CodexHome string
	// SkipGoneDirs has ResumeID pass over a conversation whose recorded
	// working directory no longer exists (dirGone), so the role starts fresh
	// instead of reading the old paths its conversation names. The daemons
	// set it; tests that record made-up directories leave it off.
	SkipGoneDirs bool
	// Log receives one line per trust entry added and per trust dialog
	// answered (optional).
	Log execx.Logger
	// Tag marks agents started outside the PR's own rounds ("eval" for
	// magnum eval): it joins their names' hash (TaggedAgentName) and leads
	// their titles and pane labels (TaggedTitle). "" = the PR's own agents.
	Tag string
	// OwnerName names the owner of a stored PR row in the titles and pane
	// labels of its agents ("PR #729" by default, "PR-12345" or "task 12" for
	// a factory's task): the title "<tag> <owner> <role> - <repo>" a claude
	// agent gets by --name and a codex agent by /rename, and the pane label
	// "<tag> <owner> <role>". nil, or a "" answer, keeps "PR #<number>". The
	// agent's herdr name (AgentName) always keeps the row's number.
	OwnerName func(store.PR) string
	// IdentityEnv is the GitHub env (identity.Source.Env) of the configured
	// identity name, false when it is not declared or cannot make its env.
	// A pane of a role with an identity (config.Role.Identity) gets that env
	// in place of the posting identity's (see paneEnv); nil = no identities,
	// so such a pane keeps the env it was given.
	IdentityEnv func(name string) (env map[string]string, ok bool)
	// FixerEnv is the git environment a fix role's pane gets beside its
	// identity's (identity.FixerGitEnv, laid over by paneEnv): for a
	// dedicated fixer App, its bot as the commits' author and committer,
	// commits unsigned and a plain `git push` to github.com refused, all as
	// process env and never as a git config write; nil for a gh identity,
	// whose pane keeps the operator's git setup. nil = none.
	FixerEnv func(identity string) map[string]string
	// Toast shows the operator a toast (key dedupes it, title and body say
	// it): Codex did not save the hook trust magnum answered
	// (EventHooksTrustUnsaved). It must not block; nil = none.
	Toast func(ctx context.Context, key, title, body string)
	// The callbacks below the collaborators (OwnerName, IdentityEnv,
	// FixerEnv, Toast, Signal, Log) may run under the Manager's observe
	// lock, on an observe pass or a look of Wake's: none may wait for a
	// pass, and a lock one of them takes must never be held around a pass
	// or a Wake call (the factory's OwnerName takes Runtime.mu).
	//
	// HookSocket is the socket of the daemon's hook listener
	// (agenthooks.Listen at paths.Layout.HookSocket or FactoryHookSocket):
	// every pane the Manager makes (EnsureWorkspace, EnsurePane, a dead
	// launch's replacement) gets it as MAGNUM_HOOK_SOCKET and the binary
	// (HookBin) as MAGNUM_HOOK_BIN, so the agents' hooks there send their
	// events to it (Wake). "" = no hooks (no listener, a socket path too
	// long, a listener that failed): no pane gets either, and the passes
	// alone see the agents, as before. A pane keeps the env it was made with.
	// Manager.SetHookSocket changes it later, under the Manager's lock.
	HookSocket string
	// HookBin is the magnum binary the panes' hooks run; "" = the layout's
	// (Layout.Binary). Without either, no pane gets the hook env.
	HookBin string
	// HookFailure receives the class of API error a Claude turn ended on,
	// as the session's own StopFailure hook names it and its screen, read
	// again (at once, and a second later when it did not show it yet),
	// shows it (Wake): the session's row, the class (never the hook's text)
	// and the screen's verdict (its ResetAt for a limit; its Detail is the
	// screen's line, as the engine's own health check reads it), so the
	// engine feeds its usage, login and overload handling at once. It comes
	// once per failure (a class per prompt of the session), on the goroutine
	// that called Wake (the listener's) or on the one that read the screen
	// again, so it must not block, and Wake's caller must hold no lock it
	// takes; nil = none.
	HookFailure func(session store.Session, failure StopFailure, screen Health)
	// Signal sends sig to process pid, or to the process group -pid when
	// pid is negative (the daemon passes syscall.Kill). Only StopShell
	// signals, and only processes of a command it proved an own run of
	// magnum (ownShell, captureJob). nil = nothing is ever signalled, so a
	// Manager built without it (a test's) cannot reach a real process.
	Signal func(pid int, sig syscall.Signal) error
}
    Deps are the Manager's collaborators.

type FallbackData struct {
	Model      string // the model the session runs now
	Previous   string // the model that hit its limit
	Role       string
	URL        string
	HeadSHA    string
	ReportPath string // the role's report or result file; "" = the prompt names none
}
    FallbackData feeds the model-fallback prompt.

type FixPromptInput struct {
	HeadRef, ReviewURL, ReviewFile, ExternalFile, ReviewerLogin, DBLockCommand, FixReplyCommand string
	FixSyncCommand, PushCommand, FixerLogin                                                     string
	NoFindings                                                                                  bool
	NotesParts                                                                                  NotesParts
	ConflictBase, ConflictSHA                                                                   string
	ConflictPaths                                                                               []string
	OwnPR                                                                                       bool
	// MergeOnly: the run merges the PR's parent alone (the conflict above),
	// with no review, finding or other reviewer's item. MergedBase and
	// MergedSHA are the base whose tip magnum merged into the PR before the
	// run ("" = none): the head the fixer starts from is that merge.
	MergeOnly             bool
	MergedBase, MergedSHA string
	// CIOnly: the run fixes the PR's failed required CI from CIFile,
	// ci-failures.json beside the report, which the fix job wrote (the CI
	// reader's: data, the output of the PR's code and its tests), and
	// replies in no thread.
	CIOnly bool
	CIFile string
}
    FixPromptInput is what the fix job knows beyond the PR, the role and the
    run that FixPrompt reads: the PR's branch (HeadRef), the review it fixes
    (ReviewURL, its review.json ReviewFile and ReviewerLogin, the login that
    posted it), the file of the other reviewers' open items (ExternalFile,
    external-threads.json beside the report; "" = none, the prompt then
    names no such file), the line the fixer runs its database commands
    through (DBLockCommand, DBLockLine; "" = derived without a checkout),
    the line it posts every reply through (FixReplyCommand, FixReplyLine;
    "" = magnum on PATH), the line it runs when a push is rejected because the
    branch moved (FixSyncCommand, FixSyncLine; "" = none, the prompt then names
    no such line), for a fixer App the line it pushes with and the login it acts
    as (PushCommand, PushLine, and FixerLogin; "" = a gh fixer, which pushes
    with git push as the author), whether the review found nothing, leaving
    the fixer the external file's items and the base merge alone (NoFindings),
    whether the PR is the operator's own, which lets the fixer edit its
    description (OwnPR; RoleData.OwnPR), the job's frozen copy of the repository
    notes in parts (NotesParts, FreezeNotes beside the report; zero = none),
    which the fixer reads and never edits, and the PR's conflict with its base,
    which the fixer merges first: the base branch (ConflictBase), the tip of it
    magnum fetched (ConflictSHA; "" = no conflict, or magnum could not check)
    and the conflicting paths (ConflictPaths, as git names them).

type Health struct {
	Kind    HealthKind
	ResetAt *time.Time // usage_limit and model_limit, when the text names a reset time
	// Model is the limited model a model_limit pattern captured (its "model"
	// group, lower case); "" = the session's current model.
	Model  string
	Detail string // the matching line, redacted, at most 300 bytes
}
    Health is the classifier's verdict.

func ClassifyAt(text string, now time.Time) Health
    ClassifyAt is ClassifyWith with config.DefaultHealthPatterns.

func ClassifyWith(rx config.HealthRegexps, text string, now time.Time) Health
    ClassifyWith classifies recent pane output of an agent session with a
    kind's compiled health patterns (config.HealthPatterns.Compile) plus the
    built-in trust-dialog, approval and stalled patterns. The match on the
    latest line wins (pane text keeps old errors above newer output); on one
    line refused > login_required > model_limit > usage_limit > trust_dialog
    > blocked > overloaded > stalled. A model_limit match sets Model from
    the pattern's "model" group. For usage_limit and model_limit, ResetAt
    comes from "try again at 3:45 PM", "try again at Oct 5th, 2026 9:05 AM",
    "try again in 1 day 4 hours", "resets 5pm (Europe/Kyiv)", "resets Oct 7,
    9am" or "limit reached|<epoch>", read relative to now (bare clock times
    in now's zone unless the text names one; a time more than 12h past means
    tomorrow) and capped at MaxReset ahead. No match is HealthOK.

type HealthKind string
    HealthKind classifies an agent pane's recent output.

const (
	HealthOK HealthKind = "ok"
	// HealthRefused: the provider flagged the content as a safety risk
	// (Codex's "flagged for possible cybersecurity risk"): the round ends at
	// once and the PR is flagged, never reviewed again.
	HealthRefused       HealthKind = "refused"
	HealthLoginRequired HealthKind = "login_required" // pause the kind; e.g. `codex login` / `claude auth login`
	HealthModelLimit    HealthKind = "model_limit"    // one model's cap: switch the session to a fallback model (Model, ResetAt)
	HealthUsageLimit    HealthKind = "usage_limit"    // pause until ResetAt (fallback 1h, doubling)
	HealthOverloaded    HealthKind = "overloaded"     // 5xx/429/reconnecting: retry with backoff
	HealthStalled       HealthKind = "stalled"        // turn interrupted / context full
	HealthBlocked       HealthKind = "blocked"        // approval (or other trust) dialog: needs the human
	HealthTrustDialog   HealthKind = "trust_dialog"   // Codex/Claude first-launch folder trust: AnswerTrustDialog
)
    Health kinds.

type Herdr interface {
	Snapshot(ctx context.Context) (herdr.Snapshot, error)
	WorkspaceCreate(ctx context.Context, o herdr.WorkspaceCreateOptions) (herdr.WorkspaceCreated, error)
	WorkspaceClose(ctx context.Context, workspaceID string) error
	PaneSplit(ctx context.Context, paneID string, o herdr.SplitOptions) (herdr.Pane, error)
	PaneRename(ctx context.Context, paneID, label string) error
	PaneRun(ctx context.Context, paneID, command string) error
	PaneWaitOutput(ctx context.Context, paneID string, o herdr.WaitOutputOptions) (herdr.OutputMatch, error)
	PaneRead(ctx context.Context, paneID string, o herdr.ReadOptions) (herdr.ReadResult, error)
	PaneGet(ctx context.Context, paneID string) (herdr.Pane, error)
	PaneSendKeys(ctx context.Context, paneID string, keys ...string) error
	PaneClose(ctx context.Context, paneID string) error
	PaneProcessInfo(ctx context.Context, paneID string) (herdr.ProcessInfo, error)
	WaitIdleShell(ctx context.Context, paneID string, timeout time.Duration) (herdr.ProcessInfo, error)
	AgentStart(ctx context.Context, o herdr.AgentStartOptions) (herdr.AgentStarted, error)
	AgentPrompt(ctx context.Context, target, text string, wait *herdr.PromptWait) (herdr.AgentInfo, error)
	AgentRead(ctx context.Context, target string, o herdr.ReadOptions) (herdr.ReadResult, error)
	AgentRename(ctx context.Context, target, name string) error
	AgentSendKeys(ctx context.Context, target string, keys ...string) error
}
    Herdr is the subset of *herdr.Client this package uses.

type HookAgreement struct {
	Kind     string `json:"kind"`
	Agreed   int    `json:"agreed"`
	Differed int    `json:"differed"`
}
    HookAgreement is how often the hooks' state of a kind's sessions agreed with
    herdr's status at the observe passes (ReadHookAgreement).

func ReadHookAgreement(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, now time.Time) ([]HookAgreement, error)
    ReadHookAgreement is how often, per agent kind (by name), the hooks' state
    of a session agreed with herdr's status at the observe passes of the current
    hour and the 23 before it, as now reads them; kinds without a reading are
    left out.

type HookState string
    HookState is a session's state as its agent's own hooks tell it.

const (
	HookReady   HookState = "ready"   // a SessionStart: the agent came up and waits
	HookWorking HookState = "working" // a UserPromptSubmit: a turn began
	HookBlocked HookState = "blocked" // a PermissionRequest: the agent waits on an approval
	HookIdle    HookState = "idle"    // the turn ended: a Stop, a StopFailure, an Interrupt, the transcript or the rollout
)
    The hooks' states ("" while the hooks said nothing, or after the session's
    SessionEnd).

type JudgeData struct {
	// Readiness is what magnum's prepare/ready probes found before the
	// reviewers (status and reason only; command output stays in
	// readiness.json because it is PR text).
	Readiness Readiness

	RunID         string
	Owner, Repo   string
	Number        int
	URL           string
	HeadSHA       string
	BaseRef       string
	BaseSHA       string
	Checkout      string // absolute checkout path the judge works in
	IdentityKind  string // gh | app
	ReviewerLogin string // REST form, e.g. talkable[bot]
	GhConfigDir   string // "" for the gh identity
	// NoFindingsEvent is APPROVE or COMMENT: COMMENT whenever a reviewer
	// of the round left no usable report or the auto-approval author lists
	// refuse the PR's author (pipeline.JudgeEvents), the round holds its
	// approval for a full pass (HoldApproval), or the approval's gates
	// refuse it (NoApproval). The post_review line passes the same value as
	// --no-findings-event (PostReviewLine).
	NoFindingsEvent string
	BlockingEvent   string // REQUEST_CHANGES | COMMENT
	SelfAuthored    bool
	Reports         []Report // one per non-judge role of the round, in pipeline order
	// LateReports are the labels of the Reports marked Late (always
	// derived): a completion's judge (SameHead) went without them in its
	// last review and decides their findings now, while the other reports
	// stand as that review judged them. Rendered as one instruction by the
	// rereview and recovery prompts, only then.
	LateReports []string
	// LateSince is the head the late reports' round reviewed from
	// (pipeline.Completion.Since): a late claude-simplify report's proposals
	// keep to the lines changed since it; "" = the lines the whole PR added
	// or modified (a first review's round). Only with LateReports.
	LateSince  string
	ResultFile string // <report dir>/<the judge's output>, e.g. codex-judge.json
	// Magnum is the magnum executable the judge's post_review line runs
	// (the daemon's own, absolute; "" = magnum on PATH). ReviewFile is
	// where the judge writes the review it posts (<report dir>/review.json,
	// derived from ResultFile when empty), and PostReviewCommand the line
	// that posts it, rendered as `post_review` (PostReviewLine; always
	// derived).
	Magnum, ReviewFile, PostReviewCommand string
	// Role is the judge role's name (Manager.RolePrompt fills it when
	// empty), and DBLockCommand the line its database commands run through
	// in Checkout, rendered as `db_lock` (DBLockLine; always derived).
	Role, DBLockCommand string
	DryRun              bool
	// Blind: an evaluation replay (pipeline.RoundInput.Blind), rendered as
	// `blind: true`; the skill then judges the local diff of HeadSHA only.
	Blind bool
	// Local (with Blind and DryRun): the factory's local round of a change
	// before its PR exists (pipeline.RoundInput.Local), rendered as
	// `local: true` with `description_file`, only then: no PR is on GitHub,
	// so the judge reads the title and the body from DescriptionFile (the
	// factory's description.md) and the ticket from TicketFile, and makes no
	// gh call (the skill's "Local round"). A round of a PR on GitHub leaves
	// both zero, and its prompts render as they always did.
	Local           bool
	DescriptionFile string
	// PostMerge: GitHub merged the PR before magnum reviewed HeadSHA
	// (pipeline.RoundInput.PostMerge), rendered as `post_merge: true` only
	// then; the skill posts a COMMENT that asks for follow-ups, and
	// NoFindingsEvent and BlockingEvent are both COMMENT.
	PostMerge     bool
	SkillPath     string // the role's skill, absolute
	Model, Effort string // the judge role's model and this round's effort (config.Role.EffortFor)
	// EffortInPrompt: the agent's kind sets the effort only at launch (its
	// effort args) and this round's Effort differs from the role's, so a
	// running session cannot switch to it; the prompt asks for it in words.
	EffortInPrompt bool
	// NotesPath is the repository notes file: the judge reads it first and
	// rewrites it at the end of a round that taught something durable. ""
	// = no notes, and the prompts leave the notes fields out. The judge
	// prompts pass it and the fields below as `notes`, `notes_dir`,
	// `notes_harness`, `notes_lock` and `notes_unlock` in the <magnum>
	// block; the steps are the skill's.
	NotesPath string
	// NotesDir is the harness directory next to NotesPath and NotesLock the
	// lock the judge holds while it rewrites the notes (NotesFiles; derived
	// from NotesPath when empty). NotesLockCommand and NotesUnlockCommand
	// are the shell lines that take and release it (NotesLockLine,
	// NotesUnlockLine; always derived).
	NotesDir, NotesLock                  string
	NotesLockCommand, NotesUnlockCommand string
	// NotesParts is the round's frozen copy of the notes, in parts
	// (FreezeNotes): the judge prompts render it as `notes_parts`, the
	// copy, its size and one command per part, with the sentence that asks
	// for one part per tool call; zero = no notes to read (none yet, or
	// empty), and the field is left out.
	NotesParts NotesParts
	// NotesRereadCommand prints the parts of the live notes file
	// (NotesRereadLine; always derived from NotesPath): rendered as
	// `notes_reread` beside `notes_lock`, which the judge runs once it holds
	// the lock, before it merges, since the frozen copy can be older.
	NotesRereadCommand string
	// NotesHarness names the harness directory's entries (sorted; a
	// directory ends in "/"), at most NotesHarnessMax of them, so the judge
	// sees scripts the notes no longer mention; NotesHarnessMore counts the
	// rest.
	NotesHarness     []string
	NotesHarnessMore int
	// NotesMaxLine is [notes] max_line: a notes line longer than this many
	// characters marks the repository for a curation. The judge prompts that
	// rewrite the notes (not the own pass, which writes none) pass it as
	// `notes_max_line` and ask the judge to keep each line within it; 0 =
	// unknown, and they leave both out.
	NotesMaxLine int

	// Re-review / recovery.
	PreviousReviewID int64
	PreviousEvent    string
	PreviousHeadSHA  string
	Since            string // RFC3339: read every comment since then
	// ForcePushed (rereview, recovery): PreviousHeadSHA is no longer in the
	// branch, so the judge reviews the full PR diff again.
	ForcePushed bool
	// ColdJudge (recovery): the judge started fresh on purpose, because its
	// conversation's prompt cache had gone cold or its session served its
	// max_session_rounds (pipeline.RoundInput.ColdJudge), not because its
	// session was lost: the earlier reviews cover the PR up to
	// PreviousHeadSHA, so the own pass reads the commits since (unless
	// ForcePushed or BaseMerged says otherwise).
	ColdJudge bool
	// FullPass (recovery): a scheduled full pass ([pipeline]
	// full_pass_every; pipeline.RoundInput.FullPass): every session started
	// fresh, and the judge reviews the full PR diff again as a first review
	// does, then decides every earlier thread under the reply contract; a
	// finding the earlier reviews missed ends its title with `(missed
	// earlier)`, and the body is headed as a full pass. Rendered as
	// `full_pass: true` and one instruction, only then.
	FullPass bool
	// AuditFile (recovery): an audit pass ([pipeline] audit_every;
	// pipeline.RoundInput.Audit): audit.json in the report directory lists
	// AuditAreas areas of the PR's evidence map (unknown or stale ones, the
	// riskiest first, and an earlier probe to run again; PR content, so
	// never in the prompt), which the judge probes through their real entry
	// points with a control before the re-review; an unknown area is a lead,
	// never a finding. Rendered as one instruction, only then; "" = none.
	AuditFile  string
	AuditAreas int
	// HoldApproval (rereview, recovery): the round cannot approve
	// ([pipeline] approve_after_full_pass; pipeline.RoundInput.HoldApproval):
	// NoFindingsEvent is COMMENT, a clean verdict posts as a comment, and a
	// full pass of the whole PR follows before the approval. Rendered as
	// one instruction, with the body line a clean verdict adds, only then.
	HoldApproval bool
	// NoApproval (initial, rereview, recovery, continue): why the round
	// cannot approve although its identity would (pipeline.RoundInput:
	// NoApproval, the gates decided at dispatch, else CIGate's refusal when
	// the prompt is written), in a few fixed words that never carry PR text
	// ("the PR changes its own workflows or actions"); NoFindingsEvent is
	// then COMMENT. Rendered as one instruction beside the events, only
	// then; "" = none.
	NoApproval string
	// PreviousHeadShort is PreviousHeadSHA cut to 7 characters (always
	// derived; see textx.ShortSHA).
	PreviousHeadShort string
	// BaseMerged (rereview): the commits since PreviousHeadSHA merged a
	// branch in, usually the base, so PreviousHeadSHA..HeadSHA carries its
	// commits: the prompt compares the PR's own diff before and after.
	BaseMerged bool
	// DeltaCheck (rereview, recovery): the round is a delta check: the judge
	// alone reviews the commits since its last review, DeltaLines changed
	// code lines in the files DeltaFile lists (a JSON file in the report
	// directory, "" when it could not be written: the file names are PR
	// content); in a recovery its fresh session first reads its previous
	// review and threads. Rendered as `delta_check: true` and one
	// instruction, only then.
	DeltaCheck bool
	DeltaLines int
	DeltaFile  string
	// SameHead (rereview, recovery): the round re-reviews the head the
	// judge's last review covered (no new commits), the judge alone: the
	// prompt asks it to re-decide its earlier findings from the replies and
	// comments since, running no check that review already ran. Rendered as
	// one instruction, only then.
	SameHead bool
	// CIRed (rereview, recovery; with SameHead): a CI follow-up: a check of
	// the head failed after the judge's last review of it was prompted, so
	// that review did not see it. The prompt asks the judge to decide each
	// check `failing_checks` lists (a P1 broken build the PR causes, with
	// the failing example or step quoted, else an unrelated Checks line) and
	// to post exactly one review. Rendered as one instruction, only then; no
	// <magnum> field.
	CIRed bool
	// Replies (rereview, recovery; with SameHead): a reply round: Replies
	// replies came on the judge's review since it last read the threads,
	// with no new commits. When its verdict and event stay those of its
	// last review, the judge posts no review but answers in the threads
	// with PostRepliesCommand. 0 = not a reply round.
	//
	// PostRepliesCommand (PostRepliesLine, rendered as `post_replies`)
	// posts RepliesFile (<report dir>/replies.json, derived from ResultFile
	// when empty): every thread reply of the judge, alone in a reply round
	// or after its review in any round with an earlier review (Replies,
	// PreviousReviewID or PreviousHeadSHA set). Both always derived; empty
	// in a first review.
	Replies                         int
	RepliesFile, PostRepliesCommand string
	// StopThreads counts the threads of Threads marked Stop: the prompt
	// says not to reply there again.
	StopThreads     int
	MovedFrom       string // previous checkout path when the PR changed slots
	PreviousReviews []PreviousReview
	// Threads are the inline threads the reviewer login started on the PR,
	// each reply classified (re-review). Replies are PR content, so no
	// prompt prints them: magnum writes Threads to ThreadsFile and a prompt
	// names that file and ThreadSummary.
	Threads []ReviewThread
	// ThreadsFile is the JSON file holding Threads; "" = magnum did not read
	// the threads, and the judge reads the replies itself.
	ThreadsFile string
	// ThreadSummary counts Threads and their replies by class, e.g. "3
	// threads (1 resolved, 1 outdated); replies: 1 fixed, 1 not a bug; 1
	// thread without a reply".
	ThreadSummary string
	// FormerLogins are the logins (REST form) this PR's earlier reviews were
	// posted as before magnum moved it to ReviewerLogin (an identity
	// migration): their reviews and threads are the judge's own history,
	// while every new write goes as ReviewerLogin. Empty for most PRs.
	FormerLogins []string

	// Mode is the round's kind (initial, rereview or recovery), which the
	// own-pass prompt renders as `mode` (each other judge prompt serves one
	// kind and names it itself).
	Mode string
	// Phase is the judge's phase of a round that prompts it twice
	// ([pipeline] judge_own_pass = "parallel"): PhaseOwnPass for its own
	// pass, prompted with the reviewers, PhaseCandidates for judging their
	// reports once both ended; "" for a round with one judge prompt.
	// Rendered as `phase` only when set.
	Phase string
	// OwnFindings is the file the own pass writes (OwnFindingsFile in the
	// report directory) and the candidates phase starts from, rendered as
	// `own_findings`; "" outside a two-phase round. OwnFindingsMissing
	// (candidates phase): the own pass left no such file, or an empty one,
	// so the prompt asks for the pass now.
	OwnFindings        string
	OwnFindingsMissing bool
	// RestartedFrom (own pass): a push cut the judge's own pass on this
	// head short and the round restarted on HeadSHA; the prompt asks it to
	// reuse what still applies.
	RestartedFrom string
	// RelatedPRs is related.json in the report directory: the repository's
	// other open PRs, and those merged lately, that change the same paths
	// (numbers, URLs, heads, the shared paths and magnum's reviews of them;
	// never PR text), rendered as `related_prs`; "" when there is none, and
	// always in a blind replay.
	RelatedPRs string
	// StackedBelow and StackedAbove are the open PRs of the related set
	// (before related.json leaves out those an earlier review named)
	// stacked under this one, their head in HeadSHA's history, and on top
	// of it, HeadSHA in theirs, as git answers in the checkout (pipeline's
	// related step), by number. RelatedStack says both in words after
	// `related_prs` on its line (RelatedStackLine; always derived). With a
	// PR below, the own pass and the initial, rereview and recovery
	// prompts say in one line, related.json or not, that a finding only on
	// that PR's lines is that PR's (`outside_diff`).
	StackedBelow, StackedAbove []int
	RelatedStack               string
	// HistoryFile is history.json in the report directory: each file the PR
	// changes (at most 40, related_ignore's paths aside) with its last 8
	// commits on the base (pipeline.FilesHistory), rendered as `history` by
	// the own pass and the initial, rereview and recovery prompts; "" when
	// magnum wrote none (no file of the PR on the base, a continued turn, a
	// git failure).
	HistoryFile string
	// DocsFile is docs.json in the report directory: for each file the PR
	// changes (related_ignore's paths aside), the .md pages of the base
	// that name it, or else that name its directory (pipeline.BaseDocs:
	// page paths, never their text; at most 10 per path), rendered as
	// `docs` by the own pass and the initial, rereview and recovery
	// prompts; "" when no page names a changed path, and as for
	// HistoryFile.
	DocsFile string
	// TicketFile is ticket.md in the report directory: the Jira issue the
	// PR's title or head branch names (pipeline.TicketFile: its key, URL,
	// summary, status, type, priority, labels, parent, description and
	// requirement fields, the text as Jira gives it, never a comment or a
	// person), rendered as `ticket` by every judge prompt, the path only
	// (it is data); "" when [jira] is off, the PR names no issue, or the
	// read failed. A continued turn names the paused turn's file.
	TicketFile string
	// PrepassFile is prepass.json in the report directory, magnum's reading
	// of the PR's diff with git (pipeline.Prepass: the removed definitions
	// files outside the diff still name, the changed source files without a
	// test change, the body of each method a hunk changes, each added
	// file's closest existing sibling; or why it was skipped), rendered as
	// `prepass` by the own pass and the initial, rereview and recovery
	// prompts, which say to read it first, a method's body before its hunk,
	// each item a lead to check, never a finding by itself; "" in a
	// continued turn and without Git.
	PrepassFile string
	// Stakes is what the PR's repository puts at risk, as the operator's
	// config states it ([[repo]] or [[watch]] stakes;
	// config.Config.StakesFor), one line: the skill sizes each harm against
	// it, never against a stakes block in the checkout (PR content).
	// Rendered as `stakes` after `prepass` by the own pass and the initial,
	// rereview and recovery prompts; "" = unsaid, and they leave it out.
	Stakes string
	// MaxSimplifications is how many of claude-simplify's proposals the
	// judge posts at most, the most substantial first, as the operator's
	// config states it ([[repo]] or [pipeline] max_simplifications;
	// config.Config.MaxSimplificationsFor). Rendered in the simplification
	// rules of the initial, rereview and recovery prompts, which carry them
	// only with a usable claude-simplify report; 0 renders
	// config.DefaultMaxSimplifications (completed), never "at most 0".
	MaxSimplifications int
	// EvidenceFile is where the judge writes what it examined in the round
	// (EvidenceFile in the report directory, beside ResultFile): one entry
	// per behaviour it read or probed and one unknown entry per file of the
	// diff it reviewed that it did not read (pipeline.Evidence), rendered
	// as `evidence_file` beside
	// `result_file` by the initial, rereview, recovery and continue
	// prompts, the first three with the instruction; "" = none (the
	// pipeline always sets it).
	EvidenceFile string
	// EvidenceMap is the PR's evidence map (pipeline.EvidenceMapPath): what
	// the earlier rounds examined, merged by the engine, each entry read,
	// probed, skipped, unknown or stale (its file changed since), rendered
	// as `evidence` by the own pass and the initial, rereview and recovery
	// prompts, which say to read the unknown and stale areas first; "" when
	// the PR has none, in a continued turn and in a blind replay.
	EvidenceMap string
	// RepeatPaths is repeat-paths.json in the report directory
	// (pipeline.RepeatPathsFile): each path of the PR with posted P1 or P2
	// findings in three or more rounds, with those rounds, the findings'
	// titles and the earlier finding each "(in the fix for ...)" names,
	// rendered as `repeat_paths` by the own pass and the rereview and
	// recovery prompts; "" when no path qualifies, in a first review, a
	// continued turn, a blind replay and a local round.
	RepeatPaths string
	// FailingChecks is failing-checks.json in the report directory: the
	// head's failed CI checks as the poller last saw them (prs.ci_json:
	// name, workflow, state, time), rendered as `failing_checks` by the
	// initial, rereview and continue prompts; "" when none failed, when
	// the checks are another commit's, and in a blind replay. A file, as
	// check names come from the PR's workflows.
	FailingChecks string
	// ProjectChecks is the review's Checks line for the round's agent CLIs
	// whose sessions of its head ran without the PR's changes to the
	// project config they load from the checkout or, for a record of
	// residue (ProjectNote.Residue), without the checkout's files there that
	// the PR's commits do not change (the PR's ProjectNote of the kind names
	// the round's head): "Codex ran without the PR's AGENTS.md changes;
	// Claude ran without the PR's CLAUDE.md and .claude/ changes", for
	// residue "Claude ran without the checkout's .claude/ files, which the
	// PR's commits do not change" (projectChecks of projectCheckOf; magnum's
	// names of the paths, never a path the PR named), rendered as
	// `project_checks` by the initial, rereview and recovery prompts; ""
	// when none did. Set by NoteDeclinedProjects, each CLI only in a round
	// with a role of its kind.
	ProjectChecks string
}
    JudgeData feeds every judge prompt (judge-*.md). Fields a template does not
    use may stay zero.

type Manager struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Manager drives agent sessions. Safe for concurrent use: the daemon tick
    (Observe) and per-round goroutines (Prompt, RunShell) share it.

func New(d Deps) *Manager
    New returns a Manager.

func (m *Manager) AnswerTrustDialog(ctx context.Context, s store.Session) (bool, error)
    AnswerTrustDialog is the fallback for an agent stopped at its CLI's
    first-launch folder-trust dialog (EnsureTrust normally prevents it). It
    acts only within TrustWindow of the session's start (StartedAt) and before
    the session was ever prompted (LastPromptAt), and only when the pane's
    visible screen shows the whole dialog of the session's agent kind (see
    detectTrustDialog) with the cursor on one of its options: Codex ("Folder
    access", "Trust this folder?", "Trust and continue" / "Quit"): Enter;
    Claude ("Accessing workspace:", "No, exit" / "Yes, I trust this folder"):
    Down (or Up) to the trust option, confirmed by a re-read, then Enter. It
    records an EventTrustDialogAnswered event and waits up to TrustReadyTimeout
    for the agent to be idle. It reports whether it answered; any other dialog
    or screen, a shell role and any kind other than codex and claude (whose
    trust handling is unknown) are left untouched (false, nil).

func (m *Manager) BackgroundProgress(ctx context.Context, run store.Run) string
    BackgroundProgress is a short text that changes whenever the transcript of
    a teammate the claude agent of run's session spawned during run, and still
    tracks, grows: each teammate's agent id and its transcript's size (0 while
    there is none), in the order of the ids. It is "" with no teammate tracked,
    for another kind and when the transcript cannot be read. A watchdog that
    sees no progress of the agent itself reads it to tell a lead waiting on its
    teammates from a stuck one.

func (m *Manager) BackgroundTasks(ctx context.Context, run store.Run) (int, bool)
    BackgroundTasks counts the background work the claude agent of run's session
    started during run and left running, and the teammates it spawned during
    run that are at work, as the transcripts show now (ok false: not a claude
    session, or no transcript to read).

func (m *Manager) CheckHealth(ctx context.Context, s store.Session) (Health, error)
    CheckHealth classifies the session's recent pane output with the health
    patterns of its kind ([kinds.<kind>] health_patterns; a shell role's Tool,
    the defaults when it has none) and the manager's clock.

func (m *Manager) ClearDeadLaunch(ctx context.Context, s store.Session) (bool, error)
    ClearDeadLaunch is clearDeadLaunch for the quit that renews session s
    (the engine's quitAgentGone, once herdr kept listing the agent it quit):
    the name s's agent ran under, and s's pane as the one to keep, so the role's
    start that follows, still holding that pane's id, starts in its replacement.
    cleared reports that herdr no longer lists the name and the role keeps a
    pane: false when herdr lists no launch that never came up under the name,
    its pane runs something, or the pane closed without a replacement.

func (m *Manager) ClearShellPanes(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, checkout string) error
    ClearShellPanes makes sure, before something switches the checkout of the
    slot at checkout (a round's, the fixer's, magnum open's, a release), that
    no command runs in a shell pane of the PR's there. First what is left of a
    job magnum captured for one of the PR's runs is stopped (stopRemembered).
    Then the PR's shell sessions, live or retired, whose cwd is checkout; herdr
    is asked only once there is one. Their panes go through the herdr id checks:
    a pane another PR's live session records is left alone, and a pane herdr
    shows as another's (another agent there, or a cwd outside the checkout) is
    left too, its live row lost for the next round to lay a pane out, unless its
    foreground runs magnum's line for this checkout (ownToken), which holds.
    A pane herdr cannot place (no cwd in its snapshot) stays in the barrier:
    a command there holds. A live session's pane busy with an own run of its
    role no longer in flight (ownShell) is stopped (stopShell, on a context
    an abort or a shutdown cannot cut between SIGTERM and SIGKILL; each step
    stays bounded). A pane still busy holds the switch: a *ShellHoldError
    (ErrShellHold), Foreign for a command magnum did not start, Tokenless for
    a custom role's line without the run token in its live pane, else magnum's
    own with why it cannot stop it. A herdr that cannot say is ErrHerdrUnread,
    no hold. It never marks a human at work, and records no event: the engine
    keeps the hold and says so.

func (m *Manager) CloseRetiredPanes(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR) error
    CloseRetiredPanes closes the panes of the PR's parked, closed and lost
    sessions that herdr still has (a park, a hard park or an agent that went
    away leaves its session's pane as an idle shell, and the next workspace
    splits a new pane for every role, so a PR's workspace grew by a pane per
    role and start: 21 for 4 live sessions on talkable#11932). A pane is closed
    only when its foreground process is the shell and no agent herdr lists there
    works or is blocked, and never when a starting or live session of the PR
    or of another PR records it or its workspace; a pane no session records (a
    shell the operator opened) is never one. A retired session whose pane or
    workspace a starting or live session of another PR records (herdr numbers
    them again after a restart), or whose pane (its workspace, when the pane is
    gone) herdr shows as no longer its own (an agent there that does not carry
    the row's agent name, or a pane without it that works outside the session's
    checkout: an eval replay's or the operator's, which no row records), has
    its herdr ids dropped, with one EventHerdrIDsReused per reason, and nothing
    of it closes. A workspace the closes leave without a pane is closed too. A
    parked or lost session keeps its conversation: the role's next start resumes
    it in a new pane. One EventPanesClosed names the count and the roles, and,
    of a lost session's pane that showed one, the CLI's last error line by role
    (last_lines; when two closed panes of a role show one, the newer session's);
    a pane herdr refuses to close is logged, and the first such failure returned
    after the others were tried.

func (m *Manager) CloseRetiredPanesIn(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, snap herdr.Snapshot) error
    CloseRetiredPanesIn is CloseRetiredPanes over snap, a herdr snapshot the
    caller took for several PRs (the engine's reconcile takes one for every
    PR with a workspace). The PR's sessions are read now, and each pane's
    foreground process is asked of herdr before it is closed, so a pane snap is
    stale about is gone or left alone.

func (m *Manager) CodexHome(role config.Role) string
    CodexHome is the Codex home a session of role reads (codexHomeFor of its
    pane env: its CODEX_HOME, else the daemon's $CODEX_HOME, else ~/.codex;
    "" in a test binary without Deps.CodexConfig).

func (m *Manager) Compact(ctx context.Context, s store.Session) error
    Compact compacts the conversation of session s: it types CompactCommand
    into the idle agent's pane, as SwitchModel types /model, and waits
    for the compaction turn to end: the agent seen working, then idle on
    CompletionIdleTicks polls in a row (compactQuietPolls when it was never seen
    working). The turn is magnum's: the session's last_prompt_at and idle_ticks
    are set as a prompt sets them, and the observer never takes the agent's work
    for a human's while Compact waits (isCompacting). An agent that is not idle
    is refused with ErrBusy before anything is typed; a turn that has not ended
    within CompactTimeout is ErrTimeout (the agent may still be at it).

func (m *Manager) ContextUsed(ctx context.Context, s store.Session) (percent int, ok bool)
    ContextUsed reads how full session s's context is, in percent, from the
    last status lines of its pane's visible screen (contextStatusLines), with
    its kind's context_pattern (config.Kind.ContextRegexp): the newest match,
    the bottom line's last first, gives the figure, its "used" group as written,
    its "left" group as 100 minus it; a figure above 100 is no figure. ok is
    false when the kind has no pattern, the pane cannot be read, or no line
    shows a figure.

func (m *Manager) Ended() <-chan struct{}
    Ended returns a channel that is closed when an observe pass next ends a run
    (ObsCompleted) or marks a session lost (ObsLost); a call after that returns
    a new one. A waiter takes it before it reads its run's row and selects on it
    beside its poll, so an end that comes between the read and the wait is not
    lost.

func (m *Manager) EnsurePane(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, ws Workspace, slotPath string, env map[string]string, role config.Role) (Workspace, error)
    EnsurePane adds a pane for role to ws unless a live session of the role
    already has a pane in that workspace (e.g. claude-simplify, which runs on
    demand and is not in EnsureWorkspace's roles). A new pane is laid out as
    the next pane of ws.Roles (see EnsureWorkspace), gets env with the role's
    env laid over it, a starting sessions row and the "PR #N <role>" name
    (Deps.OwnerName's owner in place of "PR #N"); start an agent role with
    StartAgent. The returned Workspace is a copy of ws with the pane (ws itself
    is not modified).

func (m *Manager) EnsureTrust(ctx context.Context, kind, dir string) error
    EnsureTrust records dir as trusted in the agent CLI's own config, so a
    fresh agent started there does not stop at its first-launch trust dialog
    (which blocks every prompt with agent_blocked). StartAgent calls it before
    agent.start; slots/engine may call it when they prepare a checkout.

      - codex: [projects."<path>"] trust_level = "trusted" in the Codex
        config (Deps.CodexConfig, else $CODEX_HOME/config.toml, else
        ~/.codex/config.toml) for dir and for its repository root (the main
        clone: the parent of `git -C dir rev-parse --path-format=absolute
        --git-common-dir` when that ends in /.git), which is where Codex
        applies the trust. A missing table is appended as two lines; a table
        without trust_level gets the line after its header; an explicit other
        trust_level is left alone. The file is otherwise untouched.
      - claude: projects["<dir>"].hasTrustDialogAccepted = true in the Claude
        config (Deps.ClaudeConfig, else $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.claude.json,
        else ~/.claude.json), merged into an existing project object or created
        as {"allowedTools":[],"hasTrustDialogAccepted":true}. Every other key
        and the key order are kept; the file stays indented (two spaces) when it
        was, compact otherwise. A missing file is left missing (Claude has not
        been set up there).

    The symlink-resolved form of each path is trusted too when it differs.
    Writes are atomic (temp file + rename, keeping the file mode, through a
    symlinked config to its target) and happen only when an entry is missing,
    with one log line naming what was added. In a test binary the default paths
    are never used: without Deps.CodexConfig / Deps.ClaudeConfig EnsureTrust
    does nothing.

    Trusting magnum's own checkouts (and, for codex, the repository root, i.e.
    the user's main clone) is deliberate, and the entries are never removed:
    the agents work there like the user's own sessions do, project settings
    included, and a round runs the PR's code anyway (setup hooks, the judge's
    specs); watches skip cross-repository PRs by default.

    Every other kind (shell, droid, omp, any user-declared kind) is a no-op that
    returns nil: how droid and omp record trusted folders, and whether they ask
    at all, is unknown, so magnum neither edits their config nor answers their
    dialogs (see AnswerTrustDialog); a blocked start or prompt is left for the
    human.

func (m *Manager) EnsureWorkspace(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, slotPath string, env map[string]string, label string, roles []config.Role) (Workspace, error)
    EnsureWorkspace returns the PR's workspace with a pane per role in roles
    (the watch's roles that need a pane now, e.g. Config.RolesFor minus the
    on-demand ones), creating what is missing:

      - The workspace of the PR's newest starting/live/lost session is reused
        while herdr still has it and its checkout equals slotPath. Live panes
        are kept wherever they are; a missing role pane is re-split (a lost
        session's surviving pane is reused). A workspace or a pane a starting or
        live session of another PR records is never reused (herdr numbers them
        again after a restart; the PR's retired rows that record one drop their
        herdr ids, EventHerdrIDsReused), nor is one herdr shows as no longer the
        PR's: a pane must show the agent under its row's agent name, or no agent
        and the session's checkout, and a workspace must hold no other pane than
        such panes, agents under the PR's agent names and panes in the checkout
        (an eval replay's or the operator's workspace, which no row records,
        may hold the id now). A live row whose pane fails is marked lost;
        a lost row whose pane, or workspace when the pane is gone, fails drops
        its herdr ids.
      - If that workspace belongs to another checkout, the PR is parked first
        (ErrBusy while an agent works) and MovedFrom is set.
      - Otherwise a new workspace is created (cwd slotPath, label, no focus):
        its root pane serves the judge (the first role when none is a judge)
        and every other role gets a split, in the given order, laid out in two
        columns: each pane joins the column with fewer panes, the right one on a
        tie (the judge heads the left column). The first other role splits right
        of the judge, the second down from the first (the classic codex-judge |
        claude-review over codex-review), the third below the judge, the fourth
        down the right column again, and so on.

    Every pane gets env with the role's env (Config.RoleEnv) laid over it;
    a role with an identity gets that identity's env instead of env's gh
    selection, and a fix role whose identity does not resolve fails the call
    before herdr is touched (see paneEnv). With the hook env, an agent role's
    pane also names its agent as the key of its hook events (withAgentKey).
    Every newly assigned pane gets a sessions row (state starting, agent
    name/kind or agent_kind "shell", pane/workspace/tab ids, cwd, env_json)
    and is renamed "PR #N <role>" (TaggedPaneLabel; Deps.OwnerName's owner,
    such as a factory's "PR-12345", in place of "PR #N"); a new workspace whose
    root pane cannot be recorded is closed again (nothing else would find it).
    Live rows whose pane is gone are marked lost first, keeping their session_id
    for ResumeID. Pane envs are stored in sessions.env_json, so they must not
    carry secrets (identity.Source.Env never does).

func (m *Manager) FallbackModel(ctx context.Context, s store.Session, tried []string) (string, bool)
    FallbackModel is the model session s switches to next: the first of its
    fallback models (the role's, else the kind's: fallbacksFor) that is not
    limited, not the session's current model and not among tried. ok is false
    when the kind cannot switch (switch_model unset), every fallback is used up,
    or the limits cannot be read (logged: the session keeps its model).

func (m *Manager) FallbackPrompt(d FallbackData) (string, error)
    FallbackPrompt renders FallbackPromptName from pipeline.prompts_dir or the
    embedded defaults.

func (m *Manager) FixPrompt(pr store.PR, role Role, run store.Run, in FixPromptInput) (string, error)
    FixPrompt renders the fix role's prompt (its initial prompt, fix.md by
    default) for run, a run of that role on pr (NewRun, kind store.RunFix):
    RoleData with the PR's URL and number, the run's target as HeadSHA,
    its report path and id, in's fields and the fix skill's startup copy as
    SkillPath (config.RoleSkillPath, Config.SkillFile). It never carries PR
    text. A role that is not a fix role, or a run without a report path,
    is an error.

func (m *Manager) InterruptShell(ctx context.Context, run store.Run) error
    InterruptShell sends ctrl+c to the command a shell role's run left in its
    pane, only once RunShell typed the run's line (ShellLaunched) and only
    to the pane of the role's live session. A pane whose foreground carries
    this run's own token (ownShell) has its job captured first (captureJob,
    remembered), so a later idle shell is no proof while a captured process runs
    on. A line of a role without the run token (a `command` of the operator's
    that leaves the db-lock line out: the line RunShell typed carried none) gets
    the plain ctrl+c it always got, once tokenlessPane finds the pane still
    the role's. A line never typed, an idle shell and a gone pane need nothing
    (nil); a pane whose foreground carries another run's token, one without a
    token where the typed line carried it, and a pane that is not the role's get
    nothing: ErrNotOwn, or the error that kept herdr from saying.

func (m *Manager) LatestRound(ctx context.Context, prID int64) (int, error)
    LatestRound is the highest run round of a PR (0 when it has no runs).

func (m *Manager) LoginStamp(kind string) string
    LoginStamp fingerprints an agent kind's login file (config.Kind.LoginFile:
    its mtime and size, "absent" for a missing file). The engine records it
    when a run proved the kind logged out and lifts that pause only once the
    stamp changes, because a login check that reads the saved tokens (`codex
    login status`) still says logged in while a revoked refresh token fails
    every call. "" for a kind without a login file, or one whose home magnum
    cannot tell: a relative path is under the kind's home, which only codex has
    (codexHomeFor of the kind's env). The stamp is per kind, as the pause is:
    a CODEX_HOME that only a role's own env sets (config.Role.Env) is not seen,
    while the launches of that role read it (codexOff).

func (m *Manager) NewRun(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, role Role, kind string, round int) (store.Run, error)
    NewRun inserts a pending run for pr's role (a configured role name or
    alias; the run gets the name): id = NewRunID, target_sha = pr.HeadSHA,
    prev_reviewed_sha = pr.ReviewedSHA, identity = pr.Identity, reviewer_login
    from the identity config, report_path = Layout.ReviewDir(...)/<the
    role's ReportFile> (OwnFindingsFile for the judge's own pass, kind
    store.RunOwnPass), session_id = the role's live session when there is one.
    Create the run first when the prompt must quote its id (judge templates),
    then Submit.

func (m *Manager) NoteModelLimit(ctx context.Context, s store.Session, h Health) (ModelLimit, error)
    NoteModelLimit records that the model of session s hit its own limit (h,
    a HealthModelLimit verdict on its pane): h.Model, else the session's current
    model, is limited until h.ResetAt, else for daemon.model_limit_cooldown
    (doubled for a limit hit again within a day, see RecordModelLimit), never
    shortening a later recorded end. A session on its CLI's default model also
    teaches magnum which model that default is (KVKindCLIModel). It appends a
    kind.model_limited event. A recorded limit that cannot be read is the error,
    before anything is written: the index rewritten from a partial view would
    drop limits still active.

func (m *Manager) Observe(ctx context.Context) ([]Observation, error)
    Observe takes one herdr snapshot and runs ObserveSnapshotAt with the time
    it was taken. The daemon calls ObserveSnapshotAt itself, once per tick, with
    the snapshot that tick also counts working agents from, and ObserveRunsAt on
    its observe clock between the ticks while a run is in flight (polling is the
    completion signal).

func (m *Manager) ObserveRunsAt(ctx context.Context, snap herdr.Snapshot, capturedAt time.Time) ([]Observation, error)
    ObserveRunsAt is ObserveSnapshotAt for the sessions with a run submitted
    or at work alone: the review daemon's observe clock, there to see their
    turns end every few seconds, reads and writes no other session's row (a
    pass over them all would write each one's idle count as often); the tick's
    pass observes every session. It counts as an observe tick all the same
    (nextObserveTick).

func (m *Manager) ObserveSnapshot(ctx context.Context, snap herdr.Snapshot) ([]Observation, error)
    ObserveSnapshot is ObserveSnapshotAt with the capture time now (a snapshot
    of unknown age).

func (m *Manager) ObserveSnapshotAt(ctx context.Context, snap herdr.Snapshot, capturedAt time.Time) ([]Observation, error)
    ObserveSnapshotAt updates every starting/live session from snap, taken at
    capturedAt (read the clock before herdr's snapshot call), and returns one
    Observation per session:

      - agent found (by name, else by pane): status/status_at stored; idle|done
        increments idle_ticks, working|blocked resets it; a newly reported
        agent_session.value becomes session_id; a starting session becomes
        live. working + a submitted run -> run working (working_seen_at).
        idle_ticks >= CompletionIdleTicks, this reading CompletionGap or more
        after the streak's first (see idleStreak; denyContinueGap while a deny
        awaits its continuation, endGap), + a submitted/working run -> run
        ended, ObsCompleted, and Ended's channel closed; short of the gap,
        SecondReadingAt says when the reading that may end it is due.
        working with no pending/submitted/working run (outside a short grace
        after start/prompt) -> ObsHumanActive (CooldownUntil set when it begins
        the PR's cooldown), unless the agent is a claude agent whose transcript
        shows no prompt typed into the pane after magnum's last prompt to
        it (magnum's turn going on after esc cut it short, a turn a task
        notification began; see humanTurn), a judge still finishing the turn of
        a run the round settled on its result file (see turnTail), or a session
        compacting on magnum's /compact (see Compact). blocked -> ObsBlocked, or
        ObsPromptDenied when a pending/submitted/working run is in flight, the
        role's, else the kind's, on_permission_prompt is "deny" and the screen
        shows a permission prompt, which is answered No (see answerPermission;
        never without a run in flight, where the human may be driving the agent,
        so an agent that resumes working after a deny is never human_active).
        idle after such a deny, with that run still in flight and the agent
        not seen working since -> the kind's after_deny_prompt is sent (see
        continueAfterDeny), ObsDenyContinued, and the run does not end. A claude
        agent working after a deny has not resumed: Claude Code ends its turn
        on a No, and only its background work (a forked /code-review) or the
        turn that work's notification begins keeps it working, so its deny stays
        pending, and the message is sent as soon as its transcript shows the
        turn cut by the rejection and the composer is free (see denyPending);
        any other kind, and a claude agent without a transcript to read,
        carried on by itself. A claude agent idle with a submitted/working run
        whose transcript shows background work started during the run still
        running, or a task notification not answered yet, counts as working for
        completion (idle_ticks 0, Background set; see backgroundWait), until the
        pipeline tells it (Tell) to stop waiting for that work. A codex agent
        idle with a submitted/working run whose rollout has no task_complete
        (or turn_aborted) since the run and grew within RolloutGrowth counts as
        working too (see codexTurnGoing). An agent of a kind named by a rename
        command (codex), working on a submitted/working run, whose terminal
        title lacks Title gets that command (`/rename <Title>`) typed into
        its pane (at most once per call, TitleAttempts per session row; see
        nameAgent). A codex agent that herdr still reports without a session id,
        and whose row has none, RecoverIDAfter after its start, gets the id of
        its Codex rollout, when exactly one matches (see recoverSessionID);
        herdr's id, when it comes, wins. An agent that ends a turn magnum
        prompted (working, then idle) while neither herdr nor its rollout gave a
        session id records EventSessionIDMissing, once per kind and Manager (see
        sessionIDMissing).
      - live agent session without its agent, or any session whose pane is gone
        -> session lost, ObsLost, and Ended's channel closed. A starting session
        (agent not started yet) with its pane still present is left alone,
        and so is a session that started or became live too close to capturedAt
        (LostGrace).

func (m *Manager) PaneEnv(env map[string]string, role config.Role) (map[string]string, error)
    PaneEnv is the env role's pane gets from env (paneEnv): the fix job compares
    it with the env its live fixer pane was made with, to renew a pane made for
    another identity.

func (m *Manager) Park(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR) error
    Park releases a PR's panes while keeping its conversations resumable. It
    refuses with ErrBusy while a run of the PR is pending/submitted/working, an
    agent is working or blocked, a shell role's pane runs a command, or any pane
    of a workspace it would close runs something other than an idle shell or
    an idle agent (a lost session's pane where the user started a build, say).
    Session ids visible in herdr are recorded first. A workspace of the PR's
    live or lost sessions that holds only the PR's own panes is closed; one with
    foreign panes (the user split it) stays, and only the PR's live agents are
    quit. A pane or a workspace another PR's starting or live session records is
    never the PR's (herdr numbers them again after a restart): the PR's retired
    sessions that record one drop their herdr ids first (EventHerdrIDsReused),
    and no such workspace is closed. Nor is one with a pane herdr shows
    as no longer its session's (another agent than the row's agent name,
    or a pane without it outside the session's checkout: an eval replay's or the
    operator's, which no row records); the PR's retired sessions whose pane,
    or workspace when the pane is gone, herdr shows so drop their herdr ids too.
    Live sessions with a session_id become parked, the rest closed (see Quit);
    lost sessions stay lost. A quit that fails does not stop the others:
    the PR's other live agents are still quit and the failures come back joined
    (the stuck agent's session stays live, so ErrBusy and herdr's timeout are in
    the chain as for one failure). No live or lost sessions: no-op.

func (m *Manager) ParkClosingPanes(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR) error
    ParkClosingPanes is Park, then, once the park worked, CloseRetiredPanes:
    the park of a release (cleanup's Park: `magnum release`, a closed PR's
    cleanup, a slot's removal), which the engine's own parks do in two steps.
    A close that fails is logged; the park held.

func (m *Manager) ParkHard(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR) error
    ParkHard is Park for an agent that will not quit: the live agents it quits
    go on where Quit waits (forceQuit), so one still its pane's foreground
    process after ctrl+c and its kind's exit keys has that pane closed and its
    session closed. Every refusal of Park (a run in flight, an agent working or
    blocked, a busy pane of a workspace it closes) stands.

func (m *Manager) ParkSessions(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, ids []int64) (parked []store.Session, err error)
    ParkSessions parks the live sessions of pr that ids names, and only them:
    the idle park's early park of the agents past their threshold while another
    agent of the PR stays live (the engine's parkEarly, which runs it under the
    PR's reservation). It keeps Park's guards over a fresh snapshot (ErrBusy
    while a run of the PR is pending, submitted or working, or a selected
    agent works or is blocked; the session ids herdr shows recorded first) and
    refuses, before it quits any, a selected session with no conversation to
    resume (resumable): only a conversation the next round resumes is worth an
    early park. A selected session whose agent herdr no longer lists is parked
    without a key when its pane is an idle shell (ErrBusy, before any key,
    when the pane runs something). Each selected agent herdr lists is quit by
    earlyQuit (one ctrl+c and its kind's exit keys, a kind without them two
    ctrl+c, then the wait for an idle shell; never the hard mode: one that does
    not quit stays live with ErrBusy and waits for the PR's park). Once its
    pane is an idle shell, that pane is closed and then the session is parked
    (parkOne); a pane the close refuses or herdr fails to close is left for a
    later CloseRetiredPanes, the session parked all the same. The workspace
    stays while other panes live. Ids of sessions no longer live are skipped.
    Each session's park records its begin, ok and fail (EventSessionParkBegin
    ...), and a failure does not stop the other sessions: parked are the
    sessions it parked, and the failures come back joined beside them.

func (m *Manager) Preflight(ctx context.Context, kind string) error
    Preflight checks that the agent CLI of kind is logged in before a start or
    prompt, with the kind's read-only login_check command (split on spaces,
    run without a shell, with the kind's env laid over the daemon's) judged
    by its login_ok rule (config.Kind.LoggedIn): codex `codex login status`
    must print "Logged in" (on either stream; its exit code is unreliable),
    claude `claude auth status` JSON must have "loggedIn": true. A kind without
    login_check (droid, omp) and the shell kind are not checked. A logged-out
    CLI wraps ErrLoginRequired; a CLI that could not run (missing binary,
    timeout) returns that error instead; output the rule cannot read (a format
    change) is logged and taken as logged in, so it never blocks the reviews.
    An undeclared kind is an error. PreflightRole checks with a role's own
    environment.

func (m *Manager) PreflightRole(ctx context.Context, role config.Role) error
    PreflightRole is Preflight for the agent kind of role
    (config.Role.AgentKind: a shell role's tool) with the environment the role's
    pane gets (config.Config.RoleEnv: the kind's env, then the role's), so a
    role that points its CLI at another account (CODEX_HOME, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR)
    is checked in that account.

func (m *Manager) Prompt(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, role Role, kind, text string) (string, error)
    Prompt creates a run of kind (store.RunInitial, RunRereview, RunContinue,
    RunNudge, RunRecovery) in the PR's latest round (1 when none) and submits
    text to the role's live agent (see Submit). It returns the run id, also
    when Submit fails after the run was created; a run refused before sending
    (ErrNoSession, ErrHumanActive, ErrBusy) is marked abandoned. Start a new
    round, or quote the run id in the text, with NewRun + Submit.

func (m *Manager) Quit(ctx context.Context, s store.Session) error
    Quit stops a session's agent the way a human would: ctrl+c, 1 s, ctrl+c,
    then waits up to QuitIdleTimeout for the pane to be an idle shell again
    (ErrBusy otherwise, session unchanged, herdr's timeout in the chain). An
    agent of a kind with exit keys that herdr lists for a session with a pane is
    quit as the early park quits it (earlyQuit: one ctrl+c, then its exit keys,
    each after the look at a bare composer, ErrBusy with no key sent otherwise):
    two ctrl+c did not quit Claude 2.1.303 nor 2.1.311 at its idle prompt,
    and the quit before a checkout that changed AGENTS.md failed every attempt.
    The session id is captured first (RecordSessionID); the session becomes
    parked when it is resumable (an agent session with a session id whose kind
    reports ids), else closed. A pane or agent that is already gone counts as
    quit. For a shell role's pane this interrupts the running command.

func (m *Manager) QuitHard(ctx context.Context, s store.Session) error
    QuitHard quits session s alone the way ParkHard quits each of a PR's agents:
    ctrl+c, 1 s, ctrl+c and a wait for an idle shell, then, when the pane
    is still no idle shell, the kind's exit keys and, last, the pane closed
    (forceQuit) and the session closed. Unlike ParkHard it leaves the PR's other
    sessions as they are, and neither a run in flight nor an agent at work stops
    it: a turn that hangs is what it is for (the caller abandons the hung run
    first). The session becomes parked when it is resumable and quit before the
    close, else closed.

func (m *Manager) ReadRecent(ctx context.Context, s store.Session, lines int) (string, error)
    ReadRecent returns the last lines of a session's pane output (unwrapped
    text): agent.read by agent name, falling back to pane.read (shell panes,
    agents that exited).

func (m *Manager) RecordSessionID(ctx context.Context, s store.Session) (string, error)
    RecordSessionID reads the session's pane and stores agent_session.value as
    session_id when herdr reports one (after the first prompt) and it differs.
    It returns the id now known ("" before the first prompt).

func (m *Manager) Recover(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR) ([]Recovered, error)
    Recover reconciles a PR's sessions with herdr after a daemon or herdr
    restart, before anything is started (herdr may restore Codex itself): live
    rows whose agent is gone are rebound to the pane whose agent_session.value
    equals their session_id, else marked lost; for agent roles without a live
    row (every role with an agent session row of the PR, in order of first
    appearance), the newest resumable parked/lost session of the role's current
    kind (see ResumeID) whose id herdr shows in a pane becomes live there.
    Rebound agents are renamed to the role's agent name. Starting rows whose
    pane still exists are left alone. Runs are not touched: submitted runs stay
    observed, never re-sent.

func (m *Manager) ReloadsProject(ctx context.Context, s store.Session) bool
    ReloadsProject reports whether session s runs an agent CLI that reloads
    its project config from the checkout while it runs (Claude Code watches
    its settings files and skills, and loads a .claude/settings.json created
    later) and started with that config loaded: magnum launched it without
    the kind's project_untrust, or did not launch it (an adopted agent;
    no mark of noteSessionProject). Such a session would take what a commit
    checked out under it brings there, so the engine quits it (parking its
    conversation) before it moves the checkout, and its next start decides with
    the new head (checkoutProject). False for a kind without project_untrust:
    a changed config would load anyway.

func (m *Manager) ResumeID(ctx context.Context, prID int64, role Role) (string, error)
    ResumeID is the session id to resume for a PR role: the newest parked or
    lost session of that role that recorded one and ran the role's current
    agent kind ("" when none, and always "" for a shell role or a kind with
    session_source "none"; a conversation of the role's previous kind is never
    resumed by another CLI).

func (m *Manager) RolePrompt(role config.Role, promptKind string, data any) (string, error)
    RolePrompt resolves the role's prompt of a prompt kind
    (config.PromptInitial, PromptRereview, PromptContinue, PromptRecovery,
    PromptNudge, PromptStop; see config.Role.PromptFile) in pipeline.prompts_dir
    or the embedded defaults and renders it with data (see RenderPrompt).
    A role without such a prompt, or a name that resolves nowhere, wraps
    ErrUnknownTemplate (config.ErrPromptNotFound). JudgeData and RoleData
    without a Role get role's name.

func (m *Manager) RunShell(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, role config.Role, paneID, line, marker string, timeout time.Duration) (int, error)
    RunShell types line (see ShellLine) into the pane of a shell role and blocks
    until the done marker (DoneMarker(runID)) appears on a line of its own,
    optionally followed by the command's exit status, or timeout (ErrTimeout).
    It returns that status (ShellStatusUnknown without one). The pane must be
    an idle shell (readyShell): one an earlier run of the role still holds is
    stopped at once (StopShell's steps), and one something else keeps busy past
    IdleShellTimeout is left for a new pane with the session's environment,
    where the line runs (ErrBusy without one). Like Submit it refuses with
    ErrHumanActive inside daemon.human_cooldown after a human typed into the
    PR's panes. The shell's line editor is cleared (ctrl+u) first, so text a
    human left there never joins the command. The match is a line-anchored
    regex on unwrapped output, so the echoed command line itself never matches.
    The role's session (agent_kind "shell") becomes live with last_prompt_at;
    the run row is the caller's. An agent role is refused with an error.

func (m *Manager) SetHookSocket(path string)
    SetHookSocket sets the hook socket (Deps.HookSocket) that every pane the
    Manager makes from now on names, with the binary, as MAGNUM_HOOK_SOCKET
    and MAGNUM_HOOK_BIN (hookEnv): a daemon whose listener comes up after its
    Manager was built calls it once the listener is up. "" leaves the panes
    made from then on without the hook env; a pane already made keeps its env.
    It takes the Manager's lock, under which the pane env reads the socket,
    so it may run beside a start.

func (m *Manager) ShellLaunched(runID string) bool
    ShellLaunched reports whether RunShell typed, or tried to type, the line
    of the shell role's run runID into its pane and the command may still run
    (in this daemon: an earlier daemon's rounds ended with it). Only a launched
    run's command is keyed (InterruptShell) or stopped (StopShell).

func (m *Manager) ShellLine(ctx context.Context, prID int64, role config.Role, d ShellData) (string, error)
    ShellLine is ShellLine with the role's full-line template (role.Prompt)
    resolved through the configuration (pipeline.prompts_dir, then the embedded
    defaults) unless d.Template is set, d.MCPOff, when nil, keeping out what a
    session of the role's tool kind must not load: the MCP servers and plugins
    of the Codex home (codexOff) and the PR's project config in d.Checkout
    (checkoutProject against d.BaseSHA, else d.BaseRef, or the default branch
    for a stacked PR: shellProjectBase; a rendered line records the decision for
    PR prID, recordProject), and d.ToolOutput, when nil, the kind's tool output
