```text
    ceiling (config.Kind.ToolOutputArgs), as a session of the kind gets it.
    d.Magnum, when empty, is the daemon's own executable (the layout's),
    which d.DBLockCommand runs for the checkout and the role.

func (m *Manager) StartAgent(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, role config.Role, paneID, resume string) error
    StartAgent launches (or adopts) the agent of an agent role in paneID and
    marks its session live. The role's kind (role.AgentKind(), a declared
    [kinds.<name>]) says how:

      - First, a launch that never came up which herdr lists under the role's
        name over an idle shell (launch_pending or status unknown) has its
        pane closed (clearDeadLaunch, EventLaunchCleared): herdr would refuse
        the name with agent_name_taken for as long as that pane lives.
        When that pane is paneID the agent starts in the replacement split
        from it (ErrBusy when none could be made: the session is lost and the
        next attempt's workspace lays a pane out); a paneID magnum replaced so
        earlier forwards to its replacement.
      - An agent already carrying the role's name is adopted as is,
        when it is of the role's kind and its pane works in the PR's checkout
        (the session's cwd, else paneID's); otherwise StartAgent fails,
        since the name is taken. A fresh start (resume "") never adopts one
        whose conversation magnum parked for the role (parkedConversation: herdr
        still lists an agent Quit just stopped): ErrBusy, as when the sessions
        cannot be read to tell. No start adopts the agent of a session magnum
        ended (adoptable, endedAgent): one it closed within endedAgentMemory,
        or, while a session of the name it closed or marked lost exists,
        one that never came up (status unknown, no conversation: a launch herdr
        never registered). Such an agent in paneID is launched anew there;
        one in another pane is ErrBusy.
      - With resume set (ignored for a kind with session_source "none"),
        a pane whose agent_session.value equals resume (herdr restored it) is
        adopted instead of starting a second copy, and the agent is renamed to
        the role's name so the conversation is never forked; a restored agent of
        another kind or checkout is not adopted (logged) and the conversation is
        resumed in paneID instead.
      - An adopted agent was not launched with magnum's args, so it counts as
        one with the checkout's project config loaded (ReloadsProject).
      - Otherwise it waits for an idle shell (ErrBusy after IdleShellTimeout),
        resolves the kind's wrapper mode (Wrapper), trusts the session's
        cwd in the CLI's config (EnsureTrust; a failure is only logged;
        a no-op for kinds other than codex and claude) and runs agent.start with
        Name=AgentName, Kind=the kind, Timeout AgentStartTimeout and the args
        Kind.Argv builds: resume args, name args with Title (claude --name;
        kinds without name args but with a rename command are named later,
        by ObserveSnapshot), the role's model, effort and subagent-cap args,
        the args that turn off the MCP servers of the Codex config (the
        kind's mcp_off, read at every launch: codexOff), the args that keep
        the checkout's project config (Codex's .codex/, Claude's .claude/
        and .mcp.json) out when the PR changes it, or Codex's servers under
        project_mcp "off" (checkoutProject against origin/<the PR's base>,
        recorded by recordProject and, for the session, noteSessionProject,
        which ReloadsProject reads), the kind's start args, its args only
        when it is not a wrapper, then role.Args. While the role's model
        is limited (NoteModelLimit), the model args name the kind's first
        fallback model that is not, and the session records it (KVSessionModel,
        an agent.model_switched event).
      - An agent that comes up blocked (agent.start agent_not_ready, timeout,
        or status blocked, also when adopted) gets the trust-dialog fallback:
        within TrustWindow of its start and before its first prompt,
        a Codex/Claude first-launch trust dialog on screen is answered and
        the agent awaited until idle (see AnswerTrustDialog); Codex's "Folder
        access" for a checkout the session treats as untrusted is opened
        restricted at any time; any other dialog is left for the human.

    herdr's agent.start takes no environment: the role's env (Config.RoleEnv)
    reaches the agent through its pane, which EnsureWorkspace or EnsurePane
    created with it.

    The session row (created by EnsureWorkspace, or here if missing) gets the
    pane, agent name, agent_kind = the kind, session_id/resumed_from = resume,
    started_at = the launch (an agent launched here) and state live. A fresh
    session's id appears only after the first prompt; Prompt, Observe and
    RecordSessionID record it then. Preflight is the caller's job.

func (m *Manager) StopShell(ctx context.Context, run store.Run) error
    StopShell stops the command a shell role's run (the cut run) left running
    in its session's pane, when ownShell proves it an own run of magnum's (that
    run, or a run of the role no longer in flight), and only once RunShell typed
    the run's line (a line never typed: nil). It captures the job (captureJob:
    the members of the job's process group and the tree under the run token's
    db-lock, each with its identity, from the process table), records
    EventShellStopBegin, and then for SIGTERM and SIGKILL in turn (escalate):
    reads the process table again, asks herdr again (recheck), signals the
    group, reads the table once more and signals each captured process it shows
    as itself (pid and start: execx.Find), and waits up to shellStopWait for an
    idle shell and every captured process gone. A pane SIGKILL leaves busy is
    replaced (replaceShell). A pane that is an idle shell, or gone, is a stop
    only once the job captured for the run (at its interrupt, or at an earlier
    stop) is gone too (stopRemembered). Success is nil and EventShellStopped,
    anything else fails (EventShellStopFailed) and the command counts as still
    running. Without Deps.Signal nothing is signalled. It never marks a human at
    work.

func (m *Manager) Submit(ctx context.Context, run store.Run, text string) error
    Submit sends text to the live agent of run's role and records the
    outcome. The run must be pending (a run once submitted is observed,
    never re-sent: store.ErrConflict). It refuses with ErrHumanActive
    inside daemon.human_cooldown after a human typed into the session,
    and with ErrNoSession unless the role's session is live, and it holds a
    prompt to a judge still finishing the turn of its last run until herdr
    shows the agent no longer working (awaitTail; ErrBusy after tailWait);
    each refusal leaves the run pending for the caller to retry or abandon.
    A role whose newest session is lost while a fresh herdr snapshot still shows
    its agent gets that session back live (rebindLost) instead of a refusal.
    Before sending, a session on a limited model switches to a fallback,
    and one magnum switched earlier switches back once its role's model is no
    longer limited (ensureModel). The first prompt of a Codex session (a new or
    resumed one, never prompted) waits until its screen shows the composer and
    no startup dialog for CodexPromptSettle, answering the hooks review and the
    folder access it finds (codexPromptReady); a later prompt to a Codex session
    answers them first. The prompt waits for the agent to reach working or
    blocked (PromptAckTimeout):

      - working: run working (submitted_at, working_seen_at).
      - blocked after submission: run submitted, ErrBlocked.
      - herdr agent_blocked (rejected before sending): run failed, ErrBlocked.
        Within TrustWindow of the session's start and before its first
        prompt, a first-launch trust dialog on screen is answered first
        (AnswerTrustDialog) and the prompt re-sent once.
      - agent_prompt_stalled: run submitted with error, ErrStalled. The first
        prompt of a Codex session is checked first (codexRetry): one a startup
        dialog ate is sent again once, after the dialog is answered, and one
        that is lost again fails the run, ErrNotTaken.
      - timeout, or ctx ending while the prompt was in flight: run submitted
        with error (the text may have arrived), ErrTimeout or ctx's error.
      - anything else (herdr unavailable, agent gone): run failed.

    Once the prompt was sent, the run and session rows are recorded even when
    ctx ends meanwhile, so a delivered prompt never stays pending.

    The session gets last_prompt_at, idle_ticks 0, the acked status and,
    once herdr reports it, session_id. prompt_text is stored redacted. An agent
    named by a rename command (codex) acked as working is named right away when
    its title lacks Title (nameAgent). A shell role refuses with ErrNotAgent
    (see RunShell).

func (m *Manager) SwitchModel(ctx context.Context, s store.Session, model, reason string) error
    SwitchModel switches the idle agent of session s to model with its kind's
    switch_model command (claude: `/model <model>`) typed into its pane.
    In a session with history Claude Code asks first ("Switch model?", "❯ 1.
    Yes, switch to Opus 5.5", "2. No, go back"): magnum caused that dialog,
    so it presses Enter, once and only with the cursor on the "Yes, switch to"
    option (never confused with a permission prompt, which the observer still
    always denies; the observer leaves the session alone while it switches).
    The switch counts once the dialog is gone, the agent is idle and the visible
    screen's status line names the model ("Opus 5.5 | <cwd> | …"; for the
    kind's reset_model, the CLI's default model as a limit message named it,
    unverified when that is unknown). Not confirmed within SwitchModelTimeout
    is ErrTimeout (a dialog still open is backed out of with Esc). A switch
    whose ctx ends after the command was typed reads the screen once more:
    it backs out of a dialog still open, or records the switch when the status
    line names the model already. A confirmed switch records the session's
    model (KVSessionModel; removed when model is the role's configured one,
    or the kind's reset_model for a role without one) and appends an
    agent.model_switched event with reason (SwitchLimitHit, SwitchLimited,
    SwitchExpired). A kind without switch_model returns ErrNoModelSwitch,
    an agent that is not idle ErrBusy.

    Claude Code also saves a /model choice as the default for new sessions:
    for a claude session SwitchModel snapshots the settings file's model before
    it types the command and restores exactly that afterwards (holdDefaultModel;
    EventDefaultModelRestored when it had changed). Claude switches run one at a
    time for that.

func (m *Manager) Tell(ctx context.Context, run store.Run, text string) error
    Tell sends text to the agent of run's session within that run, without a
    new run (as continueAfterDeny sends after_deny_prompt). The pipeline tells a
    reviewer three things this way, each asking it to stop its background tasks:
    the last call when its time ran out (and to write its report now), and,
    once it was interrupted, to stop the background work it left running at
    the end of a round or before a push restarts the round. From then on the
    agent's background work no longer holds the run open; a task notification
    it has not answered still does. The session's idle_ticks are reset and its
    last_prompt_at set (so the turn the text starts is not taken for someone
    typing). A run without a live agent session fails with ErrNoSession
    (ErrNotAgent for a shell role's pane).

func (m *Manager) TookNoPrompt(ctx context.Context, s store.Session) bool
    TookNoPrompt reports whether live Codex session s never took a prompt
    (DECISIONS "A Codex judge that never took a prompt starts fresh"):
    Codex writes a session's rollout at its first prompt, and the observer
    gives a session herdr reports without an id the id of its rollout from
    RecoverIDAfter after its start, so a session that still has no id longer
    than RecoverIDAfter after its last prompt went out, and whose Codex home
    holds no rollout of its checkout and start (cliRolloutIDs, read now), has
    none: no turn ever ran in it, so none runs now. A session of another kind,
    one with an id, never prompted or prompted within RecoverIDAfter, one whose
    checkout or Codex home is unknown, and a read that fails or finds a rollout
    (two Codex sessions started in one checkout keep their ids unknown) answer
    false.

func (m *Manager) TranscriptPath(ctx context.Context, s store.Session) (string, error)
    TranscriptPath is the file the turns of session s are read from:
    the transcript of a Claude session (under the session's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR,
    else Deps.ClaudeDir; see transcriptPath), the rollout of a Codex session
    (under its CODEX_HOME, else Deps.CodexHome; see rolloutPath). It is an error
    for a shell pane, a kind with no such record, a session whose id is not
    recorded yet and a file that is not there.

func (m *Manager) TurnError(ctx context.Context, run store.Run) (TurnError, bool)
    TurnError reads the error the turn of run ended with from its Codex
    session's rollout: the last task_complete event stamped at or after
    the run's creation (less transcriptSkew), when it carries an error.
    A cybersecurity refusal (cyber_policy) of a turn a helper agent of the
    session ended within the run (helperTurnError) comes before any error
    of the session's own but its own refusal, and a helper's other error
    stands in when the session's turn has none (Helper names the helper).
    The rollouts are looked for under the session's CODEX_HOME (its pane env),
    else Deps.CodexHome, else $CODEX_HOME, else ~/.codex (a test binary never
    falls back to those). ok is false for a session of another kind or without
    a Codex session id, a rollout it cannot find or read, and a turn that ended
    without an error, its helpers' turns too. A session without a rollout to
    read (no session id: herdr's session hook off) is logged once, not at each
    of its turns.

func (m *Manager) TypedDuringRun(ctx context.Context, run store.Run) bool
    TypedDuringRun reports whether someone typed into the pane of run's session
    while run was in flight, for the fix job's settle: the run's part of a
    claude agent's transcript (from the run's creation, as the observer reads
    it while the run is in flight) ends in a turn that began with, or took in,
    a prompt typed after magnum's last prompt to the session, as humanTurn
    reads it (a turn a task notification began after the typed one hides it).
    Any other kind, a run without a session or a Claude session id, and a
    transcript it cannot read report false: only Claude Code keeps a transcript
    magnum reads.

func (m *Manager) WaitWakes()
    WaitWakes waits for the later looks Wake started (lookAgain): they end with
    the context Wake was given. A receiver calls it after its listener stopped
    and the last Wake returned, before it closes the registry.

func (m *Manager) Wake(ctx context.Context, ev agenthooks.Event)
    Wake takes an event of an agent's hook (agenthooks.Listener's) as a hint to
    look at its pane now, outside the observe passes. The pane is mapped to its
    starting or live session by its pane key (agent_name), else by herdr_pane_id
    (HookSessionOf); an event of a pane no such session (of an agent) records
    is dropped. Every look takes the observe lock the passes take (obsMu),
    one herdr snapshot and the session's in-flight runs, and goes through
    observeOne, as a pass would; a pass whose snapshot started before a look's
    came back leaves the session alone, and the next pass returns the looks'
    observations (each session's newest, and every run's end and session's
    loss), so the daemon handles them as its own (the factory's turn end,
    the engine's lost pane, the clock's SecondReadingAt). A look never counts
    as an observe tick (nextObserveTick), so the deny's pace (answerPermission)
    and the namer's stay the passes'. The looks of one session merge: one
    within lookMerge of the last, or while another waits for the observe lock,
    is skipped.

      - stop, interrupt and permission_request: a look now. A Stop counts as
        the second idle reading when herdr shows the agent idle and all of
        these hold: its session id is the session's, it comes from no subagent
        (agent_id empty) or Codex helper (CODEX_THREAD_ID its session id),
        its agent is the session's kind, it reports no background task, nothing
        holds the turn (background work, a Codex rollout still writing, a deny
        awaiting its continuation), and the transcript's turn_duration (Claude)
        or the rollout's task_complete (Codex), found where magnum reads the
        session's (never the path the event names), is newer than the run's
        prompt (stopEndsTurn). Then the run ends and Ended's channel closes, as
        on a pass. A permission request has answerPermission deny the prompt the
        look sees; the hook itself decides nothing. When the look found nothing
        to act on while a run is in flight (or was merged into another), Wake
        looks again at +1 s and +2 s on a goroutine of its own (relookAfter;
        never the caller's), then leaves it to the clock. A late Stop of an
        earlier turn, a subagent's or a forged one only causes an early look.
      - stop_failure: a look now, then, when the event is the session's own (a
        Claude session, its session id, no subagent's) and the screen read again
        shows such a failure (CheckHealth, StopFailure.shownBy; read once more a
        second later when it does not yet), the failure's class and the screen's
        verdict to Deps.HookFailure, once per failure, which feeds the engine's
        usage, login and overload handling (hookFailure). The StopFailures of
        one session merge as its looks do. The agent's error text never goes on,
        nor into a log.
      - session_start: a row without a session id gets the event's, a UUID,
        once the agent's own file proves it (adoptHookID): the Claude transcript
        where magnum reads the slot's sessions, whose first record names the id
        in the slot, or the Codex rollout of the TUI in the slot. Until the file
        is there the event waits, and the pane's next event checks it again.
      - session_end: a look now.
      - user_prompt_submit: no look.

    Every event first moves the session's hooks' state (noteHookEvent),
    which the observe passes only compare with herdr's status (hook_state.go):
    nothing decides on it.

    The rules a receiver keeps: ctx bounds the later looks too, so pass the
    daemon's, not one that ends when Wake returns, and call WaitWakes once
    the listener stopped. Wake runs the Deps callbacks (HookFailure on the
    caller's goroutine; OwnerName, Toast, IdentityEnv and the rest under the
    observe lock), so never call it under a lock a callback takes: the factory's
    OwnerName (ownerName) takes Runtime.mu, so the factory calls Wake, and its
    passes, without Runtime.mu held.

func (m *Manager) WhiteboardPrompt(pr store.PR, role Role, run store.Run, in WhiteboardPromptInput) (string, error)
    WhiteboardPrompt renders the whiteboard role's prompt (its initial prompt,
    whiteboard.md by default) for run, a run of that role on pr (NewRun,
    kind store.RunWhiteboard): RoleData with the PR's URL, name and number,
    the run's target as HeadSHA, its report path and id, and in's fields. It
    never carries PR text: the writer reads the PR's title with gh. A role that
    is not a whiteboard role, a run without a report path or an input without a
    checkout is an error.

func (m *Manager) Wrapper(ctx context.Context, kind string) (bool, error)
    Wrapper reports whether the kind's command is a zsh wrapper function (or
    alias) that supplies its own flags, per [kinds.<kind>] wrapper: "true"
    and "false" are taken as is, "bypass" is false (bypassWrapper removes the
    function from the pane before the launch); "auto" (or empty) probes `zsh
    -ic 'whence -w <kind>'` once per kind and caches the answer. A probe that
    cannot tell assumes a wrapper (the M0 finding) and is retried next time.
    An undeclared kind is an error.

type ModelLimit struct {
	Kind  string
	Model string
	Until time.Time
	// Using is the first of the fallback models (fallbacksFor: the role's,
	// else the kind's) that is not limited itself ("" = none).
	Using string
}
    ModelLimit is one model of a kind that hit its own limit.

func ModelLimits(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, cfg *config.Config, kind string, now time.Time) []ModelLimit
    ModelLimits lists the per-model limits of kind recorded in st that end after
    now, by model name, each with the fallback a session uses meanwhile. A kind
    has no role, so Using names the kind's own list. cfg may be nil (Using then
    stays empty). It is for display: a limit whose row cannot be read is left
    out.

type NotesPart struct {
	From, To       int
	CutFrom, CutTo int
	Command        string
}
    NotesPart is one part of NotesParts: lines From to To (1-based, inclusive),
    or, with CutFrom set, bytes CutFrom to CutTo (1-based, inclusive,
    CutTo possibly past the line's end) of the single line From, longer than
    NotesPartMax. Command prints it: `sed -n 'From,Top' <path>`, or `sed -n
    'Fromp' <path> | cut -b CutFrom-CutTo`, the path shell-quoted.

type NotesParts struct {
	Path  string // the copy, absolute (the live file when it could not be written)
	Bytes int    // its size
	Lines int    // its lines, a last one without a newline counted
	Parts []NotesPart
}
    NotesParts is the frozen copy of the repository notes a round's roles read
    (RoleData and JudgeData.NotesParts), in parts. The zero value is no notes
    (none, or empty), and the prompts then name no parts.

func FreezeNotes(live, dir string) (NotesParts, error)
    FreezeNotes copies the notes file live into dir as NotesReadFile and returns
    the copy's parts (SplitNotes), so every role of a round reads the same text
    however the judges rewrite live meanwhile. No notes ("" live, a missing
    or empty file) is no copy and the zero NotesParts. A copy that cannot be
    written returns the live file's parts with the error: the roles still read
    the notes in parts, which a rewrite can shift.

func SplitNotes(path string, text []byte) NotesParts
    SplitNotes cuts text, the notes file at path, into NotesParts: runs of whole
    lines of at most NotesPartMax bytes (each line counted with its newline, a
    last line without one too), a line longer than that split inside into pieces
    of NotesPartMax bytes. Empty text has no parts. NotesRereadLine prints the
    same commands for a file.

type Observation struct {
	Kind    ObservationKind
	Role    Role
	PRID    int64
	Status  herdr.Status  // agent status this tick ("" for shell panes and missing agents)
	Session store.Session // row after this tick's update
	Run     *store.Run    // newest run in flight for the session (completed run for ObsCompleted)
	// Background is the work an idle claude agent started in the background
	// during Run and left running, as its transcript shows (see
	// backgroundWait); while there is any, the run does not end.
	Background int
	// CooldownUntil is, for an ObsHumanActive that began the PR's cooldown
	// (its human_active_at was unset, or daemon.human_cooldown had passed
	// since), when that cooldown ends; zero when the tick only extended a
	// cooldown already running, and when human_cooldown is 0 (none).
	CooldownUntil time.Time
	// SecondReadingAt is, for an idle reading short of the gap (the
	// streak's first idle reading plus CompletionGap, or denyContinueGap
	// while a deny awaits its continuation, is still ahead) of a session
	// with a run in flight, when the reading that may end the run is due;
	// zero otherwise, a reading neither idle nor busy (herdr's "unknown")
	// included. The review daemon's observe clock takes its next reading
	// then.
	SecondReadingAt time.Time
}
    Observation is the result of one tick for one starting/live session.

type ObservationKind string
    ObservationKind is what one tick noticed about a session.

const (
	// ObsCompleted: a submitted/working run's agent was idle|done on
	// CompletionIdleTicks consecutive ticks. The run is now ended; verify it
	// (reports on disk, the judge's review on GitHub).
	ObsCompleted ObservationKind = "completed"
	// ObsHumanActive: the agent works with no magnum run in flight; prs.human_active_at
	// was set to now, so Submit refuses for daemon.human_cooldown.
	ObsHumanActive ObservationKind = "human_active"
	// ObsBlocked: the agent waits on a dialog magnum leaves to the human (a
	// role or kind with on_permission_prompt "wait", a dialog that is not a
	// recognised permission prompt, a run past MaxPromptDenies): tell the
	// human.
	ObsBlocked ObservationKind = "blocked"
	// ObsPromptDenied: the agent was blocked on a permission prompt during
	// one of magnum's runs and magnum answered No (this tick, or the tick
	// before while the screen catches up; see answerPermission); the human
	// is not needed.
	ObsPromptDenied ObservationKind = "prompt_denied"
	// ObsDenyContinued: the agent went idle after such a deny, during the
	// same run, and was sent its kind's after_deny_prompt (see
	// continueAfterDeny); the run goes on.
	ObsDenyContinued ObservationKind = "deny_continued"
	// ObsLost: the pane or the agent is gone; the session is now lost (its
	// session_id kept for ResumeID). Run carries the run that was in flight.
	ObsLost ObservationKind = "lost"
)
    Observation kinds; "" means nothing to act on.

type OwnCodexHook struct{ Place, Definition string }
    OwnCodexHook is one of magnum's Codex hooks at its place in a hooks.json
    ("stop:0:0"): Definition is what Codex hashes of it as magnum reads it (the
    CLI's form of its group's matcher and its type, command, timeout, async and
    extra keys), so two hooks with one Definition hash the same.

type PreviousReview struct {
	ID          int64
	Event       string // APPROVE, COMMENT, CHANGES_REQUESTED, ...
	SHA         string // commit the review was on (short is fine)
	SubmittedAt string // RFC3339
}
    PreviousReview is an earlier review by the reviewer login (recovery mode).

type ProjectNote struct {
	Head     string    `json:"head"`     // the checkout's head at that launch ("" = unknown)
	At       time.Time `json:"at"`       // the launch
	Files    int       `json:"files"`    // the files of the project config that differ from the merge base
	Compared bool      `json:"compared"` // false: git could not compare, so the config was left out anyway
	// Paths name the kind's paths those files fall in, as a sentence does
	// (".codex/", "AGENTS.md", never a path the PR named); none = all of
	// them (git could not compare, or a record written before they were
	// named).
	Paths []string `json:"paths,omitempty"`
	// DocsOnly: they were all instruction files, kept out by the kind's
	// project_docs_off while the rest of the project config loaded.
	DocsOnly bool `json:"docs_only,omitempty"`
	// Residue: git compared them, and none is a file the PR's commits
	// since the merge base change: they are untracked or ignored files a
	// round left in the slot, or uncommitted edits, so they say nothing of
	// the PR (the card and the review's Checks say so). False when git
	// could not tell, and in a record written before it was kept. The
	// auto-approval's gate reads no record: the PR's file list decides
	// there, with the links of the head's tree.
	Residue bool `json:"residue,omitempty"`
}
    ProjectNote is the PR's record of a session of one kind launched without the
    checkout's project configuration (store.KVPRProject).

func ProjectDeclined(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, prID int64, kind string) (ProjectNote, bool)
    ProjectDeclined reads the PR's record of a session of kind launched without
    the checkout's project configuration; false when there is none (or it cannot
    be read).

type Readiness struct {
	Checks []ReadinessCheck
	Failed int    // checks whose Status is not ReadinessOK
	File   string // the JSON file with every check (readiness.json in the report directory); "" when it could not be written
}
    Readiness is the readiness step's outcome as a judge prompt shows it.
    The zero value means no step ran (nothing configured, a continued turn).

type ReadinessCheck struct {
	Kind    string `json:"kind"`    // ReadinessResetDB, ReadinessPrepare, ReadinessReady or ReadinessRuby
	Command string `json:"command"` // as configured (ruby: the version command)
	OK      bool   `json:"ok"`
	Status  string `json:"status"` // ReadinessOK, ReadinessFailed, ReadinessTimeout or ReadinessSkipped
	// Detail is magnum's own one-line account ("exit 1", "the checkout pins
	// Ruby 3.3.4 (.ruby-version); `zsh -lc` runs 3.2.2"): never command
	// output, so prompts may show it.
	Detail string `json:"detail,omitempty"`
	// LastLine is the last non-empty line the command printed (redacted,
	// shortened); for a failed rake task, the cause after "aborted!", not
	// its trailer. It comes from code in the PR's checkout, so it is data:
	// it goes into the readiness file, and a failed reset_db's into the
	// round.readiness event and the slot's count of failed resets, never
	// into a prompt.
	LastLine string `json:"last_line,omitempty"`
	Duration string `json:"duration"` // e.g. "4.2s"
}
    ReadinessCheck is one command of the readiness step.

type RecoverAction string
    RecoverAction says what Recover did with a session.

const (
	RecoverOK       RecoverAction = "ok"       // pane and agent are where the row says
	RecoverRebound  RecoverAction = "rebound"  // live row moved to the pane now holding its session id
	RecoverRestored RecoverAction = "restored" // parked/lost row is live again: herdr restored its conversation
	RecoverLost     RecoverAction = "lost"     // pane/agent gone and not found elsewhere
)
    Recover actions.

type Recovered struct {
	Role    Role
	Action  RecoverAction
	Session store.Session // row before the change
}
    Recovered is one Recover outcome.

type Report struct {
	Role    string // the role's name, e.g. claude-review
	Label   string // how the prompt names it ("" = Role)
	Path    string // the report file (absolute); "" when Missing
	Status  string // the role's outcome this round (ok, failed, timeout, ...); informational
	Missing bool   // no usable report this round
	// Late: a completion's report of a role the review it completes went
	// without (pipeline.Completion), rendered as `<label> (late)` in
	// `reports` and named in JudgeData.LateReports.
	Late   bool
	Detail string // why it is missing, e.g. "timed out after 40m"
	// Reason is Detail under its older name, for prompt files that still
	// render `missing ({{.Reason}})`.
	Reason string
}
    Report is one candidate report listed in a judge prompt, one per non-judge
    role of the round in pipeline order. RenderPrompt completes it: Label
    defaults to Role; a report without Path is Missing; a Missing report has
    no Path; Detail and Reason fill each other, then default to Status (or "no
    report") for a missing one.

type ReviewThread struct {
	ID string `json:"id"` // GraphQL node id
	// CommentID is the REST id of the thread's first comment: a reply goes
	// to POST repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/comments/{CommentID}/replies.
	CommentID int64  `json:"comment_id"`
	URL       string `json:"url"`
	Finding   string `json:"finding"`  // the first line of the thread's first comment
	Location  string `json:"location"` // path:line; the original line when outdated
	// ReviewID, CreatedAt and Commit say when and where the finding was
	// posted: the review the first comment belongs to, its creation time
	// (RFC3339, UTC) and the commit it was made on. Each is omitted when
	// GitHub reports none.
	ReviewID  int64         `json:"review_id,omitempty"`
	CreatedAt string        `json:"created_at,omitempty"`
	Commit    string        `json:"commit,omitempty"`
	Resolved  bool          `json:"resolved"`
	Outdated  bool          `json:"outdated"`
	Replies   []ThreadReply `json:"replies"` // oldest first
	// Rebuttals counts the reviewer's rebuttals in the thread: its replies
	// of kind rebuttal, and those without a kind (magnum's earlier rebuttals
	// carried no reply marker). Stop: after two of them someone answered
	// again; the judge replies there no more, and magnum asks the operator.
	Rebuttals int  `json:"rebuttals,omitempty"`
	Stop      bool `json:"stop,omitempty"`
}
    ReviewThread is an inline thread the reviewer login started on the PR
    (JudgeData.Threads), as magnum writes it to the threads file.

type Role string
    Role is a review role's configured name (config.Role.Name), the value
    stored in sessions.role and runs.role. Resolve what users type with
    config.Config.RoleByNameOrAlias; the role's definition (kind, prompts,
    output, ...) is the config.Role of that name.

const (
	RoleJudge       Role = config.RoleCodexJudge     // codex-judge: persistent Codex session that posts the review
	RoleClaude      Role = config.RoleClaudeReview   // claude-review: persistent Claude session running /code-review
	RoleCodexReview Role = config.RoleCodexReview    // codex-review: shell pane running `codex review` under db-lock
	RoleSimplify    Role = config.RoleClaudeSimplify // claude-simplify: on-demand Claude session running /simplify
)
    The built-in roles (config.DefaultRoles), for defaults and tests.

func (r Role) Label() string
    Label is the role's user-visible name: the role name itself (pane labels,
    titles, agent names and CLI output use it).

type RoleData struct {
	URL             string // the pull request
	Owner, Repo     string // repo is the name part, e.g. talkable
	Number          int
	HeadSHA         string // the commit under review (checked out, detached)
	PreviousHeadSHA string // the head of the role's previous run (rereview)
	BaseSHA         string // the merge base; `git diff <BaseSHA>..HEAD` is the PR's diff
	BaseRef         string // the base ref, e.g. origin/master or a stacked PR's parent branch
	ReportPath      string // where the role writes its report (its output, absolute)
	Model, Effort   string // the role's model and this round's effort (config.Role.EffortFor; claude-review passes it to /code-review)
	// EffortInPrompt: the agent's kind sets the effort only at launch and
	// this round's Effort differs from the role's (see JudgeData).
	EffortInPrompt bool
	Mode           string // ModeInitial, ModeRereview or ModeRestart
	Since          string // RFC3339: the role's previous run (rereview)
	// ForcePushed: PreviousHeadSHA is no longer in the branch (rereview).
	ForcePushed bool
	// BaseMerged: the commits since PreviousHeadSHA merged a branch in,
	// usually the base (rereview), so PreviousHeadSHA..HeadSHA carries its
	// commits: the prompt compares the PR's own diff before and after.
	BaseMerged bool
	// RestartedFrom is the head the role was reviewing when a push cut its
	// turn short (ModeRestart); HeadSHA is the new head.
	RestartedFrom string
	// NotesPath is the repository notes file the role reads first (hints from
	// earlier reviews of the repository); "" = no notes.
	NotesPath string
	// NotesParts is the round's frozen copy of the notes, in parts
	// (FreezeNotes; the fix job freezes its own): the claude reviewer
	// prompts and the fix prompt name the copy and give one command per
	// part, with the sentence that asks for one part per tool call; zero =
	// no notes to read, and they name none.
	NotesParts NotesParts
	// HistoryFile is history.json in the report directory, the changed
	// files' last commits on the base (see JudgeData.HistoryFile): the claude
	// reviewer prompts name it in one sentence; "" = none.
	HistoryFile string
	// DocsFile is docs.json in the report directory, the base's pages that
	// name the changed files (see JudgeData.DocsFile): the claude reviewer
	// prompts name it in one sentence; "" = none.
	DocsFile string
	// PrepassFile is prepass.json in the report directory, magnum's reading
	// of the PR's diff (see JudgeData.PrepassFile): the claude reviewer
	// prompts say to read it first, a changed method's body before its
	// hunk, each item a lead to check; "" = none.
	PrepassFile string
	// Stakes is what the PR's repository puts at risk, as the operator
	// states it (see JudgeData.Stakes): the claude reviewer prompts give it
	// in one sentence, to size each finding's harm against; "" = none.
	Stakes string
	// EvidenceMap is the PR's evidence map, what the earlier rounds
	// examined (see JudgeData.EvidenceMap): the claude reviewer prompts say
	// to read its unknown and stale areas first; "" = none.
	EvidenceMap string
	// Blind: an evaluation replay (pipeline.RoundInput.Blind); the role
	// must not read reviews, comments or commits after HeadSHA.
	Blind bool
	// DescriptionFile is a local round's description.md (pipeline.Local):
	// the change's title and body, which no PR on GitHub holds yet. Only the
	// local reviewer prompt (claude-review-local.md) names it; "" = a round
	// of a PR on GitHub.
	DescriptionFile string
	// PostMerge: GitHub merged the PR before magnum reviewed HeadSHA
	// (pipeline.RoundInput.PostMerge); the prompts that name the PR say it
	// is merged and to review it anyway.
	PostMerge bool
	// Budget is the role's turn timeout in words ("40 minutes"): the
	// prompts tell the agent to end its turn with the report written
	// within it.
	Budget string
	// RunID is the run the prompt starts: the shipped prompts ask for its
	// marker, ReportMarker(RunID), as the report's first line, and a role
	// whose prompt names it has a report only when the report carries it.
	RunID string
	// Magnum is the magnum executable (the daemon's own, absolute; "" =
	// magnum on PATH), Checkout the checkout the role works in and Role its
	// name (Manager.RolePrompt fills it when empty). DBLockCommand is the
	// line the role runs its database commands through (DBLockLine, derived
	// from the three when empty; the fix job passes its own): the prompts
	// of the roles that run tests name it.
	Magnum, Checkout, Role, DBLockCommand string
	// The fix prompt's (Manager.FixPrompt; empty for every other role):
	// HeadRef is the PR's branch, which the fixer pushes to; ReviewURL the
	// review it fixes and ReviewFile that review's review.json (its event,
	// body and comments, as the judge posted it); ExternalFile the other
	// reviewers' open threads, review bodies and comments, which the fixer
	// handles after the review's findings ("" = magnum could not list
	// them); ReviewerLogin the login that posted the review, whose threads
	// the fixer answers; SkillPath the fix skill's startup copy, absolute.
	HeadRef, ReviewURL, ReviewFile, ExternalFile, ReviewerLogin, SkillPath string
	// FixReplyCommand is the line the fixer posts every reply through,
	// `magnum fix-reply` (FixReplyLine, derived from Magnum when empty for
	// every role, as DBLockCommand is; the fix job passes its own): only the
	// fix prompt names it.
	FixReplyCommand string
	// FixSyncCommand is the fix prompt's too: the line the fixer runs once
	// when GitHub rejects its push because the branch moved, `magnum
	// fix-sync` with the slot's checkout, the run's start head, the PR's
	// branch and its base (FixSyncLine), which replays the fixer's commits
	// onto a merge of the base the branch gained. Never derived, since only
	// the fix job knows the PR's base: "" = the prompt names no fix-sync.
	FixSyncCommand string
	// PushCommand and FixerLogin are the fix prompt's too, set for a fixer
	// that acts as a GitHub App of its own: the line it pushes with
	// (PushLine, `magnum push`; "" = `git push origin HEAD:<HeadRef>`, a
	// gh fixer's) and the login its commits, push and replies carry ("" =
	// the PR author's, a gh fixer's).
	PushCommand, FixerLogin string
	// NoFindings is the fix prompt's too: the review found nothing and left
	// nothing open, so the fixer handles ExternalFile's unanswered items
	// alone, and merges the base when the PR conflicts with it (the fix job
	// starts on such a review only when one of the two waits).
	NoFindings bool
	// OwnPR is the fix prompt's too: the PR's author is the operator, as
	// the fix job checked before it started (a PR the factory opened
	// counts: it opens them as the operator), so the fixer may edit the
	// PR's description as the fix skill's section 5 says. false = the
	// prompt grants no such edit, and the skill changes no description.
	OwnPR bool
	// ConflictBase, ConflictSHA, ConflictPaths and ConflictFiles are the fix
	// prompt's too (FixPrompt fills them from FixPromptInput): the PR
	// conflicts with its base branch ConflictBase, whose tip magnum fetched
	// is ConflictSHA, in ConflictFiles files, ConflictPaths the first of
	// them in plain path characters (at most maxConflictPaths; a path with
	// any other character is counted, never named); the fixer merges that
	// tip first, as the fix skill's base merge says. "" and none when the PR
	// merges its base cleanly, or magnum could not check.
	ConflictBase, ConflictSHA string
	ConflictPaths             []string
	ConflictFiles             int
	// MergeOnly, MergedBase and MergedSHA are the fix prompt's too: the run
	// merges the PR's parent alone (the conflict above) with no review to
	// fix; magnum merged the tip MergedSHA of the base MergedBase into the
	// PR before the run, so the head the fixer starts from is that merge.
	// false and "" otherwise.
	MergeOnly             bool
	MergedBase, MergedSHA string
	// CIOnly and CIFile are the fix prompt's too: the run fixes the PR's
	// failed required CI (the engine's CI fix mode) from CIFile, the CI
	// reader's ci-failures.json beside the report (the failed jobs, their
	// failed steps and the end of their logs: the output of the PR's code
	// and its tests, data), with no finding or other reviewer's item to
	// answer; false and "" otherwise.
	CIOnly bool
	CIFile string
	// WhiteboardSession is the whiteboard prompt's (Manager.WhiteboardPrompt;
	// empty for every other role, ReviewURL and ReviewFile its review as
	// for the fix prompt): the Whiteboard session of an earlier head of the
	// PR, which the writer moves to HeadSHA; "" = it creates the PR's first.
	WhiteboardSession string
}
    RoleData feeds the prompts of every non-judge session role (claude-review,
    claude-simplify, a droid or omp reviewer, ...): the union of what those
    prompts may use. Fields a template does not use may stay zero.

type SessionFacts struct {
	// Entrypoint is how Claude Code was started, as its entries record it:
	// "cli" for its terminal UI, "sdk-cli" for `claude -p`, "sdk-ts" for
	// the TypeScript SDK; "" when no entry names one, and in a rollout.
	Entrypoint string
	// Originator is the client a Codex rollout's session_meta names
	// ("codex-tui", "codex_exec", "Claude Code"), and Source its source
	// ("cli", "exec", "vscode", or CodexSourceSubagent); both "" in a Claude
	// transcript.
	Originator, Source string
	// Cwd is the directory the session started in: the first entry's cwd,
	// the session_meta's.
	Cwd string
	// Branches are the git branches the session ran on, each once, in the
	// order the file first names them: the entries' gitBranch, the
	// session_meta's git.branch.
	Branches []string
}
    SessionFacts is what a transcript or a rollout says of its session.

func ClaudeSessionFacts(path string) (SessionFacts, error)
    ClaudeSessionFacts reads the facts of the Claude Code transcript at path:
    the first entrypoint and the first cwd its entries name, and every
    gitBranch. The whole file is read, a line at a time; a line that is no JSON
    is skipped.

func CodexSessionFacts(path string) (SessionFacts, error)
    CodexSessionFacts reads the facts of the Codex rollout at path from its
    first session_meta: none for a rollout without one (an older Codex wrote
    none).

type SessionIDGap struct {
	// Streak is how many of the newest sessions in a row have no id.
	Streak int
	// Sessions counts the sessions from the newest back to the oldest
	// without an id since two in a row last had one, Missing those of them
	// without one, and Since is when that oldest one started (zero when no
	// session lacks an id).
	Sessions, Missing int
	Since             time.Time
}
    SessionIDGap is what sessions say of their ids (MissingSessionIDs).

func MissingSessionIDs(sessions []store.Session) SessionIDGap
    MissingSessionIDs reads the gap in the session ids of sessions
    (RecentSessionIDs, newest first): the newest without an id in a row,
    and those without one since two sessions in a row last had one.

type ShellData struct {
	Title      string   // the pane title, e.g. "PR #729 codex-review - talkable"; "" = no title prefix
	Command    string   // the role's command template ("" = role.Command)
	Args       []string // the role's args (nil = role.Args)
	Capture    string   // the role's capture ("" = role.Capture)
	ReportPath string   // the role's output, absolute
	Marker     string   // the done marker, DoneMarker(runID); [A-Za-z0-9._-]+
	BaseRef    string   // e.g. origin/master, or the parent branch of a stacked PR
	// BaseSHA is the merge base of HeadSHA and the base; "" when unknown.
	// Unlike BaseRef it does not move when the base branch gains commits,
	// so `codex review --base {{if .BaseSHA}}{{.BaseSHA}}{{else}}{{.BaseRef}}{{end}}`
	// reviews exactly the PR's diff.
	BaseSHA string
	HeadSHA string
	URL     string
	// Model and Effort are the role's model and its effort for the round
	// (config.Role.EffortFor); "" = the role's model and effort.
	// codex-review's command passes Effort as a config override.
	Model, Effort string
	// MCPOff are the args that keep configuration out of the session of
	// the role's tool kind (config.Kind.ConfigOffArgs): the MCP servers of
	// the Codex config (mcp_off), and the checkout's project config (Codex's
	// .codex/, Claude's .claude/ and .mcp.json) when the PR changes it
	// (project_untrust), else Codex's servers under project_mcp "off";
	// codex-review's command passes them after its effort.
	// Manager.ShellLine fills it when nil.
	MCPOff []string
	// ToolOutput are the args that raise the most tokens of one tool
	// call's output the role's tool kind keeps (config.Kind.ToolOutputArgs,
	// its tool_output_limit; codex: -c tool_output_token_limit=65536), as
	// its sessions get them; codex-review's command passes them after its
	// effort. Manager.ShellLine fills it when nil.
	ToolOutput []string

	// RunID and ExtraArgs keep full-line templates written for the old
	// codex_review.sh data working: RunID is Marker without its
	// MAGNUM_DONE_ prefix (or, when Marker is empty, sets it), ExtraArgs
	// defaults to Args.
	RunID     string
	ExtraArgs []string

	// Template is the resolved full-line template of a role with Prompt
	// (config.Config.RolePrompt(role, config.PromptInitial)); nil = resolve
	// role.Prompt among the embedded defaults. Manager.ShellLine fills it
	// from the configuration. Not a template variable.
	Template *config.Prompt
	// Checkout is the PR's checkout the line runs in, whose project config
	// Manager.ShellLine compares with BaseSHA (else BaseRef), and whose
	// databases DBLockCommand locks; "" = unknown, nothing kept out and
	// db-lock takes the git work tree it runs in. Not a template variable.
	Checkout string
	// Magnum is the magnum executable DBLockCommand runs (the daemon's own,
	// absolute; "" = magnum on PATH; Manager.ShellLine fills it from the
	// layout when empty). Not a template variable.
	Magnum string
	// DBLockCommand is the line a command that touches the checkout's
	// databases runs through, as RoleData's, with the run (ShellDBLockLine
	// from Magnum, Checkout, the role's name and RunID when empty:
	// `magnum db-lock --checkout <slot> --role <role> --run <run> --`, the
	// run token StopShell looks for): codex-review's command runs
	// `{{.DBLockCommand}} codex review ...`, so its sandboxed specs take
	// turns with the other roles'. It is a ready shell line: nothing quotes
	// it again.
	DBLockCommand string
}
    ShellData feeds a shell role's line (ShellLine): the role's command
    template, or a full-line .sh prompt template. Every value is shell-quoted
    when needed before it is substituted, because the result is typed into a
    shell.

type ShellHoldError struct {
	Role, Pane, Checkout string
	Foreign, Tokenless   bool
	Cause                string
}
    ShellHoldError is ClearShellPanes' answer while a command keeps one of the
    PR's shell panes in the checkout busy: Foreign for a command magnum did not
    start (no run token of the PR's role there), Tokenless for the line of a
    custom role whose command carries no run token, still running in the role's
    live pane, else magnum's own command it could not stop, Cause saying why in
    plain words. It names the role and the pane, never the command's argv.

func (e *ShellHoldError) Error() string

func (e *ShellHoldError) Is(target error) bool
    Is makes a ShellHoldError match ErrShellHold.

type StopFailure string
    StopFailure is the class of API error a turn ended on, as an agent's
    StopFailure hook names it (Wake, Deps.HookFailure): one of a fixed list,
    never the agent's own text.

const (
	StopFailureRateLimit      StopFailure = "rate_limit"
	StopFailureOverloaded     StopFailure = "overloaded"
	StopFailureAuthentication StopFailure = "authentication_failed"
	StopFailureBilling        StopFailure = "billing_error"
	StopFailureOther          StopFailure = "other"
)
    The classes of StopFailure: Claude Code's error names, and StopFailureOther
    for any other (invalid_request, server_error, max_output_tokens, unknown,
    anything an agent made up).

type TargetMatch int
    TargetMatch says whether a path is a link's target or lies under it
    (MatchTarget).

const (
	// NotUnder says the path is neither the target nor under it.
	NotUnder TargetMatch = iota
	// MaybeUnder says it may be, and magnum cannot tell: an element of the path
	// and the target's that differ have a byte outside ASCII, which a
	// case-insensitive filesystem folds by rules of its own (APFS opens
	// claß.md for class.md, ﬁrst.md for first.md and a decomposed name for
	// its composed spelling; HFS+ also ignores some code points), and the
	// ASCII letters of the one are among the other's (MayFold).
	MaybeUnder
	// Under says the path is the target or lies under it.
	Under
)
func MatchTarget(f, t string) TargetMatch
    MatchTarget says whether f, a path relative to the checkout's root, is the
    link target t or lies under it, element by element, in ASCII case: git names
    a tracked file in its own case, while a link's text, which its target keeps
    (linkTarget), may spell it in another, and every case-insensitive filesystem
    folds ASCII alike. An element with a byte outside ASCII matches only one
    of the same bytes for sure; where it differs, the answer is MaybeUnder.
    The target "" (a link to the checkout's root, .claude/skills -> ..) covers
    every path. An exact target (ExactTarget: a slash at its end) has no path
    under it, its last element empty as no path's is; its path, and each on the
    way to it, lies under it the other way round (MatchTarget(t, f)).

type ThreadReply struct {
	ID     int64  `json:"id"` // REST comment id
	Author string `json:"author"`
	// Own: the reviewer login wrote it (an earlier rebuttal or answer); it
	// has no Class. Kind is what its reply marker says it was (ack,
	// rebuttal, answer; "" without a marker).
	Own  bool   `json:"own,omitempty"`
	Kind string `json:"kind,omitempty"`
	// Class is what the reply's first clause claims (past an
	// acknowledgement such as "Good catch,"): fixed, not a bug, won't fix or
	// other.
	Class     string `json:"class,omitempty"`
	Body      string `json:"body"`                // an excerpt: at most 600 characters
	Truncated bool   `json:"truncated,omitempty"` // Body was cut
	// CreatedAt is when the reply was written (RFC3339, UTC); omitted when
	// GitHub reports none, and in a threads file written before replies
	// carried it.
	CreatedAt string `json:"created_at,omitempty"`
}
    ThreadReply is one reply of a ReviewThread.

type TurnError struct {
	Message string // the error's message, redacted, at most 300 bytes
	Info    string // codex_error_info: cyber_policy, usage_limit_exceeded, server_overloaded, unauthorized, other
	// Helper is the thread id of the helper agent (a Codex sub-agent the
	// session spawned) whose turn ended with the error; "" for the
	// session's own turn.
	Helper string
}
    TurnError is the error a Codex turn ended with, as its rollout records it.

type UserTurn struct {
	At   time.Time // when the CLI stamped it
	Text string
	// Origin is what began the turn, as Claude Code records it ("human" for a
	// typed prompt); "" when the transcript names none (an older Claude Code,
	// every Codex rollout).
	Origin string
	// Before is what the agent said in its two turns before this one, oldest
	// first, each turn's texts joined by a line break: the text of the
	// assistant's messages (Claude) or of the agent_message events (Codex)
	// between two prompts. A turn that said nothing is skipped, and a
	// session's first turns have fewer. ClaudeUserTurns and CodexUserTurns
	// read it in the same pass over the file; ClaudeQueuedTurns leaves it nil.
	Before []string
}
    UserTurn is a prompt typed into an agent's pane, by a person or by magnum
    through herdr, as its transcript records it.

func ClaudeQueuedTurns(path string, since time.Time) ([]UserTurn, error)
    ClaudeQueuedTurns reads the prompts typed into a Claude Code agent while
    it worked that the transcript at path records, stamped at or after since
    (the zero time: all of them), in order: the text of each queue-operation
    enqueue line, and the prompt of each queued_command attachment (the entry
    Claude Code writes when it takes a queued prompt into the turn it was in,
    stamped when the prompt was queued), task notifications left out. Origin
    is OriginQueued. ClaudeUserTurns returns neither, so what proves a prompt
    arrived, or counts what someone typed, reads both; one prompt may appear
    twice (queued, then taken in). Lines that are no JSON are skipped.

func ClaudeUserTurns(path string, since time.Time) ([]UserTurn, error)
    ClaudeUserTurns reads the user turns of the Claude Code transcript at path
    that are stamped at or after since (the zero time: all of them), in order:
    the user entries that start a turn (a string, or the first text block,
    is the Text; a tool result and the line esc writes are no turns),
    not the entries of a subagent's own thread, not text Claude Code adds
    itself (isMeta), not task notifications or messages another Claude session
    sent (notTyped), and not what Claude Code writes as a command's output (a
    slash or bash-mode command's stdout and stderr, the caveat before them:
    cliOutputTags) or a compaction's summary (isCompactSummary); the command
    record a slash command leaves stays (see SlashCommand). Each carries the
    text of the assistant's messages in the agent's two turns before it (Before;
    a turn a task notification began is one of the agent's turns too).
    The whole file is read, a line at a time; a line that is no JSON, such as
    the half-written last one, is skipped. A prompt typed while the agent worked
    and taken into the turn it was in is an attachment entry, not a user entry,
    and is not returned.

func CodexUserTurns(path string, since time.Time) ([]UserTurn, error)
    CodexUserTurns reads the user turns of the Codex rollout at path that
    are stamped at or after since (the zero time: all of them), in order:
    its user_message events, with the text of payload.message, each with the
    agent_message texts of the agent's two turns before it (Before). Unlike the
    tail scan TurnError makes, it reads the whole file, so a long turn's output
    never pushes a prompt out of reach. An empty message and a line that is no
    JSON are skipped.

type WhiteboardPromptInput struct {
	Owner, Repo, Checkout, BaseRef, ReviewURL, ReviewFile, Session string
}
    WhiteboardPromptInput is what the whiteboard job knows beyond the PR, the
    role and the run that WhiteboardPrompt reads: the PR's repository (Owner,
    Repo), the slot's checkout the whiteboard's code views read (Checkout,
    absolute), the base ref the writer takes the merge base from (BaseRef,
    e.g. origin/master), the review magnum posted on the head (ReviewURL and
    its review.json ReviewFile) and the Whiteboard session of an earlier head
    (Session; "" = none yet).

type Workspace struct {
	WorkspaceID string
	TabID       string
	// Panes maps a role name to its herdr pane id, for agent and shell roles
	// alike (a shell role's pane runs its command; see RunShell).
	Panes map[Role]string
	// Roles is the layout order: the root pane's role (the judge) first, then
	// the other roles in the order they were laid out (EnsurePane appends).
	Roles []Role
	// Created is true when this call created the workspace (agents must be
	// started; resume ids come from ResumeID).
	Created bool
	// MovedFrom is the previous checkout when the PR's old workspace pointed
	// at another slot and was parked; pass it to the judge as moved_from.
	MovedFrom string
}
    Workspace is a PR's herdr workspace and the pane serving each role.

```

## app

```text
package app // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/app"

Package app wires magnum's components from config.toml: the store,
the subprocess runner (wrapped in execx.DryRun under --dry-run), the herdr,
GitHub, MySQL and git clients, the identities, and the slots, inventory, agents,
pipeline, cleanup and notify layers built on top of them. The daemon (package
engine) and the CLI share one App per process.

CONSTANTS

const (
	LogMaxBytes = 10 << 20 // rotate state/logs/daemon.log at 10 MB
	LogKeep     = 3        // keep daemon.log.1 … daemon.log.3
)
    Log rotation defaults for the daemon log.


FUNCTIONS

func Interactive(f *os.File) bool
    Interactive reports whether f is a terminal (so logs are mirrored to it
    and prompts may be shown). It asks the terminal driver (the termios ioctl
    behind isatty), so /dev/null, which launchd and background jobs hand out as
    stdin/stderr and which is also a character device, is not a terminal.

func LookupPR(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, p RefParser, ref string) (store.Repo, store.PR, error)
    LookupPR resolves ref with p and loads the repository and PR rows from st.
    A repository or PR the registry does not know wraps store.ErrNotFound.

func NewIdentity(cfg *config.Config, layout paths.Layout, run execx.Runner, id config.Identity) (identity.Source, *github.Client)
    NewIdentity is identity id's source and the GitHub client that acts as it
    over run, as New makes them for each [identity] of cfg, for a process that
    builds no App (the factory daemon): an App's mints its installation tokens
    into its gh config dir (layout's), which its client names, and mints again
    on a 401; a gh identity's is your own gh login. The App's REST calls go
    as github transport says, and its private key is read from the process's
    environment when private_key_env names it.

func NewLogger(file io.Writer, stderr io.Writer, level slog.Leveler) *slog.Logger
    NewLogger builds magnum's logger: JSON lines to file (when non-nil) plus
    human-readable text to stderr (when non-nil), both behind RedactHandler.


TYPES

type App struct {
	Config *config.Config
	Layout paths.Layout
	Store  *store.Store
	// Runner is the subprocess runner every component shares; under DryRun it
	// is DryRunner.
	Runner    execx.Runner
	DryRunner *execx.DryRun // non-nil under DryRun: the planned mutating commands
	DryRun    bool
	// AgentTag is Options.AgentTag.
	AgentTag string
	// Mise is Options.Mise.
	Mise string
	// HookSocket is Options.HookSocket: the pane agents' managers the
	// engine makes (engine.FromApp) take it too.
	HookSocket string
	// HookFailures carries the StopFailures its agents managers' hooks
	// proved (SendHookFailure, agents.Deps.HookFailure) to the engine,
	// which handles them on a goroutine of its own; nil without a hook
	// socket.
	HookFailures chan HookFailure

	// Herdr is the client of the herdr session magnum's panes are in,
	// PaneSession: the agents, the rounds' keys and the engine drive it,
	// and the registry's herdr ids are its server's.
	Herdr       *herdr.Client
	PaneSession herdr.Session
	// Yours is a client of your herdr session ([herdr] socket), nil while
	// the panes are in it (Herdr is then yours).
	Yours *herdr.Client
	// Guard is the herdr the slot guard and the inventory read: the panes'
	// session and yours, its ids prefixed (herdr.GuardView), so your agents
	// and consoles in a checkout hold it wherever magnum's panes are.
	Guard herdr.GuardView
	// GitHub returns the gh client acting as the named identity (nil for an
	// unknown name). Clients are created once and shared.
	GitHub     func(identity string) *github.Client
	Identities map[string]identity.Source
	// MySQL is the local DBngin client. mysqlx.Open never connects, so it is
	// non-nil even while MySQL is down (calls then fail and consumers degrade);
	// Ping probes it. Nil only when the DSN is invalid.
	MySQL *mysqlx.Client
	Git   *gitx.Client

	Slots     *slots.Manager
	Inventory *inventory.Scanner
	Agents    *agents.Manager
	// Pipeline holds one round runner per identity name (its GitHub client
	// acts as that identity).
	Pipeline map[string]*pipeline.Runner
	Cleanup  *cleanup.Planner
	// Notify toasts in your session (Yours, else Herdr): the one you look
	// at. Sidebar labels magnum's workspaces (herdr's sidebar tokens) in
	// the panes' session.
	Notify  *notify.Notifier
	Sidebar *notify.Notifier

	Logger *slog.Logger

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    App is the wired set of components one process uses.

func New(cfg *config.Config, layout paths.Layout, opts Options) (*App, error)
    New builds the App: it creates the state tree, opens the store (a private
    copy under DryRun), builds every client from cfg and wires the layers.

func (a *App) Close() error
    Close releases everything New opened (store, MySQL, log file, the dry-run
    store copy), in reverse order.

func (a *App) IdentityNames() []string
    IdentityNames lists the configured identity names in config order.

func (a *App) Refs() RefParser
    Refs is the App's RefParser (cfg.Daemon.DefaultRepo).

func (a *App) SendHookFailure(s store.Session, f agents.StopFailure, h agents.Health)
    SendHookFailure implements agents.Deps.HookFailure: it queues the failure
    for the engine (HookFailures) and never waits, since it runs on the hook
    listener's goroutine or on one of Wake's; a failure the full queue has no
    room for is dropped with a debug line (the run's own end reads its screen
    again). Without a listener (no queue) it does nothing.

type HookFailure struct {
	Session store.Session
	Failure agents.StopFailure
	Screen  agents.Health
}
    HookFailure is one API error an agent's turn ended on, as the session's
    own StopFailure hook named it and its screen, read again, proved it
    (agents.Deps.HookFailure): the session's row, the class (never the hook's
    text) and the screen's verdict.

type Options struct {
	// DryRun wraps the runner in execx.DryRun, puts slots in dry-run mode,
	// disables toasts and opens a private copy of the registry, so nothing
	// outside the process changes.
	DryRun bool
	// Daemon marks the process as the daemon, which owns daemon.log rotation.
	// Any other process (CLI commands) appends to daemon.log without ever
	// rotating it.
	Daemon bool
	// Logger replaces the default logger (JSON to state/logs/daemon.log,
	// rotated by size when Daemon is set, plus text to Stderr). Under DryRun
	// the default logs to Stderr only.
	Logger *slog.Logger
	// Stderr receives human-readable logs; nil means os.Stderr when it is a
	// terminal (or always under DryRun).
	Stderr io.Writer
	// LogLevel defaults to info.
	LogLevel slog.Leveler
	// Runner replaces the real subprocess runner (tests).
	Runner execx.Runner
	// MySQLDSN defaults to $MAGNUM_MYSQL_DSN, else mysqlx.DefaultDSN.
	MySQLDSN string
	// HTTPClient and Getenv are passed to App identities (tests). A nil
	// HTTPClient means the [github] transport client (see githubHTTPClient).
	HTTPClient *http.Client
	Getenv     func(string) string
	// HerdrSocket overrides the socket of the herdr session magnum's panes
	// are in (tests).
	HerdrSocket string
	// AgentTag tags the agents this App starts (agents.Deps.Tag,
	// pipeline.Runner.AgentTag) and turns its toasts off: magnum eval uses
	// "eval" with a scratch layout, so its rounds never meet the PR's own
	// agents or notify like a real review.
	AgentTag string
	// Mise is the mise executable that runs the pool's scripts: the slots
	// manager's (slots.Deps.Mise) and the readiness step's reset_db commands'
	// (pipeline.Runner.Mise). "" means "mise" on PATH.
	Mise string
	// BeforeMigrate is store.Options.BeforeMigrate for the real registry
	// (the CLI refuses to migrate it under a running daemon); a dry-run copy
	// migrates freely.
	BeforeMigrate func(from, to int) error
	// HookSocket is the socket of the daemon's hook listener, which the
	// daemon command started under the daemon lock before New
	// (engine.ClaimDaemon): the agents manager gives every pane it makes
	// the socket and the binary (agents.Deps.HookSocket). "" = no listener,
	// and no pane gets either: the CLI, a dry run, a tagged App, a daemon
	// whose socket path is too long or whose listener failed.
	HookSocket string
}
    Options tune New.

type Printf struct {
	Logger *slog.Logger
	Level  slog.Level
	Src    string
}
    Printf adapts a slog.Logger to execx.Logger (and herdr/slots/notify
    loggers): each line becomes one record at level with the given message
    prefix as the "src" attribute.

func (p Printf) LogAttrs(level slog.Level, msg string, attrs ...slog.Attr)
    LogAttrs implements execx.AttrLogger: an audit event's mirror keeps its
    subject and kind as attributes (execx.LogEvent), after "src".

func (p Printf) Logf(level slog.Level, format string, args ...any)
    Logf implements execx.LevelLogger: the runner picks the level (successful
    commands at Debug, failures at Warn).

func (p Printf) Printf(format string, args ...any)
    Printf implements execx.Logger.

type RedactHandler struct{ Inner slog.Handler }
    RedactHandler wraps a slog.Handler and passes the message and every string
    attribute (errors and Stringers included) through execx.Redact, so a token
    that slips into a log call never reaches a sink.

func (h RedactHandler) Enabled(ctx context.Context, l slog.Level) bool
    Enabled implements slog.Handler.

func (h RedactHandler) Handle(ctx context.Context, r slog.Record) error
    Handle implements slog.Handler.

func (h RedactHandler) WithAttrs(attrs []slog.Attr) slog.Handler
    WithAttrs implements slog.Handler.

func (h RedactHandler) WithGroup(name string) slog.Handler
    WithGroup implements slog.Handler.

type RefParser struct{ DefaultRepo string }
    RefParser resolves the PR references users type (URL, owner/repo#N, repo#N,
    #N, N) against a default repository ("owner/name").

func (p RefParser) ResolvePR(_ context.Context, ref string) (owner, repo string, number int, err error)
    ResolvePR parses ref with github.ParseRef and the parser's default repo.

type RotatingFile struct {
	Path string
	Max  int64
	Keep int

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    RotatingFile is an io.Writer that appends to a file and rotates it by size:
    when a write would push the file past Max bytes, path.N-1 becomes path.N
    (the oldest beyond Keep is dropped), path becomes path.1 and a new file is
    started. A rotation that fails keeps writing to path (reopened), and the
    next write past Max tries again; a file that could not be reopened is opened
    again by the next write. Only Close stops it. Safe for concurrent use.

func OpenRotating(path string, max int64, keep int) (*RotatingFile, error)
    OpenRotating opens (or creates, 0600) path for appending.

func (r *RotatingFile) Close() error
    Close closes the file.

func (r *RotatingFile) Write(p []byte) (int, error)
    Write implements io.Writer.

```

## attention

```text
package attention // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/attention"

Package attention explains why a PR needs the user. The engine stores the error
that sent a PR to needs_attention as it came: often a chain of contexts ending
in a command's whole output (a 300-line Ruby build log, a git transcript),
whose first line says nothing useful. Explain turns that text into a stage,
the one line of the output that names the cause, a one-line summary and the
next step, so every screen can say why in a line and what to do in another.
It is pure text work, so rows written before it existed are explained too.

CONSTANTS

const (
	KindFailed        = "failed"          // setup failed maxAttempts times on one head
	KindOverloaded    = "overloaded"      // the agent API stayed overloaded
	KindBlocked       = "blocked"         // the judge reported a blocker or waits on a dialog
	KindNoReview      = "needs_attention" // the judge posted nothing after a nudge, or its result was inconsistent
	KindIdentityError = "identity_error"  // the judge's identity check failed
	KindIdentityLeak  = "identity_leak"   // a review with the run's marker came from another login
	// KindFix: the fix job (a fixer fixing magnum's findings on the
	// operator's PR) needs the author: findings it left to them, or a fix
	// run that failed. Its message is the job's sentence ("fix: 2 findings
	// need your call: <report>", "fix run failed: …", "fix guard failed: …",
	// "fix settle failed: …"), with the fixer's report path when it has one,
	// or a call per finding with its thread's link and the report last
	// ("fix: reply fixed in <sha7> in … and resolve it: <url>; …; details:
	// <report>", FixCallsText), which Reason.NeedsYou and Steps carry; or
	// the look's raise of what loops left open ("fix: 2 items the fixer
	// left need you: <url>, <url>", LookRaiseText), which GitHub lifts.
	KindFix = "fix"
	// KindShellHold: a command keeps one of the PR's shell panes in its slot
	// busy, so nothing switches the slot's checkout, and the hold lasted 15
	// minutes. Its message is the hold's plain reason ("a command magnum did
	// not start keeps the shell pane of review1 busy", "magnum cannot stop
	// its own command in review1: …"); the reconcile looks again every 10
	// minutes and puts the PR back in line once the pane is free.
	KindShellHold = "shell_hold"
)
    Kinds: why the engine parked the PR (engine needsAttention's why).

const (
	StageFetch        = "fetch"
	StageWorktree     = "worktree"
	StageCheckout     = "checkout"
	StageDependencies = "dependencies"
	StageAgents       = "agents"
	StageJudge        = "judge"
	StageIdentity     = "identity"
	StageReview       = "review"
	StageFix          = "fix"
)
    Stages: where the failure happened.

const LookLift = "answer each linked item on GitHub (or its reviewer approves the PR), and magnum lifts this at its next read of the PR"
    LookLift is what lifts the look's raise (LookRaise): the look reads the
    PR again and puts it back to reviewed once each raised item is answered on
    GitHub, or its reviewer approved the PR since (engine openLift). It is the
    raise's remedy and `magnum fix --done`'s refusal of it.

const SummaryMax = 160
    SummaryMax bounds Summary and Cause (runes).

const TailLines = 8
    TailLines bounds Reason.Tail.


FUNCTIONS

func CLIChange(kind string, at, now time.Time) string
    CLIChange is the note the engine ends a launch failure's stored error with
    when the agent CLI of the role that did not start (kind) changed shortly
    before, at at: "; the codex CLI changed at 11:24", with the date ("Oct 16
    11:24") when at is of an earlier day than now. Explain moves it to the end
    of the reason's Cause and Summary, and reads it only from an error of a
    role's start ("start <role>: …"), so a command's output that ends the same
    way says nothing of a CLI.

func DecisionCall(c FixCall) bool
    DecisionCall reports whether c asks the author to decide in its thread:
    a DeclinedCall, in one of magnum's threads or in another reviewer's ("a
    human's" in the older words). `magnum fix --decide` answers it.

func FixAsks(msg string) bool
    FixAsks reports whether msg, a fix job's message, asks the author for the
    calls of what its fixer left them, whatever the loop's own words before
    them (a re-review that did not post): the calls (FixCallsText) or the
    findings and conflicts named or counted ("2 findings need your call (…)",
    the settle's "1 finding needs your call: <report>"). A loop that ended
    otherwise (its cap, a failed run, a guard) asks for something else.

func FixCallsText(calls []FixCall, more, report string) string
    FixCallsText is the part of a fix job's message that names its calls,
    joined by "; ": each call's sentence, then more (the findings named in the
    older words, "1 more finding needs your call (…)"; "" for none), then the
    report ("details: <report>"). Explain reads it back.

func FixReport(msg string) string
    FixReport is the fixer's report that a fix job's message msg (a PR's
    last_error under KindFix) names: the last absolute path to a .md file of its
    first line, as the remedy names the report (fixRemedy); "" when that line
    names none.

func Kinds() []string
    Kinds are every kind above: Explain reads each as a message's leading
    "<kind>: ", and the PR board names each in its attention pill.

func LaunchRole(msg string) (role string, ok bool)
    LaunchRole is the agent role a round setup's error msg says did not start
    (the engine's "start <role>: …"), whose CLI a CLIChange note may name;
    ok is false for any other error.

func LookRaise(msg string) bool
    LookRaise reports whether msg, a PR's last_error (with its "fix: " or
    without, as Explain reads it), is the look's raise (LookRaiseText).

func LookRaiseText(n int, links []string) string
    LookRaiseText is the message of the look's raise (engine openRaise, with
    autofix = "open"): n items that fix loops left and a later read of the look
    found still open, at links: "fix: 2 items the fixer left need you: <url>,
    <url>". No fixer's report or pane goes with it, and `magnum fix --done` does
    not take it: the look lifts it itself (LookLift).

func MagnumsDecision(c FixCall, priority, place string) bool
    MagnumsDecision reports whether c is the call to decide one of magnum's
    findings of priority at place, in magnum's thread: a DeclinedCall or an
    AuthorsCall ("decide magnum's P3 on app/models/offer.rb:42: …").

func MergeDropped(msg string) bool
    MergeDropped reports whether msg, a PR's last_error (with its "fix: " or
    without), is a dropped held merge's attention (MergeDroppedText).

func MergeDroppedNext(ref string) string
    MergeDroppedNext is the next step of a dropped held merge's attention on
    ref: a new merge of the parent.

func MergeDroppedText(what string) string
    MergeDroppedText is the attention of a held merge magnum dropped,
    what its words (whose merge, and why): "fix: merge dropped: magnum dropped
    claude-fix's held merge d3d3d3d of master at c0c0c0c: master moved on GitHub
    from c0c0c0c to d1d1d1d; P merges the parent again". Its next step is a new
    merge of the parent (MergeDroppedNext).

func MergeReady(msg string) bool
    MergeReady reports whether msg, a PR's last_error (with its "fix: " or
    without, as Explain reads it), is a held merge's attention (MergeReadyText).

func MergeReadyNext(ref string) string
    MergeReadyNext is the next step of a held merge's attention on ref: the held
    push's y/N.

func MergeReadyText(what string) string
    MergeReadyText is the attention of a merge of the parent that magnum
    holds for your y (the engine's HeldMerge), what its words, the merge and
    who pushes it: "fix: merge ready: claude-fix merged master at c0c0c0c
    and resolved 5 conflicts. …". Its next step is the held push's question
    (MergeReadyNext), never `magnum fix --done`.

func OnMagnumsSide(kind string) bool
    OnMagnumsSide reports whether kind (a Reason's Kind) is a failure on
    magnum's side rather than in the PR: a setup or round that failed,
    the agent API overloaded, the judge blocked or stopped without a review,
    or magnum's own identity. The PR status comment tells its author so.
    The fix job's attention (KindFix) asks the author for a call on the findings
    its fixer left, on the operator's own PR, and is not one.


TYPES

type FixCall struct {
	Thread string `json:"thread,omitempty"`
	URL    string `json:"url"`
	Action string `json:"action"`
}
    FixCall is one finding a fix job's fixer left to the author that its
    message names with what to do (Reason.NeedsYou): the id of the comment
    that starts the finding's thread (none for a conflict with the base,
    which has no thread), the thread's link (the PR's page for a conflict),
    and the sentence that says what to do there (FixedCall, DeclinedCall,
    AuthorsCall, ResolveCall, ConflictCall).

func AuthorsCall(thread, url, priority, place, ref string, magnums bool) FixCall
    AuthorsCall is the call of one of magnum's findings whose Fix ends "This
    is the author's call." (a P0 to P2: a P3's is optional, never a call),
    or of a product or business-logic choice another reviewer's thread asks for
    (magnums false), which the fixer left to the author without a verdict of its
    own: "decide magnum's P2 on <place>: the review leaves the choice to you;
    reply with yours at <url>, or run `magnum fix <ref> --decide <thread>="<your
    choice>"`" ("another reviewer's" in a thread another reviewer started,
    "finding" for one without a priority). Neither "the fixer declined it" nor
    "`magnum fix` sends it back" holds there: a rerun only asks again. It is a
    decision call (DecisionCall).

func ConflictCall(paths []string, url string) FixCall
    ConflictCall is the call of a conflict with the PR's base that the fixer
    left to the author: a product decision it would not make, so it aborted
    its merge of the base. The author merges the base on the PR's page url
    and decides the conflict in paths (plain path characters, which fixCallRe
    reads back): "merge the base by hand and decide the conflict in app/a.rb,
    db/schema.rb: <url>", the first 20 named and the rest counted ("… and 5
    more: <url>"), as the fix prompt names them. It has no thread.

func DeclinedCall(thread, url, priority, place, ref string, magnums bool) FixCall
    DeclinedCall is the call of a finding the fixer did not fix and left to the
```
