```text
    author to decide: "decide magnum's P2 on <place>: the fixer declined it;
    reply won't fix at <url>, or `magnum fix <ref>` sends it back" ("another
    reviewer's" in a thread another reviewer started, "a human's" in the older
    words; "finding" for one without a priority).

func FixDecisionCalls(msg string) ([]FixCall, bool)
    FixDecisionCalls are the calls of msg, a fix job's message, when it asks for
    the fixer's calls alone (fixDoneFits: none of the loop's own words before
    them and nothing under them), every one a DeclinedCall (DecisionCall),
    with no finding in the older words beside them; ok is false otherwise.
    Each asks the author to decide in that thread, and an attention of these
    alone is answered once the author decided each one there: the engine then
    lets a loop start over it and lifts it once the fixer built every decision.

func FixedCall(thread, url, sha string, magnums bool) FixCall
    FixedCall is the call of a finding the fixer fixed in commit sha but did
    not answer: when magnums, in one of magnum's threads whose reply failed,
    where the author replies and resolves it ("reply fixed in <sha7> in magnum's
    thread and resolve it: <url>"); else in a thread another reviewer started
    (its reply failed, or the author had answered there before, where the fixer
    does not write), where the author replies and that reviewer resolves it
    ("reply fixed in <sha7> in another reviewer's thread: <url>"). The words
    of the time when the fixer never wrote in a thread a human started, "in the
    thread a human started and resolve it", are still read.

func ResolveCall(thread, url string) FixCall
    ResolveCall is the call of a finding in one of magnum's threads that shows
    the answer its call asked for (a "Fixed in" reply for a fix, "Won't fix"
    or "Not a bug" for a decline) and is still open: the author resolves it
    ("resolve magnum's thread, already answered: <url>"). Magnum never asks for
    the resolution of a thread another reviewer started.

type Reason struct {
	Kind     string `json:"kind,omitempty"`
	Stage    string `json:"stage"`
	Attempts int    `json:"attempts,omitempty"`
	Head     string `json:"head,omitempty"` // the short sha the attempts were on
	// Step is the configured step that failed (a dependency command), "" when
	// not one.
	Step string `json:"step,omitempty"`
	// Cause is the line of the error that names what went wrong.
	Cause string `json:"cause"`
	// Summary is one line: the stage, the attempts and the cause.
	Summary string `json:"summary"`
	// Fix is the next step, with the PR's reference filled in.
	Fix string `json:"fix"`
	// Steps are Fix's parts, one per line for a detail view, when it has
	// several: a fix job's call per finding its fixer left to the author,
	// then the report ("details: <path>"); Fix joins them with "; ". Empty
	// for a one-part step.
	Steps []string `json:"steps,omitempty"`
	// NeedsYou are the calls of a fix job's message (KindFix): each finding
	// its fixer left to the author with its thread and what to do there.
	// Empty for every other reason, and for a message in the older words.
	NeedsYou []FixCall `json:"needs_you,omitempty"`
	// Tail is the end of the failing command's output, cleaned (at most
	// TailLines lines), for a detail view; empty when there was none.
	Tail []string `json:"tail,omitempty"`
}
    Reason is why a PR needs the user, in screen-sized parts.

func Explain(kind, msg, ref string) Reason
    Explain reads why a PR needs the user from the stored error msg (the PR's
    last_error) and kind (the engine's why, "" when unknown: then inferred).
    ref is how the user names the PR (talkable#9992), used in Fix.

```

## cleanup

```text
package cleanup // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/cleanup"

Package cleanup builds and applies storage cleanup plans: releasing the slots
of closed PRs, removing per-PR worktrees and surplus pool slots, dropping
orphan per-worktree databases and resetting a manual worktree (talkable.repoN).
The daemon and the CLI share it: the daemon applies the default plan every tick,
the CLI prints a plan (Render) and applies it after confirmation.

Plan is read-only: it reads the registry, one inventory scan and, for the
directories it would delete, `du -sk`. Apply re-checks every action against the
current registry (a plan may be minutes old by the time a human confirms it),
scans the inventory again before a database drop or an external reset, executes
it through the slots manager, MySQL or git, writes an audit event per action and
keeps going past failures. Nothing is dropped or reset on incomplete facts (a
source that could not be read).

CONSTANTS

const (
	KindRelease        = "release"         // pool slot back to the pool (placeholder reset, schema reload)
	KindRemoveSlot     = "remove_slot"     // pool slot torn down (teardown, databases, worktree, branch)
	KindRemoveWorktree = "remove_worktree" // per-PR worktree removed (its teardown/pre-remove hooks run first)
	KindDropDBs        = "drop_dbs"        // orphan databases of one slug dropped
	KindResetExternal  = "reset_external"  // manual worktree reset to origin/<base>; databases kept
)
    Action kinds.

const (
	SkipPinned       = "pinned"               // slot or PR pinned (unpin first)
	SkipHoldReason   = "hold_reason"          // slots.hold_reason is set (Detail: the reason)
	SkipGraceLeft    = "grace_left"           // closed PR inside daemon.close_grace (Detail: time left)
	SkipNotManaged   = "not_managed"          // not magnum's to touch (external slot, non-allowlisted slug)
	SkipDirty        = "dirty_without_force"  // a human's changes would be lost; --force discards them (removals)
	SkipActiveRun    = "active_run"           // a review round is in flight (run, PR state or busy slot)
	SkipAgentWorking = "agent_working"        // a human's herdr agent is in the slot, or any agent works in a manual worktree
	SkipUnpushed     = "unpushed_commits"     // the reset would orphan commits; --force accepts that
	SkipSlotState    = "slot_state"           // the slot's state does not allow the operation
	SkipInUse        = "in_use"               // the slug's databases belong to a slot or worktree
	SkipNotFound     = "not_found"            // the named PR, slot, worktree or slug does not exist
	SkipIncomplete   = "discovery_incomplete" // a source (MySQL, git worktree lists, herdr) could not be read
)
    Skip reasons: why something the options selected is not in Actions.

const (
	StatusDone        = "done"
	StatusFailed      = "failed"
	StatusUnconfirmed = "unconfirmed" // needs typed confirmation; Apply was called without it
	StatusPlanned     = "planned"     // dry-run plan: nothing executed
)
    Result statuses.

const DroppedBy = "cleanup"
    DroppedBy is slot_databases.dropped_by for databases cleanup dropped.


VARIABLES

var (
	// ErrOptions: the Options combination is invalid.
	ErrOptions = errors.New("cleanup: invalid options")
	// ErrUnconfirmed: an action needs typed confirmation that Apply was not given.
	ErrUnconfirmed = errors.New("cleanup: needs typed confirmation")
	// ErrNothingDropped says that every action of the plan needed its slug
	// typed and Apply was not given it (Report.NothingConfirmed), so nothing
	// ran. The command and the daemon's cleanup request fail with it: only a
	// terminal asks for the slug.
	ErrNothingDropped = errors.New("nothing dropped: run it on a terminal and type the slug")
)

FUNCTIONS

func Render(p Plan) string
    Render prints a plan for the CLI:

        Plan: free ~2.1G disk, 800M MySQL (3 actions)
          release          talkable#11700 (merged 14m ago) review5
          drop_dbs         slug:review9 (orphan databases ...): 8 databases, 800M MySQL
        Skipped:
          talkable#11701   grace_left (6m left)

func RenderReport(r Report) string
    RenderReport prints the outcome of Apply, one line per action plus a
    summary.


TYPES

type Action struct {
	Kind    string `json:"kind"`
	Subject string `json:"subject"` // owner/name#N, slot:<name>, slug:<slug>, path:<dir>
	Why     string `json:"why"`
	// Bytes is the disk space freed (du estimate, 0 = none or unknown);
	// DBBytes the MySQL space freed.
	Bytes   int64    `json:"bytes"`
	DBBytes int64    `json:"db_bytes"`
	DBNames []string `json:"db_names,omitempty"`

	Repo   string `json:"repo,omitempty"` // owner/name (pool lookup)
	Slot   string `json:"slot,omitempty"`
	SlotID int64  `json:"slot_id,omitempty"`
	PRID   int64  `json:"pr_id,omitempty"`
	// PRState is the PR's state at plan time; a closed/releasing PR moves to
	// releasing and then released around the slot operation.
	PRState string `json:"pr_state,omitempty"`
	Reason  string `json:"reason,omitempty"` // assignment end reason: merged, closed or cleanup
	Path    string `json:"path,omitempty"`
	Slug    string `json:"slug,omitempty"`
	// reset_external
	MainClone string `json:"main_clone,omitempty"`
	Branch    string `json:"branch,omitempty"`
	Base      string `json:"base,omitempty"`

	Force   bool `json:"force,omitempty"`
	Confirm bool `json:"confirm,omitempty"` // needs typed confirmation (Apply's confirmed)
}
    Action is one planned change. The identifying fields (SlotID, PRID, Path,
    Slug, ...) let Apply re-check it against the current state.

type Git interface {
	FetchBranch(ctx context.Context, mainClone, base string) error
	ResetPlaceholder(ctx context.Context, dir, branch, base string) error
	Status(ctx context.Context, dir string) (gitx.Status, error)
	StatusPaths(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]gitx.StatusEntry, error)
	Unpushed(ctx context.Context, dir string) (int, error)
	// UnpushedRef counts the commits reachable from ref that are on no
	// remote and no magnum ref, like Unpushed for HEAD.
	UnpushedRef(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) (int, error)
	RevParse(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) (string, error)
}
    Git is the part of *gitx.Client cleanup uses (dirty checks and the external
    reset).

type Inventory interface {
	Scan(ctx context.Context, opts inventory.Options) (inventory.Inventory, error)
}
    Inventory is the part of *inventory.Scanner cleanup reads.

type MySQL interface {
	DropAll(ctx context.Context, names []string, g mysqlx.Guard) []mysqlx.DropResult
}
    MySQL is the part of *mysqlx.Client cleanup uses.

type Options struct {
	DryRun bool   `json:"dry_run,omitempty"` // Apply executes nothing
	PR     *PRRef `json:"pr,omitempty"`      // release (pool) or remove (per-PR) this PR's slot
	// Slot names a managed slot to release (or, with Remove, to remove); with
	// External it names a manual worktree (repoN, its directory name or path).
	Slot     string `json:"slot,omitempty"`
	Remove   bool   `json:"remove,omitempty"`
	Orphans  bool   `json:"orphans,omitempty"` // orphan databases on the automatic allowlist
	Slug     string `json:"slug,omitempty"`    // with Orphans: also this slug's orphans (typed confirmation)
	Shrink   *int   `json:"shrink,omitempty"`  // remove free slots beyond max(pool.min, N), oldest idle first
	Idle     bool   `json:"idle,omitempty"`    // with Shrink: only slots idle longer than pool.idle_remove_after
	External bool   `json:"external,omitempty"`
	// Force discards a human's tracked changes and untracked files on a
	// removal (magnum's residue goes without it) and, for reset_external,
	// any change and unpushed commits; it also lets an explicitly
	// named PR be released inside its close grace. It never overrides pins,
	// hold reasons, agents, in-flight rounds or incomplete discovery.
	Force bool `json:"force,omitempty"`
}
    Options selects what a plan covers. With no selector (PR, Slot, Orphans,
    Shrink) the plan is the default one: slots of closed PRs past their grace
    plus orphan databases on the automatic allowlist. Selectors combine.

type PRRef struct {
	Repo   string `json:"repo"`
	Number int    `json:"number"`
}
    PRRef names a pull request: Repo is "owner/name".

func (r PRRef) String() string

type Plan struct {
	CreatedAt time.Time `json:"created_at"`
	DryRun    bool      `json:"dry_run,omitempty"`
	Options   Options   `json:"options"`
	Actions   []Action  `json:"actions"`
	Skipped   []Skip    `json:"skipped"`
	Totals    Totals    `json:"totals"`
	Warnings  []string  `json:"warnings,omitempty"` // inventory sources that could not be read
}
    Plan is a deterministic list of actions plus what was skipped and why.

func (p Plan) NeedsConfirmation() bool
    NeedsConfirmation reports whether any action needs typed confirmation.

type Planner struct {
	Store     *store.Store
	Slots     Slots
	Inventory Inventory
	MySQL     MySQL
	Git       Git
	// Runner runs `du -sk` on directories an action deletes (read-only);
	// nil leaves Action.Bytes at 0 (unknown).
	Runner execx.Runner
	Config *config.Config
	// Clock defaults to time.Now.
	Clock func() time.Time
	// Park, when set, is called before the slot of a PR is released or
	// removed (the app wires (*agents.Manager).ParkClosingPanes, which also
	// closes the panes the park retired); an error fails that action and
	// leaves the PR's state as it was.
	Park func(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR) error
	// Log receives one line per applied action (optional).
	Log execx.Logger
}
    Planner builds and applies plans. Store, Slots, Inventory and Config are
    required; MySQL is needed to apply drop_dbs, Git for dirty checks of per-PR
    worktrees without inventory facts and for reset_external.

func (p *Planner) Apply(ctx context.Context, plan Plan, confirmed bool) (Report, error)
    Apply executes plan in order. A dry-run plan executes nothing (every
    result is planned); an action that needs typed confirmation runs only when
    confirmed is true (otherwise unconfirmed, not an error). Each action is
    re-checked against the current registry first, so a stale plan fails that
    action (wrapping store.ErrConflict) instead of touching something that
    changed. Apply keeps going past failed actions, writes one audit event per
    executed action and returns the report plus the failures joined (nil when
    none failed).

func (p *Planner) Plan(ctx context.Context, opts Options) (Plan, error)
    Plan builds the plan for opts. It changes nothing: it reads the registry,
    scans the inventory once (with External for --external) and runs `du -sk` on
    the directories an action would delete. Only a store or inventory failure is
    an error; anything the options select but the plan leaves alone is listed in
    Skipped with a reason.

func (p *Planner) PlanFrom(ctx context.Context, opts Options, inv inventory.Inventory) (Plan, error)
    PlanFrom is Plan over an inventory the caller already scanned (with
    inventory.Options{External: opts.External}), so a reconcile that has just
    scanned plans its cleanups without scanning again. The inventory may be a
    little old: Apply re-checks every action against the current registry.

type Report struct {
	Results     []Result `json:"results"`
	Done        int      `json:"done"`
	Failed      int      `json:"failed"`
	Unconfirmed int      `json:"unconfirmed"`
	Planned     int      `json:"planned"`
	// Freed sums the estimates of the done actions.
	DiskBytes  int64    `json:"disk_bytes"`
	MySQLBytes int64    `json:"mysql_bytes"`
	DroppedDBs []string `json:"dropped_dbs,omitempty"`
}
    Report is the outcome of Apply.

func (r Report) NothingConfirmed() bool
    NothingConfirmed reports whether Apply ran nothing because every action
    of the plan needed typed confirmation it was not given: the report counts
    unconfirmed actions and nothing done, failed or planned (ErrNothingDropped).

type Result struct {
	Action Action `json:"action"`
	Status string `json:"status"`
	Error  string `json:"error,omitempty"`
}
    Result is the outcome of one action.

type Skip struct {
	Subject string `json:"subject"`
	Reason  string `json:"reason"`
	Detail  string `json:"detail,omitempty"`
	// Slot is the slot a hold_reason skip is about (its name is what `magnum
	// unpin` takes); empty for the other reasons.
	Slot string `json:"slot,omitempty"`
}
    Skip is something the options selected that the plan leaves alone.

func (s Skip) Text() string
    Text is the skip's reason as a plan prints it: "<reason> (<detail>)",
    and for a slot a guard holds "held: <hold> (acknowledge it with magnum unpin
    "<slot>")", the command that hands the slot back (a moved HEAD or commits
    on no remote are acknowledged by it; the other holds come back at the guard
    while their cause is there). The JSON keeps the reason and the detail.

type Slots interface {
	Release(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pool config.Pool, reason string) error
	Remove(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pool config.Pool, force bool) error
	RemovePRWorktree(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, force bool) error
	// GuardLive refuses a pinned or held slot and a human's agent or
	// process in it, and saves nothing (a forced removal's guard).
	GuardLive(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot) error
	// HumanEvidence says why changes in the slot's tree are a human's (its
	// PR's human_active_at after the checkout), "" when they are magnum's
	// residue, which a release or removal discards.
	HumanEvidence(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot) (string, error)
}
    Slots is the part of *slots.Manager cleanup drives.

type Totals struct {
	Actions    int   `json:"actions"`
	DiskBytes  int64 `json:"disk_bytes"`
	MySQLBytes int64 `json:"mysql_bytes"`
	Databases  int   `json:"databases"`
}
    Totals sums a plan's estimates.

```

## confedit

```text
package confedit // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/confedit"

Package confedit edits a TOML config file in place: a value replaced, a key
or a table added, a key removed, and every other byte (comments, alignment,
blank lines, line endings) kept as it was. magnum's config files carry a dated
comment on most lines that explains a choice, which a TOML encoder would drop,
so this package never re-encodes a file: a small scanner (scan.go) records
where each key, value and trailing comment is, Parse cross-checks it against
BurntSushi's own reading of the file (MetaData.Keys, in document order),
and Apply splices only the bytes an edit needs, then Verify decodes the old and
the new file and requires them to differ in exactly the edited leaves. Whatever
it does not model fails with ErrUnsupported: the file is then edited by hand.

The rules (DECISIONS "The settings screen edits config.toml in place"):
  - A replaced value keeps its trailing comment at its column (the gap before
    it takes up a length change, at least one space) and the line ending. A
    value over several lines is replaced only as a whole array without comments
    inside, one element per line, and keeps that shape.
  - A missing key goes after the last key of its table (and the indented comment
    lines that continue that key's comment), so before any subtable of it:
    inserting into a [[pool]] element puts the key above its [pool.env].
    A key of an inline table goes inside its braces.
  - A missing table goes after the last table of its family (the same first
    name: the last [spend.*], the last [[repo]] element with its subtables),
    else before the first array of tables ([[watch]], [[repo]], ...) so a plain
    table stays above them, else at the end of the file; in each case before the
    comment lines that introduce the header after it, with a blank line on each
    side.
  - A removed key (back to its default) loses its line or lines; its trailing
    comment stays as a comment line of its own, with the lines that continue it.
  - A note (Change.Note) becomes the trailing comment "# YYYY-MM-DD: note" on a
    line without one, and goes first on a line with one: "# YYYY-MM-DD: note;
    <the old comment>", less the "was" notes of earlier saves (the forms of
    dropWasNotes, such as "2026-10-19: was 5"), so a line keeps the newest only.
  - A key only dotted keys or subtables define (an implicit table), a table
    inside a nested array of tables, a multi-line inline table and anything else
    ambiguous fail with ErrUnsupported.

VARIABLES

var ErrEditor = errors.New("confedit: the edit failed the editor's own check (a bug in the editor); nothing was written")
    ErrEditor is the error of an edit whose result fails the editor's own
    checks: it does not read back, it changes a line outside the edited key's,
    or it decodes to another change than the one asked for (Verify). It is a bug
    in the editor, never a shape it refuses; nothing is returned.

var ErrUnsupported = errors.New("confedit: construct not supported; edit the file by hand")
    ErrUnsupported is the error of a file, or an edit, the editor does not
    model: nothing is written and the file is edited by hand.


FUNCTIONS

func Changed(before, after []byte) ([]string, error)
    Changed lists the leaves where before and after differ, as dotted key paths
    with array elements by index ("pipeline.spend", "watch[1].roles[2]"),
    in key order: what a save changed, named without its values.

func Literal(v any) (string, error)
    Literal is v as a one-line TOML value: BurntSushi's encoder for strings (a
    basic string, escaped), booleans, integers, floats and arrays of them, and
    "{ k = v, ... }" for a map (an inline table, its keys in config.SpendRole's
    order, then by name).

func Verify(before, after []byte, changes []Change) error
    Verify decodes before and after and reports an error unless they differ
    in exactly the leaves the changes name (array elements by index): every
    leaf that differs lies at or under a change's key, and the changes' final
    effect holds in after, in their order: each key holds the value its last
    change wrote, a removed key is absent, and a change that a later one on
    the same key (or one holding it, or one under it) overrides is not checked
    on its own. It is the check that catches an editor mistake that would
    change another key; nothing is written when it fails. Its errors name keys,
    never values.


TYPES

type Change struct {
	Key   Key
	Value any    // string, bool, int, int64, float64, []string, []any of scalars, map[string]any (an inline table)
	Note  string // non-empty: a dated note on the key's line (see the package comment)
}
    Change sets a key (Value non-nil) or removes it (nil: back to the default).

type Doc struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Doc is a scanned file: every table header and key/value with its byte spans,
    checked against BurntSushi's MetaData.Keys() order.

func Parse(src []byte) (*Doc, error)
    Parse scans src and cross-checks it with toml.Decode: a file BurntSushi
    refuses is that error, and a file whose keys the scanner reads in another
    order or number than MetaData.Keys() (or with a construct it does not model)
    is ErrUnsupported.

func (d *Doc) Apply(now time.Time, changes ...Change) ([]byte, error)
    Apply returns the new file text; d is not modified. The changes apply in
    order, each to the text the one before it left (so a [[repo]] element one
    change creates takes the next change's key), and the result passes Verify
    against d. It fails when a change cannot be placed (an implicit table,
    a shape the editor refuses: ErrUnsupported) or names an element that does
    not exist; nothing is returned then. Removing a key the file does not set
    changes nothing.

func (d *Doc) Bytes() []byte
    Bytes is the file's text.

func (d *Doc) Elements(path ...string) int
    Elements is how many [path] elements the file has (an array of tables at the
    top level).

func (d *Doc) Get(k Key) (Value, bool)
    Get reads k; false when the file does not set it (the default applies).

func (d *Doc) HeaderLine(t Table) (int, bool)
    HeaderLine is the 1-based line of t's header; false when the file has no
    header of t (0 and true for the top of the file).

func (d *Doc) Repo(name string) (Table, bool)
    Repo is the [[repo]] whose repo is name, compared as validateRepos does (any
    case); config refuses a repository configured twice, so it is unique.

func (d *Doc) Role(name string) (Table, bool)
    Role is the [[role]] whose name is name.

func (d *Doc) Sum() [32]byte
    Sum is the SHA-256 of the file's text.

func (d *Doc) TableAt(line int) Table
    TableAt is the table a 1-based line lies in: the one whose header is the
    last at or above it (the top of the file above the first header).

func (d *Doc) Watch(i int) (Table, bool)
    Watch is the i-th [[watch]] (0-based).

type Key struct {
	Table Table
	Path  []string
}
    Key is a key inside a table; Path has more than one element for a key in an
    inline table ({"claude-review", "model"} in [spend.burn]) or a dotted key.

func (k Key) String() string

type Table struct {
	Path []string // {"pipeline"}, {"spend", "burn"}, {"kinds", "codex"}, {"repo"}; nil = the keys above the first header
	// Index is the element of the array of tables in Path ({"watch"} 1 =
	// the second [[watch]]; {"pool", "env"} 1 = the [pool.env] of the
	// second [[pool]]); -1 for a plain table.
	Index int
}
    Table names a table: a [section], an element of an [[array]], or a subtable
    of one.

func Section(path ...string) Table
    Section is the plain table at path.

func (t Table) String() string

type Value struct {
	Raw string // the value's text as written
	// Comment is the trailing comment of the key's line (for a key inside an
	// inline table, of the line holding it) with its continuation lines; ""
	// if none.
	Comment   string
	Line      int // 1-based line of the key
	Multiline bool
	// Data is the value as BurntSushi decodes it: string, int64, float64,
	// bool, a date, []any or map[string]any.
	Data any
}
    Value is what the file says for a key.

```

```text
	ContextUsedGroup = "used" // the percent of the context used
	ContextLeftGroup = "left" // the percent left
)
    Capture groups of Kind.ContextPattern.

const (
	// PermissionDeny: answer the prompt's No option, once per prompt and at
	// most a bounded number of times per run, so a review agent that hits a
	// prompt its CLI shows even in its no-approval mode (Claude Code's
	// "Dangerous rm operation" check) carries on instead of stalling the round.
	PermissionDeny = "deny"
	// PermissionWait: never answer; the agent stays blocked until the human
	// answers or the round times out.
	PermissionWait = "wait"
)
    Kind.OnPermissionPrompt values.

const (
	// HooksTrustOwn: pick "Trust all and continue" when the checkout carries
	// no hooks of its own (no .codex/hooks.json, no hooks or plugins in its
	// .codex/config.toml), so every hook listed comes from the user's Codex
	// home or an installed plugin; "Continue without trusting" otherwise.
	HooksTrustOwn = "trust_own"
	// HooksDecline: always "Continue without trusting": the session runs
	// without the untrusted hooks until the user trusts them in their own
	// Codex.
	HooksDecline = "decline"
)
    Kind.OnHooksReview values.

const (
	MCPTransportURL     = "url"
	MCPTransportCommand = "command"
)
    ProjectServer.Transport values: the key of the server's table that tells how
    Codex reaches it.

const (
	// ProjectMCPAllow: the MCP servers of an unchanged .codex/config.toml
	// in the checkout (the base branch's, so the team's) load.
	ProjectMCPAllow = "allow"
	// ProjectMCPOff: they are turned off like the user's (MCPDisable),
	// except those in MCPAllow.
	ProjectMCPOff = "off"
)
    Kind.ProjectMCP values.

const (
	LearnRestartIdle   = "idle"
	LearnRestartManual = "manual"
)
    The values of [learn] restart.

const (
	CurateOverLimit = "over_limit" // a repository past a limit, once its notes changed since the last curation
	CurateWeekly    = "weekly"     // every repository with notes, once a week, once they changed
	CurateMisses    = "misses"     // a retro recorded misses of the repository for its notes (class miss, scope repo)
	// CurateOff, alone, is no trigger: only `magnum notes <repo> --curate`.
	CurateOff = "off"
)
    Curation triggers ([notes] curate).

const (
	AutofixNever = "never" // a fix loop starts only on request
	AutofixOwn   = "own"   // and after a review with findings on the operator's own PRs
	AutofixOpen  = "open"  // and on the operator's own PRs whenever something is open, once the reviewers settled
)
    Values of [pipeline] autofix.

const (
	DefaultFullPassLines = 500
	DefaultFullPassFiles = 10
)
    DefaultFullPassLines and DefaultFullPassFiles are [pipeline]
    full_pass_lines' and full_pass_files' defaults: the churn since a PR's
    baseline that makes its next automatic re-review a full pass, unless a
    quarter of the PR's size at the baseline is more.

const (
	SpendLow    = "low"    // each built-in effort one notch down, medium the floor
	SpendMedium = "medium" // the built-in efforts as config.defaults.toml writes them
	SpendHigh   = "high"   // xhigh, the strongest effort both Codex and Claude take, everywhere
)
    Values of [pipeline] spend.

const (
	OwnPassParallel = "parallel" // the judge's own pass runs with the reviewers
	OwnPassAfter    = "after"    // one judge prompt after the reviewers
)
    Values of [pipeline] judge_own_pass.

const (
	// KindShell is the Role.Kind of a role that types a shell command into
	// a plain pane instead of driving an agent CLI (codex-review).
	KindShell = "shell"

	ModeSession = "session" // an interactive agent session (every agent kind)
	ModeShell   = "shell"   // a shell pane running Role.Command (kind = "shell")

	RunsAlways = "always" // every round that runs reviewers
	RunsFirst  = "first"  // until the role has completed once for the PR, then only on request
	RunsManual = "manual" // only when requested (today `magnum review --simplify`, for claude-simplify)
	RunsNever  = "never"  // disabled; requests are refused

	CaptureFile   = "file"   // the agent (or command) writes ReportFile itself
	CaptureStdout = "stdout" // shell roles: magnum tees the command's stdout into ReportFile (stderr stays in the pane)

	WrapperAuto  = "auto"  // probe `zsh -ic 'whence -w <kind>'` once: a function or alias is a wrapper
	WrapperTrue  = "true"  // the command is a wrapper that supplies its own flags
	WrapperFalse = "false" // a plain binary: Kind.Args are appended too
	// WrapperBypass: the pane's shell function or alias named like the kind
	// is removed before every launch and resume (`unset -f`, `unalias`), so
	// the binary runs with magnum's args alone; Kind.Args are appended.
	WrapperBypass = "bypass"

	SessionHerdr = "herdr" // herdr reports the CLI's session id (pane agent_session); resume uses it
	SessionNone  = "none"  // no session id: the role always starts fresh
)
    Role kinds, modes and option values.

const (
	PromptInitial  = "initial"  // Role.Prompt: first review of a PR (shell roles: the full command line)
	PromptRereview = "rereview" // Role.Rereview: a new head after an earlier review
	PromptRestart  = "restart"  // Role.Restart: a push cut the reviewer's turn short; the round restarted on the new head
	PromptContinue = "continue" // Role.ContinuePrompt: a pause ended mid-turn (judge)
	PromptRecovery = "recovery" // Role.Recovery: a fresh session after the old one was lost (judge)
	PromptNudge    = "nudge"    // Role.Nudge: the agent stopped without a result (judge)

const (
	DefaultFixSkill  = "{{repo}}/skills/magnum-fix/SKILL.md"

    DefaultFixSkill is a fix role's default skill path, as DefaultSkill is the

const (
	WebhooksOff    = "off"
	WebhooksShadow = "shadow"
	WebhooksActive = "active"
)
    The webhooks modes. Off reads nothing. Shadow reads the relay's events
    (magnum-relay, which receives the GitHub App's webhook deliveries) and
    compares what each would refresh with what the poll finds, changing nothing
    the daemon does. Active, acting on the events, is a later phase: Validate
    refuses it.

const AutoApproveBodyMax = 500
    AutoApproveBodyMax bounds auto_approve_body, in characters.

const AutofixMaxLoopsMax = 20
    AutofixMaxLoopsMax bounds autofix_max_loops.

const BuiltinDefaults = "built-in defaults (config.defaults.toml)"
    BuiltinDefaults names the embedded base in messages and Sources.

const CandidateSkill = "skills/magnum-review/SKILL.md"
    CandidateSkill is where a candidate directory holds the judge skill,
    as magnum's checkout does.

const CriticRoleName = "notes-critic"
    CriticRoleName is the name of the role the critic runs as (CriticRole).

const DatabasePlaceholder = "{database}"
    DatabasePlaceholder is where a migrations command takes the database it runs
    on (FactoryPrecheck.MigrationDatabases).

const DatabaseSuffix = "__{slug}"
    DatabaseSuffix ends every pool database template ([[pool]] databases):
    the slot's slug follows the last "__", which is how magnum lists and guards
    a slot's databases.

const DefaultAfterDenyPrompt = "magnum denied that command: review roles never run approval-gated or destructive commands. " +
	"Continue the task without it and finish as instructed."
    DefaultAfterDenyPrompt is every built-in and declared kind's
    after_deny_prompt.

const DefaultApproveAfterFullPass = 2
    DefaultApproveAfterFullPass is [pipeline] approve_after_full_pass' default:
    the first two re-reviews after a PR's baseline approve on their delta,
    so one round of fixes after the first review approves at once.

const DefaultAuditEvery = 5
    DefaultAuditEvery is [pipeline] audit_every's default: every fifth automatic
    re-review of a PR probes what no round probed.

const DefaultAutoApproveBody = "Auto-approved: Magnum's review of `{{.Short}}` found no blocking problems{{if .ReviewURL}} ([review]({{.ReviewURL}})){{end}}."
    DefaultAutoApproveBody is the body of an automatic approval when the watch
    sets no auto_approve_body.

const DefaultAutofixMaxLoops = 3
    DefaultAutofixMaxLoops is [pipeline] autofix_max_loops' default: three loops
    a day on one PR that autofix = "open" starts, then the PR needs you.

const DefaultBudgetFloor = 500
    DefaultBudgetFloor is github budget_floor's default: about a tenth of a
    user's hourly GraphQL budget of 5,000 points.

const DefaultClaudeContextPattern = `(?:\((?P<used>\d{1,3})%\)|Context left until auto-compact: (?P<left>\d{1,3})%)`
    DefaultClaudeContextPattern is the claude kind's context_pattern: a percent
    in parentheses, as a status line shows the context used ("418k/1m (41%)"),
    or Claude Code's warning as the context fills up ("Context left until
    auto-compact: 8%").

const DefaultCodexToolOutputLimit = 65536
    DefaultCodexToolOutputLimit is the codex kind's tool_output_limit: about
    256 KiB at Codex's four bytes a token, room for today's 97 KB notes and the
    reads a model asks to make larger.

const DefaultCriticPrompt = "notes-critic.md"
    DefaultCriticPrompt is the critic's prompt file.

const DefaultEditorPrompt = "skill-edit.md"
    DefaultEditorPrompt is the skill editor's prompt file.

const DefaultFixCompactAt = 70
    DefaultFixCompactAt is [pipeline] fix_compact_at's default: a fixer whose
    context is 70% used or more compacts its conversation before its next cycle,
    well before Claude Code compacts it by itself in the middle of a turn.

const DefaultFixCycles = 3
    DefaultFixCycles is [pipeline] fix_cycles' default: three fix runs, each
    followed by a re-review, before the PR is left to the operator.

const DefaultFullPassAfter = 12 * time.Hour
    DefaultFullPassAfter is [pipeline] full_pass_after's default: a PR's next
    automatic re-review half a day after its baseline is a full pass, so the
    first push of a workday gets a whole read.

const DefaultFullPassEvery = 10
    DefaultFullPassEvery is [pipeline] full_pass_every's default: every tenth
    automatic re-review of a PR reviews the whole PR again.

const DefaultIdleRemoveAfter = 168 * time.Hour
    DefaultIdleRemoveAfter is a pool's idle_remove_after when it sets none (or
    0): a free slot above pool.min is removed once it has been idle this long.
    Without it every reconcile removed the surplus at once, and the next
    provision wrote about 1 GB again.

const DefaultJudgeFallback = RoleClaudeJudge
    DefaultJudgeFallback is [pipeline] judge_fallback's default: the built-in
    second judge, claude-judge (the operator's choice, DECISIONS "Four built-in
    defaults follow what the operator chose by hand"). A built-in default never
    makes a configuration that loads fail: where no file writes the key, it is
    off for each watch it would not be valid for (no declared judge of that
    name, or the watch's judge or one of its kind; Config.JudgeFallbackFor),
    with no error and no warning.

const DefaultJudgeSessionRounds = 6
    DefaultJudgeSessionRounds is the judge's max_session_rounds: a Codex session
    resumed round after round carries every round's context (29M tokens of
    history after fifteen rounds on one PR), and its fifteenth turn was refused
    by Codex's cybersecurity classifier, which flags the PR for good.

const DefaultJudgeSubagents = 2
    DefaultJudgeSubagents is the judge's max_subagents: on its own it started 53
    subagent threads in 36 sessions, 27% of the Codex spend.

const DefaultLearnPrompt = "retro.md"
    DefaultLearnPrompt is the retro prompt file.

const DefaultMaxSimplifications = 5
    DefaultMaxSimplifications is [pipeline] max_simplifications' default:
    the judge posts at most five simplifications, the most substantial first
    (three from 2026-10-05 until the operator asked for five on 2026-10-19).

const DefaultMigrationFolder = "db/migrate"
    DefaultMigrationFolder is the only migration folder whose migrations the
    precheck runs without FactoryPrecheck.MigrationDatabases: the primary
    database's.

const DefaultNotesPrompt = "notes-curate.md"
    DefaultNotesPrompt is the curator's prompt file.

const DefaultReadyTimeout = 5 * time.Minute
    DefaultReadyTimeout bounds a round's whole readiness step when neither the
    [[repo]] nor the [[pool]] sets ready_timeout.

const DefaultReviewFooter = "**Reviewed commit:** `{{.Short}}`\n" +
	"\n" +
	"<details><summary>ℹ️ About Magnum</summary>\n" +
	"\n" +
	"Automated review by [Magnum](https://github.com/zhuravel/magnum). Reply on a P0-P2 thread with `fixed`, `not a bug: <why>` or `won't fix: <why>`" +
	"{{if .Simplify}}; a simplification keeps behavior: apply it, or reply `won't fix: <the risk>`{{end}}. New pushes are re-reviewed automatically" +
	"{{with .QuietHours}} (during {{.}} only small ones, by a short check){{end}}{{if .DraftsSkipped}}, drafts only on request{{end}}. " +
	"A thread reply gets an answer without a push, and a review request for `{{.RequestLogin}}` starts a round.\n" +
	"\n" +
	"</details>"
    DefaultReviewFooter is the footer template of every identity that sets no
    review_footer: the reviewed commit, then what the review is, how to answer a
    P0-P2 thread, in the words the reply classifier knows, that a simplification
    keeps behavior, so a refusal names its risk (when the watch runs simplify),
    and what starts a round (a push, during the quiet hours only a small one,
    which gets a short check, and not on a draft the watch skips; a thread
    reply; a review request), collapsed under <details> (config.defaults.toml
    documents it word for word).

const DefaultSimplifyRerunLines = 150
    DefaultSimplifyRerunLines is claude-simplify's rerun_min_lines: about two
    new functions' worth of code since it last looked.

const DefaultSkill = "{{repo}}/skills/magnum-review/SKILL.md"
    DefaultSkill is the judge's default skill path ({{repo}} = magnum's home).

const DefaultTriagePrompt = "triage.md"
    DefaultTriagePrompt is the triage prompt file.

const DefaultWhiteboardPrompt = "whiteboard.md"
    DefaultWhiteboardPrompt is a whiteboard role's default prompt (it has no
    skill: the Whiteboard app's own instructions guide it).

const EditorRoleName = "skill"
    EditorRoleName is the name of the role the skill editor runs as
    (EditorRole).

const EmbeddedFixSkill = "builtin:skills/magnum-fix/SKILL.md"
    EmbeddedFixSkill names the binary's own copy of the fix skill
    (magnum.FixSkill): what a fix role gets without a checkout.

const EmbeddedSkill = "builtin:skills/magnum-review/SKILL.md"
    EmbeddedSkill names the binary's own copy of the judge skill (magnum.Skill)
    as a skill source: what a judge gets without a checkout.

const FactorySharedPrompt = prompts.FactoryShared
    FactorySharedPrompt is the factory prompts' partials file
    (prompts.FactoryShared), as SharedPrompt is the judge prompts': the blocks
    the factory-*.md prompts share, the factory mode's rules among them.
    Every factory prompt is parsed with it, resolved as SharedPrompt is;
    ResolvePrompt refuses the name itself (ErrSharedPrompt).

const LearnRoleName = "retro"
    LearnRoleName is the name of the role the retro's classifying agent runs as
    (LearnRole).

const MaxBudgetFloor = 5000
    MaxBudgetFloor is the highest budget_floor: a user's whole hourly budget.

const MaxSimplificationsMax = 10
    MaxSimplificationsMax bounds max_simplifications ([pipeline] and [[repo]]):
    one PR got 20 simplifications, next to 5 findings, before the cap of
    2026-10-05.

const MinObserveInterval = 2 * time.Second
    MinObserveInterval is the shortest [daemon] observe_interval.

const NotesRoleName = "notes"
    NotesRoleName is the name of the role the curator runs as (NotesRole).

const PlaceholderNum = "{num}"
    PlaceholderNum is the issue number in a [board] trackers template.

const RequiredWorkflowPrefix = "workflow:"
    RequiredWorkflowPrefix marks a required_checks entry naming a whole GitHub
    Actions workflow ("workflow:CI"); store.RequiredWorkflowPrefix, which the
    matcher reads, spells it too.

const ReviewFooterMax = 2000
    ReviewFooterMax bounds review_footer, in characters.

const SharedPrompt = prompts.Shared
    SharedPrompt is the judge prompts' partials file (prompts.Shared): the
    blocks two or more judge prompts share word for word, one {{define}} each,
    which a judge prompt includes with {{template}}. Every judge prompt
    (UsesShared) is parsed with it, resolved as a prompt is: <prompts_dir>/
    judge-shared.md when that file exists, else the embedded copy, and in the
    daemon the copy its snapshot loaded at startup. ResolvePrompt refuses the
    name itself.

const SkillCopyName = "SKILL.md"
    SkillCopyName is the file name of a judge skill's startup copy (<skill
    dir>/<first 12 hex of its SHA-256>/SKILL.md).

const StakesMax = 300
    StakesMax bounds a stakes line ([[repo]] or [[watch]] stakes), in
    characters: one line the judge reads with every prompt.


VARIABLES

var (
	FactoryStageTypes = []string{FactoryStageAgents, FactoryStageGate, FactoryStageReview, FactoryStageDecision, FactoryStageEffect, FactoryStageQA}
	FactoryEndFacts   = []string{FactoryEndFindings, FactoryEndReport, FactoryEndCritic, FactoryEndProof, FactoryEndClean, FactoryEndPRBody, FactoryEndPR, FactoryEndQA}
	FactoryGates      = []string{FactoryGateNoOpenQuestions, FactoryGateReproduced}
	FactoryDecisions  = []string{FactoryDecisionReadyPush}
	FactoryEffects    = []string{FactoryEffectPublish}
)
    FactoryStageTypes, FactoryEndFacts, FactoryGates, FactoryDecisions and
    FactoryEffects list what a stage may name, in the order the docs give.

var BadgeColors = []string{"red", "green", "yellow", "blue", "magenta", "cyan", "gray", "grey"}
    BadgeColors are the colors a badge may ask for: the board's ANSI colors.

var DefaultFactoryBrowsers = []string{
	"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome",
	"/Applications/Chromium.app/Contents/MacOS/Chromium",
}
    DefaultFactoryBrowsers are the browsers the factory starts for QA when
    [factory] browser names none: the first that exists.

var ErrPromptNotFound = errors.New("prompt not found")
    ErrPromptNotFound: a prompt name exists neither in prompts_dir nor among the
    embedded defaults.

var ErrSharedPrompt = errors.New("holds the blocks its prompts share and is not a prompt of its own")
    ErrSharedPrompt means a prompt name is a partials file (SharedPrompt,
    the judge prompts', or FactorySharedPrompt, the factory prompts'), which
    holds blocks for its prompts and is never a prompt of its own.

var FactorySecondJudges = []string{FactorySecondJudgeWide, FactorySecondJudgeAlways, FactorySecondJudgeNever}
    FactorySecondJudges are the values of [factory.local_review] second_judge,
    in the order the docs give.

var JiraDoneNames = []string{"Done", "Closed", "Resolved", "Released"}
    JiraDoneNames are the status names a move's target may never have: the ones
    Jira's done category goes by. The config cannot read the site's workflow,
    so a done status of another name is refused when the move is planned (its
    transition's status category).

var PromptKinds = []string{PromptInitial, PromptRereview, PromptRestart, PromptContinue, PromptRecovery, PromptNudge, PromptOwnPass}
    PromptKinds lists every prompt kind a role may name (Role.PromptFile).

var StagingBranchPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^staging-[a-z0-9-]+$`)
    StagingBranchPattern is what a [[factory.repo.staging]] branch must match:
    a deploy (R46) pushes only to a staging-<name> branch.

var TrivialDeltaClasses = []string{"comments", "whitespace", "docs", "base", "empty"}
    TrivialDeltaClasses are the values of skip_trivial_deltas: a push that only
    changes comment lines, only whitespace (blank lines, re-indented code where
    indentation carries no meaning), only documentation files, or only merges
    the base branch (or rebases onto it) and leaves the PR's own diff against
    its base as it was (base), or consists of commits that change no file,
    an empty commit to re-run CI (empty).


FUNCTIONS

func AutofixStarts(v string) bool
    AutofixStarts reports whether autofix value v starts fix loops by itself
    (AutofixOwn or AutofixOpen).

func DefaultCriticModel(kind string) string
    DefaultCriticModel is the critic's model of a kind the config names without
    choosing a model: fable, the strongest Claude model (a second opinion on the
    curator's work), for claude, and "" for every other kind, whose CLI would
    not know a Claude model name.

func DefaultFactoryKinds() map[string]FactoryKind
    DefaultFactoryKinds are the built-in kinds of task. They differ in what
    investigates (the bug's reproducer, cause and history, the feature's points,
    read by fx-points and its Codex twin, the chore's scope) and in the bug's
    gate on a reproduction; the rest is the same: a judge, a critic for every
    plan (fx-critic for a wide one, fx-critic-narrow for a narrow one), one
    batch of questions, the writer, the local review, visual QA of the change's
    pages (a repository without [factory.repo.qa] skips it), the PR body,
    your decision, and the publish that only the decision leads to.

func DefaultKinds() map[string]Kind
    DefaultKinds returns the built-in kinds (fresh copies):

      - codex (0.160): args ["--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox"],
        resume ["resume","{session}"], model ["--model","{model}"],
        effort ["-c","model_reasoning_effort={effort}"],
        rename "/rename {title}", login_check "codex login status"
        + login_ok "text:Logged in", mcp_off true with mcp_strict
        ["-c","features.apps=false", "-c","skills.include_instructions=false"]
        and mcp_disable ["-c","mcp_servers.{server}.enabled=false"],
        project_untrust ["-c","projects={projects}"], project_docs_off
        ["-c","project_doc_max_bytes=0"], project_mcp "off", tool_output_limit
        65536 with tool_output ["-c","tool_output_token_limit={limit}"].
      - claude: args ["--dangerously-skip-permissions"], resume
        ["--resume","{session}"], model ["--model","{model}"], effort
        ["--effort","{effort}"], name ["--name","{title}"], login_check
        "claude auth status" + login_ok "json:loggedIn", switch_model "/model
        {model}", fallback_models ["opus","sonnet"], reset_model "default",
        project_untrust ["--setting-sources","user"], mcp_off true with
        mcp_strict ["--strict-mcp-config"], exit_keys ["/","e","x","i",
        "t","enter"], context_pattern DefaultClaudeContextPattern.
      - droid (0.232): resume ["--resume","{session}"]; no model, effort or name
        flag in interactive mode, no login check.
      - omp (18.4): resume ["--resume={session}"], model ["--model={model}"],
        effort ["--thinking={effort}"]; no login check.

    All use wrapper "auto", session_source "herdr", on_permission_prompt
    "deny", on_hooks_review "trust_own", project_mcp "allow" (codex: "off"),
    DefaultAfterDenyPrompt and DefaultHealthPatterns. The codex and claude args
    make a plain binary run without approval prompts and (codex) without its
    sandbox, as the user's zsh wrappers do: review agents run tests and `gh`,
    and magnum answers every approval prompt No. Args apply only without a
    wrapper, so a wrapper's own flags are never doubled.

func DefaultLearnModel(kind string) string
    DefaultLearnModel is the [learn] model of a kind the config names without
    choosing a model: sonnet for claude, the cheap model the retro was written
    for, and "" for every other kind, which then runs on its own default model
    (a Claude model name passed to another CLI fails every PR's retro).

func DefaultRelatedIgnore() []string
    DefaultRelatedIgnore is [pipeline] related_ignore's default: lockfiles,
    which most dependency changes touch whatever else they do.

func Issue(title string, trackers []Tracker) (key, url string)
    Issue finds the first issue key in title that one of trackers knows
    (leftmost; at one position, the earlier tracker) and returns the key
    ("PS-38553") and its URL; "" and "" when there is none.

func LocalHost(host string) bool
    LocalHost reports whether host (a URL's hostname, without brackets or a
    port) names this Mac: localhost, a name under .localhost, 127.0.0.1 or ::1,
    case ignored.

func MatchPath(glob, name string) bool
    MatchPath reports whether the "/"-separated name matches glob.
    A "**" segment matches zero or more whole segments; every other segment
    is matched with path.Match, so "*" and "?" never cross a "/". Matching
    is case-sensitive (git paths are). A malformed glob matches nothing;
    see ValidatePathGlob.

func MigrationFolder(path string) (folder string, ok bool)
    MigrationFolder is the folder of path, a file relative to the checkout as
    git names it, and whether path is a migration: a file at any depth in a
    migration folder (as Rails' migrator loads a folder's migrations) whose
    name is a version, "_", a name and .rb; its folder is the migration folder,
    never a subfolder of it (db/migrate/archive/<version>_x.rb is db/migrate's).
    A migration folder is a db directory's child whose name holds
    "migrate", the root's or an engine's (db/migrate, db/sharded_migrate,
    engines/billing/db/migrate), but never one under a spec or test
    directory (spec/db/reporting_migrate holds the specs of migrations).
    internal/staging's isMigration is a copy of this rule (that package does
    not import config), and a test there pins the two to the same answers;
    this one also names the folder.

func ParseDuration(s string) (time.Duration, error)
    ParseDuration is time.ParseDuration plus a leading whole-day count: "7d",
    "30d", "1d12h". A day is 24 hours.

func ParseTemplate(name, text, shared string) (*template.Template, error)
    ParseTemplate parses a prompt or command template the way magnum renders
    it (internal/agents.RenderPrompt), without executing it: no funcs,
    missingkey=error, and shared (a prompt's Prompt.Shared; "" for none)
    parsed first as its own template, named for its partials file (PartialsOf:
    SharedPrompt for a judge prompt, FactorySharedPrompt for a factory one),
    so that text's {{template}} calls find its blocks, a block text defines
    itself replaces the shared one, and an error in the shared text names the
    file it is in.

func PartialsOf(name string) string
    PartialsOf is the partials file the prompt named name is parsed with:
    SharedPrompt for a judge prompt (UsesShared), FactorySharedPrompt for a
    factory prompt (factory-*.md), "" for any other prompt and for the two
    partials files themselves.

func QuietHoursLabel(spec string, at time.Time) string
    QuietHoursLabel is the quiet-hours window spec (ParseQuietHours) as an
    author anywhere can read it: both clocks as HH:MM and at's offset from UTC
    ("03:00-12:00 UTC+3", "01:00-07:00 UTC-2:30", "22:00-06:00 UTC"). "" when
    spec is blank or invalid.

func RenderAutoApproveBody(tmpl string, d AutoApproveData) (string, error)
    RenderAutoApproveBody renders an auto_approve_body template with d (Short
    filled from SHA when empty), trimmed.

func RenderFooter(tmpl string, d FooterData) (string, error)
    RenderFooter renders footer template tmpl with d, trimmed ("" = the footer
    is left out).

func RoleSkillPath(r Role, layout paths.Layout) string
    RoleSkillPath is the skill of r, a judge or a fix role, as SkillPath names
    a judge's. A fix role's falls back to the fix skill instead: the checkout's
    DefaultFixSkill when its skill is "" (Load leaves "" for a {{repo}} path
    without a checkout), and EmbeddedFixSkill where a judge gets EmbeddedSkill.

func SessionArgOK(id string) bool
    SessionArgOK reports whether a session id may go into a resume's args,
    a row or a file's name: 1 to 256 bytes of letters, digits and . _ : @ + = -,
    the first a letter or a digit (a leading "=" is zsh's EQUALS expansion in a
    pasted line). No "/", "\" or glob character: the readers name a transcript
    or a rollout by the id, which must not climb out of the agent's own
    directory nor match another session's file. An id an agent's hook planted
    (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--settings=x.json`) would be read as a
    flag after `--resume` or as an option of `codex resume`, which takes the id
    as a positional argument and has no "=" form; such an id is never passed.

func SkillPath(skill string, layout paths.Layout) string
    SkillPath is a judge's skill as a round names it: skill with {{repo}}
    replaced by layout's checkout, or layout.Skill() when skill is ""; the
    embedded skill (EmbeddedSkill) when either needs a checkout the layout lacks
    (Load expands {{repo}} and ~ already; Defaults keeps them).

func TOMLString(s string) string
    TOMLString renders s as a TOML basic string.

func UsesShared(name string) bool
    UsesShared reports whether the prompt named name is a judge prompt
    (judge-*.md, the learn editor's glob), which is parsed with SharedPrompt;
    SharedPrompt itself is not.

func ValidatePathGlob(glob string) error
    ValidatePathGlob checks a skip_paths entry: it must not be blank,
    no segment may be empty (a leading, trailing or doubled "/" would silently
    match nothing), every segment must be a well-formed path.Match pattern,
    and "**" is only allowed as a whole segment ("a**b" is rejected).


TYPES

type AutoApproveData struct {
	SHA       string // the approved commit: the head magnum reviewed
	Short     string // its first 7 characters
	ReviewURL string // magnum's review the approval follows ("" when unknown)
	Repo      string // owner/name
	Number    int    // the PR's number
}
    AutoApproveData is what an auto_approve_body template renders with.

type BadgeSpec struct {
	Text  string
	Color string // BadgeColors; "" = the terminal's (an emoji keeps its own)
}
    BadgeSpec is one badge: its text and, optionally, its color.

func (b *BadgeSpec) UnmarshalTOML(v any) error
    UnmarshalTOML reads a badge written as a text or as { text, color }.

type Board struct {
	// Badges map a GitHub label to what the board shows for it: a text
	// ({ "Flagged" = "🚩" }) or a text with a color ({ "Schema Migration" =
	// { text = "\uf1c0", color = "yellow" } }). The badge goes before the
	// title, the card shows it with the label, the summary counts it. A key
	// matches a label whatever their case and leading emoji or symbols
	// ("Flagged" matches "🚩 Flagged").
	Badges map[string]BadgeSpec `toml:"badges"`
	// Trackers link a PR to its issue: URL templates with {num} right after
	// the issue key's prefix ("https://linear.app/example/issue/DMA-{num}",
	// "https://example.atlassian.net/browse/PS-{num}"). The first issue key
	// of any of them in a PR's title ("[PS-38553] …") names the issue: t on
	// the board opens it, the card shows it. A [[watch]] or [[repo]] block's
	// trackers win for its PRs (Config.TrackersFor).
	Trackers []string `toml:"trackers"`
	// RecentClosed is how long a merged or closed PR stays on the board, in
	// its own section after the open PRs (merged_at, else closed_at, within
	// it); 0 turns the section off. `magnum tui --all` lists every closed PR
	// whatever it says.
	RecentClosed Duration `toml:"recent_closed"`
	// Shimmer slides a rainbow across the state cell of a PR magnum approved
	// that GitHub still blocks on the operator's approval ("✔ needs you",
	// "✔ lift your ✗") while one is on screen; false keeps it still. A
	// terminal without colors (NO_COLOR) shows it in reverse video either way.
	Shimmer bool `toml:"shimmer"`
	// OwnPRs says where your own open PRs are listed: OwnPRsBoard (the
	// default) keeps them on the PR board, each marked with its autofix =
	// "open" verdict; OwnPRsFactory lists them on the factory screen alone
	// (beside its tasks) and the board leaves them out of its open PRs (a
	// draft, which the factory screen does not list, and a closed one
	// stay). "" is the default.
	OwnPRs string `toml:"own_prs"`
}
    Board tunes the PR board ([board]).

type Config struct {
	Daemon     Daemon     `toml:"daemon"`
	Herdr      Herdr      `toml:"herdr"`
	Terminal   Terminal   `toml:"terminal"`
	GitHub     GitHub     `toml:"github"`
	Pipeline   Pipeline   `toml:"pipeline"`
	Usage      Usage      `toml:"usage"`
	Triage     Triage     `toml:"triage"`
	Learn      Learn      `toml:"learn"`
	Notes      Notes      `toml:"notes"`
	Board      Board      `toml:"board"`
	Webhooks   Webhooks   `toml:"webhooks"`
	Jira       Jira       `toml:"jira"`
	Staging    Staging    `toml:"staging"`
	Factory    Factory    `toml:"factory"`
	Identities []Identity `toml:"identity"`
	Watches    []Watch    `toml:"watch"`
	Pools      []Pool     `toml:"pool"`
	Repos      []Repo     `toml:"repo"`

	// Kinds are the agent CLIs ([kinds.<name>]) and Roles the review
	// pipeline ([[role]]). After Load or Defaults both hold the merged,
	// normalized result: built-in defaults, then the base
	// (config.defaults.toml or a file), then the user config. Read them
	// through KindSpec, RolesFor, JudgeFor and RoleByNameOrAlias.
	Kinds map[string]Kind `toml:"kinds"`
	Roles []Role          `toml:"role"`
	// SpendLevels are the [spend.<level>] tables, by level name, then role
	// name: the keys a level of [pipeline] spend sets on a role, a review
	// [[role]] or a [[factory.role]]. A level that is not low, medium or
	// high is the operator's own. Load merges the user config's tables into
	// the base's level by level, role by role and key by key, and Roles and
	// Factory.Roles already hold the active level's keys (applySpend).
	SpendLevels map[string]map[string]SpendRole `toml:"spend"`

	// Layout is filled by Load; it is not part of the file.
	Layout paths.Layout `toml:"-"`
	// Sources are what Load read, base first: a file, or BuiltinDefaults,
	// then the user layer when there was one.
	Sources []string `toml:"-"`

	// Has unexported fields.
}

func Defaults() *Config
    Defaults returns the built-in defaults (Kinds and Roles normalized, {{repo}}
    paths unexpanded); Load overlays the file on top.

func Load(layout paths.Layout, file string) (*Config, error)
    Load reads the configuration (see LoadWithOptions) with the zero
    LoadOptions.

func LoadWithOptions(layout paths.Layout, file string, opts LoadOptions) (*Config, error)
    LoadWithOptions reads the configuration in two layers and validates it.

    The base is file (or $MAGNUM_CONFIG): a complete configuration replacing
    the built-in defaults; else a config.toml in the layout's home (a checkout
    from before the defaults were built in); else the built-in defaults,
    the repository's config.defaults.toml embedded in the binary.

    The user layer goes over it unless opts.NoOverlay: the layout's UserConfig
    (~/.config/magnum/config.toml) when it exists. It appends [[identity]],
    [[watch]], [[pool]] and [[repo]], and overrides keys (see applyOverlay).
    cfg.Sources lists what was read.

func (c *Config) AllFixerLogins() []string
    AllFixerLogins is the union of every watch's FixerLogins, each login once
    (any case, with or without "[bot]").

func (c *Config) AllRoles() []Role
    AllRoles returns every declared role in [[role]] order, the judges held
    in reserve and the fix and whiteboard roles included (RolesFor leaves them
    out): what names a role on the command line, lists roles, or copies the
    configuration.

func (c *Config) AllowsBotAuthor(fullName, login string) bool
    AllowsBotAuthor reports whether allow_bot_authors lets repository fullName's
    ("owner/name") PRs by login through skip_bot_authors: the covering watch's
    list or the repository's [[repo]] block's names login, in any case, with
    or without "[bot]" (github.SameLogin, so a bot's GraphQL login "helper" is
    helper[bot]). A blank login matches nothing. Whether login is a bot is the
    caller's business: the list only lifts the bot rule.

func (c *Config) AutoApproveAllowsAuthor(fullName, login string) bool
    AutoApproveAllowsAuthor reports whether auto_approve_authors lets magnum
    approve repository fullName's ("owner/name") PRs by login as the operator:
    the repository's [[repo]] list when it is set (non-empty), which replaces
    the watch's there, else the covering watch's when it is set, names login
    in any case, with or without "[bot]" (as AutoApproveSkipsAuthor matches).
    With neither list set there is no allowlist: true for every login.
    A blank login is on no list. It does not ask the skip list, which wins:
    the engine asks AutoApproveSkipsAuthor first.

func (c *Config) AutoApproveBodyFor(fullName string) string
    AutoApproveBodyFor is the approval body template of repository fullName's
    PRs: its watch's auto_approve_body, trimmed, else DefaultAutoApproveBody.

func (c *Config) AutoApproveFor(fullName string) *Identity
    AutoApproveFor is the identity magnum auto-approves repository fullName's
    ("owner/name") PRs as: the covering watch's auto_approve_as when its
    auto_approve names the repository, or "*"; nil otherwise.

func (c *Config) AutoApproveRefusesAuthor(fullName, login string) bool
    AutoApproveRefusesAuthor reports whether the author lists keep
    magnum from approving repository fullName's PRs by login on its own:
    auto_approve_skip_authors names login (AutoApproveSkipsAuthor), or an
    auto_approve_authors that applies does not (AutoApproveAllowsAuthor). The
    automatic approval asks each list to say why (the engine's authorRefusal);
    the judge's no-findings event asks this (pipeline.JudgeEvents), so a clean
    review of such an author is no approval either. A nil c refuses nobody.

func (c *Config) AutoApproveSkipsAuthor(fullName, login string) bool
    AutoApproveSkipsAuthor reports whether auto_approve_skip_authors keeps
    magnum from approving repository fullName's ("owner/name") PRs by login as
    the operator: the covering watch's list or the repository's [[repo]] block's
    names login, in any case, with or without "[bot]" (as skip_authors matches).
    A blank login matches nothing.

func (c *Config) AutoApproves() bool
    AutoApproves reports whether any watch auto-approves a repository.

func (c *Config) AutofixFor(w *Watch) string
    AutofixFor is the autofix that applies to w's PRs: the watch's when it sets
    one, else [pipeline]'s, else AutofixNever. A nil w is [pipeline]'s.

func (c *Config) BaseFile() string
    BaseFile is the base configuration Load read in place of the built-in
    defaults (its file argument, $MAGNUM_CONFIG or a checkout's config.toml);
    "" when it read the built-in defaults. Loading again with it and the same
    layout reads the same layers.

func (c *Config) BaseRole(name string) (Role, bool)
    BaseRole is the role named name as the layers set it (the built-in role,
    the base configuration's and the user config's [[role]] blocks), before any
    spend level: its model is the one a level whose table does not name the role
    runs. False for a name no role has, or a configuration Load did not build.

func (c *Config) CIDispatch(fullName string) string
    CIDispatch returns the workflow file the [[repo]] block of repository
    fullName ("owner/name", any case) names as the one that produces its
    required checks (ci_dispatch), "" when none does: autofix = "open" starts
    it once per head on an own PR whose required check did not run at its head,
    and the engine 2 minutes after each push it made to a PR.

func (c *Config) CIDispatchAs(fullName string) string
    CIDispatchAs returns the identity the [[repo]] block of repository fullName
    ("owner/name", any case) names to start its CIDispatch workflow and to
    re-run a run of an own PR's head that started no job (ci_dispatch_as),
    "" when none does: the look does both as the watch's poll identity, else its
    identity.

func (c *Config) CommentIdentity(fullName string) (*Watch, *Identity, error)
    CommentIdentity is the watch that covers repository fullName
    ("owner/name") and the identity `magnum comment` posts on its PRs as:
    the watch's fix_identity, which must be a GitHub App of the fixer's own
    (DedicatedFixApp) whose tokens reach the repository (token_repositories).
    The identity is a copy whose Login is in Account form (with its "[bot]",
    which the config may leave out): the author GitHub must show. It never
    falls back to another identity (FixRoleFor's fix role or poll identity,
    the operator's gh login): each refusal names the key to set.

func (c *Config) CommentsWhenClean(repo, identity, author string) bool
    CommentsWhenClean reports whether the identity named identity posts
    a comment, not an approval, for a clean verdict on repository
    repo ("owner/name") on a PR by author: VerdictsFor's no-findings
    event is COMMENT, or the auto-approval author lists refuse author
    (AutoApproveRefusesAuthor), which turns the judge's APPROVE into COMMENT
    (pipeline.JudgeEvents).

func (c *Config) CriticRole() Role
    CriticRole is the role the critic runs as: CriticRoleName, the [notes]
    critic_kind in session mode with its model, effort, args, prompt, timeout
    and fallback models, normalized like a configured role.

func (c *Config) DaemonMintsActions(name string) bool
    DaemonMintsActions reports whether the daemon makes the Actions calls as the
    identity named name (ci_dispatch_as: the start of ci_dispatch's workflow,
    the re-run of a run that started no job, the reads of runs and jobs;
    engine ci_actions.go) over a token of its own with Actions write added, not
    over the identity's own tokens: name is a dedicated App (DedicatedFixApp)
    whose token_permissions are set and name no actions at all, as the fixer
    rule keeps a fixer App's (fixerAppProblem: contents and pull_requests write
    alone, which its panes hold), so its own tokens can never use Actions
    and the operator cannot add it. Neither half is exact alone: a dedicated
    App need not have a fixer's scope (it may read Actions), and an App whose
    token_permissions leave actions out may be one a watch reviews or polls as,
    which the engine falls back to without ci_dispatch_as. Every other App keeps
    the scope the operator chose for its own tokens, which a mint with Actions
    write would widen, and which GitHub answers with 422 where the installation
    grants Actions read alone; an App without token_permissions has its
    installation's whole access.

func (c *Config) DedicatedFixApp(name string) bool
    DedicatedFixApp reports whether the identity named name is a GitHub App
    the fixer may act as: kind app, and no watch reviews as it (identity),
    polls as it (poll_identity) or approves as it (auto_approve_as), by its name
    or through another App block of the same login. The App magnum reviews as
    never is: the fixer's replies would read as magnum's own and its rebuttals
    would count as magnum's.

func (c *Config) EditorRole() Role
    EditorRole is the role the skill editor runs as: EditorRoleName, the
    [learn] editor_kind in session mode with its editor_model, editor_effort,
    editor_args, editor_prompt, editor_timeout and editor_fallback_models,
    writing changes.json, normalized like a configured role.

func (c *Config) FactoryHerdr() herdr.Session
    FactoryHerdr is the herdr session of the factory's panes: [factory]
    herdr_session, on [factory] herdr_socket, else on that session's own socket
    (herdr.SessionSocket; herdr's default session, "default", keeps herdr's
    default socket).

func (c *Config) FactoryRepo(full string) (FactoryRepo, bool)
    FactoryRepo returns the [[factory.repo]] for owner/name (case ignored).

func (c *Config) FactoryRole(name string) (Role, bool)
    FactoryRole returns the factory role named name (an exact name: a factory
    role takes no alias).

func (c *Config) FixCyclesFor(w *Watch) int
    FixCyclesFor is the fix_cycles that apply to w's PRs: the watch's when it
    sets one, else [pipeline]'s, else DefaultFixCycles. A nil w is [pipeline]'s.

func (c *Config) FixRoleFor(w *Watch) (Role, bool)
    FixRoleFor is the fix role of watch w: the watch's fix_role when it sets
    one (an empty one switches the fix job off for the watch), else [pipeline]
    fix_role, found among every declared role (not only the watch's). ok is
    false when none is set or the name matches no fix role; Validate reports the
    latter. The role acts as w's fix_identity when the watch sets one; else a
    fix role that names no identity acts as w's poll identity (its identity when
    it has no poll_identity, as Normalize sets it): the operator's own gh login
    in a `magnum init` config, which polls as it. Without a watch the identity
    stays the role's.

func (c *Config) FixRoleName(w *Watch) string
    FixRoleName is the fix_role that applies to w: the watch's when it sets one,
    else [pipeline]'s ("" = no fix job). FixRoleFor resolves it.

func (c *Config) FixRoles() []Role
    FixRoles returns every declared fix role in [[role]] order: the built-in
    claude-fix, and the fix roles a configuration adds for the watches whose
    fix_role names them (FixRoleFor).

func (c *Config) FixerLogins(w *Watch) []string
    FixerLogins are the logins the fixer of w's PRs posts as that are not the
    PR author's: the login of a dedicated App (DedicatedFixApp) the fix role
    acts as (FixRoleFor), none for a gh fixer, which acts as the operator,
    the author of the PRs it fixes, or for a watch without a fix job.

func (c *Config) IdentityByName(name string) *Identity
    IdentityByName returns the identity or nil.

func (c *Config) IgnoreChecks(fullName string) []string
    IgnoreChecks returns the checks magnum treats as absent wherever it reads
    the CI of repository fullName's PRs: the covering watch's ignore_checks and,
    added to them, the [[repo]] block's (nil when neither sets any). Entries
    are check-name globs and "workflow:<glob>", matched as required_checks' are
    (store.RequiredNames); store.SeenCI and store.PR.IgnoringChecks leave the
    checks they name out. The list is a copy when both set some.

func (c *Config) JudgeFallbackFor(w *Watch) (Role, bool)
    JudgeFallbackFor is the judge role that takes over a PR of watch w (nil:
    a PR no watch covers) after its judge's kind refused a round: the watch's
    judge_fallback, else [pipeline] judge_fallback, found among every declared
    role (not only the watch's). ok is false when none is set or the name
    matches no judge role; Validate reports the latter for a value a file
    writes. The built-in default (DefaultJudgeFallback, which no file wrote) is
    off instead wherever Validate would refuse it for w: a base configuration
    whose own [[role]] list has no claude-judge, a watch whose judge is
    claude-judge or of its kind.

func (c *Config) JudgeFallbackName(w *Watch) string
    JudgeFallbackName is the name of the fallback judge that resolves for w
    (JudgeFallbackFor), "" for none: what `magnum roles` and the settings screen
    show.

func (c *Config) JudgeFor(w *Watch) Role
    JudgeFor returns the watch's judge (validation guarantees exactly one);
    the zero Role when there is none.

func (c *Config) JudgeOwnPassFor(w *Watch) string
    JudgeOwnPassFor is the judge_own_pass that applies to w's PRs: the watch's
    when it sets one, else [pipeline]'s, else OwnPassParallel.

func (c *Config) Judges() []Role
    Judges returns every declared judge role in [[role]] order: the first is
    the judge of a watch without a roles list, the others stand in reserve
    (JudgeFallbackFor) or serve the watches whose roles name them.

func (c *Config) KeepApprovals(fullName string) bool
    KeepApprovals reports whether an App identity's approval on a PR of
    repository fullName stays when the PR gets new commits: the [[repo]]
    block's keep_approvals when set, else the covering watch's (default false:
    magnum dismisses it until the re-review posts).

func (c *Config) KindNames() []string
    KindNames lists the declared kinds, sorted.

func (c *Config) KindSpec(name string) (Kind, bool)
    KindSpec returns the merged [kinds.<name>] spec (user keys over
    DefaultKinds); false for "shell" and undeclared names.

func (c *Config) LearnRole() Role
    LearnRole is the role the retro's classifying agent runs as: LearnRoleName,
    the [learn] kind in session mode with its model, effort, args, prompt,
    timeout and fallback models, writing retro.json, normalized like a
    configured role.

func (c *Config) MagnumThreadLogins() []string
    MagnumThreadLogins are the logins whose review threads magnum's review
    started, in Account form, each once: every watch's posting identity
    (the operator's gh login too, in a config that posts as it) and every
    App identity, whatever it is for (a former reviewer's identity is a
    declared one). A comment of magnum's own in such a thread answers nothing:
    the daemon's poll, which reads no comment text, takes the fixer App's reply
    there for the author's.

func (c *Config) MaxSimplificationsFor(fullName string) int
    MaxSimplificationsFor is how many simplifications the judge posts
    at most on a PR of repository fullName ("owner/name"): the [[repo]]
    block's max_simplifications when set (above 0), else [pipeline]'s, else
    DefaultMaxSimplifications (a nil config, or one built in code without the
    key).

func (c *Config) Normalize()
    Normalize fills the defaulted fields of Kinds and Roles in place (Load
    and Defaults call it; call it again after editing either in code). It is
    idempotent and never overrides a value that is set.

func (c *Config) NotesRole() Role
    NotesRole is the role the curator runs as: NotesRoleName, the [notes] kind
    in session mode with its model, effort, args, prompt, timeout and fallback
    models, normalized like a configured role.

func (c *Config) OperatorIdentity(w Watch) *Identity
    OperatorIdentity is the gh identity of the operator's own account for
    watch w: the login whose review requests start a round, whose PRs count as
    self-authored and whom the review footer names. It is w's poll identity
    when that is a gh identity (its identity when it has no poll_identity, as
    Normalize sets it), else w's auto_approve_as when that names a gh identity,
    else the first gh identity declared; nil when the config declares none.
    An App that polls is never the operator: GitHub offers no bot as a reviewer,
    and its login authors no one's PRs.

func (c *Config) OperatorLogin(w Watch) string
    OperatorLogin is OperatorIdentity's login, "" when none resolves.

func (c *Config) OwnPRsOnFactory() bool
    OwnPRsOnFactory reports whether your own open PRs are listed on the factory
    screen and not on the board ([board] own_prs = "factory").

func (c *Config) PRThreadLogins(identity string, former []string) []string
    PRThreadLogins is MagnumThreadLogins with one PR's own logins: the identity
    it posts as (a pin of `magnum review --as`, or its watch's; one no longer
    declared counts by its name) and its former identities still declared (the
    engine's KVPRFormerIdentities), as the engine's ownLogins and the threads
    file take them for magnum's on that PR.

func (c *Config) PoolFor(fullName string) *Pool
    PoolFor returns the pool for owner/name, or nil (per-PR worktree repos).

func (c *Config) PromptSnapshot() *PromptSnapshot
    PromptSnapshot returns the snapshot SnapshotPrompts installed; nil when
    prompts are read from disk (every CLI command).

func (c *Config) ReadinessFor(fullName string) Readiness
    ReadinessFor returns the readiness step of repository fullName
    ("owner/name"): each of prepare, ready and ready_timeout from its [[repo]]
    block when the block sets it, else from its [[pool]]; the timeout defaults
    to DefaultReadyTimeout.

func (c *Config) RelatedFor(w *Watch) Related
    RelatedFor is the related_lookback and related_ignore that apply to w's PRs:
    the watch's when it sets them (any lookback, "0s" included: open PRs only;
    any list, [] included), else [pipeline]'s. A nil w is [pipeline]'s.

func (c *Config) RepoFor(fullName string) *Repo
    RepoFor returns the [[repo]] block for owner/name, or nil.

func (c *Config) RequiredChecks(fullName string) []string
    RequiredChecks returns the [[repo]] block's required_checks for repository
    fullName (nil when none): check-name globs and "workflow:<glob>" entries
    that replace GitHub's list (store.Store.RequiredChecks). The automatic
    approval's CI gate counts only the checks they name; GitHub's list does not
    change it.

func (c *Config) ResolvePrompt(name string) (Prompt, error)
    ResolvePrompt reads a prompt by name: <pipeline.prompts_dir>/<name> when
    that file exists, else the embedded default of the same name; an unknown
    name wraps ErrPromptNotFound. Names are plain file names (no directories).
    A judge prompt (UsesShared) comes with the partials file (Prompt.Shared),
    resolved the same way, and a factory prompt with the factory's (PartialsOf);
    a partials file's own name wraps ErrSharedPrompt. In the daemon, which
    loaded its prompts at startup (SnapshotPrompts), a name the snapshot holds
    resolves to the text loaded then, whatever the file holds now, and so does
    the partials file.

func (c *Config) ReviewHerdr() herdr.Session
    ReviewHerdr is the herdr session of magnum's review panes: yours while
    herdr review_session is "", else that session, on herdr review_socket or
    the session's own socket (herdr.SessionSocket: "default" is herdr's default
    session on its default socket).

func (c *Config) RoleByNameOrAlias(w *Watch, s string) (Role, bool)
    RoleByNameOrAlias finds one of the watch's roles by name or alias (case and
```
