    surrounding space ignored, so stored ids such as codex_review match too);
    "" is the watch's judge.

func (c *Config) RoleEnv(r Role) map[string]string
    RoleEnv is the pane environment of a role: its kind's env (the Tool's for
    shell roles) overlaid by the role's env.

func (c *Config) RoleModel(r Role) string
    RoleModel is the model a role's sessions are configured to run: the role's
    own model, else its kind's default_model ("" = the CLI's default; a shell
    role: its own model only).

func (c *Config) RolePrompt(r Role, kind string) (Prompt, error)
    RolePrompt resolves the role's prompt of a prompt kind (see PromptFile);
    a role without one wraps ErrPromptNotFound.

func (c *Config) RolesAtLevel(level string) []Role
    RolesAtLevel is every role as it resolves when its spend level is level,
    whatever the kinds' and [pipeline] spend name: the level's notch mapping
    and its [spend.<level>] table applied to the roles as the layers set them
    (applySpend). nil for a configuration Load did not build.

func (c *Config) RolesFor(w *Watch) []Role
    RolesFor returns the roles a watch runs, in [[role]] order: every role
    when w is nil or w.Roles is empty, else the ones w.Roles names (names or
    aliases). A fix or whiteboard role is never one of them (FixRoleFor and
    WhiteboardRoleFor find them), and when w names no roles only the first judge
    is, the others standing in reserve.

func (c *Config) SelfLogins() []string
    SelfLogins are the logins that count as the operator's own (the board's
    "mine", ★): every watch's posting identity and every gh identity (the user),
    each once (textx.FoldLogin tells them apart).

func (c *Config) SelfMatch() func(login string) bool
    SelfMatch returns a test of whether a login is one of SelfLogins
    (textx.FoldLogin: case, "@" and "[bot]" do not matter).

func (c *Config) SkillFile(src string) string
    SkillFile is the file a judge or fix prompt names for the skill at src
    (SkillPath, RoleSkillPath): its startup copy when the daemon's snapshot
    holds one, else src itself.

func (c *Config) SnapshotPrompts(skillDir string, now time.Time, extra ...string) (*PromptSnapshot, error)
    SnapshotPrompts loads every prompt file the roles name (each prompt kind),
    the extra names (model-fallback.md) and the partials file of each
    prompt among them (PartialsOf: SharedPrompt with a judge prompt,
    FactorySharedPrompt with a factory prompt), copies each judge's and
    each fix role's skill file (RoleSkillPath) to skillDir/<hash>/SKILL.md
    ("" = no copies; the roles keep their configured skill paths), removes
    copies older than a week that no role uses, and installs the result:
    from now on ResolvePrompt answers from it and SkillFile names the copies.
    A prompt that does not resolve is an error and nothing is installed; a skill
    that cannot be copied is a warning (PromptSnapshot.Warnings). Call it once,
    before the goroutines that resolve prompts start.

func (c *Config) SpendLevel(kind string) string
    SpendLevel is the spend level of the roles whose agent kind (Role.AgentKind)
    is kind: the kind's own spend ([kinds.<name>] spend), else [pipeline] spend,
    SpendMedium when neither names one. A shell role without a tool (kind "")
    and an undeclared kind take [pipeline] spend.

func (c *Config) Stages(w *Watch) [][]Role
    Stages orders the watch's roles for a round: non-judge roles layered by
    After (a stage holds the roles whose dependencies all ran in earlier stages;
    dependencies outside the watch's set are ignored), then the judge alone.
    Validation guarantees After is acyclic.

func (c *Config) Stagings(repo string) []FactoryStaging
    Stagings returns the staging environments of the [[factory.repo]] for
    owner/name (case ignored), in the order the block lists them: a copy,
    nil when no block or no entry names one.

func (c *Config) StakesFor(fullName string) string
    StakesFor returns what repository fullName ("owner/name") puts at risk,
    as the operator states it: the [[repo]] block's stakes when set, else the
    covering watch's; "" when neither says. The judge sizes each harm against it
    (the `stakes` field of its prompts).

func (c *Config) StatusCommentFor(w *Watch) bool
    StatusCommentFor reports whether the review status comment is on for
    watch w: the watch's status_comment when it sets one, else [pipeline]
    status_comment. A nil w is [pipeline]'s.

func (c *Config) ThrottleFor(w *Watch) Daemon
    ThrottleFor is the [daemon] section with w's burst, re-review delta,
    delta check and own PR interval overrides applied: the throttle settings
    (eligibility.Throttle) of w's PRs. A nil w is the daemon's.

func (c *Config) TrackersFor(fullName string) []Tracker
    TrackersFor returns the issue trackers of repository fullName's PRs:
    the [[repo]] block's, then the covering [[watch]]'s, then [board]'s,
    each issue key prefix taken from the first of them that names it. So one
    owner's "PR-" may lead to Linear while every other owner's leads to Jira.
    Templates that do not parse are left out (Validate reports them).

func (c *Config) TrivialDeltas(w *Watch) []string
    TrivialDeltas is the skip_trivial_deltas that applies to w's PRs:
    the watch's when it sets one, else the daemon's. Empty = every push is
    re-reviewed.

func (c *Config) UserSum() ([32]byte, bool)
    UserSum is the SHA-256 of the user layer's bytes as Load read them (the
    file, or LoadOptions.UserData); false when Load read no user layer
    (no file, or LoadOptions.NoOverlay). The daemon records it at startup
    (engine.KVDaemonConfigSum), so a saved config it does not run yet is told
    apart from the one it runs by content, not by a modification time.

func (c *Config) Validate() error
    Validate checks cross references and required fields.

func (c *Config) VerdictsFor(fullName string, id *Identity) (noFindings, blocking string)
    VerdictsFor returns the review events the judge posts for repository
    fullName ("owner/name") as identity id: noFindings when it finds
    nothing (APPROVE | COMMENT), blocking when it finds a blocking issue
    (REQUEST_CHANGES | COMMENT). Each comes from the repository's [[repo]] block
    when it sets it, else from the identity, else the default: APPROVE for a gh
    identity and COMMENT for an app or an unknown one (a bot approval must not
    unlock a merge by accident), and REQUEST_CHANGES.

func (c *Config) Warnings() []string
    Warnings lists human-readable problems that do not make the config invalid:
    zero [[identity]] or zero [[watch]] blocks are valid (the built-in defaults
    have neither; they live in the user's ~/.config/magnum/config.toml),
    but magnum then cannot post or reviews nothing; a [daemon] reviewer_timeout
    or judge_timeout set while every role it would be the fallback of sets its
    own timeout changes nothing; a watch with autofix = "own" or "open" whose
    fix job cannot run as it should (fixRoleWarnings). Print them from `magnum
    doctor` and `magnum config`.

func (c *Config) WatchFor(fullName string) *Watch
    WatchFor returns the watch that covers owner/name, or nil.

func (c *Config) WhiteboardFor(w *Watch) bool
    WhiteboardFor reports whether the whiteboard job is on for watch w:
    the watch's whiteboard when it sets one, else [pipeline] whiteboard. A nil w
    is [pipeline]'s. The job still needs a role: WhiteboardRoleFor.

func (c *Config) WhiteboardRoleFor(w *Watch) (Role, bool)
    WhiteboardRoleFor is the whiteboard role of watch w: the watch's
    whiteboard_role when it sets one (an empty one switches the whiteboard job
    off for the watch, automatic or by hand), else [pipeline] whiteboard_role,
    found among every declared role (not only the watch's). ok is false when
    none is set or the name matches no whiteboard role; Validate reports
    the latter. A whiteboard role that names no identity acts as w's poll
    identity (its identity when it has no poll_identity, as Normalize sets it):
    the operator's own gh login in a `magnum init` config, which polls as it.
    Without a watch the identity stays empty.

func (c *Config) WhiteboardRoleName(w *Watch) string
    WhiteboardRoleName is the whiteboard_role that applies to w: the
    watch's when it sets one, else [pipeline]'s ("" = no whiteboard job).
    WhiteboardRoleFor resolves it.

func (c *Config) WhiteboardRoles() []Role
    WhiteboardRoles returns every declared whiteboard role in [[role]] order:
    the built-in claude-whiteboard, and the whiteboard roles a configuration
    adds for the watches whose whiteboard_role names them (WhiteboardRoleFor).

func (c *Config) WithCandidate(dir string) (*Config, error)
    WithCandidate is the config a replay or a check of candidate dir runs with:
    a copy of c (WithoutSnapshot: read from disk, whatever the daemon loaded
    at startup) whose prompts_dir is <dir>/prompts and whose every judge reads
    <dir>/skills/magnum-review/SKILL.md, both absolute. dir is a checkout or
    a worktree of magnum with a change to the prompts or the skill (an eval
    candidate, the skill editor's worktree); a prompt it lacks resolves to the
    embedded default, as in any checkout. An error when dir has no prompts
    directory or no skill file; c is never changed.

func (c *Config) WithoutSnapshot() *Config
    WithoutSnapshot is a copy of c that reads its prompts and judge skills
    from disk, as the CLI does, whatever the daemon loaded at startup (a
    candidate replay reads another directory's), with its own Roles slice (every
    normalized role, AllRoles) for the caller to change.

func (c *Config) YourHerdr() herdr.Session
    YourHerdr is your herdr session: [terminal] session ("" = herdr's default
    session) on herdr socket. Toasts show there, and the slot guards read your
    agents there.

type CurateTriggers []string
    CurateTriggers is [notes] curate: the triggers of a curation, written as
    a list (`["over_limit", "misses"]`, `[]` for none). The earlier string
    form still reads as it meant: "over_limit" that trigger alone, "weekly"
    over_limit and weekly, "off" none.

func (c CurateTriggers) Has(t string) bool
    Has reports whether trigger t is on.

func (c CurateTriggers) String() string
    String is the list as the config writes it.

func (c *CurateTriggers) UnmarshalTOML(v any) error
    UnmarshalTOML reads a list of trigger names or one of the earlier strings.
    Values are checked by Validate.

type Daemon struct {
	PollInterval Duration `toml:"poll_interval"`
	// ObserveInterval is the review daemon's observe clock: how often it
	// reads herdr for the turns of the runs in flight, between the ticks
	// (0 = off: the tick observes alone).
	ObserveInterval          Duration `toml:"observe_interval"`
	MaxConcurrentReviews     int      `toml:"max_concurrent_reviews"`
	MaxTotalWorkingCodex     int      `toml:"max_total_working_codex"`
	PushQuietPeriod          Duration `toml:"push_quiet_period"`
	MinRereviewInterval      Duration `toml:"min_rereview_interval"`
	DraftMinRereviewInterval Duration `toml:"draft_min_rereview_interval"`
	OwnMinRereviewInterval   Duration `toml:"own_min_rereview_interval"` // MinRereviewInterval for the operator's own PRs (SelfLogins; an own draft takes the longer of it and the draft one; 0 = MinRereviewInterval; Config.ThrottleFor)
	MaxRoundsPerPRPerDay     int      `toml:"max_rounds_per_pr_per_day"`
	CloseGrace               Duration `toml:"close_grace"`
	ReviewerTimeout          Duration `toml:"reviewer_timeout"` // timeout of a non-judge role that sets none (a role's own wins; config.defaults.toml's roles set theirs)
	JudgeTimeout             Duration `toml:"judge_timeout"`    // timeout of a judge role that sets none (likewise)
	AgentStartStagger        Duration `toml:"agent_start_stagger"`
	MinWarm                  Duration `toml:"min_warm"`
	HumanCooldown            Duration `toml:"human_cooldown"`
	ReconcileInterval        Duration `toml:"reconcile_interval"`
	DefaultRepo              string   `toml:"default_repo"`
	QuietHours               string   `toml:"quiet_hours"` // "01:00-07:00" local, optional
	MinFreeDiskGB            int      `toml:"min_free_disk_gb"`
	// KeepEvents and KeepRequests are how long the daemon keeps audit events
	// and handled CLI requests (0 = forever); it prunes older rows on every
	// reconcile.
	KeepEvents   Duration `toml:"keep_events"`
	KeepRequests Duration `toml:"keep_requests"`
	// MaxRoundRestarts bounds how often one round starts its reviewers over
	// on a head pushed while they run (before the judge is prompted); later
	// pushes leave the round on the head it has. 0 = never restart.
	MaxRoundRestarts int `toml:"max_round_restarts"`
	// BurstQuietPeriod replaces PushQuietPeriod (when longer) for a PR whose
	// head changed BurstPushes times or more within BurstWindow up to its
	// last push: an author pushing in a burst gets a longer quiet period
	// before the next round. A zero value turns the rule off. A [[watch]]
	// may override each (Config.ThrottleFor).
	BurstQuietPeriod Duration `toml:"burst_quiet_period"`
	BurstPushes      int      `toml:"burst_pushes"`
	BurstWindow      Duration `toml:"burst_window"`
	// ModelLimitCooldown is how long a model that hit its own limit
	// (health pattern model_limit) counts as limited when the pane text
	// names no reset time (a limit hit again within a day of the last one's
	// end lasts twice that one's span, up to 24h: agents.RecordModelLimit);
	// sessions use their role's fallback_models, else the kind's, meanwhile.
	ModelLimitCooldown Duration `toml:"model_limit_cooldown"`
	// ParkIdleAfter parks a live agent of a reviewed or ineligible PR (a
	// draft, a mute or a skip after its review) once it has been idle this
	// long since its own last activity and the end of the PR's last round,
	// fix job or whiteboard job, whichever is later (it resumes on the PR's
	// next round); 0 = never; 15m by default. A judge role waits
	// Pipeline.JudgeFreshAfter instead when that is longer. While some agent
	// of the PR is not past its threshold, the ones past theirs that have a
	// conversation to resume are parked alone; once all are, the PR's park
	// takes them with the workspace. A PR waiting for a round is parked the
	// same way when its wait is a pause, a drain, the daily cap or ends more
	// than this far away. Pinned or held slots, PRs that need attention and
	// PRs with human activity within HumanCooldown are left alone.
	ParkIdleAfter Duration `toml:"park_idle_after"`
	// SkipTrivialDeltas are the kinds of change a push may consist of
	// without a re-review (TrivialDeltaClasses: comments, whitespace,
	// docs, base, empty; default all five, [] = re-review every push): the review
	// of the earlier commit then stands for the new head. A [[watch]] may
	// override it (Config.TrivialDeltas).
	SkipTrivialDeltas []string `toml:"skip_trivial_deltas"`
	// RequestDebounce is how long a review round waits after a review
	// request for your login (Config.OperatorIdentity) or a posting
	// identity (or a team in a watch's request_teams), or after a draft
	// became ready for review, counted from the later of that and the last
	// push. Such a requested round skips every other timing rule and the
	// daily cap; 0 = no wait.
	RequestDebounce Duration `toml:"request_debounce"`
	// ReplyDebounce is how long after the last reply on magnum's latest
	// review (the PR author's review or comment, or a reply in one of
	// magnum's threads by the author or a repository owner, member or
	// collaborator) a reviewed PR whose head has not moved waits before
	// its judge alone re-decides the threads; 0 = replies start no round.
	// ReplyMinInterval spaces such rounds of one PR and head (0 = no wait).
	// A push meanwhile wins: the re-review it gets reads the replies.
	ReplyDebounce    Duration `toml:"reply_debounce"`
	ReplyMinInterval Duration `toml:"reply_min_interval"`
	// RereviewMinLines is the smallest unreviewed delta an automatic
	// re-review runs for after the quiet period: changed lines (additions
	// plus deletions) the trivial-delta classifier counts as code, since the
	// reviewed commit (after a push that merged the base branch or rebased,
	// the change in the PR's own diff against its base). A smaller delta
	// without an added file waits for more pushes or RereviewMaxWait since
	// its first push, whichever is first.
	// 0 = no threshold. A [[watch]] may override both (Config.ThrottleFor).
	RereviewMinLines int      `toml:"rereview_min_lines"`
	RereviewMaxWait  Duration `toml:"rereview_max_wait"`
	// DeltaCheck (default true): a re-review whose delta since the reviewed
	// commit has more than 0 and fewer than RereviewMinLines changed code
	// lines and adds no file (modified binary files count 0 lines) does not
	// wait for RereviewMaxWait: after the quiet period only the judge
	// checks those commits, in its own session at its rereview_effort, and
	// an App's approval stands meanwhile (for at most an hour after the
	// push). false keeps the threshold's wait and a full round. A [[watch]]
	// may override it (Config.ThrottleFor).
	DeltaCheck bool `toml:"delta_check"`
	// RestartOnNewBuild lets the daemon restart itself on a new binary
	// on disk (the one launchd starts) once it passes its configuration
	// check: at the first tick no round is claiming, reviewing or
	// verifying, it exits for launchd to start the new build. Dispatch never
	// stops for it. Needs launchd (`magnum install`).
	RestartOnNewBuild bool `toml:"restart_on_new_build"`
	// ShellPath (default true): at its start, before it runs anything, the
	// daemon asks the operator's login shell for its PATH (`$SHELL -ilc`, 20
	// s at most) and appends the directories its own PATH lacks, which stays
	// first, so every command it starts finds the tools only the shell's
	// exports name (DBngin's MySQL, PostgreSQL and Redis). A change of the
	// shell's PATH takes effect at the next start. The CLI keeps its own
	// environment. The factory daemon takes the same PATH at its start, for
	// its copies' setup, reset and precheck commands.
	ShellPath bool `toml:"shell_path"`
	// OpenHold is how long a restore by `magnum open` (the board's o) holds
	// the PR and its slot for the operator, as a pin does: until the later
	// of the open plus OpenHold and the end of HumanCooldown after the last
	// input in the PR's panes (OpenHoldEnd), when the hold ends by itself.
	// 0 pins for good, until `magnum unpin`.
	OpenHold Duration `toml:"open_hold"`
}

func (d Daemon) CooldownUntil(at *time.Time) time.Time
    CooldownUntil is at + human_cooldown, the end of the human cooldown a PR's
    human_active_at (at: someone typed into its panes) began: the PR's prompts,
    rounds, parking and slot release wait while now is before it. Zero, which
    holds nothing, when at is nil or human_cooldown is 0.

func (d Daemon) OpenHoldEnd(until time.Time, humanAt *time.Time) time.Time
    OpenHoldEnd is when a hold `magnum open` set ends: until (the open
    plus open_hold), or the end of human_cooldown after humanAt (the PR's
    human_active_at, the last input in its panes) when that is later.

type Duration struct{ time.Duration }
    Duration is a time.Duration that unmarshals from Go syntax ("30s", "5m",
    "2h") with whole days allowed in front ("30d", "1d12h").

func (d *Duration) UnmarshalText(b []byte) error

type Factory struct {
	// MaxActive is how many tasks may have live agents or a held copy at
	// once; a task over it waits queued.
	MaxActive int `toml:"max_active"`
	// MemoryGateSwap is the swap use, in percent of the swap file, at which
	// new tasks wait for memory (the same reading as `magnum doctor`);
	// 0 = no gate.
	MemoryGateSwap int `toml:"memory_gate_swap"`
	// HeavyStages is how many heavy stages run at once across tasks (a local
	// review round, local QA or a copy's server). At least 1.
	HeavyStages int `toml:"heavy_stages"`
	// HerdrSocket is the socket of the herdr session the factory's panes
	// live in; "" = the named session's own socket. Absolute after ~
	// expands.
	HerdrSocket string `toml:"herdr_socket"`
	// HerdrSession is the name of that herdr session (`herdr --session
	// <name>`): a separate server with its own windows, apart from the
	// panes of magnum's reviews.
	HerdrSession string `toml:"herdr_session"`
	// Browser is the headless Chrome the factory starts for a qa stage, an
	// absolute path after ~ expands; "" = the first of
	// DefaultFactoryBrowsers that exists.
	Browser string `toml:"browser"`
	// DiffPager is the pager of the screen's d, the diff of a ready card
	// (GIT_PAGER, which git prefers over core.pager), such as "hunk pager";
	// "" = git's own. The card's file order stays: it is git's diff.
	DiffPager string `toml:"diff_pager"`
	// Observe is how often the factory reads its panes; Poll how often its
	// main tick runs (the holds, your requests, the published tasks' PRs as
	// magnum's registry has them, then a step of each live task); a request
	// kicks a tick at once. The factory itself reads nothing from GitHub
	// after the publish.
	Observe Duration `toml:"observe"`
	Poll    Duration `toml:"poll"`
	// HumanCooldown is how long the factory leaves a pane alone after you
	// type into it.
	HumanCooldown Duration `toml:"human_cooldown"`

	// ProvisionalLoneAnswer lets the no_open_questions gate pass on the
	// recommended option of a lone question (the only question of its batch,
	// asked after you answered an earlier batch, with a recommended option,
	// and neither the reproduction question nor intake's): coding starts on
	// it while the question stays open for you, and another answer of yours
	// goes to the writer. false: every question waits for your answer.
	ProvisionalLoneAnswer bool `toml:"provisional_lone_answer"`

	// Sensitive are the path globs (MatchPath's: "**" matches whole
	// directories) of the files whose change the ready card's FLAGS line
	// names for a second look: by default Gemfile.lock, the workflows and
	// the config files.
	Sensitive []string `toml:"sensitive"`

	// LocalReview is magnum's review loop on the change before the PR.
	LocalReview FactoryLocalReview `toml:"local_review"`
	// Repos are the repositories the factory writes code in
	// ([[factory.repo]]), appended from every layer. A repository needs a
	// [[watch]] that covers it: the first local round runs the review roles
	// of that watch.
	Repos []FactoryRepo `toml:"repo"`
	// Roles are the factory's agents ([[factory.role]]): session roles that
	// each carry a why and a doing (Role.Why, Role.Doing). After Load they
	// hold the spend level of their kind as the review roles do: its notch
	// on the built-in roles' efforts and its [spend.<level>] table
	// (applySpend).
	Roles []Role `toml:"role"`
	// CodexFallback maps a factory role that runs on Codex to the factory
	// role of the Claude kind that takes its work after a Codex refusal. The
	// user's table merges entry by entry, and an empty value removes the
	// built-in entry. An entry whose key is a role that no longer runs on
	// Codex (a [[factory.role]] moved it to Claude) is not an error: it is
	// not used, so read it only for a role of the Codex kind (Warnings says
	// so). A fallback that a stage of the role runs already makes the role
	// a second reader there (fx-points-codex beside fx-points): it has no
	// questions file of its own (its open questions stay in its findings,
	// for the judge), and after a refusal it leaves that stage, the
	// fallback's own run standing for both.
	CodexFallback map[string]string `toml:"codex_fallback"`
	// Kinds are the kinds of task ([factory.kinds.<name>]) and their stages.
	Kinds map[string]FactoryKind `toml:"kinds"`
	// KindByJiraType maps a Jira issue type to a kind of task, KindWords a
	// kind of task to the words of a free prompt that suggest it.
	KindByJiraType map[string]string   `toml:"kind_by_jira_type"`
	KindWords      map[string][]string `toml:"kind_words"`
}
    Factory is [factory]: the factory daemon that writes code from a Jira key
    or a prompt (internal/factory). The code knows a few generic stage types;
    everything specific to a repository or a team is configuration, as magnum's
    own roles and kinds are. config.defaults.toml ships the roles, the kinds of
    task and their stages, and names no repository and no staging environment
    (those are [[factory.repo]] blocks of the user's config).

    The user config merges into the built-in values key by key where that
    is safe: [factory.kinds.<name>] replaces that kind of task and keeps the
    others, a [[factory.role]] named like a role overrides the keys it sets
    (any other name is appended), [factory.local_review] and the three tables
    codex_fallback, kind_by_jira_type and kind_words merge entry by entry,
    and [[factory.repo]] blocks are appended. The other keys replace the value.

func DefaultFactory() Factory
    DefaultFactory returns the built-in [factory] values, the ones
    config.defaults.toml writes out (TestFactoryGoDefaultsEqualTheEmbeddedFile
    holds the two together). The roles are not normalized: Normalize does.

type FactoryInstall struct {
	Lock string `toml:"lock"`
	Run  string `toml:"run"`
}
    FactoryInstall is an `installs` entry of a repository: Run runs when the
    file Lock differs from the copy's last install.

type FactoryJiraMove struct {
	To   string   `toml:"to"`
	From []string `toml:"from"`
}
    FactoryJiraMove is one milestone's move of a task's Jira issue: the
    status To it goes to, from one of the statuses From (only a forward move:
    a status not in From is past it, and nothing moves). Names are Jira's,
    matched case aside.

func (m FactoryJiraMove) Moves(status string) bool
    Moves reports whether status (a name, trimmed, case aside) is one the move
    moves from.

type FactoryKind struct {
	Stages []FactoryStage `toml:"stages"`
	Proof  string         `toml:"proof"`
}
    FactoryKind is a kind of task: the stages it runs, in order, and what its
    coding stage's proof needs (Proof): FactoryProofRed (the default, ""),
    a spec of the change that fails on the base and passes at the head (a bug,
    a feature), or FactoryProofGreen, its specs green at the head with no run on
    the base (a chore: the existing specs stay green).

func (k FactoryKind) RedRun() bool
    RedRun reports whether the kind's proof needs its spec red on the base.

type FactoryLocalReview struct {
	// Cycles is the most rounds the loop runs (1 to MaxFactoryCycles).
	Cycles int `toml:"cycles"`
	// ExtraCycles is how many rounds past Cycles a converging loop runs by
	// itself (0 to MaxFactoryCycles; 0 turns them off): a round at the cap
	// that blocks goes on, its findings to the writer, while it has no P0 or
	// P1 finding, fewer blocking findings than the round before and a
	// verdict that does not block. The loop never counts more than
	// MaxFactoryCycles rounds.
	ExtraCycles int `toml:"extra_cycles"`
	// LaterWithout names the review roles that run in round 1 only.
	LaterWithout []string `toml:"later_without"`
	// SecondJudge says when a clean round of a Codex judge is followed by
	// one more round with the watch's judge_fallback in its place, once per
	// task: on a wide change (FactorySecondJudgeWide), always or never.
	SecondJudge string `toml:"second_judge"`
	// LeftBlocks makes the P3 defects a round leaves open (never its
	// simplifications) block the loop's exit as P0 to P2 ones do: the
	// writer gets them like any finding, and the loop ends clean only when
	// a round leaves none. Off by default: they are then listed under
	// KNOWN on the ready card, which sends them to the writer in one key.
	LeftBlocks bool `toml:"left_blocks"`
	// CapGoOn is how many times over a task's life a safe stop at the cap
	// goes on by itself, as your retry would (0 to MaxFactoryCapGoOn; 0
	// turns it off): the cap round has no P0 or P1, its verdict does not
	// block, and the writer declined nothing in the loop. Its findings go
	// to the writer and a fresh loop starts. A safe stop after them has the
	// writer fix the findings, and the stage passes once the factory's
	// checks pass on the fix, the ready card and the PR body naming them.
	CapGoOn int `toml:"cap_go_on"`
}
    FactoryLocalReview is [factory.local_review]. Round 1 runs the review roles
    of the repository's [[watch]]; later rounds run without LaterWithout.

type FactoryPrecheck struct {
	Lint       []string `toml:"lint"`
	Specs      string   `toml:"specs"`
	Jest       string   `toml:"jest"`
	Migrations []string `toml:"migrations"`
	// MigrationDatabases maps a migration folder (MigrationFolder:
	// db/migrate, db/reporting_migrate, engines/<name>/db/migrate) to the
	// databases its migrations run on, by the names the application gives
	// them (primary, shard_1), as a multi-database Rails application needs:
	// it refuses a plain db:migrate:up there. With it, each migration's
	// Migrations commands run once for each database of its folder, in its
	// order, {database} its name, and every command must hold {database};
	// without it, only DefaultMigrationFolder's migrations run, once, and no
	// command may. A migration of a folder with no databases is not run: the
	// precheck, the ready card and the PR body name it.
	MigrationDatabases map[string][]string `toml:"migration_databases"`
	// Cap stops a precheck that runs this long (default DefaultPrecheckCap),
	// CapPerFile longer for each file of the change it checks (default
	// DefaultPrecheckCapPerFile; never above CapMax), CapMax at most
	// (default DefaultPrecheckCapMax, or Cap when that is longer; never
	// below Cap). A precheck its cap stops in the specs or jest goes on with
	// a note when nothing else failed; one it stops in the lint needs you.
	// The proof's spec runs and the precheck's migrations keep Cap alone;
	// the base run of its red specs grows from the red files the same way,
	// or gets twice the head's spec run when that is longer.
	Cap        Duration `toml:"cap"`
	CapPerFile Duration `toml:"cap_per_file"`
	CapMax     Duration `toml:"cap_max"`
	// SkipSpecsForKinds names the kinds of task whose precheck skips the
	// specs (a gem upgrade).
	SkipSpecsForKinds []string `toml:"skip_specs_for_kinds"`
}
    FactoryPrecheck is [factory.repo.precheck]: what runs after the writer's
    last commit and after each fix of the local review. A command takes {files}
    (the changed files, shell-quoted) and {base}; a migrations command also
    {version} (the digits a migration's file name starts with) and {file},
    and runs once per migration the branch adds, or once per database of its
    folder with MigrationDatabases ({database}).

type FactoryQA struct {
	// When reads the changed files on stdin and prints the user-facing ones,
	// one per line, in the copy (required): none printed, no QA; a failing
	// command means "cannot tell", never "nothing user-facing". It has 30
	// seconds: a quick filter of paths, which boots nothing.
	When string `toml:"when"`
	// URL is the copy's server as a browser reaches it, with {port} as its
	// port (required): "http://app.example.localhost:{port}". Its host is on
	// this Mac (LocalHost).
	URL string `toml:"url"`
	// Ready is the path whose 2xx or 3xx answer says the server is up
	// (default DefaultQAReady).
	Ready string `toml:"ready"`
	// Skill is the repository's QA skill, one word, that the walker reads
	// for its sign-in, test data and page conventions ("" = none).
	Skill string `toml:"skill"`
	// SignIn is one line that says how the walker signs in locally ("" =
	// none): never a password, but the env var that holds one.
	SignIn string `toml:"sign_in"`
	// ServerStop runs in the copy before the server's process group is
	// killed (such as "overmind kill"); "" = none.
	ServerStop string `toml:"server_stop"`
	// Boot is how long the server may take to answer Ready (default
	// DefaultQABoot), Cap how long one run may take in all, the boot
	// included (default DefaultQACap, at most MaxQACap).
	Boot Duration `toml:"boot"`
	Cap  Duration `toml:"cap"`
	// MaxPages is how many pages the walker captures at most (default
	// DefaultQAMaxPages, at most MaxQAPages); Fixes how many writer turns
	// QA's defects get before the task waits on you (default DefaultQAFixes,
	// at most MaxQAFixes).
	MaxPages int `toml:"max_pages"`
	Fixes    int `toml:"fixes"`
}
    FactoryQA is [factory.repo.qa]: what a qa stage needs to walk the pages a
    change shows. The factory starts the copy's server (the repository's Server,
    on the PORT of its Env), waits until URL answers Ready, and has the fx-qa
    walker look at the pages through the factory's own headless browser,
    for at most Cap.

func (q FactoryQA) PageURL(port int, path string) string
    PageURL is the page at path of the copy whose server listens on port:
    URL with {port} rendered, then path, one slash between them whether path
    starts with one or not (so a path never runs into the port, where "@x" would
    make x the host).

type FactoryRepo struct {
	Repo string `toml:"repo"` // owner/name
	// Base is the branch tasks start from and the PR targets (default
	// master). The factory never merges into it.
	Base      string `toml:"base"`
	MainClone string `toml:"main_clone"`
	// Copies is the path of copy {n}; CopyName its name (default
	// factory{n}). Neither may render a name or path a [[pool]] renders.
	Copies   string `toml:"copies"`
	CopyName string `toml:"copy_name"`
	// MaxCopies is how many copies exist at most (default [factory]
	// max_active); MinFreeDiskGB the free disk a copy needs (default
	// [daemon] min_free_disk_gb).
	MaxCopies     int `toml:"max_copies"`
	MinFreeDiskGB int `toml:"min_free_disk_gb"`
	// Setup, Teardown, PostCheckout and ResetDB are the commands of a
	// copy's life, as a [[pool]] has them.
	Setup        []string `toml:"setup"`
	Teardown     []string `toml:"teardown"`
	PostCheckout []string `toml:"post_checkout"`
	ResetDB      []string `toml:"reset_db"`
	// Installs run Run when Lock differs from the one the copy last
	// installed.
	Installs []FactoryInstall `toml:"installs"`
	// Server is the command that starts a copy's local server.
	Server string `toml:"server"`
	// Env is the copy's environment: {copy} (or {slot}) renders the copy's
	// name, {n} its number and {n*16} its Redis offset, and REDIS_DB_OFFSET,
	// when it is named, is copy n's n*16 whatever its value (the factory's
	// copies). Databases its databases, named like a pool's
	// (DatabaseSuffix).
	Env       map[string]string `toml:"env"`
	Databases []string          `toml:"databases"`
	CopyFiles []string          `toml:"copy_files"`
	StripEnv  []string          `toml:"strip_env"`
	// Reviewer is the GitHub login the factory requests as the PR's
	// reviewer (milestone 2).
	Reviewer string          `toml:"reviewer"`
	Precheck FactoryPrecheck `toml:"precheck"`
	// ErrorSkill is the read-only error-tracker skill an investigator reads
	// the ticket's error through. GhostMarker is what a migration names the
	// environments with, where a person changes the table with gh-ost;
	// TableStats the file (relative to the checkout) that lists the size of
	// each table, and LargeTableRows the row count from which a table is
	// large (a change to it needs gh-ost or an online algorithm). Consoles
	// are the remote console commands that no factory command runs. None has
	// a default.
	ErrorSkill     string   `toml:"error_skill"`
	GhostMarker    string   `toml:"ghost_marker"`
	TableStats     string   `toml:"table_stats"`
	LargeTableRows int64    `toml:"large_table_rows"`
	Consoles       []string `toml:"consoles"`
	// PRBodySkill is the skill the judge writes a published PR's description
	// with, the team's own layout ("" = none: the factory's outline). It is
	// a skill's name, trimmed, one word; no default.
	PRBodySkill string `toml:"pr_body_skill"`
	// TitleFormat is the template of a PR's title, with {key} (the task's
	// issue key) and {title} (its title; the format must hold it once). A
	// task with no key gets its title alone. "" = DefaultFactoryTitleFormat
	// ("{key} {title}"); "[{key}] {title}" is what a repository that
	// requires "[ABC-123] Title" sets.
	TitleFormat string `toml:"title_format"`
	// Staging are the staging environments, in the order they are listed.
	Staging []FactoryStaging `toml:"staging"`
	// QA is [factory.repo.qa], how a qa stage looks at the change's pages in
	// the copy's own server; nil = no QA for the repository.
	QA *FactoryQA `toml:"qa"`
	// JiraMoves is what the factory does with the status of a task's own
	// Jira issue at the task's milestones: JiraOff (or "", the default)
	// nothing, JiraShadow plans each move (JiraMoveStart when the coding
	// stage begins, JiraMovePublished when the PR is published) from the
	// issue's status and transitions, records the plan beside your own
	// move, and writes nothing to Jira. "ask" and "auto" come after the
	// shadow week. JiraComment is the same for the issue's one comment of
	// the factory's (the PR and the task's state, at the start, the publish
	// and the merge): shadow writes it to the task's folder, never to Jira.
	JiraMoves         string          `toml:"jira_moves"`
	JiraMoveStart     FactoryJiraMove `toml:"jira_move_start"`
	JiraMovePublished FactoryJiraMove `toml:"jira_move_published"`
	JiraComment       string          `toml:"jira_comment"`
}
    FactoryRepo is a [[factory.repo]]: a repository the factory writes code in,
    with the copies of its checkout the tasks work in. The copies are a block of
    their own, never a second [[pool]] of the repository (Pool turns them into
    the Pool the slot code provisions).

func (r FactoryRepo) JiraCommentShadow() bool
    JiraCommentShadow reports whether the factory writes the repository's Jira
    comment in shadow (to the task's folder, never to Jira).

func (r FactoryRepo) JiraMove(milestone string) (FactoryJiraMove, bool)
    JiraMove is the repository's move at milestone (JiraMilestoneStart or
    JiraMilestonePublished), its names trimmed, false when it has none.

func (r FactoryRepo) JiraMovesShadow() bool
    JiraMovesShadow reports whether the factory plans the repository's Jira
    moves in shadow.

func (r FactoryRepo) Pool() Pool
    Pool is the repository's copies as the Pool the slot code provisions:
    slots named CopyName at Copies, at most MaxCopies of them, none kept ready
    (Min 0), the commands and databases the repository sets. The slices and the
    map are copies.

type FactoryStage struct {
	Name     string   `toml:"name"`
	Type     string   `toml:"type"`
	Roles    []string `toml:"roles"`
	End      string   `toml:"end"`
	Gate     string   `toml:"gate"`
	Decision string   `toml:"decision"`
	Effect   string   `toml:"effect"`
	When     string   `toml:"when"`
	Prompt   string   `toml:"prompt"`
}
    FactoryStage is one stage of a kind of task. Its Type picks the code that
    runs it and which of the other fields it takes: an agents stage launches
    Roles in parallel and ends when its End fact holds; a gate waits until
    its Gate holds; a review stage runs the local review loop (End "clean");
    a decision waits for your Decision; an effect does its Effect (End "pr").
    When "wide" skips the stage unless the plan touches 3 or more files,
    the database or security, and "narrow" skips it for such a plan: two stages,
    one of each, run one role on a wide plan and another on a narrow one (the
    built-in critic at xhigh, the narrow critic at high); only an agents stage
    takes one. Prompt, for an agents stage, is the prompt file every role of the
    stage gets in place of its own role's (a stage that asks a role for another
    file than its usual one, such as the judge's PR body); empty, each role's
    own.

type FactoryStaging struct {
	Name   string `toml:"name"`
	Branch string `toml:"branch"`
	QA     string `toml:"qa"`
	After  string `toml:"after"`
}
    FactoryStaging is a `staging` entry of a repository: an environment with
    a branch the factory merges into after your approval. Name is also the
    GitHub deployment environment the deploys record; Branch is staging-<name>
    (StagingBranchPattern), never master, main, the base or production*.
    QA names the skill that tests it ("" = no QA); After the environment whose
    QA must pass first. Config.Stagings lists a repository's; internal/staging
    reads which PRs are live on them.

type FooterData struct {
	SHA    string // the reviewed commit
	Short  string // its first 10 characters
	Repo   string // owner/name
	Number int    // the PR's number
	Login  string // the login that posted the review
	// Simplify: the PR's watch runs a role answering to the alias
	// "simplify", so the review may carry simplifications.
	Simplify bool
	// Clean: the review has no findings (still-open earlier ones included)
	// and no simplifications, by the judge's result counts.
	Clean      bool
	Event      string // APPROVE, COMMENT or REQUEST_CHANGES
	PostMerge  bool   // a review of commits GitHub merged before magnum reviewed them
	DeltaCheck bool   // the judge alone checked a small delta since its last review
	// QuietHours is [daemon] quiet_hours with the daemon's offset from UTC
	// (QuietHoursLabel: "03:00-12:00 UTC+3"); "" = none.
	QuietHours string
	// DraftsSkipped: the PR's watch skips drafts (include_drafts = false),
	// so a push to a draft starts no round; a review request does.
	DraftsSkipped bool
	// RequestLogin is the login a review request names to start a round:
	// your login (Config.OperatorIdentity: the watch's poll login when a gh
	// identity polls, else a gh identity's), else, with no gh identity
	// declared, Login.
	RequestLogin string
}
    FooterData is what a review_footer template renders with: the verified
    review magnum appends the footer to and the round that posted it.

type GitHub struct {
	// Transport is "gh" (default: requests run as `gh api --include`, so only
	// the signed gh binary talks to GitHub, which outbound firewalls such as
	// Little Snitch already allow) or "direct" (Go net/http).
	Transport string `toml:"transport"`
	// BudgetFloor is the GraphQL budget (points left of the hour's) below
	// which the daemon starts no new work that reads GitHub as an identity:
	// rounds, fix jobs, whiteboards, the retro and notes curations wait for
	// that identity's budget to recover, while running rounds finish and the
	// poll keeps its own floor of 50. 0 = off; at most 5000.
	BudgetFloor int `toml:"budget_floor"`
}
    GitHub tunes how magnum reaches the GitHub REST API itself (App JWT and
    installation-token calls; everything else already runs through gh), and how
    much of an identity's GraphQL budget new work leaves (budget_floor).

type HealthPatterns struct {
	Refused       []string `toml:"refused"`        // end the round and flag the PR: never reviewed again
	LoginRequired []string `toml:"login_required"` // pause the kind until the human logs in
	ModelLimit    []string `toml:"model_limit"`    // switch the session to a fallback model (see Kind.FallbackModels)
	UsageLimit    []string `toml:"usage_limit"`    // pause until the reset time the text names
	Overloaded    []string `toml:"overloaded"`     // retry with backoff
}
    HealthPatterns are regular expressions (RE2, matched case-insensitively)
    that classify an agent pane's recent output. Setting one list replaces that
    list only.

    ModelLimit patterns name a cap on one model while the account still has
    usage left ("You've reached your Fable limit"). They are checked before
    UsageLimit; a named group "model" captures the model, else the session's
    current model is the limited one.

    Refused patterns name a safety warning of the agent's provider about the
    content (Codex's "flagged for possible cybersecurity risk"): the round ends
    at once and the PR is never reviewed again (a provider may block an account
    it takes for an abuser), so they are checked first.

func DefaultHealthPatterns() HealthPatterns
    DefaultHealthPatterns returns the classifier patterns magnum has always used
    for Codex and Claude (a fresh copy); every kind starts from them.

func (h HealthPatterns) Compile() (HealthRegexps, error)
    Compile compiles every pattern with the (?i) flag.

type HealthRegexps struct {
	Refused, LoginRequired, ModelLimit, UsageLimit, Overloaded []*regexp.Regexp
}
    HealthRegexps are compiled HealthPatterns.

type Herdr struct {
	// Socket is your herdr session's socket: toasts show there, the slot
	// guards read your agents there, and the plugin and the LaunchAgent's
	// HERDR_SOCKET_PATH name it.
	Socket string `toml:"socket"`
	// ReviewSession is the herdr session magnum's review panes live in
	// (`herdr --session <name>`): "" = yours, Socket and [terminal]
	// session (Config.ReviewHerdr).
	ReviewSession string `toml:"review_session"`
	// ReviewSocket is that session's socket: "" = the named session's own
	// (herdr.SessionSocket). Absolute after ~ expands; it needs
	// ReviewSession, whose name the reveal opens.
	ReviewSocket     string `toml:"review_socket"`
	Notify           bool   `toml:"notify"`
	ToastEveryReview bool   `toml:"toast_every_review"`
}

type Identity struct {
	Name            string `toml:"name"`
	Kind            string `toml:"kind"` // gh | app
	Login           string `toml:"login"`
	AppID           int64  `toml:"app_id"`
	ClientID        string `toml:"client_id"`
	InstallationID  int64  `toml:"installation_id"`
	PrivateKeyEnv   string `toml:"private_key_env"`   // the env var holding the PEM (text or a path)
	PrivateKeyFile  string `toml:"private_key_file"`  // the PEM file (~ and paths relative to the user config's directory resolved); wins over private_key_env
	NoFindingsEvent string `toml:"no_findings_event"` // APPROVE | COMMENT
	BlockingEvent   string `toml:"blocking_event"`    // REQUEST_CHANGES | COMMENT
	DismissOwnStale *bool  `toml:"dismiss_own_stale_change_requests"`
	// ReviewFooter is the template of the footer magnum appends to the
	// identity's reviews, for the PR's author (nil = DefaultReviewFooter,
	// "" = none); see Footer and FooterData.
	ReviewFooter *string `toml:"review_footer"`
	// TokenRepositories and TokenPermissions narrow every installation
	// token magnum mints for an App identity (kind app only): the
	// repositories, by name within the installation's account, and the
	// permissions ("read" or "write" by GitHub's permission name) GitHub's
	// access_tokens call takes. Unset = the installation's whole access, as
	// before. A fixer App (Config.DedicatedFixApp) must set both, with
	// contents and pull_requests write and nothing else.
	TokenRepositories []string          `toml:"token_repositories"`
	TokenPermissions  map[string]string `toml:"token_permissions"`
	// UserID is an App's bot user's numeric GitHub id (kind app only; 0 =
	// unset): a fixer App's commits carry <user_id>+<login>@users.noreply.github.com.
	UserID int64 `toml:"user_id"`
}

func (i Identity) DismissStale() bool
    DismissStale reports whether the identity dismisses its own stale
    CHANGES_REQUESTED.

func (i Identity) Footer() string
    Footer is the identity's footer template, which magnum renders
    (RenderFooter) and appends to every review the identity posts once it is
    verified: review_footer, trimmed, else DefaultReviewFooter; "" = no footer.

type Jira struct {
	// URL is the Jira site, https only ("https://example.atlassian.net");
	// "" = off. Only a [board], [[watch]] or [[repo]] tracker whose template
	// starts with it names an issue to read.
	URL string `toml:"url"`
	// User is the account's email, which reads the issues with the token.
	User string `toml:"user"`
	// TokenFile holds the account's API token alone on one line: a regular
	// file of mode 0600 (~ and a path relative to the user config's
	// directory resolved). The token goes to curl on stdin, never in argv,
	// a log or an error.
	TokenFile string `toml:"token_file"`
}
    Jira is the [jira] table: the site a round reads the PR's issue from
    (internal/jira), named by the first issue key of a tracker on that site in
    the PR's title or head branch. Off by default (no url).

func (j Jira) Names(tracker string) bool
    Names reports whether a tracker template (Tracker.URL) is one of the site's:
    it starts with the site's URL and a slash.

func (j Jira) On() bool
    On reports whether rounds read the PR's Jira ticket.

type Kind struct {
	// Start: extra args always appended.
	Start []string `toml:"start"`
	// Args: appended only when the command is not a wrapper (wrapper
	// "false", or "auto" found a plain binary); the old [codex]/[claude] args.
	Args []string `toml:"args"`
	// Resume: args that resume session {session}, e.g. ["resume", "{session}"].
	Resume []string `toml:"resume"`
	// Model: args that select model {model}; empty = the kind cannot pick a
	// model (a role setting model, or DefaultModel, is then invalid).
	Model []string `toml:"model"`
	// DefaultModel: the model of the kind's roles that set none, passed
	// through Model (e.g. "gpt-6.1-sol" for codex); "" = the CLI's own
	// default.
	DefaultModel string `toml:"default_model"`
	// Effort: args that set reasoning effort {effort}; empty = the effort
	// reaches prompts only (Role.Effort is a template variable either way).
	Effort []string `toml:"effort"`
	// Spend: the spend level of the kind's roles (those whose
	// Role.AgentKind is the kind, a shell role's tool counting), in place
	// of [pipeline] spend: its notch mapping and its [spend.<level>] table
	// apply to them (Config.SpendLevel, applySpend). A built-in level or
	// one a [spend.<level>] table declares; "" = [pipeline] spend.
	Spend string `toml:"spend"`
	// Subagents: args that cap the subagents a session may have open at
	// once to {subagents} (Role.MaxSubagents, 1 or more), e.g. codex's
	// ["-c", "agents.max_concurrent_threads_per_session={subagents}"];
	// NoSubagents: args that turn subagents off (max_subagents = 0). Empty =
	// the kind cannot cap them, and the role key is ignored.
	Subagents   []string `toml:"subagents"`
	NoSubagents []string `toml:"no_subagents"`
	// MCPOff: keep the user's MCP servers out of every session of the kind
	// (see MCPOffArgs; codex and claude: true), through MCPStrict, which
	// turns servers off whatever their names, and MCPDisable, which turns
	// off each server a session would load from the Codex config
	// ([mcp_servers.<name>] tables not set enabled = false) except those in
	// MCPAllow: Codex merges -c tables into its config, so servers go off
	// only one by one, by name. A kind with neither ignores it.
	MCPOff   bool     `toml:"mcp_off"`
	MCPAllow []string `toml:"mcp_allow"`
	// PluginDisable: args that turn off plugin {plugin} (name@marketplace),
	// passed once per plugin under MCPOff, e.g. codex's ["-c",
	// "plugins.{plugin}.enabled=false"]: a Codex plugin's MCP servers (a
	// browser, a docs or GitHub server) are no [mcp_servers] table, so
	// MCPDisable does not reach them. PluginAllow are the plugins left on.
	PluginDisable []string `toml:"plugin_disable"`
	PluginAllow   []string `toml:"plugin_allow"`
	// MCPStrict: args passed once under MCPOff that keep MCP servers out of
	// a session whatever their names: claude's ["--strict-mcp-config"]
	// (Claude Code 2.1.292 then loads only the servers of --mcp-config:
	// none of the user, local, project or plugin servers, nor claude.ai
	// connectors), codex's ["-c", "features.apps=false"] (Codex 0.160's
	// built-in apps connector, the codex_apps server of ChatGPT's
	// connectors, which no [mcp_servers] table declares), and with it
	// ["-c", "skills.include_instructions=false"], which keeps the user's
	// skills list out of every turn (the judge reads the skill its prompt
	// links). MCPAllow does not apply; args naming a file of servers to
	// keep ("--mcp-config", "<path>") go in this list.
	MCPStrict []string `toml:"mcp_strict"`
	// MCPDisable: args that turn off MCP server {server}, passed once per
	// server, e.g. codex's ["-c", "mcp_servers.{server}.enabled=false"].
	MCPDisable []string `toml:"mcp_disable"`
	// MCPDisableURL, MCPDisableCommand: args that give MCP server {server} a
	// transport of the stated kind with a fixed value, passed once before its
	// MCPDisable for a server only the checkout's config declares (project_mcp
	// "off"; ProjectServer.Transport), e.g. codex's
	// ["-c", "mcp_servers.{server}.url=\"https://mcp.invalid\""] for a table with
	// a url and ["-c", "mcp_servers.{server}.command=\"true\""] for one with a
	// command. Codex 0.166 reads the tables of the session's -c flags before it
	// merges the checkout's, so enabled=false alone makes a table with no
	// transport and Codex stops at its start. The value is never the file's:
	// the PR controls it. Empty = no transport is passed for that kind of
	// table (claude and a custom kind have none).
	MCPDisableURL     []string `toml:"mcp_disable_url"`
	MCPDisableCommand []string `toml:"mcp_disable_command"`
	// ProjectMCP: the MCP servers the checkout's own .codex/config.toml
	// declares when the PR leaves .codex/ as its merge base has it (the
	// team's servers): "off" (the codex kind's default) turns each off
	// through MCPDisable like the user's, except those in MCPAllow, a server
	// the user's config does not declare first getting a transport
	// (MCPDisableURL, MCPDisableCommand; see ConfigOffArgs); "allow" (the
	// other kinds' default, "" counting as it) keeps them. A PR that changes
	// .codex/ loads none of them (ProjectUntrust).
	ProjectMCP string `toml:"project_mcp"`
	// ProjectUntrust: args that keep the checkout's own project
	// configuration out of one session, passed when the PR changes it
	// against its merge base (the paths the agents package knows for the
	// kind: codex .codex/, AGENTS.md and AGENTS.override.md; claude
	// .claude/, .mcp.json, and CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md and AGENTS.md in
	// any directory); {projects}, when present, is a TOML inline table
	// marking each of the checkout's paths untrusted (UntrustArgs). codex:
	// ["-c", "projects={projects}"], so the session treats the checkout as
	// an untrusted folder and loads nothing from its .codex/ (config, MCP
	// servers, hooks, rules) nor its AGENTS.md; claude:
	// ["--setting-sources", "user"], so it loads the user's settings only
	// (no project or local settings with their hooks, no .mcp.json servers,
	// skills, commands, agents, CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md of the checkout).
	// Empty = such a session loads the PR's project config like any trusted
	// project's (ProjectDocsOff does not apply either).
	ProjectUntrust []string `toml:"project_untrust"`
	// ProjectDocsOff: args that keep only the checkout's instruction files
	// out of one session, passed instead of ProjectUntrust when they are
	// all the PR changes of the kind's project config, so the rest of it,
	// the team's, still loads. codex: ["-c", "project_doc_max_bytes=0"]:
	// Codex 0.160 then reads no AGENTS.md or AGENTS.override.md of the
	// project (core/src/agents_md.rs) and keeps its global AGENTS.md, and a
	// -c flag outranks the checkout's .codex/config.toml (session flags
	// over the project layer, config/src/config_layer_source.rs). Empty =
	// ProjectUntrust covers them (claude: --setting-sources user keeps its
	// CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md out with the rest).
	ProjectDocsOff []string `toml:"project_docs_off"`
	// ToolOutputLimit: the most tokens of one tool call's output the CLI
	// keeps for the model, passed through ToolOutput (ToolOutputArgs) to
	// every launch and resume, and to the line of a shell role whose tool
	// is the kind; 0 = the CLI's own. codex: DefaultCodexToolOutputLimit.
	// A ceiling, not the size of a read: Codex 0.162.1 still cuts a
	// command's output at the 10,000 tokens its exec tool asks for by
	// default, so the roles read the repository notes in parts.
	ToolOutputLimit int `toml:"tool_output_limit"`
	// ToolOutput: args that set ToolOutputLimit {limit}, e.g. codex's
	// ["-c", "tool_output_token_limit={limit}"]; empty = the kind cannot
	// set it, and tool_output_limit is ignored.
	ToolOutput []string `toml:"tool_output"`
	// Name: args that name the session {title} at launch (claude --name).
	Name []string `toml:"name"`
	// Rename: a slash command typed while the agent works to (re)name its
	// session, e.g. "/rename {title}" (Codex has no name flag); "" = none.
	Rename string `toml:"rename"`
	// LoginCheck: a read-only command proving the CLI is logged in, split on
	// spaces (no shell, no quoting), e.g. "codex login status"; "" = none.
	LoginCheck string `toml:"login_check"`
	// LoginOK: how LoginCheck's output reads as logged in (see LoggedIn):
	// "text:<substring>", "regex:<expr>", "json:<dotted.path>" (a boolean in
	// the first JSON object of stdout) or "" (exit status 0).
	LoginOK string `toml:"login_ok"`
	// LoginFile: the CLI's login file, a relative path under the kind's
	// home (codex: CODEX_HOME, else ~/.codex); "" = none. A login pause
	// that a run proved (a reviewer's run or the judge's pane showed the
	// login error) holds until LoginCheck passes and this file changes,
	// because a check that reads the saved tokens says logged in while a
	// revoked refresh token fails every call (agents.Manager.LoginStamp).
	LoginFile string `toml:"login_file"`
	// Wrapper: "auto" (default), "true", "false" or "bypass" (see
	// WrapperAuto, WrapperBypass).
	Wrapper string `toml:"wrapper"`
	// Env: extra environment for the kind's panes (a role's env wins).
	Env map[string]string `toml:"env"`
	// HealthPatterns classify the pane's output (the trust-dialog, approval
	// and stalled patterns stay built in).
	HealthPatterns HealthPatterns `toml:"health_patterns"`
	// SessionSource: "herdr" (default) or "none" (see SessionHerdr).
	SessionSource string `toml:"session_source"`
	// OnPermissionPrompt: what magnum does when the agent stops at a
	// permission (approval) prompt during one of magnum's runs: "deny"
	// (default) answers No, "wait" leaves it for the human (see
	// PermissionDeny). The first-launch folder-trust dialog is handled
	// separately either way.
	OnPermissionPrompt string `toml:"on_permission_prompt"`
	// OnHooksReview: how magnum answers Codex's startup hooks review (hooks
	// new or changed since Codex last trusted them): "trust_own" (default)
	// trusts them when the checkout declares no hooks of its own, so all are
	// the user's, and declines them otherwise; "decline" always declines
	// (see HooksTrustOwn). Only a kind whose CLI shows that dialog uses it.
	OnHooksReview string `toml:"on_hooks_review"`
	// AfterDenyPrompt: the message sent (once per denied prompt, through
	// herdr agent.prompt, within the same run) when an agent whose
	// permission prompt magnum denied stops its turn and goes idle, so it
	// finishes the task without the command (Claude Code ends its turn on a
	// No). Default DefaultAfterDenyPrompt; "" sends nothing.
	AfterDenyPrompt string `toml:"after_deny_prompt"`
	// SwitchModel: the slash command typed into an idle agent's pane to
	// switch its session to model {model} (claude: "/model {model}"); "" =
	// the kind cannot switch in-session, so a per-model limit (health
	// pattern model_limit) pauses the kind like a usage limit.
	SwitchModel string `toml:"switch_model"`
	// FallbackModels: the models a session switches to, in order, when its
	// model hits a per-model limit (claude: ["opus", "sonnet"]); unused
	// without SwitchModel, so switch_model = "" alone turns switching off.
	// Empty = no fallback.
	FallbackModels []string `toml:"fallback_models"`
	// ResetModel: the SwitchModel argument that returns a session to the
	// CLI's own default model once the limit is over, for a role (and kind)
	// without a model (claude: "default"); "" = such a session stays on its
	// fallback.
	ResetModel string `toml:"reset_model"`
	// ExitKeys: the keys a hard quit sends, as herdr's pane send-keys takes
	// them (key combos: a printable key, "enter", "esc", "ctrl+d"), when
	// the agent is still the pane's foreground process two ctrl+c after
	// magnum asked it to quit; the pane is closed alone when it is still
	// not an idle shell after them (agents.Manager.ParkHard). The idle
	// park's early park (agents.Manager.ParkSessions) and the quit of one
	// session (agents.Manager.Quit) send them a second after one ctrl+c,
	// only when herdr shows the session's own conversation idle in the pane
	// and its screen a bare prompt and no dialog, and close nothing they
	// leave running. claude: "/exit" then enter, one key each (send-keys
	// takes no word). Empty = the hard quit goes straight to the close, and
	// the early park and Quit send two ctrl+c.
	ExitKeys []string `toml:"exit_keys"`
	// ContextPattern reads how full a session's context is from its pane's
	// status lines (agents.Manager.ContextUsed): a Go regexp with a capture
	// group named "used" (the percent of the context used) or "left" (the
	// percent left, read as 100 minus it), or both in alternatives; the
	// newest match counts. claude: DefaultClaudeContextPattern, which reads
	// a status line's "418k/1m (41%)" and Claude Code's own "Context left
	// until auto-compact: 8%". "" = the kind's panes show no figure, so
	// [pipeline] fix_compact_at never compacts its fixer.
	ContextPattern string `toml:"context_pattern"`
}
    Kind is a [kinds.<name>] block: how magnum drives one agent CLI that
    herdr knows by that name (`herdr agent start --kind <name>`). User blocks
    are merged key by key onto DefaultKinds (a key that is not set keeps the
    default); a name without a default starts from DefaultHealthPatterns,
    wrapper "auto" and session_source "herdr". KindSpec returns the result.

    herdr types the command into the pane's shell, so the CLI may be a zsh
    wrapper function or alias that adds its own flags. The launch argv is built
    by Argv in this order: Resume (resumed sessions only), Name (when a title
    is known), Model (the role's model, else DefaultModel), Effort (when the
    role sets it), Subagents or NoSubagents (when the role sets max_subagents),
    ToolOutput (when ToolOutputLimit is set; ToolOutputArgs), MCPStrict and
    MCPDisable per MCP server to turn off and ProjectUntrust for a checkout
    whose project config (.codex/ and AGENTS.md; .claude/, .mcp.json, CLAUDE.md
    and AGENTS.md) the PR changes, or ProjectDocsOff when it changes only the
    instruction files (ConfigOffArgs), Start, Args (only without a wrapper),
    then the role's args.

func (k Kind) Argv(a LaunchArgs) []string
    Argv builds the args after the command name (herdr shell-quotes each one):
    Resume, Name, Model (a.Model, else DefaultModel), Effort, Subagents
    (or NoSubagents for 0), ToolOutputArgs, ConfigOffArgs(a.MCPServers,
    a.ProjectServers, a.Untrusted, a.DocsOff), Start, Args (no wrapper only),
    then a.Extra. A group whose value is empty is skipped; placeholders are
    replaced in every element. A session that is no SessionArgOK is skipped too:
    the launch goes without the resume rather than with an id the CLI could read
    as a flag.

func (k Kind) ConfigOffArgs(servers, plugins []string, project []ProjectServer, untrusted []string, docsOff bool) []string
    ConfigOffArgs are the args that keep configuration out of a session:
    MCPStrict under MCPOff, MCPDisable once per server to turn off (servers
    under MCPOff, then under ProjectMCP "off" each project server not among
    them; none in MCPAllow, nothing without MCPDisable), a project server with
    a Transport first getting that kind's MCPDisableURL or MCPDisableCommand,
    PluginDisable once per plugin (PluginOffArgs), then ProjectDocsOff when
    docsOff and UntrustArgs(untrusted).

func (k Kind) ContextRegexp() (*regexp.Regexp, error)
    ContextRegexp compiles ContextPattern: nil without one, an error naming
    the key for a pattern that does not compile or names neither capture group
    (ContextUsedGroup, ContextLeftGroup).

func (k Kind) LoggedIn(stdout, stderr string, exitOK bool) (loggedIn, readable bool)
    LoggedIn reads LoginCheck's output per LoginOK. exitOK is whether the
    command exited 0. readable is false when the output could not be read (json:
    no JSON object in stdout, or the path is not a boolean); the caller then
    decides between "not logged in" and "the check could not run".

        text:<s>   loggedIn = stdout+stderr contains s (case-sensitive)
        regex:<re> loggedIn = stdout+stderr matches re
        json:<p>   loggedIn = the boolean at dotted path p of stdout's first JSON object
        ""         loggedIn = exitOK

func (k Kind) LoginArgv() []string
    LoginArgv splits LoginCheck on spaces: the command name and its args (nil
    when the kind has no login check).

func (k Kind) MCPOffArgs(servers []string) []string
    MCPOffArgs are the args that keep the user's MCP servers out of a session:
    MCPStrict, then MCPDisable with {server} replaced, once per given server not
    in MCPAllow, in order; nil when MCPOff is false or the kind has neither.

func (k Kind) PluginOffArgs(plugins []string) []string
    PluginOffArgs are the args that keep the user's plugins out of a session:
    PluginDisable with {plugin} replaced, once per given plugin not in
    PluginAllow, in order; nil when MCPOff is false or the kind has no
    PluginDisable.

func (k Kind) RenameCommand(title string) string
    RenameCommand is Rename with {title} replaced ("" when the kind has none).

func (k Kind) SwitchModelCommand(model string) string
    SwitchModelCommand is SwitchModel with {model} replaced ("" when the kind
    cannot switch or model is empty).

func (k Kind) ToolOutputArgs() []string
    ToolOutputArgs are ToolOutput with {limit} replaced by ToolOutputLimit;
    nil when the limit is 0 (the CLI's own) or the kind has no ToolOutput.

func (k Kind) UntrustArgs(paths []string) []string
    UntrustArgs are ProjectUntrust for a checkout at paths, with {projects},
    where an arg has it, replaced by one TOML inline table marking each path
    untrusted, e.g. {"/p/x"={trust_level="untrusted"}} (a second -c of the same
    key would replace the first); args without it (claude's --setting-sources
    user) as they are. nil without paths or ProjectUntrust.

type LaunchArgs struct {
	Session string   // session id to resume; "" = a fresh session (Resume is skipped)
	Title   string   // the pane title; "" skips Name
	Model   string   // Role.Model; "" = the kind's DefaultModel, and Model is skipped when that is "" too
	Effort  string   // Role.Effort; "" skips Effort
	Wrapper bool     // the command is a wrapper function (Args are skipped)
	Extra   []string // Role.Args, appended last as given

	// Subagents is Role.MaxSubagents: nil skips Subagents and NoSubagents,
	// 0 takes NoSubagents, more takes Subagents.
	Subagents *int
	// MCPServers are the MCP servers the session would load (the Codex
	// config's); MCPOffArgs turns them off. Plugins are the Codex plugins
	// the session would load (name@marketplace); PluginOffArgs turns them
	// off.
	MCPServers, Plugins []string
	// ProjectServers are the MCP servers the checkout's unchanged
	// .codex/config.toml declares, turned off under project_mcp "off";
	// Untrusted are the checkout's paths whose project config the session
	// must not load (the PR changes .codex/). See ConfigOffArgs.
	ProjectServers []ProjectServer
	Untrusted      []string
	// DocsOff: the session gets ProjectDocsOff (the PR changes only the
	// checkout's instruction files).
	DocsOff bool
}
    LaunchArgs are the per-start values Kind.Argv substitutes.

type Learn struct {
	// Enabled turns the daily schedule on; off by default (it spends a model
	// turn per candidate PR). `magnum retro` runs regardless.
	Enabled bool `toml:"enabled"`
	// DailyAt is the local time of day, "HH:MM", after which the daily retro
	// runs once.
	DailyAt string `toml:"daily_at"`
	// Lookback: PRs merged or closed within it are candidates.
	Lookback Duration `toml:"lookback"`
	// Settle: the daily retro and a plain `magnum retro` take a PR only once
	// it was closed or merged at least this long ago, so the reviews posted
	// after it closed are in (0 = at once). `magnum retro <ref>` ignores it.
	Settle Duration `toml:"settle"`
	// MaxPRs bounds the PRs classified per retro, newest closed first.
	MaxPRs int `toml:"max_prs"`
	// MinCommentChars: comments shorter than this are dropped.
	MinCommentChars int `toml:"min_comment_chars"`
	// IncludeBots counts bot accounts other than magnum's own as reviewers.
	IncludeBots bool `toml:"include_bots"`
	// Kind is the classifying agent's [kinds.<name>]; Model, Effort and Args
	// are passed to it like a role's (LearnRole). Model "" is the kind's own
	// default (its default_model, else the CLI's). A config that names a kind
	// but no model gets DefaultLearnModel(kind): sonnet for claude, "" for any
	// other kind, whose CLI would not know a Claude model name.
	Kind   string   `toml:"kind"`
	Model  string   `toml:"model"`
	Effort string   `toml:"effort"`
	Args   []string `toml:"args"`
	// Prompt is the template file (Config.ResolvePrompt); see prompts/README.md.
	Prompt string `toml:"prompt"`
	// Timeout bounds the agent's turn on one PR.
	Timeout Duration `toml:"timeout"`
	// FallbackModels are the models the classifier starts again on, in
	// order, when Model hits its own limit (Role.FallbackModels); empty =
	// the kind's fallback_models.
	FallbackModels []string `toml:"fallback_models"`

	// The self-improving loop (internal/engine/learn_edit.go, DECISIONS "The
	// editor proposes skill and prompt changes on a branch"). Editor turns
	// on the editor after a retro that found new general misses or
	// declines (`magnum learn --propose` runs it regardless): a pane agent
	// that drafts a change to the judge skill and the prompts on a branch
	// of the checkout. EditorKind, EditorModel, EditorEffort and EditorArgs
	// are its role's (EditorRole; editor_kind without editor_model gets
	// DefaultLearnModel of that kind), EditorPrompt its template,
	// EditorTimeout the bound of one turn and EditorFallbackModels the
	// models it starts again on when EditorModel hits its own limit (empty =
	// the kind's fallback_models).
	Editor               bool     `toml:"editor"`
	EditorKind           string   `toml:"editor_kind"`
	EditorModel          string   `toml:"editor_model"`
	EditorEffort         string   `toml:"editor_effort"`
	EditorArgs           []string `toml:"editor_args"`
	EditorPrompt         string   `toml:"editor_prompt"`
	EditorTimeout        Duration `toml:"editor_timeout"`
	EditorFallbackModels []string `toml:"editor_fallback_models"`
	// GateCases bounds the eval cases the gate of a proposal replays, its
	// targets and the newest others; GateGuards (0 to 10, 0 = none) adds
	// that many guards on top, cases whose newest replay found a defect,
	// which the candidate must find again (learn.SelectCases);
	// LandPerDay the proposals that land per local day; Restart is idle
	// (the daemon restarts on a landed change once nothing is in flight) or
	// manual (it asks for `magnum daemon-restart --when-idle`). The newest
	// landed version whose declined and argued share of its posted
	// findings grows by RegressionPoints over the previous version's, both
	// with at least RegressionMinFindings posted findings, gets one revert
	// proposal, which the gate holds for review (internal/engine
	// learn_revert.go).
	GateCases             int    `toml:"gate_cases"`
	GateGuards            int    `toml:"gate_guards"`
	LandPerDay            int    `toml:"land_per_day"`
	Restart               string `toml:"restart"`
	RegressionPoints      int    `toml:"regression_points"`
	RegressionMinFindings int    `toml:"regression_min_findings"`
}
    Learn is the [learn] section: the daily retro. After a PR closes,
    magnum collects what the other reviewers commented on it, drops what its own
    review already posted, and has an interactive agent classify the rest; the
    real misses go to the registry's misses table (`magnum misses` lists them).
    Enabled runs it once a day after DailyAt; `magnum retro` runs one whether
    or not it is enabled (internal/engine/retro.go, DECISIONS "Learning loop:
    daily retro").

func DefaultLearn() Learn
    DefaultLearn returns the built-in [learn] values: off, a week of lookback,
    a day to settle, Claude sonnet classifying; the editor off, Claude sonnet
    editing for at most 45 minutes a turn, a gate of 6 cases, one landing a day,
    an idle restart, a regression of 10 points over 20 findings.

func (l Learn) DailyTime(day time.Time) (time.Time, error)
    DailyTime is the daily_at time on the local calendar day of day (in day's
    location). daily_at must be "HH:MM", 00:00 to 23:59, two digits each.

type LoadOptions struct {
	// NoOverlay skips the user layer (the user config) even when it exists,
	// so the result depends on the base alone.
	NoOverlay bool
	// UserData, when non-nil, is the user layer's content, read from here
	// instead of the layout's UserConfig, which still names it in messages
	// and Sources (whether or not that file exists): a candidate checked
	// before it is written (the settings screen's save), exactly as Load
	// would read it from the file. An empty non-nil slice is an empty layer.
	UserData []byte
}
    LoadOptions tunes LoadWithOptions.

type Notes struct {
	MaxBytes        int64 `toml:"max_bytes"`
	MaxLine         int   `toml:"max_line"`
	MaxHarnessFiles int   `toml:"max_harness_files"`
	MaxHarnessBytes int64 `toml:"max_harness_bytes"`
	// Curate lists the curation triggers (CurateOverLimit, CurateWeekly,
	// CurateMisses); empty: only on demand.
	Curate CurateTriggers `toml:"curate"`
	// Kind is the curator's [kinds.<name>]; a config that names a kind but no
	// model gets DefaultLearnModel(kind), as [learn] does.
	Kind   string   `toml:"kind"`
	Model  string   `toml:"model"`
	Effort string   `toml:"effort"`
	Args   []string `toml:"args"`
	// Prompt is the curator's template file (Config.ResolvePrompt).
	Prompt string `toml:"prompt"`
	// Timeout bounds the curator's turn.
	Timeout Duration `toml:"timeout"`
	// FallbackModels are the models the curator starts again on, in order,
	// when Model hits its own limit (Role.FallbackModels); empty = the
	// kind's fallback_models.
	FallbackModels []string `toml:"fallback_models"`

	// The notes critic (critic.go): Critic turns it on; CriticKind,
	// CriticModel, CriticEffort, CriticArgs, CriticPrompt, CriticTimeout and
	// CriticFallbackModels are its role's (CriticRole; critic_kind without
	// critic_model gets DefaultCriticModel of that kind). CriticDeclines is
	// how many proposals of a repository it may reject or send back in a row
	// before the next one waits for the operator, CriticPerDay how many
	// critiques start per local day.
	Critic               bool     `toml:"critic"`
	CriticKind           string   `toml:"critic_kind"`
	CriticModel          string   `toml:"critic_model"`
	CriticEffort         string   `toml:"critic_effort"`
	CriticArgs           []string `toml:"critic_args"`
	CriticPrompt         string   `toml:"critic_prompt"`
	CriticTimeout        Duration `toml:"critic_timeout"`
	CriticFallbackModels []string `toml:"critic_fallback_models"`
	CriticDeclines       int      `toml:"critic_declines"`
	CriticPerDay         int      `toml:"critic_per_day"`
}
    Notes is the [notes] section: the repository notes every review role reads
    first and the judge rewrites (engine.NotesPath). The four limits are hints
    to organize, not caps: after each judge round (and at startup) magnum
    measures the notes and the harness directory of QA scripts beside them
    (the archive apart), and a repository past any limit is marked past it (a
    notes.over_limit event, `magnum notes`). Nothing blocks a review, and a
    curated proposal may stay above a limit. Curate lists what starts a curation
    besides `magnum notes <repo> --curate`: a retro that recorded misses of the
    repository for its notes (the default), a repository marked past a limit
    (size alone, off by default), or once a week. A curation organizes and never
    loses a line (notes.Validate). The curator is an interactive agent like the
    retro's ([learn]): Kind, Model, Effort and Args as a role's (NotesRole).

func DefaultNotes() Notes
    DefaultNotes returns the built-in [notes] values.

type Pipeline struct {
	// PromptsDir holds the editable prompt files; default "{{repo}}/prompts"
	// ({{repo}} = magnum's home; Load expands ~ and makes a relative path
	// relative to the home). A prompt name resolves to <PromptsDir>/<name>
	// when that file exists, else to the embedded default of the same name
	// (package prompts); see ResolvePrompt. A missing directory leaves only
	// the embedded defaults.
	PromptsDir string `toml:"prompts_dir"`
	// JudgeOwnPass is when the judge does its own pass of a round:
	// OwnPassParallel (default) prompts it for that pass together with the
	// reviewer roles (its own-pass prompt, Role.OwnPass) and for the
	// candidates once both ended; OwnPassAfter prompts it once, after the
	// reviewers, for both. A [[watch]] may override it (Watch.JudgeOwnPass);
	// see Config.JudgeOwnPassFor.
	JudgeOwnPass string `toml:"judge_own_pass"`
	// RelatedLookback is how long a merged PR stays related: the judge's
	// related.json lists the open PRs of the repository and those merged
	// within it that change the same paths (default 14 days; 0 = open PRs
	// only). A [[watch]] may override it (Watch.RelatedLookback).
	RelatedLookback Duration `toml:"related_lookback"`
	// RelatedIgnore are path globs (see MatchPath) whose paths never make
	// two PRs related and that the changed files' history.json and docs.json
	// leave out (default DefaultRelatedIgnore, the lockfiles; [] = none). A
	// [[watch]] may override it (Watch.RelatedIgnore).
	RelatedIgnore []string `toml:"related_ignore"`
	// JudgeFreshAfter: a judge whose last turn on the PR ended longer ago
	// than this starts the PR's next round in a fresh session (the recovery
	// path, which reads the earlier reviews and threads from GitHub) instead
	// of resuming its conversation, whose prompt cache has gone cold by
	// then (it lasts about 1.5 hours), so its first turn would re-read the
	// whole conversation uncached. Default 90m; 0 = always resume. Only the
	// judge; a continue of a paused turn keeps its conversation.
	JudgeFreshAfter Duration `toml:"judge_fresh_after"`
	// FullPassEvery: the Nth automatic re-review of a PR, counted since its
	// first review or its last full pass, runs as a scheduled full pass:
	// every role starts in a fresh session, the reviewers review the whole
	// PR with their first-review prompts and effort, and the judge reviews
	// the full diff again through the recovery prompt (engine fullpass.go).
	// A re-review of the same head, a reply round, a CI check and a round
	// someone asked for never become one; a delta check does, when one is
	// due, and so does `magnum review --fresh` (by this rule, FullPassLines,
	// FullPassFiles or FullPassAfter). Default DefaultFullPassEvery; 0 =
	// this rule off.
	FullPassEvery int `toml:"full_pass_every"`
	// FullPassLines: an automatic re-review is also a full pass once the
	// lines the PR's re-reviews changed since its baseline (its last full
	// pass, else its first review), added plus deleted, lockfiles and
	// related_ignore's paths left out, reach the larger of this and a
	// quarter of the PR's lines at the baseline (engine fullpass.go).
	// Default DefaultFullPassLines; 0 = this rule off.
	FullPassLines int `toml:"full_pass_lines"`
