	CurateTriggerRequest   = "request"
	// CurateTriggerRecover marks the proposal `magnum notes <repo>
	// --recover` makes (a curation proposal no curator wrote): the archive
	// of the lines the history held and the notes lack. It is no curation of
	// the repository: the triggers' spacing and the curator's rejections
	// leave it out.
	CurateTriggerRecover = "recover"

	// ProposalTTL is how long a proposal waits for the operator before it
	// expires.
	ProposalTTL = 7 * 24 * time.Hour
	// NotesLockWait is how long a curation's copy and an apply wait for the
	// notes lock, as long as a judge waits for it.
	NotesLockWait = 3 * time.Minute
)
const (
	// KVNotesCurating holds the curation running now (CurateMark as JSON),
	// deleted when it ends and at every start of the daemon.
	KVNotesCurating = "notes.curating"
	// KVNotesCurateQueue holds the curations waiting for a start
	// ([]CurateQueued as JSON, oldest first, one per repository).
	KVNotesCurateQueue = "notes.curate_queue"

	// CurateTriggerStale is the daemon's follow-up of a stale proposal
	// (notes_proposals.trigger_reason).
	CurateTriggerStale = "stale"

	// QueuedJudge is why a curation waits (CurateQueued.Why) while a round
	// of the repository is in its judge stage.
	QueuedJudge = "judge"
	// QueuedBusy is why a curation waits (CurateQueued.Why) while another
	// learn job runs: a curation, the retro, a skill edit or revert, or a
	// skill gate.
	QueuedBusy = "busy"
	// QueuedDrain is why a curation waits (CurateQueued.Why) while the
	// daemon drains for a restart: asked for during the drain, it starts
	// after the restart (or once the drain is lifted without one).
	QueuedDrain = "drain"
	// QueuedGitHub is why a curation waits (CurateQueued.Why) while a
	// watch's poll identity's GitHub budget is below [github] budget_floor:
	// it starts once the budget recovered (github_floor.go).
	QueuedGitHub = "github"
)
const (
	KVDaemonPausedAt   = "daemon.paused_at"
	KVDaemonPausedHeld = "daemon.paused_held"
)
    KVDaemonPausedAt holds when the running `magnum pause` began
    (store.FormatTime); a pause renewed while it runs keeps it.
    KVDaemonPausedHeld is how many review requests the pause holds
    (pauseHeldRequest), rewritten by every tick while paused. Both go with the
    pause.

const (
	// KVHerdrPanesMove is the move of magnum's panes that waits (PanesMove
	// as JSON): written by each idle tick whose try stopped short, read by

	KVHerdrPanesMove = "herdr.panes_move"
)
const (
	// PollFailingShown is how long a watch's radar calls must have failed
	// before the screens and `magnum status` show it: a 502 or two between
	// good polls is GitHub's weather, not news.
	PollFailingShown = 10 * time.Minute
)
const (
	// KVPromptsLoadedAt is when the running daemon loaded its prompts
	// (store.FormatTime). KVPromptsChanged counts the prompt and skill files

	// names them, comma-separated. See PromptsLine.

	KVPromptsChanged      = "daemon.prompts_changed"
	KVPromptsChangedFiles = "daemon.prompts_changed_files"
)
const (
	RefundStopped     = "stopped"      // a shutdown, restart, drain or abort stopped the round
	RefundUnprompted  = "unprompted"   // the round failed before any agent was prompted
	RefundRender      = "render"       // a prompt did not render (a prompt edited for another build)
	RefundModelLimits = "model_limits" // every fallback model was limited too: the kind paused
	RefundInfra       = "infra"        // an infrastructure failure paused dispatch
	RefundShell       = "shell"        // a restart kept the checkout under a shell command that still runs

const (
	ReqReview  = "review"
	ReqRelease = "release"
	ReqPin     = "pin"
	ReqUnpin   = "unpin"
	ReqMute    = "mute"
	ReqUnmute  = "unmute"
	ReqCleanup = "cleanup"
	ReqKick    = "kick"
	ReqPause   = "pause"
	ReqResume  = "resume"
	// ReqOpen restores a parked PR for a human (magnum open): see
	// OpenPayload.
	ReqOpen = "open"
	// ReqProvision, ReqRepair and ReqAdopt are `magnum slots provision |
	// repair | adopt` handed to the running daemon (heavy worker).
	ReqProvision = "provision"
	ReqRepair    = "repair"
	ReqAdopt     = "adopt"
	// ReqIdentityVerdict records a `magnum identities check` verdict
	// (IdentityVerdictPayload) as the daemon records its own checks.

	// ReqRetro starts a retro now (RetroPayload, retro.go).
	ReqRetro = "retro"
	// ReqLearnPropose starts a skill edit now (LearnProposePayload,
	// learn_edit.go); ReqLearnLand lands a held proposal and ReqLearnReject
	// rejects a held or gating one, stopping its gate first
	// (LearnDecisionPayload), as `magnum learn --review` asks.
	ReqLearnPropose = "learn_propose"
	ReqLearnLand    = "learn_land"
	ReqLearnReject  = "learn_reject"
	// ReqLearnRevert proposes a revert of a landed version
	// (LearnRevertPayload, learn_revert.go), as `magnum learn --revert`
	// asks.
	ReqLearnRevert = "learn_revert"
	// ReqRestartSessions parks the live sessions of an agent kind so that
	// their next prompt resumes them in new processes
	// (RestartSessionsPayload, session_restart.go), as `magnum
	// restart-sessions` asks.
	ReqRestartSessions = "restart_sessions"
)
    Request kinds (requests.kind) the daemon consumes.

const (
	// KVRetroDay is the local day (store.DayKey) of the last daily retro
	// that finished; the next one waits for another day.
	KVRetroDay = "learn.retro_day"
	// KVRetroLast is the last retro's RetroSummary (JSON).
	KVRetroLast = "learn.retro_last"
)
const (
	// LearnAgentTag tags the retro's agent (agents.Deps.Tag), as "eval"
	// tags a replay's.
	LearnAgentTag = "learn"
)
const (
	// ReqStagingDeploy plans (DryRun) or starts a staging deploy of a PR
	// (StagingDeployPayload); its answer is StagingDeployAnswer.
	ReqStagingDeploy = "staging_deploy"
	// ReqStagingCancel stops a staging deploy's effect

	ReqStagingCancel = "staging_cancel"

    The request kinds of the staging deploys.

const (
	DeltaComments   = "comments"
	DeltaWhitespace = "whitespace"
	DeltaDocs       = "docs"
	// DeltaBase is a push that only merged the base branch into the PR (or
	// rebased it onto the base) and left the PR's own diff against its base
	// as it was (base_merge.go). TrivialDelta never returns it: checkDelta
	// does, from the PR's own diff.
	DeltaBase = "base"
	// DeltaEmpty is a push of at least one commit, ahead of the reviewed
	// commit, that changes no file: an empty commit (re-running CI), or
	// commits whose changes cancel out. Its head has the reviewed commit's
	// tree. TrivialDelta never returns it (it has no files to read):
	// checkDelta does, from GitHub's comparison.
	DeltaEmpty = "empty"
)
    Delta classes ([daemon] skip_trivial_deltas).

const (
	// KVDaemonDraining is set (to the time it started) by `magnum
	// daemon-restart --drain`: no new round starts; the restart, or the
	// command giving up, deletes it.
	KVDaemonDraining = "daemon.draining"
	// KVInfraPausedUntil holds when the infrastructure probe runs next while
	// dispatch is paused for an infrastructure failure (infra.go);
	// KVInfraPausedReason names the cause, KVInfraPausedDetail is the
	// failure's redacted text and KVInfraBackoff the current wait.
	KVInfraPausedUntil  = "daemon.infra_paused_until"
	KVInfraPausedReason = "daemon.infra_paused_reason"
	KVInfraPausedDetail = "daemon.infra_paused_detail"
	KVInfraBackoff      = "daemon.infra_backoff"

	// KVUsageCodexPercent is the Codex budget used (percent, no decimals)
	// as the newest Codex session reported it; KVUsageCodexResetsAt is when
	// the binding window resets (store.FormatTime), KVUsageCodexWindow its
	// length in minutes, KVUsageCodexPlan the plan and KVUsageCodexAt when
	// Codex reported it (budget.go). KVUsageCodexPace24h is the binding
	// window's pace over the last 24 hours (the share of the budget used in
	// them over the share of the window they are, two decimals); absent
	// when Codex's reading from a day ago is unknown or of another window.
	KVUsageCodexPercent  = "usage.codex_percent"
	KVUsageCodexResetsAt = "usage.codex_resets_at"
	KVUsageCodexWindow   = "usage.codex_window_minutes"
	KVUsageCodexPlan     = "usage.codex_plan"
	KVUsageCodexAt       = "usage.codex_at"
	KVUsageCodexPace24h  = "usage.codex_pace_24h"
	// KVUsageCodexOverruledAt is when `magnum resume --tool` lifted a
	// budget-cap pause (store.FormatTime): the caps wait for a snapshot
	// stamped after it (budget.go, overruleBudget).
	KVUsageCodexOverruledAt = "usage.codex_overruled_at"
)
    kv keys of the daemon's own operations, read by `magnum status`.

const (
	ReqApprove        = "approve"
	ReqRequestChanges = "request_changes"
)
    Manual verdicts: `magnum approve` and `magnum request-changes` (and
    the board's A and C) post the reviewer's own verdict on the head magnum
    reviewed, as the PR's posting identity, for a repository whose policy only
    lets magnum comment or when the reviewer disagrees with its event. On a
    PR GitHub blocks on the operator's own approval (an App's never counts),
    an approval goes as the watch's auto_approve_as instead (approveAsOperator).

const (
	WaitQuiet         = "quiet"          // the push quiet period
	WaitBurst         = "burst"          // the longer quiet period after a burst of pushes
	WaitInterval      = "interval"       // the minimum re-review interval since the last round
	WaitDraftInterval = "draft_interval" // the same for a draft
	WaitOwnInterval   = "own_interval"   // the same for the operator's own PR
	WaitSnoozed       = "snoozed"        // magnum snooze: no automatic round until it ends
	WaitCap           = "cap"            // the daily round cap
	WaitDelta         = "delta"          // the re-review threshold: a small delta waits for more
	WaitRequested     = "requested"      // a review request (or ready for review): the debounce, then the next dispatch
	WaitReplies       = "replies"        // replies on the review: the reply debounce after the last one
	WaitReplyInterval = "reply_interval" // one reply round per PR and head every reply_min_interval
	WaitCIRed         = "ci_red"         // CI turned red after the review: its judge check starts at the next dispatch
	WaitRetry         = "retry"          // the backoff after a failed round
	WaitMuted         = "muted"          // magnum mute
	WaitQuietHours    = "quiet_hours"    // [daemon] quiet_hours
	WaitPaused        = "paused"         // magnum pause, or an infrastructure pause past its probe time
	WaitDraining      = "draining"       // magnum daemon-restart --drain: no round starts until the restart
	WaitInfra         = "infra"          // an infrastructure failure paused dispatch
	WaitHerdr         = "herdr"          // herdr is unreachable
	WaitKind          = "kind"           // an agent kind the round needs is paused
	WaitBudget        = "budget"         // the Codex budget's soft cap holds full re-reviews
	WaitGitHub        = "github"         // an identity's GitHub budget is below [github] budget_floor: no round starts until its reset
	WaitIdentity      = "identity"       // the posting identity is unhealthy
	WaitSlot          = "slot"           // the PR's slot, or a free pool slot
	WaitPinned        = "pinned"         // the PR's slot is pinned (magnum open, magnum pin): the round waits for the unpin
	WaitCapacity      = "capacity"       // max_concurrent_reviews or max_total_working_codex
	WaitFixing        = "fixing"         // the fix job's fixer works on the PR (fix.go): its re-review comes after
	WaitWhiteboard    = "whiteboard"     // the whiteboard job writes the PR's whiteboard (whiteboard.go): the round comes after
	WaitOther         = "other"          // any other dispatch gate (details, a human, a paused watch, ...)
	WaitNext          = "next"           // nothing holds it: the next dispatch starts it
)
    Wait reasons (Wait.Reason).

const (
	KVWebhooksCursor = "webhooks.cursor"
	KVWebhooksHealth = "webhooks.health"
	KVWebhooksHours  = "webhooks.hours"
)
    The consumer's kv keys: the cursor it reads after (webhooksCursor),
    the stream's health (WebhooksHealth) and the hourly totals (WebhooksHour).

const (

	// WebhooksKeepHours is how many hourly totals are kept.
	WebhooksKeepHours = 24
)
const ApprovalDismissMessage = "magnum: new commits since this approval; a re-review follows"
    ApprovalDismissMessage is the reason a dismissed approval shows on GitHub.

const AutofixBy = "autofix"
    AutofixBy is who starts a loop autofix starts (FixState.By, and the "by" of
    its fix.start event); any other is a start by hand (`magnum fix`, f on the
    board). The factory's stats count the two apart.

const BudgetOverruledNote = "the Codex budget caps wait for Codex's next reading"
    BudgetOverruledNote is what a resume of a budget-cap pause means (the CLI's
    offline resume says it too).

const CIFixDry = "dry run: would fix the failed CI of "
    CIFixDry is how the words of a CI fix's plan start (CIFixPlan.Text).

const CLIChangeRecent = 24 * time.Hour
    CLIChangeRecent is how long a change of a kind's CLI is news: `magnum
    status` says "(changed at 11:24)", and a launch failure of one of the kind's
    roles that parks a PR names it (attention.CLIChange).

const EvPRMuted = "pr.muted"
    EvPRMuted is the event a mute records, its reason in the data's "reason"
    (requestMute); the board's card shows the latest one's next to the flag.

const EventCodexHooksUntrusted = "codex.hooks_untrusted"
    EventCodexHooksUntrusted (warn, subject tool:codex) says, once per
    hooks.json fingerprint, that the hooks without a trust entry of a Codex home
    hold new Codex sessions (data: hooks, the fingerprint; places; roles).

const EventKindVersionChanged = "kind.version_changed"
    EventKindVersionChanged is recorded (subject tool:<kind>) when an agent
    kind's CLI reports another version than the one recorded (KVKindVersion):
    the kind, the versions and the binary. It is a warning, with one toast,
    when mise pins the CLI (cliPin; the pin and its config file too), and info
    without a toast otherwise: a routine update.

const EventKindVersionUnknown = "kind.version_unknown"
    EventKindVersionUnknown is recorded (warn, subject tool:<kind>) once when
    reading an agent kind's CLI version failed at cliVersionUnknownAfter health
    checks in a row (the one at the daemon's start counts): the kind, the number
    of failed checks, the binary and the last failure. The reads go on at every
    check.

const EventMemoryPressure = "machine.memory_pressure"
    EventMemoryPressure is recorded at each change of the machine's memory
    pressure level, a new level counting once two samples in a row read it:
    the first known level since the daemon started (info, at once), a return to
    normal (info), warn (warn) and critical (error; the one urgent toast of a
    run of critical goes out at its first critical sample). A sample whose level
    is unknown changes nothing.

const EventSharedFailure = "agents.shared_failure"
    EventSharedFailure is recorded (warn) when two or more PRs' agent launches
    ended with the same pane line within sharedFailureWindow, once per line
    within sharedFailureQuiet: the PRs, the roles and the line (data last_line,
    prs, roles); its subject is tool:<kind> when the roles share one agent kind.

const FixModeCI = "ci"
    FixModeCI is the mode of a fix loop's first cycle that fixes the PR's failed
    required CI (FixState.Mode, FixPayload.Mode).

const FixModeMerge = "merge"
    FixModeMerge is the mode of a fix request and loop that merges the PR's
    parent alone (FixPayload.Mode, FixState.Mode).

const FormerDismissMessage = "magnum: superseded by the review of %s posted as %s (this PR's reviewer changed)"
    FormerDismissMessage is the reason a dismissed review of a former identity
    shows on GitHub; the arguments are the new review's commit (short) and the
    login it was posted as.

const HeldMergeFile = "held-merge.diff"
    HeldMergeFile is the file in the PR's report directory
    (paths.Layout.PRReviews) that shows what a held merge does to the workflow
    files: the merge, how the fixer resolved their conflicts, then what its push
    changes in them. The screens' e opens it in the pager.

const HooksOverruledNote = "new Codex sessions start although hooks.json has hooks without a trust entry, until it changes again"
    HooksOverruledNote is what a resume that overrules the hold means, as its
    answer says it.

const HooksReviewPauseReason = "hooks_review"
    HooksReviewPauseReason is the codex kind's pause reason while a hook of
    the hooks.json of a Codex home its session roles read has no trust entry
    (checkCodexHooksTrust). The check renews it and ends it; it has no end of
    its own.

const KVCodexSessionIDsMissing = "codex.session_ids_missing"
    KVCodexSessionIDsMissing is when the run of Codex sessions without a session
    id the daemon warned of started (store.FormatTime); absent when there is no
    such run.

const KVDaemonHooks = "daemon.hooks"
    KVDaemonHooks is the running daemon's hook listener as its start found it,
    DaemonHooks's JSON, for `magnum status`; absent when the start took no claim
    (a dry run).

const KVDaemonShellPATH = "daemon.shell_path"
    KVDaemonShellPATH is what the running daemon took from the login shell's
    PATH at its start, as ShellPATH's JSON (the count, never a directory);
    absent with [daemon] shell_path off.

const KVDaemonWork = "daemon.work"
    KVDaemonWork holds the work in flight that no registry row shows (WorkMark
    as JSON), which the CLI reads before it stops the daemon: the jobs queued or
    running on the heavy worker and the GitHub writes as the operator under way.
    The engine keeps it to its own state (beginWork): written whenever that
    changes, deleted when nothing is in flight, at the shutdown and at every
    start of the daemon.

const KVLearnEditing = "learn.editing"
    KVLearnEditing holds the skill edit running now (EditMark as JSON), which
    the CLI reads before it stops the daemon: set when it starts, deleted when
    it ends and at every start of the daemon.

const KVLearnGating = "learn.gating"
    KVLearnGating holds the gate of a skill proposal running now (GateMark as
    JSON), which the CLI reads before it stops the daemon: set when it starts,
    deleted when it ends and at every start of the daemon (the proposal stays
    gating, and its gate starts again).

const KVLearnRegression = "learn.regression"
    KVLearnRegression is the newest version a regression revert was proposed for
    (its id): the scan proposes one revert per version, never two.

const KVMachineMemory = "machine.memory"
    KVMachineMemory holds the daemon's newest memory sample (MemorySample,
    JSON), which `magnum status` shows on its memory line.

const KVRetroRunning = "learn.retro_running"
    KVRetroRunning holds the start of the retro running now (store.FormatTime),
    which the CLI reads before it stops the daemon: set by the tick or the
    request that sees it started, deleted by the first one that sees it ended,
    at a restart for a new build, at shutdown and at every start of the daemon.

const KVStagingDeploys = "staging.deploy.*"
    KVStagingDeploys matches every staging deploy's record (KVStagingDeploy) in
    one KVValues read.

const KVStagingResolves = "staging.resolve.*"
    KVStagingResolves matches every staging resolver job's row
    (kvStagingResolve) in one KVValues read: StagingResolverSays reads them for
    the card and `magnum staging`.

const ReqCodexFlag = "codex-flag"
    ReqCodexFlag flags a PR or clears its flag (CodexFlagPayload).

const ReqFix = "fix"
    ReqFix starts a fix loop on a PR, or switches the fix job off or on for it
    (FixPayload).

const ReqSnooze = "snooze"
    ReqSnooze snoozes a PR or lifts its snooze (SnoozePayload).

const ReqUnapprove = "unapprove"
    ReqUnapprove is `magnum unapprove` and the board's D (UnapprovePayload).

const ReqWhiteboard = "whiteboard"
    ReqWhiteboard starts the whiteboard job on a PR's reviewed head
    (WhiteboardPayload).

const RequestReadyForReview = "(ready for review)"
    RequestReadyForReview is KVPRRequestBy for a draft that became ready for
    review.

const SkipIgnored = "ignored"
    SkipIgnored is the skip_reason `magnum ignore` stores on a muted PR:
    classify keeps it instead of the generic "muted", and the board shows such a
    PR as ignored.

const StagingAll = "all"
    StagingAll asks for every staging env of the PR's repository.

const StagingDeployWait = 10 * time.Minute
    StagingDeployWait is how long a staging deploy waits for its answer: the CLI
    waits that long, and a deploy asked longer ago is refused (nobody waits for
    it any more).

const StagingResolvePrompt = "staging-resolve.md"
    StagingResolvePrompt is the staging resolver's prompt file.

const StagingResolverWords = "the resolver merges it first (at most 2 tries)"
    StagingResolverWords say, in a few words, what becomes of a conflict
    at a deploy (the 2 tries are internal/staging's bound, maxResolveTry):
    the question and the plan name them.

const WhiteboardCommand = "whiteboard"
    WhiteboardCommand is the Whiteboard CLI magnum runs: `whiteboard` on PATH
    (the daemon's LaunchAgent PATH has ~/.local/bin).


VARIABLES

var (
	// ErrFixReportMarker is the error for a report whose first line is not the
	// marker of the run asked for: another run wrote it, or none did.
	ErrFixReportMarker = errors.New("fix report: the first line is not the run's marker")
	// ErrFixReportPartial is the error for a report with a section missing,
	// empty or out of order, as when the fixer ran out of time before it
	// finished writing.
	ErrFixReportPartial = errors.New("fix report: a section is missing")
)
var (
	// ErrNotesChanged: the notes are not what the decider saw.
	ErrNotesChanged = errors.New("the notes changed since the proposal was reviewed")
	// ErrTargetChanged: the state the apply would write is not the one the
	// decider approved (its fingerprint differs).
	ErrTargetChanged = errors.New("the state to write is not the one that was approved")
	// ErrStaleConflict: the notes changed since the proposal was made and
	// its changes conflict with theirs; it cannot be applied.
	ErrStaleConflict = errors.New("the notes changed since the proposal was made, and the changes conflict")
)
    Errors of ApplyNotesProposal.

var DeltaClasses = config.TrivialDeltaClasses
    DeltaClasses lists every class, the default of skip_trivial_deltas
    (config.TrivialDeltaClasses, the list the configuration accepts).

var ErrClassifierDown = errors.New("engine: the retro's classifier is not available")
    ErrClassifierDown wraps a Classifier's error that is not the PR's: the agent
    could not be set up or started, or went away (herdr down, a prompt refused
    before it was sent). The retro stops without recording the PR.

var ErrCriticDown = errors.New("engine: the notes critic is not available")
    ErrCriticDown wraps a Critic's error that is not the decision's: the agent
    could not be set up or started, or went away.

var ErrCuratorDown = errors.New("engine: the notes curator is not available")
    ErrCuratorDown wraps a Curator's error that is not the proposal's: the agent
    could not be set up or started, or went away.

var ErrEditorDown = errors.New("engine: the skill editor is not available")
    ErrEditorDown wraps an Editor's error that is not the edit's: the agent
    could not be set up or started, or went away.

var ErrEvalLayout = errors.New("engine: magnum eval needs a scratch layout (paths.Layout.Scratch), never the live registry")
    ErrEvalLayout: RunEval needs an engine built on a scratch layout.

var ErrOpsLockHeld = errors.New("a magnum command holds state/ops.lock for in-process slot work; exiting so launchd starts the daemon again")
    ErrOpsLockHeld is what Run returns when the daemon lock is held by a magnum
    command running slot work in-process (it holds layout.OpsLock() too):
    the daemon exits non-zero so launchd starts it again once that work is done.

var ErrRestartForBuild = errors.New("a new build is on disk and nothing is in flight; exiting for launchd to start it")
    ErrRestartForBuild is what Tick and Run return when the daemon exits for a
    new build on disk ([daemon] restart_on_new_build): the exit is non-zero,
    so launchd starts the new binary.

var ErrRestartForConfig = errors.New("a config was saved and nothing is in flight; exiting for launchd to start the daemon on it")
    ErrRestartForConfig is what Tick and Run return when the daemon exits
    to restart on a saved config (KVConfigRestart): the exit is non-zero,
    so launchd starts it again, and the new daemon reads the saved file.

var ErrRestartForLearn = errors.New("a skill version landed and nothing is in flight; exiting for launchd to start the daemon on it")
    ErrRestartForLearn is what Tick and Run return when the daemon exits
    to restart on a landed skill version (learn restart idle): the exit is
    non-zero, so launchd starts it again, and the new daemon reads the landed
    prompts and skill.

var ErrRestartForPanes = errors.New("magnum's panes moved to another herdr session and nothing is in flight; exiting for launchd to start the daemon there")
    ErrRestartForPanes is what Tick and Run return once the daemon moved
    magnum's panes to the herdr session the config names: the exit is non-zero,
    so launchd starts it again, and the new daemon's App opens its panes there.

var ErrSchemaChanged = errors.New("schema migrated under the daemon; exiting for launchd to restart")
    ErrSchemaChanged is what Tick and Run return once another magnum binary
    migrated the registry under the running daemon (store.SchemaChanged):
    this binary's queries target the old schema, so the daemon exits non-zero
    and launchd starts it again from the new binary.

var EvalObserveEvery = 10 * time.Second
    EvalObserveEvery is how often RunEval observes herdr during a replay.

var RetroObserveEvery = 10 * time.Second
    RetroObserveEvery is how often the retro's agent is observed.

var WaitingStates = []string{store.ProposalPending, store.ProposalApplying}
    WaitingStates are the states of a proposal that waits for a decision or is
    being applied: a repository with one gets no new curation or recovery.


FUNCTIONS

func AcquireLock(path string) (unlock func(), held bool, err error)
    AcquireLock takes a non-blocking exclusive flock on path (the daemon uses
    layout.Lock(); the CLI takes the same lock before running slot or cleanup
    operations in-process). held reports that another process has it; unlock
    releases it.

func ApplyNotesProposal(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, nr notes.Repo, p store.NotesProposal, a NotesApply) (store.NotesProposal, error)
    ApplyNotesProposal applies proposal id (p, as the decider reviewed it)
    to nr's notes, decided by a.By, under the notes lock: the proposal
    must still be pending (else ProposalDecidedError), the notes must be
    what the decider saw (ErrNotesChanged), the state to write the one it
    approved (ErrTargetChanged) and a clean merge when the proposal is stale
    (ErrStaleConflict), and a curation must lose no line (NotPreservedError).
    Then the claim, the write and the record: the notes as found are recorded
    first (an import, when the registry did not hold them), and the state
    written is recorded as a version (a curation's, or the operator's for a
    restore) linked to the proposal. A write that fails is settled by what the
    notes hold afterwards (settleFailedWrite): as found, the claim is released
    and the proposal waits again; as meant to be written, the apply goes on;
    any other state, the proposal stays applying for the recovery.

func ApplyTarget(check StaleCheck) (notes.State, bool)
    ApplyTarget is what applying p writes to the notes now (check): its proposed
    state, or when it is stale its merge with the notes' changes since; false
    when that merge conflicts.

func ApproveAsFor(cfg *config.Config, fullName string) *config.Identity
    ApproveAsFor is the identity A (on a row GitHub blocks on the operator)
    and `magnum approve --as` post the operator's own approval of repository
    fullName's PRs as: the covering watch's auto_approve_as, whether or not its
    auto_approve names the repository; nil when the watch names none (GitHub
    then counts only an approval by hand).

func AutoApprovalMarker(head string) string
    AutoApprovalMarker is the marker of an automatic approval of head: "<!--
    magnum:auto-approval head=<sha7> -->".

func BudgetKinds(cfg *config.Config) []string
    BudgetKinds are cfg's declared agent kinds backed by Codex: the usage caps
    hold them (their pause holds every role whose AgentKind is one of them,
    shell roles with tool = "codex" included), and a resume of one overrules
    Codex's reading at a cap (liftToolPause, the CLI's offline resume).

func CIConfigPath(p string) bool
    CIConfigPath reports whether p, a path a PR or a push changes, is CI config
    a CI fix never changes, in any case: a file GitHub Actions runs as the head
    has it (changesActions) or a script of .github/bin that a workflow runs.
    The look gives no CI fix to a PR that changes one (ciFixRefusal: its fixer
    could only answer config, and spend one of 3), and `magnum push --ci`
    refuses a push that changes one from the base's.

func CheckPrompts(cfg *config.Config) (int, error)
    CheckPrompts renders, with representative data and this binary's renderer,
    every prompt file the configured roles name (judges with agents.JudgeData,
    other session roles with agents.RoleData in each mode, shell roles' command
    or full-line template through agents.ShellLine), the model-fallback prompt,
    the triage prompt, the retro prompt, the notes curation prompt,
    the skill editor's prompt and every identity's review footer template
    (config.RenderFooter, which magnum renders after each verified review).
    Each template is rendered twice, once with every field set and once with
    the optional ones empty, so both sides of an {{if}} run. It returns how many
    renders passed and every failure, joined: a template field this binary's
    data lacks (a prompt edited for a newer build) fails here instead of in a
    round.

func ClearModelLimits(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, kind string) ([]string, error)
    ClearModelLimits deletes the per-model limits recorded for kind
    (agents.KVModelLimited rows indexed by agents.KVModelLimits) with what they
    were (agents.KVModelLimitedAt, so a limit after the clear is no repeat
    that doubles), so new sessions start on their roles' models again and live
    ones switch back before their next prompt. It returns the models that were
    limited. `magnum resume --tool` runs it (through the daemon, or directly
    when no daemon runs).

func ContentOf(s notes.State) store.NotesContent
    ContentOf is a notes state as the registry stores it.

func CriticAttempts(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, id int64) (int, error)
    CriticAttempts counts proposal id's undecided critiques: at
    CriticMaxAttempts the proposal is left to the operator for good.

func CriticDeclines(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, repoID int64) int
    CriticDeclines counts the proposals of repoID the critic rejected or
    sent back in a row, newest first: an apply by anyone or a decision of
    the operator ends the run; magnum's own decisions (an expiry, an invalid
    proposal, a stale follow-up) and waiting proposals neither count nor end it.
    At notes critic_declines the critic steps back: the repository's next
    proposal waits for the operator.

func DaemonPID(layout paths.Layout) (int, error)
    DaemonPID returns the pid of the running daemon from the pidfile, or 0 when
    there is no pidfile or that process is gone. It never touches the lock
    (probing it could make a starting daemon exit as "already running").

func DeciderName(by string) string
    DeciderName says who decided a proposal (store.DecidedBy*), for a sentence:
    "you", "the critic", "magnum".

func DeltaLabel(classes []string) string
    DeltaLabel is how a review note and events name the classes: "comments
    only", "whitespace only", "docs only", "base merge only", "comments and
    whitespace only", "comments, whitespace and docs only". The order is always
    comments, whitespace, docs, base, whatever the order given; unknown classes
    are left out and no known class at all is "". The class empty stands alone
    (checkDelta never combines it) and is "no file changes".

func DrainerAlive(pid int) bool
    DrainerAlive reports whether the drainer pid still runs as a magnum process.
    A pid that is gone, or that now belongs to another program (pids are
    reused), is not; a process ps cannot describe counts as alive (the drain
    stays: lifting it by mistake would start rounds the restart then abandons).

func EditNext(editor bool, evidence, editDay string, now time.Time) string
    EditNext says when the scheduled editor runs next, for `magnum learn` and
    its JSON: from learn editor, the evidence mark (KVLearnEvidence) and the day
    of its last start (KVLearnEditDay).

func FileModTime(path string) (time.Time, bool)
    FileModTime is SkewNote's reader of a binary's mtime on disk.

func FixCalls(st FixState, prURL, ref string) []attention.FixCall
    FixCalls are the calls of the findings the fixer of the loop st left to
    the author when it pushed (FixState.NeedsYou, kept while the loop waits
    for the re-review of its push), with those its earlier cycles left and
    the loop carries (FixState.Carried, each call once: loopCalls), as the
    loop's end names them: the files beside each report place their threads,
    prURL is the PR's page and ref how `magnum fix` names it, and a thread the
    settle found answered (FixState.Answered) asks only for the resolution,
    as the settle's toast said: no thread is read again here. None for entries
    magnum cannot read so.

func FixNeedsAsked(msg string, entries []string) []string
    FixNeedsAsked keeps of entries, the "## Needs you" of the fixer's report
    that msg (a fix job's message, a PR's last_error) names, those that
    msg still asks the author for. The settle and the loop's end leave out
    the entries whose magnum thread is resolved or that the fixer answered
    (freshNeedsYou, dropFixerAnswered) before they write the message, and its
    first line names each one left: by its call's link or its comment id in the
    older words (needsYouNames), a conflict by its paths, and the entries magnum
    cannot read by their count, whatever the loop's own words before them.
    A message that only counts them keeps all of entries when it counts them
    all and none otherwise, since it cannot say which went; one that asks for no
    call keeps none. The factory screen draws what it keeps.

func FormerIdentities(v string) []string
    FormerIdentities is the identity names v, a value of KVPRFormerIdentities,
    holds (nil when v is empty or unreadable): the engine's and `magnum
    comment`'s one reader of it.

func GitHubOpWords(op string) string
    GitHubOpWords is op in the words `magnum status` shows: an engine label
    in plain words ("round.setup": "round setup"), a call's own kind as it is
    ("radar", "details").

func HeldFixStarts(raw string) string
    HeldFixStarts is when the held fix raw (a KVPRFixHeld value) starts,
    for `magnum fix --wait`: "after the restart" for a drain's, "when the GitHub
    budget recovers" for the GitHub budget's, "when claude's pause ends" for the
    fixer's pause.

func HeldMergeRef(prID int64) string
    HeldMergeRef is the ref that keeps the held merge of the PR whose
    registry id is prID from git gc, in the clone its objects live in: under
    refs/magnum/held/, never under refs/heads or refs/remotes, and by the id,
    so no repository's name (".github") makes a name git refuses.

func HeldReviewID(v string) (int64, bool)
    HeldReviewID is the review a KVPRApprovalHold value names: the one whose
    approval waits for the full pass after it, while it is the PR's latest
    (heldReviewOf's rule, which the board's FINDINGS follows: a later review
    drops the record, and one left behind names an older review). ok is false
    for a value that names none.

func InfraCause(err error) string
    InfraCause names the infrastructure failure err reports, "" for none of
    the known patterns (an SSH key refused, then the network's: DNS, timeouts
    and refusals, TLS, a server curl could not reach): what pauses the review
    daemon's dispatch, for the factory's infrastructure hold.

func KVGitHubCost(identity string) string
    KVGitHubCost holds the cost record of one identity's GitHub calls
    (GitHubCost as JSON).

func KVGitHubLow(identity string) string
    KVGitHubLow holds identity's run of low budget (GitHubLow as JSON), from
    the tick that found its budget below github budget_floor until the one that
    finds it recovered (noteGitHubBudget), written at once, apart from the cost
    record the flush writes once a minute.

func KVKindHold(kind string) string
    KVKindHold holds kind's hold (KindHold, JSON) while it lasts.

func KVKindHoldLifted(kind string) string
    KVKindHoldLifted holds when kind's last hold was lifted: only launch lines
    after it hold the kind again, so the lines that held it, still within
    sharedFailureWindow, do not hold it again at once.

func KVKindVersion(kind string) string
    KVKindVersion holds what the daemon last read of agent kind kind's CLI
    version (KindVersion, JSON).

func KVNotesCriticOver(fullName string) string
    KVNotesCriticOver marks a repository whose notes a critic apply left past a
    limit: the apply's time. Its next over_limit curation waits a week from it,
    so a busy repository does not cost a curation and a critique a day.

func KVNotesMisses(fullName string) string
    KVNotesMisses marks a repository whose retro recorded misses for its notes:
    the time of the retro that did (store.FormatTime). The misses trigger
    curates it, and a curation that began after that time clears it.

func KVNotesOver(fullName string) string
    KVNotesOver holds the notes limits a repository's notes are past,
    comma-separated ("max_bytes,max_line"): the mark a curation looks for.
    It is set when they are measured past a limit and deleted when they are back
    within all of them.

func KVNotesRecurate(fullName string) string
    KVNotesRecurate marks a repository whose proposal the critic rejected or
    sent back: the proposal's id. The next curation scan starts a curation of
    trigger review (dueCurations); a curation that stores its proposal clears
    it.

func KVPRApprovalHold(prID int64) string
    KVPRApprovalHold holds the PR's held review whose full pass follows
    (heldReview as JSON); any later review that posts deletes it.

func KVPRAttention(prID int64) string
    KVPRAttention holds why the engine parked a PR in needs_attention (the kind
    attention.Explain takes: failed, blocked, identity_error, …); read only
    while the PR is in that state.

func KVPRAutoApproveRefused(prID int64) string
    KVPRAutoApproveRefused holds why auto-approval does not approve the PR as
    the operator although its review left nothing to fix (AutoApproveRefused as
    JSON); the board's card says it.

func KVPRDelta(prID int64) string
    KVPRDelta holds the size of a PR's unreviewed delta (DeltaRecord as JSON),
    which the re-review threshold reads ([daemon] rereview_min_lines).

func KVPRDeltaCheck(prID int64) string
    KVPRDeltaCheck holds the delta check a PR's round in flight runs
    (DeltaCheckRound as JSON), which `magnum status` reads while the PR is in
    flight; the round's end deletes it.

func KVPRFix(prID int64) string
    KVPRFix holds a PR's fix loop (FixState as JSON).

func KVPRFixHeld(prID int64) string
    KVPRFixHeld holds a fix that could not start yet (heldFix as JSON):
    a `magnum fix` a drain for a restart held until the restart, or the drain's
    end without one, starts it; a `magnum fix` or an autofix the GitHub budget
    held until it recovers; one the fixer's paused kind held until the pause
    ends.

func KVPRFixOff(prID int64) string
    KVPRFixOff holds a PR's opt-out of the fix job (FixOff as JSON).

func KVPRFormerIdentities(prID int64) string
    KVPRFormerIdentities holds the identities a PR posted as before it migrated
    to its current one (a JSON list of identity names, newest last).

func KVPRHeldMerge(prID int64) string
    KVPRHeldMerge holds the merge of the PR's parent that magnum holds for your
    y (HeldMerge as JSON).

func KVPRIdentityPinned(prID int64) string
    KVPRIdentityPinned holds the identity `magnum review --as` pinned the PR to;
    a pinned PR never migrates.

func KVPRManualVerdict(prID int64) string
    KVPRManualVerdict holds the id of the review a manual verdict posted: rounds
    never dismiss it as their own stale review (it is the reviewer's decision),
    while an approval still follows the head (approval.go).

func KVPROpen(prID int64) string
    KVPROpen holds autofix = "open"'s verdict on an own PR (OpenVerdict as
    JSON), written by the engine's look; no row for a PR the look does not
    cover.

func KVPROpenHold(prID int64) string
    KVPROpenHold holds the hold `magnum open` set on a PR it restored (OpenHold
    as JSON).

func KVPRReplyRound(prID int64) string
    KVPRReplyRound holds the last reply round of a PR (ReplyRound as JSON):
    the head it ran on and when it started, for reply_min_interval, and whether
    a continued turn of it may still end replied.

func KVPRRequestAt(prID int64) string
    KVPRRequestAt holds the time of the newest review request magnum handled
    for a PR (the edge it reacted to); KVPRRequestBy who asked: the login of the
    request's actor (else the reviewer it named), or RequestReadyForReview.

func KVPRRequestBy(prID int64) string
func KVPRSkippedBaseline(prID int64) string
    KVPRSkippedBaseline marks a baseline PR skipBaseline made ineligible:
    its value is the head it was skipped on.

func KVPRSnooze(prID int64) string
    KVPRSnooze holds a PR's snooze (Snooze as JSON).

func KVPRStaging(prID int64) string
    KVPRStaging holds where the PR stands on its repository's staging envs
    as the review daemon last told it (StagingRecord as JSON): written when
    it changes, dropped once the PR is no longer open. The board and `magnum
    staging` read it (StagingShown); the daemon alone writes it.

func KVPRStalemate(prID int64) string
    KVPRStalemate holds the threads of a PR where magnum stopped arguing and
    the operator has not acted since (Stalemate as JSON); the board flags the PR
    while it is set.

func KVPRTrivial(prID int64) string
    KVPRTrivial holds the last push magnum skipped as trivial for a PR
    (TrivialSkip as JSON), for the PR card; a review posted afterwards deletes
    it.

func KVPRWait(prID int64) string
    KVPRWait holds why a waiting PR has no round yet (Wait as JSON).

func KVPRWhiteboard(prID int64) string
    KVPRWhiteboard holds the whiteboard of a PR's latest written head
    (WhiteboardRecord as JSON).

func KVStagingDeploy(id string) string
    KVStagingDeploy is effect id's record: StagingDeployRecord as JSON,
    its event of the newest Seq. The review daemon alone writes it.

func KickDaemon(layout paths.Layout) (int, error)
    KickDaemon asks the running daemon for a tick now (SIGUSR1, `magnum kick`);
    it returns the daemon's pid, or 0 when none runs. The pidfile can outlive
    the daemon (SIGKILL) and its pid be reused, and SIGUSR1 terminates a process
    that does not handle it: the pid is signalled only after ps shows a magnum
    daemon, as `magnum daemon stop` checks.

func LiveAgents(live []store.Session) (n, working int)
    LiveAgents counts the registry's live sessions (starting or live,
    as Store.LiveSessions lists them) and those of them herdr last saw working;
    the others are idle.

func LooksLikeDaemon(comm, args string) bool
    LooksLikeDaemon reports whether a process is a magnum daemon from what
    ProcessCommand read: the executable (comm) is named magnum, the command
    line starts with it (so a path with spaces is one word) and its first
    argument that is not a flag is "daemon" (--config takes a value). An editor
    opening a file named magnum ("/usr/bin/vim /tmp/magnum daemon") is not one:
    its executable is vim.

func LooksLikeDaemonArgs(args []string, sub ...string) bool
    LooksLikeDaemonArgs reports whether the arguments after the executable
    name the subcommand sub: the arguments that are not flags start with sub,
    word for word (--config takes a value). No sub names nothing.

func LooksLikeMagnum(comm, args string, sub ...string) bool
    LooksLikeMagnum is LooksLikeDaemon for any subcommand path: the executable
    is magnum and the first arguments that are not flags are sub, as in
    LooksLikeMagnum(comm, args, "factory", "daemon").

func NotesDir(l paths.Layout, owner, repo string) string
    NotesDir is the harness directory next to the notes file: the notes path
    without ".md". "" under the same conditions as NotesPath.

func NotesLockPath(l paths.Layout, owner, repo string) string
    NotesLockPath is the lock of the notes file: the harness directory with
    ".lock". "" under the same conditions as NotesPath. The judge takes it
    with agents.NotesLockLine, which derives the same path from the notes file
    (agents.NotesFiles).

func NotesPath(l paths.Layout, owner, repo string) string
    NotesPath is the repository notes file of owner/repo under l, "" when l
    has no home or owner or repo is not a single plain path element (empty,
    "." or "..", or containing a path separator), which GitHub names never are.

func NotesRoot(l paths.Layout) string
    NotesRoot is the directory holding every repository's notes, "" when l names
    no place (paths.Layout.Valid).

func OpenHolds(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store) (map[int64]OpenHold, error)
    OpenHolds reads every PR's hold record in one query, by PR id; a record it
    cannot read is left out. A record of a PR no longer pinned holds nothing
    (the next tick drops it): callers read it beside the PR's pin.

func OpenMergeIsYours(g *store.ReviewGate) bool
    OpenMergeIsYours reports whether GitHub's review gate g leaves the merge of
    an own PR with nothing open to the operator (rule 12's "merge is yours"):
    approved, or read with no decision (a base that requires no review); not
    before magnum read it (nil), nor while it still wants a review or changes.
    The board reads it with the look's idle verdict, as the factory screen's
    wait on your merge does.

func OpenRestorable(cfg *config.Config, full string) func(string) bool
    OpenRestorable reports whether a parked session of a role may stand in for
    the judge's in `magnum open` of a PR of repository full (OpenRestoreRole):
    the role is one the daemon's open restores, one the repository's watch
    runs (config.Config.RolesFor). Park parks every session with a session id,
    the fixer's, the whiteboard writer's and a judge's in reserve too, and the
    daemon refuses those roles ("unknown role"). Without a config any role may.

func OpenRestoreRole(all []store.Session, role string, restorable func(string) bool) string
    OpenRestoreRole is the role `magnum open` without --role restores the
    PR through when role, the one it would open, has nothing to open:
    its newest session is lost or closed, none of its sessions is parked or up,
    and no session of the PR is starting or live (a live pane is what the open
    focuses). The newest parked session by started_at (the later one of two
    that started together) of a role the daemon's open restores (restorable,
    OpenRestorable) then stands in for it; with none, role stays and the open
    refuses, as it did. A role named with --role is never replaced.

func OpenRole(cfg *config.Config, full string, fix *FixState, all []store.Session) string
    OpenRole is the role `magnum open` of a PR of repository full opens without
    --role, as the CLI's open resolves it under cfg: the fixer's while a fix
    loop's fixer works (fix: the PR's loop, nil for none), else the watch's
    judge; the parked role that stands in for it when its session is gone
    (OpenRestoreRole over all, the PR's sessions, among the roles the daemon's
    open restores, OpenRestorable).

func OpenSessions(all []store.Session, role string) (parked, latest *store.Session, starting bool)
    OpenSessions is what the PR's sessions of role say an open of it does:
    latest is the newest, parked the newest parked one, and starting says the
    newest is starting or live (the open waits for its pane). An open restores
    when one is parked and none is starting (OpenWouldRestore).

func OpenWouldRestore(all []store.Session, role string, restorable func(string) bool) bool
    OpenWouldRestore reports whether `magnum open` of role (as it opens
    without --role) asks the daemon to restore the PR (claim a slot, resume
    its sessions, hold it): no session of role is up (starting, or live with a
    pane or an agent: the open focuses it), and one is parked, role's own or,
    when role's session is gone, a restorable role's (OpenRestoreRole).
    The screens' o asks first when it does.

func OperatorApprovalRefusal(pr store.PR, sum *store.ReviewSummary, login string) string
    OperatorApprovalRefusal says why the operator's own approval of pr cannot
    be posted as login (their auto_approve_as account) now, "" when it can:
    auto-approval's preconditions (autoApproveRefusal), less the two that exist
    only because auto-approval acts without asking. The operator's stop (their
    changes request or review by hand, a dismissal, magnum unapprove) and a
    manual verdict posted after magnum's round both keep auto-approval from
    overriding the operator, who here is the one asking: A lifts their own ✗
    on purpose. What auto-approval holds a PR back for besides (authorRefusal:
    an author auto_approve_skip_authors lists or auto_approve_authors leaves
    out; autoGateRefusal: a reviewer's missing report, a PR its watch would
    not review on its own, the agents' instructions, the head's checks) does
    not refuse it either: the operator decides by hand, the board shows those.
    sum is magnum's latest posted round of pr (nil: none).

func OptionalCallsWords(links []string) string
    OptionalCallsWords names the optional calls whose links are links,
    as the idle verdict and the factory screen's merge move end with them:
    "1 optional call: <link>", "2 optional calls: <link>, <link>"; "" for none.

func OverruleHooksHold(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store) (bool, error)
    OverruleHooksHold lets the hooks.json files whose hooks without a trust
    entry the daemon told about (KVCodexHooksUntrusted) start new Codex sessions
    until they change (KVCodexHooksOverruled), for `magnum resume --tool codex`
    (or all): the daemon's, and the CLI's when no daemon runs. It reports
    whether it overruled a file not overruled yet.

func PRSubject(repo store.Repo, number int) string
    PRSubject is the audit subject of PR number of repo ("pr:owner/name#N"),
    which the PR's events carry: the factory reads a PR's fix loops by it.

func PinnedSince(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store) (map[string]time.Time, error)
    PinnedSince is when each subject that is pinned now was pinned, by the
    registry's pin events: "pr:owner/name#N" for a PR pinned by `magnum open`,
    `magnum pin` or `magnum slots pin` (pr.opened, pr.pinned), "slot:<name>" for
    a slot pinned without a PR (slot.pinned); an unpin, or the end of an open's
    hold (pr.open_hold_ended), forgets the subject. A pin older than the events
    kept (store.Prune), or set by hand, has no entry.

func PreservationProblems(p store.NotesProposal, live, target notes.State) ([]string, error)
    PreservationProblems is notes.CheckPreserved of applying p over live
    (target, ApplyTarget's): nil for a restore, which brings back a recorded
    version the operator chose (the registry keeps the state it replaces).

func PressureName(level int) string
    PressureName names a pressure level: "normal", "warn", "critical",
    or "unknown" for any other.

func ProcessCommand(ctx context.Context, run execx.Runner, pid int) (comm, args string, err error)
    ProcessCommand reads what ps knows about pid: comm (`ps -o comm=`, the
    executable as started, its full path when it was started by path) and args
    (`ps -o args=`, the whole command line). LooksLikeDaemon judges them.

func PromptsLine(loadedAt time.Time, changed int) string
    PromptsLine is what `magnum status` shows after "prompts: ": when the daemon
    loaded them, and how many files changed on disk since (they take effect at
    the next restart). "" when loadedAt is zero (no daemon has recorded it).

func ProposalStale(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, nr notes.Repo, p store.NotesProposal) (bool, error)
    ProposalStale reports whether p is stale: the notes on disk are not the
    state of its base version. It reads the version's listing from the registry
    and hashes the files on disk, never a version's content.

func ReadDaemonConfigSum(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store) (string, bool)
    ReadDaemonConfigSum reads KVDaemonConfigSum: the hex SHA-256 of the user
    config the running daemon loaded, "" when it read none; false when no daemon
    recorded one (one older than the record, or none ever ran).

func ReadWebhooks(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store) (WebhooksHealth, []WebhooksHour)
    ReadWebhooks reads what the consumer recorded: the stream's health and the
    hourly totals, oldest first (zero and nil when nothing was).

func RecordedBudgetAtCap(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, u config.Usage, now time.Time) (bool, error)
    RecordedBudgetAtCap reports whether the Codex reading the daemon
    last recorded in st (KVUsageCodexPercent, of the window resetting at
    KVUsageCodexResetsAt) is at u's soft or hard cap at now, with no overrule
    pending (KVUsageCodexOverruledAt): the reading the CLI's offline `magnum
    resume --tool` of a Codex kind overrules, as liftToolPause does the
    daemon's. No reading, or one whose window reset since, is at no cap.

func RecoverNotesApply(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, nr notes.Repo, p store.NotesProposal, now time.Time, wait time.Duration) (string, error)
    RecoverNotesApply finishes or reverts proposal p, which an apply left
    applying (a crash between its claim and its record), under the notes lock
    (waiting at most wait): when the notes hold the state the claim meant
    to write (its target, computed again from the base, the prior and the
    proposed versions and checked against the target the claim recorded),
    the proposal is recorded applied; when they hold the state the claim
    found (its prior version), nothing was written and the claim is released;
    when they hold the notes of one and the harness of the other (the write cut
    short between its two steps), the target is written whole and recorded.
    Anything else (a writer after the crash) is recorded as an import, so the
    registry holds it, and the claim is released: the proposal waits again,
    stale against those notes. It reports what it did ("" when p no longer waits
    for a recovery) and writes an event.

func RestartableSessions(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, cfg *config.Config, kind string, prID int64) (sessions []store.Session, pinned int, err error)
    RestartableSessions are the live sessions `magnum restart-sessions --tool
    kind` restarts: each one runs an agent of kind (its recorded kind, else its
    role's; "all" = any kind; a shell role's pane never), of PR prID unless it
    is 0, and pinned counts those it leaves alone because their PR or its slot
    is pinned. The settings screen counts them for its question.

func SkewNote(daemon Build, cliVersion string, modTime func(path string) (time.Time, bool)) string
    SkewNote says when the running daemon is older than what is built: the CLI's
    version (cliVersion) differs from the daemon's, or the daemon's binary on
    disk changed since it started (its mtime; modTime reads it, false when it
    cannot). "" when neither. A version that is empty or "dev" (a build `make
    build` did not stamp) is not compared.

func SkillCopyDir(state string) string
    SkillCopyDir is where the daemon keeps the copies of the judges' skills it
    took at startup (<state>/skill/<hash>/SKILL.md).

func StagingEnvs(cfg *config.Config, repo string) []staging.Env
    StagingEnvs is repo's staging environments (config.Stagings) as
    internal/staging names them, in config order; nil for none.

func StagingFirst(files store.PRFiles, listed bool, head string, shown []StagingEnv) []string
    StagingFirst is the migrations a PR at head must take to a staging before
    its merge: staging.DeployBeforeMerge over files, the head's file list
    (store.PRFilesOf, which the poll writes from GitHub's Details), and shown,
    the envs as StagingShown shows them (unknown, and a state word this build
    does not know, hold nothing back), every one in byte order and its control
    characters spaces; nil when it need not, or files is another head's or not
    listed (listed false). The board says it in staging.DeployBeforeMergeWords
    on the wait on your merge the look's idle verdict leaves (OpenMergeIsYours),
    as the factory screen does from the same rows.

func StagingNeverDeploys(pr store.PR) bool
    StagingNeverDeploys reports whether pr can never deploy to a staging,
    whoever asks and whenever (stagingDeployRefusal): its head lives in a fork,
    or its head branch is master, main or a staging branch. The board says no
    staging deploy before such a PR's merge, since E would be refused.

func StagingPlanSays(ep StagingPlanEnv) string
    StagingPlanSays is what one env's plan says in words: why it takes no merge,
    its conflicts (and that the resolver merges them first), or a clean merge,
    with the migrations it adds and its workflow changes.

func StagingRepos(cfg *config.Config) []string
    StagingRepos lists the repositories with staging environments a [[watch]]
    covers, as their [[factory.repo]] names them, in config order: the ones the
    review daemon tells the staging status of.

func StagingResolverSays(values map[string]string, effect string) string
    StagingResolverSays is what the newest live resolver job of effect does now,
    among values (a KVValues read of KVStagingResolves): "try N: " and its
    Why made safe for a terminal, which names the agent's pane while the agent
    works; "" when no job of effect is live.

func StagingStale(lastTick, now time.Time) string
    StagingStale is why the daemon's staging records no longer follow staging at
    now, its last tick being lastTick: "the daemon has not run" (zero), "stale:
    the daemon's last tick is 1h old" (more than staging.StaleAfter ago);
    "" while they do.

func StateOf(c store.NotesContent) notes.State
    StateOf is a version's content as a notes state.

func TrivialDelta(files []github.FileDelta, allowed []string) (classes []string, trivial bool)
    TrivialDelta reports whether a delta needs no re-review under the allowed
    classes, and the classes it used (sorted, unique; nil when not trivial).
    The delta is trivial when it has at least one file and every file is:
    a modified file with a complete patch that is documentation (docs), or whose
    every added and removed line is blank or differs from its counterpart only
    in whitespace (whitespace) or is a comment of the file's type (comments).
    A class missing from allowed makes the files that need it non-trivial,
    so an empty allowed never skips.

func WhiteboardOpenCmd(session string) execx.Cmd
    WhiteboardOpenCmd opens the whiteboard session in Whiteboard Desktop,
    focused: `whiteboard app pick --session <id> --focus`.

func WhiteboardStatusCmd() execx.Cmd
    WhiteboardStatusCmd is Whiteboard's readiness check, `whiteboard api
    whiteboard_status`: it exits 0 only while a Whiteboard server runs
    (Whiteboard Desktop, or `whiteboard server start`). A failed exit is an
    answer (Probe).

func WriteTabBarFile(path string, at time.Time, maxAge time.Duration, text string) error
    WriteTabBarFile replaces the tab-bar file with two lines: when it was
    written and how long it stays fresh (unix seconds and seconds, "1791710538
    90"), then text flattened to one plain line (secrets redacted). herdr
    renders only the last line a tab-bar command prints, so `cat` of the file
    still shows the status; the command magnum suggests (TabBarCommand in the
    cli) prints "magnum down" once the first line is older than its own max age.
    The write is fsx.ReplaceFile, with no disk sync: the file is written at the
    start and the end of every tick, a reader sees the old file or the new,
    and a file a crash loses (missing, empty or without a timestamp) reads as
    "magnum down" as well.


TYPES

type AdoptPayload struct {
	Pool string `json:"pool,omitempty"`
	Path string `json:"path"`
}
    AdoptPayload registers the existing checkout at Path as a free slot of the
    pool of repository Pool ("" = the pool whose slot_path matches Path).

type Agents interface {
	ObserveSnapshotAt(ctx context.Context, snap herdr.Snapshot, capturedAt time.Time) ([]agents.Observation, error)
	// ObserveRunsAt is ObserveSnapshotAt for the sessions with a run
	// submitted or at work alone: the observe clock's pass.
	ObserveRunsAt(ctx context.Context, snap herdr.Snapshot, capturedAt time.Time) ([]agents.Observation, error)
	EnsureWorkspace(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, slotPath string, env map[string]string, label string, roles []config.Role) (agents.Workspace, error)
	EnsurePane(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, ws agents.Workspace, slotPath string, env map[string]string, role config.Role) (agents.Workspace, error)
	StartAgent(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, role config.Role, paneID, resume string) error
	ResumeID(ctx context.Context, prID int64, role agents.Role) (string, error)
	Preflight(ctx context.Context, kind string) error
	// LoginStamp fingerprints the kind's login file ("" = none): a login
	// pause a run proved holds until it changes (health).
	LoginStamp(kind string) string
	Park(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR) error
	// ParkHard is Park for an agent that will not quit: one still its
	// pane's foreground process after ctrl+c and its kind's exit keys has
	// that pane closed alone and its session closed (a fresh start's second
	// try, parkFresh; a stop's last, parkForStop).
	ParkHard(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR) error
	// ParkSessions parks the PR's live sessions ids names and only them,
	// with Park's guards, each once its quit reached an idle shell and its
	// own pane was closed: the idle park's early park of the agents past
	// their threshold while another agent of the PR stays (parkEarly). It
	// never parks hard, and returns the sessions it parked beside the
	// failures of the others.
	ParkSessions(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, ids []int64) ([]store.Session, error)
	// PaneEnv is the env a pane of role gets from env: the fix job compares
	// it with the env of a live fixer pane, made for another identity
	// (fixRenewPane).
	PaneEnv(env map[string]string, role config.Role) (map[string]string, error)
	// CloseRetiredPanes closes the idle panes of the PR's parked, closed
	// and lost sessions that no starting or live session of the PR or of
	// another PR records, after every park that worked and a session
	// marked lost (closeRetiredPanes, closePanesJob).
	CloseRetiredPanes(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR) error
	// CloseRetiredPanesIn is CloseRetiredPanes over a snapshot the
	// reconcile took once for every PR with a pane (closeLeftoverPanes).
	CloseRetiredPanesIn(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, snap herdr.Snapshot) error
	// ClearShellPanes makes sure, before a round's checkout switches the
	// slot at checkout, that no command runs in the PR's shell panes there:
	// an own leftover is stopped, anything else holds the round
	// (agents.ErrHumanActive, the PR's cooldown started; prepare).
	ClearShellPanes(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, checkout string) error
	// Quit stops one session's agent and parks its conversation (a cold
	// judge, coldJudge; a session that served its max_session_rounds,
	// rotateSessions; a session parkReloading takes out of the checkout's
	// way).
	Quit(ctx context.Context, s store.Session) error
	// ReloadsProject reports whether a session's agent reloads the
	// checkout's project config it loaded while it runs (parkReloading).
	ReloadsProject(ctx context.Context, s store.Session) bool
	// TookNoPrompt reports whether a live Codex session never took a
	// prompt: no id and no rollout longer than agents.RecoverIDAfter after
	// its last prompt (coldJudge).
	TookNoPrompt(ctx context.Context, s store.Session) bool
	// ClearDeadLaunch closes the pane of a launch that never came up which
	// herdr lists under the agent name of session s over an idle shell,
	// replacing s's pane when it is that one, and reports whether the name
	// is gone and the role keeps a pane (quitAgentGone).
	ClearDeadLaunch(ctx context.Context, s store.Session) (bool, error)
	Recover(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR) ([]agents.Recovered, error)
	// Wake takes an agent's hook event as a hint to look at its pane now
	// (agents.Manager.Wake: ctx bounds its later looks, so it is the
	// daemon's), and WaitWakes waits for those looks once the listener
	// stopped (hooks.go).
	Wake(ctx context.Context, ev agenthooks.Event)
	WaitWakes()
	// NewRun, FixPrompt and Submit start the fix job's run (fix.go); Tell
	// gives a fixer whose time ran out its last call within the run.
	NewRun(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, role agents.Role, kind string, round int) (store.Run, error)
	FixPrompt(pr store.PR, role agents.Role, run store.Run, in agents.FixPromptInput) (string, error)
	// WhiteboardPrompt renders the whiteboard job's prompt (whiteboard.go),
	// whose run NewRun and Submit start as the fix job's.
	WhiteboardPrompt(pr store.PR, role agents.Role, run store.Run, in agents.WhiteboardPromptInput) (string, error)
	Submit(ctx context.Context, run store.Run, text string) error
	Tell(ctx context.Context, run store.Run, text string) error
	// ContextUsed reads how full a session's context is from its pane's
	// status lines (ok false: no figure), and Compact has its agent compact
	// its conversation and waits for that turn to end: the fix job's
	// compaction before a cycle that resumes the fixer (fix_compact.go).
	ContextUsed(ctx context.Context, s store.Session) (int, bool)
	Compact(ctx context.Context, s store.Session) error
	// TypedDuringRun reports whether someone typed into the pane of run's
	// session while run was in flight, as a claude agent's transcript shows
	// it (false for any other kind): the fix job's settle says so.
	TypedDuringRun(ctx context.Context, run store.Run) bool
}
    Agents is the part of *agents.Manager the engine drives.

	Head   string    `json:"head"`

}
    AutoApproveRefused is why auto-approval holds a PR back (autoGateRefusal),
    for the head (Head) and magnum's latest posted round (RunID) it decided
    on; RunID is "" for a refusal of the PR whatever round reviewed it
    (authorRefusal).

func ParseAutoApproveRefused(v string) (AutoApproveRefused, bool)
    ParseAutoApproveRefused reads a KVPRAutoApproveRefused value.

type Build struct {
	Version   string    `json:"version"`

    Build identifies a magnum binary: the version `make build` stamps

func CurrentBuild(version, path string) Build
    CurrentBuild is this process's build: version as stamped, the revision from

func ReadDaemonBuild(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store) (Build, bool)
    ReadDaemonBuild reads the build the daemon recorded at startup (false when
    none did: a daemon older than the record, or none ever ran).

func (b Build) Label() string

    version does not say it ("dev (8ad5bb2)").

type CIFixAsked struct {
	Head    string    `json:"head"`
	Entries []string  `json:"entries"`
	Count   int       `json:"count"`
	At      time.Time `json:"at"`
}
    CIFixAsked is what the y/N of a CI fix asked about, which the start it
    confirms is bound to: the PR's head, the failed required entries, the CI
    fixes the PR had then, and when the daemon planned it.

type CIFixPlan struct {
	Ref   string     `json:"ref"`
	Asked CIFixAsked `json:"ci_asked"`
	Text  string     `json:"text"`
}
    CIFixPlan is the daemon's answer to a dry run of a CI fix: the PR
    (owner/name#N), what its y/N asks about, and the plan in words (Text, the
    answer's last line: "dry run: would fix the failed CI of <PR>: claude-fix
    fixes required check Completion at a1a1a1a (2 failed jobs) in review1 as
    fixer-app[bot], CI fix 1 of 3").

func ParseCIFixPlan(result string) (CIFixPlan, bool)
    ParseCIFixPlan reads the answer to a dry run of a CI fix (its first line);
    false when it is none (a refusal's words, a merge's plan).

type Claim struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Claim is what a review daemon takes before it builds its App (ClaimDaemon):
    the daemon lock and, when it got it, the hook listener on Layout.HookSocket.
    Run takes the lock it holds (Options.Claim) and serves the listener; Release
    gives both up.

func ClaimDaemon(l paths.Layout) (*Claim, error)
    ClaimDaemon takes the daemon lock (Layout.Lock) for a daemon that is about
    to build its App, and, when it got it, starts the agents' hook listener on
    Layout.HookSocket (paths.CheckSocketPath first; Listen replaces a socket an
    earlier daemon left, since the lock's holder owns the path, and leaves alone
    a file that is no socket). The lock taken by another process is no error:
    the claim says so (Held), and Run exits as when it finds the lock taken
    itself. A path too long for a Unix socket and a listener that cannot start
    are no errors either: the claim has no listener and says why (Off), so the
    daemon makes no pane with the hook env and polls. Only a lock that cannot be
    taken at all is an error.

func (c *Claim) Held() bool
    Held reports whether another process held the daemon lock.

func (c *Claim) HookSocket() string
    HookSocket is the listener's socket, the panes' MAGNUM_HOOK_SOCKET;
    "" without a listener (no claim, the lock held, a path too long, a listener
    that failed).

func (c *Claim) Off() string
    Off says why the claim has no listener while it holds the lock ("" with
    one).

func (c *Claim) Release()
    Release closes the listener and gives the lock up, once; a nil claim does
    nothing.

type Classifier interface {
	Classify(ctx context.Context, job ClassifyJob) (ClassifyResult, error)
	Close(ctx context.Context) error
}
    Classifier sorts the candidates of one PR at a time, writing
    ClassifyJob.OutputPath. One serves a whole retro; Close ends it.

type ClassifyJob struct {
	Dir            string
	CandidatesPath string
	OutputPath     string
	PR             store.PR
	Repo           store.Repo
	// ReviewedSHAs are the commits magnum reviewed, oldest first.
	ReviewedSHAs []string
	// Candidates are the candidates file's, for checking the answer, and
	// Rejected its rejected findings, which the answer may name; Threads
	// are its own threads, each of which the answer must classify.
	Candidates []learn.Candidate
	Rejected   []learn.Rejected
	Threads    []learn.OwnThread
	// Factory is the directory of the copies of the factory task's plan,
	// ticket and answers (learn.FactoryDir) on a pull request the factory
	// published with a candidate its local round missed; "" otherwise.
	Factory string
}
    ClassifyJob is one PR's candidates for a Classifier: Dir holds
    CandidatesPath (learn.Candidates) and the commented files (learn.FilePath);
    the classifier writes its answer (learn.Output) to OutputPath.

type ClassifyResult struct {
	// Unclassified: nothing classified the candidates (no classifier is
	// set up); they are stored unclassified, not as a failure.
	Unclassified bool
	// Pause: the classifier's agent hit a limit (Kind: usage_limit,
	// login_required, overloaded, or model_limit with no fallback model
	// left). The retro stops without recording the PR, which stays due; a
	// usage limit and a logout also pause the tool, as after a round.
	Pause *pipeline.Pause
	// Model is the model the answer came from ("" = unknown), which the
	// retro.ok event names.
	Model string
}
    ClassifyResult is how a Classifier's turn ended, besides its error.

type Cleaner interface {
	Plan(ctx context.Context, opts cleanup.Options) (cleanup.Plan, error)
	PlanFrom(ctx context.Context, opts cleanup.Options, inv inventory.Inventory) (cleanup.Plan, error)
	Apply(ctx context.Context, plan cleanup.Plan, confirmed bool) (cleanup.Report, error)
}

    over an inventory the reconcile already scanned.

type CleanupPayload struct {
	Options   cleanup.Options `json:"options"`
	Plan      *cleanup.Plan   `json:"plan,omitempty"`
	Confirmed bool            `json:"confirmed,omitempty"`
}
    CleanupPayload is a cleanup request: Plan (re-checked by Apply) or Options
    (planned again by the daemon). Confirmed is the typed confirmation for
    actions that need it.

type CodexFlag struct {
	Kind   string    `json:"kind"`
	Role   string    `json:"role,omitempty"`
	Run    string    `json:"run,omitempty"`
	Head   string    `json:"head,omitempty"`
	Detail string    `json:"detail,omitempty"`
	At     time.Time `json:"at"`
	By     string    `json:"by,omitempty"`
	// Fallback is the judge role the PR's rounds run with since the flag,
	// without the flagged kind's roles ([pipeline] judge_fallback;
	// judge_fallback.go); "" = the PR is never reviewed again.
	Fallback string `json:"fallback,omitempty"`

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    CodexFlag is why magnum never reviews a PR again: the agent kind whose
    provider flagged it, the role and run it refused (none when set by hand),
    the PR's head then, the refusal's line or the operator's reason, when and by
    whom ("round 3", "magnum codex-flag").

func ParseCodexFlag(s string) CodexFlag
    ParseCodexFlag reads a store.KVPRCodexFlag value. A value it cannot read is
    a flag still (UnreadableCodexFlag): magnum never reviews a PR on a flag it
    failed to read.

func UnreadableCodexFlag(why string) CodexFlag
    UnreadableCodexFlag is the flag of a PR whose flag record could not be read
    (why): it counts as flagged.

func (f CodexFlag) Sentence(ref string) string
    Sentence is the flag in full, for the card, `magnum status` and the
    refusals: when and where it was flagged, what happens and how to lift it
    (ref names the PR on the command line).

func (f CodexFlag) Short() string
    Short is the flag in one cell: "Codex flagged · never reviewed again", or
    "Codex flagged · judge claude-judge" for a PR that goes on with a fallback
    judge.

func (f CodexFlag) SkipReason() string
    SkipReason is the flagged PR's skip_reason.

func (f CodexFlag) Who() string
    Who names the provider that flagged the PR: "Codex".

type CodexFlagPayload struct {
	PRTarget
	Clear  bool   `json:"clear,omitempty"`
	Reason string `json:"reason,omitempty"`
	By     string `json:"by,omitempty"`
}
    CodexFlagPayload is a `magnum codex-flag set|clear` request: flag the
    PR (Reason: why, from the operator) or clear its flag. By says who asks

type DeltaCheckRound struct {
	Lines  int    `json:"lines"`  // the delta's changed code lines
	Files  int    `json:"files"`  // its files
	Target string `json:"target"` // the commit the check reviews
}
    DeltaCheckRound is a delta check in flight (KVPRDeltaCheck).

func ParseDeltaCheckRound(s string) (DeltaCheckRound, bool)
    ParseDeltaCheckRound reads a KVPRDeltaCheck value; ok is false for "" or a
    value it cannot read.

type DeltaRecord struct {
	// Version is deltaRecordVersion for a delta measured with the PR's own
	// diff in view (base_merge.go); 0 is a record from before.
	Version int    `json:"version,omitempty"`
	From    string `json:"from"`
	To      string `json:"to"`
	DeltaSize
	// Since is the first push the review does not cover: kept while From
	// stays the reviewed commit.
	Since time.Time `json:"since"`
}
    DeltaRecord is the measured delta of a PR from its reviewed commit to a head
    (KVPRDelta). It describes the PR only while From is its reviewed_sha and To
    its head.

type DeltaSize struct {
	// Lines counts the added and removed lines that change code: not
	// blank, not a comment, not a line that only moved in whitespace
	// within its run of changes, not in a documentation file.
	Lines int `json:"lines"`
	// AddedFiles counts the files added, renamed or copied.
	AddedFiles int `json:"added_files"`
	// Complete is false when a file other than an added one had no
	// complete patch (binary, too large, a cut-off file list): its lines
	// are unknown, so the threshold cannot hold the delta back.
	Complete bool `json:"complete"`
	// Binaries are the files of the delta modified without a patch whose
	// type is binary (binaryDeltaPath: an image, a font, an archive): they
	// make it incomplete like any file without a patch, but a delta check
	// (eligibility.DeltaCheck) reads them as 0 lines and names them to the
	// judge. Unread counts the other files without a complete patch (too
	// large, a cut-off file list, a removed binary).
	Binaries []string `json:"binaries,omitempty"`
	Unread   int      `json:"unread,omitempty"`
}
    DeltaSize is how big a delta is for the re-review threshold ([daemon]
    rereview_min_lines).

func MeasureDelta(files []github.FileDelta) DeltaSize
    MeasureDelta counts a delta's lines the way TrivialDelta judges them, with
    every class allowed, but line by line instead of all or nothing: a comment,
    a blank line, a documentation file and a line whose counterpart in the
    same run of changes differs only in whitespace count nothing; every other
    added or removed line counts one, and so does each line of a run whose code
    lines only changed order. A context line that one side has inside a block
    comment and the other does not (code commented out, or back in) counts one,
    like a line it cannot read.

func (s DeltaSize) Readable() bool
    Readable reports whether every file of the delta is read in full or is a
    modified binary file (Binaries): what a delta check needs.

type Deps struct {
	Config *config.Config
	Layout paths.Layout
	Store  *store.Store
	Logger *slog.Logger
	// Now is the clock (nil = time.Now); Sleep waits honouring ctx (nil = a
	// timer). Tests replace both.
	Now   func() time.Time
	Sleep func(ctx context.Context, d time.Duration) error
	// ObserveSleep is the observe clock's wait between its passes
	// (observe_clock.go; nil = a timer honouring ctx). Tests step it.
	ObserveSleep func(ctx context.Context, d time.Duration) error
	// DryRun: every decision is made (against the store the caller passes,
	// which app.New makes a private copy) but nothing outside the store is
	// changed: no herdr calls besides the snapshot, no agents, no rounds, no
	// slot or cleanup side effects, no toasts. See Recorder.
	DryRun bool

	GitHub func(identity string) GitHub // poll client per identity (nil = none)
	// GitHubEnv is identity's client over env, a token of the daemon's own
