```text
	Repair(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pool config.Pool) error
	Adopt(ctx context.Context, pool config.Pool, path string) (store.Slot, error)
	// CheckSchema, ForgetSchema and RecordSchema decide and record a round's
	// schema reload (readinessPlan), ResetFailed counts a reload that failed
	// (RecordSchema clears the count); EnsureSchema reloads for magnum open.
	CheckSchema(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pool config.Pool) (slots.SchemaCheck, error)
	ForgetSchema(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot) error
	RecordSchema(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, c slots.SchemaCheck) error
	ResetFailed(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, cause string) (int, error)
	EnsureSchema(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pool config.Pool) (string, error)
	// RecreateDatabases empties the slot's databases when MySQL refused the
	// round's reload with 3730 (the readiness plan's Recreate).
	RecreateDatabases(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pool config.Pool) error
}
    Slots is the part of *slots.Manager the engine drives.

type Snooze struct {

type Staging interface {

    named on the command line.

    "re-review · small delta 8/30 lines → 16:40", "re-review · requested by
    alice → now", "delta check · quiet → 14:09", "re-review · retry 2/3 setup →
    22:57", "re-review · pinned → u" (u: the screens' unpin key), "re-review ·
    held → 03:21" (an open's hold, which ends by itself).
```

## escapes

```text
package escapes // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/escapes"

Package escapes matches one review round's findings against another's by place:
a finding of the other round escaped the local one when no local finding sits
on its path within NearLines of its lines, at a head whose line numbers name
the same code. It is the one near rule of the review retro (internal/learn: a
comment near one of magnum's findings) and of the factory's local review against
the rounds after it (DECISIONS "The review retro tags factory-origin misses and
their stage").

The package is pure: no registry, no I/O, nothing of a pull request beyond what
a Finding holds. A caller that knows that two heads name the same code for a
path (the file did not change between them) says so with SameCode.

CONSTANTS

const NearLines = 3
    NearLines is how far apart, in lines, two findings on the same path may be
    and still be about the same code.


FUNCTIONS

func Distance(a, b Finding) (int, bool)
    Distance is how many lines lie between a's and b's ranges (0 when they
    overlap or touch the same line), whatever their paths; false when either has
    no line.


TYPES

type Escape struct {
	Finding Finding
	Reason  Reason
	// Nearest is the local finding on the path nearest to it at a
	// comparable head, the first in local's order on a tie, and Distance
	// how many lines lie between their ranges; both are set for ReasonFar
	// only.
	Nearest  Finding
	Distance int
}
    Escape is a finding of the other round that no local finding caught,
    and why.

func Match(local, other []Finding, opts ...Option) []Escape
    Match returns, in other's order, an Escape for every finding of other that
    no finding of local caught. A local finding catches one of other when both
    are placed (a path and a line), their paths are equal, their heads are
    comparable (equal, both unknown, or the same code by SameCode) and their
    ranges are at most NearLines apart (Distance). A finding of other that
    cannot be placed is an escape of its own (ReasonUnplaced), never matched;
    a local one that cannot be placed catches nothing. Match never filters by
    priority, and one local finding may catch several.

type Finding struct {
	Source Source
	// Ref is the caller's own key, opaque here, to find its row again.
	Ref  string
	Path string
	// StartLine and EndLine are the lines the finding is on, [StartLine,
	// EndLine], in the file at Head: equal for a one-line finding, and a
	// finding with only a line has StartLine = EndLine = that line.
	// StartLine 0 means EndLine alone; EndLine 0 means no line (a file or
	// review-body finding), which cannot be placed.
	StartLine, EndLine int
	// Priority is P0 to P3 as the registries write it ("" when unknown).
	// Match never filters by it: callers do.
	Priority string
	// Title may be empty: the factory keeps only TitleHash.
	Title, TitleHash string
	// Round is magnum's round or the factory's review cycle that raised
	// it (0 when unknown).
	Round int
	// Head is the commit the line numbers name ("" when unknown).
	Head string
}
    Finding is one finding as Match places it.

func (f Finding) Lines() (from, to int, ok bool)
    Lines is f's range as [from, to] with from <= to, false when f has no line.

type Option func(*config)
    Option changes how Match compares heads.

func SameCode(same func(path, localHead, otherHead string) bool) Option
    SameCode lets Match compare a local finding with one of the other round at
    two different heads: same(path, localHead, otherHead) reports whether path's
    line numbers name the same code at both (the file did not change between
    them). Match asks it only when both heads are set and differ. Without it,
    two findings are compared only at the same head (or both unknown).

type Reason string
    Reason says why no local finding caught a finding of the other round.

const (
	// ReasonNoLocal: no local finding on its path at a comparable head.
	ReasonNoLocal Reason = "no_local"
	// ReasonFar: the nearest local finding on its path at a comparable
	// head is more than NearLines away (Escape.Nearest, Escape.Distance).
	ReasonFar Reason = "far"
	// ReasonUnplaced: it has no path or no line, so nothing can catch it.
	ReasonUnplaced Reason = "unplaced"
)
    Reasons.

type Source string
    Source says which round, or who, a finding is of.

const (
	SourceLocal   Source = "local"   // the factory's local review round (factory.db review_findings)
	SourcePosted  Source = "posted"  // magnum's posted review round (magnum.db findings)
	SourceComment Source = "comment" // a person's comment on the pull request
)
    Sources.

```

## eval

```text
package eval // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/eval"

Package eval scores an evaluation replay of magnum's pull request review against
a corpus of pull requests with known ("seeded") defects.

The corpus (corpus.go) lists, per pull request, the reviewed head and the
defects a good review must report. The judge's result file of a no-post run
(findings.go) is parsed into findings, and ScoreCase (score.go) tells which
defects were found, at which severity, and how many findings matched nothing
(noise). Runs (report.go) collect the scores of one replay, persist them, can be
rescored after the corpus is corrected, and render a text or markdown report.

The package is pure: it starts no process, touches no network and knows nothing
of the registry. Its only file access is the corpus file and the run directories
it is told about.

CONSTANTS

const (
	KindPosted = ""
	KindLocal  = "local"
)
    The kinds of case (Case.Kind): a pull request's posted round, and a round of
    the factory's local review.

const (
	ExpectFound  = "found"
	ExpectAbsent = "absent"
)
    What a review is expected to do with a defect (Defect.Expect): report it,
    the default, or not report it, a finding an author declined as wrong (a
    match is a false positive, Score.AbsentHits).

const (
	// OutcomeFlagged: the case is not replayed, since an earlier replay of
	// it or of its PR was refused or the live registry holds a Codex flag
	// for its PR.
	OutcomeFlagged = "flagged"
	// OutcomeBudget: the Codex budget is at or past [usage] codex_soft; no
	// later case should start either.
	OutcomeBudget = "budget"
	// OutcomeSkipped: the case is not replayed, since an earlier case of the
	// run hit a usage limit, needed a login or reached the Codex budget, or
	// the run was interrupted; `magnum eval run` records it so.
	OutcomeSkipped = "skipped"
	// OutcomeMissingRole: a local case's round went without a reviewer's
	// report (a lost pane, a timeout): what it would have found is unknown,
	// so it is not scored, never a miss.
	OutcomeMissingRole = "missing_role"
	// OutcomeConfigError: a local case's round cannot run for a
	// configuration problem (no gh identity to run as, a frozen role the
	// config no longer declares): not scored, and running it again changes
	// nothing until the config does.
	OutcomeConfigError = "config_error"
	// OutcomeEnvironment: the case's worktree could not be prepared as a
	// review checkout of its repository is (its copy_files, its setup):
	// what the round would have found is unknown, so it is not scored,
	// never a miss; the error names the command and its first error line.
	OutcomeEnvironment = "environment"
)
    Case outcomes of a replay besides the round's (pipeline.Outcome*), which
    evalrun.RunCase records (OutcomeSkipped: `magnum eval run`) and the daemon's
    gate of a skill proposal reads.

const FlaggedFile = "flagged.json"
    FlaggedFile holds the flagged cases (Flagged by case name) under the runs'
    root.

const LocalNumberBase = 900000
    LocalNumberBase is where the synthetic PR numbers of the factory's local
    rounds start (evalrun.LocalNumber: LocalNumberBase + task id × 10 + round
    for rounds 1 to 10, 9000000 + task id × 100 + round past them), far above
    any PR number of the repositories magnum reviews. A local case's PR number
    is one of them.

const RunIDFormat = "20060102-150405"
    RunIDFormat is a run id's time part: sortable, to the second.


FUNCTIONS

func AgentTag(id string) string
    AgentTag tags the agents of run id (agents.Deps.Tag): "eval-" and the
    first 6 hex digits of the id's SHA-256, the same for all the run's cases.
    The tag joins the agents' names' hash, so they are named apart from the
    PR's own agents and from every other run's: StartAgent adopts an agent that
    carries a role's name, and a run once adopted the agents the run before it
    left behind. It also leads their titles and pane labels.

func CaseInputs(r Run, cr CaseRun) string
    CaseInputs are the inputs replay cr of run r read, which Baselines,
    JudgeBaselines and NewestReplay match on: the case's own (CaseRun.Inputs,
    a local case's round), else the run's (Run.Inputs). A local case's replay
    that recorded none ran before its round's reviewer read the factory's
    local reviewer prompt: it read the posted one, as no local round does,
    so its inputs are "", which no inputs match.

func FullReplayFor(runs []Run, caseName, head string, like *Run) (Run, CaseRun, bool)
    FullReplayFor finds the replay a judge-only replay of case caseName at head
    takes its reviewers' reports from: the newest run whose case of that name
    reviewed head with every role (not JudgeOnly), ended a scored dry run and,
    unless like is nil, whose reviewers read what the judge-only replay's would,
    like's (ReviewedOtherwise: the same reviewer inputs and notes setting).
    A nil like takes any such run, so a refusal can name the newest. runs are
    oldest first (ListRuns); ok is false when none did.

func HashNotes(file, dir string) (map[string]string, error)
    HashNotes is the SHA-256 (hex) of each notes file a replay gives the judge:
    the repository's notes file, keyed by its base name ("" when there is none),
    and every regular file under its harness directory dir, keyed by the
    directory's base name and the path below it ("web/qa.sh"). Two runs whose
    maps differ for a case gave its judge other notes (WriteText says so).

func LoadFlagged(root string) (map[string]Flagged, error)
    LoadFlagged reads the flagged cases under root by case name; a missing file
    is none.

func MarkFlagged(root string, f Flagged) error
    MarkFlagged adds f to the flagged cases under root (the first record of a
    case stands).

func NewRunDir(root string, now time.Time) (id, dir string, err error)
    NewRunDir creates the directory of a run started at now under root and
    returns the run's id and directory. The id is now to the second, with "-2",
    "-3"... when a run started in the same second holds it (os.Mkdir fails
    with ErrExist), so no two runs share a directory, a record or an agent tag
    (AgentTag).

func ReplayedAt(r Run, cr CaseRun) time.Time
    ReplayedAt is when run r replayed its case cr: the case's start, else the
    run's (zero when neither was recorded). A run can outlive many of its cases'
    replays (the skill gate replays a lost guard's base into the base run it
    made at its first baseline), so its own start dates only its first.

func SaveRun(dir string, r Run) error
    SaveRun writes dir/run.json atomically (a temporary file in dir, then a
    rename), mode 0600; dir is created with mode 0700.

func ValidName(name string) bool
    ValidName reports whether name may name a case (and a defect):
    [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,47}.

func WriteCorpus(path string, c Corpus) error
    WriteCorpus writes c to path as TOML that LoadCorpus reads back as c,
    atomically (a temporary file, then a rename) with mode 0600, creating
    the directory (0700). A corpus LoadCorpus would refuse is not written,
    and a file that already holds the same text is left as it is.

func WriteMarkdown(w io.Writer, r Run)
    WriteMarkdown writes the report of r as markdown (report.md): a summary
    table, then per case each defect as found or missed with its severity,
    and the findings that matched no defect.

func WriteText(w io.Writer, r Run, prev *Run)
    WriteText writes the human report of r: a table with one row per case
    and a total, how many absent defects were hit (when the run has any),
    the Codex points the cases used, then, when prev is not nil, how the totals
    moved since it and which cases read other notes than in prev, then one line
    per missed defect, per absent defect hit and per case error.


TYPES

type Baseline struct {
	Run    string    // the stored run's ID
	Commit string    // magnum's commit that ran it
	Case   CaseRun   // the case as that run recorded it
	At     time.Time // when the run replayed the case (ReplayedAt)
}
    Baseline is a stored replay of a case that a run with the same inputs need
    not repeat.

func Baselines(runs []Run, inputs string, c Case) []Baseline
    Baselines lists, newest run first, the stored replays of c that a run with
    inputs (Run.Inputs: the judge skill, the roles' prompts, the role config,
    the stakes lines and the simplification caps; a local case's own,
    CaseInputs) may reuse instead of replaying c: replays that recorded the same
    inputs in runs from a clean checkout, whose case of c's name reviewed c's
    head with every role (not a judge-only replay, CaseRun.JudgeOnly) and has
    a score. Unknown inputs ("") reuse nothing. The inputs leave magnum's code
    out, so the caller decides whether the code of Commit reviews as its own
    does (eval-at.sh compares the Go files of the two commits).

func JudgeBaselines(runs []Run, inputs string, c Case, reports string) []Baseline
    JudgeBaselines lists, newest run first, the stored replays of c whose
    judge read inputs on the reviewer reports of run reports (the full replay a
    judge-only replay of c takes them from, FullReplayFor): that run's own case
    of c when it recorded inputs, and judge-only replays of c on its reports
    (CaseRun.ReportsRun) that recorded inputs; clean runs with a score only,
    as for Baselines. Comparing a judge-only candidate with one of these,
    never with another full replay, keeps the reviewers' variance between two
    full replays out of the comparison.

type Case struct {
	Name string `toml:"name"`           // unique, [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,47}
	Kind string `toml:"kind,omitempty"` // KindPosted ("", every case before kinds) or KindLocal
	PR   string `toml:"pr"`             // owner/repo#N
	Head string `toml:"head"`           // the reviewed head, 40 lower-case hex
	Base string `toml:"base,omitempty"` // base branch name, optional; never on a local case
	Why  string `toml:"why,omitempty"`  // why the case is in the corpus, optional

	Defects []Defect `toml:"defect"`

	// Owner, Repo and Number are parsed from PR.
	Owner  string `toml:"-"`
	Repo   string `toml:"-"`
	Number int    `toml:"-"`
}
    Case is one pull request pinned to the head that is reviewed, with the
    defects a review must find. A local case (Kind KindLocal) is one round of
    the factory's local review instead, before any PR existed: its PR is the
    round's synthetic number (evalrun.LocalNumber: LocalNumberBase + task ×
    10 + round for rounds 1 to 10, 9000000 + task × 100 + round past them,
    as the round ran under), its head the one the round reviewed, and the rest
    of what the round read (its base commit, branch, title, plan, ticket, the
    operator's answers and roles) is frozen in a directory of its own beside the
    learned corpus when it is added (`magnum eval add`, evalrun.LocalCaseDir),
    never read from the factory's task directory again.

func (cs Case) Local() bool
    Local reports whether cs is a round of the factory's local review
    (KindLocal).

func (cs *Case) Validate() error
    Validate reports every rule cs breaks, as LoadCorpus does for a corpus that
    holds it, and fills Owner, Repo and Number from PR; nil when cs is valid.

type CaseRun struct {
	Case       string    `json:"case"`
	Kind       string    `json:"kind,omitempty"` // the case's kind (Case.Kind): "" posted, KindLocal
	PR         string    `json:"pr"`
	Head       string    `json:"head"`
	Outcome    string    `json:"outcome"` // dry_run, error, needs_attention, usage_limit, skipped, ...
	Error      string    `json:"error,omitempty"`
	ResultFile string    `json:"result_file,omitempty"` // absolute path of the judge result
	ReportDir  string    `json:"report_dir,omitempty"`
	Started    time.Time `json:"started,omitzero"`
	Finished   time.Time `json:"finished,omitzero"`
	Score      *Score    `json:"score,omitempty"` // nil when there was no result to score
	// Notes is what notes the judge read (HashNotes): file -> SHA-256, "" for a notes file there
	// was none of; nil when the run withheld them (Run.NoNotes) or did not record them.
	Notes map[string]string `json:"notes,omitempty"`
	// CodexBefore and CodexAfter are the Codex budget used (percent, in Codex's whole points) as
	// the gauge read when the case started and when it ended; nil when it could not be read. The
	// gauge counts every Codex session of the account, live rounds included.
	CodexBefore *float64 `json:"codex_before,omitempty"`
	CodexAfter  *float64 `json:"codex_after,omitempty"`
	// JudgeOnly: the judge alone reviewed, on the reviewers' reports of the case in run ReportsRun,
	// the newest full replay of it at the same head (FullReplayFor; `magnum eval run --judge-only`).
	JudgeOnly  bool   `json:"judge_only,omitempty"`
	ReportsRun string `json:"reports_run,omitempty"`
	// Findings are what a local case was scored on: its round's findings as the factory acts on
	// them (evalrun.LocalResult's, a question marked), then the review's body; Rescore scores them
	// again. A posted case's are re-read from ResultFile, so they are not kept.
	Findings []Finding `json:"findings,omitempty"`
	// Inputs are what a local case's replay read (evalrun.LocalReviewInputs: its round's reviewer
	// reads the factory's local reviewer prompt, which the run's Inputs leave out), "" for a posted
	// case, whose inputs are the run's, and for a local replay from before they were recorded
	// (CaseInputs).
	Inputs string `json:"inputs,omitempty"`
}
    CaseRun is one case of a replay: what became of the review round and,
    when it left a result, the score.

func (c CaseRun) Points() (float64, bool)
    Points is how far the Codex gauge moved while the case ran; ok is false when
    either reading is missing or the window reset in between (the gauge fell).

type Corpus struct {
	Cases []Case `toml:"case"`
}
    Corpus is the set of pull requests with seeded defects a replay is scored
    against.

func LoadCorpora(user string, others ...string) (*Corpus, error)
    LoadCorpora reads the operator's corpus at user ("" = none), then the
    corpora kept beside it, in the order given: the learned corpus the
    daemon writes (paths.Layout.LearnCorpus) and the local cases' corpus
    (paths.Layout.LearnLocalCorpus), each "" or a file that does not exist
    adding nothing, and returns their cases in that order. A case name in two
    files is an error that names it and both files. Without a user corpus and
    without any of the others the error is the first other file's. A path given
    twice (a run given the learned corpus as --corpus, scored again) is read
    once.

func LoadCorpus(path string) (*Corpus, error)
    LoadCorpus reads and parses the corpus file at path.

func (c *Corpus) Select(names []string) ([]Case, error)
    Select returns the cases called names, in corpus order; no names selects
    every case. A name the corpus does not know is an error.

type Defect struct {
	ID    string `toml:"id"`    // unique within the case, same charset as a case name
	Title string `toml:"title"` // shown in reports
	// Severity is, for a defect to find, the weakest severity that still counts as right; for an
	// absent one, the weakest at which a matching finding is a hit (a weaker one is neither a hit
	// nor noise). P0..P3, optional.
	Severity string   `toml:"severity,omitempty"`
	Paths    []string `toml:"paths,omitempty"`  // globs on the slash path, "**" spans directories
	Lines    []int    `toml:"lines,omitempty"`  // inclusive head-side range [from, to]
	Match    []string `toml:"match,omitempty"`  // case-insensitive regexps on the finding body
	Body     bool     `toml:"body,omitempty"`   // a mention in the review body also counts; needs Match
	Expect   string   `toml:"expect,omitempty"` // ExpectFound ("" too) or ExpectAbsent
	// Question asks that the finding be a question for the operator (a local round's provenance
	// marks it, Finding.Question) at Severity or stronger, P2 when it gives none:
	// the factory asks the operator only P0 to P2 questions, so a P3 question goes to the task's
	// leftovers, never to the operator, and a P3 Severity is refused; a finding that is no question
	// has the writer decide. Only a local case's defect to find may ask it.
	Question bool `toml:"question,omitempty"`

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Defect is one thing a review must report, or with Expect ExpectAbsent one
    it must not. A finding matches it when its path matches one of Paths (any
    path when empty), its range comes within three lines of Lines (any line when
    empty) and one of Match matches its body (anything when empty). Paths and
    Match must not both be empty.

type DefectResult struct {
	ID         string `json:"id"`
	Title      string `json:"title"`
	Want       string `json:"want,omitempty"` // the defect's severity
	Found      bool   `json:"found"`
	By         []int  `json:"by,omitempty"`       // indexes into Result.Findings that matched
	Severity   string `json:"severity,omitempty"` // the strongest among matching inline findings, "" if none
	SeverityOK bool   `json:"severity_ok"`        // found, and at Want or stronger (or no Want)
	Question   bool   `json:"question,omitempty"` // the defect wants a question for the operator (Defect.Question)
}
    DefectResult is the outcome for one defect of a case.

type Finding struct {
	Path           string `json:"path,omitempty"`
	Line           int    `json:"line,omitempty"`
	StartLine      int    `json:"start_line,omitempty"` // 0 = single line
	Body           string `json:"body"`
	Severity       string `json:"severity,omitempty"`       // P0..P3 or ""
	Simplification bool   `json:"simplification,omitempty"` // an optional suggestion, never a defect
	InBody         bool   `json:"in_body,omitempty"`        // the review body rather than an inline comment
	// Question: the judge marked it a question for the operator (a local round's provenance,
	// evalrun.LocalFinding.Question); ParseResult never sets it, since a posted round asks none.
	Question bool `json:"question,omitempty"`
}
    Finding is one thing the review reported: an inline comment, or the review
    body as a whole.

type Flagged struct {
	Case   string    `json:"case"`
	PR     string    `json:"pr"`
	Head   string    `json:"head"`
	Run    string    `json:"run"`
	Reason string    `json:"reason"`
	At     time.Time `json:"at"`
}
    Flagged is a case whose replay was refused: in which run, at which head,
    why and when.

func FlaggedCase(flagged map[string]Flagged, c Case) (Flagged, bool)
    FlaggedCase is the flagged record of case c: the one of its name, else one
    of its PR (owner/repo#N, letter case aside), so a refused PR stays out under
    another case name.

func (f Flagged) Refusal() string
    Refusal says why the case is not replayed.

type Replay struct {
	Run    string
	Inputs string
	At     time.Time
	Case   CaseRun
}
    Replay is a stored replay of a case (NewestReplay): the run that made it,
    the inputs it read (CaseInputs: the run's, a local case's own; "" before
    they were recorded), when it replayed the case (ReplayedAt) and the case as
    the run recorded it.

func NewestReplay(runs []Run, c Case, skip string) (Replay, bool)
    NewestReplay is the newest stored replay of c at the head the corpus pins
    that has a score, a full or a judge-only one, from a clean checkout or not,
    leaving out the replays that read inputs skip (CaseInputs; "" leaves none
    out; the skill gate leaves out its candidate's own): the one replayed last
    (ReplayedAt), in whatever run, two dated alike ordered by their runs (oldest
    first: ListRuns) and within a run by their order. ok is false when there is
    none.

type Result struct {
	Status   string
	Event    string
	Counts   map[string]int // the "findings" object: severity -> number
	Findings []Finding      // inline comments in order, then the review body when it is not empty
	Planned  bool           // planned_review was present
}
    Result is what a judge result file says about one round.

func ParseResult(data []byte) (Result, error)
    ParseResult reads the judge's result file. The inline comments of
    planned_review become findings in order, followed by one InBody finding
    holding the review body when it is not empty.

    The severity of a comment comes from the provenance entry that was posted
    (or has no verdict) on the same path and line, else from the first P0..P3
    token in the first 80 characters of its body.

type Run struct {
	ID       string            `json:"id"`               // sortable, e.g. 20261004-153000
	Label    string            `json:"label"`            // free text
	Commit   string            `json:"commit"`           // magnum's git HEAD (short) when the run started, "" unknown
	Dirty    bool              `json:"dirty"`            // magnum's checkout had uncommitted changes
	Models   map[string]string `json:"models,omitempty"` // role name -> model, "" = the kind's default
	Corpus   string            `json:"corpus"`           // corpus path
	Started  time.Time         `json:"started,omitzero"`
	Finished time.Time         `json:"finished,omitzero"`
	Cases    []CaseRun         `json:"cases"`
	// Inputs identifies what the review read besides the PR and the notes: a hash of the judge
	// skill, the roles' prompts, the role config, the stakes lines and the simplification caps
	// (max_simplifications; "" in runs before it was recorded). Baselines matches on it.
	Inputs string `json:"inputs,omitempty"`
	// ReviewerInputs is the part of Inputs the reviewer roles read: their prompts, role config and
	// the stakes lines, the judges' and the simplification caps left out ("" in runs before it was
	// recorded). A judge-only replay takes the reports of a full replay whose reviewers read what
	// its own would (FullReplayFor).
	ReviewerInputs string `json:"reviewer_inputs,omitempty"`
	NoNotes        bool   `json:"no_notes,omitempty"` // no role was given the notes (--no-notes)
	// Candidate is the directory whose prompts and judge skill the run replayed (--candidate,
	// evalrun.WithCandidate); "" = the configured ones.
	Candidate string `json:"candidate,omitempty"`
	// CorpusAlone is set when the run read Corpus alone (--corpus FILE), without the learned corpus
	// the daemon writes; `eval score` reads it alone again. Runs before it was recorded read both.
	CorpusAlone bool `json:"corpus_alone,omitempty"`
}
    Run is one replay of a corpus.

func ListRuns(root string) ([]Run, error)
    ListRuns loads every root/*/run.json, oldest ID first. A directory without a
    readable run.json is skipped; a missing root has no runs.

func LoadRun(dir string) (Run, error)
    LoadRun reads dir/run.json.

func Rescore(r Run, c *Corpus, read func(path string) ([]byte, error)) Run
    Rescore recomputes the score of every case of r from its saved result
    file against the current defects of the corpus, so a corrected match
    expression takes effect without running the agents again. read loads a file
    (os.ReadFile when nil). The run it returns is a copy; r is not changed.

    A case the corpus no longer has, or that has no result file, keeps its
    score. A case the corpus now pins to another head than the run reviewed
    keeps its score (the defects name the new head's lines), and so does a
    result that cannot be read or parsed; either sets Error to say so when the
    case has a score or no other error. A rescore that succeeds clears an Error
    an earlier one set. A local case (CaseRun.Kind KindLocal) that was scored
    is scored again on the findings the run kept (CaseRun.Findings), its result
    file unread; one the corpus now has as another kind of case keeps its score
    and says so.

func RunsBefore(runs []Run, t time.Time) []Run
    RunsBefore is runs as they stood at t: each run with only the cases it
    replayed before t (ReplayedAt; an undated replay counts as before), a run
    left with none dropped. A zero t keeps them all. runs is not changed.

func (r Run) ReviewedOtherwise(like Run) string
    ReviewedOtherwise says how r's reviewers read other inputs than like's
    would ("" = they read the same): other reviewer inputs (ReviewerInputs;
    a run that recorded none, from before they were recorded, counts as other),
    or the notes given where like withholds them or withheld where like gives
    them (NoNotes: the reviewers' prompts point at the notes too). The notes'
    content is not compared: it moves with every curation, and a judge-only
    replay measures a judge change on the same reports, not on the notes the
    reviewers read then.

func (r Run) Totals() Totals
    Totals adds up the scores of the run. Cases without a score count in Cases
    only.

type Score struct {
	Case            string         `json:"case"`
	Status          string         `json:"status,omitempty"`
	Event           string         `json:"event,omitempty"`
	Defects         []DefectResult `json:"defects"`
	Found           int            `json:"found"`
	Total           int            `json:"total"`
	Noise           int            `json:"noise"`               // inline findings that matched no defect, simplifications aside
	Simplifications int            `json:"simplifications"`     // optional simplification suggestions, neither defect nor noise
	Unmatched       []Finding      `json:"unmatched,omitempty"` // the noise findings
	// Absent counts the case's absent defects (Defect.Expect ExpectAbsent), which Defects, Found and
	// Total leave out; AbsentHits are the ones a finding reported, each a false positive (the
	// findings that hit them are not noise).
	Absent     int            `json:"absent,omitempty"`
	AbsentHits []DefectResult `json:"absent_hits,omitempty"`
}
    Score is the outcome for one case.

func ScoreCase(c Case, r Result) Score
    ScoreCase tells, for every defect of c, whether the findings of r report it.
    An inline finding matches a defect when its path matches one of the
    defect's paths (any when none), its line range comes within three lines
    of the defect's lines (when set) and its body matches one of the defect's
    regexps (when set). A review body matches only a defect with body = true,
    by its regexps alone, and only with its finding list and nearby block
    (bodyFindings). Simplification suggestions match nothing and are not noise.
    One finding may match several defects. An absent defect (expect =
    "absent") is matched the same way, but a finding that matches it is a hit
    (Score.AbsentHits) when the defect has no severity or the finding is at it
    or stronger (or has none to compare); a weaker one is the finding ranked as
    it should be. Neither is noise, and absent defects count in neither Found
    nor Total. A question defect (question = true) is found only by a question
    for the operator at its severity or stronger, P2 when it gives none (asks);
    a finding on it that is not one is neither found nor noise.

func (s Score) SeverityOK() int
    SeverityOK counts the found defects that were reported at the wanted
    severity or stronger.

type Totals struct {
	Cases           int // all cases of the run
	Scored          int // cases that have a score
	Found           int
	Total           int
	Noise           int
	Simplifications int
	SeverityOK      int
	Recall          float64 // Found/Total, 0 when Total is 0
	Absent          int     // absent defects of the scored cases (Score.Absent)
	AbsentHits      int     // the ones a finding reported (Score.AbsentHits): false positives
}
    Totals sums the scored cases of a run.

```

## evalrun

```text
package evalrun // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/evalrun"

Package evalrun replays one case of an eval corpus (internal/eval) as a blind
dry-run round and scores it: what `magnum eval run` does for each case,
in a package the daemon can call too. Each case runs in its own scratch layout
(registry, reports, a copy of the notes) under the run's directory and in
a detached worktree of the repository's clone, prepared as a per-PR review
checkout of the repository is (its copy_files and setup, then its teardown),
with agents tagged for the run, so the live registry, the PR's own agents,
another run's agents and the PR's reports are never touched. A candidate
directory (WithCandidate) replays another checkout's prompts and skill.

CONSTANTS

const (
	LocalReviewPrompt = "claude-review-local.md"
	LiveReviewPrompt  = "claude-review.md"
)
    LocalReviewPrompt is the factory's local reviewer prompt, which reviews the
    change in the copy (`git diff <base>..<head>`) and reads the title and the
    description from a file; LiveReviewPrompt is the posted reviewer prompt it
    stands in for in a local round (`/code-review <PR URL>`, whose URL no GitHub
    serves for a synthetic number).

const (
	// MaxLocalRound is the last round a synthetic number is kept for: two
	// digits of it, past the loop's config.MaxFactoryCycles (a second
	// opinion's round runs outside the loop's count).
	MaxLocalRound = 99
	// MaxLocalTask is the last task a synthetic number is kept for: past
	// it, task T's rounds 1 to 10 would take a round of task T+1 or one of
	// the numbers of rounds 11 and up.
	MaxLocalTask = 99_999
)
    The bounds of the local rounds' synthetic numbers (LocalNumber).

const (
	LocalDescriptionFile = "description.md"
	LocalTicketFile      = pipeline.TicketFile
)
    LocalDescriptionFile and LocalTicketFile are the files a local round writes
    in its scratch directory for the judge: the change's title and body, and its
    ticket with the operator's answers after it.

const (
	// OutcomeFlagged: the case is not replayed: an earlier replay of it or
	// of its PR was refused (eval.FlaggedCase), or the live registry holds
	// a Codex flag for its PR (Refused).
	OutcomeFlagged = eval.OutcomeFlagged
	// OutcomeBudget: the Codex budget is at or past [usage] codex_soft
	// (Options.Force runs anyway); no later case should start either.
	OutcomeBudget = eval.OutcomeBudget
	// OutcomeError: the case could not run (the round's error outcome).
	OutcomeError = pipeline.OutcomeError
)
    Case outcomes of RunCase besides the round's (pipeline.Outcome*).

const CandidateSkill = config.CandidateSkill
    CandidateSkill is where a candidate directory holds the judge skill,
    as magnum's checkout does.

const ReleaseTimeout = 2 * time.Minute
    ReleaseTimeout bounds closing a case's agents after its round.


VARIABLES

var ErrNoFullReplay = errors.New("no full replay to take the reviewers' reports from")
    ErrNoFullReplay is a judge-only replay's error when it finds no scored full
    replay of its case at the same head whose reviewers read what its own would
    to take the reviewers' reports from, or the one it finds left none.


FUNCTIONS

func FreezeLocal(ctx context.Context, d Deps, taskID int64, round, cycle int) (LocalInputs, LocalResult, error)
    FreezeLocal reads what round `round` of task taskID's local review read, for
    its eval case (`magnum eval add --local-task`), from the round's own records
    wherever they are kept, and from nothing that changed since it began;
    cycle picks the review cycle when the task's loops ran that round in several
    (0 = the only one). It reads, read only:

      - the factory's registry (factoryread.LocalReview): the task's repository
        and branch, whether Codex never works on it again, the cycle's head and
        start, and the round's roles from its begin event;
      - the round's result in the task's directory (LocalResultFile),
        which must be this round's and names the round's scratch directory,
        inside the task's local review (LocalRoot);
      - in that scratch directory, the description.md the judge read (the title
        and the plan), its ticket.md (the ticket; "" when the round had none)
        and the report directory's prepass.json, whose base is the commit the
        round diffed from and whose head must be the cycle's;
      - the operator's answers: those under their heading in the round's ticket
        file when it has them, else the task's answers.md ("" when there is
        none) when no answer was given at the round's start or later and the
        file was not written after it began; else the answers rebuilt from the
        factory's registry as they stood when the round began (answersAt).

    The base branch is the [[factory.repo]]'s (default master). What cannot be
    frozen whole is an error that says what is missing; it returns the round's
    result too, whose findings `eval add` prints.

func Inputs(cfg *config.Config) string
    Inputs is a hash (12 hex) of what a replay's review reads besides the PR
    and the notes (eval.Run.Inputs): every role's config with the model it
    resolves to and its kind's config, the prompt files the roles name as
    they resolve now (the checkout's prompts_dir, else the embedded ones),
    with the judge prompts' partials file (config.SharedPrompt) their blocks
    come from, each judge's skill file, the stakes lines of the [[watch]] and
    [[repo]] blocks (what the judge and the reviewers size a harm against),
    and the simplification caps the judge posts by: the pipeline table's
    max_simplifications in effect and each [[repo]] block's that is set
    (config.Config.MaxSimplificationsFor), and with [jira] on the site and
    the account the judge reads the PR's ticket from (not the token file).
    The texts count, not where they are: a judge's skill path is left out of its
    role config, so a candidate directory with the same texts as the checkout
    has its inputs (a landed candidate's replays are the next baseline).
    magnum's own code is not part of it. "" without a config.

func LocalCaseDir(l paths.Layout, name string) string
    LocalCaseDir is where local case name keeps its frozen inputs:
    paths.Layout.LearnLocalCases()/<name>, beside the learned corpus, outside
    any checkout (a case name is a file name: eval's idPattern).

func LocalCaseName(taskID int64, round int) string
    LocalCaseName is the name `magnum eval add` gives the case of round `round`
    of task taskID unless told another: task-<id>-round-<n>.

func LocalIdentity(cfg *config.Config, w *config.Watch) (string, error)
    LocalIdentity is the name of the identity a local round runs as: the watch's
    when it is a gh identity, else the first gh identity configured. An App's
    would have its token minted from GitHub, and the round reads nothing there.
    A config without one is a ConfigError. The factory opens its PRs as the same
    identity.

func LocalNumber(taskID int64, round int) int
    LocalNumber is the synthetic PR number of round n of task taskID's local
    review: 900000 + task id × 10 + round for rounds 1 to 10, the numbers
    every round ran under before a round could pass the loop's ten (900011 to
    1900000), and 9000000 + task id × 100 + round for rounds 11 to MaxLocalRound
    (9000111 to 18999999), so no two tasks' rounds share one (round 11 of task T
    would be round 1 of task T+1 by the first rule). It is 0 for a task of 1 to
    MaxLocalTask or a round of 1 to MaxLocalRound it is not: no number is kept
    apart for it.

func LocalNumberFormula(round int) string
    LocalNumberFormula is the rule LocalNumber numbers round `round` by,
    as text: what `eval add` prints beside a local case's pr.

func LocalResultFile(n int) string
    LocalResultFile is the file in a task's directory where the factory keeps
    the result of review cycle n's round (an evalrun.LocalResult as JSON),
    as the factory names it (internal/factory's reviewRoundFile).

func LocalReviewConfig(cfg *config.Config) *config.Config
    LocalReviewConfig is the config a local round reviews with: a copy of
    cfg (its prompt snapshot, if any, kept) whose every role that names
    LiveReviewPrompt, for any prompt kind, names LocalReviewPrompt in its place,
    resolved as cfg resolves prompts (a candidate's prompts_dir, else the
    embedded one). RunLocal applies it, so the factory's rounds and the replays
    of a local case review alike; cfg is never changed.

func LocalReviewInputs(cfg *config.Config) string
    LocalReviewInputs are the Inputs of a local round reviewed with cfg
    (LocalReviewConfig: its reviewer reads the factory's local reviewer prompt,
    LocalReviewPrompt, where cfg's names the posted one), which a local case's
    replay records as its own (eval.CaseRun.Inputs) and the skill gate matches
    a local case's stored replays on. An edit of the posted reviewer prompt,
    which no local round reads, leaves them alone.

func LocalRoot(l paths.Layout, taskID int64) string
    LocalRoot is where task taskID's local rounds keep their scratch
    directories: local-review/ in the task's directory.

func LocalRoundOf(n int) (taskID int64, round int, ok bool)
    LocalRoundOf is LocalNumber undone: the task and the round whose synthetic
    PR number n is. Below localHighBase, round 10 is where the next task's tens
    start (task 7's is 900080), so the round is counted from 1, not taken as n's
    last digit; from it, the round is n's last two digits and must be past 10.
    ok is false for a number no round of a task has.

func LocalTicket(ticketMD, answersMD string) string
    LocalTicket is the text of a local round's ticket file: the ticket, then,
    when the operator answered anything, localAnswersHeading and the answers
    (operatorAnswers); the answers alone under their heading when the change
    has no ticket, the ticket and a newline when it has no answers, "" when it
    has neither. RunLocal writes it as ticket.md; it is exported so that the
    factory's tests read what a task's ticket.md and answers.md become.

func Refused(ctx context.Context, d Deps, ec eval.Case) string
    Refused says why case ec is not replayed ("" = it may be): an earlier
    replay of it or of its PR, under any case name, was refused (the runs root's
    eval.FlaggedFile, which cannot be read refuses too), or the live registry
    holds a Codex flag for its PR (liveFlag). A local case, whose synthetic PR
    is in no registry, is refused for Codex's sake instead when its round ran a
    Codex role on a task Codex must not see again (localCodexRefusal).

func ReviewerInputs(cfg *config.Config) string
    ReviewerInputs is the part of Inputs the reviewer roles read
    (eval.Run.ReviewerInputs): the same hash over the roles that are not judges,
    with the stakes lines the reviewers read too and without the simplification
    caps and [jira], which only the judges read, so a change to a judge's
    prompts, skill, caps or ticket leaves it alone and a judge-only replay can
    take the reports of a full replay whose reviewers read what its own would
    (eval.FullReplayFor). "" without a config.

func RunCase(ctx context.Context, d Deps, ec eval.Case, o Options) (out eval.CaseRun)
    RunCase replays case ec and scores it. Every failure becomes the case's
    outcome (OutcomeError, OutcomeBudget, OutcomeFlagged or the round's);
    a refused replay is flagged (eval.MarkFlagged) so that it never runs again.
    It starts nothing for options without an absolute RunDir or an AgentTag
    (checked first), for a case Refused names, of a repository no watch covers,
    or whose candidate is no candidate. One replay of a case runs at a time,
    whoever starts it (`magnum eval run`, eval-at.sh through it, the daemon's
    gate): it holds the case's lock (lockCase) from its first check to the end
    of its cleanup, a second replay of the case waiting for it, and Started
    is when it took the lock. Its worktree is prepared as a per-PR review
    checkout of the repository for the PR's number and torn down before it goes
    (addCaseWorktree): a setup that fails ends the case eval.OutcomeEnvironment,
    never scored. A local case (eval.KindLocal) replays its round from its
    frozen inputs (replayLocal) after the same checks, the budget's included.

func RunsRoot(l paths.Layout) string
    RunsRoot is where a layout's eval runs live: <state>/eval/<run id>/,
    with the flagged cases (eval.FlaggedFile) and the cases' worktrees (wt/)
    (paths.Layout.Eval).

func SaveLocalInputs(dir string, in LocalInputs) error
    SaveLocalInputs writes in to the new directory dir (0700, its files 0600):
    inputs.json and the three texts, all in a directory beside dir that is
    renamed into place at the end, so a case is either whole or not there.
    A dir that exists is refused: a frozen case is never overwritten.

func WithCandidate(cfg *config.Config, dir string) (*config.Config, error)
    WithCandidate is the config a replay of candidate dir reviews with
    (config.Config.WithCandidate, which the skill editor's checks share):
    a copy of cfg (config.Config.WithoutSnapshot: read from disk, whatever the
    daemon loaded at startup) whose prompts_dir is <dir>/prompts and whose every
    judge reads <dir>/skills/magnum-review/SKILL.md, both absolute. dir is a
    checkout or a worktree of magnum with a change to the prompts or the skill;
    a prompt it lacks resolves to the embedded default, as in any checkout.
    An error when dir has no prompts directory or no skill file; cfg is never
    changed.


TYPES

type ConfigError struct {
	Key, Why string
}
    ConfigError is a local round that cannot run for a configuration problem
    (no gh identity to run as): Key names what to configure, Why what is wrong.
    Running it again changes nothing.

func (e *ConfigError) Error() string

type Deps struct {
	// Layout is the install's: its logs, locks and gh config directories,
	// the live notes a case copies and the runs root (RunsRoot). A case's
	// scratch layout is a copy of it with Scratch set.
	Layout paths.Layout
	// Config is the config the case reviews with (WithCandidate's for
	// Options.Candidate is applied by RunCase).
	Config *config.Config
	// Store is the live registry, read for the PR's Codex flag only; nil =
	// the registry file at Layout.DB(), opened read-only for each check
	// (never created).
	Store *store.Store
	// Logger is the case app's logger (nil = warnings and errors as text to
	// Stderr).
	Logger *slog.Logger
	// Stderr receives the case app's human-readable logs (app.Options).
	Stderr io.Writer
	// Now is the case's clock (nil = time.Now).
	Now func() time.Time
	// Runner replaces the case app's subprocess runner (app.Options; nil =
	// the real one).
	Runner execx.Runner
	// Progress reports a step of the case ("fetching ...", "reviewing in
	// ..."), Warn a problem that does not end it (a worktree left behind,
	// agents that stay open); nil = none.
	Progress func(format string, args ...any)
	Warn     func(format string, args ...any)

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Deps is what a replay works with.

type LocalCase struct {
	Checkout, BaseSHA, HeadSHA, Branch, Title, Body, TicketMD, AnswersMD string
	Watch                                                                config.Watch
	Roles                                                                []string
	Round                                                                int
	TaskID                                                               int64
	Repo, Base                                                           string
	Env                                                                  map[string]string
	ScratchRoot                                                          string
	NoNotes                                                              bool
}
    LocalCase is one round of the factory's local review: magnum's full review
    of a change in the task's copy, as a blind dry run, before any PR exists
    (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-factory-design.md, section 6.5). Checkout
    is the copy, BaseSHA and HeadSHA the change's ends, Branch its branch,
    Title (with the Jira key), Body and TicketMD what the judge reads from
    files instead of GitHub; Body is the factory's own plan, not a person's
    description, and AnswersMD the operator's answers to the factory's
    questions (the task's answers.md, "" when it has none), the only statement
    of intent a person made: they follow the ticket in the ticket file under
    one fixed heading. Watch is the repository's [[watch]], whose review roles
    round 1 runs, Roles the roles of this round and Round its number, from 1.
    TaskID is the task whose change it is and Repo its repository (owner/name):
    the round's synthetic PR number (LocalNumber) and its scratch directory
    (LocalRoot) come from them. Base is the base branch ("" = master), Env the
    round's environment (engine.LocalRound.Env): the factory gives the copy's,
    the one its agents get in it; the replay of a local case (RunCase) the
    per-PR worktree env of the synthetic number, never a copy's. The factory's
    LocalReviewer takes it. A replay of the round as an eval case (RunCase of
    a local case) sets ScratchRoot, where the round's scratch directory goes
    instead of the task's directory (LocalRoot), and NoNotes, which withholds
    the repository notes (Options.NoNotes); the factory sets neither.

type LocalFinding struct {
	Severity, Title, Path    string
	Line                     int
	Body                     string
	Simplification, Question bool
	Sources                  []string `json:",omitempty"`
}
    LocalFinding is one finding of a local round: its Severity (P0 to P3, "" for
    a simplification), Title, Path and Line (0 for one in the review's body),
    its Body, whether it is a simplification or a question for the operator (the
    judge's provenance marks it, the skill's Local round), and its Sources,
    the roles that raised it as the provenance names them (`judge` for the
    judge's own pass; none for a finding no entry of the provenance names).

type LocalInputs struct {
	Task    int64     `json:"task"`
	Round   int       `json:"round"`
	Cycle   int       `json:"cycle"`
	Repo    string    `json:"repo"`
	BaseSHA string    `json:"base_sha"`
	HeadSHA string    `json:"head_sha"`
	Branch  string    `json:"branch"`
	Base    string    `json:"base"`
	Title   string    `json:"title"`
	Roles   []string  `json:"roles"`
	Frozen  time.Time `json:"frozen"`
	// CodexNever is the factory's mark that Codex never works on the task
	// again (factoryread.LocalTask.CodexNever) as it was when the case was
	// added: a replay whose roles run Codex is refused on it (Refused).
	CodexNever bool `json:"codex_never,omitempty"`

	AnswersAsOf    time.Time `json:"answers_as_of,omitzero"`
	AnswersLeftOut int       `json:"answers_left_out,omitempty"`

	Body      string `json:"-"`
	TicketMD  string `json:"-"`
	AnswersMD string `json:"-"`
}
    LocalInputs are what one round of the factory's local review read, frozen
    when its eval case is added (`magnum eval add --local-task`, FreezeLocal)
    in the case's own directory (LocalCaseDir), so that its replay never reads
    the factory's task directory, which can be cleaned: the task and the loop's
    round (Cycle the review cycle it ran in), the repository (owner/name),
    the change's base and head commits, its branch and base branch,
    the title (with the Jira key), the plan as the judge's description (Body),
    the ticket (TicketMD) and the operator's answers (AnswersMD) its ticket file
    joins (LocalTicket), and the round's roles; Frozen is when it was added.
    The texts are files of their own beside inputs.json (plan.md, ticket.md,
    answers.md). AnswersAsOf is set when the answers are not a file the round
    read but rebuilt from the factory's registry as they stood when the round
    began (its cycle's start), and AnswersLeftOut counts the answers given at
    that start or later, which the rebuild left out.

func LoadLocalInputs(dir string) (LocalInputs, error)
    LoadLocalInputs reads the frozen inputs in dir (SaveLocalInputs). A file
    missing, or inputs that cannot be replayed, are an error (its round frozen
    again, `magnum eval add`, makes them whole).

func (in LocalInputs) Number() int
    Number is the synthetic PR number the round ran under (LocalNumber),
    which its replay runs under again.

func (in LocalInputs) PR() string
    PR is the round's synthetic PR, owner/repo#Number: the local case's pr in
    the corpus (eval.Case.PR).

type LocalResult struct {
	Outcome, ReportDir, Verdict string
	ResultFile                  string
	Counts                      [4]int
	OpenCounts                  *[4]int
	Findings                    []LocalFinding
	Round                       int
	Number                      int
	Tag, Scratch                string
	Refused                     string
	Missing                     []string
	MissingStatus               map[string]string
	MissingDetail               string
	Error                       string
	// ConfigKey names what to configure when the round could not run for
	// a configuration problem (ConfigError); "" otherwise.
	ConfigKey string
}
    LocalResult is what a local round found: the round's Outcome (dry_run when
    it finished), its ReportDir, the judge's Verdict ("" when its result file is
    missing or does not parse) and ResultFile, the judge's result file it read
    (that of the judge among the round's roles, "" without a report directory),
    the findings' counts by priority (P0 to P3) and, for a later round, the
    counts of the earlier findings still open, the findings themselves, and the
    round's number. Number, Tag and Scratch are the round's synthetic PR number,
    its agents' tag and its scratch directory; Refused the agent kind whose
    provider refused the round (OutcomeRefused: "codex" for a Codex warning);
    Missing the reviewer roles whose report the judge went without (a lost pane,
    a timeout), MissingStatus each one's report status (a pipeline report
    status, or the health kind its pane showed: usage_limit, login_required,
    ...), and MissingDetail the report detail of the first of them, in name
    order, that carries its pane's error line (an agent that died at its launch:
    agents.PaneErrorOf reads it), "" when none does; Error why a round that did
    not finish ended, in the round's words.

func ParseLocalResult(data []byte) LocalResult
    ParseLocalResult reads a judge's result file (the skill's section 8 JSON)
    as a local round has it: the verdict, the counts and the earlier findings
    still open (store.ParseReviewResult; Verdict "" when data is no result), and
    the findings: each posted entry of the provenance with its severity, title,
    path and line, the body of the planned comment on that line, and whether
    the judge marked it a question; each simplification of the planned review;
    a planned comment no entry names, by its own severity and first line; and,
    when the counts hold a P0 to P2 that no finding carries, the review's body
    as one finding of that priority, so what blocks always reaches the writer.
    A planned review this code does not read leaves the provenance's findings
    without their bodies.

func RunLocal(ctx context.Context, d Deps, c LocalCase) (LocalResult, error)
    RunLocal runs local round c and reads its judge's result (ParseLocalResult).
    Each round is its own: a fresh scratch directory under the task's
    (LocalRoot/<round>-<tag>; c.ScratchRoot/<round>-<tag> when set) with its
    registry, reports and a copy of the repository notes (none with c.NoNotes),
    a new agent tag, and the synthetic PR number LocalNumber, so two rounds
    never share an agent, a herdr workspace label or an eval case lock (it holds
    the case lock "local-<number>" for the round). It writes the title and
    body (description.md) and the ticket with the operator's answers after it
    (ticket.md, when c has either: LocalTicket) there, and runs engine.RunLocal
    in the task's copy at c.HeadSHA, always with c.BaseSHA (post-review's
    --local-base), as a gh identity (the watch's, else the first configured:
    an App's token would be minted from GitHub), with the branch as the head
    ref and the title with the Jira key. The round's config is d.Config (the
    factory's review candidate, config.WithCandidate; a replay's candidate) with
    the local reviewer prompt in the posted one's place (LocalReviewConfig).
    A case it cannot run is an error and nothing starts; a round that ran is a
    result, whatever its outcome, and only the end of ctx (a drain) is an error
    after it started.

type Options struct {
	// Candidate replays a candidate directory's prompts and skill
	// (WithCandidate); "" = Config's.
	Candidate string
	// JudgeOnly runs the judge alone on the reviewers' reports of the
	// case's newest full replay at the same head whose reviewers read what
	// this replay's would (eval.FullReplayFor: ReviewerInputs of the config
	// the case reviews with, and NoNotes), copied into the case's report
	// directory (engine.EvalCase.JudgeOnly); a case without one, or whose
	// full replay left no reviewer report, fails with ErrNoFullReplay before
	// it reads GitHub or checks anything out.
	JudgeOnly bool
	// NoNotes withholds the repository notes from every role; Keep leaves
	// the case's worktree in place; Force runs past [usage] codex_soft.
	NoNotes, Keep, Force bool
	// AgentTag tags the case's agents (agents.Deps.Tag), the run's own;
	// required, so the agents are never named as the PR's own.
	AgentTag string
	// RunDir is the run's directory (RunsRoot/<run id>), an absolute path:
	// the case's scratch tree is RunDir/cases/<case>, and a refused replay
	// is flagged under the run's id, its base name.
	RunDir string
	// Worktrees is the directory the case's worktree goes in,
	// Worktrees/<case> (caseWorktree); "" = RunsRoot/wt, `magnum eval
	// run`'s. The daemon's gate gives its own
	// (paths.Layout.LearnEvalWorktrees), so the two never replace each
	// other's worktree of a case.
	Worktrees string
}
    Options are a case's settings, the run's.

```

## execx

```text
package execx // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/execx"

Package execx is the single choke point for every subprocess magnum runs (git,
gh, mysql, mise exec, launchctl, osascript, codex/claude probes).

Every call carries a timeout, runs in its own process group so a cancelled
context terminates the whole tree (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL), gets an explicit
env overlay and a working directory, captures at most MaxOutput per stream,
and logs a redacted transcript. Tests use Fake; --dry-run wraps the real runner
in DryRun so mutating commands are printed instead of run.

CONSTANTS

const DefaultTimeout = 2 * time.Minute
    DefaultTimeout applies when Cmd.Timeout is zero.

const MaxOutput = 8 << 20
    MaxOutput caps each captured stream (stdout and stderr separately). Output
    past it is drained and discarded so the child never blocks on a full pipe;
    the kept prefix is followed by TruncationMarker and Result.Truncated is set.

const TruncationMarker = "\n[execx: output truncated at 8 MiB]\n"
    TruncationMarker is appended to a stream cut at MaxOutput.


FUNCTIONS

func EventLevel(level string) slog.Level
    EventLevel is the slog level of an audit event's level ("debug", "info",
    "warn", "error"; anything else is info), for the line that mirrors the event
    in the log.

func FailLevel(ctx context.Context, err error) slog.Level
    FailLevel is the level of a line that reports err, a failure the caller
    tolerates: slog.LevelWarn, or slog.LevelInfo when err is the daemon stopping
    (IsStop), which cuts short every call in flight and is no fault.

func IsStop(ctx context.Context, err error) bool
    IsStop reports whether a failure is the daemon stopping rather than a fault:
    ctx ended (a shutdown cancels it, an abort cancels a round's) or err says
    the work was canceled.

func LogAt(l Logger, level slog.Level, format string, args ...any)
    LogAt sends one line to l: at level through Logf when l is a LevelLogger,
    else through Printf (a plain Logger has no levels). A nil l drops it.

func LogEvent(l Logger, level, subject, kind, line string)
    LogEvent mirrors an audit event to l as line: at the event's level
    (EventLevel), with its subject and kind as attributes when l is an
    AttrLogger, else as LogAt sends it. The caller redacts line.

func MergeEnv(base []string, env map[string]string, unset []string) []string
    MergeEnv returns base with env's keys overriding and unset's keys removed;
    it is what Run gives every subprocess and what other runners (the CLI's TTY
    runner) use to honour Cmd.Env and Cmd.Unset the same way.

func ProcessStart(ctx context.Context, r Runner, pid int) (string, error)
    ProcessStart is when process pid started, as ProcessTable reads it (ps's
    lstart in the C locale and in UTC, its words joined by one space): with the
    pid, the process's lifetime identity, the same text whatever TZ the reader
    has (the install drain compares the command's read with the daemon's).
    A pid no process has is an error.

func Redact(s string) string
    Redact masks GitHub tokens, JWTs, Authorization header values and PEM
    private keys in free text. An Authorization header keeps its name.

func ShellQuote(s string) string
    ShellQuote single-quotes s unless it consists only of characters a POSIX
    shell never interprets; the empty string becomes two single quotes. Newlines
    and carriage returns inside quotes are kept verbatim; callers that need one
    log line should escape them first.


TYPES

type AttrLogger interface {
	LevelLogger
	LogAttrs(level slog.Level, msg string, attrs ...slog.Attr)
}
    AttrLogger is a LevelLogger that also takes slog attributes with a line:
    the bridge to the daemon's slog.Logger (app.Printf) keeps an audit event's
    subject and kind as attributes of its record (LogEvent).

type Cmd struct {
	Name string   // executable; resolved through PATH unless absolute
	Args []string // argv after the executable
	Dir  string   // working directory ("" = inherit)
	// Env overlays the parent environment. An empty value blanks the variable
	// (exported as KEY= so shells and Ruby .presence treat it as unset).
	Env map[string]string
	// Unset removes variables from the inherited environment entirely (git,
	// for one, treats an empty GIT_DIR differently from an absent one). A key
	// that is also in Env keeps its Env value.
	Unset []string
	// Timeout bounds the run; zero means DefaultTimeout.
	Timeout time.Duration
	// Mutates marks commands that change state. DryRun refuses to execute them.
	Mutates bool
	// Stdin, when non-nil, is written to the process.
	Stdin []byte
	// Label is a short human name used in logs ("git fetch pr 123").
	Label string
	// Probe marks a command whose non-zero exit is an expected answer (is
	// this a git repository? does this ref exist?): a failed exit is logged
	// at Debug instead of Warn. Start failures and timeouts still warn.
	Probe bool
	// Expected, when set, picks the non-zero exits that are expected answers,
	// logged at Debug as Probe logs every one: gh api exits 1 for a 404 as
	// for a 500, and only its output tells them apart. Other exits still warn.
	Expected func(Result) bool
	// NoTTY starts the process in a new session, without a controlling
	// terminal (setsid), as launchd starts the daemon. An interactive shell
	// (`zsh -ic`) run from a CLI in a terminal otherwise shares that
	// terminal from a background process group, where shell startup that
	// touches the terminal stops it until the timeout.
	NoTTY bool
	// Quiet marks a command whose caller reports every failure itself (the
	// memory probe warns once per cause): Real logs its line at Debug
	// whatever the outcome, a timeout and a failed start included.
	Quiet bool
	// KeepTail, when positive, keeps the last KeepTail bytes of stdout
	// (at most MaxOutput) in place of its first MaxOutput: a CI job's log
	// ends where it failed. A longer stdout sets Result.Truncated, with no
	// TruncationMarker; stderr is captured as always.
	KeepTail int
	// Stream, when non-nil, gets what the process writes on stdout as it
	// writes it, besides the capture (Result keeps the output as before),
	// and stderr too unless StreamErr is set: a reader that cuts lines
	// keeps the two streams apart with a writer for each. Each stream is
	// written from its own goroutine, so one writer for both must be safe
	// for concurrent use. A failed write is ignored: the capture and the
	// process go on.
	Stream, StreamErr io.Writer
}
    Cmd describes one subprocess.

func (c Cmd) String() string
    String renders the command the way a shell would show it: every argument
    that is not plainly shell-safe is single-quoted (see ShellQuote). The result
    is not redacted; pass it through Redact before logging.

type DryRun struct {
	Inner Runner
	Out   Logger

	// Planned records the mutating commands that would have run.
	Planned []Cmd
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    DryRun executes read-only commands through Inner and only prints mutating
    ones.

func (d *DryRun) Run(ctx context.Context, c Cmd) (Result, error)
    Run implements Runner.

type ExitError struct {
	Cmd  Cmd
	Code int
	// Stderr is what the process wrote to stderr, redacted, and when longer
	// than 64 KiB only its first and last 32 KiB around a "[N bytes cut]"
	// line (Result.Stderr keeps it whole): the error is wrapped into step
	// rows, a PR's last_error and log lines.
	Stderr string
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    ExitError is returned when the process ran but exited non-zero.

func (e *ExitError) Error() string

type Fake struct {
	Rules []Rule

	Calls []Cmd
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Fake is a scripted Runner for tests. Unmatched commands fail loudly.

func (f *Fake) CallsWithPrefix(prefix ...string) []Cmd
    CallsWithPrefix returns the recorded calls whose argv starts with prefix.

func (f *Fake) Run(ctx context.Context, c Cmd) (Result, error)
    Run implements Runner.

type LevelLogger interface {
	Logger
	Logf(level slog.Level, format string, args ...any)
}
    LevelLogger is a Logger that also takes a level per line. Real logs a
    command that succeeded at slog.LevelDebug and one that failed (a non-zero
    exit, a failed start, a timeout) at slog.LevelWarn when its Log implements
    it, except one the caller's context cancellation ended (the daemon stopping)
    and a Quiet command, which are logged at slog.LevelDebug; a plain Logger
    gets every line through Printf.

type Logger interface {
	Printf(format string, args ...any)
}
    Logger receives one line per finished command (already redacted).

type Process struct {
	PID    int    `json:"pid"`
	PPID   int    `json:"-"`
	PGID   int    `json:"pgid"`
	Start  string `json:"-"`
	Zombie bool   `json:"-"`
	Name   string `json:"name"`
}
    Process is one row of the process table (ProcessTable): its id, its
    parent's, its process group's, when it started (ps's lstart, which tells a
    process from a later one that got its id), whether it is a zombie (it ended;
    its parent has not reaped it) and its executable's base name (ps's comm,
    never its arguments).

func Descendants(table []Process, pid int) []Process
    Descendants are the processes of table under pid: its children, theirs and
    so on, parents before their children; pid itself is not one. A process that
    left pid's process group (a sandbox's child in a session of its own) is
    still one while its parent is.

func Find(table []Process, p Process) (Process, bool)
    Find is the process of table that is p (Same) and still runs (no zombie).

func ProcessTable(ctx context.Context, r Runner) ([]Process, error)
    ProcessTable reads the process table through r (`ps -A -o
    pid=,ppid=,pgid=,stat=,lstart=,comm=` in the C locale, on macOS and Linux
    alike). A line it cannot read is skipped.

func (p Process) Same(q Process) bool
    Same reports whether p and q are one process: the same id and start (its
    lifetime identity). The process group is not part of it: a process may move
    to another group or session (setsid) and stays itself; the group only says
    what a group signal reaches. A process without a start is never the same as
    another.

type Real struct {
	// Log, when set, receives a redacted one-line transcript per command:
	// at debug level for a success and at warn level for a failure when it
	// is a LevelLogger (a command the caller's cancellation ended: debug).
	// A failed command's line ends with " stderr=" and the first non-blank
	// line of its stderr, redacted and cut to 200 runes; no Cmd flag
	// withholds it.
	Log Logger
	// BaseEnv, when non-empty, replaces os.Environ() as the parent environment.
	BaseEnv []string
}
    Real runs commands with os/exec.

func (r *Real) Run(ctx context.Context, c Cmd) (Result, error)
    Run executes the command in its own process group. When the context is
    cancelled or the timeout elapses the whole group gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL
    after killGrace. Descendants that outlive the leader while still holding its
    output pipes are killed too. Every error renders the command redacted.

type Result struct {
	Stdout   []byte
	Stderr   []byte
	Code     int
	Duration time.Duration
	// Truncated reports that a stream exceeded MaxOutput: the kept prefix is
	// followed by TruncationMarker and the rest was discarded.
	Truncated bool
}
    Result is the outcome of a finished subprocess.

func (r Result) Out() string
    Out returns trimmed stdout.

type Rule struct {
	Prefix []string
	Result Result
	Err    error
	// Fn, when set, computes the response from the actual command.
	Fn func(c Cmd) (Result, error)
}
    Rule scripts one Fake response. Prefix matches the leading argv words (Name
    followed by Args); the first matching rule wins.

type RunError struct {
	Cmd Cmd
	Err error
}
    RunError is a runner failure other than a non-zero exit: a missing working
    directory, a failed start, a cancelled or timed-out context. Its message
    shows the redacted command line; Unwrap exposes the cause (context errors,
    fs.ErrNotExist, exec.ErrNotFound) for errors.Is.

func (e *RunError) Error() string

func (e *RunError) Unwrap() error

type Runner interface {
	Run(ctx context.Context, c Cmd) (Result, error)
}
    Runner executes commands. Implementations: Real, Fake, DryRun.

```

## factory

```text
package factory // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/factory"

Package factory is the magnum factory: a second daemon, in the magnum
binary and with a registry of its own, that takes a Jira key or a free
prompt and does the work up to the final merge, which stays the operator's.
Agents investigate in parallel, one writer writes the change test
first, and the operator answers only what no agent can answer. See
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-factory-design.md, section 5 for the processes
and the state the factory keeps.

The registry lives in the registry package (SQLite, its own migrations);
the daemon, its stages and its screen build on it.

CONSTANTS

const (
	LocalReviewPrompt = evalrun.LocalReviewPrompt
	LiveReviewPrompt  = evalrun.LiveReviewPrompt
)
    LocalReviewPrompt is the local reviewer prompt, the candidate's
    claude-review.md; LiveReviewPrompt the prompt it stands in for. They are
    evalrun's, whose RunLocal gives every local round, the factory's and a
    replay's of a local case alike, the local prompt in the live one's place
    (evalrun.LocalReviewConfig): the swap here is the same text again.

const (
	HoldInfra  = "infra"
	HoldHerdr  = "herdr"
	HoldDisk   = "disk"
	HoldMemory = "memory"
	// HoldDrain is the drain `magnum factory install --drain` asks for:
	// nothing new starts until the restart.
	HoldDrain = "drain"
)
    The kinds of Hold.

const (
	QAEscapedMarkup = "escaped_markup"
	QARawI18nKey    = "raw_i18n_key"
	QAErrorPage     = "error_page"
	QABrokenLayout  = "broken_layout"
	QAConsoleError  = "console_error"
	QAFlow          = "flow"
)
    The classes of a QA defect. The factory finds the first three, the console's
    errors and a page that scrolls sideways itself; flow is the walker's alone
    (a step of a check that does not do what it says).

const (
	QAOutcomeClean       = "clean"
	QAOutcomeDefects     = "defects"
	QAOutcomeUnavailable = "unavailable"
	QAOutcomeNotNeeded   = "not_needed"
	QAOutcomePressure    = "pressure"
	QAOutcomeInterrupted = "interrupted"
)
    The outcomes of a QA run: clean, defects (one blocks), unavailable (no page
    to judge), not_needed (no user-facing file changed), pressure (the Mac's
    memory stopped it) and interrupted (the daemon stopped it).

const (
	ReqStart   = "start"
	ReqAnswer  = "answer"
	ReqDecide  = "decide"
	ReqStop    = "stop"
	ReqPreview = "preview"
	ReqLetGo   = "let_go"
	ReqRetry   = "retry"
	ReqFocus   = "focus"
	ReqTalk    = "talk"
	ReqRate    = "rate"
)
    Request kinds.

const (
	WorkRound  = "round"  // a round of the local review
	WorkCheck  = "check"  // the factory's proof and precheck of a head
	WorkClaim  = "claim"  // a claim of a copy
	WorkTalk   = "talk"   // a talk with a task's liaison
	WorkQA     = "qa"     // a QA run: its server, its browser and its walk
	WorkRepair = "repair" // a broken copy's repair on its backoff
)
    The kinds of WorkItem.

const (
	ChoicePush     = "push"
	ChoiceSendBack = "send_back"
	ChoiceDrop     = "drop"
)
    The choices of the ready card.

const AmendPrompt = "factory-amend.md"
    AmendPrompt is the prompt of the judge's turn that amends report.md when
    your answers change the plan: the report stage's roles get it in place of
    their own prompt.

const DiffOrderFile = "diff-order.txt"
    DiffOrderFile is the order file (git diff -O) of a ready card's diff in
    the task's directory: its files as the card lists them, flagged first,
    so the pager shows them in that order.

const HandoffFile = "handoff.md"
    HandoffFile is the file of a task's directory a release writes: how the task
    left its copy, for whoever claims a copy for it next.

const LaunchLabel = "zhuravel.magnum.factory"
    LaunchLabel is the launchd label of the factory daemon's LaunchAgent,
    apart from the review daemon's (launchd.DefaultLabel), so either restarts
    without the other.

const LocalRoundCap = 3 * time.Hour
    LocalRoundCap ends a round of the local review that runs this long (a hang):
    a round takes 39 minutes at the median, its roles' own timeouts end within
    the hour. `magnum factory install --drain` waits longer.

const QAFixPrompt = "factory-qa-fix.md"
    QAFixPrompt is the prompt of the writer's fix turn of QA's defects:
    the coding stage's roles get it in place of their own prompt.

const QAMaxShots = 30
    QAMaxShots is the most screenshots one QA run may leave in its folder.

const QAVerdictVersion = 1
    QAVerdictVersion is the version of the QA verdict this build reads;
    a verdict of any other version is refused.

const ReasonKnown = "known"
    ReasonKnown is the reason of the send back that hands the writer the known
    defects of the card's review (knownDefects): the factory writes its note
    from the card, so it takes no note of yours.

const RedisDBsPerCopy = 16
    RedisDBsPerCopy is how many Redis databases a copy has: copy n's start at n
    × RedisDBsPerCopy (REDIS_DB_OFFSET).

const RedisOffsetEnv = "REDIS_DB_OFFSET"
    RedisOffsetEnv is the variable a copy's Redis configuration reads its first
    database from. A repository whose env names it gets each copy's own offset
    there, whatever value the env gives it.

const RetryFixTurns = 2
    RetryFixTurns is how many more fix turns a role whose change the factory's
    checks still refuse gets after your retry at its stage's cap (StageFixTurns
    fix turns in the attempt), counted from that retry; each later retry at the
    cap gives them again (fixBudgetOf).

const ReviewFixPrompt = "factory-review-fix.md"
    ReviewFixPrompt is the prompt of the writer's fix turn in the local review:
    the coding stage's roles get it in place of their own prompt.

const StageFixTurns = runtime.MaxStagePrompts - 1
    StageFixTurns is how many fix turns a role whose change the factory's
    checks refuse gets in its stage's attempt: the runtime's prompt cap
    (runtime.MaxStagePrompts) less the attempt's first prompt, so a role that
    got no other prompt reaches both at once. Only fix turns count (fixTurn):
    the watchdog's nudge of a hung turn, the resume of a lost pane, the nudge
    for a file and the prompt of your answers spend none (fixBudgetOf).


VARIABLES

var (
	// ErrNoCopy is a claim no copy is free for: every copy the repository
	// may have is busy or broken. It costs the task nothing (it is ErrHeld
	// too): the task waits with the reason the error gives, "copy: all 3
	// busy" (claimCopy).
	ErrNoCopy = errors.New("factory: no free copy")
	// ErrPaneInCopy is a release refused while one of the factory's
	// sessions works in the copy.
	ErrPaneInCopy = errors.New("factory: a pane runs in the copy")
)
var (
	// ErrKeyRuns is a start for a Jira key that a task holds (it is not
	// done or stopped): the start returns that task and makes none. The
	// error's text names the task, or its PR.
	ErrKeyRuns = errors.New("factory: the key has a task")
	// ErrLater is a start of a later milestone: a PR link (adoption,
	// milestone 2) or a run link (CI tasks, milestone 3).
	ErrLater = errors.New("factory: not in this milestone")
)
var ErrDenied = errors.New("denied")
    ErrDenied marks a command the deny list refused (Guard): it never started.

var ErrHeld = errors.New("held")
```
