    ErrHeld marks a launch or an effect that the engine held back: the daemon
    drains, or a hold of the machine is on. It costs the task nothing.

var ReproductionOptions = []string{"give a hint", "take the other cause", "try Docker or a staging", "drop"}
    ReproductionOptions are the options of the question a bug that did not
    reproduce asks (spec 6.3), in the judge's prompt's words: one of them is
    recommended.


FUNCTIONS

func Blocks(r evalrun.LocalResult) (blocks, unavailable bool, why string)
    Blocks reads local round r: blocks when a P0, P1 or P2 finding is new
    (Counts) or still open (OpenCounts), or the judge's verdict is "blocking";
    unavailable when the round did not finish as a dry run (needs_attention,
    blocked, error, timeout, a refusal, a stop, no outcome at all) or its result
    does not parse (no verdict): review unavailable, never clean, whatever the
    result says (Review Focus 1). why says which, in plain words that carry no
    finding's text ("" when nothing blocks).

func CheckEnd(fact string, dir string, since time.Time, roles ...string) (ok bool, why string)
    CheckEnd reports whether end fact fact holds in task directory dir for a
    stage that started at since; why names the file at fault and what is wrong
    ("findings-fx-cause.md: missing"). roles are the stage's roles, as the stage
    names them:
      - findings: findings-<role>.md of each role, newer than since and not
        empty, and its questions-<role>.json, when it is there, valid as
        questions.json is;
      - report: report.md, newer than since, whose first section is `##
        Architecture decisions` (its decisions, or none) and whose Helpers and
        Files sections exist (Files naming at least one file); acceptance.json,
        newer than since, with at least one check; and questions.json,
        when it is there, newer than since and holding questions the operator
        can answer. A report whose Proof says the bug did not reproduce needs
        the reproduction question among them, with ReproductionOptions and a
        recommendation;
      - critic: critic.md, newer than since and not empty, and each role's
        questions-<role>.json, when it is there, valid as questions.json is;
      - pr_body: pr-body.md, newer than since and not empty;
      - proof: proof.json, newer than since, naming the spec files of the
        writer's proof as clean paths relative to the checkout (ProofFile),
        and its questions-<role>.json, when it is there, valid. The rest of the
        fact (commits on the branch after origin/<base>, no tracked change,
        the factory's own proof and the precheck passed at the head) is the
        coding stage's to check (provenHead);
      - qa: the QA walker's verdict.json in the newest run's folder
        (qa-run.json), newer than since, valid for the run and covering
        acceptance.json's checks (checkQAEnd). The outcome (clean, defects,
        unavailable) is the qa stage's to decide from the saved pages
        (evaluateQA).

    The clean and pr facts are checked by the stages that own them, not here
    (not done, saying so).

func CheckPrompts(cfg *config.Config) error
    CheckPrompts renders the prompt of every factory role ([[factory.role]]),
    every agents stage's own prompt (FactoryStage.Prompt), the amend turn's
    (AmendPrompt, for the roles of each kind's report stage) and the writer's
    fix turns' (ReviewFixPrompt and QAFixPrompt) with data whose every field
    is set, as the factory daemon does once at startup, after it loaded its
    prompts: a prompt (or factory-shared.md) that names a field the data lacks,
    or a block the partials file does not define, is an error naming the role or
    the stage and its file.

func ConfirmSentence(t registry.Task, frees string, starts string) string
    ConfirmSentence is the y/N question of the ready card's push: the branch it
    pushes (the task's remote branch, else its own), the copy it frees and the
    queued task that then starts (each left out when "").

func DaemonPID(l paths.Layout) (int, error)
    DaemonPID returns the pid of the running factory daemon from its pidfile
    (paths.Layout.FactoryPid), or 0 when there is no pidfile or that process is
    gone. Like the review daemon's it never touches the lock: probing it could
    make a starting daemon exit as "already running".

func DaemonPIDWith(l paths.Layout, procs engine.Processes) (int, error)
    DaemonPIDWith is DaemonPID with the processes it asks about given, so a test
    needs no real process.

func Denied(argv []string, repo config.FactoryRepo) (why string, denied bool)
    Denied reports whether the factory may not run argv, and why, in plain
    words: gh-ost with any argument, kubectl exec (and the other verbs that
    reach into a pod: attach, debug, run, cp, port-forward), and each of repo's
    consoles at a command's place. It reads through the wrappers a command
    runs another under (mise exec, env and its assignments, bundle exec, exec,
    command, nohup, time, nice, timeout, xargs, sudo) and into a shell's -c
    script, each command of it (; && || | & and newlines, $( and backticks);
    gh-ost and kubectl's verbs are also found as words anywhere in a script,
    quoted or not, so a substitution inside quotes does not hide them. A
    console's own file as an argument (lint of bin/remote-console) is no console
    run.

func DiffArgs(c ReadyCardFile, orderFile string) []string
    DiffArgs are the arguments of git that page the diff of ready card c in its
    copy, as every diff of the factory reads one (no external diff, no textconv:
    the copy's attributes are the change's), its files in the order of orderFile
    ("" for git's own order: git refuses an order file it cannot read):
    `git --paginate -C <copy> diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv [-O<order>]
    <base>...<head> --`. It reads nothing.

func DiffOrderPath(l paths.Layout, id int64) string
    DiffOrderPath is task id's DiffOrderFile in layout l.

func Fingerprint(f evalrun.LocalFinding) string
    Fingerprint is how the factory follows a finding across rounds: its path,
    its line rounded down to a window of 10, and a hash of its title without its
    priority ("app/credit.rb:40:1a2b3c4d5e6f"). A finding re-ranked, or moved
    within its window, is the same one.

func FixLoopsOf(ctx context.Context, l paths.Layout, refs []PRRef) (map[PRRef]FixLoops, error)
    FixLoopsOf counts, per PR of refs, the fix loops magnum's registry in
    layout l recorded: its fix.start events of cycle 1 (a later cycle is
    the same loop), by who started each (engine.AutofixBy, or by hand),
    and its fix.pushed events with the commits each names (one that names none
    is one commit: a push carries at least one), over the whole history the
    registry keeps ([daemon] keep_events). A PR it has no event of counts zero.
    It reads and never writes or migrates the registry, as PRStates; no registry
    counts nothing and creates none.

func Guard(next execx.Runner, cfg *config.Config) execx.Runner
    Guard puts the deny list (Denied) in front of next, with the consoles of
    every [[factory.repo]] of cfg: a command it denies never starts, and its
    error (ErrDenied) says why. A runner Guard made is returned as it is;
    nil stays nil. The factory daemon runs every command of its own through one.

func Kick(l paths.Layout) (int, error)
    Kick asks the running factory daemon for a pass now (SIGUSR1); it returns
    the daemon's pid, or 0 when none runs. The pidfile can outlive the daemon
    and its pid be reused, and SIGUSR1 terminates a process that does not handle
    it: the pid is signalled only when ps shows `magnum factory daemon` (not the
    review daemon, `magnum daemon`, whose pidfile is another file).

func KickWith(l paths.Layout, procs engine.Processes) (int, error)
    KickWith is Kick with the processes it asks about given, so a test needs no
    real process.

func LiftDrain(l paths.Layout, value string) error
    LiftDrain removes the drain asked of the factory daemon of layout l when it
    is value; a drain asked since by another command, or none, is left alone.

func Lock(l paths.Layout) (unlock func(), err error)
    Lock takes the factory daemon's lock (Layout.FactoryLock), held for the
    daemon's whole life; another daemon holding it is ErrRunning, naming that
    daemon's pid. The daemon command takes it before it opens its log or a
    store, so a second daemon touches neither (RunLocked).

func LooksLikeFactoryDaemon(comm, args string) bool
    LooksLikeFactoryDaemon reports whether a process is a magnum factory daemon
    from what engine.ProcessCommand read: the executable is magnum and its first
    arguments that are not flags are "factory daemon".

func NextQueued(tasks []registry.Task) string
    NextQueued is the key of the queued task that starts when a copy frees:
    the oldest queued task, when it waits for a copy ("" when none waits,
    or the oldest waits on something a copy does not free, such as memory:
    no queued task jumps another).

func OperatorReadEnv(ctx context.Context, id config.Identity, run execx.Runner) (map[string]string, error)
    OperatorReadEnv is the env of a read as you, gh identity id, for a caller
    that can only set variables (internal/staging's fetch, a GitHub client's
    Env): identity.GH's (GH_HOST pinned) with your gh config dir named
    (operatorGHDir) and every GitHub token of the daemon's environment set
    empty, which gh reads as unset. So gh, and git through gh's credential
    helper, answer as your login, never as a token the daemon inherited
    (asOperator unsets them for the publish).

func PickKind(cfg config.Factory, t *jira.Ticket, prompt string) (kind, why string)
    PickKind picks the kind of a task: the kind kind_by_jira_type maps the
    ticket's issue type to (the type's case ignored), else the kind whose
    kind_words the ticket's summary and prompt use most (a word's own forms,
    "crashes" for "crash", count; a tie goes to the kind used first), else bug.
    Only a configured kind is picked. why says how, in the words the new-task
    screen shows.

func PromptNames(cfg *config.Config) []string
    PromptNames are the prompt files the factory renders: each factory role's
    (of each prompt kind), each agents stage's own, the amend turn's and
    the writer's fix turns', once each; the daemon loads them at startup
    (config.SnapshotPrompts).

func QuestionKey(text string) string
    QuestionKey is how a question is told from the questions the task asked,
    here and in the CLI: registry.QuestionKey (its text, lowercased, without its
    marks, spaces and end punctuation), the rule by which answers.md keeps only
    the newest answer of a question asked again.

func RatingReasons() []string
    RatingReasons are the keys a rating takes for its reason, in order.

func ReadDrain(l paths.Layout) (string, error)
    ReadDrain is the drain asked of the factory daemon of layout l ("" for
    none).

func ReadSeen(l paths.Layout) (time.Time, error)
    ReadSeen is when you last saw the factory screen's home, as SaveSeen kept it
    in layout l; the zero time before the first.

func ReadyRecommendation(ctx context.Context, reg *registry.Registry, t registry.Task, card ReadyCardFile) (choice, why string)
    ReadyRecommendation is the choice task t's ready card recommends (push,
    send_back) and why, as the screen's card says it once you read the diff and
    `magnum factory decide` prints it: from card and the checks the factory ran
    itself at its head, read from reg (a registry that cannot be read counts
    none failed).

func ReviewCandidateDir(l paths.Layout) string
    ReviewCandidateDir is where the factory writes its review candidate:
    <data>/factory/review-candidate/.

func SaveSeen(l paths.Layout, at time.Time) error
    SaveSeen keeps that you saw home at at in seen.json of layout l, so it
    survives a restart of the screen and of the daemon. The time only moves
    forward: an earlier time than the one kept changes nothing, and two screens
    saving at once take turns on a lock of the file's own, so the later time
    stays.

func ScreenData(ctx context.Context, reg *registry.Registry, agents *store.Store, now, lastSeen time.Time, o ScreenOptions) (tui.FactoryData, error)
    ScreenData is the factory screen's data at now for an operator last seen
    on home at lastSeen (zero: never): see the file's comment. agents may be
    nil (no agent ran yet): the tasks then have no agents. reg may be nil (the
    factory has no registry yet: no task was ever started): home then has no
    task, news or alert, and lists your PRs alone.

func StagingIdentity(cfg *config.Config, repo string) (config.Identity, error)
    StagingIdentity is the identity the staging status of repo reads
    as (internal/staging: its mirror's fetch and its GitHub reads):
    the poll identity of the watch that covers repo (its identity without
    a poll_identity), as magnum's review daemon reads that repository,
    so both daemons fill the mirror's shared state as one login, the one
    Deployments: read is to be granted to (until it is, no deploy is confirmed:
    a pushed PR stays deploying, never latest); a repository no watch covers
    reads as the gh identity the factory publishes as (operatorIdentity),
    as you (OperatorReadEnv).

func TaskKey(t registry.Task) string
    TaskKey names a task as the screen and the waits do: its Jira key, else
    "task <id>".

func WriteDrain(l paths.Layout, value string) error
    WriteDrain asks the factory daemon of layout l for a drain: value is
    Drain.Value (since when, and the asking command's pid and start), and it
    replaces any drain asked before.

func WriteReviewCandidate(l paths.Layout) (string, error)
    WriteReviewCandidate writes the review candidate the factory's local rounds
    run with (their config is cfg.WithCandidate(dir)) and returns its directory:
    prompts/ with every prompt this build embeds, the partials files included,
    LocalReviewPrompt as claude-review.md, and the build's judge skill at
    skills/magnum-review/SKILL.md (magnum.Skill). The factory daemon writes it
    once, at startup, as it loads its own prompts: whatever an earlier build
    left there goes. Magnum's live rounds never read it.


TYPES

type AcceptanceCheck struct {
	ID    string `json:"id"`
	Point string `json:"point"`
	Given string `json:"given"`
	Then  string `json:"then"`
	How   string `json:"how"`
}
    AcceptanceCheck is one check: its id (A1), the ticket's point it proves,
    the setup, what must hold, and how it is checked (a spec, a QA step).

type AcceptanceFile struct {
	Checks []AcceptanceCheck `json:"checks"`
}
    AcceptanceFile is acceptance.json, the judge's checks that prove the task,
    from the ticket: the writer and QA reuse them.

type AnswerPayload struct {
	TaskID   int64
	Revision int
	Answers  map[int]string
	Needless map[int]string
	Surface  string
	Shown    time.Time `json:",omitzero"`
}
    AnswerPayload is a ReqAnswer: your answers to the questions of revision
    Revision of task TaskID, by question index (from 0): an option's label,
    your own words, or "ask:<login>" (then, optionally, the comment for that
    person in your words) to ask someone else; Needless are the questions you
    call needless, by index, with the key of your reason. Surface is where you
    answered (the screen, the CLI, the liaison), for the record of your input.
    Shown is when the questions of Revision were shown to you, when the surface
    knows it (the liaison notes it before it asks): the stats count your time on
    the batch from it. It is left out of the request when zero, so a daemon that
    predates it still takes an answer that names no time.

type CardFile struct {
	Path    string `json:"path"`
	Added   int    `json:"added,omitempty"`
	Removed int    `json:"removed,omitempty"`
	InPlan  bool   `json:"in_plan"`
	Flagged bool   `json:"flagged,omitempty"`
}
    CardFile is one file the change of a ready card changes: its path, the lines
    its diff adds and removes (both 0 for a binary file), whether the plan
    named it, and whether a FLAGS line names it (a migration the branch adds,
    a sensitive file, an old guard, a conflict with the base).

type Copies interface {
	Claim(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task) (Copy, error)
	Release(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task, reason string) error
	Free(ctx context.Context) (int, error)
	Reserved(ctx context.Context) ([]Reservation, error)
	StartServer(ctx context.Context, c Copy) error
	StopServer(ctx context.Context, c Copy) error
	StartBrowser(ctx context.Context, c Copy, dir string) (cdp string, err error)
	StopBrowser(ctx context.Context, c Copy) error
	Reconcile(ctx context.Context) error
	RepairDue(ctx context.Context) (string, error)
	Repair(ctx context.Context, name string) error
	Outages(ctx context.Context) ([]Outage, error)
}
    Copies are the repositories' copies the tasks work in (copies.go): a claim
    for a task (the copy it used last first), its release, how many are free,
    the copies reserved and for which task, the copy's local server, the
    factory's headless Chrome for a copy's QA run (its profile in dir/chrome,
    cdp its DevTools endpoint, http://127.0.0.1:<port>), the reconcile of the
    servers and the browsers after a restart, and the broken copies (the one
    whose backoff repair is due, its repair, and the repositories whose every
    copy broke the same way: repair.go).

func NewCopies(cfg *config.Config, sm *slots.Manager, st *store.Store, git *gitx.Client, run execx.Runner, my slots.MySQL,
	panes func(context.Context) (herdr.Snapshot, error), owner func(context.Context, registry.Task) (store.PR, error),
	atWork func(context.Context, registry.Task) (role string, you bool, err error)) Copies
    NewCopies returns the factory's copies: sm is magnum's slot manager over st,
    the factory's agents store (Layout.FactoryAgentsDB, magnum's schema), whose
    guard sees herdr.GuardView; git and run run the claim protocol's commands,
    my reads a copy's development database (nil: no reset_db at a claim), panes
    is the factory's herdr session's snapshot (a pane in a copy that no session
    row names holds it; nil: no such check), owner is the runtime's Owner,
    the task's row in st a copy is claimed for, and atWork the runtime's AtWork,
    who of the claiming task is at work in the copy (its own sessions hold a
    claim only then; nil: they always do). A claim adds copy n on demand with
    sm.ProvisionPool (FactoryRepo.Pool with the copy's env), up to max_copies.

type Copy = runtime.Copy
    Copy is a task's copy of a repository: its name and path, its number (copy
    {n}), the port of its server and its environment (runtime.Copy: a launch
    runs the task's panes in it).

type DecidePayload struct {
	TaskID                                              int64
	Choice, Reason, Note, HeadSHA, ReportHash, DiffHash string
	DiffOpened, Shown                                   time.Time
	DiffDwell                                           time.Duration
	Surface                                             string
	Recommended                                         string
}
    DecidePayload is a ReqDecide: your decision on task TaskID's ready card.
    Choice is push, send_back or drop; a send back takes the key of its
    Reason and a Note to the writer (the reason ReasonKnown takes none:
    the factory writes the note). HeadSHA, ReportHash and DiffHash are what
    the card showed (ReadyCardFile), Shown when it was shown, DiffOpened when
    you opened the diff (zero: you did not) and DiffDwell how long you read it.
    Surface is where you decided (the screen, the CLI). Recommended is the
    choice the card recommended as it showed it to you (push, send_back or drop;
    the screen draws it once you read the diff, the CLI's card always), "" when
    it showed none: the decision records that one was shown and whether your
    choice took it.

type Deps struct {
	Config   *config.Config
	Layout   paths.Layout
	Registry *registry.Registry
	Runtime  Runtime
	Copies   Copies
	Jira     Jira
	GitHub   GitHub
	Magnum   Magnum
	Review   LocalReviewer
	// ReviewCandidate is the directory of the review candidate the local
	// rounds run with (WriteReviewCandidate): its skill's hash goes on each
	// round's cycle. Usage reads Codex's budget (nil: usage.Codex of [usage]
	// codex_home), which a local round with a Codex role yields to at
	// [usage] codex_soft.
	ReviewCandidate string
	Usage           func(ctx context.Context, now time.Time) (usage.Snapshot, error)
	Git             *gitx.Client
	// Run runs the overlap line's reads (Overlap: git log in the main
	// clone, gh pr list as your gh login) and the factory's own commands in
	// a task's copy (its precheck and its proof), every one through the deny
	// list (Guard: New wraps it). The daemon builds Git over the same
	// guarded runner.
	Run execx.Runner
	// Memory reads the machine's memory (engine.ReadMemory); Disk the free
	// bytes of the filesystem that holds path; MemProcs the process table
	// (ReadMemProcs), whose largest processes and Codex brokers the memory
	// hold names (nil names none).
	Memory   func(ctx context.Context) engine.MemorySample
	Disk     func(path string) (free uint64, err error)
	MemProcs func(ctx context.Context) ([]MemProc, error)
	// MySQL pings the copies' database server; HerdrUp asks the factory's
	// herdr session whether it answers; Reveal opens a terminal on it
	// (`herdr --session <herdr_session>`, internal/reveal).
	MySQL   func(ctx context.Context) error
	HerdrUp func(ctx context.Context) error
	Reveal  func(ctx context.Context) error
	// ReviewHerdrUp asks the herdr session of magnum's review panes, where
	// the local review opens its panes (config.Config.ReviewHerdr: [herdr]
	// review_session, yours by default), whether it answers; nil takes it
	// as up. ReviewReveal opens a client of it in a new terminal window,
	// which starts its server; nil while that session is yours, which the
	// factory never opens.
	ReviewHerdrUp func(ctx context.Context) error
	ReviewReveal  func(ctx context.Context) error
	// Notifier shows the alerts' toasts (alerts.go): magnum's notify, through
	// your herdr session (osascript after), deduplicated in a store of
	// magnum's schema (the factory's agents store); the delivery toasts
	// through a copy of it that waits out less of herdr's rate limit, so a
	// toast fits its bound on the loop. nil shows none, and the alerts wait
	// for a build that has one. Sidebar reports a task's sidebar
	// token on a workspace of the factory's herdr session
	// (notify.Notifier.Sidebar); nil reports none.
	Notifier *notify.Notifier
	Sidebar  func(ctx context.Context, workspaceID string, tokens map[string]string) error
	// Staging reads where the published tasks' PRs stand on their
	// repositories' staging envs (staging.go: NewStaging, over
	// internal/staging's client, which the daemon builds only when a
	// [[factory.repo]] has staging entries); nil reads none, and no row has
	// staging cells.
	Staging Staging
	// Clock returns the current time; nil means time.Now.
	Clock func() time.Time
	Log   *slog.Logger
}
    Deps are the engine's collaborators. Config, Layout and Registry are
    required; any other may be nil, and what needs it waits (a collaborator a
    build does not wire yet) or is skipped (a function field: no memory read,
    no disk check, no MySQL ping, herdr taken as up, no reveal).

type Drain struct {
	Since time.Time
	PID   int
	Start string
}
    Drain is a drain install asks for (drain.json): when it started, and the pid
    and the start (ps's lstart: a pid another process took since has another) of
    the command that asks.

func ParseDrain(v string) (Drain, bool)
    ParseDrain reads a drain.json value (Drain.Value); false for anything else.

func (d Drain) Value() string
    Value is d as drain.json holds it.

type Engine struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Engine is the factory daemon's loop. New builds it, Run runs it until a stop
    signal, and Tick is one pass of it.

func New(d Deps) *Engine
    New builds the engine over d.

func (e *Engine) Blocking() []string
    Blocking is the factory's NEEDS YOU blockers of the home screen, one line
    each ("infra: SSH key refused, held since 14:02"), sorted.

func (e *Engine) Kick()
    Kick asks the loop for a tick now (SIGUSR1, `magnum factory start` and the
    screen's requests); a kick already pending absorbs it.

func (e *Engine) MayLaunch() (who, what string, ok bool)
    MayLaunch is mayLaunch for the runtime, which passes the same holds when
    it starts a role outside a launch (runtime.Deps.MayStart). It reads the
    engine's holds, so it is called on the engine's loop.

func (e *Engine) Overlap(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task, files []string) (string, error)
    Overlap is the advisory line of what else touches task t's work ("" for
    nothing): the commits that name its key, the PRs that name it, and the
    open PRs that change files (the report's). Each part is read on its own;
    one that fails leaves the others' line, and the error says what failed.
    A build without a runner (Deps.Run) reads nothing.

func (e *Engine) Run(ctx context.Context) error
    Run takes the factory lock (Lock; another daemon holding it is ErrRunning)
    and runs the daemon (RunLocked) until it stops.

func (e *Engine) RunLocked(ctx context.Context) error
    RunLocked runs the daemon, whose lock the caller holds (Lock), until SIGTERM
    or SIGINT, or until ctx ends: it writes the pidfile, opens its hook socket
    (listenHooks), runs startup, serves the socket (serveHooks), then runs a
    tick at once, every factory poll and on SIGUSR1, and an observe pass every
    factory observe and, at most once a second, at once when the agents' hooks
    ask for one (hookPasses; one that saw an event a stage acts on kicks a tick
    right after it), none once the stop signal came. A stop signal drains:
    no new launch or effect starts (a launch that waits for the stagger is cut),
    the tick in progress ends with the task it advances (the others, and the
    alerts, wait for the next daemon), the waits for the hooks' looks and for
    the work off the loop end within drainBudget of the signal, and it returns
    nil, so launchd (KeepAlive on a failed exit only) starts the daemon again
    only after a crash.

func (e *Engine) Tick(ctx context.Context) error
    Tick runs one pass of the loop: the holds (herdr, disk and memory,
    then the infrastructure hold and a MySQL ping before a pass that advances),
    the requests, the published tasks' PRs (followPRs, whether or not the
    pass advances), their staging status (stagingPass, whose Refreshes run
    off the loop), the answers of the last batch of reads of the tasks'
    Jira issues (takeTracking) and the PRs' status files (writePRStatuses),
    then each live task's advance under its own panic guard (safely), then the
    Jira comment each task's milestone would keep, in shadow (jiraComments),
    and the next batch of those reads, off the loop, with what the intake's
    tries left of the tick's Jira budget (trackJira), the reads of the plans
    of the Jira moves among them (jira_plans.go). During an infrastructure or
    a herdr hold no task advances except on the hold's tries, and while herdr
    does not answer no copy a base run left detached is swept (sweepDetached,
    each under safely too); a failure that a hold covers costs its task nothing.
    Last, the alerts are delivered (deliverAlerts). The returned error joins
    what failed, for the log; each step records its own. A task's held wait is
    no error of the tick: logHeld logs it once, at WARN only past heldWarnAfter.
    A task whose stage failed for a cause of its own is advanced no sooner than
    a poll after the failure (retryLater).

type ErrRunning struct {
	PID  int
	Lock string
}
    ErrRunning is Run's answer when another factory daemon holds the lock:
    PID is that daemon's, from its pidfile (0 when it could not be read).

func (e ErrRunning) Error() string
    Error implements error.

type FixLoops struct {
	ByHand, ByAutofix int
	Pushes, Commits   int
}
    FixLoops counts the fix loops magnum started on a PR: by hand (`magnum fix`,
    f on the board) and by autofix; and the fixers' pushes on it (fix.pushed)
    and the commits they pushed.

type FixRecord struct {
	Loops, Cycle, Pushes, Threads int
	LeftToYou                     bool
}
    FixRecord is what magnum's registry recorded of the fix loops on a PR
    (Magnum.FixRecords), from its fix events over the history it keeps ([daemon]
    keep_events): the loops started (a fix.start of cycle 1), the cycle of the
    newest fix.start, the fixers' pushes (fix.pushed), the review threads they
    replied in (fix.replied's count), and whether the newest of the loop's
    starts and ends left the PR to you (fix.needs_you, fix.capped, fix.failed)
    rather than ending it (fix.done, fix.ended, fix.stopped) or starting a
    cycle. Counts only, never an event's text.

type Flags struct {
	Migrations                         []MigrationFlag
	Sensitive, NotInPlan, CIJobsNotRun []string
	OldGuards                          []OldGuard
	Conflicts                          []string
	PrecheckUnfinished                 string
}
    Flags are what the ready card's FLAGS line names: the migrations
    the branch adds (with their flags), the sensitive files it changes,
    the files it changes that the plan did not name, the old guards it touches,
    the CI jobs whose commands did not run locally ("<workflow>: <job>"), the
    paths merging origin/<base> into it would conflict in, and what the precheck
    that passed at the head did not finish (its cap's note, from precheck.json;
    "" for nothing).

func (f Flags) Lines() []string
    Lines are the flags as the card's FLAGS line says them, one each; none when
    nothing needs a second look.

type FocusPayload struct {
	Focused bool
	PID     int
	At      time.Time
}
    FocusPayload is a ReqFocus: the factory screen of process PID gained
    (Focused) or lost its terminal's focus at At. It carries no words and is no
    input of yours.

func ReadScreenFocus(l paths.Layout) (FocusPayload, error)
    ReadScreenFocus is the screen's latest focus as the daemon keeps it
    (Layout.FactoryFocus); none yet is the zero FocusPayload, which is not Live.

func (f FocusPayload) Live() bool
    Live reports whether f is the focus of a screen that still runs: it is
    focused, and its process lives as a magnum process (a pid reused by another
    program does not count). A screen that ended while focused holds nothing.

type GitHub interface {
	CreatePR(ctx context.Context, repo, base, branch, title, bodyFile string) (PRView, error)
	PRByBranch(ctx context.Context, repo, branch string) (PRView, bool, error)
	ViewPR(ctx context.Context, repo string, number int) (PRView, error)
	ActiveLogin(ctx context.Context, repo string) (string, error)
	MergeMethods(ctx context.Context, repo string) (MergeMethods, error)
}
    GitHub opens a task's PR (ready for review, never a draft) and reads it
    back, by its branch or its number; ActiveLogin is the login gh acts as for
    repo now (the account active in your gh config dir), and MergeMethods the
    ways repo's settings let a PR merge, which the prompts of the roles that ask
    you questions name.

func NewGitHub(cfg *config.Config, run execx.Runner) GitHub
    NewGitHub is the factory's GitHub over run: gh as your gh identity for each
    repository, the one its local review runs as.

type Hold struct {
	Kind, Reason string
	Repo         string `json:",omitempty"`
	Since, Next  time.Time
	Tries        int
}
    Hold is a stop of the machine's: its kind (HoldInfra, HoldHerdr, HoldDisk,
    HoldMemory), its reason without the kind ("SSH key refused"), the repository
    it holds ("" for all: only an infrastructure hold of a repository whose
    every copy broke the same way has one, copyHolds), since when it holds,
    when it tries again (an infrastructure hold's next try, a herdr hold's next
    reveal) and how many tries ran.

func ReadHolds(l paths.Layout) ([]Hold, error)
    ReadHolds are the holds of the machine in force as the factory daemon last
    saved them (holds.json in layout l); none before its first tick.

type Jira interface {
	Ticket(ctx context.Context, key string) (jira.Ticket, error)
	Search(ctx context.Context, words string, limit int) ([]jira.Ticket, error)
	StatusSince(ctx context.Context, key string, prior jira.IssueStatus) (jira.IssueStatus, error)
	Transitions(ctx context.Context, key string) ([]jira.Transition, error)
}
    Jira reads a task's ticket, searches issues by the words of a free prompt,
    reads where a task's issue stands after the read before (tracking.go)
    and the moves its workflow offers it, which a plan of a move reads
    (jira_plans.go). It only reads: the factory writes nothing to Jira.

type LetGoPayload struct {
	TaskID        int64
	Role, Surface string
}
    LetGoPayload is a ReqLetGo: you looked at the pane of task TaskID's Role,
    whose last prompt may or may not have arrived, and let the prompt go.

type Link struct {
	URL, Repo string
	Number    int64
}
    Link is a GitHub link of a start: its URL as given, the repository
    (owner/name) and the PR's or the run's number.

type LocalReviewer interface {
	Round(ctx context.Context, c evalrun.LocalCase) (evalrun.LocalResult, error)
}
    LocalReviewer runs one round of magnum's review on a task's change in its
    copy, as a blind dry run (evalrun.LocalCase).

func NewLocalReviewer(d evalrun.Deps) LocalReviewer
    NewLocalReviewer is the local reviewer that runs each round with
    evalrun.RunLocal over d.

type Magnum interface {
	Busy(ctx context.Context) (busy bool, why string, err error)
	PRStates(ctx context.Context, refs []PRRef) (map[PRRef]PRState, error)
	OwnPRs(ctx context.Context) ([]PRState, error)
	FixRecords(ctx context.Context, refs []PRRef) (map[PRRef]FixRecord, error)
	FirstPostedRound(ctx context.Context, ref PRRef, since time.Time) (PostedRound, bool, error)
}
    Magnum is the review daemon as the factory sees it: busy while its real
    rounds in flight and due fill its limit (max_concurrent_reviews), so a
    local round takes a free round or waits; and what its registry says of the
    factory's PRs (PRStates: the row, the verdict, the loop), which the screen
    draws and the tick follows, of their fix loops over time (FixRecords),
    which the PRs' status files count, of your own open PRs (OwnPRs), which the
    screen lists, and of its first round on a PR that posted a review since a
    time (FirstPostedRound), which the escape check of a published task's local
    review reads (escapes.go).

func NewMagnum(l paths.Layout, cfg *config.Config) Magnum
    NewMagnum is magnum's review daemon of layout l, configured by cfg, as the
    factory's local review sees it (Magnum).

type MemProc struct {
	PID, PPID int
	RSS       int64
	Name      string
	Broker    bool
	Age       time.Duration
}
    MemProc is a process as the memory hold names it: its id, its parent's, its
    resident memory in bytes, its executable's base name (never its arguments),
    whether it is a Codex app-server broker and how long it has run.

func ReadMemProcs(ctx context.Context, r execx.Runner) ([]MemProc, error)
    ReadMemProcs reads the process table through r for the memory hold: `ps
    -A -o pid=,ppid=,rss=,etime=,comm=` for the ids, the resident memory, the
    ages and the names (each through execx.Redact), then `ps -A -o pid=,args=`
    to tell the brokers, both in the C locale. The arguments stay here: only
    whether they name a broker leaves. It runs nothing else. A line it cannot
    read is skipped.

type MergeMethods struct{ Merge, Squash, Rebase bool }
    MergeMethods are the ways a repository's GitHub settings let a pull request
    merge: a merge commit, a squash, a rebase.

func (m MergeMethods) String() string
    String is the methods m allows, as a prompt names them: "squash", "merge
    commit or squash", "merge commit, squash or rebase"; "" for none.

type MigrationFlag struct {
	Path                                   string
	Ghost                                  bool
	Envs, Tables, Large                    []string
	Online, Irreversible, TwoTablesInGhost bool
	NoDatabases                            string

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    MigrationFlag is one migration the branch adds, as the lint reads it:
    its path (relative to the checkout), whether it uses the repository's gh-ost
    marker and the environments it names there, the tables it changes, those
    of them at or over large_table_rows, whether it says an online algorithm
    (ALGORITHM=INPLACE or INSTANT, LOCK=NONE, algorithm: :inplace, :instant or
    :concurrently), whether it has no way back (only an up, a down that raises,
    a change Rails cannot reverse; a gh-ost migration's down refuses by the
    marker's design and is not counted), and whether it is a gh-ost migration of
    more than one table. NoDatabases is its folder when no databases are set for
    it (migrationDatabases): the precheck does not run it, and says so.

func ScanMigrations(checkout string, added []string, repo config.FactoryRepo) ([]MigrationFlag, error)
    ScanMigrations reads each of added (paths of migrations relative to
    checkout, the task's copy at the head) and names it with its flags,
    in order. The marker comes from repo's ghost_marker (none: no migration
    is a gh-ost one), the sizes from its table_stats file in the checkout
    and its large_table_rows (none: no table is large); a table_stats file
    that is missing or not JSON is an error, since the sizes cannot be told.
    A migration that is no gh-ost one and that the precheck has no databases for
    (migrationDatabases) has its folder as NoDatabases.

func (f MigrationFlag) Problems() []string
    Problems are what the lint flags in f, in plain words; none for a migration
    it lets go.

func (f MigrationFlag) String() string
    String is f in one line: its file, its gh-ost environments, its tables,
    its problems and, when the precheck does not run it, why.

type OldGuard struct {
	Path string
	Line int
	Age  time.Duration
	Why  string
}
    OldGuard is a guard the change touches (a condition, a rescue, a validation,
    an early return): its place in the base, how long ago the line was written,
    and why it was added, as the history agent found it.

type Outage struct {
	Repo, Cause string
}
    Outage is a repository whose every copy broke with one cause (Cause,
    the copies' signature, copySignature): each copy it may have (max_copies,
    2 at least) is broken, or being repaired, with the same one. No claim gets a
    copy of it until a repair works.

type PRRef struct {
	Repo   string
	Number int
}
    PRRef names a PR as the factory knows it: its repository (owner/name) and
    number.

type PRState struct {
	Ref                                   PRRef
	ID                                    int64
	Title, URL                            string
	Found, DaemonUp, Watched, OpenWatch   bool
	GHState                               string
	MergedAt, ClosedAt                    *time.Time
	Draft                                 bool
	Head, ReviewedSHA, State, AuthorLogin string
	UpdatedAt                             time.Time
	Approved                              bool
	Open                                  engine.OpenVerdict
	HasOpen, Stale                        bool
	Fix                                   engine.FixState
	Fixing, Stalemate, FixOff             bool
	FixHeld                               string
	Attention, AttentionMsg               string
	FixReport                             string
	FixNeeds                              []string
	HeldMerge                             string

	Autofix                   string
	HeadRef, BaseRef          string
	HeadChangedAt, ActivityAt time.Time
	CreatedAt                 time.Time
	CI                        *tui.CIInfo
	Review                    *store.ReviewSummary
	Findings                  *tui.FindingsInfo
	ReviewEvent               string
	Gate                      *store.ReviewGate
	Asked                     []ReviewAsk
	LastTick                  time.Time
	OldBuild                  *engine.Build
	Replies                   []store.Reply
	OpenRestores              bool
	OpenHold                  time.Duration

	// NeverDeploys says the PR can never deploy to a staging, whoever asks
	// (engine.StagingNeverDeploys: its head lives in a fork, or its head
	// branch is master, main or staging-*): the deploy before the merge is
	// not asked of it, E would be refused.
	NeverDeploys bool

	// Files, DeployingHead and Stagings are read only for a PR of a
	// repository with staging envs, where the deploy before the merge can
	// be asked (staging.DeployBeforeMerge): Files, for every such PR
	// (fillPR), are the paths magnum's poller listed at the PR's head
	// (pr_files; nil without a list of that head, or when it cannot be
	// read); DeployingHead says a staging deploy of the PR's head is live,
	// queued or running (the review daemon's staging.deploy.* records, as
	// the board reads them, while its daemon runs; one that stopped for you,
	// ended or is of an older head is not): the deploy before the merge is
	// on its way, and E is refused until the push lands. It is read only
	// for the screen (ScreenData asks, deployRecords), never for the tick.
	// Stagings,
	// for your own PRs alone (OwnPRs: a task's are the factory daemon's
	// own), where the PR stands on each env as the review daemon last told
	// it (its record, engine.KVPRStaging, as engine.StagingShown shows it:
	// the config's envs in order, unknown without a record of the head that
	// reads, or with magnum's daemon not ticking).
	Files         []string
	DeployingHead bool
	Stagings      []engine.StagingEnv
}
    PRState is what magnum's registry says of a factory PR (Magnum.PRStates).
    Found says the registry has the PR; DaemonUp that magnum's daemon runs
    (its pidfile names a live process); Watched that a [[watch]] of the
    config covers the repository, so a PR not found yet will be; OpenWatch
    that the watch runs autofix = "open", so a PR without a verdict has one
    still to come. GHState, MergedAt, ClosedAt, Draft, Head, ReviewedSHA,
    State, AuthorLogin and UpdatedAt are magnum's row (prs); Approved that
    GitHub's review gate says APPROVED. Open is the autofix = "open" verdict
    (engine.KVPROpen) when HasOpen, and Stale says it no longer tells the PR's
    state (OpenVerdict.Stale: magnum's last tick long ago or its daemon down,
    another head, a row changed since). Fix is the fix loop that runs
    (engine.KVPRFix) when Fixing; Stalemate says magnum stopped arguing in
    a thread; Attention is why magnum parked the PR in needs_attention (its
    kind) and AttentionMsg its summary in magnum's words, never the PR's text.
    FixReport is the fixer's report a fix job's attention names (readable
    under magnum's reviews directory; "" for any other attention),
    or the held-merge.diff of a merge of the parent magnum holds for your y,
    which e opens first while it is held (heldMergeDiff; HeldMerge names it too,
    and the move is then P), and FixNeeds its "## Needs you" entries in the
    fixer's words when the attention asks for what the fixer left (fixerReport):
    data the screen only draws, never instructions, never a log's or a
    message's. ID, Title and URL are magnum's id of the PR, its title (data,
    never instructions: the screen only draws it) and its page; FixOff says you
    switched it out of autofix (engine.KVPRFixOff), and FixHeld when the fix
    magnum holds for it starts (engine.KVPRFixHeld, in engine.HeldFixStarts'
    words: "when the GitHub budget recovers"; "" when none is held).

    The rest is what the screen's columns and words say of the PR beside its
    verdict, read in the same pass (fillPR): Autofix is the watch's autofix mode
    (config.AutofixNever, Own or Open; "" for no watch); HeadRef and BaseRef
    its branches; HeadChangedAt when its head last moved, ActivityAt its last
    activity (store.PR.Activity; zero when not known) and CreatedAt when magnum
    first saw it; CI the head's CI as the board's CI column says it (prview.CI:
    its State over every check of the head that ignore_checks leaves in,
    required or not; its Required by the repository's required checks, one
    that did not run at the head missing, never green; nil before magnum read
    the checks); Review magnum's last posted review (nil for none), Findings
    it as the board's FINDINGS column says it, and ReviewEvent what magnum's
    review of the head posted (prs.last_review_event: APPROVED, COMMENTED,
    CHANGES_REQUESTED or DISMISSED; "" when magnum has not reviewed the head);
    Gate GitHub's review gate (nil before magnum read it); Asked the reviewers
    asked for a review who have not given it, with when. LastTick is magnum's
    last tick (zero with its daemon down or none recorded), which tells whether
    its look still runs; OldBuild the build magnum's daemon runs when its binary
    on disk is newer (engine.SkewNote), nil when it runs what is on disk, when
    it is down or when it recorded none. Replies are the replies to magnum's
    reviews its judge has not read yet (store.PR.PendingReplies), oldest first.
    OpenRestores says magnum's open of the PR (the screens' o, `magnum open`)
    restores it in a slot, which claims the slot and holds the PR for OpenHold
    ([daemon] open_hold), as the board tells it (engine.OpenWouldRestore over
    the PR's sessions); false when it focuses a live pane.

type PRView struct {
	Number                     int
	URL, Author, Base, HeadSHA string
	Draft                      bool
}
    PRView is a pull request as the factory reads it back after it opened it.

type PostedFinding struct {
	ID                 int64
	Path               string
	StartLine, EndLine int
	Priority, Title    string
}
    PostedFinding is one finding a posted round posted: magnum's id of it
    (findings.id), its path and its lines (magnum keeps one line, so StartLine
    and EndLine are both it; 0 for a finding in the review's body), its priority
    as the judge wrote it, and its title. The title is the judge's words about
    the PR, data only: the escape check keeps nothing of it but the factory's
    hash (titleHash), and nothing writes it to the factory's registry, a log,
    an event or a message.

type PostedRound struct {
	RunID    string
	Round    int
	Head     string
	ReviewID int64
	Start    time.Time
	Posted   time.Time
	Findings []PostedFinding
	Counts   [4]int
	Counted  bool
}
    PostedRound is magnum's round on a PR that posted a review
    (Magnum.FirstPostedRound): the run of its judge that posted it (RunID,
    magnum's runs.id), the round's number, the head it reviewed,
    the review's id on GitHub, when the round began (its first run),
    when magnum recorded the post (Posted: the posting run's verification,
    else its end; zero when the run has neither), and the findings it posted,
    in the judge's order. Counts are the new findings the round's result counts,
    P0 to P3 (store.ReviewSummary.Counts), when Counted: a result without
    provenance counts findings magnum recorded no row of.

type PrecheckResult struct {
	Passed     bool
	Checks     []registry.Check
	Migrations []MigrationFlag
	Why        string
	ForYou     bool
	Unfinished string
	Command    string
}
    PrecheckResult is a precheck's end: whether it passed, the checks it
    recorded (the factory's), the migrations the branch adds with their flags,
    and why it did not pass (its first failure, in plain words, such as
    "precheck: lint: 1 offense on the changed lines (bin/lint)"). ForYou says
    the writer cannot fix why: a command the deny list refuses or that does not
    start, a lint whose output names no offense by path:line, a table_stats
    it cannot read (the configuration's or the machine's, named by its key);
    such a failure is the one Why says. Unfinished is what its cap kept it from,
    the specs or jest ("the specs did not finish within 30m, and the jest
    tests did not run"; "" when it ran to its end): no failure of its own,
    so a precheck its cap stopped there passes unless something failed before
    (precheck.json keeps it, and the ready card and the PR body name it).
    Command is the command of the failure Why says, as it ran (its files in it),
    when that failure is the writer's to fix: its fix turn asks for a run of it
    until it passes; "" for none.

type PreviewPayload struct {
	Text, Repo string
}
    PreviewPayload is a ReqPreview: the new-task screen's text and the
    repository you picked ("" = the one the text tells, as a start's), whose
    preview the daemon answers as the JSON of a tui.NewTaskForm.

type PromptData struct {
	TaskID                                                 int64
	Key, Kind, Repo, Branch, Base, Copy, TaskDir           string
	Ticket, Guidance, Prompt, Answers, Rules               string
	Findings, Report, Questions, Acceptance, Proof, Review string
	ReviewReply, FactoryProof, ReviewSummary, Precheck     string
	PRBody, PRTemplate                                     string
	SendBack, SendBackReason, MergeBase                    string
	Conflicts                                              []string
	HeadMoved, HeadWas                                     string
	RedRun                                                 bool
	ErrorSkill, PRBodySkill, DBLockCommand                 string
	Port                                                   int
	// Magnum is the factory daemon's own build (Layout.Binary, as
	// DBLockCommand names it), shell-quoted: the liaison runs its
	// `magnum factory` commands with it, so they reach the daemon's build,
	// never whatever magnum the PATH finds first.
	Magnum string
	// Tracker names the tracker of Key when it is not Jira's ("linear.app"):
	// the prompts call the key the issue of that tracker, never a Jira
	// issue. Empty for a Jira key, and for a task of a free prompt.
	Tracker string
	// MergeMethods are the ways Repo's GitHub settings let a pull request
	// merge ("squash", "merge commit, squash or rebase": MergeMethods.String),
	// which the prompts of the roles that ask the operator questions name;
	// "" while no read of them went through.
	MergeMethods string
	// SatOut are, in a stage that ends on the judge's report, the findings
	// files of the second readers that sat out the newest attempt of a
	// findings stage after Codex's usage limit, left as they stood, perhaps
	// unfinished (satOutFindings), as paths joined with " and "; "" for none.
	SatOut string
	// Checks are the repository's precheck lint lines and its jest line, as
	// configured ({files} and {base} in them): the writer's prompts name them
	// for the writer to run before its turn ends; none without them.
	Checks []string
	// Changed names, in the judge's amend turn (AmendPrompt), the questions
	// coding went on the recommended answer of and you answered otherwise
	// ("question 1 of revision 2 (asked by fx-critic)", by their place in
	// answers.md): coding began, and the writer follows the amended report
	// next. "" in any other turn, and for an amend before coding.
	Changed string
	// LastFix is set in the local review's fix turn (factory-review-fix.md)
	// whose fix passes the stage with no review round after it: a stop at
	// the cap past [factory.local_review] cap_go_on (passAfterCap). The
	// prompt then says that no round follows, asks the writer to run the
	// specs of every file it changes and to check each fix itself, and says
	// that the PR's review checks the result after publish. false in any
	// other turn.
	LastFix bool
	// The QA walker's turn of a qa stage (factory-qa.md), each "" (0) in any
	// other: QARun is the run's folder (qa/<n>-<sha7> in TaskDir), where the
	// walker saves its pages and console logs; QAURL the copy's server
	// (config.FactoryQA.PageURL of its port, no path); QACDP the DevTools
	// endpoint of the factory's headless Chrome of the run's session
	// (http://127.0.0.1:<port>, as agent-browser's --cdp takes it), the one
	// browser
	// the walker attaches to, and QASession the walker's own session of its
	// browser tool (agent-browser's --session, one per run); QAProbe the
	// probe script the walker evaluates on each page, QAVerdict the verdict it
	// writes last and QAChanged the user-facing files the change touches (the
	// repository's qa.when), all in QARun, and QARecheck the pages of the
	// defects earlier runs handed the writer, which it walks again
	// (recheck.json in QARun, "" for none); QASignIn and QASkill the
	// repository's qa.sign_in and qa.skill ("" = none); QAMaxPages its
	// qa.max_pages and QAMaxShots the most shots of a run.
	QARun, QAURL, QACDP, QAProbe, QAVerdict, QAChanged string
	QASignIn, QASkill, QASession, QARecheck            string
	QAMaxPages, QAMaxShots                             int
}
    PromptData is what a factory prompt (factory-*.md, with the blocks of
    factory-shared.md) renders with: paths, keys and commands, never the
    ticket's text, which reaches the agents only as the task's files (spec 12).
    Key is the Jira key ("" for a task of a free prompt), Kind and Repo
    the task's, Branch its local branch, Base the repository's base branch
    (the branch starts at origin/<Base>), Copy the checkout of its copy
    and TaskDir its directory. Ticket (ticket.md), Guidance (guidance.md),
    Prompt (prompt.md, the operator's request), Answers (answers.md) and Rules
    (rules.md, the learned rules) are paths in TaskDir, each "" while its file
    is not there. Findings is the role's findings-<role>.md in a findings
    stage, else the pattern of every investigator's file (findings-*.md);
    Questions the file the role writes its questions to (questions.json in the
    judge's report stage, questions-<role>.json for any other role); Report,
    Acceptance and Proof the judge's report.md and acceptance.json and the
    writer's proof.json; Review the local review's findings for the writer
    (review-<n>.json, the newest round's) and ReviewReply the writer's reply
    to them (review-reply-<n>.json), or in QA's fix turn (QAFixPrompt) the
    newest run's defects (qa/<k>-<sha7>/defects-<k>.json) and the reply to them
    (reply-<k>.json beside it), both "" outside a fix turn. FactoryProof is the
    factory's proof (factory-proof.json), ReviewSummary the local review's end
    (review-summary.json), Precheck the end of the precheck (precheck.json:
    unfinished names what its cap kept it from), PRBody the PR body the pr_body
    stage writes (pr-body.md) and PRTemplate the repository's PR template in
    the copy ("" when it has none). A coding turn back from the ready card
    carries what it is back for (rework.json): SendBack your note's file and
    SendBackReason the key of your reason (a send back), MergeBase the base
    to merge (origin/<base>) and Conflicts the paths merging it conflicts
    in (a conflict at the card), or HeadMoved the commit the branch moved to
    after the checks passed at HeadWas (a commit the factory did not make);
    each "" (nil) in any other turn. RedRun is the kind's proof: its specs must
    fail on the base (config.FactoryKind.RedRun; a kind whose proof is "green"
    keeps them green). ErrorSkill is the repository's error_skill ("" = none:
    no prompt names one) and PRBodySkill its pr_body_skill ("" = none: the PR
    body prompt writes the factory's own outline), DBLockCommand the `magnum
    db-lock` line of the copy for the role as it runs, and Port the copy's
    server's (0 when its env names none).

type Proof struct {
	Specs   []string `json:"specs"`
	Base    ProofRun `json:"base"`
	Head    ProofRun `json:"head"`
	HeadSHA string   `json:"head_sha"`
	BaseSHA string   `json:"base_sha"`
	Passed  bool     `json:"passed"`
	Why     string   `json:"why,omitempty"`
	ForYou  bool     `json:"for_you,omitempty"`
}
    Proof is the factory's proof of a head: the spec files it ran, its run
    on the base (none for a kind whose proof is green) and at the head,
    the head and the base (the merge base with origin/<base>) it ran on,
    whether it passed, and why not; ForYou when the writer cannot fix why (the
    configuration's or the machine's: the task needs you, naming the key).

func (p Proof) Holds(head string) bool
    Holds reports whether p passed at head: another head voids it.

type ProofFile struct {
	Specs []string `json:"specs"`
}
    ProofFile is proof.json as the writer writes it: the spec files of its
    proof, relative to the checkout (never their results, which the factory
    finds itself).

type ProofRun struct {
	Command string        `json:"command,omitempty"`
	Exit    int           `json:"exit"`
	Output  string        `json:"output,omitempty"`
	Tree    string        `json:"tree,omitempty"`
	Took    time.Duration `json:"took,omitempty"`
	Hung    bool          `json:"hung,omitempty"`

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    ProofRun is one spec run of a proof: the command, its exit, the end of its
    output (its secrets masked: outputOf), the tree of the commit it ran on (the
    base's, with the head's spec files on it, for the base run), how long it
    took, and whether it hung (the factory stopped it at its bound: exit -1).

type QABlocked struct {
	What        string `json:"what"`
	Why         string `json:"why"`
	Check       string `json:"check"`
	Fingerprint string `json:"fingerprint,omitempty"`
	Accepted    bool   `json:"accepted,omitempty"`
}
    QABlocked is a state or page the walker could not reach, why, and the
    acceptance check it was for. Fingerprint and Accepted are the factory's own,
    never the walker's: Fingerprint that of the defect an earlier run handed
    the writer whose page the run did not walk again (qaCheckFixes), "" for any
    other; Accepted true in the result that passed the stage when you accepted
    the state as one QA could not check (`magnum factory retry --accept-qa`),
    which the card and the PR body flag as accepted by you.

type QADefect struct {
	ID          string   `json:"id"`
	Class       string   `json:"class"`
	Severity    string   `json:"severity"`
	Page        string   `json:"page"`
	Title       string   `json:"title"`
	Quote       string   `json:"quote"`
	Source      string   `json:"source"`
	Paths       []string `json:"paths"`
	PreExisting bool     `json:"pre_existing"`
	Fingerprint string   `json:"fingerprint"`
	FoundPath   string   `json:"found_path,omitempty"`
	FoundState  string   `json:"found_state,omitempty"`
}
    QADefect is one defect: its id, class, severity (P1 to P3) and page id,
    a title, the quote as the page shows it, the code paths suspected, who found
    it (Source: walker or factory), whether the walker thinks it was there
    before the change (read, never trusted in slice 1), and the fingerprint
    the factory follows it by (qaFingerprint). FoundPath and FoundState are the
    factory's own, never a verdict's (walkerDefect clears them): for a defect
    you accepted that the run did not see (Page empty), the path and state of
    the page an earlier run found it on.

type QAFixed struct {
	Run         int    `json:"run"`
	Class       string `json:"class"`
	Severity    string `json:"severity"`
	Path        string `json:"path"`
	State       string `json:"state,omitempty"`
	Fingerprint string `json:"fingerprint,omitempty"`
}
    QAFixed is a defect an earlier QA run of the task handed the writer that
    the run walked again, its page in its state, and no longer finds: the run
    that found it, its class and severity, and the path and state of its page;
    in Unchecked, one whose fix the run did not walk again, with its fingerprint
    (no later run takes the pass as a check of it).

type QANotShown struct {
	Check string `json:"check"`
	Why   string `json:"why"`
}
    QANotShown is an acceptance check no page shows (a background job,
    an email), and why.

type QAPage struct {
	ID      string   `json:"id"`
	Path    string   `json:"path"`
	State   string   `json:"state"`
	Side    string   `json:"side"`
	Shot    string   `json:"shot"`
	Probe   string   `json:"probe"`
	Console string   `json:"console"`
	Status  int      `json:"status"`
	Checks  []string `json:"checks"`
	// ProbePath is the path the page's probe read (qaProbePath), which the
	// factory keeps in a run's result (QAResult.Walk) and matches a fixed
	// defect's page by; a verdict's is never read.
	ProbePath string `json:"probe_path,omitempty"`
}
    QAPage is one page the walker captured: its id (P1), the path it loaded,
    the state it reached, its side (after), its shot, probe and console files
    relative to the run's folder, its HTTP status as the walker saw it, and the
    acceptance checks it shows.

type QAProbe struct {
	Nonce     string `json:"nonce"`
	URL       string `json:"url"`
	Title     string `json:"title"`
	Text      string `json:"text"`
	HTML      string `json:"html"`
	Status    int    `json:"status"`
	OverflowX bool   `json:"overflow_x"`
	Truncated bool   `json:"truncated"`
	Error     string `json:"error"`
}
    QAProbe is what the factory's probe (qa_probe.js) returned in one page:
    the run's nonce, the page's URL, title, visible text and HTML, its HTTP
    status (0 when unknown), whether it scrolls sideways, whether the text or
    the HTML was cut at its cap, and the error that broke the probe in the page
    ("" when none did).

type QAResult struct {
	Version   int         `json:"version"`
	Run       int         `json:"run"`
	Pages     int         `json:"pages"`
	Shots     int         `json:"shots"`
	Dir       string      `json:"dir"`
	Head      string      `json:"head"`
	Outcome   string      `json:"outcome"`
	Why       string      `json:"why"`
	Cut       string      `json:"cut,omitempty"`
	Walked    bool        `json:"walked,omitempty"`
	Blocking  []QADefect  `json:"blocking"`
	Known     []QADefect  `json:"known"`
	Accepted  []QADefect  `json:"accepted,omitempty"`
	Blocked   []QABlocked `json:"blocked"`
	Walk      []QAPage    `json:"walk,omitempty"`
	Fixed     []QAFixed   `json:"fixed,omitempty"`
	Unchecked []QAFixed   `json:"unchecked,omitempty"`
	Started   time.Time   `json:"started"`
	Ended     time.Time   `json:"ended"`
}
    QAResult is how a QA run ended (result.json in its folder; qa-summary.json
    in the task's directory is the one that passed the stage): its version, the
    run's number, folder and head, the pages it walked and the shots it took,
    its outcome (QAOutcome*) and why, what cut an interrupted run (qaCutDrain,
    qaCutTask, qaCutCrash), whether the walker's verdict decided it (Walked:
    the factory's checks of the pages it saved), the defects that block and
    those that do not (Known), the defects that would block but you accepted at
    the run's head (Accepted, `magnum factory retry --accept-qa`), the states
    the walker could not reach, the pages it walked (Walk: each one's id, path,
    state and shot, as its verdict has them, the words clipped, and the path
    each one's probe read), what an earlier run handed the writer that this run
    walked again and found no more (Fixed), what it handed that this run did not
    walk again and you let go unchecked at the head (Unchecked, `magnum factory
    retry --accept-qa`), and when it started and ended.

func (r QAResult) CardLine() string
    CardLine is the ready card's QA line of r, the QA run that passed the stage
    (qaCardLine), as `magnum factory decide` prints it: "" for none.

type QAVerdict struct {
	Version  int          `json:"version"`
	Head     string       `json:"head"`
	Base     string       `json:"base"`
	URL      string       `json:"url"`
	Walker   string       `json:"walker"`
	Pages    []QAPage     `json:"pages"`
	Defects  []QADefect   `json:"defects"`
	Blocked  []QABlocked  `json:"blocked"`
	NotShown []QANotShown `json:"not_shown"`
}
    QAVerdict is verdict.json, the walker's verdict on one QA run: its version
    (QAVerdictVersion), the copy's head it walked, the pages it captured, its
    defects, the states it could not reach (Blocked) and the acceptance checks
    no page shows (NotShown). Base, URL and Walker are the factory's to fill.

type QuestionFile struct {
	Text        string            `json:"text"`
	Context     string            `json:"context"`
	Example     string            `json:"example"`
	Options     []registry.Option `json:"options"`
	Recommended *int              `json:"recommended"`
	Why         string            `json:"why"`
	RaisedBy    string            `json:"raised_by"`
	Evidence    string            `json:"evidence"`
}
    QuestionFile is one question of a questions file (questions.json, or a
    role's questions-<role>.json), as an agent writes it: the question, the line
    that says why it is asked, a concrete example, two or more options (a label
    and what it means for the example), the index of the recommended one (nil:
    no recommendation) and why, the role that raised it and what it rests on.
    The gate turns each into a registry.Question.

type RatePayload struct {
	TaskID     int64
	Value      int
	Reason     string
	DiffOpened bool
	Surface    string
}
    RatePayload is a ReqRate: task TaskID is rated Value, 1 for + and -1 for −,
    with the key of a reason (one of RatingReasons; "" for none). DiffOpened
    says the screen showed you the task's diff before (the d key, or the ready
    card's diff in this run of the screen); the daemon adds the diff your newest
    push on the task's ready card recorded as opened. Surface is where you
    asked, for the record of your input.

type ReadyCardFile struct {
	Revision   int           `json:"revision"`
	Drawn      time.Time     `json:"drawn"`
	Head       string        `json:"head"`
	Base       string        `json:"base"`
	Commits    int           `json:"commits"`
	ReportHash string        `json:"report_hash"`
	DiffHash   string        `json:"diff_hash"`
	Branch     string        `json:"branch"`
	Remote     string        `json:"remote"`
	Title      string        `json:"title"`
	Copy       string        `json:"copy"`
	CopyPath   string        `json:"copy_path"`
	Flags      []string      `json:"flags"`
	Review     ReviewSummary `json:"review"`
	Files      []CardFile    `json:"files"`
	QA         *QAResult     `json:"qa,omitempty"`
}
    ReadyCardFile is ready-card.json, the ready card as the factory drew it:
    its revision (a new one each time what it shows changed) and when it was
    drawn, the head and the base of the change (the PR's diff is base...head),
    the branch's commits after origin/<base> (0 in a card an older build drew;
    the PR's status file counts them), the hash of report.md and pr-body.md as
    shown and the hash of the diff (the patch id of base...head), the branch,
    the PR's title, the copy a push frees (its directory's name) and its path,
    the FLAGS lines (Flags.Lines, then a line for each state QA did not reach),
    the local review's end and the changed files, the flagged ones first
    (cardFilesOf), and the QA run that passed at the head (qa-summary.json,
    its quotes left out), nil for none.

func ReadReadyCard(l paths.Layout, id int64) (ReadyCardFile, error)
    ReadReadyCard reads the ready card of task id in layout l.

type Reservation struct {
	TaskID int64
	Copy   string
}
    Reservation is a copy a task's owner row holds, from its claim (one that got
    the copy, waits or failed) until its release.

type RetryPayload struct {
	TaskID  int64
	Surface string
	// AcceptQA is your acceptance of what QA's newest run left you at the
	// task's head (`magnum factory retry --accept-qa`): the defects that
	// block which the writer declined, its fixes or declines the run did not
	// walk again, or the states a walk that reached its pages could not
	// reach. The next QA run there lets the defects pass, the task goes on
	// at once with the states flagged, and the PR body names each as
	// accepted by you.
	AcceptQA bool
}
    RetryPayload is a ReqRetry: task TaskID, which waits on you, goes on at its
    stage. Surface is where you asked, for the record of your input.

type ReviewAsk struct {
	Who string
	At  time.Time
}
    ReviewAsk is a review asked of Who ("rev-ann", "team:<slug>") that is still
    asked, since At (the newest request of the PR's timeline; zero when the
    timeline does not name it).

type ReviewFile struct {
	Round          int          `json:"round"`
	Head           string       `json:"head"`
	AttemptsBefore int          `json:"attempts_before"`
	Findings       []ReviewItem `json:"findings"`
}
    ReviewFile is review-<n>.json, what a blocking round hands the writer:
    the cycle's number, the head it reviewed, how many attempts the review stage
    had when it was written (the fix turn is the first attempt after them) and
    the findings to fix, the questions among them.

type ReviewItem struct {
	ID          string `json:"id"`
	Fingerprint string `json:"fingerprint"`
	Severity    string `json:"severity,omitempty"`
	Title       string `json:"title"`
	Path        string `json:"path,omitempty"`
	Line        int    `json:"line,omitempty"`
	Body        string `json:"body,omitempty"`
	Question    bool   `json:"question,omitempty"`
	Risk        string `json:"risk,omitempty"`
	// Simplification is not in the summaries written before it was kept: it
	// reads false on every leftover of one.
	Simplification bool `json:"simplification,omitempty"`
}
    ReviewItem is one finding of the local review as the factory hands it on:
    its id in the round's file (F1, F2, ...), its fingerprint, severity, title,
    path, line and body, whether the judge marked it a product question,
    whether it is a simplification (a suggestion, never a defect: the ready
    card's key that sends the known defects to the writer leaves it out) and,
    for one the writer declined, the risk it named.

type ReviewReply struct {
	Replies []struct {
		ID     string `json:"id"`
		Action string `json:"action"`
		Risk   string `json:"risk"`
	} `json:"replies"`
}
    ReviewReply is review-reply-<n>.json, the writer's: per finding, fixed,
    or declined with the risk of its suggested change.

type ReviewSummary struct {
	Exit      string       `json:"exit"`
	Rounds    int          `json:"rounds"`
	Head      string       `json:"head"`
	Leftovers []ReviewItem `json:"leftovers"`
	Declined  []ReviewItem `json:"declined"`
	Doubts    []ReviewItem `json:"doubts"`
	Missing   []string     `json:"missing,omitempty"`
	// SecondJudge and SecondRound are the judge and the round of the loop's
	// second opinion (review-second.json), "" and 0 for a loop without one.
	SecondJudge string `json:"second_judge,omitempty"`
	SecondRound int    `json:"second_round,omitempty"`
	// FixedAfter are the findings of the last round, at the cap, that the
	// writer fixed after it with no round reviewing the fix (exit
	// cap_fixed): the ready card and the PR body name them.
	FixedAfter []ReviewItem `json:"fixed_after,omitempty"`
}
    ReviewSummary is review-summary.json: how the local review ended (exit clean
    or oscillation, or cap_fixed for a loop that passed at its cap after the
    writer's fix: passAfterCap), after how many rounds, at which head (the one
    its last round reviewed; for cap_fixed, the head of that fix, which no round
    reviewed), and what it left that does not block, for the ready card and the
    PR body's "Known": the leftovers of its last round (P3s, simplifications,
    product questions you answered, and on a clean exit the findings at a
    blocking priority that the round's counts and verdict left out), the
    findings the writer declined with their risks (whichever round raised them),
    the doubts (findings that came back twice after their fix, each told there
    only) and the reviewers a round of the loop went without (Missing).

type Runtime interface {
	Owner(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task) (store.PR, error)
	Launch(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task, a registry.Attempt, c Copy, roles []config.Role) error
	Send(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task, a registry.Attempt, role config.Role, text string) (runID string, err error)
	Observe(ctx context.Context) ([]runtime.Event, error)
	Verify(ctx context.Context, runID string, ok bool, why string) error
	Void(ctx context.Context, runID, why string) error
	Park(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task) error
	Reconcile(ctx context.Context, e registry.LedgerEntry) (string, error)
	Watchdog(ctx context.Context, now time.Time) ([]runtime.Event, error)
	RecoverLost(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task, a registry.Attempt, role config.Role) error
	LetGo(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task, role string) (int, error)
	Shift(gap time.Duration)
	BeginDrain()
	RunsAs(t registry.Task, role config.Role) (config.Role, error)
	Paused(kind string) *runtime.WaitError
	QuitCodex(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task) error
	QuitRole(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task, role, why string) error
	RunState(ctx context.Context, runID string) (state, why string, err error)
	AtWork(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task) (role string, you bool, err error)
	TouchedSince(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task, since time.Time) (who string, err error)
	Recover(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task) (changed []string, err error)
	SettleWorkspaces(ctx context.Context) ([]runtime.Orphan, error)
	Proving(entry int64) bool
	PaneFocus() runtime.PaneFocus
	Workspaces(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task) ([]string, error)
	Talk(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task, prompt string) (pane string, err error)
	UseHookSocket(path string)
	Wake(ctx context.Context, ev agenthooks.Event)
	WaitWakes()
	Ended() <-chan struct{}
	ObserveSoon() <-chan struct{}
}
    Runtime is the factory's agent runtime (internal/factory/runtime): the owner
    row of a task in the factory's agents store, the launch of a stage's roles
    (recorded before any workspace exists), the prompts it sends through its
    ledger, the panes it observes and the watchdog over them, the verification
    of a run's end (or its setting aside, a turn that asked questions: Void),
    parking a task's sessions, the reconcile of a prompt of unknown delivery,
    the recovery of a lost pane or of a role a recovery left without a turn
    (RecoverLost, which a rebuilt stage calls), the shift of every turn deadline
    after the Mac slept, the role that runs for a role (its Claude fallback on a
    task Codex never works on), an agent kind's pause in force (Paused: Codex's
    usage limit yields its roles), the quit of such a task's Codex sessions,
    the quit of one role's sessions (a QA walker whose run was cut, QuitRole),
    a run's state as the agents store keeps it across a restart, who is at work
    in a task's copy now (a run in flight, you in a pane: the factory's own
    commands that change the copy wait for them), and who could have changed it
    since a time (the factory puts back what its checks changed only when nobody
    else could have). After a restart it binds a task's sessions to the panes
    herdr shows again (Recover) and settles the workspaces a crash left that
    no row names (SettleWorkspaces: kept for their attempt's launch to adopt,
    or closed). Proving says whether the proof that a prompt of unknown delivery
    never arrived is under way (its read after RedeliverAfter settles it).
    PaneFocus is what the observe passes saw of you in the factory's panes,
    from the snapshot they read anyway, and Workspaces the herdr workspaces of
    a task's live sessions: the alerts' toasts hold while you are in a factory
    pane, and a task's sidebar token goes on its workspaces (alerts.go).
    UseHookSocket has the panes it makes from then on name the factory's hook
    socket, Wake looks at the pane an agent's hook event names, and WaitWakes
    waits for the later looks a Wake started (hooks.go).

type ScreenOptions struct {
	Config *config.Config
	Layout paths.Layout
	// ReadyCards, when set, gets each ready card the data draws, as read
	// once for it (the pager pages the card drawn).
	ReadyCards func(id int64, c ReadyCardFile)
	// DaemonDown says no factory daemon runs (its pidfile names no live
	// process): nothing moves, so home's one blocker says so and how to
	// start it, the last daemon's holds.json is not read, and no working
	// mark turns.
	DaemonDown bool
	// Magnum reads the published tasks' PRs in magnum's registry
	// (Magnum.PRStates), once per call: a published task's row then says
	// its PR's verdict; and your own open PRs (Magnum.OwnPRs), once per
	// call, for their rows. nil keeps the words of a screen without it
	// ("magnum: review of #N"), and lists no PR of yours.
	Magnum Magnum
}
    ScreenOptions are what ScreenData reads besides the registries: the config
    (the roles' words, the kinds' stages, the repositories) and the layout (the
    tasks' directories, the holds the daemon saved).

type Staging interface {
	Refresh(ctx context.Context, repo string, open []staging.OpenPR) error
	Status(pr staging.PR, envs []staging.Env) []staging.EnvStatus
	ReadAt(repo string) time.Time
	Close()
}
    Staging is the staging status the factory reads: internal/staging's Client,
    its read side alone, and when it last read a repository (ReadAt:
    the last fetch of the repository's mirror that worked; zero before one),
    which NewStaging adds.

func NewStaging(cfg *config.Config, d staging.Deps, gitEnv func(ctx context.Context, repo string) map[string]string) Staging
    NewStaging is the factory daemon's staging client: internal/staging's on d,
    with the repositories' envs from cfg (config.Stagings), the time of each
    mirror's last fetch that worked (ReadAt; a Refresh within the minute,
    or one that took another process's read, fetches nothing), and its fetch's
    git env from gitEnv on the context of the Refresh that asks for it, which
    the daemon's stop cancels (an App's token mint ends with the drain).

    Its client is read only, by design: the fetch clock that wraps d.Git hides
    the deploy's git, so the Plan and Deploy its internal/staging Client
    carries answer staging's refusal ("this git cannot deploy") and run no git,
    whatever git d brings. The factory daemon never deploys: the factory
    screen's E deploys through magnum's daemon (its staging_deploy request),
    the one deployer, whose Step loop runs every effect.

type StartInput struct {
	Key, Guidance, Prompt string
	PR, Run               *Link
	Found                 []string
}
    StartInput is what a start's text holds (ParseStart): a Jira key with your
    guidance after it, a GitHub PR link (PR) or an Actions run link (Run),
    with the words after the link as Guidance, or else the whole text as a
    prompt. Found are the keys such a prompt names elsewhere than at its start:
    the distinct keys of its words and of its Jira links, in their order,
    which Jira still has to know to count.

func ParseStart(text string, trackers string) StartInput
    ParseStart reads a start's text. trackers are the Jira sites and the
    tracker templates (config.ParseTracker) that tell a Jira link, separated by
    white space: a site's URL ("https://example.atlassian.net") or a template
    ("https://example.atlassian.net/browse/PR-{num}"). The text is trimmed;
    its first word is:
