```text
      - a Jira key in upper case ("PR-12345"), or a Jira link: /browse/<KEY>
        on the host of one of trackers (on any host when trackers is empty),
        or a template's link; the words after it are the guidance (a colon or a
        dash between the two is dropped);
      - a GitHub PR link (PR) or an Actions run link (Run), the words after it
        the guidance;
      - anything else: the whole text is the prompt, and Found are the keys it
        names elsewhere (foundKeys). ParseStart reads no Jira: a word of the
        shape of a key ("UTF-8") is found, and the start asks Jira which of them
        count.

type StartPayload struct {
	Text, Kind, Repo string
	Surface          string `json:",omitempty"`
	WordsOnly        bool   `json:",omitempty"`

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    StartPayload is a ReqStart (and the start of the new-task screen):
    your text, the kind of task you chose ("" = the daemon picks it,
    PickKind), the repository ("" = the one the text tells: a GitHub link
    of a [[factory.repo]], a key of the tracker of one, or the only one),
    and where you asked (Surface, for the record of your input; "" = the CLI).
    WordsOnly starts a task from your words only: the whole text is the prompt,
    a key at its start (one Jira does not know) is words, and no key of it is
    read from Jira as the task's ticket or as a key found in the text.

type StopPayload struct {
	TaskID  int64
	Surface string
}
    StopPayload is a ReqStop: stop task TaskID for good. Surface is where you
    asked (the screen, the CLI), for the record of your input.

type TalkPayload struct {
	TaskID  int64
	Surface string
}
    TalkPayload is a ReqTalk: you want to talk with the liaison of task TaskID.
    Surface is where you asked, for the record.

type WorkItem struct {
	Kind  string    `json:"kind"`
	Task  int64     `json:"task"`
	What  string    `json:"what"`
	Since time.Time `json:"since"`
}
    WorkItem is one piece of work a restart would cut: its kind (Work*),
    its task, what it is in words ("local review round 2 of PR-12345") and since
    when it runs.

type WorkRecord struct {
	PID   int        `json:"pid"`
	Drain string     `json:"drain,omitempty"`
	Work  []WorkItem `json:"work"`
}
    WorkRecord is work.json (paths.Layout.FactoryWork): the pid of the daemon
    that wrote it, the drain it holds (drain.json's value it took; "" for none)
    and the work it runs that a restart would cut, oldest first.

func ReadWork(l paths.Layout) (WorkRecord, bool, error)
    ReadWork reads the record the factory daemon of layout l keeps; ok is false
    when there is none (no daemon of this build runs, or it stopped).

```

## registry

```text
package registry // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/factory/registry"

Package registry is the factory's own SQLite registry: tasks, the stage attempts
that run them, questions and the operator's decisions, the prompt ledger,
external effects, the event log and the CLI's requests. It also keeps the
evidence records of the factory's design (section 11.1) from the first task on,
because evidence that was not written at the time cannot be read later: the
spans of a task's states, the facts of each role of an attempt, the operator's
inputs, ratings, the rounds and findings of the local review, artifacts,
the PR link, checks and suspensions.

It is a file of its own with its own migration list (migrations/NNNN_*.sql,
tracked by PRAGMA user_version and applied by the store package's runner),
so a factory migration never touches magnum's review registry. It follows that
registry's conventions: WAL with busy_timeout 5 s and foreign keys on, one
connection per process, BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions, timestamps as fixed-width
RFC3339 UTC text, and compare-and-set state changes that return ErrConflict or
ErrNotFound.

Callers scrub text before they put it into an event or an error column
(scrub.Text: secrets, emails and hosts) or into a request's result, the answer
you read (scrub.Secrets: its hosts stay): the registry stores what it is given.

CONSTANTS

const (
	EffectBegin = "begin"
	EffectOK    = "ok"
	EffectFail  = "fail"
)
    Effect states: begin while the effect may be half done, then ok or fail.

const (
	EscapeNoLocal  = "no_local"
	EscapeFar      = "far"
	EscapeUnplaced = "unplaced"
)
    Why no local finding caught a posted one (Escape.Reason): none on its path
    at a comparable head, the nearest one more than 3 lines away, or the posted
    finding has no path or no line to place.

const (
	PhaseBegin = "begin"
	PhaseOK    = "ok"
	PhaseFail  = "fail"
	PhaseInfo  = "info"
)
    Event phases: begin, ok and fail bracket a destructive step; info is
    everything else.

const (
	InputTaskText   = "task_text"
	InputGuidance   = "guidance"
	InputAnswer     = "answer"
	InputDecision   = "decision"
	InputSendBack   = "send_back"
	InputRating     = "rating"
	InputStop       = "stop"
	InputDrop       = "drop"
	InputRetry      = "retry"
	InputPaneTyped  = "pane_typed"
	InputSayOneLine = "say_one_line"
)
    Input kinds: what the operator did. The text of an input is whatever words
    came with it; a stop, a drop or a retry has none.

const (
	OriginHerdr   = "herdr"
	OriginUnknown = "unknown"
)
    The origins of a turn typed into a pane (InputPaneTyped): the proof that the
    operator, and nobody else, typed it. OriginHerdr: herdr showed the operator
    in the turn's own pane (its agent at work on no prompt of the factory's)
    within two minutes of the turn. OriginUnknown: nothing proves who typed it;
    such a turn, like one of any origin but OriginHerdr, is kept for evaluation
    only, never counted as a typed message and never a lesson's source.

const (
	ClassStepStart  = "step_start"
	ClassApproval   = "approval"
	ClassCorrection = "correction"
	ClassAccess     = "access"
	ClassInfo       = "info"
)
    Input classes, set later by a classifier: what an input was for.

const (
	EffectJiraPlan    = "jira_plan"
	EffectJiraSeen    = "jira_seen"
	EffectJiraComment = "jira_comment"
)
    The factory's Jira plans (the factory's jira_plans.go) are effects,
    no table of their own: a plan is the effect of its task and milestone
    (JiraPlanKey, jira-plan:<task>:<milestone>, kind EffectJiraPlan), begun when
    the milestone comes and settled ok (a move planned, or nothing to move)
    or fail (one the factory could not plan) with its JiraPlanResult as JSON;
    what the factory saw after it is the effect beside it (JiraSeenKey,
    jira-seen:<task>:<milestone>, kind EffectJiraSeen, begun and settled at
    once with its JiraSeenResult); the comment it would keep on the issue is
    an effect per milestone (JiraCommentKey, jira-comment:<task>:<milestone>,
    kind EffectJiraComment). In shadow mode none of them wrote anything to Jira.
    The key jira:<task>:<milestone> is none of theirs: it stays free for the
    real move of a later phase.

const (
	PlanPlanned       = "planned"
	PlanAlready       = "already"
	PlanAssignedOther = "assigned_other"
	PlanNoTransition  = "no_transition"
	PlanNeedsFields   = "needs_fields"
	PlanTargetDone    = "target_done"
	PlanUnread        = "unread"
)
    The outcomes of a plan (JiraPlanResult.Outcome): a move planned (from a
    status of its from list to its target, through a transition); nothing to
    move (the status is the target, or not one the move goes from); and the
    plans the factory could not make: the issue is assigned to someone else,
    no transition goes to the target, the transition wants fields, the target's
    category is done, or no read of the issue worked before the next milestone
    or the task's end.

const (
	SeenTarget    = "target"
	SeenElsewhere = "elsewhere"
	SeenNone      = "none"
)
    The moves the factory saw after a planned move (JiraSeenResult.Moved):
    the issue went to the plan's target, to another status, or did not move by
    the task's end.

const (
	DeliveredUnknown   = "unknown"
	DeliveredYes       = "yes"
	DeliveredNo        = "no"
	DeliveredAbandoned = "abandoned"
)
    Delivery verdicts of a ledger entry. magnum sends a prompt before it saves
    that the prompt was sent, so a crash between the two leaves the entry
    unknown until recovery reads the agent's transcript for the prompt's hash.
    Abandoned is a prompt the factory gave up on (its run abandoned for a fresh
    session, or the operator let it go after a look at the pane): it may or may
    not have arrived, and it is never sent again.

const (
	QuestionOpen     = "open"
	QuestionAnswered = "answered"
	QuestionVoided   = "voided"
)
    Question states: open until the operator answers it or newer evidence
    replaces it (voided).

const (
	FlagNeedless = "needless"
	FlagNeeded   = "needed"
	FlagUnclear  = "unclear"
)
    Question flags, the operator's verdict on a question: it was needless,
    it was needed, or it was unclear.

const (
	RequestPending = "pending"
	RequestDone    = "done"
	RequestFailed  = "failed"
)
    Request states.

const (
	ExitClean       = "clean"
	ExitCap         = "cap"
	ExitOperator    = "operator"
	ExitOscillation = "oscillation"
	ExitUnavailable = "unavailable"
)
    Exits of a review cycle: the loop ended clean, at its cap of rounds,
    by the operator, on an oscillation, or because the review was unavailable.
    A cycle after which the loop goes on has no exit.

const (
	FindingOpen     = "open"
	FindingFixed    = "fixed"
	FindingWaived   = "waived"
	FindingRebutted = "rebutted"
)
    Finding outcomes.

const (
	CheckSpec      = "spec"
	CheckLint      = "lint"
	CheckReview    = "review"
	CheckCI        = "ci"
	CheckQA        = "qa"
	CheckMigration = "migration"

	CheckPass    = "pass"
	CheckFail    = "fail"
	CheckSkipped = "skipped"

	// SourceGitHub is a check GitHub ran (its CI on the task's PR), and
	// CauseNotOurs a failure that is not of the task's change.
	SourceGitHub = "github"
	CauseNotOurs = "not_ours"
)
    Check kinds, results, causes and sources.

const (
	TaskQueued    = "queued"
	TaskActive    = "active"
	TaskNeedsYou  = "needs_you"
	TaskWaiting   = "waiting"
	TaskPublished = "published"
	TaskDone      = "done"
	TaskStopped   = "stopped"
	TaskFailed    = "failed"
)
    Task states. A task is queued until the daemon has room for it, active while
    agents or the daemon work on it, needs_you while only the operator can move
    it, waiting while someone or something else must (a reviewer, CI, a person
    the operator asked), published while its PR is open and the work goes on,
    and done (merged), stopped or failed once it has ended. A published task
    holds its Jira key, as a failed one does.

const (
	AttemptLaunching = "launching"
	AttemptRunning   = "running"
	AttemptEnded     = "ended"
	AttemptVerified  = "verified"
	AttemptFailed    = "failed"
	AttemptAbandoned = "abandoned"
)
    Attempt states. An attempt is launching from the moment the daemon records
    the intent to start a stage's agents (before any workspace exists), running
    while they work, ended when they stopped, then verified or failed by the
    stage's end fact; abandoned is an attempt a restart found and gave up.

const ReadyWait = "ready to push"
    ReadyWait starts what a task at its ready card waits on you for ("ready to
    push (card 2): PR-12345 a title"): the stats find the card's wait by these
    words, whatever the kind names the stage that draws it.

const RoleIntake = "intake"
    RoleIntake is the Role of the input that starts a task: the words it was
    started with, whether they are recorded as its text (a prompt, a key alone)
    or as the guidance after a key. It is the mark of the start's message,
    which the statistics count as typed and never as a step start, and which
    tells it from guidance given later. The answers to the intake's own question
    carry the role too; their kind tells them apart.


VARIABLES

var ErrConflict = errors.New("factory registry: conflict")
    ErrConflict is returned (wrapped) when a compare-and-set update matched no
    row because the state moved on, or when a write hits a uniqueness rule.

var ErrNotFound = errors.New("factory registry: not found")
    ErrNotFound is returned (wrapped) when a looked-up row, or a row that
    another row refers to, does not exist.

var ErrStaleRevision = errors.New("factory registry: stale question revision")
    ErrStaleRevision is returned (wrapped) when a question revision is not the
    newest one the task has: answers to older questions are never taken.


FUNCTIONS

func AnswersMarkdown(qs []Question) string
    AnswersMarkdown is a task's answers.md, rendered from its question rows qs
    (by revision and position, as Questions returns them): each answered one,
    by revision and position, with whether the answer took the recommended
    option, another option or the operator's own words, its secrets redacted
    (execx.Redact); a question asked again (the same text, QuestionKey) shows
    only its newest answer, the one that stands; "" when none is answered. The
    factory writes it into the task's directory, and `magnum eval add` renders
    the answers a local round read with it when it rebuilds them from the rows
    as they stood when the round began.

func JiraCommentKey(id int64, milestone string) string
    JiraCommentKey is the key of task id's Jira comment at milestone.

func JiraPlanKey(id int64, milestone string) string
    JiraPlanKey is the key of task id's plan at milestone.

func JiraSeenKey(id int64, milestone string) string
    JiraSeenKey is the key of what was seen after task id's plan at milestone.

func LatestSchemaVersion() int
    LatestSchemaVersion is the highest migration version embedded in this
    binary.

func NormLabel(s string) string
    NormLabel is an option's label as answers are matched to it: trimmed,
    lowercased, without a final period.

func QuestionKey(text string) string
    QuestionKey is how a question is told from the questions the task asked, in
    the factory, its CLI and answers.md: its text, lowercased, without backticks
    and double quotes, its runs of spaces made one and its end punctuation
    trimmed (an agent's copy of a question changes those), so that a question
    two roles raise in the same words is one question, whichever role raised it.


TYPES

type AnswerEdit struct {
	Answer string
	At     time.Time
}
    AnswerEdit is one answer a question has had and when it was given.

type Artifact struct {
	TaskID int64
	Kind   string
	Path   string
	SHA256 string
	Rev    int
	At     time.Time
}
    Artifact is a file of a task's directory as the factory saw it:
    its kind (base_sha, ticket, guidance, answers, report, acceptance, proof,
    patch, pr_body or test_commands), its path relative to the task directory,
    the sha256 of its content and its revision. A file that changes gets the
    next revision, so the report that the operator approved can be told from the
    one before it.

type Attempt struct {
	ID     string // t<task>-<stage>-<n>
	TaskID int64
	Stage  string
	N      int // 1 for the first attempt of the stage, then 2, 3, ...
	State  string
	// WorkspaceLabel is the herdr workspace label that carries the attempt id.
	WorkspaceLabel string
	Error          string
	Started, Ended time.Time // Ended is the zero time until the attempt has ended
}
    Attempt is one launch of a stage of a task.

type AttemptUpdate struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    AttemptUpdate collects the column assignments of TransitionAttempt.
    Settable columns: workspace_label and error. The state moves through
    TransitionAttempt's `to`, and ended_at is stamped when the attempt first
    reaches ended, verified, failed or abandoned.

func (u *AttemptUpdate) Inc(col string, n int)
    Inc adds n to the integer column col.

func (u *AttemptUpdate) Set(col string, v any)
    Set assigns v to column col. v is nil (NULL), a string, an int, an int64,
    a bool or a time.Time (the zero time stores NULL).

type Check struct {
	ID, TaskID                  int64
	AttemptID, HeadSHA          string
	Kind, Result, Cause, Source string
	Command                     string
	Exit                        int
	Took                        time.Duration // kept to the millisecond
	At                          time.Time
}
    Check is one run of a check on a head: its kind (spec, lint, review, ci, qa
    or migration), result (pass, fail or skipped), the source that ran it (the
    writer's claim, the factory's own run, or GitHub), the command and its exit
    code and duration. Cause is set only on a failure (code, infra, flaky, env,
    access, not_ours or unknown) and may stay empty until someone classifies it.
    AttemptID is empty for a check that no attempt ran, such as GitHub's.

type Cycle struct {
	ID, TaskID            int64
	N                     int
	HeadBefore, HeadAfter string
	Delta, SkillHash      string
	Started, Ended        time.Time // Ended is the zero time while the round runs
	Tokens                int64
	Exit                  string
}
    Cycle is one round of the local magnum review of a task: the heads before
    and after it, the change between them (the sha256 of a patch artifact, say),
    the hash of the review skill, the time and the tokens it took, and the exit.
    N counts the task's rounds from 1.

type Decision struct {
	TaskID                        int64
	Kind, Choice, Note            string
	HeadSHA, ReportHash, DiffHash string
	Shown, DiffOpened, At         time.Time
	DiffDwell                     time.Duration // kept to the millisecond
	RecommendationShown           bool
	RecommendationFollowed        bool
	Patch, Proof                  string
}
    Decision is what the operator decided on a card. HeadSHA, ReportHash and
    DiffHash are what the card showed, so a later change to any of them voids
    the decision. Shown is when the card was shown, DiffOpened when the operator
    opened the diff (the zero time if they did not) and DiffDwell how long they
    read it. RecommendationShown and RecommendationFollowed say whether the card
    carried a recommendation and the choice took it. Patch and Proof are the
    sha256 of the ready patch and of the proof snapshot (artifacts).

type Effect struct {
	Key, Kind string
	TaskID    int64
	State     string
	Result    string
	// Begun is when the effect was first begun, whatever ran it again later;
	// Ended is the zero time while the effect is begun.
	Begun, Ended time.Time
	// Resumed says the effect was begun again after a crash or a failure.
	Resumed bool
}
    Effect is one external side effect (a push, a PR, a comment, a merge) under
    an idempotency key. Result is what an ok effect made: a PR url, a commit
    sha, the reason a failed one failed.

type ErrActiveKey struct {
	Key    string
	TaskID int64 // the task that holds the key
}
    ErrActiveKey is returned (as a value; use errors.As) by CreateTask when
    a task for the same Jira key is not done or stopped. It also matches
    ErrConflict.

func (e ErrActiveKey) Error() string
    Error implements error.

func (e ErrActiveKey) Unwrap() error
    Unwrap makes errors.Is(err, ErrConflict) true.

type Escape struct {
	ID, TaskID                  int64
	FindingID                   int64
	Path                        string
	StartLine, EndLine          int
	Priority, TitleHash, Reason string
	NearestID                   int64
	Distance                    int
	At                          time.Time
}
    Escape is one P0 to P2 finding of magnum's posted round that no finding of
    the task's local review caught: magnum's finding (FindingID, findings.id),
    its path and lines, its priority, the hash of its title (the factory's own,
    as Finding.TitleHash; never the title), why (Reason), and for EscapeFar only
    the nearest local finding (NearestID, review_findings.id) and how many lines
    lie between them. At is the check's time.

type EscapeCheck struct {
	TaskID                   int64
	RunID                    string
	Round                    int
	HeadSHA                  string
	Posted, Comparable       int
	SameHeadOnly, Unrecorded int
	At                       time.Time
}
    EscapeCheck is the one check of a published task's local review against
    magnum's first round on the task's PR that posted a review and began
    after the publish (migrations/0007_escapes.sql): magnum's run that posted
    the review (RunID, runs.id) and its Round, the head that round reviewed,
    how many P0 to P2 findings it posted, how many of the task's local
    findings were placed at a head comparable with it, and when the check ran.
    SameHeadOnly counts the files of the posted findings the check compared at
    the same head only, as git could not compare them at two heads (none means
    every comparison ran); Unrecorded the P0 to P2 findings the round's result
    counts that magnum recorded no row of (above zero, the escapes are unknown,
    not none).

type Event struct {
	ID     int64
	At     time.Time
	TaskID int64 // 0 for the daemon's own events
	Kind   string
	Phase  string
	Text   string
}
    Event is one row of the audit log.

type Finding struct {
	ID, TaskID            int64
	Fingerprint, Path     string
	StartLine, EndLine    int
	TitleHash             string
	Priority, Class       string
	Sources               []string
	Verdict, VerdictWhy   string
	Blocking              bool
	FirstCycle, LastCycle int
	Outcome, FixCommit    string
	Reopened              int
}
    Finding is one finding of the local review, followed across the rounds
    by its fingerprint (path, lines and a hash of the title). Sources are
    the reviewers that reported it, Verdict and VerdictWhy the judge's,
    and Blocking whether it blocks the round. FirstCycle and LastCycle are round
    numbers (Cycle.N), Reopened counts how often a fixed finding came back,
    and FixCommit is the last commit that claimed to fix it.

type Input struct {
	ID, TaskID    int64
	Kind          string
	Surface       string
	Stage, Role   string
	Text          string
	DroppedReason string
	Origin        string
	Before        string
	AgentState    string
	Class         string
	At            time.Time
}
    Input is one thing the operator said or did to a task. Surface is where it
    came from (a screen, a pane, the CLI), Stage and Role where in the task,
    Text the scrubbed words or DroppedReason why the words were not kept (never
    both), Origin the proof that the operator and no agent produced it, Before
    the agent's two turns before it (scrubbed, at most 1 KiB) and AgentState the
    agent's state when it arrived. Class stays empty until classified.

type JiraPlan struct {
	TaskID    int64
	Milestone string
	State     string
	Begun     time.Time
	Result    JiraPlanResult
	Seen      *JiraSeenResult
}
    JiraPlan is one plan of a task's Jira move at a milestone: its effect's
    state (EffectBegin while it waits for its read) and begin, its result (zero
    while begun) and what was seen after it (nil before anything was).

type JiraPlanResult struct {
	Mode        string    `json:"mode"`
	Outcome     string    `json:"outcome"`
	From        string    `json:"from,omitempty"`
	To          string    `json:"to"`
	Transition  string    `json:"transition,omitempty"`
	Transitions []string  `json:"transitions,omitempty"`
	Cause       string    `json:"cause,omitempty"`
	At          time.Time `json:"at,omitzero"`
}
    JiraPlanResult is what a settled plan holds: its mode (shadow), its outcome,
    the status it read (From) and the target (To), the transition it would take
    (planned), the transitions Jira offers (no transition), the read's failure
    in the jira package's words (unread, never ticket text), and when its read
    was. Names are Jira's: statuses and transitions, never a person.

func (p JiraPlanResult) Encode() string
    Encode is the result as its effect keeps it.

type JiraSeenResult struct {
	Moved   string    `json:"moved"`
	To      string    `json:"to,omitempty"`
	At      time.Time `json:"at,omitzero"`
	LagSecs int64     `json:"lag_secs,omitempty"`
	By      string    `json:"by,omitempty"`
}
    JiraSeenResult is what the factory saw after a planned move: where the
    issue moved (SeenTarget, SeenElsewhere, SeenNone), to which status, when
    (the changelog's time of the move when known, else the read that saw it;
    the task's end for none), how long after the plan's read, and who moved it:
    "you", "other" or "" when unknown (the changelog entry's author against your
    account, jira.IssueStatus.MovedBy), never a name or an id.

func (s JiraSeenResult) Encode() string
    Encode is the result as its effect keeps it.

func (s JiraSeenResult) Lag() time.Duration
    Lag is how long after the plan the move came.

func (s JiraSeenResult) Yours() bool
    Yours reports whether you made the move seen.

type LedgerEntry struct {
	ID        int64
	TaskID    int64
	AttemptID string
	Role      string
	RunID     string
	Hash      string
	Text      string
	Delivered string
	Sent      time.Time
}
    LedgerEntry is one prompt the factory sends (or is about to send) to an
    agent: the scrubbed text and its hash, written before the prompt leaves.

type Option struct {
	Label string `json:"label"`
	Means string `json:"means"`
}
    Option is one answer a question offers: its label, and what it means for the
    question's example.

type Options struct {
	// Clock returns the current time; nil means time.Now. Tests replace it.
	Clock func() time.Time
	// BeforeMigrate, when set, runs before pending migrations are applied,
	// with the file's schema version and the one this binary migrates to; an
	// error from it aborts Open and leaves the file untouched. The CLI sets it
	// to refuse while a factory daemon runs on the older schema, and so does
	// the daemon's builder, which writes its own pidfile only later.
	BeforeMigrate func(from, to int) error
}
    Options tune Open.

type PRLink struct {
	TaskID       int64
	Repo         string
	Number       int
	Branch       string
	OpenedHead   string
	ApprovedHead string
	Opened       time.Time
}
    PRLink ties a task to its one PR: the repository, the number, the task's
    branch, the head the PR was opened with and the head the operator approved.

type Question struct {
	ID       int64
	TaskID   int64
	Revision int
	Index    int
	Text     string
	// Context is the one line that says why it is asked, Example a concrete
	// case the options can be read against.
	Context, Example string
	Options          []Option
	// Recommended is an index into Options, or -1 for "no recommendation";
	// Why is the reason for the recommendation.
	Recommended int
	Why         string
	Answer      string
	State       string
	// RaisedBy is the role that asked the question, Evidence what it cited.
	RaisedBy, Evidence string
	// Asked is when the revision was stored, Shown when a card first showed
	// it, Answered when the first answer was (the zero time while the
	// question is open or voided).
	Asked, Shown, Answered time.Time
	// TookRecommendation says the current answer is the recommended option.
	TookRecommendation bool
	// Flag is the operator's verdict (needless, needed or unclear; empty
	// until given) and FlagWhy its reason.
	Flag, FlagWhy string
	// VoidedBy is the revision that voided the question, 0 if none did.
	VoidedBy int
}
    Question is one question of a task to the operator. A revision is the set of
    questions the agents asked at one time; Index is the position within it.

type Rating struct {
	TaskID          int64
	Value           int
	ReasonKey       string
	DiffOpenedFirst bool
	At              time.Time
}
    Rating is a + (Value 1) or − (Value -1) on a finished task, with the one key
    for the reason and whether the operator opened the diff before giving it (a
    rating given without opening the diff counts as noise).

type Registry struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Registry is the factory's registry handle. It is safe for concurrent use.

func Open(path string, opts Options) (*Registry, error)
    Open creates the parent directory (0700), opens the database at path
    with WAL, busy_timeout=5000, foreign_keys=ON, synchronous=NORMAL and
    temp_store=MEMORY, and applies pending migrations after opts.BeforeMigrate
    agrees. It refuses a database whose schema version is newer than this binary
    knows. The database, its -wal and its -shm file are made 0600 whatever the
    umask.

func OpenDB(db *sql.DB, opts Options) (*Registry, error)
    OpenDB is Open for a database the caller opened: the in-memory registries
    of tests (registrytest, sqlitetest.Open). Production opens files with Open,
    and OpenDB refuses to run outside a test binary (testing.Testing).
    It pins db to the one connection Open keeps, applies pending migrations
    after opts.BeforeMigrate agrees and refuses a schema newer than this binary,
    as Open does. It closes db when it fails.

func (r *Registry) AnswerBatch(ctx context.Context, taskID int64, rev int, answers map[int]string) error
    AnswerBatch records answers (question Index -> the answer text) to the open
    questions of revision rev, all or none, and keeps each as the first entry
    of the question's answer history. It returns ErrNotFound when the task does
    not exist, ErrStaleRevision when rev is not the task's newest revision,
    so answers to questions that newer evidence replaced are never taken, and
    ErrConflict when a batch names a question that is not open in that revision
    (ReviseAnswer edits an answered one). Questions the batch does not name stay
    open. An empty batch or a blank answer is refused.

func (r *Registry) AnswerHistory(ctx context.Context, questionID int64) ([]AnswerEdit, error)
    AnswerHistory returns every answer a question has had, the first one and
    each edit, oldest first; a question that was never answered, or does not
    exist, has none.

func (r *Registry) AppendEvent(ctx context.Context, taskID int64, kind, phase, text string) error
    AppendEvent writes an audit row at the clock's time. taskID 0 is an event of
    the daemon itself; any other must be an existing task (ErrNotFound). Kind
    is required and phase must be begin, ok, fail or info. Callers scrub text
    (scrub.Text: secrets, emails and hosts) before they put it into an event.

func (r *Registry) AppendLedger(ctx context.Context, e LedgerEntry) (LedgerEntry, error)
    AppendLedger writes e before its prompt is sent and returns the stored
    entry. TaskID, AttemptID (an existing attempt, ErrNotFound if there is
    none), Role, Hash and Text are required, and TaskID must be the task of the
    attempt (checked in the same transaction as the insert); Delivered starts
    unknown, and Sent defaults to the clock.

func (r *Registry) Artifacts(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) ([]Artifact, error)
    Artifacts returns every revision of every artifact of a task, in the order
    they were recorded.

func (r *Registry) AttemptByID(ctx context.Context, id string) (Attempt, error)
    AttemptByID looks up an attempt; a missing one is ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) Attempts(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) ([]Attempt, error)
    Attempts returns a task's attempts in the order they began.

func (r *Registry) BeginAttempt(ctx context.Context, taskID int64, stage string) (Attempt, error)
    BeginAttempt records a launching attempt for the next number of the task's
    stage and returns it. The task must exist (ErrNotFound).

func (r *Registry) BeginCycle(ctx context.Context, taskID int64, headBefore, skillHash string) (Cycle, error)
    BeginCycle starts the next round of the task's local review, numbered after
    its last one, on the head it starts from and with the review skill's hash.
    A missing task is ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) BeginEffect(ctx context.Context, key, kind string, taskID int64) (Effect, bool, error)
    BeginEffect records that the effect under key is about to run, and reports
    whether the caller should run it. The bool is false when the key already has
    an ok result (the returned Effect holds it): the effect is never repeated.
    A key that was begun and never ended (a crash) or that failed runs again,
    so the caller first looks for what the effect may already have made;
    the effect is then Resumed, keeps the time it first began, and the reason
    of a failed run goes into an info event of kind effect. A key belongs to one
    kind and one task: reusing it for another is ErrConflict.

func (r *Registry) Checks(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) ([]Check, error)
    Checks returns a task's checks in the order they were recorded.

func (r *Registry) ClassifyInput(ctx context.Context, id int64, class string) error
    ClassifyInput sets the class of input id: step_start, approval, correction,
    access or info. A classifier may set it again. A missing input is
    ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) Close() error
    Close closes the database.

func (r *Registry) CloseLoop(ctx context.Context, id int64, exit string) error
    CloseLoop ends the loop at round id after all: a round that ended with the
    loop going on (exit "") takes exit, and keeps its heads, its end and its
    tokens (the round the local review's second opinion was to follow, once that
    opinion is void). A round with exit already is fine; a running round or one
    that ended with another exit is ErrConflict, a missing one ErrNotFound,
    and exit must be one of the exits.

func (r *Registry) CompleteRequest(ctx context.Context, id int64, state, result string) error
    CompleteRequest marks a pending request done or failed with a result
    message. Completing a request twice is ErrConflict.

func (r *Registry) CreateTask(ctx context.Context, t Task) (Task, error)
    CreateTask inserts t and returns the stored row, and writes the task's
    first span in the same transaction. A task needs a Jira key or a prompt;
    an empty State is queued; Created and Updated are the clock's and the
    question revision starts at 0. It returns an ErrActiveKey naming the holder
    when a task for the same Jira key is not done or stopped.

func (r *Registry) Cycles(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) ([]Cycle, error)
    Cycles returns a task's review rounds in order.

func (r *Registry) Decisions(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) ([]Decision, error)
    Decisions returns a task's decisions in the order they were made.

func (r *Registry) EffectByKey(ctx context.Context, key string) (Effect, error)
    EffectByKey looks up an effect; a missing one is ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) EffectsOfKind(ctx context.Context, kind string) ([]Effect, error)
    EffectsOfKind returns the effects of kind, oldest first.

func (r *Registry) EndCycle(ctx context.Context, id int64, headAfter, delta, exit string, tokens int64) error
    EndCycle ends a running round with the head it left, the change between
    the heads, its exit (empty when the loop goes on) and the tokens it took.
    A round ends once (ErrConflict) and a missing one is ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) EndEffect(ctx context.Context, key, state, result string) error
    EndEffect settles a begun effect as ok or fail with its result. Ending an
    effect that is not begun is ErrConflict, and an unknown key ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) EnqueueRequest(ctx context.Context, kind string, payload any) (int64, error)
    EnqueueRequest inserts a pending request with payload marshalled as JSON
    (nil = {}) and returns its id.

func (r *Registry) EscapeCheck(ctx context.Context, id int64) (EscapeCheck, error)
    EscapeCheck is task id's escape check; ErrNotFound before it ran.

func (r *Registry) Escapes(ctx context.Context, id int64) ([]Escape, error)
    Escapes are task id's escapes in the order they were stored (magnum's
    findings' order); none before its check, or after one that found none.

func (r *Registry) Events(ctx context.Context, taskID int64, limit int) ([]Event, error)
    Events returns a task's events oldest first (taskID 0: the daemon's own);
    limit > 0 keeps only the newest limit rows.

func (r *Registry) EventsAfter(ctx context.Context, after int64, limit int, kinds ...string) ([]Event, error)
    EventsAfter returns the events of the given kinds written after event
    after (an id; 0: from the first), of every task and of the daemon itself,
    oldest first, at most limit of them (limit <= 0: all). No kind is no event.

func (r *Registry) Findings(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) ([]Finding, error)
    Findings returns a task's findings in the order they were first seen.

func (r *Registry) FlagQuestion(ctx context.Context, id int64, flag, why string) error
    FlagQuestion records the operator's verdict on question id: needless, needed
    or unclear, with the reason in words. A later flag replaces an earlier one.
    A missing question is ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) ForgetPayload(ctx context.Context, id int64) error
    ForgetPayload empties the payload of request id once it is done or failed
    (a pending one is ErrConflict: the daemon still reads it), so a request that
    carried your draft (a preview) keeps none of it.

func (r *Registry) Inputs(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) ([]Input, error)
    Inputs returns a task's inputs in the order they were recorded.

func (r *Registry) JiraPlans(ctx context.Context) ([]JiraPlan, error)
    JiraPlans are every task's Jira plans, by task id and then milestone (start
    before published), each with what was seen after it. A result that does not
    decode is left zero.

func (r *Registry) LastDone(ctx context.Context, since time.Time, kinds ...string) (Request, bool, error)
    LastDone is the newest request of kinds the daemon answered done at or after
    since (false for none): the status rule's news, read typed.

func (r *Registry) LedgerOf(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) ([]LedgerEntry, error)
    LedgerOf returns the task's entries in the order they were written:
    the prompts its agents were sent, or were about to be.

func (r *Registry) LetGone(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) ([]LedgerEntry, error)
    LetGone are task taskID's prompts that are each role's newest and abandoned
    (the operator let it go, or the factory gave up on it), oldest first:
    the screen's let-go line, read without the delivered prompts.

func (r *Registry) LinkKey(ctx context.Context, id int64, key string) error
    LinkKey gives task id the Jira key key (a task of a free prompt, once you
    named its issue) under CreateTask's rule: of the tasks that are not done
    or stopped, one key has at most one, so a key another such task holds is
    an ErrActiveKey naming it. A task that holds key already is no change, one
    that holds another key is ErrConflict, and a missing task is ErrNotFound.
    The key changes nothing else of the task (its branch stays).

func (r *Registry) LinkPR(ctx context.Context, l PRLink) error
    LinkPR records the PR of task l.TaskID. A task has one PR, and a PR one task
    at a time: linking another number or repository to a task that has a PR,
    or a PR that another task has while that task holds its work (it is not
    done or stopped, holdsWork), is ErrConflict; linking the PR it already
    has is a no-op that leaves the first record as it was. The PR of a task
    that is done or stopped may be linked to another (adoption, milestone 2),
    and the ended task's link stays as it was. Repo and Number are required,
    Opened defaults to the clock, and the task must exist (ErrNotFound).

func (r *Registry) LinkedPR(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) (PRLink, error)
    LinkedPR returns the PR of a task; a task without one is ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) MarkDelivered(ctx context.Context, id int64, delivered string) error
    MarkDelivered settles an unknown entry as yes (the agent got the prompt),
    no (it did not) or abandoned (nobody knows, and nobody sends it again).
    Settling an entry with the verdict it already has is not an error;
    a different verdict is ErrConflict, and a missing entry ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) OpenEffects(ctx context.Context) ([]Effect, error)
    OpenEffects returns the effects still begun, oldest first: the ones a
    restart must settle by running each one's guard again.

func (r *Registry) OpenSuspension(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) (Suspension, error)
    OpenSuspension returns the task's open suspension; a task that is not
    suspended is ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) PendingRequests(ctx context.Context, limit int) ([]Request, error)
    PendingRequests returns up to limit pending requests, oldest first (limit <=
    0 = all), so a consumer can skip a request it already handed to a background
    worker.

func (r *Registry) PruneRequests(ctx context.Context, before time.Time, kinds ...string) (int, error)
    PruneRequests deletes the requests of kinds the daemon answered before
    before, and the `request` events of their answers ("request <id> (<kind>):
    ..."), and returns how many requests went. A pending request stays.

func (r *Registry) Questions(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) ([]Question, error)
    Questions returns every question of a task, voided and answered ones
    included, by revision and position.

func (r *Registry) Ratings(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) ([]Rating, error)
    Ratings returns a task's ratings in the order they were given.

func (r *Registry) RecentEvents(ctx context.Context, limit int, kinds ...string) ([]Event, error)
    RecentEvents returns the newest limit events of the given kinds, of every
    task and of the daemon itself, newest first (limit <= 0: all). No kind is no
    event.

func (r *Registry) RecordArtifact(ctx context.Context, a Artifact) error
    RecordArtifact stores a as a new revision of its kind and path, unless the
    latest revision of that kind and path already has the same sha256 (a no-op:
    nothing is written and the first time stays). New content, including going
    back to earlier content, gets the next Rev, counted from 1 for each task,
    kind and path; a.Rev is ignored. The path must be relative to the task
    directory and clean, and the hash a lowercase hex sha256. At defaults to the
    clock and the task must exist (ErrNotFound).

func (r *Registry) RecordCheck(ctx context.Context, c Check) (int64, error)
    RecordCheck stores c and returns its id. Kind, Result and Source are
    required and must be listed; Cause must be empty unless the result is a
    failure. At defaults to the clock; the task (and the attempt, if given) must
    exist (ErrNotFound).

func (r *Registry) RecordDecision(ctx context.Context, d Decision) error
    RecordDecision stores d. Kind and Choice are required, At defaults to the
    clock, and the task must exist (ErrNotFound).

func (r *Registry) RecordEscapeCheck(ctx context.Context, c EscapeCheck, es []Escape) (bool, error)
    RecordEscapeCheck stores task c.TaskID's escape check and its escapes
    es (each of the task, at the check's time), in one transaction, once:
    a task checked before writes nothing more, whatever c and es hold, and false
    says so. The check needs magnum's run and the head; each escape is of a P0
    to P2 finding, a known reason, and a nearest finding and a distance for far
    only (anything else is refused, and nothing is written). At defaults to the
    clock; a task that does not exist is ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) RecordGitHubCI(ctx context.Context, taskID int64, head, result, cause string) (bool, error)
    RecordGitHubCI stores GitHub's CI on task taskID's PR at head as a check
    of kind ci from source github with result (a pass or a failure; cause,
    a failure's only, as Check.Cause), once per task, head and result:
    the same again writes nothing, and false says so (the look and the write are
    one transaction, which takes the registry's write lock first, so two writers
    cannot both write it). A head that failed and then passed after a rerun has
    both rows. A task that does not exist is ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) RecordInput(ctx context.Context, in Input) (int64, error)
    RecordInput stores in and returns its id. The kind is required and must be
    one of the input kinds; Text and DroppedReason are never both set. Before
    keeps its last 1 KiB (the turns nearest the input), cut at a rune boundary.
    Class is normally empty (ClassifyInput sets it later) but may carry a class
    the caller already knows. At defaults to the clock and the task must exist
    (ErrNotFound). The caller scrubs the text and Before (secrets, tokens,
    emails, hosts) first: the registry stores what it is given.

func (r *Registry) RecordRating(ctx context.Context, rt Rating) error
    RecordRating stores r for its task (ErrNotFound if there is none).
    Value must be 1 or -1; At defaults to the clock. A task may be rated again;
    every rating is kept.

func (r *Registry) RecordRoleRun(ctx context.Context, rr RoleRun) error
    RecordRoleRun stores rr, a row for each attempt and role: the first call
    inserts, later calls fill in what they know. A field left at its zero
    value never clears one that is set, and a value replaces an earlier one,
    so the launch and the end of a role can each record their own facts.
    The attempt must exist (ErrNotFound), the role is required, and Outcome must
    be one of the outcomes or failed:<cause>.

func (r *Registry) ReplaceQuestions(ctx context.Context, taskID int64, rev int, qs []Question) error
    ReplaceQuestions stores qs as revision rev of the task's questions and voids
    the open questions of every earlier revision (answered ones stay), recording
    rev as the voiding revision. Each question's Index is its position in qs,
    whatever it carries; its State is open; RaisedBy and Evidence are kept.
    rev must be above the task's newest revision (ErrStaleRevision), so a caller
    asks for newest+1, and it becomes the task's newest even when qs is empty:
    an empty qs voids the open questions and asks nothing. A question needs
    Text, and Recommended must be -1 or an index into its Options.

func (r *Registry) RequestByID(ctx context.Context, id int64) (Request, error)
    RequestByID looks up a request; a missing one is ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) Resume(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) error
    Resume closes the task's open suspension at the clock's time. A task
    with none open (it never suspended, or already resumed) is ErrNotFound,
    so a suspension resumes once.

func (r *Registry) ReviseAnswer(ctx context.Context, taskID int64, rev, idx int, answer string) error
    ReviseAnswer replaces the answer of an answered question of the task's
    newest revision and keeps the old one in the answer history. The same words
    again are not an edit. It returns ErrNotFound when the task does not exist,
    ErrStaleRevision when rev is not its newest revision and ErrConflict when
    the question is not answered (AnswerBatch answers an open one). The question
    keeps the time of its first answer.

func (r *Registry) RoleRuns(ctx context.Context, attemptID string) ([]RoleRun, error)
    RoleRuns returns the roles of an attempt in the order they were first
    recorded.

func (r *Registry) SchemaVersion(ctx context.Context) (int, error)
    SchemaVersion returns PRAGMA user_version.

func (r *Registry) SeeFinding(ctx context.Context, cycleID int64, f Finding) (Finding, error)
    SeeFinding records that round cycleID saw f, and returns the finding as the
    registry now holds it. The finding of a task is told by its fingerprint:
    a new one is stored open with that round as its first and last; one seen
    before moves LastCycle to this round, takes the newest sighting's location,
    priority, class, verdict and blocking flag (a value left empty keeps the
    old one) and the union of the sources, and, if it was fixed and this round
    is after its last, comes back open with Reopened + 1. Waived and rebutted
    findings stay so. f.TaskID may be left 0; f.Outcome, FirstCycle, LastCycle
    and Reopened are the registry's. A missing round is ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) SetTracking(ctx context.Context, t Tracking) error
    SetTracking writes task t.TaskID's tracking row whole, replacing the one it
    had. A row needs its try's time; a missing task is ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) SettleFinding(ctx context.Context, id int64, outcome, fixCommit string) error
    SettleFinding sets the outcome of finding id: fixed, waived, rebutted or
    open. A non-empty fixCommit is kept as the commit that claimed the fix.
    A missing finding is ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) ShowQuestions(ctx context.Context, taskID int64, rev int) error
    ShowQuestions records that a card showed the questions of revision rev of
    the task. A question keeps the first time it was shown, whatever later shows
    say. A revision that has no questions (or a task that does not exist) is
    ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) ShowQuestionsAt(ctx context.Context, taskID int64, rev int, at time.Time) error
    ShowQuestionsAt is ShowQuestions for a batch that was shown at the time at,
    which the registry could not see (the liaison notes it before it asks);
    the zero time is the registry's own moment.

func (r *Registry) Spans(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) ([]Span, error)
    Spans returns a task's spans oldest first; a task with none, or no task,
    has an empty list.

func (r *Registry) Suspend(ctx context.Context, s Suspension) error
    Suspend opens a suspension of s.TaskID, stamped with the clock. The task
    must exist (ErrNotFound) and have no open suspension (ErrConflict); a stage
    is required, and an empty AttemptID means no attempt.

func (r *Registry) TaskByID(ctx context.Context, id int64) (Task, error)
    TaskByID looks up a task; a missing one is ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) TaskByKey(ctx context.Context, key string) (Task, error)
    TaskByKey returns the task that holds a Jira key: the one that is not done
    or stopped (a published or failed task holds it). No such task, and the
    empty key, are ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) TaskByRequest(ctx context.Context, id int64) (Task, error)
    TaskByRequest returns the task start request id made (Task.RequestID); none,
    and an id under 1, are ErrNotFound.

func (r *Registry) TaskEvents(ctx context.Context, taskID int64, kind string, limit int) ([]Event, error)
    TaskEvents returns task taskID's events of kind, oldest first; limit >
    0 keeps only the newest limit of them. A read that a screen repeats,
    or a check of a task's own stage events, stays bounded by its kind and limit
    however long the task's log grows.

func (r *Registry) Tasks(ctx context.Context) ([]Task, error)
    Tasks returns every task, oldest first.

func (r *Registry) Tracking(ctx context.Context, id int64) (Tracking, error)
    Tracking is task id's tracking row; ErrNotFound before its first try.

func (r *Registry) Trackings(ctx context.Context) (map[int64]Tracking, error)
    Trackings are every task's tracking row, by task id.

func (r *Registry) TransitionAttempt(ctx context.Context, id string, from []string, to string, set func(*AttemptUpdate)) error
    TransitionAttempt is TransitionTask for attempts.

func (r *Registry) TransitionTask(ctx context.Context, id int64, from []string, to string, set func(*TaskUpdate)) error
    TransitionTask moves task id to state `to` only if its current state is
    one of from (nil from = any state; empty to = keep the state), applying
    set's assignments and the new updated_at in the same UPDATE. It returns
    ErrConflict when the state did not match (or when the move would give a Jira
    key a second unfinished task) and ErrNotFound when the task does not exist.

    A move that changes the state, the stage, who the task waits on or for what,
    or that has a reason (TaskUpdate.Because), also writes a span in the same
    transaction; a refused move and an update of bookkeeping columns (the head,
    the copy) write none.

func (r *Registry) Undelivered(ctx context.Context) ([]LedgerEntry, error)
    Undelivered returns the entries whose delivery is still unknown, oldest
    first: the prompts recovery has to settle after a restart.

func (r *Registry) UnlinkKey(ctx context.Context, id int64, key string) error
    UnlinkKey takes key back from task id (Jira refused a key LinkKey gave it),
    compare-and-set: a task that holds another key, or none, is no change.
    The key is then free for another task. A missing task is ErrNotFound.

type Request struct {
	ID      int64
	Kind    string
	Payload json.RawMessage
	State   string
	Result  string
	Created time.Time
	Handled time.Time // the zero time while the request is pending
}
    Request is a CLI to daemon work item.

type RoleRun struct {
	AttemptID, Role string
	CLI, Model      string
	CLIVersion      string
	MagnumBuild     string
	PromptHash      string
	SkillHash       string
	ConfigHash      string
	Rules           []RuleRef
	SessionID       string
	Transcript      string
	Launched        time.Time
	FirstOutput     time.Time
	Ended           time.Time
	Verified        time.Time
	EndFact, EndWhy string
	Nudges          int
	Outcome         string
	Tokens          map[string]int64
	ActiveSecs      int
	IdleSecs        int
}
    RoleRun holds the facts of one role of one stage attempt (an attempt runs
    several roles): what ran it (CLI, model, versions, the hashes of the prompt,
    the skill and the config, the rules the prompts carried), where (session
    and transcript), when (launch, first output, end, verification), how it
    ended (the end fact and why, the nudges, the tokens by model, the active and
    idle seconds) and the outcome: verified, failed:<cause>, voided, stopped,
    lost or paused. A field that is not known is its zero value.

type RuleRef struct {
	ID      string `json:"id"`
	Version int    `json:"version"`
}
    RuleRef names a rule that went into a role's prompts, by id and version.

type Span struct {
	ID, TaskID int64
	From, To   string
	Stage      string
	// WaitsWho and WaitsWhat are the task's after the move; OnYou is true when
	// WaitsWho is "you".
	WaitsWho, WaitsWhat string
	OnYou               bool
	Reason              string
	At                  time.Time
}
    Span is one move of a task between states: where it came from and where it
    went, the stage, who it then waited on and for what, whether that is the
    operator, and why. CreateTask writes the first span (From is empty) and
    TransitionTask one for each move.

type Suspension struct {
	TaskID    int64
	Stage     string
	AttemptID string
	Role      string
	Open      []string
	Suspended time.Time
	Resumed   time.Time
}
    Suspension records a task held while it waits for the operator, for the
    stage's attempt and role that were running and the things that were open
    (question ids, say) when it stopped. At most one suspension of a task is
    open (Resumed is the zero time); Resume closes it.

type Task struct {
	ID int64
	// JiraKey is the ticket, "" for a task that started from a free prompt. Of
	// the tasks that are not done or stopped, one key has at most one.
	JiraKey string
	// Prompt is the operator's free text; Guidance the words after a Jira key.
	Prompt, Guidance string
	// Kind is a configured kind of task (bug, feature, chore, ...), Repo the
	// configured repository's name.
	Kind, Repo string
	Title      string
	State      string
	// Stage is the configured stage the task is in, Branch the local branch,
	// Copy the repository copy it holds and HeadSHA the branch's head.
	Stage, Branch, Copy, HeadSHA string
	// WaitsWho and WaitsWhat say who the task waits on and for what, in the
	// words the screen shows.
	WaitsWho, WaitsWhat string
	// Attempt counts the attempts of the current stage; PRNumber is the PR's
	// number, 0 before it exists.
	Attempt, PRNumber int
	// QuestionRev is the newest question revision of the task, 0 before it
	// has asked anything; ReplaceQuestions keeps it, so a revision that asks
	// nothing still counts.
	QuestionRev int
	// CodexNever says Codex never works on this task again (a cybersecurity
	// warning marked it).
	CodexNever bool
	// RemoteBranch is the branch the task's PR is pushed to, "" until its
	// ready card names it: Branch's own name, or <login>-<KEY>-<slug> for a
	// task whose key was linked after its branch was made (Branch keeps its
	// name).
	RemoteBranch string
	// RequestID is the start request that made the task (requests.id), 0
	// for one no request made: a replay of that request finds the task
	// (TaskByRequest) and makes no second one.
	RequestID        int64
	Created, Updated time.Time
}
    Task is one piece of work: a Jira key or a free prompt, taken to a PR.

type TaskUpdate struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    TaskUpdate collects the column assignments of TransitionTask. Settable
    columns: kind, repo, title, guidance, stage, branch, copy, head_sha,
    waits_who, waits_what, attempt, pr_number, codex_never and remote_branch.
    The state moves through TransitionTask's `to`, the question revision through
    ReplaceQuestions, and updated_at is the registry's.

func (u *TaskUpdate) Because(reason string)
    Because sets the reason of the span that the move writes (Span.Reason).

func (u *TaskUpdate) Inc(col string, n int)
    Inc adds n to the integer column col.

func (u *TaskUpdate) Quiet()
    Quiet marks an update of the wait's words alone (a number in them moved:
    a percentage, the gigabytes free): it writes no span while the state,
    the stage and who the task waits on stay as they were.

func (u *TaskUpdate) Set(col string, v any)
    Set assigns v to column col. v is nil (NULL), a string, an int, an int64,
    a bool or a time.Time (the zero time stores NULL).

type Tracking struct {
	TaskID  int64
	JiraKey string
	// Status is the status's name, StatusID its id, Category Jira's
	// category of it (new, indeterminate, done; "" unknown), Since when the
	// issue moved into it (zero: unknown) and Searched whether the changelog
	// was searched for that (jira.IssueStatus's).
	Status, StatusID, Category string
	Since                      time.Time
	Searched                   bool
	// Assigned says the issue has an assignee, AssigneeYou that it is you.
	Assigned, AssigneeYou bool
	// MovedBy is who moved the issue into Status: "you", "other", or ""
	// when unknown (jira.IssueStatus's); never a name or an id.
	MovedBy string
	// ReadAt is the read the facts are from, zero before one worked;
	// TriedAt the last try, never zero; LastError that try's failure, ""
	// after a read that worked: a class of failure, never ticket text.
	ReadAt, TriedAt time.Time
	LastError       string
}
    Tracking is where a task's Jira issue stands as the factory daemon last
    read it (migrations/0006_tracking.sql, and 0008 for who moved it): the
    facts of the last read that worked, of the key JiraKey, and the last try,
    which a failure moves with its cause while the facts stay.

```

## registrytest

```text
package registrytest // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/factory/registry/registrytest"

Package registrytest gives tests a factory registry without migrating one for
each of them: the first call in a test binary migrates a template database
in memory, and every call starts from a copy of its bytes. Open and OpenWith
keep that copy in memory, so the test writes no database file; Seed, OpenFile
and OpenPair write it to a file, which registry.Open then finds current.
Only _test.go files import it.

FUNCTIONS

func Open(tb testing.TB) *registry.Registry
    Open gives the test a migrated registry in memory, private to it; the
    registry is closed when the test ends.

func OpenFile(tb testing.TB, path string, opts registry.Options) *registry.Registry
    OpenFile seeds path (see Seed) and opens it with registry.Open; the registry
    is closed when the test ends. It is for a test whose code under test opens
    the registry by path, such as the CLI's commands.

func OpenPair(tb testing.TB) (first, second *registry.Registry)
    OpenPair opens two registries on one database file, the way the daemon and
    the CLI each hold one in production; both are closed when the test ends.

func OpenWith(tb testing.TB, opts registry.Options) *registry.Registry
    OpenWith is Open with options, for a test that moves the registry's clock.

func Seed(tb testing.TB, path string)
    Seed writes a migrated database to path, creating its directory (0700),
    for code under test that opens the registry itself. A file already at path
    is left as it is.

```

## runtime

```text
package runtime // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/factory/runtime"

Package runtime is the factory's agent runtime: the owner rows of its tasks in
the factory's own agents store, the launches it records before any workspace
exists, the prompt ledger that never sends a prompt of unknown delivery twice,
the pauses that are not failures, and a watchdog with its recovery steps
(docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-factory-design.md, sections 4.3, 10 and
10.1).

The factory engine (package factory) drives it through its Runtime interface;
this file holds the events that interface reports, which the engine declares
before the runtime itself exists.

CONSTANTS

const (
	// Stagger is how far apart launches start while the Mac's memory
	// pressure is at warn.
	Stagger = 20 * time.Second
	// RedeliverAfter is the least time between the two reads of a
	// transcript that prove a prompt never arrived (Reconcile).
	RedeliverAfter = 2 * time.Minute
	// UnknownAfter is how long a prompt's delivery may stay unknown before
	// the operator is asked to look at the pane (EventDeliveryUnknown).
	UnknownAfter = 15 * time.Minute
	// NoProgressAfter is how long a run's transcript and screen stay the
	// same before the watchdog takes its next step, and how long a
	// recovery waits for progress before the next one.
	NoProgressAfter = 10 * time.Minute
	// MaxResumes is how often a lost pane's conversation is resumed in one
	// attempt before a fresh session starts from the files.
	MaxResumes = 2
	// MaxStagePrompts is how many prompts a role gets in one stage before a
	// loop without progress is assumed; MaxContext the share of its context
	// (percent) past which it is; SameFailures how often the same failing
	// output in a row says so.
	MaxStagePrompts = 6
	MaxContext      = 85
	SameFailures    = 3
)
    The runtime's timing and budgets (spec sections 5 and 10.1).

const LetGoWhy = "its prompt was let go"
    LetGoWhy is why a run that held only prompts you let go (LetGo) was
    abandoned: its turn was never watched (RunState says it).

const LiaisonRole = "fx-liaison"
    LiaisonRole is the factory role of a task's liaison, the agent that talks
    with you about the task (Talk); no stage names it.

const PausedPrefix = "paused: "
    PausedPrefix leads the error of a run its CLI's pause ended (a usage limit,
    a login, an overload): the run is abandoned with "paused: " and the pause's
    wait ("usage: claude limit until 16:00"), which RunState returns, so a stage
    rebuilt after a restart knows the role is to go on once the pause is over.

const RecoveryPrefix = "recovery: "
    RecoveryPrefix leads the error of a run a recovery gave up: the watchdog
    quit its session (or found it gone) to resume the role or start it afresh.
    While such a run is the role's last whose prompt may have arrived, no turn
    took its place (a step failed after the quit, or the new turn's prompt
    is proven never to have arrived), so the role is due a recovery: a stage
    rebuilt after a restart, or on EventUndelivered, calls Runtime.RecoverLost
    for it.

const SurfaceLiaison = "liaison"
    SurfaceLiaison is the Surface of an EventTyped of the turns typed into a
    task's liaison's pane (Runtime.Talk), and the surface the liaison records
    your answers and decisions with.

const Tag = "factory"
    Tag marks the factory's agents (agents.Deps.Tag): it leads their titles and
    pane labels and joins their herdr names' hash, so they never collide with a
    review's.


VARIABLES

var ErrDeliveryUnknown = errors.New("the last prompt's delivery is unknown")
    ErrDeliveryUnknown is Send's answer while one of the role's prompts has a
    delivery nobody can prove either way (Reconcile): a prompt is never sent
    twice.

var ErrDraining = errors.New("factory runtime: the daemon drains: no new launch")
    ErrDraining is a launch the daemon's drain stopped while it waited for the
    stagger (BeginDrain): no agent started.

var ErrNoProgress = errors.New("the agent makes no progress")
    ErrNoProgress is Send's answer once a loop without progress outlived
    its compaction and its fresh session: the task needs the operator
    (EventNoProgress).

var ErrOperatorInPane = errors.New("you're in that pane")
    ErrOperatorInPane is Send's answer while the operator types in the role's
    pane (agents.ErrHumanActive): the prompt waits; nothing was sent.


FUNCTIONS

func DeniedLine(volume, app string) string
    DeniedLine is what a task waits on you for once macOS still blocks the
    factory's herdr server from reading volume after its one heal: whom to
    allow (herdr, magnum and app, the [terminal] app the engine's reveal starts
    the server from, when it is one) and where, as macOS names the setting:
    Removable Volumes under Files & Folders for a mounted volume, Full Disk
    Access where that toggle is absent; then your retry.

func IsUnknownReason(what string) bool
    IsUnknownReason reports whether a task's wait is UnknownReason's, as this
    build or an older one (whose wait named no command) wrote it.

func LiaisonSession(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, id int64) (store.Session, error)
    LiaisonSession is the live session of task id's liaison in st, the agent you
    step into after a talk: store.ErrNotFound before the task's first talk and
    once its liaison is parked.

func LiaisonTask(nodeID string) (int64, bool)
    LiaisonTask is the task a liaison row's node id names, false for a row that
    is no liaison's.

func OwnerTask(nodeID string) (int64, bool)
    OwnerTask is the task an owner row's node id names (Owner), false for a row
    that is no task's.

func PromptHash(text string) string
    PromptHash is the ledger's hash of a prompt: the sha256 of its text with the
    line ends made \n and the surrounding space trimmed, as a transcript records
    it.

func Scrub(text string) (clean string, kept bool)
    Scrub cleans text before the factory keeps it: scrub.Text (execx.Redact:
    GitHub tokens, JWTs, Authorization values, private keys; then AWS keys and
    other token shapes, the values of password=, token: and the like, also under
    a quoted key ("password": "x") (the key stays), emails and host names).
    clean is the scrubbed text; kept is false for a long pasted block (more
    than 40 lines or 4000 bytes), which a capture of what the operator typed
    drops (the ledger keeps the factory's own prompts, scrubbed, whatever their
    length).

func TaskSessions(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, id int64) ([]store.Session, error)
    TaskSessions are the sessions of task id in the factory's agents store st,
    oldest first: every generation of every role the runtime launched for it.
    A task never launched has none.

func TaskSlot(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, id int64) (store.Slot, error)
    TaskSlot is the slot of the copy task id's owner row holds in the factory's
    agents store st: the copy its claim reserved, before the task notes it
    (store.ErrNotFound for none, and for a task never launched or claimed).

func TurnText(text string) string
    TurnText is the prompt of the turn a ledger entry's text (scrubbed) starts:
    what the caller meant to say, which the prompt of a fresh session
    (freshText) carries after the attempt's first prompt, else text itself.
    The factory tells its fix turns by it.

func UnknownReason(task int64, roles ...string) string
    UnknownReason is the wait of task whose prompts to roles may or may not have
    arrived (EventDeliveryUnknown): it names every one, and the command that
    lets one go once you looked at its pane (`magnum factory let-go`).

func WorkspaceLabel(t registry.Task, a registry.Attempt) string
    WorkspaceLabel is the herdr workspace label of a task's attempt, unique per
    task and attempt: "factory <key> <attempt id>". A restart finds a workspace
    no row names by it.


TYPES

type Copy struct {
	Name, Path   string
	Number, Port int
	Env          map[string]string
}
    Copy is a task's copy of a repository as the factory's copies claimed it
    for the task (factory.Copies): its name (factory2) and checkout, its number
    (copy {n}), the port of its local server (0 when the copy's env names none)
    and its environment, the repository's env rendered for the copy (its name,
    its number, its Redis offset). Its panes run in Path with Env.

type DeniedError struct{ Volume, App, Held string }
    DeniedError is Send's answer while macOS blocks the factory's herdr server
    from reading Volume after the heal, or while the factory may not heal it
    (its herdr session is yours, its herdr has no server.stop), or once Held
    (what lives in its session) held the stop for holdLimit: the task needs
    you until your retry, with DeniedLine (App is the [terminal] app), or with
    heldLine once something held it.

func (e *DeniedError) Error() string
    Error is the line the task waits on you for: heldLine when Held is set,
    else DeniedLine.

type Deps struct {
	Config   *config.Config
	Layout   paths.Layout
	Herdr    agents.Herdr
	Store    *store.Store
	Registry *registry.Registry
	Runner   execx.Runner
	Memory   func(ctx context.Context) engine.MemorySample
	MayStart func() (who, what string, ok bool)
	Clock    func() time.Time
	Log      *slog.Logger
}
    Deps are the runtime's collaborators. Config, Herdr, Store,
    Registry and Runner are required. Store is the factory's agents store
    (Layout.FactoryAgentsDB). Memory nil reads no memory (taken as normal);
    MayStart is the engine's holds of a launch (a disk or memory hold,
    a drain for an install: who and what, as a task's wait says them), which a
    start outside a launch passes too (mayStart), called on the engine's loop;
    nil holds nothing. Clock nil is time.Now; Log nil discards.

type Event struct {
	TaskID  int64
	Role    string
	RunID   string
	Kind    EventKind
	Reason  string
	Turns   []Turn
	Surface string
}
    Event is one thing the runtime saw on a run of a task's role. Turns are
    an EventTyped's, and Surface where they were typed: SurfaceLiaison for the
    task's liaison's pane, "" for a pane of the task's roles.

type EventKind string
    EventKind is what happened to a run of a factory agent.

const (
	// EventEnded: the run ended (its pane went idle); the stage checks its
	// end fact.
	EventEnded EventKind = "ended"
	// EventBlocked: the pane shows a dialog the factory does not answer.
	EventBlocked EventKind = "blocked"
	// EventPaused: a usage limit, a login or an overload screen; Reason says
	// which and until when, when known. A pause is not a failure.
	EventPaused EventKind = "paused"
	// EventLost: the pane is gone and its recoveries ran out.
	EventLost EventKind = "lost"
	// EventStuck: the watchdog's steps ran out on a hung turn; Reason holds
	// the pane's last line.
	EventStuck EventKind = "stuck"
	// EventNoProgress: a loop without progress outlived its compaction and
	// its fresh session.
	EventNoProgress EventKind = "no_progress"
	// EventRefused: a Codex cybersecurity warning; the task never runs on
	// Codex again.
	EventRefused EventKind = "refused"
	// EventHooksTrust: a Codex session shows the hooks-trust dialog.
	EventHooksTrust EventKind = "hooks_trust"
	// EventDeliveryUnknown: a prompt to the role may or may not have
	// arrived, and no transcript can tell (Runtime.Reconcile): the role gets
	// no prompt until the operator looked at its pane and let it go
	// (Runtime.LetGo).
	EventDeliveryUnknown EventKind = "delivery_unknown"
	// EventUndelivered: a prompt of unknown delivery is proven never to
	// have arrived (Runtime.Reconcile's no): its entry is settled no and its
	// run abandoned, and the stage sends the role what it is due once more.
	EventUndelivered EventKind = "undelivered"
	// EventDelivered: a prompt of unknown delivery is found in its
	// transcript by a later read (Runtime.Reconcile's yes): its entry is
	// settled yes and its run watched as submitted; nothing is sent again,
	// and a wait on you for it is settled.
	EventDelivered EventKind = "delivered"
	// EventTyped: a read of the role's transcript found turns the factory
	// did not send (Turns): typed into its pane by the operator, or by
	// somebody nothing proves. Each read hands every such turn the
	// transcript holds, recorded or not; the engine records each once. It is
	// a record, nothing a stage waits for.
	EventTyped EventKind = "typed"
	// EventVolumeDenied: macOS still blocks the factory's herdr server from
	// reading the volume of the task's copy after the one heal, or the
	// factory may not heal it (volume.go): Reason is the line the task
	// waits on you for (DeniedLine), until your retry.
	EventVolumeDenied EventKind = "volume_denied"
	// EventHerdrStopped: a heal stopped the factory's herdr server (Reason
	// names the volume it could not read): the engine opens the session
	// again at once, whenever it opened it last, so the fresh server the
	// task's roles are relaunched in comes up. It is no task's to wait for.
	EventHerdrStopped EventKind = "herdr_stopped"
)
    The kinds of Event.

type Orphan struct {
	Workspace, Label, Attempt string
	TaskID                    int64
	Adopted                   bool
	Why                       string
}
    Orphan is a workspace of the factory's herdr session that no session row
    names: its id and label, the attempt the label names (its last word;
    "" for a liaison's workspace, liaisonLabel) and that attempt's task,
    or the task the liaison's label names by its key (0 when the registry has no
    such attempt or task), whether it is kept for the attempt's next launch to
    adopt (Adopted) or was closed, and why.

type PaneFocus struct {
	// Pane is herdr's focused pane when it is in a task's workspace (its
	// label is the factory's, WorkspaceLabel), "" when the focus is
	// elsewhere or herdr did not answer the last pass.
	Pane string
	// Since is when herdr last showed you at work in a factory pane
	// (agents.ObsHumanActive: an agent at work on no prompt of the
	// factory's, the human_active_at of its owner row), zero when no pass
	// of this process did; Left is when a pass first saw the focus off the
	// factory's panes after it was on one (zero when none did).
	Since, Left time.Time
}
    PaneFocus is what the observe passes saw of herdr's focus in the factory's
    session, and of you in its panes. herdr's focus alone proves nothing of you:
    it rests where it was when nobody is attached, at a daemon start too,
    and herdr moves it by itself when a workspace opens or closes; herdr showing
    you at work in a factory pane does.

type Runtime struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Runtime is the factory's agent runtime (package doc). It is safe for
    concurrent use; the engine calls it from its loop.

func New(d Deps) (*Runtime, error)
    New builds the runtime over d.

func (r *Runtime) AtWork(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task) (role string, you bool, err error)
    AtWork names who is at work in task t's copy, "" for nobody: the role whose
    run is in flight (pending, submitted or working: its agent may be changing
    the copy), or, you true, the role whose pane you are in (you typed into
    one of the task's panes within the human cooldown, or herdr shows its pane
    focused; a herdr that cannot say counts as in it), where your edits are. The
    factory's own commands that change the task's copy (its proof's base run,
    its restore) wait for both. A task that never launched has nobody at work.

func (r *Runtime) BeginDrain()
    BeginDrain stops the launches that wait for the stagger, and any that would:
    the daemon drains on SIGTERM, and launchd kills it ExitTimeOut after, so a
    tick must not sleep Stagger per role meanwhile. A second call does nothing.

func (r *Runtime) DBLockCommand(copyPath string, role config.Role) string
    DBLockCommand is the command prefix a role runs every command that touches
    its copy's databases with (`magnum db-lock --checkout <copy> --role <role>
    --`, the prompts' .DBLockCommand): the roles of a task take turns on the
    copy's databases.

func (r *Runtime) Ended() <-chan struct{}
    Ended is the agents manager's Ended: a channel that closes once a pass,
    or a hook's look, ends a run or loses a session after it was taken, so the
    loop takes a turn's end that a later look of Wake's found at once (each pass
    takes a fresh one).

func (r *Runtime) HerdrUp(ctx context.Context) error
    HerdrUp asks the factory's herdr session whether it answers (a snapshot):
    the engine's herdr hold.

func (r *Runtime) Launch(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task, a registry.Attempt, c Copy, roles []config.Role) error
    Launch starts the roles of attempt a of task t in copy c, the copy the
    task claimed. It records the attempt's workspace label first (the attempt
    stays launching), then, before any pane exists, reads the memory and,
    for a Codex role, the budget for every role it launches: critical memory, a
    Codex budget at its soft cap and a kind's pause are a WaitError, no failure.
    A logged-out CLI pauses its kind. Then the task's workspace with a pane per
    role (EnsureWorkspace; the attempt's workspace a crash left before its first
    row is adopted, adopt), each agent started with the resume id of the role's
    earlier session when it has one, launches Stagger apart while the memory
    pressure is at warn, the RoleRun facts of each, and the attempt running.

func (r *Runtime) LetGo(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task, role string) (int, error)
    LetGo settles every prompt to role (as it runs) of task t whose
    delivery is unknown as abandoned: the operator looked at the pane
    (EventDeliveryUnknown). The role gets prompts again, none of those is sent
    a second time, and a run of theirs that was never submitted, and carries no
    prompt that arrived, is abandoned. It returns how many it settled.

func (r *Runtime) Observe(ctx context.Context) (evs []Event, err error)
    Observe runs one observe pass over herdr's snapshot and returns its events
    (and those Send and the recoveries found since the last pass), reading every
    session at most fullObserveEvery apart and the turns in flight on every
    pass (observeSessions): a run that ended (EventEnded), one that paused
    on its CLI's limit, login or overload (EventPaused, its reason and end),
    a refusal (EventRefused), a dialog left to the operator (EventBlocked,
    EventHooksTrust), a lost pane whose recoveries ran out (EventLost) and a
    loop without progress (EventNoProgress), and the turns typed into its panes
    (EventTyped, typed). It parks the liaisons their task's park left live
    (parkLeftLiaisons). A pass reads the user turns of an agent's transcript
    once, for the turns typed and the delivery of a prompt alike. A panic is
    contained: it comes back as the error.

func (r *Runtime) ObserveSoon() <-chan struct{}
    ObserveSoon is where the runtime asks the daemon's loop for an observe pass
```
