```text
    now (a StopFailure hook its screen proves: hookFailure); one request pending
    absorbs the others.

func (r *Runtime) Owner(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task) (store.PR, error)
    Owner upserts task t's owner row: repository factory/<repo name>, number the
    task's id, URL file://<task dir>, head the task's newest attempt (the task's
    id while it has none).

func (r *Runtime) PaneFocus() PaneFocus
    PaneFocus is what the observe passes saw of you in the factory's panes.

func (r *Runtime) Park(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task) error
    Park parks the agents of task t (agents.Manager.Park), then its liaison
    (parkLiaison): their conversations stay resumable, their panes are released.
    A run in flight or an agent at work on the task's row refuses with
    agents.ErrBusy; the liaison never stops the task's own park.

func (r *Runtime) Paused(kind string) *WaitError
    Paused is the wait of agent kind's pause in force (a usage limit's,
    a logout's, an overload's: Who says which), nil for none: while Codex is
    paused on its usage limit, a stage launches a Codex role's codex_fallback in
    its place rather than wait for the limit's reset.

func (r *Runtime) Proving(id int64) bool
    Proving reports whether the proof that ledger entry id never arrived
    is under way: a read (Reconcile) found no such turn in a transcript
    written past the prompt less than provingBound ago, and the read after
    RedeliverAfter decides. A proof whose later reads failed (the registry or
    the agents store refused) is under way no longer once its bound passed,
    so its task is told to you rather than held for good; a read that settles it
    or finds no proof ends it. It is the runtime's own: a fresh runtime after a
    restart starts every proof again.

func (r *Runtime) QuitCodex(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task) error
    QuitCodex quits the live Codex sessions of task t, once Codex never works
    on it again (Task.CodexNever, a refusal): none of them gets another prompt,
    and no conversation of theirs is resumed (a restart or a recovery of a Codex
    role refuses on such a task, mayRestart). Each session's runs in flight are
    abandoned first, and the session is quit hard (agents.Manager.QuitHard):
    a Codex agent at work on the task must stop. A session whose pane you are
    in is left for a later call (ErrOperatorInPane in the error), its runs
    abandoned all the same, and a quit that fails does not stop the others;
    the errors come back joined. A task that never launched has nothing to quit.

func (r *Runtime) QuitRole(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task, role, why string) error
    QuitRole quits the live sessions of task t's role (as it runs), whatever its
    kind, because why: a qa stage's walker whose run was cut (its browser and
    its server stopped) must not go on driving them, nor hold the Mac's memory.
    Its runs in flight are abandoned first, and each session is quit hard,
    as QuitCodex quits; its conversation stays resumable. A session whose pane
    you are in is left (ErrOperatorInPane in the error), its runs abandoned all
    the same; a task that never launched has nothing to quit.

func (r *Runtime) Reconcile(ctx context.Context, e registry.LedgerEntry) (string, error)
    Reconcile settles the delivery of ledger entry e from its agent's
    transcript and returns the verdict (registry.DeliveredYes, DeliveredNo or
    DeliveredUnknown, or the stored DeliveredAbandoned of a prompt you let go).
    A turn holding the prompt's hash, stamped after it was sent, is yes:
    the entry is settled and a run still pending is marked submitted, so it is
    observed and never sent again. No needs proof: a read that finds no such
    turn, and another at least RedeliverAfter later that finds none either, in a
    transcript written past the prompt, with the run never submitted (pending,
    or failed before it was) and the session not prompted since. Every other
    case (no transcript, a run that went further) stays unknown.

func (r *Runtime) Recover(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task) ([]string, error)
    Recover reconciles task t's sessions with herdr after a restart, before
    anything is launched or sent (agents.Manager.Recover on its owner row):
    a live row whose agent herdr shows elsewhere is bound to that pane again,
    a conversation herdr restored is live again, and a row whose agent is gone
    is lost (the watchdog recovers it). Runs are not touched: a submitted prompt
    is observed, never sent again. The task's liaison's row (Talk) is reconciled
    the same way, so a liaison herdr shows elsewhere is bound there again and
    its next Talk finds it live. It returns what changed ("fx-repro rebound");
    a task without an owner row or a liaison has nothing to recover.

func (r *Runtime) RecoverLost(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task, a registry.Attempt, role config.Role) error
    RecoverLost recovers role (as it runs) of attempt a of task t whose pane
    was lost, or whose last turn a recovery gave up with no turn in its place
    (RecoveryPrefix, which a stage rebuilt after a restart reads): a resume of
    its conversation (at most MaxResumes in the attempt), then a fresh session
    from the files; then the recoveries ran out (EventLost, "no progress after
    <n> recoveries", at the next Observe). Each recovery that shows no progress
    within NoProgressAfter takes the next step (Watchdog). A role this runtime
    already recovers is left to the watchdog. One whose steps ran out (stuck,
    lost) is left so while a turn of it is at work in a live pane (its end,
    or you in the pane, moves it); with nothing at work, its ladders start over:
    the stage asks only once your retry rebuilt it. One whose recovery cannot
    run now (a pause, you in its pane, a failure) is due it, and the watchdog
    takes it once it may. One a heal of the factory's herdr server is to
    relaunch is left to the heal.

func (r *Runtime) RunState(ctx context.Context, id string) (state, why string, err error)
    RunState is run id as the agents store keeps it: its state (store.Run*:
    pending, submitted or working while in flight, then ended, verified,
    failed or abandoned) and, for a run that failed or was given up, why (a
    run its CLI's pause ended is abandoned with PausedPrefix and the pause).
    The store holds it across a restart, which the events the observe pass gave,
    and the pauses, do not survive. An unknown run wraps store.ErrNotFound.

func (r *Runtime) RunsAs(t registry.Task, role config.Role) (config.Role, error)
    RunsAs is the role that runs for role on task t: role itself, or, on a task
    Codex never works on again (Task.CodexNever, or a refusal this runtime saw
    before the engine marked the task), a Codex role's codex_fallback. A Codex
    role without a fallback there is an error: it cannot run.

func (r *Runtime) Send(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task, a registry.Attempt, role config.Role, text string) (string, error)
    Send sends text to role's agent in attempt a of task t (role as it runs:
    RunsAs) as a new run, and returns the run's id. The ledger entry,
    with the text scrubbed and its hash, is written before the prompt leaves. It
    refuses without sending: a pause of the role's kind (a *WaitError), an entry
    of the role whose delivery is unknown (ErrDeliveryUnknown), the operator
    typing in the pane (ErrOperatorInPane), and a loop without progress whose
    steps ran out (ErrNoProgress, with EventNoProgress at the next Observe).
    Past MaxStagePrompts prompts in the stage, a context over MaxContext or the
    same failure SameFailures times, it first compacts the session, the next
    time starts a fresh session with the attempt's first prompt and text after
    it (returning that run), then refuses; a step that would compact or quit a
    pane the operator is in waits, ErrOperatorInPane. A role with no session
    at all, which no recovery brings back, is started again first (bringBack).
    A role a heal of the factory's herdr server holds (volume.go) waits for its
    relaunch on the fresh server, a *WaitError, or needs you, a *DeniedError;
    a first prompt herdr refuses because the agent is gone (agent_not_ready,
    agent_not_found) has the role's pane read for macOS's refusal of its copy
    (launchDenied).

func (r *Runtime) SettleWorkspaces(ctx context.Context) ([]Orphan, error)
    SettleWorkspaces settles, after a restart, the factory's workspaces (a label
    of WorkspaceLabel's shape, labelAttempt, or a liaison's, labelLiaison) that
    no session row names and that hold no agent (a workspace with an agent is
    Recover's to bind), a crash's leftovers between a workspace's creation
    and its first row: one whose attempt still launches or runs is kept,
    and the attempt's next launch adopts it (Launch); any other is closed,
    its attempt ended or unknown to the registry, and so is every liaison's (the
    next Talk makes the liaison a workspace of its own). What it settled comes
    back in herdr's order; a workspace it could not settle is in the error,
    and is settled at the next restart.

func (r *Runtime) Shift(gap time.Duration)
    Shift moves every turn deadline and progress window by gap, the time the Mac
    slept (the engine's wake): no run counts as hung for a sleep.

func (r *Runtime) Talk(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task, prompt string) (string, error)
    Talk starts or finds task t's liaison (LiaisonRole, on a row of its own:
    liaisonRow) and returns its pane. A live liaison whose agent herdr shows
    in its pane is kept as it is. A starting or live row herdr does not show so
    (its agent exited and left a shell, before an observe pass marked it lost;
    a restart moved it) is reconciled with herdr first (agents.Manager.Recover):
    a moved agent is bound to its pane again, a conversation herdr restored
    is live again, and a gone agent's row is lost, so its conversation is
    resumed rather than a fresh agent taking the row. Otherwise the liaison
    gets a workspace of its own in the factory's herdr session (liaisonLabel;
    the one its row's sessions hold is reused) whose working directory is the
    task's folder (Layout.FactoryTaskDir), never the copy, so it starts as well
    once a push or a drop freed the copy, and whose env names the daemon's
    MAGNUM_HOME (liaisonEnv). Its agent resumes the role's newest parked or
    lost conversation (ResumeID). Either way the conversation gets prompt,
    once, as its first (store.RunInitial), while no prompt of it ever went
    out (firstPromptDue): a fresh one, or one whose first prompt was refused
    or rejected before it was sent; a conversation that had one gets nothing,
    and the talk is you in the liaison's pane (its row's human_active_at,
    which operatorOn reads: a park leaves it for the human cooldown). When that
    prompt fails, the liaison is live in its pane all the same: Talk returns the
    pane with the error (you may step in; agents.ErrHumanActive while you typed
    into it), and the next Talk sends the prompt. Talks take turns, so two never
    start two liaisons, and a park of the task that comes meanwhile leaves its
    liaison alone (parkLiaison; the engine parks it again when the task ended
    while Talk ran, and an observe pass once it may: parkLeftLiaisons).

func (r *Runtime) TouchedSince(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task, since time.Time) (string, error)
    TouchedSince names who could have changed task t's copy since the time
    since, "" for nobody: a prompt to one of its agents after it (a run made
    after it), or your input into one of its panes after it (the owner row's
    human_active_at). The factory's checks ask it before they put back what
    their own commands changed: with somebody else at work since they began,
    they cannot tell their changes from that person's or that agent's.

func (r *Runtime) UseHookSocket(path string)
    UseHookSocket has every pane the runtime makes from now on carry
    the factory daemon's hook socket at path and the magnum binary
    (agents.Manager.SetHookSocket: MAGNUM_HOOK_SOCKET, MAGNUM_HOOK_BIN), so its
    agents' hooks send their events there; a pane already made keeps its env.
    The daemon calls it under its lock once its listener is up, before its
    startup, so every pane it makes names the socket. "" leaves the panes made
    from then on without the hook env.

func (r *Runtime) Verify(ctx context.Context, runID string, ok bool, why string) error
    Verify settles an ended run: verified when ok, failed with why otherwise,
    so the agents store's active runs stay few. It records the RoleRun's end:
    the stage's end fact and why, the outcome, the nudges, the tokens by model
    and the active and idle seconds. A failure feeds the loop detector: the same
    why SameFailures times in a row is a loop without progress.

func (r *Runtime) Void(ctx context.Context, runID, why string) error
    Void settles an ended run whose turn did what it was asked and is set aside,
    neither verified nor failed: it ended on questions, which wait for your
    answers or got them since. The agents store keeps it failed with why and the
    outcome voided, so a stage rebuilt after a restart takes its end again (a
    failed run's), and nothing that counts failed turns counts it; its RoleRun
    records its end as Verify's does, the outcome voided. It feeds the loop
    detector nothing: it is no failure, and no progress either.

func (r *Runtime) WaitWakes()
    WaitWakes waits for the later looks the events' Wake calls started
    (agents.Manager.WaitWakes): the daemon calls it once its listener stopped
    and the last Wake returned.

func (r *Runtime) Wake(ctx context.Context, ev agenthooks.Event)
    Wake hands an event of an agent's hook to the agents manager
    (agents.Manager.Wake), which looks at the event's pane now; the next observe
    pass returns what the look saw. ctx is the daemon's: it bounds the later
    looks Wake starts, which WaitWakes waits for. Wake takes no lock of the
    runtime's: the manager runs the runtime's callbacks inside it (ownerName and
    hookFailure take r.mu), so a caller must hold none either.

func (r *Runtime) Watchdog(ctx context.Context, now time.Time) (evs []Event, err error)
    Watchdog checks the runs in flight at now (the engine's observe pass):
    the hung-turn steps, and the recoveries that show no progress. It returns
    EventStuck and EventLost when their steps ran out. A panic is contained:
    it comes back as the error.

func (r *Runtime) Workspaces(ctx context.Context, t registry.Task) ([]string, error)
    Workspaces are the herdr workspaces of task t's live sessions, each once:
    where its sidebar token goes. None for a task that never launched.

type Turn struct {
	At         time.Time
	Text       string
	Before     string
	Stage      string
	AgentState string
	Origin     string
}
    Turn is a user turn of a factory agent's transcript that the factory did
    not send: At when the CLI stamped it, Text as typed (the engine scrubs it),
    Before what the agent said in its two turns before it (as said, oldest
    first, blank-line apart: the engine scrubs it whole before the registry
    keeps its last 1 KiB), Stage the stage of the attempt the agent worked in,
    AgentState herdr.StatusWorking when a run of the factory's was in flight
    in the pane when the turn arrived (else herdr.StatusIdle), and Origin
    registry.OriginHerdr or registry.OriginUnknown.

type WaitError struct {
	Who, What string
	Until     time.Time
}
    WaitError is a launch or a prompt that waits on something outside the task:
    Codex's budget, the Mac's memory, a usage limit, a login, an overload. It is
    no failure: the task waits with Who and What, as its wait says them ("usage:
    codex at 96%, waits till 16:00"), until Until when it is known.

func CodexBudgetWait(u config.Usage, snap usage.Snapshot, now time.Time) *WaitError
    CodexBudgetWait is the wait of a launch of a Codex role while Codex's budget
    snap is at or past usage codex_soft (or codex_hard), now being the clock's
    time ("codex at 96%, waits till 16:00", until the binding window's reset
    when snap names one); nil below the caps. Runtime.Launch holds every Codex
    role on it, so a stage's yield (the engine's) comes before the launch.

func (w *WaitError) Error() string
    Error implements error.

```

## stats

```text
package stats // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/factory/stats"

Package stats measures how much the factory still asks of the operator:
per task, the messages typed, the messages that only start a step, the answer
batches, the card decisions, the operator's time on cards and the time a task
waited on them, computed from the factory registry's evidence records alone
(spans, inputs, questions, decisions and review rounds) and set against the
baseline frozen before the first task (milestone 1's exit test); and, for a task
with a published PR, the PR's quality: what the local review missed at magnum's
first posted round (the escape checks) and the PR's CI failures after the
publish (its CI checks). Compute only reads the registry.

CONSTANTS

const (
	// EscapesChecked: the task's check is stored.
	EscapesChecked = "checked"
	// EscapesUnrecorded: the check is stored, but magnum recorded none of
	// the P0 to P2 findings its round's result counts: the escapes are
	// unknown.
	EscapesUnrecorded = "unrecorded"
	// EscapesNotYet: the task is published and magnum has posted no round
	// since the publish (or its check is still to run).
	EscapesNotYet = "not_yet"
	// EscapesNotChecked: the task ended (done, stopped, failed) without a
	// check, which only a published task gets: none will come.
	EscapesNotChecked = "not_checked"
)
    The states of a task's escapes (Quality.EscapesState).

const SendBackChoice = "send_back"
    SendBackChoice is the choice of a decision that sent the ready card back
    to the writer, whose note holds the key of its reason (the factory's
    ChoiceSendBack, which a test of the factory pins this to).


VARIABLES

var ErrBaselineFrozen = errors.New("the baseline is frozen once and never rewritten")
    ErrBaselineFrozen is FreezeBaseline's refusal: the file exists.


FUNCTIONS

func Classify(text string) string
    Classify returns the class of a message: step_start (it only starts a
    step: open the PR, push, merge the parent in, merge or release into a
    staging branch, take the recommendation, run or test things, resolve
    the conflicts or the review, submit the review, run a skill of such a
    step (/resolve-review, /create-pr), or let the agent go on: "go ahead",
    "implement it", "apply", "next step", "fix it", "do it", a bare "go", after
    any yes or none), approval (a yes: "yes", "ok", "sounds good", "confirm"
    alone or with "both", or a choice among the options the agent offered:
    "go with B", "option 2"), correction (the agent was wrong or must do it
    otherwise: "make sure ...", "you do that", "no need to ...", "don't push",
    "the summary was not posted", "I don't see you ...", "instead", "I said",
    "still broken"), access (credentials, a login, permission, a server to
    connect to) or info (anything else, which is also the class of an empty
    message, of a slash command of no step and of pasted output). It reads the
    words alone, the operator's own (ownWords: not the wrapper a tool puts
    around them, not the output they paste), in this order: a message that hands
    over a credential or grants access is access whatever else it says, and one
    that refuses a step ("don't push yet") is a correction, not a step start; a
    guard ("... and make sure they pass") or a report of what is not done ("the
    branch isn't pushed, push it") yields to the step the message asks for.
    Only the acts count: "log in to the sandbox" is access, "fix the login page"
    is information, "push it" starts a step and "the push failed" does not,
    what a thing should (not) be ("the export should be configurable") is no
    correction, and neither is a wish or a fact ("I don't want to expose it",
    "don't need this alert"). Stagings live in the operator's config, not here:
    any staging-<name> branch counts. The classes are the registry's;
    the factory's engine stores the class of your words with the input when it
    records them.

func FreezeBaseline(path string, b Baseline) error
    FreezeBaseline writes b to path, once. A path that exists, whatever it is (a
    file, a link, a directory), is refused with ErrBaselineFrozen and left as
    it is; the file appears whole or not at all (it is written beside path and
    linked into place, which cannot replace a file). A zero Frozen becomes the
    clock's now. The file is private (0600) and holds counts, no text.

func HasWords(kind string) bool
    HasWords reports whether an input of the kind holds the operator's own
    words, which the engine classifies when it records them: the typed kinds
    (IsTyped) and an answer. A decision's text is the machine's choice ("push"),
    not the operator's words, and the other kinds have no text.

func IsTyped(kind string) bool
    IsTyped reports whether an input of the kind holds the operator's own words:
    the task's text, guidance, a send-back's note, what was typed into a pane
    and what was said in one line. The engine classifies the words of these when
    it records them, and Compute counts them as typed. An answer, a decision,
    a rating, a stop, a drop and a retry are the operator's acts, not messages.

func ReadSessions(dir string, keyOf func(string) string, magnum map[string]bool, magnumDir func(string) bool) (sessions []Session, skipped Skipped, err error)
    ReadSessions reads the operator's old transcripts under dir (every
    .jsonl file: a Claude Code transcript, or a Codex rollout when the file
    is named rollout-*) into sessions: the messages the operator typed,
    from the user turns agents.ClaudeUserTurns and agents.CodexUserTurns read,
    less turns a tool or a task notification began and the records of the slash
    commands magnum types (magnum: agents.MagnumCommands, the list the factory
    drops from what it records of its panes, so both sides count the same; nil
    drops none). Only the operator's interactive sessions are read: a transcript
    of a headless run, a subagent's, a Codex session Claude Code started, or one
    whose session started in a directory magnumDir reports as one where magnum
    or the factory starts its own (nil: none) is left out before its messages
    are read (agents.ClaudeSessionFacts, agents.CodexSessionFacts; Skipped says
    which is which). A session's ticket is the key keyOf finds in the file's
    path below dir, else in its first message that holds one, else in the
    first of its git branches that holds one: a session that moved between the
    branches of two tickets counts for the first one only, all its messages with
    it. The session keeps the branches that name its key and whether its first
    message names it (OwnTickets). A transcript with no message or no key is not
    guessed at either. Every transcript left out is counted in skipped, by its
    reason. The sessions come oldest first, by the time of their first message,
    so that the first session of a ticket is the first one (BuildBaseline); a
    transcript whose turns carry no timestamp comes after the rest, and is never
    a ticket's first session. Prompts queued while an agent worked are not read,
    so a count is never above what was typed. Symbolic links are not followed.


TYPES

type Baseline struct {
	Frozen              time.Time `json:"frozen"`
	Tickets             int       `json:"tickets"`
	TypedPerTicket      Dist      `json:"typed_per_ticket"`
	StepStartsPerTicket Dist      `json:"step_starts_per_ticket"`
	Accuracy            float64   `json:"accuracy"`
}
    Baseline is the operator's way of working before the factory: over Tickets
    tickets, the typed messages and the step-starting messages per ticket,
    and Accuracy, the share of the operator's labelled messages that Classify
    got right (so how far the step-start counts can be trusted).

func BuildBaseline(sessions []Session, labelled []Labelled) (Baseline, error)
    BuildBaseline counts the operator's messages per ticket: the sessions of
    one key are one ticket, with the sum of their messages (a blank message is
    none), and the median, quartiles and extremes are taken over the tickets,
    never over the sessions. The sessions come oldest first (ReadSessions
    sorts them): the first message of a ticket's first session is the one
    that starts the work, so it counts as typed and never as a step start,
    as the message that starts a task does on the factory's side; the first
    message of a later session keeps its class, because a session opened only
    to start the next step is what the measure counts. Accuracy is the share of
    labelled that Classify gets right. It refuses sessions without a key, a set
    with no message and an empty or mislabelled labelled set, because a baseline
    it cannot measure is worse than none. The result has no Frozen time;
    FreezeBaseline sets it.

func LoadBaseline(path string) (*Baseline, error)
    LoadBaseline reads the frozen baseline at path: nil and no error when there
    is none yet, an error for a file that is not a baseline.

type Dist struct {
	Median float64 `json:"median"`
	P25    float64 `json:"p25"`
	P75    float64 `json:"p75"`
	Min    float64 `json:"min"`
	Max    float64 `json:"max"`
}
    Dist is how a count spreads over the tickets: the median, the quartiles
    (linear interpolation between the two nearest tickets) and the extremes.

func (d Dist) String() string
    String spells the distribution: its median, its middle half and its
    extremes, each to one decimal at most.

func (d Dist) Where(v float64) string
    Where says where v lies against the middle half of the tickets: "below" the
    first quartile, "above" the third, else "within".

type Escapes struct {
	Posted, P0, P1, P2, Unplaced int
	SameHeadOnly, Unrecorded     int
}
    Escapes counts what the local review missed at magnum's first posted round
    on a task's PR (the registry's escape check): Posted is how many P0 to P2
    findings that round posted, P0, P1 and P2 the escapes by priority (the P0
    to P2 findings no local finding caught), and Unplaced those of them with
    no line any local finding could be near (a finding of the review's body,
    say). SameHeadOnly counts the files of the posted findings the check
    compared at the same head only (git could not compare them at two heads,
    so a local finding at another head caught nothing there), and Unrecorded the
    P0 to P2 findings the round's result counts that magnum recorded no row of
    (the escapes are then unknown).

func (e Escapes) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error)
    MarshalJSON writes the counts with fixed keys, and their total.

func (e Escapes) Total() int
    Total is the escapes of every priority.

type FixLoops struct {
	ByHand    int `json:"by_hand"`
	ByAutofix int `json:"by_autofix"`
	Pushes    int `json:"pushes"`
	Commits   int `json:"commits"`
}
    FixLoops counts the fix loops magnum started on a PR: by hand (`magnum fix`,
    f on the board) and by autofix. The loops started by hand are the "no manual
    start" measure: the target is zero. Pushes and Commits are the fixers'
    pushes on the PR and the commits they pushed: the fix-loop commits after the
    publish, a measure of what the factory's PR still needed.

type JiraMoves struct {
	Plans           int            `json:"plans"`
	Planned         int            `json:"planned"`
	Matched         int            `json:"matched"`
	MedianLagSecs   int64          `json:"median_lag_secs"`
	TargetByOther   int            `json:"target_by_other"`
	TargetByUnknown int            `json:"target_by_unknown"`
	Elsewhere       int            `json:"elsewhere"`
	NotMoved        int            `json:"not_moved"`
	Open            int            `json:"open"`
	NothingToMove   int            `json:"nothing_to_move"`
	CouldNot        map[string]int `json:"could_not"`
	Pending         int            `json:"pending"`
}
    JiraMoves count the factory's plans of the Jira moves of a report's tasks,
    from the records the factory writes (registry.JiraPlans): Plans the plans
    made (settled); Planned those that planned a move, and of them Matched
    those your own move to the target followed (MedianLagSecs the median lag
    from the plan), TargetByOther and TargetByUnknown those moved to the target
    by someone else (Jira's automation among them) or by an author not known,
    Elsewhere those moved elsewhere, NotMoved those whose task ended with no
    move, Open those nothing was seen after yet; NothingToMove the plans of an
    issue at the target or past it; CouldNot the plans the factory could not
    make, by outcome (registry.PlanAssignedOther and the others); Pending the
    plans that wait for their read.

type Labelled struct {
	Text  string `json:"text"`
	Class string `json:"class"`
}
    Labelled is a message with the class the operator gave it by hand.

func ReadLabelled(path string) ([]Labelled, error)
    ReadLabelled reads the operator's labelled messages: one JSON object per
    line, {"text": "...", "class": "step_start"}, blank lines skipped. An error
    names the line, never its text.

type PR struct {
	Repo   string
	Number int
}
    PR names a task's PR: its repository (owner/name) and number.

func (p PR) String() string
    String is "owner/name#N", "" for none.

type Quality struct {
	EscapesState string   `json:"escapes_state"`
	Escapes      *Escapes `json:"escapes"`
	CIFailed     int      `json:"ci_failed"`
	CINotOurs    int      `json:"ci_failed_not_ours"`
}
    Quality is what a task's published PR said of the factory's work after the
    publish: EscapesState whether its local review was checked (EscapesChecked
    and the others), Escapes what the check found (nil without a check),
    CIFailed the failed CI on the PR's heads (GitHub's ci checks, one per head
    and result) but those marked not ours, and CINotOurs those apart.

type QualityTotals struct {
	PRs                int  `json:"prs"`
	Checked            int  `json:"checked"`
	NotYet             int  `json:"not_yet"`
	NotChecked         int  `json:"not_checked"`
	ChecksUnrecorded   int  `json:"checks_unrecorded"`
	ChecksSameHeadOnly int  `json:"checks_same_head_only"`
	Posted             int  `json:"posted"`
	EscapesTotal       int  `json:"escapes_total"`
	P0                 int  `json:"p0"`
	P1                 int  `json:"p1"`
	P2                 int  `json:"p2"`
	Unplaced           int  `json:"unplaced"`
	CIFailed           int  `json:"ci_failed"`
	CINotOurs          int  `json:"ci_failed_not_ours"`
	FixPushes          *int `json:"fix_pushes,omitempty"`
	FixCommits         *int `json:"fix_commits,omitempty"`
}
    QualityTotals are the quality numbers over a report's tasks with a PR: how
    many PRs; how many were checked for escapes (Checked, those whose round's
    findings magnum recorded), how many are not yet, not checked, or checked
    with their findings unrecorded (ChecksUnrecorded), and how many of the
    checked ones compared some files at the same head only (ChecksSameHeadOnly);
    the P0 to P2 findings the checked ones' first posted rounds posted,
    the escapes in all and by priority with those with no line apart; the CI
    failures after the publish with those not ours apart; and, when SetFixLoops
    read them, the fixers' pushes and their commits (nil: not read).

type RatingTotals struct {
	Count    int            `json:"count"`
	Tasks    int            `json:"tasks"`
	Changed  int            `json:"changed"`
	Plus     int            `json:"plus"`
	Minus    int            `json:"minus"`
	Reasons  map[string]int `json:"reasons"`
	NoReason int            `json:"no_reason"`
	Noise    int            `json:"noise"`
}
    RatingTotals are the ratings the operator gave with + and −. Count is how
    many were given (the registry keeps every one, so a task rated twice counts
    twice) on Tasks tasks, and Changed the tasks whose newest rating has another
    sign than an earlier one. The rest counts the newest rating of each task,
    the operator's last word: Plus and Minus, the key of the reason (NoReason:
    given with none), and Noise, those given without the diff opened first.

type Report struct {
	Since          time.Time
	Tasks          []TaskStats
	Baseline       *Baseline
	FixLoopsRead   bool
	FixLoopsUnread string
	// JiraMoves are the factory's plans of its Jira moves over the tasks
	// (nil when none has one): the shadow week's evidence.
	JiraMoves *JiraMoves
	// Take is whether your answers took the recommendations, and Ratings
	// what you rated with + and −, over the tasks (nil when none is
	// recorded): your explicit signals, from the registry's records.
	Take    *TakeTotals
	Ratings *RatingTotals
}
    Report is the stats of the tasks started at or after Since (the zero time:
    all of them), oldest first, and the baseline to read them against (nil when
    none is frozen; Compute leaves it to the caller to load). FixLoopsRead says
    SetFixLoops counted the tasks' fix loops, and FixLoopsUnread why it could
    not ("" when it could, or was not asked).

func Compute(ctx context.Context, reg *registry.Registry, since time.Time) (Report, error)
    Compute is ComputeAt at the clock's now.

func ComputeAt(ctx context.Context, reg *registry.Registry, since, now time.Time) (Report, error)
    ComputeAt measures the tasks of reg started at or after since (the zero
    time: all), whole, whatever happened to them later, from their spans,
    inputs, questions, decisions and review rounds, and a published task's
    escape check, escapes and CI checks. now ends a wait on the operator that
    is still open. It reads and never writes. Nothing here reads a transcript or
    GitHub, so the numbers are the evidence the factory recorded.

func (r Report) Markdown() string
    Markdown renders the report for reading and for the exit test: a table of
    the tasks, then each task set against the baseline's middle half.

func (r Report) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error)
    MarshalJSON writes the report with fixed keys, an empty list for no tasks
    and null for no window and no baseline.

func (r Report) Quality() *QualityTotals
    Quality totals the report's tasks with a PR (Quality); nil when no task has
    one.

func (r *Report) SetFixLoops(loops map[PR]FixLoops, unread string)
    SetFixLoops gives each task with a PR the fix loops magnum started on it
    (loops, read from magnum's registry by the caller: this package reads only
    the factory's; a PR loops lacks counts zero), or, with unread set, records
    why they could not be read and counts none.

type Session struct {
	Key      string
	Messages []string
	// Branches are the git branches the session ran on that name its key
	// (a branch of another ticket is not one), and KeyInFirst whether its
	// first message names its key, the way the operator starts a task: they
	// tell the operator's own tickets (OwnTickets).
	Branches   []string
	KeyInFirst bool
}
    Session is one agent session of the operator's: the ticket it worked on and
    the messages the operator typed to it.

func OwnTickets(sessions []Session, prefix string) (own []Session, others int)
    OwnTickets keeps, in order, the sessions of the tickets that were the
    operator's own work: a ticket counts when one of its sessions ran on a
    branch of that ticket (Session.Branches) that starts with prefix (the
    operator's GitHub login and a dash, as the factory names its branches;
    letter case aside) or began with a message that names its key. A ticket
    whose sessions all ran on other people's branches, or on none, without such
    a first message is someone else's (a review, a deploy of a colleague's
    work): its sessions are dropped, and others counts those tickets. An empty
    prefix makes no branch the operator's.

type Skipped struct {
	// Headless: nobody typed in it: Claude Code run by its SDK (claude -p,
	// the TypeScript or Python SDK: an sdk-* entrypoint; the terminal's cli
	// and an IDE's or the desktop app's are typed in) or `codex exec`
	// (originator codex_exec, or source exec).
	Headless int
	// Subagent: another agent's thread: a Claude Code subagent's transcript
	// (a file under a subagents directory) or a Codex subagent's rollout (a
	// source that names a subagent).
	Subagent int
	// ByAgent: a Codex session Claude Code started (originator "Claude
	// Code").
	ByAgent int
	// Magnum: it started in a directory where magnum or the factory starts
	// sessions of its own, which hold magnum's prompts.
	Magnum int
	// NoMessage: no message of the operator's.
	NoMessage int
	// NoKey: no ticket key in its path, its messages or its git branches.
	NoKey int
}
    Skipped counts the transcripts ReadSessions leaves out, by why: each is
    counted once, under the first reason that holds, in this order.

func (s Skipped) Total() int
    Total is how many transcripts were left out.

type Take struct {
	Of   int `json:"of"`
	Took int `json:"took"`
}
    Take counts the cases Of, out of which the operator Took the recommendation:
    the answered questions that carried one, or the decisions on a card that did
    (and followed it).

type TakeTotals struct {
	Questions Take            `json:"questions"`
	ByRole    map[string]Take `json:"by_role"`
	ByKind    map[string]Take `json:"by_kind"`
	Decisions Take            `json:"decisions"`
}
    TakeTotals are the take rates over a report's tasks: the answered questions
    with a recommendation in all (Questions), by the source that raised them
    (ByRole: the sources the stats count a question under, several joined with
    "+") and by the kind of the task (ByKind); and the decisions on a card
    that carried a recommendation (Decisions, whose Took is the decisions that
    followed it). A question counts once per task, by its text, with its current
    answer.

type TaskStats struct {
	TaskID   int64
	Key      string
	PR       PR
	FixLoops *FixLoops
	Quality  *Quality

	Typed, StepStarts, Approvals, Corrections, Access int
	UnknownOrigin                                     int
	AnswerBatches, Decisions, ReviewRounds            int
	Questions                                         int
	QuestionsFrom, QuestionsShared                    map[string]int
	ReviewJudges                                      []string
	SecondOpinion                                     int
	SendBacks                                         map[string]int

	OperatorSecs time.Duration //nolint:staticcheck // ST1011: the spec's name for the measure ("the operator's seconds per task")
	WaitedOnYou  time.Duration
	StartToReady time.Duration
}
    TaskStats is what one task asked of the operator. Typed counts the messages
    the operator typed (the task's text, typed in a pane, said in one line,
    the start's guidance, the note of a send-back); StepStarts, Approvals,
    Corrections and Access count those of them by class (a retry is a step
    the operator started by hand, so it counts as a step start and not as a
    typed message; the message that starts the task, however it is recorded,
    is the one the factory needs, so it is typed and never a step start,
    whatever its words say); a message of another class, or of none,
    is only typed. UnknownOrigin counts apart the turns typed in a pane that
    nothing proves the operator typed (any origin but registry.OriginHerdr:
    a turn counts as the operator's only with positive proof): kept for
    evaluation only, they are never a typed message, a step start or any class.
    AnswerBatches counts the revisions of questions that were answered, and
    Decisions the decisions on cards; both are counted apart. OperatorSecs is
    the operator's time on cards: for each decision, from the card shown to the
    decision, and for each answered revision of questions, from the questions
    shown to the first answer, each at most cardCap (a card never shown has no
    time to measure). WaitedOnYou is how long the task waited on the operator,
    asleep or not (its spans that wait on "you"). StartToReady is how long it
    took to reach the ready card (zero before it does). PR is the task's PR
    (zero before it has one), FixLoops the fix loops magnum started on it (nil:
    not counted, SetFixLoops), and Quality what the PR said of the factory's
    work after the publish (nil for a task without a PR). Questions counts
    the questions the task asked, each once whatever revisions carried it;
    QuestionsFrom counts those of one source by that source, and QuestionsShared
    those of several by the sources joined with "+" (questionSources): what
    each role, a second reader of the ticket's points among them, adds alone to
    what the operator is asked, and what two readers raise both. ReviewJudges
    is the agent kind of the judge each round of the local review ran with,
    by cycle ("" for a round whose begin event names no judge: an older build's;
    nil when no round names one), and SecondOpinion the cycle of the task's
    second opinion (0 for none), from the rounds' begin events (roundJudges).
    SendBacks counts the decisions that sent the ready card back to the writer
    by the key of their reason ("known" for the defects the local review left
    open, sent by the card's w; nil for none).

func (t TaskStats) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error)
    MarshalJSON writes the task's stats with fixed keys and the durations in
    whole seconds.

```

## factoryread

```text
package factoryread // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/factoryread"

Package factoryread is the review side's read of what the factory keeps:
the local review round of a pull request the factory published, from its
registry (factory.db), and the task's plan, ticket and answers, from the task's
directory, for the review retro (DECISIONS "The review retro tags factory-origin
misses and their stage"); and a task's local review rounds, their heads and
roles and its answered questions with every answer they had, for the replay
of a round as an eval case (LocalReview, `magnum eval add --local-task`),
and a task's Codex mark and published PR before its replay (TaskCodex).
It only reads: the registry is opened read only (mode=ro, never created,
so nothing writes its file or its WAL), with a busy timeout, and closed after
each read; a task's files are read inside an os.Root of its directory. It knows
the factory's schema only as far as these reads need (pr_links, review_findings,
review_cycles, tasks, events, questions, question_answers) and never migrates
it: internal/factory/registry owns it, whose types (registry.Question) the
questions are read into.

CONSTANTS

const (
	KindPlan    = "plan"    // the plan: the report the factory's judge wrote
	KindTicket  = "ticket"  // the Jira issue, or the prompt a task started from
	KindAnswers = "answers" // the operator's answers to the task's questions
)
    The kinds of a task's files the retro's classifier reads (TaskFile.Kind).

const TaskFileMax = 1 << 20
    TaskFileMax is the largest task file read, in bytes.


VARIABLES

var ErrNoRegistry = errors.New("the factory's registry does not exist")
    ErrNoRegistry is Published's error when the factory's registry does not
    exist: no factory ever ran on this machine.

var ErrNoTask = errors.New("the factory's registry has no such task")
    ErrNoTask is LocalReview's error when the factory's registry holds no task
    of that id.


FUNCTIONS

func TaskCodex(ctx context.Context, path string, taskID int64) (never bool, pr string, err error)
    TaskCodex is what the factory's registry at path says of Codex and
    task taskID, read only: whether Codex never works on the task again
    (tasks.codex_never, which the factory sets when Codex refuses it:
    the account is at stake) and the PR the task published (pr_links,
    "owner/repo#N"; "" before its publish). The replay of a local case reads it
    before anything starts (evalrun.Refused). A registry that does not exist is
    ErrNoRegistry, a task it does not hold ErrNoTask; one that cannot be read is
    another error.


TYPES

type LocalQuestion struct {
	registry.Question
	History []registry.AnswerEdit
}
    LocalQuestion is one of a task's answered questions: its row, with the
    fields answers.md renders (registry.AnswersMarkdown: its revision, position,
    text, options, recommendation, answer, who raised it, when it was first
    answered and whether its answer takes the recommendation), and every answer
    it had (History, question_answers, oldest first). A row from before the
    registry kept them has none: its one answer is the one given when it was
    answered.

type LocalRound struct {
	Cycle   int
	Round   int
	Head    string
	Started time.Time
	Roles   []string
}
    LocalRound is one cycle of a task's local review (review_cycles):
    its number, the head it reviewed (head_before) and when it began,
    with the loop's round and the roles the cycle's newest begin event names
    (the factory's "round 1 (cycle 1) at <short head>: <role>, <role>", and ";
    judge <role> (<kind>)" after them; a round that ran again in its cycle names
    the roles of its last run). Round is 0 and Roles nil when no begin event of
    the cycle reads so for its head.

type LocalTask struct {
	ID                           int64
	Repo, Branch, Title, JiraKey string
	CodexNever                   bool
	Rounds                       []LocalRound
	Questions                    []LocalQuestion
}
    LocalTask is a task of the factory as the replay of a round of its
    local review needs it (`magnum eval add --local-task`): its repository
    (owner/name), branch, title and Jira key, whether Codex never works on it
    again (CodexNever, tasks.codex_never: Codex refused it), each cycle of its
    local review the registry records (Rounds, by cycle), and its answered
    questions (Questions, by revision and position), from which the answers a
    round could read are rebuilt (AnswersAt).

func LocalReview(ctx context.Context, path string, taskID int64) (LocalTask, error)
    LocalReview reads task taskID of the registry at path, read only and in
    one transaction (one snapshot of what the factory writes): the task,
    its review cycles with their round and roles (LocalRound), and its answered
    questions with their answers (LocalQuestion). A registry that does not exist
    is ErrNoRegistry, a task it does not hold ErrNoTask; one that cannot be read
    is another error.

func (t LocalTask) AnswersAt(at time.Time) (qs []registry.Question, left int)
    AnswersAt are t's questions as they stood at at (a round's start),
    by revision and position, for registry.AnswersMarkdown: each one answered
    before at, with its newest answer before at and whether that answer takes
    the recommendation (as the factory decides it: the recommended label,
    spaces trimmed). left counts the answers given at at or later, first answers
    and revisions alike, which are not there.

type Task struct {
	ID           int64
	OpenedHead   string
	ApprovedHead string
	// Findings are the local review's findings, first seen first, each
	// escapes.SourceLocal with Ref "<task id>/<finding id>", Round its last
	// cycle (where the registry took its place from) and Head the head
	// that cycle reviewed (review_cycles.head_before), which a later
	// cycle's fix may have moved on from; the task's Head when the
	// registry holds no head for that cycle.
	Findings []escapes.Finding
}
    Task is one factory task that published a pull request: the heads its PR
    opened on and its local review approved, and that review's findings.

func Published(ctx context.Context, path, repo string, number int) ([]Task, error)
    Published returns the tasks of the registry at path that published pull
    request number of repo ("owner/name", any case), newest first, each with
    its local review's findings; none when the factory published no such pull
    request. A registry that does not exist is ErrNoRegistry; one that cannot
    be opened or read (not a database, a schema without these tables) is another
    error.

func (t Task) Head() string
    Head is the commit the task's local findings are taken to name: the head its
    local review approved, else the one its PR opened on.

type TaskFile struct {
	Kind    string
	Name    string
	Data    []byte
	Skipped string
}
    TaskFile is one of a task's files: its kind, its name in the task's
    directory and its bytes, or why it was not read (Skipped).

func TaskFiles(dir string) []TaskFile
    TaskFiles reads the plan, the ticket and the answers in the task directory
    dir, in that order, read only and inside dir: a kind none of whose names
    exists is left out, and one larger than TaskFileMax or that cannot be read
    says why (Skipped). A directory that does not exist has no files.

```

## fsx

```text
package fsx // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/fsx"

Package fsx holds the file helpers several packages share: an atomic file
write, plain or confined to an os.Root, a replacement without disk syncs,
a size-limited read of a regular file, plain or inside an os.Root, the check
of a file holding a secret, an existence check and a canonical path. It imports
only the standard library.

VARIABLES

var (
	// ErrNotRegular: the path is a symbolic link, a directory, a device, a
	// FIFO or a socket.
	ErrNotRegular = errors.New("not a regular file (no symbolic links or special files)")
	// ErrTooLarge: the file holds more than the bytes the caller allows.
	ErrTooLarge = errors.New("file too large")
)
    ReadRegular's errors, each inside an *fs.PathError naming the path.


FUNCTIONS

func Canon(p string) string
    Canon cleans p and resolves its symlinks when it exists, so the /var and
    /private/var spellings of one directory compare equal; "" stays "".

func CheckPrivate(path string) error
    CheckPrivate checks a file that holds a secret (a token): a regular file,
    symlinks followed, that neither its group nor others may read or write (0600
    or narrower). A missing file is fs.ErrNotExist. The errors name the file and
    what is wrong with it, never its content.

func Exists(path string) bool
    Exists reports whether path names something os.Stat can see (a symlink
    counts by its target).

func ReadRegular(path string, limit int64) ([]byte, error)
    ReadRegular reads the regular file at path, at most limit bytes: the read
    for a file a pull request controls (a checkout's lockfiles, its schema,
    the marker its setup writes, its project config). A symbolic link at path
    is refused, not followed, so a file a checkout commits as a symlink never
    leads the daemon out of the checkout, to /dev/zero or to anyone's file;
    a directory, a device, a FIFO or a socket is refused before it is opened,
    so no read runs without end and no open waits for a FIFO's writer. Both are
    ErrNotRegular. Only path's last element is checked: its parent directories
    resolve as usual, and what they lead to is held to the same rules. A file
    over limit bytes, by its size or by what the read finds (it may grow),
    is ErrTooLarge, and none of it is returned. A missing file is the error
    os.Lstat returns, unwrapped (errors.Is fs.ErrNotExist).

func ReadRegularIn(root *os.Root, name string, limit int64) ([]byte, error)
    ReadRegularIn is ReadRegular for the file name inside root, for a file
    whose directory something untrusted wrote (a curator's scratch, a review
    round's leftovers in a copy): a symbolic link (even to a file inside root),
    a directory or a special file is ErrNotRegular and nothing it points
    to is read, a file past limit is ErrTooLarge and none of it is read,
    and root keeps every path inside it. The open does not wait for a FIFO put
    in the file's place since the Lstat (O_NONBLOCK; SameFile then refuses it).
    The errors are bare (no path): the caller names the file.

func ReplaceFile(path string, data []byte, perm fs.FileMode) error
    ReplaceFile is WriteFileAtomic without the file sync and the directory sync:
    the temporary file is written and renamed over path at once, so a reader
    still sees the old content or the new, never part of a file, but a crash
    or a power loss can leave an empty or a missing file. A caller picks it
    for a file that is rewritten all the time and that nothing misses when it
    is lost, where the two syncs (each a full disk flush on macOS, about 9 ms,
    which also holds up every other process writing to the disk) cost more than
    the file is worth: the tab-bar heartbeat, whose missing or stale first
    line already reads as "magnum down". Everything that must survive a crash
    uses WriteFileAtomic. The mode, the symlink and the temporary file follow
    WriteFileAtomic.

func ReplaceFileIn(root *os.Root, name string, data []byte, perm fs.FileMode) error
    ReplaceFileIn is ReplaceFile for name inside root, confined as
    WriteFileAtomicIn is: for many files a later write puts back when they are
    lost (copy_files' directory of generated fixtures), where a disk flush for
    each one would hold the disk for seconds.

func WriteFileAtomic(path string, data []byte, perm fs.FileMode) error
    WriteFileAtomic replaces path with data, mode exactly perm whatever the
    umask: a temporary file with a unique name in path's directory is written,
    synced and renamed over path, then the directory is synced, so a reader (or
    a crash) sees the old content or the new, never part of a file. A symlink at
    path is replaced, not followed. The directory must exist; the temporary file
    is removed on failure. A test binary (testing.Testing) skips both syncs:
    no test can observe them, and each is a full disk flush on macOS (about 9
    ms) that the suite's thousands of writes queued on.

func WriteFileAtomicIn(root *os.Root, name string, data []byte, perm fs.FileMode) error
    WriteFileAtomicIn is WriteFileAtomic for name inside root: a name that is
    absolute or escapes root (.., or a symlink in a parent pointing outside) is
    an error and nothing is written outside root. name's directory is resolved
    once, so the temporary file and the rename land in the same one.

```

## github

```text
package github // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/github"

Package github is magnum's GitHub access layer. Every call is a `gh api`
subprocess run through execx.Runner, so the identity is chosen by the client's
env (GH_CONFIG_DIR per identity), tests script gh with execx.Fake and --dry-run
turns writes into no-ops.

Reads use GraphQL (`gh api graphql --input -`): the per-owner Radar poll (a
user or an organization) and the CIStates of its pull requests' heads, batched
Details, ConfirmStates for PRs that left the OPEN list, ReviewsWithMarker for
verification, and Reviews and ReviewThreads for the whole conversation of one
pull request. A Radar page or CIStates call GitHub could not answer in time
is asked again once at half the size (retrySmaller). REST is used where only
REST carries the data (ReviewREST: the "[bot]"-suffixed author login; Compare,
CompareFiles and ComparePush: the size, the patches and the merge commits of
an arbitrary base...head range; FileAt: the raw content of a file at a ref,
a response that is bytes and not JSON) and for writes (DismissReview).

GraphQL partial errors are tolerated only for NOT_FOUND paths, which the
batched calls report as missing numbers; any other error fails the whole call,
so a half-read poll never looks like closed pull requests. Failures that reached
GitHub come back as *APIError, which matches ErrNotFound, ErrUnauthorized,
ErrForbidden and ErrRateLimited through errors.Is.

Every command carries --hostname github.com, so an inherited GH_HOST can never
send a call (or an identity's token) to another server. Client.Reauth lets the
caller refresh an identity's credentials after a 401.

CONSTANTS

const (
	CheckPassed  = "passed"  // a check run's SUCCESS or NEUTRAL, a status's SUCCESS
	CheckFailed  = "failed"  // FAILURE, TIMED_OUT, CANCELLED, ACTION_REQUIRED, STARTUP_FAILURE, STALE; a status's FAILURE or ERROR
	CheckPending = "pending" // a check run not COMPLETED, a status PENDING or EXPECTED
	CheckSkipped = "skipped" // SKIPPED
)
    Check.State values.

const CompareFileLimit = 300
    CompareFileLimit is the most files GitHub lists for one comparison;
    a comparison listing exactly this many is treated as truncated.

const ComparePushCommits = 100
    ComparePushCommits is the most commits ComparePush reads (one page at
    GitHub's per_page maximum).

const FileAtLimit = 512 << 10
    FileAtLimit caps FileAt: a larger file is not returned.

const FirstParentDepth = 5
    FirstParentDepth is how many commits FirstParentChecks reads: a commit and
    its first parents, four deep.

const MaxAnnotations = 50
    MaxAnnotations is the most annotations AnnotationPaths reads of one check
    run: one page, GitHub's own limit per page being higher.

const MaxIssueComments = issueCommentsPage * issueCommentsMaxPages
    MaxIssueComments is how many conversation comments IssueComments reads at
    most (issueCommentsMaxPages pages of issueCommentsPage).

const MaxReviewThreads = threadsPageSize * threadsMaxPages
    MaxReviewThreads is how many review threads ReviewThreads and
    AllReviewThreads read at most (threadsMaxPages pages of threadsPageSize).

const MaxReviews = reviewsPageSize * reviewsMaxPages
    MaxReviews is how many reviews AllReviews reads at most (reviewsMaxPages
    pages of reviewsPageSize).

const PullFilesMaxPages = 30
    PullFilesMaxPages is how many pages of 100 PullFiles reads: GitHub's own cap
    for the endpoint, 3000 files.


VARIABLES

var (
	ErrNotFound     = errors.New("github: not found")
	ErrUnauthorized = errors.New("github: unauthorized")
	ErrForbidden    = errors.New("github: forbidden")
	ErrRateLimited  = errors.New("github: rate limited")
)
    Errors matched by *APIError through errors.Is.

var ErrFileTooLarge = errors.New("github: file too large")
    ErrFileTooLarge matches FileAt's error for a file above FileAtLimit; callers
    skip such a file.


FUNCTIONS

func Account(login, typename string) string
    Account is a login as REST names the account: a bot's GraphQL login
    ("zhuravel" with __typename "Bot") gets its "[bot]" suffix, so an App named
    like a user ("zhuravel[bot]", the user "zhuravel") stays another account.
    A user's login, one already suffixed and "" come back as they are. The
    registry keeps logins in this form.

func BetweenCalls(ctx context.Context)
    BetweenCalls runs the function WithBetweenCalls put into ctx, if any.
    The client calls it before each gh command; a fake GitHub can do the same.

func ConnectionCause(msg string) string
    ConnectionCause names the connection-class failure msg reports ("" = none:
    a real verdict from GitHub, or about an identity): the network's (DNS, a
    timeout, a refused or reset connection, TLS, a server curl could not reach),
    gh unable to connect, a closed connection, a GitHub server error (5xx, 499,
    an empty answer) or a rate limit (429, secondary or primary).

func IsAccount(author, typename, login string, bot bool) bool
    IsAccount reports whether an author (its login in either form and its
    GraphQL __typename) is the account login names, an App's when bot:
    the same name (SameLogin) and the same kind of account (IsBot), so the user
    "zhuravel" is never the App "zhuravel[bot]".

func IsBot(typename, login string) bool
    IsBot reports whether an author is a bot: GraphQL __typename "Bot" or a REST
    login ending in "[bot]".

func NetworkCause(msg string) string
    NetworkCause names the failure of the network itself that msg reports (""
    = none): DNS, a timeout, a refused or reset connection, an unreachable
    network or server, TLS. What git, ssh and curl print when a remote cannot be
    reached.

func NormalizeLogin(s string) string
    NormalizeLogin strips a trailing "[bot]" so REST logins ("talkable[bot]")
    compare equal to GraphQL logins ("talkable").

func OpOf(ctx context.Context) string
    OpOf is the label WithOp put into ctx ("" for none).

func ParseRef(s, defaultRepo string) (owner, repo string, number int, err error)
    ParseRef resolves a pull request reference: a URL
    https://github.com/o/r/pull/N[/...], "o/r#N", "r#N" (owner from
    defaultRepo), "#N" or "N" (both from defaultRepo, "owner/name").

func SameAccount(a, b string) bool
    SameAccount compares two logins in Account form case-insensitively:
    "zhuravel[bot]" and "zhuravel" are different accounts.

func SameLogin(a, b string) bool
    SameLogin compares two logins case-insensitively after NormalizeLogin:
    the same name whether or not either is a bot, so an App and a user of the
    same name match. Use it only next to a check of the kind (IsAccount);
    SameAccount otherwise.

func ValidLogin(s string) bool
    ValidLogin reports whether s is a GitHub user's login as GitHub allows it:
    letters, digits and hyphens, 1 to 39 of them, not starting with a hyphen (no
    "@", no "[bot]").

func ValidWorkflowFile(name string) bool
    ValidWorkflowFile reports whether name is a workflow file DispatchWorkflow
    takes: a plain file name of .github/workflows ending in .yml or .yaml.

func WithBetweenCalls(ctx context.Context, fn func()) context.Context
    WithBetweenCalls returns ctx carrying fn, which the client runs before
    every gh command it makes with that context (BetweenCalls), on the caller's
    goroutine: the daemon's poll answers the requests a CLI queued meanwhile, so
    one waits for a single GitHub call, not the whole poll. fn gets no context:
    it must not make its calls with this one.

func WithOp(ctx context.Context, op string) context.Context
    WithOp returns ctx labelled with what the calls made with it read GitHub
    for, which each call hands its client's Meter (Call.Op). A label set deeper
    in the call chain wins: a round's setup reads under "round.setup" though the
    round's context says "round".


TYPES

type APIError struct {
	Op      string         // what magnum was doing ("details talkable/talkable")
	Status  int            // HTTP status when known, else 0
	Message string         // REST message or gh's stderr line
	Errors  []GraphQLError // GraphQL errors, if any
	// Details are the entries of a REST error body's "errors" array (a
	// string as it is, an object as its field and message), e.g. "Can not
	// approve your own pull request" under the message "Unprocessable
	// Entity".
	Details []string
}
    APIError is a failure GitHub reported: an HTTP status from gh, a REST error
    body, or GraphQL errors.

func (e *APIError) Error() string

func (e *APIError) Is(target error) bool
    Is maps the error onto the package sentinels.

type CICounts struct {
	Failed, Pending, Passed, Skipped, Total int
}
    CICounts are a check rollup's check runs and commit statuses by state as
    GitHub counts them (checkRunCountsByState, statusContextCountsByState),
    normalized as Check.State is: every run the rollup holds, a superseded one
    and those past a page of 100 included, so they are not CIRollup.Checks'
    tally. A zero Total is unknown.

type CIRollup struct {
	SHA   string // the commit; "" when GitHub listed none
	State string // GitHub's rollup: SUCCESS | FAILURE | PENDING | ERROR | EXPECTED; "" when the commit has no checks
	// Total is len(Checks) plus the checks GitHub did not return (past its
	// page of 100).
	Total int
	// Complete is true when Checks is every check: GitHub returned a single
	// page of at most 100.
	Complete bool
	// Checks is the latest run of each check (a check run's WorkflowFile
	// and Name, a commit status's context apart), in GitHub's order; never
	// nil. A re-run, or a SKIPPED run left from a draft, supersedes or is
	// superseded by the same job's other runs.
	Checks []Check
	// Counts are the rollup's own counts by state, as CIStates reads them
	// (superseded runs included, so not Checks' tally): the poll compares
	// the two to tell that a check finished on a rollup whose state did not
	// move. A zero Total when GitHub gave none.
	Counts CICounts
}
    CIRollup is the status check rollup of a pull request's head commit.

type CIState struct {
	State  string
	Counts CICounts
}
    CIState is a pull request's head check rollup as CIStates reads it:
    its State (SUCCESS, FAILURE, PENDING, ERROR, EXPECTED; "" when the head has
    no checks) and its Counts by state (a zero Total when GitHub gave none).

type Call struct {
	// Op is what the caller read GitHub for: the label WithOp put into the
	// call's context ("" when it carries none).
	Op string
	// Kind is the call's own name ("details", "review threads", "compare").
	Kind string
	// GraphQL: a GraphQL call, whose Rate is the rateLimit block GitHub
	// answered (Cost: the points it charged); zero when no answer carried
	// one (a call that failed before GraphQL answered). Otherwise a REST
	// call: one request against the core budget, with a zero Rate.
	GraphQL bool
	Rate    RateLimit
	// RateLimited: GitHub refused the call for its rate limit (an *APIError
	// matching ErrRateLimited), so the identity's budget is spent, whatever
	// its last reading said.
	RateLimited bool
}
    Call is one gh api command a Client ran, as its Meter hears of it.

type Check struct {
	Name  string // the check run's name or the status's context
	State string // CheckPassed | CheckFailed | CheckPending | CheckSkipped
	// Workflow is the name the GitHub Actions workflow whose run the check
	// belongs to declares; "" for a commit status or another app's check
	// run. Any workflow file may declare any name, a file the PR adds
	// included.
	Workflow string
	// WorkflowFile is that workflow's file as GitHub's path to the workflow
	// ends ("ci.yml" for .github/workflows/ci.yml, from the workflow's
	// resourcePath "/<owner>/<repo>/actions/workflows/ci.yml"); "" where
	// Workflow is. Runs are told apart by it, not by Workflow.
	WorkflowFile string
	// Status is true for a commit status (the statuses API, which anyone
	// who can write to the repository posts), false for a check run: the
	// two are never taken for runs of one check.
	Status bool
	// At is when the check finished, else started (a check run), or was
	// posted (a commit status); zero for a check run not started yet.
	At time.Time
	// URL is the page of the run: a check run's detailsUrl (a GitHub
	// Actions job's page), else its check run page on GitHub, a commit
	// status's targetUrl; "" for a status that posted none. Whoever posts
	// the check sets it: a link to show, never one to follow.
	URL string
}
    Check is one check run or commit status of a CIRollup.

type Client struct {
	// Run executes gh. Required.
	Run execx.Runner
	// Env overlays gh's environment, e.g. GH_CONFIG_DIR for an identity.
	// It wins over the defaults (GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1, GH_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1).
	Env map[string]string
	// Dir is gh's working directory ("" = inherit).
	Dir string
	// Reauth, when set, runs once after a call fails with ErrUnauthorized
	// (the identity's token was revoked or expired); the call is then retried
	// once. A 401 means GitHub applied nothing, so retrying a write is safe.
	// If Reauth fails the call returns the unauthorized error together with
	// Reauth's error. It may be called from several goroutines at once.
	Reauth func(ctx context.Context) error
	// Meter, when set, hears of every gh api command the client runs, right
	// after it returned, on the caller's goroutine: a GraphQL call with the
	// rate limit GitHub answered (its cost), a REST call as one request
	// (meter.go). It must return at once and never call GitHub; a Meter that
	// panics fails no call. Set it before the client's first call.
	Meter func(Call)

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Client runs gh as one identity. The zero value is unusable; set Run.

func (c *Client) AllReviewThreads(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int) ([]Thread, bool, error)
    AllReviewThreads is ReviewThreads that also reports whether the list is
    complete: false when the pull request has more than MaxReviewThreads
    threads, the later ones left out. A caller that acts on what the list lacks
    (no open thread of another reviewer) reads it.

func (c *Client) AllReviews(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int) ([]Review, bool, error)
    AllReviews lists every review of a pull request, oldest first:
    reviewsPageSize (100) per page, at most reviewsMaxPages (5) pages.
    It reports whether the list is complete: false when the pull request has
    more reviews than that, the later ones left out. A missing repository or
    pull request is an error matching ErrNotFound.

func (c *Client) AnnotationPaths(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, checkRunID int64, limit int) ([]string, error)
    AnnotationPaths lists the repository paths the annotations of
    check run id of owner/repo name, in their order without repeats:
    GET /repos/{o}/{r}/check-runs/{id}/annotations, one page of limit (1
    to MaxAnnotations). The identity needs Checks: read (an App; Actions:
    read covers the runs and jobs only). An annotation tied to no file (path
    ".github") names none, and no annotation's message is read: it may quote a
    PR.

func (c *Client) CIStates(ctx context.Context, prs []PRRadar) (map[string]CIState, RateLimit, error)
    CIStates reads the check rollup of each pull request's head (its state
    and counts by state, CIState) by node id. A CI run does not move a pull
    request's updatedAt, so the radar alone cannot tell that it ended, and the
    state alone cannot tell that a further check failed on a head whose rollup
    failed already: the counts can. The rollup is read through the head branch:
    it is the pull request's only while the branch's tip is the HeadRefOid the
    radar read, and a fork's pull request is not asked about (its branch carries
    the fork's checks, not the ones the pull request runs); a pull request
    missing from the result is unknown.

    Each call asks about ciPage pull requests; one GitHub could not answer in
    time is asked once more at half the size (retrySmaller), which the calls
    after it keep. A call that still fails ends the read: the states read before
    it come back with the error. The RateLimit sums Cost over the calls (1 point
    each).

func (c *Client) CommitChecks(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, sha string) ([]Check, error)
    CommitChecks reads the checks of commit sha of owner/repo (a base branch's
    tip, for auto-approval): the latest run of each check (a check run's
    workflow file and name, a commit status apart), normalized as Details'
    CIRollup.Checks, in GitHub's order; empty, never nil, for a commit without
    checks. It reads one page of 100: a check past it is not listed. A missing
    repository or commit is an error matching ErrNotFound; a sha that is no full
    commit id is refused before any call.

func (c *Client) CommitRuns(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, workflow, sha string) ([]WorkflowRun, error)
    CommitRuns lists the runs of the workflow file workflow ("ci.yml") of
    owner/repo at commit sha, of any event (a push to a branch, a dispatch),
    newest first: GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/workflows/{file}/runs filtered
    by head_sha, one page of commitRunsPage. A run of another commit in the
    answer is left out. The identity needs read access to the repository's
    Actions (an App: Actions: read). A workflow that is not a plain file name of
    .github/workflows (ValidWorkflowFile) or a sha that is no full commit id is
    refused before any call.

func (c *Client) Compare(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, base, head string) (CompareStats, error)
    Compare reads GET /repos/{o}/{r}/compare/{base}...{head} with per_page=1:
    total_commits still counts every commit and the first page carries the
    whole (≤300) file list, but only one commit object comes back. A missing
    repository or commit is an error matching ErrNotFound.

func (c *Client) CompareFiles(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, base, head string) ([]FileDelta, error)
    CompareFiles reads the changed files of base...head with their patches
    in one call (GET /repos/{o}/{r}/compare/{base}...{head}, per_page=1:
    the first page carries the whole file list, at most CompareFileLimit files).
    A missing repository or commit is an error matching ErrNotFound.

func (c *Client) CompareFilesStatus(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, base, head string) (string, []FileDelta, error)
    CompareFilesStatus is CompareFiles that also returns the comparison's
    status as GitHub reports it: "ahead" (head descends from base), "identical",
    "behind" (base descends from head) or "diverged". The file list is three-dot
    (head's changes since the merge base), so only "ahead" and "identical" make
    it the difference between base and head.

func (c *Client) ComparePush(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, base, head string) (PushComparison, error)
    ComparePush is CompareFilesStatus that also reads up to ComparePushCommits
    of the commits (per_page=100: the first page still carries the whole file
    list) to tell whether the range brings a merge commit: a push that merged
    the base branch into the PR.

func (c *Client) ConfirmStates(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, numbers []int) (map[int]PRState, []int, error)
    ConfirmStates reads state/merged/mergedAt/closedAt/headRefOid for pull
    requests that disappeared from the radar's OPEN list. Numbers GitHub cannot
    resolve are returned in notFound (callers treat them as UNKNOWN and never
    clean them up); any other error fails the call.

func (c *Client) CreateIssueComment(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, body string) (IssueComment, error)
    CreateIssueComment posts body on the conversation of pull request (or issue)
    number (POST /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/{n}/comments) as the client's identity,
    the request {"body": …} sent as JSON on gh's stdin so no text reaches argv.
    It is marked Mutates, so execx.DryRun only plans it.

func (c *Client) CreateReview(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, commitID, event, body string) (RESTReview, error)
    CreateReview submits a review without inline comments (POST
    /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/reviews) on commitID as the client's identity.
    event is APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES or COMMENT; GitHub wants a body for the
    last two. GitHub counts each reviewer's latest review, so a new APPROVE or
    REQUEST_CHANGES supersedes the identity's earlier verdict. The request goes
    as JSON on gh's stdin, so a failing call logs none of the body. It is marked
    Mutates, so execx.DryRun only plans it.

func (c *Client) DeletePendingReview(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, reviewID int64) error
    DeletePendingReview deletes a review that was never submitted (DELETE
    /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/reviews/{id}) as the client's identity; GitHub
    refuses a submitted review (an *APIError with status 422). It is marked
    Mutates, so execx.DryRun only plans it.

func (c *Client) DeploymentStatuses(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, id int64) ([]string, error)
    DeploymentStatuses lists the states of deployment id's
    statuses, newest first, one page of statusesPage: GET
    /repos/{o}/{r}/deployments/{id}/statuses. A state is success, failure,
    error, inactive (a newer deployment replaced it), in_progress, queued or
    pending. No description is read.

func (c *Client) Deployments(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, environment, etag string) (list []Deployment, newETag string, notModified bool, err error)
    Deployments lists the deployments of environment of owner/repo,
    newest first, one page of deploymentsPage: GET /repos/{o}/{r}/deployments,
    sending etag as If-None-Match ("" = none). A 304 answers notModified with
    no list and etag as it was; else newETag is the answer's ETag. The identity
    needs Deployments: read: without it GitHub answers 403 or 404 (ErrForbidden,
    ErrNotFound). An empty environment, or one or an ETag with a control
    character, is refused before any call.

func (c *Client) Details(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, numbers []int) (map[int]PRDetails, []int, error)
    Details fetches the full view of the given pull requests of owner/repo,
    batched as aliases p<N> (at most 40 per query). Numbers GitHub cannot
    resolve (NOT_FOUND, including a missing repository) are returned in missing
    instead of failing the call; any other error fails it.

func (c *Client) DismissReview(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, reviewID int64, message string) error
    DismissReview dismisses a review (PUT
    /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/reviews/{id}/dismissals) as the client's identity,
    the message as JSON on gh's stdin, so a failing call logs none of it.
    It is marked Mutates, so execx.DryRun only plans it. A missing permission is
    an error matching ErrForbidden; callers report it and do not retry.

func (c *Client) DispatchWorkflow(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, workflow, ref string) error
    DispatchWorkflow starts a run of the workflow file workflow ("ci.yml")
    on ref, a branch of owner/repo, as the client's identity: POST
    /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/workflows/{file}/dispatches. GitHub runs the workflow
    as the branch has it, at its tip, and refuses (HTTP 422) one whose file
    there has no workflow_dispatch trigger; the identity needs the right to
    run workflows (a gh login that can push, an App with Actions: write). The
    branch, which a PR names, goes as JSON on gh's stdin, so a failing call logs
    none of it. A workflow that is not a plain file name of .github/workflows
    (ValidWorkflowFile) or an empty ref is refused before any call. It is marked
    Mutates, so execx.DryRun only plans it.

func (c *Client) DispatchedRuns(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, workflow, sha string) ([]WorkflowRun, error)
    DispatchedRuns lists the runs of the workflow file workflow ("ci.yml") of
    owner/repo that a workflow_dispatch started at commit sha, newest first: GET
    /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/workflows/{file}/runs filtered by event and head_sha,
    one page of dispatchedRunsPage. A run is listed from the moment GitHub
    creates it, queued, before any of its jobs or checks: what a PR's check
    rollup, which leaves a dispatched run's check suite out, cannot show. A run
    of another event or commit in the answer is left out. The identity needs
    read access to the repository's Actions (an App: Actions: read). A workflow
    that is not a plain file name of .github/workflows (ValidWorkflowFile) or a
    sha that is no full commit id is refused before any call.

func (c *Client) EditIssueComment(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, commentID int64, body string) (IssueComment, error)
    EditIssueComment replaces the body of issue comment commentID (PATCH
    /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/comments/{id}) as the client's identity, the body as
    JSON on gh's stdin. GitHub lets only the comment's author edit it; a comment
    someone deleted is an error matching ErrNotFound. It is marked Mutates,
```
