```text
    so execx.DryRun only plans it.

func (c *Client) FileAt(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, path, ref string) ([]byte, error)
    FileAt reads the raw content of path at ref (a commit SHA, a branch
    or a tag): GET /repos/{o}/{r}/contents/{path}?ref={ref} with Accept:
    application/vnd.github.raw. The bytes come back verbatim; an empty file
    is an empty, non-nil slice. path is relative to the repository root
    ("app/models/order.rb"): empty, "." and ".." segments, backslashes and NULs
    are refused before any call, as is a ref that is not a plain ref name or
    SHA (the shape Compare accepts, without ".."). Call it only for paths that
    name files (a diff does): what GitHub answers for a directory is not file
    content. A missing file, ref or repository is an error matching ErrNotFound;
    a file above FileAtLimit an error matching ErrFileTooLarge (checked on the
    bytes received).

func (c *Client) FirstParentChecks(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, sha string) ([]CommitWithChecks, error)
    FirstParentChecks reads commit sha of owner/repo and its first parents,
    FirstParentDepth commits at most, newest first, each with its checks as
    CommitChecks reads them, in one GraphQL query: the CI fix's read of whether
    a check the PR failed passes on its base (internal/engine's ci_fix.go),
    at the base tip the look fetched. The list ends early at a commit with no
    parent. No branch name reaches the command line: the commit goes in the
    query's variables. A missing repository or commit is an error matching
    ErrNotFound; a sha that is no full commit id is refused before any call.

func (c *Client) HeadRuns(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, sha string) ([]WorkflowRun, error)
    HeadRuns lists the runs of every workflow of owner/repo at commit sha,
    of any event, newest first, each with its event, its attempt and its
    workflow's file: GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs filtered by head_sha,
    one page of headRunsPage. A run that started no job is there (its check
    suite holds no check run, so a PR's check rollup cannot show it), and so
    is one still queued. A run of another commit in the answer is left out.
    The identity needs read access to the repository's Actions (an App: Actions:
    read). A sha that is no full commit id is refused before any call.

func (c *Client) IssueComments(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, stop func(PRComment) bool) (comments []PRComment, complete bool, err error)
    IssueComments lists the comments on the conversation of pull request number
    (review bodies and inline comments are not among them: AllReviews and
    ReviewThreads read those), oldest first. It reads issueCommentsPage at a
    time from the newest back, until a page holds a comment that stop (nil:
    none) reports true for, or it reached the first comment, and then
    returns every comment it read; complete is false when it stopped at
    issueCommentsMaxPages pages with older comments, none of which stop was
    asked about, left unread. A missing repository or pull request is an error
    matching ErrNotFound.

func (c *Client) JobLogTail(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, jobID int64, keep int) (log string, cut bool, err error)
    JobLogTail reads the log of job id of owner/repo and keeps its last
    keep bytes (at most execx.MaxOutput), where a failed job's error is:
    GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/jobs/{id}/logs, whose redirect to the log's
    signed URL gh follows, with --allow-escape-sequences (a job whose tools
    colour their output, FORCE_COLOR, has a log gh 2.103 otherwise refuses to
    print, printing its refusal in place of the log). The whole log downloads;
    execx keeps its tail (Cmd.KeepTail). cut reports that the log was longer
    than keep. The log is the output of the PR's code and its tests: data for an
    agent's file, never for an event or a log line. A log GitHub no longer keeps
    (90 days) answers HTTP 404 or 410, and a job id that is no id is refused
    before any call. The identity needs Actions: read.

func (c *Client) ListFiles(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int) (files []string, complete bool, err error)
    ListFiles reads the files a pull request changes: GET
    /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/files, up to three pages of 100. A rename
    contributes both its new and its previous name (moving a file out of src/
    into docs/ still touches src/). complete is false when the third page is
    full: the PR changes more files than were read and a caller must not draw
    conclusions from the list (GitHub itself caps this endpoint at 3000 files).
    A missing repository or pull request is an error matching ErrNotFound.

func (c *Client) Pull(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int) (Pull, error)
    Pull reads pull request number (GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}). A missing
    repository or pull request is an error matching ErrNotFound.

func (c *Client) PullFiles(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int) (files []FileDelta, complete bool, err error)
    PullFiles reads the files a pull request changes with their patches as
    GitHub shows them in the PR's diff (GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/files,
    up to PullFilesMaxPages pages of 100). A file GitHub sends no patch for
    (binary, or too large) is Truncated with an empty Patch. complete is false
    when the last page read was full: the PR changes more files than were read.
    A missing repository or pull request is an error matching ErrNotFound.

func (c *Client) PullSHAs(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int) (base, head string, err error)
    PullSHAs reads a pull request's base and head commits as REST reports them
    (GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}: base.sha, head.sha). A missing repository or
    pull request is an error matching ErrNotFound.

func (c *Client) Radar(ctx context.Context, org string) ([]RepoRadar, RateLimit, error)
    Radar lists every non-archived repository owned by owner (an organization
    or a user) with all its open pull requests, following both the repository
    and the per-repository pull request cursors. It is all-or-nothing:
    any failed page fails the call and no repository list is returned, so the
    caller never mistakes a partial list for closed pull requests. A page GitHub
    could not answer in time is asked once more at half the size (retrySmaller),
    and the pages after it keep that size. The returned RateLimit sums Cost over
    all calls; the other fields are the reading to keep (RateLimit.Tighter:
    the lowest live one). When a later page fails it still carries what the
    earlier pages reported, so the caller can pause on a low budget.

func (c *Client) RecentReviews(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, stop func(Review) bool) (reviews []Review, complete bool, err error)
    RecentReviews lists the reviews of a pull request, oldest first,
    the way IssueComments lists the conversation: reviewsPageSize (100) at a
    time from the newest back, until a page holds a review that stop (nil:
    none) reports true for, or it reached the first review, and then it returns
    every review it read. A reader of what came after a time stops at the first
    review submitted before it, so how many reviews the pull request has does
    not matter. complete is false when it stopped at reviewsMaxPages pages with
    older reviews, none of which stop was asked about, left unread. A missing
    repository or pull request is an error matching ErrNotFound.

func (c *Client) RecentRuns(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, workflow string) ([]WorkflowRun, error)
    RecentRuns lists the newest runs of the workflow file workflow ("ci.yml")
    of owner/repo, of any event and branch, newest first, each with its commit,
    branch and event: GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/workflows/{file}/runs,
    one page of recentRunsPage. The caller picks a branch's runs out of it,
    so no branch name reaches the command line, which a failed call logs.
    The identity needs read access to the repository's Actions (an App: Actions:
    read). A workflow that is not a plain file name of .github/workflows
    (ValidWorkflowFile) is refused before any call.

func (c *Client) ReplyToReviewComment(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, commentID int64, body string) (ReviewCommentReply, error)
    ReplyToReviewComment posts body as a reply in the thread whose first comment
    is commentID (POST /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/comments/{id}/replies) as the
    client's identity, the request {"body": …} sent as JSON on gh's stdin so no
    text reaches argv. GitHub refuses a reply to a reply, so commentID is the
    thread's first comment. It is marked Mutates, so execx.DryRun only plans it.

func (c *Client) RequestReviewers(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, logins []string) error
    RequestReviewers asks the users logins for a review of pull request
    number (POST /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/requested_reviewers) as the client's
    identity, the request {"reviewers": […]} sent as JSON on gh's stdin.
    Each login is a user's (ValidLogin: no App, no team, no "@"); GitHub
    refuses the PR's author and anyone who is no collaborator with HTTP 422.
    Asking someone who reviewed already asks again. It is marked Mutates,
    so execx.DryRun only plans it.

func (c *Client) RequiredChecks(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, branch string) (checks []string, known bool, err error)
    RequiredChecks reads the status checks a pull request into
    branch of owner/repo must pass: the contexts of the rulesets'
    required_status_checks rules (GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rules/branches/{branch},
    readable with read access), else of the classic branch protection
    (.../branches/{branch}/protection/required_status_checks, which usually
    answers 404 without admin access). known is false when GitHub does not say:
    403 (a private repository on a free plan) or 404 from the endpoint that
    would have to answer, logged at Debug (restProbe). Any other failure is an
    error.

func (c *Client) RerunRun(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, runID int64) error
    RerunRun re-runs every job of run id of owner/repo as the client's identity,
    a new attempt of the same run (its run_attempt goes up by one): POST
    /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs/{id}/rerun. GitHub runs it with the run's own
    event, commit and workflow file, and refuses (HTTP 403) an identity that
    may not run workflows (a gh login that cannot push, an App without Actions:
    write). A run id that is no id is refused before any call. It is marked
    Mutates, so execx.DryRun only plans it.

func (c *Client) ReviewAnswers(ctx context.Context, ids []string) (map[string]ReviewAnswer, error)
    ReviewAnswers reads what the inline comments of each review answer
    (ReviewAnswer), by the review's node id (Remark.ID): Details reads it for
    a pull request's last two reviews only (Remark.AnswersKnown), and the poll
    asks for the reviews it needs beyond them (DECISIONS "An author's own inline
    threads are not replies"). A review GitHub does not know is missing from
    the result. Each call asks about answersPage reviews and costs 1 point:
    each review's comments connection is one request of GitHub's count,
    so a hundred reviews are a hundred requests (GitHub's dry run, 2026-10-16:
    1 point for 1, 10, 40 and 100 reviews). A call that fails ends the read:
    the answers read before it come back with the error.

func (c *Client) ReviewComments(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, reviewID int64) ([]ReviewComment, error)
    ReviewComments lists the inline comments of a review (GET
    /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/reviews/{id}/comments), 100 a page until a page is
    not full, at most reviewCommentsMaxPages pages.

func (c *Client) ReviewDismissals(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int) ([]ReviewDismissal, error)
    ReviewDismissals lists the last 100 review dismissals of a pull request,
    oldest first: who dismissed each review, or that GitHub did on a push.
    A missing repository or pull request is an error matching ErrNotFound.

func (c *Client) ReviewREST(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, id int64) (RESTReview, error)
    ReviewREST reads one review over REST (GET
    /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/reviews/{id}) for the "[bot]"-suffixed user.login.
    REST has no review lookup without the pull request number.

func (c *Client) ReviewThreads(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int) ([]Thread, error)
    ReviewThreads lists the inline review threads of a pull request with
    their comments, oldest thread first (at most threadsMaxPages pages of
    threadsPageSize threads, threadCommentsMax comments each, and the newest
    threadTailMax of a longer thread as its Tail, read in one more query per
    threadTailBatch such threads). The diff hunk and the original commit are
    read once per thread, for its first comment only (see ThreadComment),
    so replies cost no hunk. A missing repository or pull request is an error
    matching ErrNotFound.

func (c *Client) Reviews(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int) ([]Review, error)
    Reviews is AllReviews without saying whether the list is complete: for a
    reader that takes the first reviewsMaxPages pages as they are. A caller that
    acts on what the list lacks (a review to dismiss, a review already posted)
    reads AllReviews.

func (c *Client) ReviewsWithMarker(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, marker string) ([]Review, error)
    ReviewsWithMarker returns the last 30 reviews of a pull request whose
    body contains marker, oldest first; an empty marker returns all of them.
    A missing repository or pull request is an error matching ErrNotFound.

func (c *Client) RunJobs(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, runID int64) ([]WorkflowJob, error)
    RunJobs lists the jobs of the latest attempt of run
    id of owner/repo, each with its steps and times: GET
    /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs/{id}/jobs?filter=latest, one page of
    runJobsPage. No log is read (JobLogTail).

func (c *Client) SubmitReview(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, r ReviewRequest) (RESTReview, error)
    SubmitReview posts one review with its inline comments (POST
    /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/reviews) as the client's identity, the request sent
    as JSON on gh's stdin so no review text reaches argv. It checks only what
    the request needs to be well formed (event, a full commit id); GitHub checks
    the rest. It is marked Mutates, so execx.DryRun only plans it.

func (c *Client) UpdatePullTitle(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, title string) (Pull, error)
    UpdatePullTitle sets the title of pull request number (PATCH
    /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}) as the client's identity, the request {"title":
    …} sent as JSON on gh's stdin so the text never reaches argv, and returns
    the pull request as GitHub answered. A title that is blank or spans lines is
    refused before gh runs. It is marked Mutates, so execx.DryRun only plans it.

func (c *Client) UpdateReviewBody(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, reviewID int64, body string) error
    UpdateReviewBody replaces the summary body of a review (PUT
    /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/reviews/{id}) as the client's identity; GitHub
    lets only the review's author edit it, so another login's review fails (an
    error matching ErrForbidden or ErrNotFound). The body, which quotes the PR,
    goes as JSON on gh's stdin, so a failing call logs none of it. It is marked
    Mutates, so execx.DryRun only plans it.

func (c *Client) WithEnv(env map[string]string) *Client
    WithEnv is a client that runs gh as c does with env laid over c's Env:
    the daemon's client of one batch of Actions calls over a token minted for
    it (GH_TOKEN, which gh answers with before GH_CONFIG_DIR's hosts.yml).
    It keeps c's Run, Dir and Meter (the calls count against the identity's
    budget) and has no Reauth: a 401 of that token is no reason to refresh the
    identity's own. c is not changed.

type CommitWithChecks struct {
	SHA    string
	Checks []Check
}
    CommitWithChecks is a commit and its checks, normalized as CommitChecks
    reads them (empty, never nil, for none).

type CompareStats struct {
	Commits   int // total_commits
	Files     int // changed files; -1 when GitHub truncated the file list (CompareFileLimit)
	Additions int // summed over the listed files: a lower bound when Files is -1
	Deletions int // likewise
}
    CompareStats is the size of base...head as GitHub's compare API reports it
    (three-dot: what head adds on top of its merge base with base).

type Deployment struct {
	ID int64
	// SHA is the commit GitHub resolved the deployment's ref to; Ref is the
	// ref as created (a branch, a tag or a sha).
	SHA, Ref    string
	Environment string
	CreatedAt   time.Time
}
    Deployment is a deployment of an environment as Deployments lists it.

type DraftComment struct {
	Path      string `json:"path"`
	Line      int    `json:"line"`
	Side      string `json:"side,omitempty"`
	StartLine int    `json:"start_line,omitempty"`
	StartSide string `json:"start_side,omitempty"`
	Body      string `json:"body"`
}
    DraftComment is one inline comment of a ReviewRequest, anchored on line
    (and, for a multi-line comment, from start_line) of path on side: RIGHT
    for the head's lines (added or context), LEFT for the base's (deleted or
    context).

type FileDelta struct {
	Path         string // the file's path at head
	PreviousPath string // its path at base when renamed or copied; "" otherwise
	Status       string // added | removed | modified | renamed | copied | changed | unchanged
	// Patch holds the file's unified-diff hunks ("@@ ... @@" lines and
	// " ", "+", "-" lines); "" when GitHub left it out.
	Patch string
	// BlobSHA is GitHub's sha of the file: its blob at head (for a removed
	// file, what GitHub lists; "" when GitHub sends null). It tells two
	// listings of a file without a patch apart (an empty or binary file).
	BlobSHA string
	// Truncated: the patch is missing or may be incomplete: GitHub left out
	// a patch too large to send (it still counts the lines), and a
	// comparison listing CompareFileLimit files may have dropped some, so
	// every file of it is marked. A file GitHub lists without a patch and
	// without a line added or removed (an empty or binary file), with its
	// blob, in a listing below the cap is complete: its diff is empty, not
	// missing.
	Truncated bool
	// Lines is what GitHub counts of the file's diff, its additions plus
	// deletions, a patch it left out included (a comparison's file only).
	Lines int
}
    FileDelta is one changed file of a comparison (CompareFiles).

type GraphQLError struct {
	Type    string   // NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, RATE_LIMIT, ...; "" for validation errors
	Message string   //
	Path    []string // e.g. ["repository", "p123"]
}
    GraphQLError is one entry of a GraphQL response's "errors" array.

func (g *GraphQLError) UnmarshalJSON(b []byte) error
    UnmarshalJSON accepts GitHub's mixed string/number paths.

type IssueComment struct {
	ID  int64  // REST comment id
	URL string // html_url
	// AuthorLogin and AuthorType are who GitHub shows wrote it (user.login,
	// an App's with its "[bot]", and user.type); "" when it did not say.
	AuthorLogin, AuthorType string
}
    IssueComment is a comment on the conversation of an issue or a pull request,
    as GitHub answered its creation or edit.

func (c IssueComment) Author() string
    Author is the comment's author in Account form.

type JobStep struct {
	Number      int
	Name        string
	Status      string
	Conclusion  string
	StartedAt   time.Time
	CompletedAt time.Time
}
    JobStep is one step of a job: its number in the job (the log's group order),
    name, status, conclusion once completed, and when it started and completed
    (zero for a step that did not run).

type LatestReview struct {
	State       string // APPROVED | CHANGES_REQUESTED | COMMENTED | DISMISSED | PENDING
	SubmittedAt time.Time
	AuthorLogin string // "" for a ghost
	AuthorType  string
	CommitOid   string // "" when the commit is gone
}
    LatestReview is one entry of a pull request's latestReviews.

type PRComment struct {
	ID          int64  // REST comment id
	URL         string // its link: <pull request>#issuecomment-<id>
	Body        string
	CreatedAt   time.Time
	EditedAt    time.Time // when its body was last edited (lastEditedAt); zero when it never was
	AuthorLogin string    // "" for a ghost
	AuthorType  string    // GraphQL __typename: User | Bot | ...
	// AuthorAssociation is the author's authorAssociation with the
	// repository (OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR, CONTRIBUTOR, NONE, ...), as
	// the reading identity sees it; "" when GitHub did not say.
	AuthorAssociation string
}
    PRComment is a comment on a pull request's conversation (an issue comment)
    as GraphQL reports it. AuthorLogin is the GraphQL login (no "[bot]" suffix);
    compare it with Account and SameAccount.

type PRDetails struct {
	NodeID      string
	Number      int
	Title       string
	URL         string
	AuthorLogin string // "" for a deleted (ghost) author
	AuthorType  string // GraphQL __typename: User, Bot, Mannequin, ...
	// AuthorAssociation is the author's relationship with the repository
	// (OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR, CONTRIBUTOR, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR,
	// FIRST_TIMER, MANNEQUIN, NONE), as of now.
	AuthorAssociation string
	Labels            []string
	// LabelsComplete is true when Labels is every label of the pull request.
	// GitHub returned a single page of at most 100 labels; when the
	// connection reports more, the list is truncated and must not be used to
	// decide that a skip label is absent.
	LabelsComplete    bool
	HeadRefName       string
	BaseRefName       string
	IsCrossRepository bool
	State             string // OPEN | CLOSED | MERGED
	Merged            bool
	MergedAt          time.Time // zero when not merged
	ClosedAt          time.Time // zero when open
	UpdatedAt         time.Time
	IsDraft           bool
	HeadRefOid        string
	BaseRefOid        string   // the base of the PR's last sync, which trails the branch until its next push
	BaseTipOid        string   // the base branch's tip now (baseRef's target); "" when the branch is gone
	Assignees         []string // logins; never nil
	ReviewRequests    []Reviewer
	LatestReviews     []LatestReview // latest review per reviewer; never nil
	// LatestReviewsComplete is true when LatestReviews has every reviewer's
	// latest review (one page of at most 100); when false, the
	// identity's own review may be missing from the list.
	LatestReviewsComplete bool
	// ReviewRequestEvents are the newest review requests of the timeline
	// (at most 10, oldest first); never nil.
	ReviewRequestEvents []ReviewRequestEvent
	// Size of the whole pull request (merge base of BaseRefOid ... HeadRefOid).
	Additions    int
	Deletions    int
	ChangedFiles int
	Commits      int
	// Files are the paths the pull request changes at HeadRefOid, in
	// GitHub's order: one page of at most 100 (a rename lists its new path
	// only); nil when GitHub returned no list. FilesComplete is true when
	// they are every changed file. FilesRenamed is true when one of them is
	// a rename (changeType RENAMED), whose previous path the list leaves
	// out: ListFiles names both.
	Files         []string
	FilesComplete bool
	FilesRenamed  bool
	// CI is the head commit's checks.
	CI CIRollup
	// ActivityAt is the pull request's last activity: the latest of its
	// opening, a description edit, the head commit (its committer date, never
	// past UpdatedAt), a force push, a comment, a review (a reply in a thread
	// is one), a label added or removed, a review requested or removed, ready
	// for review or back to draft, a title rename, a base change, a close, a
	// reopen and a merge (activityTypes; bots count, checks do not). Unlike
	// UpdatedAt it does not move for what a reviewer never sees (a project
	// field, a resolved thread, someone's pending review, a deleted comment).
	// Zero when GitHub returned no timeline.
	ActivityAt time.Time
	// ReviewGate is what GitHub's merge gate says of the reviews; nil when
	// GitHub returned no reviewDecision or latestOpinionatedReviews.
	ReviewGate *ReviewGate
	// MergeState is GitHub's mergeStateStatus of the pull request: BEHIND,
	// BLOCKED, CLEAN, DIRTY, DRAFT, HAS_HOOKS, UNKNOWN (GitHub is still
	// computing it) or UNSTABLE; "" when GitHub did not say.
	MergeState string
	// Remarks are the submitted reviews and issue comments among the
	// activity timeline's last ten items, as it lists them (oldest first),
	// and those of the last two reviews it does not list, each before the
	// first remark submitted after it; nil when GitHub returned no
	// timeline. A reply in a review thread is a review of its own, with no
	// body, which the timeline never lists.
	Remarks []Remark
}
    PRDetails is what the poller stores for a pull request whose radar row
    changed. Logins are GraphQL logins, which never carry the "[bot]" suffix;
    compare them with SameLogin.

type PRRadar struct {
	NodeID      string
	Number      int
	IsDraft     bool
	UpdatedAt   time.Time
	HeadRefOid  string
	BaseRefName string
	// IsCrossRepository is true for a pull request from a fork.
	IsCrossRepository bool
	// CIState is the head commit's check rollup (SUCCESS, FAILURE, PENDING,
	// ERROR, EXPECTED), "" when it has no checks, CICounts its counts by
	// state (a zero Total: unknown), and CIKnown says whether they were
	// read. Radar leaves them unset: the caller fills them from CIStates.
	CIState  string
	CICounts CICounts
	CIKnown  bool
}
    PRRadar is the scalar-only view of an open pull request the poller diffs.

type PRState struct {
	State      string // OPEN | CLOSED | MERGED
	Merged     bool
	MergedAt   time.Time // zero when not merged
	ClosedAt   time.Time // zero when open
	HeadRefOid string
	// MergeCommitOid is the commit the merge put on the base branch: the
	// merge commit, the squash commit or the last rebased commit ("" until
	// merged). Its first parent is the base branch before the merge.
	MergeCommitOid string
}
    PRState is the closed/merged confirmation of one pull request.

type Pull struct {
	Number int
	Title  string
	State  string // open | closed
	URL    string // html_url
	// Author is who opened it, in Account form (REST logins of Apps end
	// in "[bot]"); "" for a deleted account.
	Author string
	// RequestedReviewers are the users asked for a review now (REST
	// logins); GitHub drops a user from the list once they review.
	RequestedReviewers []string
}
    Pull is a pull request as REST reports it (GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}):
    what `magnum comment` checks before it writes.

type PushComparison struct {
	// Status is GitHub's: "ahead", "identical", "behind" or "diverged"
	// (CompareFilesStatus).
	Status string
	// Commits is total_commits: the commits head has since the merge base.
	Commits int
	// Merge: one of those commits has more than one parent, or GitHub
	// listed fewer of them than Commits (more than ComparePushCommits), so
	// a merge cannot be ruled out.
	Merge bool
	// SHAs are the commits GitHub listed, oldest first: all Commits of them
	// unless there are more than ComparePushCommits.
	SHAs  []string
	Files []FileDelta
	// Stats is what Compare reads of the same range (the commits, the
	// files, -1 at GitHub's file cap, and their additions and deletions),
	// so this comparison answers that question too.
	Stats CompareStats
}
    PushComparison is a comparison read with its commits (ComparePush).

type RESTReview struct {
	ID          int64
	NodeID      string
	UserLogin   string
	UserType    string // User | Bot
	State       string
	Body        string
	HTMLURL     string
	CommitID    string
	SubmittedAt time.Time
}
    RESTReview is a review as REST reports it; UserLogin keeps the "[bot]"
    suffix ("talkable[bot]"), which identifies the posting App.

type RateLimit struct {
	Limit     int
	Cost      int // points the call(s) cost
	Remaining int
	Used      int
	ResetAt   time.Time
}
    RateLimit is GitHub's GraphQL rateLimit{} block.

func (r RateLimit) Tighter(o RateLimit, now time.Time) bool
    Tighter reports whether r is the reading to keep over o, the one kept so
    far, at now. A reading whose window has ended (its reset at or before now)
    never is, and any live reading is over one whose window ended (or none). Of
    two live readings the one with less left is, whatever their resets say (of
    equal remaining the later reset): one login can show two windows at once.
    On 2026-10-21 at 11:14Z the radar read 44 points with reset 11:28:11Z while
    a call a second before had read 3,838 with reset 11:29:16Z, and GitHub's
    rate_limit endpoint gave a third reset; a comparison of resets kept the
    3,838, and GitHub refused the next work.

type Remark struct {
	Review bool      // a submitted review (a reply in a thread is one); false: an issue comment
	ID     string    // a review's node id (ReviewAnswers); "" for an issue comment
	At     time.Time // the review's submittedAt, the comment's createdAt
	Author string    // Account form ("app[bot]" for a bot); "" for a ghost
	Bot    bool      // the author is a bot
	// Association is the author's authorAssociation with the repository
	// (OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR, CONTRIBUTOR, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR,
	// FIRST_TIMER, MANNEQUIN, NONE), as the reading identity sees it; ""
	// when GitHub did not say.
	Association string
	// Answers are the authors (Account form) of the threads the review's
	// inline comments reply to: GitHub's replyTo, a thread's first comment.
	// Details reads them for the last two reviews only
	// (AnswersKnown; ReviewAnswers reads them for others, Resolve), with
	// Comments, how many inline comments the review has (of its first ten):
	// a comment that starts a thread answers none, so a review whose
	// comments all start threads has Comments and no Answers, and one with a
	// body alone has neither.
	Answers      []string
	AnswersKnown bool
	Comments     int
}
    Remark is a submitted review or an issue comment on a pull request
    (PRDetails.Remarks): who wrote it and when, never what it says.

func (r *Remark) Resolve(a ReviewAnswer)
    Resolve records what r's inline comments answer: AnswersKnown, Answers and
    Comments.

type RepoRadar struct {
	NodeID        string
	NameWithOwner string    // "talkable/talkable"
	PushedAt      time.Time // zero for an empty repository
	DefaultBranch string    // "" for an empty repository
	PRs           []PRRadar
}
    RepoRadar is one non-archived repository of an organization or user with its
    open pull requests.

type Review struct {
	DatabaseID  int64  // REST review id
	State       string // APPROVED | CHANGES_REQUESTED | COMMENTED | DISMISSED | PENDING
	Body        string
	URL         string
	SubmittedAt time.Time
	EditedAt    time.Time // when its body was last edited (lastEditedAt); zero when it never was
	CommitOid   string    // "" when the commit is gone
	AuthorLogin string    // "" for a ghost
	AuthorType  string    // GraphQL __typename
	// AuthorAssociation is the author's authorAssociation with the
	// repository (OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR, CONTRIBUTOR, NONE, ...), as
	// the reading identity sees it; "" when GitHub did not say.
	AuthorAssociation string
}
    Review is a pull request review as GraphQL reports it. AuthorLogin is the
    GraphQL login (no "[bot]" suffix); ReviewREST has the REST login.

type ReviewAnswer struct {
	Answers  []string // the authors (Account form) of the threads they reply to, each once; nil: none
	Comments int      // how many inline comments the review has (of its first ten)
}
    ReviewAnswer is what a review's inline comments answer (Remark.Answers and
    Remark.Comments), as Details and ReviewAnswers read it.

type ReviewComment struct {
	ID      int64
	Path    string
	Line    int // 0 when GitHub reports none (an outdated comment)
	Body    string
	HTMLURL string
}
    ReviewComment is one inline comment of a review as REST reports it.

type ReviewCommentReply struct {
	ID        int64     // REST comment id
	URL       string    // html_url
	CreatedAt time.Time // created_at
	// AuthorLogin and AuthorType are who GitHub shows wrote it (user.login,
	// an App's with its "[bot]", and user.type); "" when it did not say.
	AuthorLogin, AuthorType string
}
    ReviewCommentReply is a reply posted to a review thread.

func (r ReviewCommentReply) Author() string
    Author is the reply's author in Account form.

type ReviewDismissal struct {
	ReviewID int64  // the dismissed review's REST id; 0 when the review is gone
	Actor    string // who dismissed it, in Account form ("" for a deleted account)
	// ByPush: GitHub dismissed it as stale when Commit was pushed (branch
	// protection's "dismiss stale approvals"), not a person.
	ByPush bool
	Commit string
	At     time.Time
}
    ReviewDismissal is a review's dismissal as a pull request's timeline records
    it (a ReviewDismissedEvent).

type ReviewGate struct {
	// Decision is GitHub's reviewDecision: APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED or
	// REVIEW_REQUIRED; "" (null) when the base branch requires no review.
	Decision string
	// Opinions are latestOpinionatedReviews(writersOnly: true): the latest
	// approval or changes request (DISMISSED once dismissed) of each
	// reviewer with write access, which is what Decision counts; never nil.
	// SubmittedAt is not read.
	Opinions []LatestReview
	// Complete is true when Opinions is every one (one page of at most 100).
	Complete bool
}
    ReviewGate is what GitHub's branch protection makes of a pull request's
    reviews: its reviewDecision and the reviews that decision counts. A GitHub
    App's review never counts, so a PR an App approved can still wait for a
    person's approval.

type ReviewRequest struct {
	CommitID string         `json:"commit_id"`
	Event    string         `json:"event"` // APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES or COMMENT
	Body     string         `json:"body"`
	Comments []DraftComment `json:"comments"`
}
    ReviewRequest is the body of POST /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/reviews:
    one submitted review with all its inline comments (SubmitReview).

type ReviewRequestEvent struct {
	CreatedAt time.Time
	// Actor is the login that asked for the review ("" for a ghost).
	Actor string
	// Reviewer is who was asked: Type User, Bot, Mannequin or Team (Login is
	// then the team's slug). GraphQL logins carry no "[bot]" suffix; compare
	// them with SameLogin.
	Reviewer Reviewer
}
    ReviewRequestEvent is one ReviewRequestedEvent of a pull request's timeline.

type Reviewer struct {
	Type  string // User | Bot | Mannequin | Team
	Login string
}
    Reviewer is a requested reviewer. For Type "Team", Login is the team slug.

type Thread struct {
	ID           string // GraphQL node id (PRRT_…)
	Path         string
	Line         int // 0 when GitHub reports none (an outdated thread); the last line of a multi-line thread
	OriginalLine int // the line the thread was started on (the last line of a multi-line range)
	// StartLine is the first line of a multi-line thread's range, so the
	// thread covers StartLine..Line; 0 for a single-line thread (and when
	// GitHub reports none, as for an outdated thread). OriginalStartLine is
	// the same for the range the thread was started on (OriginalLine is its
	// last line).
	StartLine         int
	OriginalStartLine int
	// DiffSide is the side of the diff the thread is on: "RIGHT" (the
	// new file's lines) or "LEFT" (deleted lines, numbered in the old file).
	DiffSide string
	Resolved bool
	// ResolvedBy is who resolved the thread (Account form: an App's login
	// keeps its "[bot]"); "" for an unresolved thread and for a deleted
	// account.
	ResolvedBy string
	Outdated   bool
	// Comments are oldest first; Comments[0] started the thread and the rest
	// are its replies. At most threadCommentsMax per thread: the first ones.
	Comments []ThreadComment
	// CommentCount is how many comments the thread has, Comments' and
	// beyond. Tail is set only when it has more than Comments holds: its
	// newest comments (at most threadTailMax) that Comments does not hold,
	// oldest first, so that the thread's latest comment is Tail's last;
	// CommentCount minus both is the middle neither holds. Callers that
	// read only Comments see the first threadCommentsMax as before.
	CommentCount int
	Tail         []ThreadComment
}
    Thread is an inline review thread of a pull request as GraphQL reports it.

func (t Thread) AllComments() []ThreadComment
    AllComments are t's comments as ReviewThreads read them, oldest first:
    Comments, then Tail; its last is the thread's latest comment.

type ThreadComment struct {
	ID          int64  // REST comment id (in_reply_to for a reply)
	AuthorLogin string // GraphQL login (no "[bot]" suffix); "" for a ghost
	AuthorType  string // GraphQL __typename: User | Bot
	Body        string
	URL         string
	CreatedAt   time.Time
	ReviewID    int64 // the review the comment belongs to; 0 when unknown
	// AuthorAssociation is the author's authorAssociation with the
	// repository (OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR, CONTRIBUTOR, NONE, ...), as
	// the reading identity sees it; "" when GitHub did not say.
	AuthorAssociation string
	// OriginalCommitOid is the commit the comment was made on, and DiffHunk
	// the diff hunk it was made on (the lines around the commented one, as
	// they were then). Both are set on a thread's first comment (Comments[0])
	// only, the comment that anchors the thread; replies carry neither, and
	// OriginalCommitOid is "" when GitHub reports no commit (it is
	// gone).
	OriginalCommitOid string
	DiffHunk          string
}
    ThreadComment is one comment of a review thread.

type WorkflowJob struct {
	ID          int64
	Name        string
	Status      string
	Conclusion  string
	Steps       []JobStep
	StartedAt   time.Time
	CompletedAt time.Time
	URL         string
	RunAttempt  int
}
    WorkflowJob is a job of a workflow run as RunJobs lists it: its id,
    name, status and conclusion once completed (success, failure, cancelled,
    timed_out, skipped, ...), its steps, when it started and completed (zero
    for neither yet), its page (URL) and the attempt of its run it ran in
    (RunAttempt). An Actions job's id is also its check run's (AnnotationPaths),
    and its name the check run's.

type WorkflowRun struct {
	ID         int64
	Status     string
	Conclusion string
	URL        string
	CreatedAt  time.Time
	HeadSHA    string
	HeadBranch string
	Event      string
	Attempt    int
	Workflow   string
}
    WorkflowRun is a run of a workflow as DispatchedRuns, CommitRuns, RecentRuns
    and HeadRuns list it: its id, its status (queued, waiting, requested,
    pending, in_progress or completed), its conclusion once completed (success,
    failure, cancelled, timed_out, startup_failure, ...), its page and when
    GitHub created it; RecentRuns also says the commit, the branch and the
    event it ran for (the branch is a PR's text: never logged), and HeadRuns
    the commit, the event, the run's attempt (Attempt: its run_attempt, 1, then
    2 after a re-run) and its workflow's file in .github/workflows (Workflow:
    "ci.yml"; "" for a run of no such file, GitHub's own dynamic runs).

func (r WorkflowRun) Done() bool
    Done reports whether r ended (completed, whatever its conclusion).

```

## gitx

```text
package gitx // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/gitx"

Package gitx holds every git operation magnum needs: fetching PR heads into
refs/magnum/pr/N, detached switches and placeholder resets in review slots,
worktree management, dirty/unpushed guards and the diff queries behind "did this
PR touch db/".

All commands go through an execx.Runner (never os/exec), run as `git -C <dir>
...`, and are marked Mutates when they change repository state so --dry-run only
prints them. Inputs that end up as git arguments (refs, branch names, worktree
paths) are validated so a hostile branch name can never be parsed as an option.
The variables that redirect git to another repository (GIT_DIR and friends,
see ScrubbedEnv) are removed from the environment of every command, and none
runs the clone's hooks (see Env).

CONSTANTS

const (
	ConflictBinary       = "CONFLICT (binary)"
	ConflictRenameRename = "CONFLICT (rename/rename)"
)
    The kinds of conflict merge-tree's messages name (MergeMessage.Kind) that a
    staging merge's resolver refuses to resolve: git's stable names for them.

const AnyDir = "**/"
    AnyDir is the prefix of a path that names a file in any directory of
    the repository, its top included ("**/CLAUDE.md"; pathspecs), or, with
    AnyDirTree after the name, every file under a directory of that name in any
    directory ("**/.claude/**").

const AnyDirTree = "/**"
    AnyDirTree follows a name after AnyDir for the files under a directory of
    that name in any directory (pathspecs).

const EvalRefPrefix = "refs/magnum/eval/"
    EvalRefPrefix holds the refs magnum eval fetches pinned commits into,
    apart from refs/magnum/pr/* (the daemon's PR heads), which it never touches.

const GHCredentialHelper = "!gh auth git-credential"
    GHCredentialHelper is the git credential helper that answers with gh's login
    for github.com (`gh auth git-credential`).

const WorktreesSuffix = "__worktrees"
    WorktreesSuffix is appended to a main clone's path to name the directory
    holding magnum's per-PR worktrees (<clone>__worktrees/pr-N). FindClone skips
    such directories.


VARIABLES

var (
	// ErrNotFastForward is MergeFFOnly refusing a branch that does not
	// descend from the checkout's HEAD.
	ErrNotFastForward = errors.New("gitx: not a fast-forward")
	// ErrRebaseConflict is RebaseOnto stopping on a conflict; the rebase
	// was aborted and the branch is as it was.
	ErrRebaseConflict = errors.New("gitx: the rebase conflicts")
	// ErrNotOnBranch is MergeFFOnly finding another branch (or a detached
	// HEAD) checked out than the one it is to fast-forward, right before
	// its merge, or that branch not at the commit it merged right after.
	ErrNotOnBranch = errors.New("gitx: the checkout is not on the branch to fast-forward")
	// ErrBranchExists is SwitchCreate finding the branch it is to create.
	ErrBranchExists = errors.New("gitx: the branch exists")
)
var (
	// ErrNoSuchRef is returned when a ref or revision does not resolve.
	ErrNoSuchRef = errors.New("gitx: no such ref")
	// ErrNoMergeBase is returned when two revisions share no history.
	ErrNoMergeBase = errors.New("gitx: no merge base")
)
var ErrFileTooLarge = errors.New("gitx: file too large")
    ErrFileTooLarge is FileAt's error for a file past execx.MaxOutput.

var ErrNoClone = errors.New("gitx: no clone of the repository")
    ErrNoClone is returned by FindClone when no directory under the clone root
    is a git clone of the repository.

var ErrNotDescendant = errors.New("gitx: the commit does not descend from the remote head")
    ErrNotDescendant is PushLease's refusal of a commit that does not descend
    from the remote head it expects: the push would rewrite history.

var ErrTreeTooLarge = errors.New("gitx: tree too large to list")
    ErrTreeTooLarge is Symlinks' error for a tree, and ChangedNames' for a list
    of names, whose listing passes execx.MaxOutput: a link or a path it would
    leave out may be one that matters.


FUNCTIONS

func Env(mutates bool) map[string]string
    Env returns the environment gitx sets on its git commands: no credential
    prompt, the clone's hooks off (core.hooksPath=/dev/null) and, for a command
    that does not mutate, no optional locks. Code that runs git outside gitx
    should put it in execx.Cmd.Env, with ScrubbedEnv in Unset.

func EnvConfig(environ []string, key string) (string, bool)
    EnvConfig is the value environ's GIT_CONFIG_COUNT pairs give key,
    as git reads them (the first GIT_CONFIG_COUNT pairs of GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>
    and GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<n>, the last pair of the key winning, the key compared
    without case, as git compares a key without a subsection); ok is false
    when no pair sets it. gitx replaces the pairs with its own (hooksOff),
    so a command that must keep one of the caller's, as `magnum fix-sync` keeps
    a fixer App pane's commit.gpgsign, reads it here and passes it with -c.

func GitHubHTTPSURL(owner, repo string) string
    GitHubHTTPSURL is the https clone URL of github.com/<owner>/<repo>.

func GitHubSSHURL(owner, repo string) string
    GitHubSSHURL is the scp-like SSH clone URL of github.com/<owner>/<repo>.

func IsRepo(dir string) bool
    IsRepo reports whether dir has a .git entry (a directory for a clone,
    a file for a linked worktree or submodule). It never runs git.

func IsSSHURL(raw string) bool
    IsSSHURL reports whether a remote URL goes over SSH: an ssh:// (or
    git+ssh://) URL, or git's scp-like [user@]host:path form, which git
    recognises only when no slash comes before the first colon (so a local path
    is never one).

func NetworkRemote(originURL string, https bool) (opts []string, target string)
    NetworkRemote is how a network command (fetch, ls-remote) reaches a
    clone whose origin is originURL. With https set, a github.com SSH origin
    is reached at its HTTPS URL with gh as the only credential helper:
    opts go before the subcommand and target replaces "origin", so a locked or
    empty ssh-agent does not matter. Anything else (https off, an HTTPS origin,
    an SSH origin on another host, an unknown origin) names origin itself with
    no options.

func OriginMatches(remoteURL, owner, name string) bool
    OriginMatches reports whether remoteURL is a GitHub remote of owner/name,
    as FindClone and the per-PR clones of slots require: https://github.com/o/r,
    git@github.com:o/r, ssh://git@github.com/o/r and the other forms
    ParseRemote reads, with or without .git or a trailing slash. The host
    must be exactly github.com, so github.com in a path or a longer host name
    (evilgithub.com, notgithub.com) does not match; owner and name are compared
    case-insensitively, as GitHub does.

func PRRef(number int) string
    PRRef is the local ref a PR head is fetched into.

func ScrubbedEnv() []string
    ScrubbedEnv returns the environment variables gitx removes from every git
    command it runs. Code that runs git outside gitx should put the same list in
    execx.Cmd.Unset.

func ShellSafeRef(ref string) bool
    ShellSafeRef reports whether ref is a branch name magnum lets reach a
    command line an agent runs (the judge prompts' `git diff origin/<base>…`
    when the merge base is unknown): only letters, digits, '.', '_', '/' and
    '-', no "..", no leading '-'. Git allows '$', '|', '&' and parentheses in
    branch names, and anyone who can push may name a base branch.


TYPES

type Client struct {

	// HTTPSFetch makes fetches from a clone whose origin is a github.com SSH
	// URL go over HTTPS with gh as the credential helper (see fetchArgs).
	// The app turns it on; the zero value keeps fetching from origin.
	HTTPSFetch bool

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Client runs git through an execx.Runner. It is safe for concurrent use;
    fetches into the same clone are serialized because concurrent fetches of
    the same ref (two PRs sharing a base branch) fail with "cannot lock ref".
    The lock only covers this process; a fetch that still loses the race to
    another process (the CLI next to the daemon) is retried once.

func New(r execx.Runner) *Client
    New returns a Client that executes commands with r.

func (c *Client) AbortOperation(ctx context.Context, dir, op string) error
    AbortOperation ends op, the operation dir is in the middle of as InProgress
    names it ("rebase", "merge", "cherry-pick" or "revert"), with `git <op>
    --abort`: HEAD, the index and the work tree go back to where it started.
    Callers ask InProgress first; with nothing in progress git fails, and any
    other op is an error before git runs.

func (c *Client) BlameLine(ctx context.Context, dir, rev, path string, line int) (sha string, at time.Time, err error)
    BlameLine is the commit that last wrote line (from 1) of path at rev, and
    when it was authored (`git blame --porcelain -L <line>,<line> rev -- path`;
    path is relative to dir, the top of a work tree: blame takes no pathspec
    magic). A line the file does not have at rev is an error.

func (c *Client) Blobs(ctx context.Context, dir, rev string, paths []string) (map[string]string, error)
    Blobs reads the files paths name in rev's tree (each from the top,
    as git stores it) from the object store, in one `git cat-file --batch`
    of "<rev>:<path>": each regular file or link found with its content (a
    link's is its text); a path rev lacks, or names a directory, is left out.
    A path with a line feed cannot be asked and fails, and so does an output
    past execx.MaxOutput (ErrTreeTooLarge). rev must name a commit.

func (c *Client) BranchDelete(ctx context.Context, mainClone, branch string, force bool) error
    BranchDelete deletes a local branch (force = -D, otherwise -d). A branch
    that does not exist counts as deleted; git's refusal to delete an existing
    branch (checked out, unmerged) is returned.

func (c *Client) BranchPR(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) (number int, ok bool, err error)
    BranchPR returns the PR number recorded in `git config branch.<b>.pr` (the
    convention of Bohdan's `pull` helper; a PR URL is accepted too). ok is false
    when the key is not set.

func (c *Client) BranchesUnder(ctx context.Context, repo, prefix string) ([]string, error)
    BranchesUnder lists the local branches of repo under prefix, one or more
    path segments ending in "/" ("learn/"), by their short names, sorted:
    the skill editor's orphan cleanup finds the branches no proposal holds.

func (c *Client) ChangedBetween(ctx context.Context, dir, from, to string) ([]string, error)
    ChangedBetween lists the files whose content differs between the commits
    from and to (git diff --name-only from to: the two trees, whatever the
    history between them), a rename as a deletion plus an addition. Unlike
    ChangedPaths it names a file an earlier head changed and a rewritten branch
    left as the base has it. nil when the trees are the same.

func (c *Client) ChangedFiles(ctx context.Context, dir, base, head string) ([]FileChange, error)
    ChangedFiles lists the files head changed relative to its merge base with
    base, each with its status (git diff --name-status base...head; a rename as
    a deletion plus an addition), in git's order; nil when head changes nothing.
    Unlike DiffLines it reads no patch, so a change of any size fits.

func (c *Client) ChangedNames(ctx context.Context, dir, base, head string) ([]string, error)
    ChangedNames lists every file head changes since its merge base with
    base (git diff --name-only base...head, with no pathspec), a rename as a
    deletion plus an addition, for a caller that matches the paths itself:
    git's icase pathspec folds ASCII only, so a literal .agents/skills misses
    a commit's .agents/ſkills/x/SKILL.md, which a case-insensitive filesystem
    (macOS's) writes into .agents/skills/x/. A listing past execx.MaxOutput
    fails (ErrTreeTooLarge): a path it would leave out may be one that matters.
    nil when nothing changed.

func (c *Client) ChangedPaths(ctx context.Context, dir, base, head string, pathspecs ...string) ([]string, error)
    ChangedPaths lists the files head changed relative to its merge base with
    base (git diff base...head), optionally limited to pathspecs such as "db/".
    Renames are reported as a deletion plus an addition so a move out of a
    watched directory still shows up. The result is nil when nothing matches.

func (c *Client) ChangedUnder(ctx context.Context, dir, base, head string, paths ...string) ([]string, error)
    ChangedUnder is ChangedPaths limited to the files paths name, each relative
    to the repository's top in any ASCII case (pathspecs: a directory or a file
    taken literally, or "**/<name>" in any directory): what head changes there
    since its merge base with base, whatever base did since. One git diff;
    nil when head leaves them all alone.

func (c *Client) Clone(ctx context.Context, repoURL, dest string) error
    Clone clones url into the absolute path dest (parents are created). URLs
    with embedded credentials are refused; authentication comes from the user's
    git credential helper or ssh agent.

func (c *Client) CloneWith(ctx context.Context, repoURL, dest string, opt CloneOptions) error
    CloneWith is Clone with options (see CloneOptions).

func (c *Client) CommitAll(ctx context.Context, dir, message string, paths ...string) (string, error)
    CommitAll commits paths of the work tree at dir (their changes, additions
    and deletions; nothing else, whatever else is dirty) on its current branch
    with message, unsigned (commit.gpgsign=false whatever the repository says),
    and returns the new commit's id. Nothing to commit is an error.

func (c *Client) CommitTime(ctx context.Context, dir, rev string) (time.Time, error)
    CommitTime is the committer time of revision rev in the repository at dir
    (git show -s --format=%ct, to the second).

func (c *Client) CommitTree(ctx context.Context, dir, tree string, parents []string, message string, who Signature) (string, error)
    CommitTree writes the commit of tree with parents (the first is the
    branch it goes on: a merge's are the PR's head, then the base's tip) and
    message, by who as author and committer whatever the environment or the
    repository says, unsigned (commit.gpgsign=false), and returns its id:
    `git commit-tree <tree> -p <parent>... -F -`, the message on stdin. No ref,
    index or work tree changes. A tree or parent that is no revision, no parent,
    or a signature with an empty, multi-line or bracketed part is refused before
    git runs.

func (c *Client) CommitsAfter(ctx context.Context, dir, from, to string, firstParent bool) ([]ListedCommit, error)
    CommitsAfter lists the commits of to that from lacks (`git rev-list
    --parents from..to`), newest first, each with its parents. With firstParent,
    only to's first-parent chain (--first-parent): a merge is then one commit,
    without the commits it brought in, as GitHub's "Update branch" adds one
    merge to a PR's branch. Nothing when from has every commit of to.

func (c *Client) CurrentBranch(ctx context.Context, repo string) (string, error)
    CurrentBranch is the branch checked out in repo, "" when its HEAD is
    detached (a rebase in progress included).

func (c *Client) DiffHead(ctx context.Context, dir string, paths ...string) ([]byte, error)
    DiffHead is the binary patch of paths of the work tree at dir against
    HEAD (`git diff --binary HEAD`, each path taken literally from the top):
    each path as the work tree has it, which `git apply` puts back in a work
    tree as HEAD has them. A version staged and then changed in the work tree
    is not in it. Its prefixes are a/ and b/ whatever the config says, and it
    runs no external diff or textconv. A patch over execx.MaxOutput is an error,
    never part of one. It is read-only and does not take the index lock.

func (c *Client) DiffLines(ctx context.Context, dir, base, head string, skip ...string) ([]FileLines, error)
    DiffLines is the diff head made relative to its merge base with base,
    file by file in git's order, with its hunks' places in head's files and
    without context lines (git diff -U0 base...head; a rename as a deletion plus
    an addition; none of the user's settings that change it: an external diff,
    textconv, path prefixes, quoted non-ASCII names), leaving out the paths skip
    names (relative to the top, taken literally). nil when nothing is left.

func (c *Client) DiffStat(ctx context.Context, dir, base, head string) ([]FileStat, error)
    DiffStat counts the lines of each file head changed relative to its merge
    base with base (git diff --numstat base...head; a rename as a deletion plus
    an addition, no external diff or textconv), in git's order; nil when head
    changes nothing.

func (c *Client) DifferingPaths(ctx context.Context, dir, a, b string, paths ...string) ([]string, error)
    DifferingPaths is ChangedBetween limited to paths (each relative to the
    repository's top, a directory or a file, taken literally): which of them
    differ between the commits a and b, in content, mode or presence, sorted;
    nil when both have them alike. It compares the two trees alone, so a merge
    that carries the base's files as the base has them shows none of them
    against the base's tip. At least one path, none empty.

func (c *Client) DirFiles(ctx context.Context, dir, rev string, dirs ...string) ([]string, error)
    DirFiles lists the files directly in each of dirs (relative to the top,
    "." for the top itself) at rev, never a directory, a submodule or a file
    of a subdirectory: one `git ls-tree` of rev's tree, each file as its path
    from the top, in git's order. nil when there are none or dirs is empty.
    rev must name a commit.

func (c *Client) DirtyPaths(ctx context.Context, dir string, paths ...string) ([]string, error)
    DirtyPaths returns the paths among paths (relative to the top of the work
    tree at dir) that differ from HEAD or are untracked, sorted, nil when none;
    ignored files are not listed. At least one path.

func (c *Client) FastForward(ctx context.Context, dir, to string) error
    FastForward moves the branch checked out in the work tree at dir to to,
    a commit ahead of it (`git merge --ff-only --no-autostash <to>`): a factory
    task's branch with no commit of its own, to a fresh origin/<base>. The work
    tree's changes the move does not touch are carried, staged ones staged; one
    it would overwrite makes git refuse, which is an error, and nothing moves,
    as does a file git does not track at a path the move writes, an ignored
    one included (--no-overwrite-ignore; MergeFFOnly, the skill editor's, keeps
    git's default). A to that HEAD is not an ancestor of is ErrNotFastForward
    and a detached HEAD ErrNotOnBranch, nothing moved; to at HEAD is a no-op.

func (c *Client) FetchBranch(ctx context.Context, mainClone, base string) error
    FetchBranch updates refs/remotes/origin/<base> in mainClone from the remote.

func (c *Client) FetchCommit(ctx context.Context, mainClone, sha string, number int) error
    FetchCommit makes sha (a full commit id) present in mainClone for a magnum
    eval replay, or for a post-merge round whose clone lacks the PR's merge
    commit. A commit already there costs one rev-parse. Otherwise it fetches the
    commit by id into refs/magnum/eval/<sha>, and when the server refuses that,
    PR number's head into refs/magnum/eval/pr-<number> (the commit is there
    unless the PR was force-pushed past it). It never writes refs/magnum/pr/*,
    so the daemon's checkouts are unaffected.

func (c *Client) FetchPR(ctx context.Context, mainClone string, number int) (string, error)
    FetchPR fetches the PR head (refs/pull/N/head) into refs/magnum/pr/N
    of mainClone, forcing the update so a force-pushed PR moves the ref,
    and returns the commit sha it now points to. Under --dry-run the fetch is
    only planned, so the final lookup returns whatever refs/magnum/pr/N already
    holds (the sha of an earlier real fetch, possibly stale) or fails with
    ErrNoSuchRef.

func (c *Client) FileAt(ctx context.Context, dir, rev, file string) (string, error)
    FileAt is the content of file (a clean path from the top) as rev has it:
    `git cat-file blob <rev>:<file>`, the object store's bytes without
    textconv or filters, never the work tree's. A file past execx.MaxOutput is
    ErrFileTooLarge; a path rev lacks fails. rev must name a commit.

func (c *Client) FileDiff(ctx context.Context, dir, base, head, path string) (string, error)
    FileDiff returns the unified diff of one file from base to head (git diff
    base head -- path; path is relative to the repository's top and taken
    literally) as GitHub shows a pull request's patch: three lines of context,
    hunks never merged across a gap, and none of the user's settings that change
    the hunks (an external diff, textconv, a context size). "" when the file did
    not change; a binary file has a header and no hunks.

func (c *Client) FileLog(ctx context.Context, dir, rev, path string, n int) ([]Commit, error)
    FileLog returns the last n commits reachable from rev that changed path,
    newest first (git log -n <n> <rev> -- path, with git's default history
    simplification: a merge shows only when it changed the file against every
    parent; path is relative to the repository's top and taken literally).
    A path rev never had has no commits.

func (c *Client) FindClone(ctx context.Context, cloneRoot, owner, name string) (string, error)
    FindClone returns the main clone of github.com/<owner>/<name> under
    cloneRoot (an absolute, already expanded directory). Candidates are tried
    in order: <root>/<name>, <root>/<owner>-<name>, <root>/<owner>_<name>; the
    first that is a git repository whose `git remote get-url origin` is a GitHub
    URL of <owner>/<name> wins (see OriginMatches; owner and name are compared
    case-insensitively). Otherwise every directory directly under the root (not
    recursively; names containing "__worktrees" are skipped) is checked the same
    way, in name order. A directory is asked once however many names reach it
    (symlinks, case-insensitive filesystems). A directory without a .git entry
    is never handed to git, so a same-named folder that is not a repository
    costs no subprocess and no warning.

    Origins are cached per directory until its git config changes, so repeated
    lookups cost a directory listing and a few stats. ErrNoClone (wrapped) means
    nothing matched; any other error is an unreadable root.

func (c *Client) FirstParentIdentities(ctx context.Context, dir, from, to string) ([]CommitIdentity, error)
    FirstParentIdentities lists the commits of to that from lacks on to's
    first-parent chain (`git log --first-parent ^from to`), newest first,
    each with its parents and its author's and committer's emails (%ae and %ce,
    which ignore .mailmap: the commit's own words). A merge is one entry,
    without the commits it brought in. Nothing when from has every commit of to.
    `magnum push` checks that each is the fixer's.

func (c *Client) HasFile(ctx context.Context, dir, rev, file string) (bool, error)
    HasFile reports whether rev has file (a clean path from the top) as a file,
    the existence probe FileAt is not: `git ls-tree --full-tree <rev> --
    <file>` lists the path's entry, and a path rev lacks (one on disk only,
    one nowhere, a directory's) lists none, a plain no that logs nothing,
    where `cat-file blob` fails and warns. A revision dir lacks is an error.
    rev must name a commit.

func (c *Client) InProgress(ctx context.Context, repo string) (string, error)
    InProgress names the operation repo is in the middle of: "rebase", "merge",
    "cherry-pick", "revert", or "" for none.

func (c *Client) IsAncestor(ctx context.Context, dir, ancestor, rev string) (bool, error)
    IsAncestor reports whether ancestor is in rev's history (`git merge-base
    --is-ancestor`; a commit is its own ancestor). Its exit 1 is the answer no,
    logged at Debug; any other failure, a revision dir lacks among them (exit
    128), is an error, never a no.

func (c *Client) LsRemote(ctx context.Context, dir string, timeout time.Duration, patterns ...string) (string, error)
    LsRemote runs `git ls-remote <origin> patterns...` in dir, reaching origin
    the way fetches do (NetworkRemote with HTTPSFetch), and returns its output.
    A failure is an expected answer (logged at Debug): callers probe with it.

func (c *Client) LsRemoteGitHub(ctx context.Context, dir, owner, repo string, timeout time.Duration, patterns ...string) (string, error)
    LsRemoteGitHub is LsRemoteVia of github.com/<owner>/<repo> over HTTPS
    (GitHubHTTPSURL).

func (c *Client) LsRemoteVia(ctx context.Context, dir, url string, timeout time.Duration, patterns ...string) (string, error)
    LsRemoteVia runs `git ls-remote <url> patterns...` in dir with gh as
    git's only credential helper, and returns its output; `magnum push` reads
    a branch's head on GitHub so, whatever form origin has. A failure is an
    expected answer (logged at Debug).

func (c *Client) Mentions(ctx context.Context, dir, rev string, words []string, pathspecs ...string) (map[string]map[string]int, error)
    Mentions returns where the files of rev name each of words: for each word,
    the files that pathspecs match (pathspec magic allowed) whose text contains
    it, with the number of its occurrences in each. It is one `git grep -o -F`
    on rev's tree, which reads the object store only: a file the work tree
    or the index has in another version, or only there, is never read. Words
    are taken literally and in their case, one line each; where two overlap,
    an occurrence counts for the one that starts first, then for the longer
    (git grep -o). Binary files are left out. A word no file names is absent;
    nil when none is named or words is empty. rev must name a commit (no range,
    no "<rev>:<path>").

func (c *Client) MergeBase(ctx context.Context, dir, a, b string) (string, error)
    MergeBase returns the best common ancestor of a and b, or ErrNoMergeBase.
    It is a question: a non-zero exit (1: no common ancestor; 128: a revision
    the checkout has not fetched yet, as a restart check asks about a head the
    poller saw before the checkout did) is an answer the caller reads from the
    error, so the command runs as a probe and a failure logs at Debug.

func (c *Client) MergeConflicts(ctx context.Context, dir, head, base string) ([]string, error)
    MergeConflicts says where merging base into head would conflict, as GitHub's
    CONFLICTING does, without merging: the conflicting paths of `git merge-tree
    --write-tree head base` (git 2.40 or later), sorted, nil for a clean merge.
    As ReplayConflicts, it writes the merge's objects and no ref, index or
    work tree, so dir, any work tree of the repository that has both commits,
    is left exactly as it was. An error for revisions git does not know,
    histories without a common commit and an answer it cannot read.

func (c *Client) MergeFFOnly(ctx context.Context, repo, base, branch string) error
    MergeFFOnly fast-forwards base, the branch checked out in repo, to branch:
    ErrNotFastForward, with nothing changed, when branch does not descend from
    HEAD. git merges into whatever HEAD is, so HEAD must be refs/heads/<base>
    right before the merge (symbolic-ref; ErrNotOnBranch, with nothing changed,
    for another branch or a detached HEAD), and refs/heads/<base> must be
    branch's commit right after it (ErrNotOnBranch too: a checkout that switched
    branch in between had the other branch moved). Local changes the move would
    overwrite make git refuse, which is an error too; the others stay as they
    are, staged ones staged: the merge never stashes them (--no-autostash,
    whatever merge.autoStash says, as RebaseOnto).

func (c *Client) MergeNoCommit(ctx context.Context, dir, rev string, who Signature) ([]string, error)
    MergeNoCommit merges rev into the work tree at dir and stops before
    it commits (`git merge --no-commit --no-ff`): HEAD stays where it is,
    the merge is in progress (MERGE_HEAD), and the conflicted paths, sorted,
    are what it returns (nil when the merge applied cleanly). who stands in
    for the committer git asks for; nothing is committed. Rerere is off,
    so no recorded resolution resolves a path in the agent's place.

func (c *Client) MergeTree(ctx context.Context, dir, head, base string) (tree string, conflicts []string, err error)
    MergeTree is MergeConflicts with the merge itself: the id of the tree `git
    merge-tree --write-tree head base` writes for a clean merge (no conflicts),
    else no tree and the conflicting paths, sorted. It writes the merge's
    objects and no ref, index or work tree, so CommitTree can make the merge
    commit of that tree with nothing checked out.

func (c *Client) MergeTreeMessages(ctx context.Context, dir, a, b string) ([]MergeMessage, error)
    MergeTreeMessages lists the messages of merging b into a, in git's
    order (`git merge-tree --write-tree -z --name-only a b`, read from its
    informational messages section); none for a clean merge. It writes objects
    alone: no ref, index or work tree.

func (c *Client) MergeTreeWrite(ctx context.Context, dir, a, b string) (tree string, conflicts []string, err error)
    MergeTreeWrite is `git merge-tree --write-tree a b` with both its answers:
    the merged tree (conflict markers in its conflicted files) and the
    conflicted paths, sorted, nil for a clean merge. It writes objects alone:
    no ref, index or work tree.

func (c *Client) ModifiedPaths(ctx context.Context, dir, base, head string) ([]string, error)
    ModifiedPaths is ChangedPaths without the files head adds: the paths that
    exist at the merge base and that head modifies, deletes or changes the type
    of (a rename counts as the deletion of its old path), whose history the base
    holds.

func (c *Client) NotTracked(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]string, error)
    NotTracked lists what git tracks none of in the work tree whose top is dir
    (`git ls-files --others --directory`): untracked and ignored files alike,
    and a directory git tracks nothing in as one entry ending in "/", relative
    to the top, in git's order. A switch that writes one of their paths loses
    it, which the factory reads before it switches a copy. It is read-only and
    does not take the index lock.

func (c *Client) OwnDiffID(ctx context.Context, dir, base, head string) (string, error)
    OwnDiffID is the verbatim patch id of head's own diff against base:
    the change from their merge base to head (`git diff-tree --patch --unified=0
    --full-index <merge base> head | git patch-id --verbatim`), the PR as
    GitHub's base...head shows it. With no context lines, a merge of the base
    into head that changes other lines, near the PR's own or not, leaves the
    id as it was, as line numbers and the order of files do not count; one that
    changes a line of the PR's own (a conflict resolved, a change slipped into
    the merge, its indentation or the spaces inside it, which --stable would not
    see and YAML, Haml, Python or a Makefile read) or brings a branch the base
    lacks changes it. A binary file counts by its blob ids. "" when head changes
    nothing against base; ErrNoMergeBase for histories without a common commit.

func (c *Client) OwnerUsesSSH(ctx context.Context, cloneRoot, owner string) (bool, error)
    OwnerUsesSSH reports whether a clone directly under cloneRoot of any
    github.com/<owner>/* repository has an SSH origin. Directories are read as
    FindClone reads them (".git" required, "__worktrees" skipped, origins cached
    until the clone's config changes), so right after a FindClone miss over the
    same root it costs no subprocess. A missing root is (false, nil).

func (c *Client) Parents(ctx context.Context, dir, rev string) ([]string, error)
    Parents lists the parents of commit rev, in order.

func (c *Client) PatchID(ctx context.Context, dir, rev string) (string, error)
    PatchID is the stable patch id of commit rev's change from its first
    parent (`git diff-tree --patch --unified=0 rev | git patch-id --stable`):
    with no context lines, a commit rebased onto a branch that changed lines
    near its own keeps the id it had, and a commit that changes anything else
    has another. An error for a commit with no change to hash.

func (c *Client) PathsDiff(ctx context.Context, dir, a, b string, paths ...string) (string, error)
    PathsDiff is the diff from a to b in paths (each taken literally from the
    top): `git diff a b -- paths`, with no external diff, textconv or color;
    "" when the two commits do not differ there.

func (c *Client) PushLease(ctx context.Context, dir, sha, branch, expect string) error
    PushLease pushes commit sha (a full id) to origin's refs/heads/<branch>
    from dir with a lease: `git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<branch>:
    <expect> origin <sha>:refs/heads/<branch>`, reaching origin the way
    fetches do (NetworkRemote with HTTPSFetch). expect is the remote head the
    caller recorded, "" for a new branch, which must not exist on origin then.
    The remote branch moved since (or a branch that exists for an expect of
    "") fails the push and leaves it as it is. A sha that does not descend from
    expect is refused before anything is pushed (ErrNotDescendant), so the
    lease never rewrites history; an expect dir does not have is an error too,
    never a push.

func (c *Client) PushLeaseGitHub(ctx context.Context, dir, owner, repo, sha, branch, expect string) error
    PushLeaseGitHub is PushLeaseVia to github.com/<owner>/<repo> over HTTPS
    (GitHubHTTPSURL).

func (c *Client) PushLeaseGitHubAs(ctx context.Context, dir, owner, repo, sha, branch, expect string, env map[string]string) error
    PushLeaseGitHubAs is PushLeaseViaAs to github.com/<owner>/<repo> over HTTPS
    (GitHubHTTPSURL).

func (c *Client) PushLeaseVia(ctx context.Context, dir, url, sha, branch, expect string) error
    PushLeaseVia is PushLease to url instead of origin, with gh as git's only
    credential helper (`git -c credential.helper= -c credential.helper='!gh auth
    git-credential' push --force-with-lease= refs/heads/<branch>:<expect> <url>
    <sha>:refs/heads/<branch>`), with PushLease's guards: never a bare --force
    or a + refspec, and a sha that does not descend from expect refused before
    anything is pushed (ErrNotDescendant). `magnum push` pushes a fixer App's
    commits so, as the App, whatever form origin has and whichever helper the
    operator's config names.

func (c *Client) PushLeaseViaAs(ctx context.Context, dir, url, sha, branch, expect string, env map[string]string) error
    PushLeaseViaAs is PushLeaseVia with env over the push, never over a key
    of gitx's own: the daemon's push as a fixer App, whose GH_CONFIG_DIR (with
    GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN blanked, identity.Source.Env) holds the token
    gh answers git with, or whose GH_TOKEN is the daemon's own push token
    (identity.App.DaemonPushEnv), which gh answers with first. No value of env
    is ever logged.

func (c *Client) RebaseOnto(ctx context.Context, dir, onto, upstream string) error
    RebaseOnto replays the commits of the branch checked out at dir that
    follow upstream onto onto, unsigned (`git rebase --onto onto upstream`):
    only those, so a commit onto no longer has (one the operator dropped from
    master after the branch was cut on it) does not come back with them.
    A rebase that stops (a conflict) is aborted, so the branch and its work tree
    are as they were, and the error is ErrRebaseConflict.

func (c *Client) RemergeDiff(ctx context.Context, dir, merge string, paths ...string) (string, error)
    RemergeDiff is how merge, a merge commit, resolved its conflicts in paths
    (each taken literally from the top): `git show --remerge-diff` of it, the
    diff from git's own merge of its parents, conflict markers and all, to the
    merge as it was committed, with no commit header, no external diff, textconv
    or color. "" when the merge resolved no conflict there and changed nothing
    there that git's own merge would not have. The magnum daemon shows it to the
    operator before the y that pushes a merge it holds (engine.HeldMerge).

func (c *Client) RemoteURL(ctx context.Context, dir string) (string, error)
    RemoteURL returns the URL of origin in dir. Credentials embedded in the URL
    are stripped (see stripUserinfo) so the value is safe to log.

func (c *Client) ReplayConflicts(ctx context.Context, dir, onto, rev string) ([]string, error)
    ReplayConflicts says where the change commit rev makes from its first
    parent would conflict if replayed onto onto, as RebaseOnto would replay it,
    without replaying it: the conflicting paths, sorted, nil when it applies.
    It is `git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<rev>^ onto rev` (git 2.40
    or later), which writes the merge's objects and no ref, index or work tree,
    so dir, any work tree of the repository, is left exactly as it was and a
    conflict leaves nothing to abort. An error for a commit with no parent,
    for revisions git does not know and for an answer it cannot read.

func (c *Client) ReplayOnto(ctx context.Context, dir, onto, from string, config ...string) ([]string, error)
    ReplayOnto replays the commits from..HEAD of the checkout at dir (a detached
    HEAD, or a branch, which then moves) onto onto (`git rebase --onto onto
    from`): only those, as RebaseOnto, and no other branch moves with them
    (--no-update-refs). Unlike RebaseOnto's, the commits are signed as the
    repository's config says, with config laid over it ("key=value" settings
    passed as `git -c`, which no file keeps): the fixer, whose commits these
    are, made them with that config (`magnum fix-sync`, which passes a fixer App
    pane's commit.gpgsign=false). A replay that stops (a conflict) is aborted,
    so HEAD, the index and the work tree are as they were; the error is then
    ErrRebaseConflict, with the paths that conflicted in the commit it stopped
    at, sorted.

func (c *Client) ResetPlaceholder(ctx context.Context, dir, branch, base string) error
    ResetPlaceholder points the slot's placeholder branch at origin/<base>
    without upstream tracking, discarding tracked changes. It is idempotent.
    `switch -C --no-track` only stops git from creating tracking; a branch
    that already tracks something keeps it, so an existing upstream is unset
    afterwards (placeholders must not follow, or push to, a remote branch).

func (c *Client) RestoreFrom(ctx context.Context, dir, rev string, paths ...string) error
    RestoreFrom sets paths (relative to the top of the work tree at dir) in
    the work tree to their content at rev, and removes a path rev does not have
    (`git restore --source=<rev> --worktree`; the index stays, so CommitAll of
    the same paths commits the change): a revert of a skill version restores its
    files as the commit before it had them. At least one path; nothing else in
    the work tree changes.

func (c *Client) RestoreIndex(ctx context.Context, dir string, paths ...string) error
    RestoreIndex puts paths back in the index of the work tree at dir as HEAD
    has them (`git restore --source=HEAD --staged`), and leaves their files in
    the work tree as they are: a file the index got only since HEAD (`git add`,
    `git add -N`) is untracked again, with its content.

func (c *Client) RestoreTracked(ctx context.Context, dir string, paths ...string) error
    RestoreTracked puts paths (relative to the top of the work tree at dir) back
    as HEAD has them, in the index and the work tree (`git restore --source=HEAD
    --staged --worktree`): a change of a factory command to a tracked file
```
