```text
    path, as Install does once it has written the file (bootout, the wait for
    the job to go, enable, bootstrap with its retries), and writes nothing. The
    plist must be the job's: one that is missing, has no label or names another
    job is refused, so the job is never unloaded without its own definition to
    load again. ready, when not nil, runs after that check and right before the
    bootout, with nothing between them: the caller's last look at the job, whose
    error stops the reload. Every error before the bootout wraps ErrNotReloaded.

func Uninstall(ctx context.Context, run execx.Runner, uid int, label, path string) error
    Uninstall unloads the job and deletes its plist at path. It is idempotent:
    a job that is not loaded and a missing file are not errors. If bootout fails
    while the job is still loaded, the error is returned and the file is kept so
    the daemon is not orphaned without its definition.


TYPES

type Info struct {
	State State
	// PID is the running process, 0 when none.
	PID int
	// Runs is how many times launchd has started the job.
	Runs int
	// LastExitCode is meaningful only when Exited is true; launchd prints
	// "(never exited)" or a non-numeric exit reason otherwise.
	LastExitCode int
	Exited       bool
	// SpawnFailed is launchd's "job state = spawn failed": its last attempt
	// to start the job failed before the program ran.
	SpawnFailed bool
}
    Info is the parsed result of `launchctl print gui/<uid>/<label>`.
    It deliberately carries no raw output: `print` echoes the job's arguments
    and environment.

func Status(ctx context.Context, run execx.Runner, uid int, label string) (Info, error)
    Status runs `launchctl print gui/<uid>/<label>`. Only launchd's "no
    such service" answer (exit 113, or "Could not find service" on stderr)
    yields State NotLoaded and a nil error. Every other failure (a domain or
    permission error, a missing binary, a timeout) is returned as an error,
    alongside NotLoaded as the zero Info: the job may well still be loaded,
    so callers such as Bootout and Uninstall must not read it as "gone".

func (s Info) CannotSpawn() bool
    CannotSpawn reports whether launchd says it cannot start the job: the job
    is loaded with no process, and its last spawn failed (SpawnFailed) or it
    last exited EX_CONFIG. On 2026-10-28 launchd failed every spawn of a rebuilt
    binary so ("needs LWCR update"), and unloading and loading the job again
    started it. A program that ran and exited is not that.

func (s Info) Loaded() bool
    Loaded reports whether launchd knows the job.

type Options struct {
	// Label is the job label; required. By convention it is also the plist's
	// file name stem (see AgentPath).
	Label string
	// ProgramArguments is the full argv, including argv[0]; required.
	ProgramArguments []string
	// WorkingDir sets WorkingDirectory when non-empty.
	WorkingDir string
	// Env becomes EnvironmentVariables when non-empty, rendered in sorted key order.
	Env map[string]string
	// StdoutPath and StderrPath set StandardOutPath / StandardErrorPath when
	// non-empty. launchd creates the file but not its parent directory.
	StdoutPath, StderrPath string
	// KeepAlive restarts the job when it exits abnormally. It renders
	// KeepAlive = { SuccessfulExit = false }: a clean exit (the daemon exits 0
	// on SIGTERM and when another instance already holds the lock) is not
	// restarted, so launchd does not spin. False omits the key.
	KeepAlive bool
	// ThrottleSeconds sets ThrottleInterval (minimum seconds between launches)
	// when greater than zero; launchd's own default is 10.
	ThrottleSeconds int
}
    Options describes the LaunchAgent job.

type State string
    State is launchd's own description of a loaded job, or NotLoaded.

const (
	// NotLoaded means launchd does not know the job (`launchctl print` exited
	// 113 or said "Could not find service"). Status also returns it next to
	// an error, as the zero answer when the state could not be read.
	NotLoaded State = "not loaded"
	// Running means the job has a live process.
	Running State = "running"
	// Unknown means the job is loaded but `print` output had no state line.
	Unknown State = "unknown"
)
```

## learn

```text
package learn // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/learn"

Package learn is the deterministic half of the retro (DECISIONS "Learning loop:
daily retro"): after a pull request magnum reviewed closes, Build turns what
other reviewers said about it into candidates for a classifier, after dropping
what cannot be a miss (the author's and magnum's own comments, short approvals,
comments on code magnum never saw, findings magnum already posted or dropped as
a duplicate of the comment), and ParseOutput reads the classifier's answer back,
refusing anything off schema and any lesson that retells the pull request
instead of teaching (ScrubLesson). The threads magnum started that someone
answered go to the classifier too (OwnThreads), which says what the author did
with each finding.

The package is pure: it starts no process and touches no network or registry.
The engine reads GitHub and the registry and hands the data in; the one
comparison Build may need is a function of Input.

CONSTANTS

const (
	KindThread = store.MissSourceThread
	KindReview = store.MissSourceReview
)
    Candidate kinds (store.MissSourceThread, store.MissSourceReview).

const (
	// InputsFile and PinsFile are in the run directory, which the agent
	// reads; ChangesFile is the answer it writes at the root of its
	// worktree (magnum keeps a copy in the run directory).
	InputsFile  = "inputs.json"
	PinsFile    = "pins.json"
	ChangesFile = "changes.json"
	// SkillFile is the judge skill, relative to a checkout.
	SkillFile = "skills/magnum-review/SKILL.md"
	// PinsSource is the pins file the skill tests generate, relative to a
	// checkout (FormatPins).
	PinsSource = "internal/agents/testdata/skill_pins.txt"
	// DecisionsFile is where magnum appends the edit's DECISIONS entry.
	DecisionsFile = "docs/DECISIONS.md"
)
    The files of an editor run.

const (
	DecisionMaxRunes = 1200 // the DECISIONS entry
	EditReasonRunes  = 300  // a one-line reason
	// ChangesMaxBytes bounds changes.json.
	ChangesMaxBytes = 256 << 10
)
    Limits of the editor's answer.

const (
	FileEdited    = "edited"
	FileUnchanged = "unchanged"
	InputNoted    = store.MissNoted
	InputSkipped  = store.MissSkipped
)
    What changes.json says of a file and of an input.

const (
	GatePassed = store.LearnPassed // it lands
	GateHeld   = store.LearnHeld   // the operator decides
	GateFailed = store.LearnFailed // it goes
)
    The gate's verdicts (Verdict.State), the proposal's next state.

const (
	GateJudgeOnly = "judge_only" // the judge alone, on a full replay's reviewer reports
	GateFull      = "full"       // every role
)
    The gate's modes (Mode).

const (
	GateRunCandidate   = "candidate"
	GateRunSecond      = "second"
	GateRunBase        = "baseline"
	GateRunBaseJudge   = "baseline judge"
	GateRunLocal       = "local candidate"
	GateRunLocalSecond = "local second"
	GateRunBaseSecond  = "baseline second"
)
    The kinds of eval run a gate makes, the end of their label (GateRunLabel):
    the candidate's first and second replays, the base's full and judge-only
    ones, a local guard's two candidate replays (every role, in runs of their
    own) and the base's second replay of a local guard the candidate lost twice.

const (
	SkipNotInCorpus = "not in the corpus"
	SkipFlagged     = "flagged: never replayed"
	SkipNotWatched  = "not watched"
	// SkipLocal is a local case (a round of the factory's local review,
	// eval.KindLocal) in a place no gate gives one: a target (no learned
	// input names one), an other, or a guard of a gate that takes no local
	// guard (Guards.Local: `magnum eval guards`, a gate without the local
	// cases' corpus or whose candidate changes nothing a local round reads).
	SkipLocal = "a local case: eval run replays it, no gate does"
	// SkipFoundAtBaseline and SkipNotReportedAtBaseline are a target the
	// baseline covers already: its input retires (store.LearnTargetBaseline).
	SkipFoundAtBaseline       = store.LearnDismissedFound
	SkipNotReportedAtBaseline = store.LearnDismissedNotReported
	// SkipLostAtBase is a guard the candidate lost a defect of on both
	// replays that the base lost too (GateRow.AtBase): the loss is not the
	// candidate's.
	SkipLostAtBase = "lost at the base too"
)
    Why SelectCases leaves a target out, and why the gate does once it has the
    target's baseline (AtBaseline).

const (
	CandidatesFile = "candidates.json" // what Build kept, for the classifier
	OutputFile     = "retro.json"      // the classifier's answer (ParseOutput)
	FilesDir       = "files"           // the commented files: files/<sha12>/<path>
	// FactoryDir holds the copies of the factory task's plan, ticket and
	// answers (plan.md, ticket.md, answers.md) on a pull request the
	// factory published, for a factory-origin candidate's stage.
	FactoryDir = "factory"
)
    Files of a pull request's retro directory.

const (
	TitleMax   = 80  // runes
	MatchMax   = 3   // patterns per miss
	PatternMax = 120 // bytes per pattern
)
    Limits of the classifier's answer.

const (
	LessonIssueRef  = "issue_ref"  // a pull request or issue number (#123)
	LessonURL       = "url"        // a link
	LessonLogin     = "login"      // a login of the pull request, with or without "@"
	LessonNamesRepo = "names_repo" // the repository's owner or name, in a general lesson
)
    Why ScrubLesson dropped a lesson (the reason of a lesson_rejected event).

const DecisionWidth = 104
    DecisionWidth is the design log's line width.

const FixerAuthor = "(magnum fix)"
    FixerAuthor is a reply's Author when magnum's fixer wrote it
    (postreview.FixReplyMarker): the fixer answers for the PR's author, as that
    author's login, but what it chose is no person's answer.

const LearnedHeading = "## Learned rules"
    LearnedHeading heads the design log's last section, which holds the entries
    of the self-improving loop (the editor's decisions and the reverts of skill
    versions) and nobody else's: the operators append theirs to the sections
    before it, so an entry of theirs on master and a candidate's entry never
    touch the same lines, and a landing's rebase does not conflict over them.

const NearLines = escapes.NearLines
    NearLines is how far, in lines, a comment may be from one of magnum's
    findings on the same path and still be about it: escapes' near rule,
    which the factory's local round is matched by too.

const OriginFactory = store.MissOriginFactory
    OriginFactory is a candidate's Origin on a pull request the factory
    published when the factory's local round did not catch it.

const OwnAuthor = "(magnum)"
    OwnAuthor is a reply's Author when magnum wrote it: no GitHub login has
    parentheses, so it never names a person.

const OwnTitleMax = 200
    OwnTitleMax bounds an own thread's Title, in runes.

const RejectedMax = 40
    RejectedMax bounds the rejected findings the classifier gets: the newest of
    the pull request's.

const RuleOnlyDeclines = "only declined findings improved: review the rule it adds"
    RuleOnlyDeclines opens the rule of a proposal the gate holds because the
    only targets it improved are declined findings (Judge).


VARIABLES

var EditAllowedGlobs = []string{"skills/magnum-review/SKILL.md", "prompts/judge-*.md", "prompts/claude-*.md"}
    EditAllowedGlobs are the files the editor may change, relative to the
    checkout: the judge skill, the judge prompts and the Claude reviewers'
    prompts. Nothing else: no Go code, no test, no configuration, not the
    retro's or the curator's prompts.


FUNCTIONS

func AllowedEditFile(p string) bool
    AllowedEditFile reports whether p (slash-separated, relative to the
    checkout) is one of EditAllowedGlobs.

func AppendLearned(doc []byte, entry string) []byte
    AppendLearned adds entry to the design log doc at the end of its Learned
    rules section (LearnedHeading), before a section someone added after it;
    the section's first entry follows its introduction after a blank line.
    A log without the section gets it at its end, with the introduction, after a
    blank line.

func AtBaseline(name string, before *eval.Score) string
    AtBaseline is why target name is no target once before, its baseline's
    score, is known ("" = it is one): a miss- case whose every defect the
    baseline found (SkipFoundAtBaseline) or a decline- case whose declined
    finding the baseline no longer reports (SkipNotReportedAtBaseline): nothing
    is left to improve.

func BothFound(a, b *eval.Score) *eval.Score
    BothFound is the score of two replays of a case taken as one (a local
    guard's base, which a candidate's loss of it on both replays is weighed
    against): a defect is found only when both found it; a and b's other fields
    are a's. nil when either is.

func CaseFromDecline(d store.Decline) (eval.Case, bool)
    CaseFromDecline is the learned case of decline d: ok when the author's
    answer showed magnum's finding wrong or ranked too high (verdict wrong or
    over_ranked) for every repository (scope general), and d is still new or
    used (or dismissed as covered at a gate's baseline, learnedState). The case
    is decline-<id> on d's PR at the reviewed commit, why the finding's title,
    with one absent defect, decline-<id>, on the finding's path (literally) and
    line with d's match expressions: a finding that reports it again is a false
    positive. An over-ranked one is a hit only at the priority magnum posted or
    stronger (eval.Defect.Severity), so the point ranked lower is no hit; one
    whose posted priority is not P0 to P3 makes no case, since every matching
    finding would be a hit and the point could stop being one only by not being
    reported.

func CaseFromMiss(m store.Miss) (eval.Case, bool)
    CaseFromMiss is the learned case of miss m: ok when m is a miss (class miss)
    of scope general, P0 to P2, still new or used (or dismissed as covered at a
    gate's baseline, learnedState), on a reviewed commit the case can pin. The
    case is miss-<id> on m's PR at that commit, why its title, with one defect
    to find, miss-<id>: m's path (literally, not as a glob), its lines (or its
    line), the match expressions that compile and its severity. A row the corpus
    would refuse (no path nor match left, a PR it cannot name) makes no case.

func DecisionEntry(decision, day string, inputs []string) string
    DecisionEntry is the design log's entry for an editor's decision:
    its headline in bold without the final stop, the day and the inputs the
    proposal answers in parentheses, then the rest, one paragraph wrapped at
    DecisionWidth runes with two-space continuation lines, as every entry of
    docs/DECISIONS.md.

func DeclineInputID(id int64) string
    DeclineInputID is a decline's id in inputs.json.

func FilePath(sha, p string) string
    FilePath is where the copy of path at sha lives under a retro directory's
    files: files/<sha12>/<path>, slash-separated.

func FormatPins(pins []string, limit int) []byte
    FormatPins renders the pins file (PinsSource): a comment, the skill's size
    cap, then one pinned sentence per line, sorted.

func GateRunLabel(id int64, kind string) string
    GateRunLabel is the label (eval.Run.Label) of the eval run of kind
    (GateRunCandidate, GateRunSecond, GateRunBase, GateRunBaseJudge) that the
    gate of proposal id makes. A stored run says what it replayed only by its
    label, which GuardsFrom reads back (candidateRun).

func Headline(decision string) (headline, rest string)
    Headline splits a decision into its first sentence (up to the first ".",
    "!" or "?" that ends the text or is followed by a space) and the rest.

func IsMagnum(author string) bool
    IsMagnum reports whether a reply's Author is one of magnum's (OwnAuthor,
    FixerAuthor) and so names no person.

func MissInputID(id int64) string
    MissInputID is a miss's id in inputs.json.

func Mode(files []string) string
    Mode is how the gate replays a proposal that changes files: the judge
    alone (GateJudgeOnly) when the only files a review reads that it changes
    are the judge skill and the judge prompts (prompts/judge-*.md), every role
    (GateFull) when it changes anything else; the design log and the golden
    files the format gate regenerated change no review.

func ParseInputID(s string) (kind string, id int64, ok bool)
    ParseInputID reads an id of inputs.json: its kind (store.LearnInputMiss or
    store.LearnInputDecline) and row id.

func ParseOutput(data []byte, cands []Candidate, rejected []Rejected, threads []OwnThread) (map[string]Item, map[string]ThreadItem, error)
    ParseOutput reads the classifier's answer for cands, the rejected findings
    it was given and the own threads: one item per candidate, no other id,
    a known class, and a rejected finding it names one of rejected's;
    a miss also has a severity (P0 to P3), a title of at most TitleMax runes,
    a lesson, a scope (repo or general), lines [from, to] with 1 <= from <= to
    and one to MatchMax patterns of at most PatternMax bytes that compile as
    case-insensitive Go regular expressions. Only a miss keeps those fields: the
    other classes keep their id, class and rejected finding. A factory-origin
    candidate (Candidate.Origin) of class miss, style or outside also keeps
    its stage when it is plan, code or review (itemStage); any other stage is
    dropped, never an error. Likewise one thread item per own thread, no other
    id and a known outcome; a declined or argued one also has a verdict, and a
    wrong, over_ranked or missing_context verdict a lesson, a scope and patterns
    as a miss has (checkThread), except on a thread only magnum's fixer answered
    (OwnThread.Fixer), which keeps none. The error names ids and fields,
    never the classifier's text, so it can go back into a prompt.

func ParsePins(b []byte) ([]string, int, error)
    ParsePins reads a pins file: the pins and the skill's cap. A file without a
    cap line is an error.

func PromoteTarget(cases []GateCase, after int) bool
    PromoteTarget gives the place of the target at cases[after], which the
    baseline covers, to the first target after it that SelectCases left out over
    its cap, which becomes runnable; false when there is none.

func Regressions(rows []GateRow) []string
    Regressions names how rows regressed (none = they did not): a defect the
    baseline found and the candidate lost, once replayed again (Retried), or a
    declined finding the candidate reports and the baseline did not. A guard
    compared with a stored replay of other inputs (Stored) counts for neither:
    only the base's score may (AtBase).

func RevertEntry(decision, day string) string
    RevertEntry is the design log's entry for a revert of a skill version:
    its headline in bold without the final stop, the day and what made it,
    then the rest, wrapped as DecisionEntry wraps.

func ScrubLesson(lesson, scope string, people, own, repo []string) (string, string)
    ScrubLesson returns lesson when it teaches without retelling the pull
    request, else "" and why (Lesson*): a pull request or issue reference
    (#123), a URL, one of people (the author's and the reviewers' logins),
    with or without "@", or an @mention of one of own (magnum's logins,
    whose bare name is often the organization's); a "[bot]" suffix is ignored,
    and "@" before anything else is code (@property, @Transactional). A lesson
    of scope general may not name the repository's owner or name either (repo),
    backticks or not, since general lessons can reach the public judge skill;
    a repo lesson goes to that repository's own notes and may. Words match whole
    and case-insensitively.

func TargetName(kind string, id int64) string
    TargetName is the learned case of a proposal's input of kind
    (store.LearnInputMiss, store.LearnInputDecline) and id: miss-<id>
    (CaseFromMiss) or decline-<id> (CaseFromDecline).

func TemplateActions(text string) []string
    TemplateActions lists the template actions of a prompt in order: an edit of
    the prompts may change the text around them, never them (a dropped field,
    a new define or template call, a changed condition).

func ValidateEdit(c EditCheck, changes Changes) []string
    ValidateEdit returns what is wrong with an editor's answer (nil = valid),
    in words fit for a nudge and the registry: every input of c is accounted for
    exactly once, noted with where or skipped with a one-line reason of at most
    EditReasonRunes; every changed file is an allowed one and listed edited,
    and a file listed edited changed; the skill is within its cap and keeps
    every pin; the diff's added lines and the decision pass notes.CheckLeaks
    and ScrubLesson's rules for a general lesson (no pull request number, link,
    login or repository); and the decision is 1 to DecisionMaxRunes runes.

func WriteFileAtomic(root *os.Root, name string, data []byte) error
    WriteFileAtomic writes data to name inside root: a temporary file next
    to it, then a rename, so a reader never sees half a file. name comes from
    GitHub (a commented path), and root confines it to the retro directory.


TYPES

type Candidate struct {
	ID       string `json:"id"`
	Kind     string `json:"kind"` // KindThread | KindReview
	URL      string `json:"url"`
	Reviewer string `json:"reviewer"` // Account form
	// Path and the line range [StartLine, Line] are where an inline comment
	// sits in the file at ReviewedSHA (both 0 for a file comment, and for a
	// comment on deleted lines, Side "LEFT", whose lines are the old
	// file's); a review body has neither.
	Path      string `json:"path,omitempty"`
	StartLine int    `json:"start_line,omitempty"`
	Line      int    `json:"line,omitempty"`
	Side      string `json:"side,omitempty"` // the diff side: RIGHT, or LEFT for deleted lines
	// ReviewedSHA is the commit magnum reviewed that the comment applies
	// to: the comment's own commit, or a reviewed commit since which the
	// commented file did not change (for an outside comment, the review
	// before it, else its own commit). CommentSHA is the commit the comment
	// was made on.
	ReviewedSHA string    `json:"reviewed_sha"`
	CommentSHA  string    `json:"comment_sha,omitempty"`
	DiffHunk    string    `json:"diff_hunk,omitempty"`
	Body        string    `json:"body"`
	CreatedAt   time.Time `json:"created_at"`
	// Raised is store.MissRaisedRejected when the judge raised a finding
	// near the comment and rejected it (FindingRef "<run id>/<finding id>",
	// ReasonCode its reason; not for a duplicate of a comment made before
	// the review, which is caught), else store.MissRaisedNone. A rejected
	// finding the classifier names replaces it (LinkRejected).
	Raised     string `json:"raised"`
	FindingRef string `json:"finding_ref,omitempty"`
	ReasonCode string `json:"reason_code,omitempty"`
	// Origin is OriginFactory for a comment on a pull request the factory
	// published, on code its local review round saw, that the round did
	// not catch (Input.Local, tagLocal), "" otherwise. The classifier gives
	// such a candidate a stage.
	Origin string `json:"origin,omitempty"`
	// PostedCaught: magnum's posted round caught the comment (a finding it
	// posted near it, or one it rejected as a duplicate of it) though the
	// factory's local round, which saw its code, did not. Without the
	// factory such a comment is caught and no candidate; here it is one,
	// recorded only as a factory-origin miss that teaches the review skill
	// nothing.
	PostedCaught bool `json:"posted_caught,omitempty"`
	// File is the commented file at ReviewedSHA, relative to the candidates
	// file's directory; FileSkipped says why there is no copy. The engine
	// fills both.
	File        string `json:"file,omitempty"`
	FileSkipped string `json:"file_skipped,omitempty"`

	// OutsideReason says why Build put the comment in Result.Outside
	// (store.MissOutside*); "" for a candidate. The classifier never sees
	// an outside comment, so it is not in the candidates file.
	OutsideReason string `json:"-"`
}
    Candidate is one comment of another reviewer for the classifier: the root
    comment of a review thread ("t<comment id>") or the body of a review
    ("r<review id>").

func LinkRejected(cands []Candidate, items map[string]Item, rows []Rejected) []Candidate
    LinkRejected returns a copy of cands in which each candidate whose item
    names a rejected finding of rows (Item.Rejected) raised that finding:
    Raised rejected, FindingRef the finding's and ReasonCode its reason.
    A candidate whose item names none, or that has no item, keeps what Build
    found near it by path and line.

func (c Candidate) Lines() []int
    Lines is the candidate's line range as [from, to] (nil without a line).

type Candidates struct {
	PR           string      `json:"pr"`            // the pull request's URL
	ReviewedSHAs []string    `json:"reviewed_shas"` // what magnum reviewed, oldest first
	FilesDir     string      `json:"files_dir"`     // relative to the file's directory
	Candidates   []Candidate `json:"candidates"`
	// Rejected are the findings the judge rejected (Result.Rejected).
	Rejected []Rejected `json:"rejected,omitempty"`
	// Threads are magnum's own findings that someone answered
	// (Result.Threads), with the replies' text: data for the classifier,
	// pruned with the run.
	Threads []OwnThread `json:"threads,omitempty"`
}
    Candidates is the candidates file.

type Changes struct {
	Files    []FileChange  `json:"files"`
	Inputs   []InputChange `json:"inputs"`
	Decision string        `json:"decision"`
}
    Changes is changes.json: what the editor did with every file it may change
    and every input it was given, and the DECISIONS entry it drafts.

func ParseChanges(b []byte) (Changes, error)
    ParseChanges decodes changes.json strictly (an unknown field is an error).

type Comparison struct {
	// Descendant: the later commit descends from the reviewed one (GitHub's
	// status "ahead" or "identical"). The file list is three-dot, so only
	// then is it the difference between the two: for an older commit or a
	// history a force push replaced it lists nothing that matters.
	Descendant bool
	// Paths are the files that differ (renames under both names); Complete
	// is false when GitHub cut the list.
	Paths    []string
	Complete bool
}
    Comparison is what Build needs of GitHub's comparison of two commits.

type EditCheck struct {
	Inputs EditInputs
	// Changed are the paths the worktree's status lists (relative to it,
	// slash-separated), changes.json and magnum's own files left out.
	Changed []string
	// Allowed are the globs a changed file must match (nil =
	// EditAllowedGlobs).
	Allowed []string
	// Skill is the edited SKILL.md, Pins the sentences it must keep.
	Skill []byte
	Pins  []string
	// Diff is the worktree's diff against the base (its added lines are
	// checked), Decision the DECISIONS entry.
	Diff     string
	Decision string
	// Leaks is what names one pull request (notes.CheckLeaks): the
	// branches of the inputs' pull requests. People, Own and Repos are
	// ScrubLesson's for the decision: the inputs' authors and reviewers,
	// magnum's logins, the inputs' repositories' owners and names.
	Leaks              notes.Check
	People, Own, Repos []string
}
    EditCheck is what ValidateEdit compares an answer with.

type EditDecline struct {
	ID       string   `json:"id"` // "d<id>"
	Priority string   `json:"priority,omitempty"`
	Verdict  string   `json:"verdict"`
	Title    string   `json:"title,omitempty"`
	Lesson   string   `json:"lesson,omitempty"`
	Match    []string `json:"match"`
	// History is as EditMiss's.
	History []store.LearnInputGate `json:"history,omitempty"`
}
    EditDecline is a general finding of magnum's an author declined: wrong,
    or ranked too high.

type EditInputs struct {
	Misses     []EditMiss             `json:"misses"`
	Declines   []EditDecline          `json:"declines"`
	LeftOut    int                    `json:"left_out"`
	Rejections []EditRejection        `json:"rejections"`
	Versions   []store.VersionMeasure `json:"versions"`
	SkillBytes int                    `json:"skill_bytes"`
	SkillCap   int                    `json:"skill_cap"`
	Files      []string               `json:"files"`
}
    EditInputs is inputs.json: the inputs to account for (the newest, each
    with the earlier proposals that noted it and failed at the gate), how many
    older ones it leaves out (LeftOut), the operator's reasons for rejecting
    earlier proposals, what the last landed versions did (newest first,
    store.VersionMeasure: a version whose reviews had fewer of their findings
    declined than the one before measured a gain), the skill's size and cap and
    the files the editor may change.

func (in EditInputs) IDs() []string
    IDs lists every input's id, the misses first.

type EditMiss struct {
	ID       string   `json:"id"` // "m<id>"
	Severity string   `json:"severity,omitempty"`
	Title    string   `json:"title,omitempty"`
	Lesson   string   `json:"lesson,omitempty"`
	Match    []string `json:"match"`
	// History is the earlier proposals that noted it and failed at the
	// gate, oldest first, with the gate's rule (store.LearnInputHistory).
	History []store.LearnInputGate `json:"history,omitempty"`
}
    EditMiss is a general miss: what another reviewer caught that magnum did
    not.

type EditRejection struct {
	Input  string `json:"input,omitempty"`
	Reason string `json:"reason"`
}
    EditRejection is the operator's reason for rejecting an earlier proposal:
    of one input (Input, its id) or of the proposal (Input "").

type FileChange struct {
	Name   string `json:"name"`
	Action string `json:"action"`
	Reason string `json:"reason"`
}
    FileChange is one file of Changes: edited or unchanged, and why.

type GateCase struct {
	Case   eval.Case
	Target bool
	Guard  bool
	Skip   string
}
    GateCase is a case the gate replays, or a target it cannot (Skip says why;
    Case has the target's name alone when the corpus lacks it). Guard marks a
    guard place (Guards).

func SelectCases(corpus *eval.Corpus, targets []string, watched func(pr string) bool, flagged func(pr string) bool, limit int, guards Guards) []GateCase
    SelectCases picks a proposal's cases from corpus (nil = none): every target,
    in its order, first (one the corpus lacks, whose PR is flagged or in no
    watch is skipped with why, and one past limit too), then the guard places
    (guards, on top of limit, so targets never crowd them out; a guard is
    never a target), then the newest other cases (the corpus's last first: the
    learned ones come after the operator's, oldest first) whose PR is watched
    and not flagged, until limit targets and others can run. A flagged PR is
    never replayed, watched or not, and a local case only in a guard place,
    when guards.Local (else SkipLocal): it is no learned input's target,
    and as an other it would take a place of every gate (the corpus's last) at
    30 minutes or more a replay, whatever its baseline found.

type GateRow struct {
	Case      string      `json:"case"`
	Target    bool        `json:"target,omitempty"`
	Guard     bool        `json:"guard,omitempty"`
	Before    *eval.Score `json:"before,omitempty"`
	After     *eval.Score `json:"after,omitempty"`
	Stored    bool        `json:"stored,omitempty"`
	Retried   bool        `json:"retried,omitempty"`
	Rechecked bool        `json:"rechecked,omitempty"`
	Confirmed bool        `json:"confirmed,omitempty"`
	Skip      string      `json:"skip,omitempty"`
	Note      string      `json:"note,omitempty"`
	Local     bool        `json:"local,omitempty"`
	First     *eval.Score `json:"first,omitempty"`
}
    GateRow is a case of the gate: its score at the baseline (the newest replay
    with master's prompts and skill) and with the candidate's, or why it was not
    compared (Skip). Retried is set once the caller replayed a lost case again,
    After then being the second replay's and First the first's: only then does
    a loss count, and only of a defect both lost. A local row (Local: a round
    of the factory's local review, replayed with every role) is a guard. A
    guard (Guard) keeps the newest stored replay not made by a gate's candidate
    as its baseline (Stored, GuardsFrom: an operator's run or a gate's base,
    of whatever inputs), while the candidate finds what that replay found;
    one it lost twice takes the base's score (AtBase). A miss target won on
    one replay counts once a second finds it too (Confirmed, Confirm, which
    sets Rechecked: a second replay was made). Note says, for the operator,
    what a guard's baseline or a second replay was.

func (r *GateRow) AtBase(base *eval.Score) bool
    AtBase gives guard row r, whose candidate lost a defect of its stored
    baseline on both replays, the base's score as its baseline, and reports
    whether the base lost every such defect too: the row is then skipped
    (SkipLostAtBase), the loss not the candidate's; otherwise a defect the base
    finds and the candidate lost is a regression (Judge).

func (r *GateRow) Confirm(second *eval.Score)
    Confirm records the second candidate replay of row r (WonOnce, Rechecked):
    the win counts (Confirmed) only when second finds more than the baseline
    too.

func (r GateRow) Lost() []string
    Lost names the defects the baseline found that the candidate did not:
    on both replays, once a second replaced the first (First), so two replays
    that each lost another defect lost none twice.

func (r GateRow) NewHits() []string
    NewHits names the absent defects (findings authors declined) the candidate
    reported that the baseline did not.

func (r GateRow) TargetGate() string
    TargetGate is what target row r says of its input's learned case
    (store.LearnTarget*): covered at the baseline, improved or not once
    compared; "" for a row that is no target, was not compared, or won on a
    first replay that no second checked (unchecked: neither a win nor a loss,
    so it never counts toward the dismissal after two failed gates).

func (r GateRow) WonOnce() bool
    WonOnce reports whether target row r is a miss case its candidate's first
    replay found more of than the baseline: the gate replays it again (Confirm)
    before the win counts. A declined finding no longer reported is not replayed
    again.

type Guards struct {
	N      int
	Found  func(c eval.Case) bool
	Last   func(c eval.Case) time.Time
	Replay func(c eval.Case) (eval.Replay, bool)
	Local  bool
}
    Guards are a gate's guard places (SelectCases): up to N cases besides
    the targets whose newest stored replay found a defect (Found), the least
    recently replayed first (Last; zero = never, a nil Last orders none),
    so successive gates take turns through them: a gate always has cases whose
    baseline found something the candidate can lose, which its targets (their
    baseline finds nothing yet) and the newest others (mostly declined findings,
    with nothing to find) seldom are. N = 0 or a nil Found gives none. Replay,
    which GuardsFrom sets, is the stored replay Found reads, which the gate
    takes as a guard's baseline. Local lets a local case (eval.KindLocal) take
    a guard place, which the gate replays with every role; false leaves every
    local case out (SkipLocal).

func GuardsFrom(runs []eval.Run, n int, skip string, since time.Time, reviewers string) Guards
    GuardsFrom are n guard places over the stored runs (oldest first:
    eval.ListRuns), which the gate and `magnum eval guards` both take:
    a case guards when its newest scored replay at its head (eval.NewestReplay,
    the one replayed last among those replays) not made by a gate's candidate
    found a defect, and is ordered by when it was replayed last in any run,
    scored or not (lastReplayed). Both read only the replays made before since
    (eval.RunsBefore; zero = every replay: `magnum eval guards`): the gate's
    proposal's creation, so every gate of one proposal takes the same guards
    with the same baselines whatever was replayed since (the gate's own replays
    of the base, an improve run's eval-at.sh). Which cases guard, and their
    baselines (Replay), come only from replays not made by a gate's candidate:
    every gate's replays of its candidate, of any proposal (candidateRun),
    are left out, since one that found a defect master's skill does not would
    make a guard that the next proposal's candidate "loses" and its base loses
    too. The order (Last) counts those replays too: a gate replays its guards
    only as its candidate's first and second replays (the base only for one
    the candidate lost twice), so without them a guard's last replay would
    never move and every gate would take the same guards; and it counts a
    replay that ended without a score (an error, a refusal, a cut replay), so
    a case that never scores goes to the back instead of taking a guard place,
    and a replay, in every later gate. Both leave out the runs with inputs skip
    (the gate's candidate's own; "" = none). reviewers, for a judge-only gate,
    are its candidate's reviewer inputs (eval.Run.ReviewerInputs): its judge
    reads the reports of a full replay whose reviewers read them, and none is
    made for a guard, so a case guards it only with such a full replay among the
    replays that decide which cases guard (eval.FullReplayFor); "" for a gate
    of every role. A local case needs no such replay (the gate replays it with
    every role), but its newest replay must have recorded its round's inputs
    (eval.CaseRun.Inputs): one from before replayed the posted reviewer prompt,
    no local round's.

type Input struct {
	// Author is the pull request's author in Account form
	// (github.Account): its own comments are never candidates.
	Author string
	// Reviewed are the commits magnum reviewed; their order does not matter.
	Reviewed []Reviewed
	// Own are magnum's logins in Account form: every configured identity's,
	// and the ones the pull request's reviews were posted as. A gh
	// identity's is the operator's own, so a comment by one of them is
	// never a candidate, and is magnum's finding only in one of magnum's
	// reviews (ReviewRuns, OwnThreads).
	Own []string
	// Threads and Reviews are the pull request's review threads and
	// reviews as GitHub reports them. The reviews magnum posted are among
	// them: a review in ReviewRuns gives the time its run's findings were
	// posted at (SubmittedAt).
	Threads []github.Thread
	Reviews []github.Review
	// Findings are the judge's findings of the pull request
	// (store.Store.FindingsByPR): a posted one near a comment means magnum
	// caught it; a rejected one, that magnum raised it and let it go, or,
	// for a duplicate of a thread the comment predates the review of, that
	// it caught. The rejected ones also go to the classifier
	// (Result.Rejected).
	Findings []store.Finding
	// ReviewRuns names, by review id (runs.review_id), the run of each
	// review magnum posted whose findings are the review's: a thread is
	// magnum's only when its root is in one of these reviews, and its
	// finding is one of that run's (OwnThreads). A finding's review, and so
	// the time it was judged at, is the one its RunID is bound to here.
	ReviewRuns map[int64]string
	// Targets names, by run id, the commit each of magnum's runs on the
	// pull request reviewed (runs.target_sha): a finding is of its run's
	// head. A posted finding catches a comment measured against that head
	// or a later one (postedNear); a rejected finding links only a comment
	// of its head, or of a later reviewed head the commented file did not
	// change since (rejectedNear). A finding whose run is not in it is near
	// none.
	Targets map[string]string
	// MinChars drops a comment whose text, without quotes and code blocks,
	// is shorter.
	MinChars int
	// IncludeBots counts comments of bot accounts other than magnum's.
	IncludeBots bool
	// Compare compares a reviewed commit with a later one (GitHub's
	// comparison). Build asks it only for an inline comment on a commit
	// magnum did not review and, on a pull request the factory published
	// (Local), for a comment on another reviewed commit than a head the
	// factory approved and for a local finding at another head than a
	// comment's; nil means no comparison, so such a comment is outside or
	// not on the factory's code, and such a finding catches nothing.
	Compare func(from, to string) (Comparison, error)
	// Local is the factory's local review round of a pull request the
	// factory published (nil for every other pull request): the second
	// caught set. A candidate on code the round saw that none of its
	// findings caught is the factory's miss (Candidate.Origin), and so is
	// such a comment magnum's posted round caught (Candidate.PostedCaught).
	Local *LocalRound
}
    Input is everything Build reads about one pull request.

type InputChange struct {
	ID     string `json:"id"`
	Action string `json:"action"`
	Where  string `json:"where,omitempty"`
	Reason string `json:"reason,omitempty"`
}
    InputChange is one input of Changes: noted, with where the change covers it,
    or skipped, with a one-line reason.

type Item struct {
	ID       string   `json:"id"`
	Class    string   `json:"class"`
	Severity string   `json:"severity,omitempty"`
	Title    string   `json:"title,omitempty"`
	Lesson   string   `json:"lesson,omitempty"`
	Scope    string   `json:"scope,omitempty"`
	Lines    []int    `json:"lines,omitempty"`
	Match    []string `json:"match,omitempty"`
	// Rejected is the id of the rejected finding (Candidates.Rejected) that
	// reports the comment's problem, by meaning; "" when none does. Any
	// class may name one.
	Rejected string `json:"rejected,omitempty"`
	// Stage is where a factory-origin candidate went wrong
	// (store.MissStages): kept only on such a candidate of class miss,
	// style or outside, and only when it is one of them.
	Stage string `json:"stage,omitempty"`
}
    Item is the classifier's verdict on one candidate.

type LocalRound struct {
	// Heads are the heads the factory approved, one per task that
	// published the pull request (factoryread.Task.Head): the code the
	// local round passed.
	Heads []string
	// Findings are the round's findings (escapes.SourceLocal), each of the
	// head its line numbers name (the head of the review cycle that last
	// saw it).
	Findings []escapes.Finding
}
    LocalRound is the factory's local review round of a pull request it
    published, as factory.db keeps it.

type Output struct {
	Items   []Item       `json:"items"`
	Threads []ThreadItem `json:"threads,omitempty"`
}
    Output is the classifier's answer file: an item per candidate and a thread
    item per own thread.

type OwnThread struct {
	ID        string `json:"id"`
	URL       string `json:"url"` // GitHub's link to the root comment
	CommentID int64  `json:"comment_id"`
	ReviewID  int64  `json:"review_id,omitempty"` // the review magnum posted the root comment in (Input.ReviewRuns)
	// Path and Line are where the root comment sits (Line 0 for a file
	// comment or a comment on deleted lines, as for a Candidate).
	Path string `json:"path,omitempty"`
	Line int    `json:"line,omitempty"`
	// Title is the root comment's first line without its emphasis and
	// priority tag, Priority the first P0 to P3 on that line ("" when none).
	Title    string `json:"title"`
	Priority string `json:"priority,omitempty"`
	// ReviewedSHA is the commit the finding was about: the root comment's
	// when magnum reviewed it, else the newest reviewed before the comment.
	ReviewedSHA string `json:"reviewed_sha"`
	// FindingRef is the posted finding ("<run id>/<finding id>") of the
	// root's review on the same path within NearLines; "" when none.
	FindingRef string `json:"finding_ref,omitempty"`
	// File is the finding's file at ReviewedSHA, relative to the
	// candidates file's directory, which the classifier judges the finding
	// against; FileSkipped says why there is no copy. The engine fills
	// both, as for a Candidate.
	File        string        `json:"file,omitempty"`
	FileSkipped string        `json:"file_skipped,omitempty"`
	Replies     []ThreadReply `json:"replies"`
	// Fixer is set when magnum's fixer gave the thread's only answers
	// (FixerAuthor): its outcome is stored, but no lesson is drawn from it
	// (parseThreads), since no person answered the finding.
	Fixer bool `json:"fixer,omitempty"`
}
    OwnThread is a review thread magnum started that someone else answered, for
    the classifier ("o<comment id>"): the finding as magnum posted it (where,
    its title and priority) and every reply after it.

func OwnThreads(in Input) []OwnThread
    OwnThreads returns the threads of in whose root comment is by one of in.Own
    in a review magnum posted (in.ReviewRuns: a gh identity is the operator's
    own login, and what he writes by hand is no finding of magnum's) with at
    least one reply by someone else (the author or another reviewer; not a
    ghost, not a bot unless in.IncludeBots), in the order GitHub listed them.
    A reply is the fixer's (FixerAuthor) when it carries the fixer's marker
    and comes from the PR's author or one of in.Own (fixerReply): it answers
    the finding, and the thread is Fixer when no one else did. A reply is
    magnum's (OwnAuthor) when it carries magnum's reply marker or comes from
    one of in.Own's Apps; the operator replying by hand is someone else. The
    finding binds to a posted one of the root's review's run by path and line,
    as Build's nearness does.

type Rejected struct {
	ID       string `json:"id"` // "<run id>/<finding id>", the miss's FindingRef
	Title    string `json:"title"`
	Path     string `json:"path,omitempty"`
	Reason   string `json:"reason"`             // the judge's reason code
	Priority string `json:"priority,omitempty"` // P0..P3 as the judge wrote it
}
    Rejected is a finding the judge raised and rejected, as the classifier
    gets it to name the one that reports a comment's problem by meaning
    (Item.Rejected): a test gap sits on the spec file while a person comments
    on the code under test, and the finding nearest the comment by line can be
    about something else. Every field is magnum's own text.

type Result struct {
	// Candidates are the comments to classify, Outside the ones about code
	// magnum did not review, stored as such without a classifier.
	Candidates []Candidate
	Outside    []Candidate
	// Caught counts comments near a finding magnum posted, or near one the
	// judge rejected as a duplicate of a comment made before that review
	// (reasonDuplicate), Dropped the comments too short or only an
	// approval. Neither is stored. On a pull request the factory published
	// a comment on code its local round saw is caught only when that round
	// caught it too (else it is a candidate, PostedCaught).
	Caught, Dropped int
	// Rejected are the findings the judge rejected, the newest RejectedMax
	// with a title, oldest first: the classifier names the one that
	// reports a candidate's problem (Item.Rejected, LinkRejected).
	Rejected []Rejected
	// Threads are magnum's own findings that someone answered
	// (OwnThreads), for the classifier beside the candidates.
	Threads []OwnThread
}
    Result is what Build made of a pull request.

func Build(in Input) (Result, error)
    Build makes the candidates of a pull request: the root comment of every
    review thread and the body of every review by another reviewer (not the
    author, not one of magnum's logins, not a bot unless IncludeBots). Replies
    are never candidates. A thread magnum started that someone answered is not a
    candidate either: it goes to Result.Threads (OwnThreads).

    A comment shorter than MinChars without its quotes and code blocks, or that
    only approves, is dropped. A comment made on a reviewed commit applies to
    it; an inline comment on another commit applies to the newest commit magnum
    reviewed before the comment when that commit descends from the reviewed
    one and the commented file did not change between the two (Compare), and is
    outside otherwise, as is a review body on a commit magnum did not review;
    an outside comment says why (OutsideReason). Only a failing Compare is an
    error; one GitHub answers with a 404 (github.ErrNotFound: a commit it no
    longer has) proves nothing, so the comment is outside and the build goes on.

    A comment within NearLines of a finding magnum posted on the same path, at
    the reviewed commit the comment applies to (for an outside one, the review
    before it) or at one reviewed before that, is caught (postedNear): the
    finding stays open as a thread on the later heads, so the comment repeats
    magnum's own finding, whatever changed in the file. One near a rejected
    finding is raised (a comment on deleted lines has no line, so neither),
    until the classifier names another (Result.Rejected lists them); near here
    counts only the findings of the commit the comment applies to and of the
    earlier reviewed commits the file did not change since (rejectedNear),
    since a line number of another version of the file names other code, and an
    outside comment's lines hold at no reviewed commit, so it raises nothing.
    The exception is a finding rejected as a duplicate (reasonDuplicate:
    an existing thread already covers it) when the comment was made before the
    review that rejected it (rejectedAsDuplicate): the judge read the comment
    and agreed, so it is caught. A rejection for any other reason says the judge
    disagreed, and a comment made after the review was never read by it.

    On a pull request the factory published (Input.Local), every candidate on
    code the factory's local round saw that the round did not catch (tagLocal)
    has Origin factory, a comment that cannot be placed (a review body, deleted
    lines) included. A comment magnum caught (posted near it, or rejected as
    its duplicate) that the local round did not becomes such a candidate too,
    PostedCaught, instead of being caught; one both rounds caught is caught. A
    comment on code the local round never saw takes no part, and is a candidate,
    caught or outside as on any other pull request: an outside one (on code
    magnum's review did not see either) and one on a file that changed after the
    factory approved it (localSaw).

type Reviewed struct {
	SHA string
	At  time.Time // when the review was posted
}
    Reviewed is a commit magnum posted a review of.

type ThreadItem struct {
	ID      string   `json:"id"`
	Outcome string   `json:"outcome"`
	Verdict string   `json:"verdict,omitempty"`
	Lesson  string   `json:"lesson,omitempty"`
	Scope   string   `json:"scope,omitempty"`
	Match   []string `json:"match,omitempty"`
}
    ThreadItem is the classifier's answer for one own thread: what the author
    did with the finding (Outcome, store.Decline*), whether magnum was right
    for a declined or argued one (Verdict, store.Verdict*), and for a wrong,
    over-ranked or missing-context one a lesson with its scope and the patterns
    that recognize the same finding again.

type ThreadReply struct {
	Author string `json:"author"`
	Body   string `json:"body"`
}
    ThreadReply is one reply in an own thread: who wrote it (Account form,
    OwnAuthor for magnum, FixerAuthor for its fixer) and what it says, data for
    the classifier only.

type Verdict struct {
	State string    `json:"state"`
	Rule  string    `json:"rule"`
	Rows  []GateRow `json:"rows"`
}
    Verdict is the gate's decision on a proposal: State (GatePassed, GateHeld,
    GateFailed), the Rule that decided it, as a sentence, and the rows it read.

func Judge(rows []GateRow) Verdict
    Judge decides a proposal on its rows. It fails one that regressed
    (Regressions); else it passes one whose targets include a miss that improved
    on both replays (improved), and holds one whose improved targets are all
    declines (RuleOnlyDeclines: one author's reply and one classifier's answer
    would otherwise remove a class of findings from every review unseen);
    a target the baseline covers (AtBaseline) is no target, so it fails one
    whose every target is so (nothing to improve); else it holds one none of
    whose targets could be compared, and fails the rest (no target improved,
    a miss its second replay did not find again included).

```

## mysqlx

```text
package mysqlx // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/mysqlx"

Package mysqlx inventories and drops the per-worktree MySQL databases that
Talkable's bin/worktree-setup creates (talkable_<env>[_<role>]__<slug>) on the
local DBngin server.

Reads are unrestricted; the destructive operations, Drop and Recreate (a drop,
then an empty database of the same name), are gated by a Guard that refuses
unsuffixed base databases, system schemas and any slug the caller has not
explicitly allowed. SQL identifiers are validated against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ and
back-quoted before they reach the server.

mysqlx talks to MySQL over the wire (database/sql + go-sql-driver/mysql),
not through a subprocess, so it does not use execx; it never logs a DSN.

CONSTANTS

const DefaultDSN = "root:@tcp(127.0.0.1:3306)/?timeout=5s"
    DefaultDSN is DBngin's stock local server: root, empty password,
    127.0.0.1:3306. The timeout bounds only the TCP dial; per-call deadlines
    come from the context passed to each method, or from callTimeout and
    dropTimeout when it has none.


VARIABLES

var DefaultPattern = likePattern("talkable_")
    DefaultPattern is the schemata LIKE pattern ListSuffixed uses: talkable_%__%
    with every literal underscore escaped by likeEscape. Queries pass it with
    an explicit ESCAPE clause, so it means the same thing under every sql_mode
    (NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES turns the backslash into a plain character in LIKE
    patterns).

var ErrGuard = errors.New("mysqlx: drop refused by guard")
    ErrGuard is wrapped by every refusal from Guard.Check, Drop and DropAll,
    so callers can tell "magnum declined to drop this" from "MySQL failed".

var ErrInvalidDSN = errors.New("mysqlx: invalid DSN")
    ErrInvalidDSN is wrapped by Open when the DSN cannot be parsed.
    The error never carries the driver's message or any part of the DSN:
    those can echo the password (the driver reads "root:secret/" as a network
    named "root:secret").

var ErrNotFound = errors.New("mysqlx: database or table not found")
    ErrNotFound is wrapped when MySQL reports an unknown database (1049) or a
    missing table (1146), so callers can treat "no schema loaded yet" apart from
    a connection or permission failure.


FUNCTIONS

func Slug(name string) (slug string, ok bool)
    Slug returns the part of a database name after its last "__". ok is false
    when the name has no "__", an empty base (name starts with "__") or an empty
    slug (name ends with "__"): such names are not per-worktree databases.


TYPES

type Client struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Client is a handle on the local MySQL server. It is safe for concurrent use.

func Open(dsn string) (*Client, error)
    Open prepares a client for dsn (go-sql-driver/mysql format); an empty
    dsn means DefaultDSN. It validates the DSN but does not connect,
    so the daemon can start while DBngin is down; use Ping to probe the server.
    multiStatements is refused: every statement magnum sends is a single
    statement.

func (c *Client) Close() error
    Close releases the client's connections.

func (c *Client) Drop(ctx context.Context, name string, g Guard) error
    Drop removes one database (DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS, so a retry after a crash
    is harmless) after g.Check approves its name, within dropTimeout when ctx
    has no deadline. A refusal wraps ErrGuard and sends nothing to the server.

func (c *Client) DropAll(ctx context.Context, names []string, g Guard) []DropResult
    DropAll drops each name in order with Drop and returns one result per name,
    in input order. A failure (guard refusal or server error) does not stop the
    remaining names; a cancelled context fails the names it never reached.

func (c *Client) ListPrefixed(ctx context.Context, prefixes []string) ([]Database, error)
    ListPrefixed returns every schema named <prefix><slug> for one of prefixes,
    with its slug and on-disk size, ordered by name. Each prefix is a pool's
    database base followed by the separator ("talkable_development__");
    the slug is the non-empty rest of the name and must be what Slug reports,
    so a name like talkable_development__a__b (slug "b" to Slug and the guard)
    is not listed under that prefix. Prefixes are matched literally (LIKE
    wildcards in them are escaped) and case-sensitively, whatever the server's
    collation. Duplicate prefixes are ignored; no prefix at all lists nothing.
    A prefix that does not end in "__" or has an empty base is an error:
    no database under it could ever be dropped through Guard.

func (c *Client) ListSuffixed(ctx context.Context) ([]Database, error)
    ListSuffixed returns every schema named talkable_%__% (the per-worktree
    databases) with its slug and on-disk size, ordered by name. Schemas whose
    name ends in "__" (empty slug) are not worktree databases and are skipped.
    It only sees the talkable_ family; ListPrefixed lists any other prefix.

func (c *Client) Ping(ctx context.Context) error
    Ping verifies that the server is reachable and the credentials work.

func (c *Client) Recreate(ctx context.Context, name string, g Guard) error
    Recreate empties one database the way a schema load cannot: a table the
    load does not know (one a PR's schema added) that refers to a table it
    drops makes MySQL refuse the DROP TABLE (3730), so the load fails until the
    database starts empty. After g.Check approves name, as for Drop, it reads
    the database's character set and collation, drops it (Drop's statement
    and bound) and creates it again with them (CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS,
    so a retry is harmless; the server's defaults when it was gone). A refusal
    wraps ErrGuard and sends nothing to the server; a character set or collation
    that is not an identifier drops nothing.

func (c *Client) SchemaMigrationsMax(ctx context.Context, dbName string) (string, error)
    SchemaMigrationsMax returns MAX(version) from dbName's Rails
    schema_migrations table. Versions are compared as strings, which is correct
    for Rails' fixed-width timestamps. An empty table yields "". A missing
    database or table wraps ErrNotFound.

type Database struct {
	Name   string  // full schema name, e.g. talkable_development__review3
	Slug   string  // text after the last "__", e.g. review3
	SizeMB float64 // data_length + index_length of its tables, in MiB (0 when it has none)
}
    Database is one per-worktree schema found on the server.

type DropResult struct {
	Name string
	Err  error
}
    DropResult is the outcome for one name in DropAll; Err is nil on success.

type Guard struct {
	// AllowRegexp must match the whole slug (the text after the last "__"); it
	// is implicitly anchored, so an unanchored expression cannot match a
	// fragment. A nil AllowRegexp refuses every name.
	AllowRegexp *regexp.Regexp
	// Prefix, when non-empty, is a required name prefix (callers acting on the
	// Talkable pool set "talkable_" so a foreign schema with a "__" in its name
	// can never be dropped).
	Prefix string
}
    Guard decides which databases Drop may remove. The zero value refuses
    everything.

func (g Guard) Check(name string) error
    Check reports nil when the guard would allow dropping name, or an error
    wrapping ErrGuard saying why not. It is pure: it never touches the server.

    A name is refused unless all of these hold: it is a plain identifier
    ([A-Za-z0-9_]+); it has a non-empty base and a non-empty slug around a "__"
    (so unsuffixed base names such as "talkable_development" and system schemas
    are never droppable); it carries Prefix when one is set; and its slug fully
    matches AllowRegexp.

```

## notes

```text
package notes // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/notes"

Package notes measures, versions and curates the repository notes (the file
every review role reads first and the judge rewrites, engine.NotesPath)
and their harness directory of QA scripts. It reads and writes files only:
the engine decides when (after a round, at startup, on a schedule) and the CLI
shows and applies what is here.

    <root>/<owner>/<repo>.md                    the notes
    <root>/<owner>/<repo>/                      the harness
    <root>/<owner>/<repo>/ARCHIVE.md            the archive of retired notes lines (archive.go)
    <root>/<owner>/<repo>.lock/                 the lock the judges take (agents.NotesLockLine)
    <root>/.curate/<owner>/<repo>/<id>/         one curation's scratch copy and proposal (curate.go)

Every version of the notes and the harness is kept in the registry
(store.RecordNotesVersion), not here. GitHub owners never start with a dot,
so ".curate" never collides with an owner's directory.

CONSTANTS

const (
	MaxDecisionItems = 60
)
    Bounds on the decision's lists: free text kept with the decision for the
    operator, so each item is one line.

const (
	DecisionApply    = "apply"    // apply the proposal as reviewed
	DecisionReject   = "reject"   // reject it, with a reason the next curation reads
	DecisionRecurate = "recurate" // supersede it: a new curation from the notes now reads it and the reason
)
    The critic's decisions.

const (
	MissNoted   = "noted"
	MissSkipped = "skipped"
)
    The actions of a MissChange.

const (
	ActionKept    = "kept"
	ActionAdded   = "added"
	ActionMerged  = "merged"
	ActionRemoved = "removed" // a section
	ActionDeleted = "deleted" // a harness file
)
    The actions of a Change.

const (
	LimitBytes        = "max_bytes"
	LimitLine         = "max_line"
	LimitHarnessFiles = "max_harness_files"
	LimitHarnessBytes = "max_harness_bytes"
)
    The limits by their notes key, in the order Over reports them.

const (
	MaxFileBytes  = 8 << 20
	MaxStateBytes = 64 << 20
)
    Caps on what ReadState reads: a harness this large is not notes, and a
    version must fit the registry.

const ArchiveLine = "retired lines, word for word; search it when a lesson seems missing"
    ArchiveLine is how the notes name the archive, once: what it holds and when
    to read it. Roles do not read the archive by default.

const ArchiveName = "ARCHIVE.md"
    ArchiveName is the archive's path in the harness directory.

const CriticDirName = ".critic"
    CriticDirName is the directory under the notes root that holds every
    critique's run directory (<notes>/.critic/<owner>/<repo>/<run>).

const CurateDirName = ".curate"
    CurateDirName is the curations' directory under the notes root.

const MaxReasonRunes = maxReasonRunes
    MaxReasonRunes bounds a one-line reason: a curator's for a change, the
    critic's for its decision.

const SnapshotFile = "notes-before.json"
    SnapshotFile is the snapshot a round takes of the notes before its judge is
    prompted, in the round's report directory.


VARIABLES

var ErrBusy = errors.New("notes busy: another writer holds the notes lock")
    ErrBusy is Lock's error when another holder kept the lock past the wait.

var ErrTooLarge = errors.New("notes: the harness is too large to record")
    ErrTooLarge is ReadState's error for a harness past MaxFileBytes or
    MaxStateBytes.


FUNCTIONS

func ArchiveHeader(full string) string
    ArchiveHeader is the start of a new archive.

func CheckLeaks(text string, check Check) []string
    CheckLeaks applies Validate's leak rules to one text that is not notes
    (the skill editor's diff and DECISIONS entry): it returns, as phrases to
    follow the text's name, that it names a pull request or issue number, one of
    check's branches, holds what looks like a secret, or names a home directory
    path. nil = none.

func CheckPreserved(before, after State, changes Changes) []string
    CheckPreserved is the preservation check an apply runs before it writes
    anything (engine.ApplyNotesProposal), for the operator and the critic alike:
    after, the state the apply would write (a curation's proposed state, or a
    stale one's merge with the notes' changes since), loses no line of before,
    the notes now. Every non-empty line of before's notes is in after's notes
    or among the lines after adds to the archive, word for word (the title,
    a leaking line and a "## " heading the curator's changes account for exempt,
    as in Validate); the archive keeps every line it held. Unlike Validate it
    asks only that nothing be lost: not that changes.json account for every
    section of before (a section a judge added since the proposal was made
    is kept by the merge, line by line), nor that the notes name the archive
    (a recovery leaves the notes text as it is). nil = the apply may go on;
    a proposal that fails it can only be rejected or curated again.

func Fingerprint(notes []byte, files []File) string
    Fingerprint identifies a state of the notes and the harness: the notes'
    content (a missing file is empty notes, as a version records it) and every
    harness file's name and content.

func HarnessDelta(before, after []File) (added, removed, changed []string)
    HarnessDelta compares two listings: the names only in after (added), only in
    before (removed) and in both with another content (changed), each sorted.

func IsArchive(p string) bool
    IsArchive reports whether the harness path p is the archive.

func Leftovers(r Repo, cutoff time.Time) ([]string, error)
    Leftovers lists the directories next to r's harness that a write left behind
    (".old-" or ".new-" and WriteState's eight random characters after the
    harness's name) and whose modification time is before cutoff. A directory
    that is not there, or a file of that name, is none.

func LineChanges(a, b string) (added, removed int)
    LineChanges counts the lines b adds to a and the lines it removes, with the
    same line matching as Unified (a changed line counts once in each).

func Lock(ctx context.Context, path string, wait time.Duration) (func(), error)
    Lock takes the notes lock at path (Repo.Lock) as the judges do, retrying
    until wait has passed (ErrBusy) or ctx ends; it returns the release. A stale
    lock it cannot remove (a directory with something in it) is waited for like
    a live one: every retry sleeps, and the deadline and ctx hold.

func Measure(r Repo, l Limits) (Size, []File, error)
    Measure measures r's notes file and harness (the archive apart). A missing
    notes file or harness measures zero; any other read error is returned.

func Printable(text string) string
    Printable replaces the control characters other than newline and tab in
    text written by an agent with spaces, and its invalid UTF-8 with U+FFFD,
    so it cannot drive a terminal: a raw byte 0x9b is an 8-bit CSI to a terminal
    that reads C1 controls.

func ReasonLeaks(text string, c Check) []string
    ReasonLeaks applies the leak rules to a decider's one-line reason that the
    next curation reads (the critic's): CheckLeaks (a pull request or issue
    number, one of c's branches, a secret, a home directory path), and a probe
    file name. nil = none.

func Sections(text []byte) []string
    Sections lists the "## " headings of notes text.

func SweepLeftovers(r Repo, cutoff time.Time) ([]string, error)
    SweepLeftovers removes the Leftovers of r before cutoff and returns the ones
    it removed; the first failure ends it, joined to what it removed. The caller
    holds r's lock (Lock): a write in flight keeps its old harness there until
    it is done.

func TextSHA(text []byte) string
    TextSHA is the SHA-256 of notes text, hex.

func Unified(nameA, nameB, a, b string, ctx int) string
    Unified returns a unified diff of a and b, compared line by line,
    with ctx lines of context around each change: the header "--- <nameA>\n+++
    <nameB>\n", then hunks "@@ -<start>,<count> +<start>,<count> @@\n" followed
    by lines prefixed with ' ', '-' or '+', each ending in "\n". It returns ""
    when a == b.

    Start numbers are 1-based. A range of one line is written as its start
    alone ("@@ -3 +3 @@") and a range of no lines as the number of the line
    before it and a zero count ("-0,0" when a is empty), as GNU diff does.
    Changes whose context would overlap or touch (at most 2*ctx unchanged lines
    between them) share one hunk. Lines are split on "\n" only, so a "\r" stays
    part of its line, and a line without its "\n" (only the last one of a side
    can be) differs from the same text with it. Such a line is printed followed
    by "\n\\ No newline at end of file\n". A negative ctx counts as 0.

func Validate(p Proposal, c Check) []string
    Validate returns what is wrong with proposal p (nil = valid), in words
    fit for a nudge and the operator's review: names and rules, and the first
    few lines a proposal would lose (checkPreserved), never more notes text.
    The notes and changes.json must be there; every proposed section and
    harness file must be accounted for as kept or added with a one-line reason,
    and every current section and harness file with what became of it;
    every proposed harness file must be named in the notes; no line of the notes
    may be lost: each stays in the notes or goes to the archive word for word,
    and the archive keeps every line it held (checkPreserved); nothing may
    name a pull request, one of its branches or probe files, carry what looks
    like a secret or a home directory path (the archive, which is history,
    may name a pull request); every miss given must be accounted for once,
    noted with a section of the proposal or skipped with a reason. The archive
    is no QA script: it needs no changes.json item. Size is not checked:
    the limits mark notes to organize, they do not cap them. A proposal that
    changes nothing is invalid unless it was given misses and skips them all
    (the operator confirms the skips).

func ValidateDecision(d Decision, c DecisionCheck) []string
    ValidateDecision returns what is wrong with decision d (nil = valid),
    in words fit for a nudge: the decision is one of the three; the target is
    the fingerprint the prompt gave; a proposal that cannot be applied (its
    stale merge conflicts, or it would lose lines) is rejected or re-curated,
    and only such a proposal is re-curated; reject and recurate need a reason;
    the reason is one line of at most maxReasonRunes runes and passes c.Leaks;
    losses and checked hold at most MaxDecisionItems one-line items with no
    secret and no home directory path.

func WriteArchive(r Repo, text []byte) error
    WriteArchive makes r's archive text (removes it when text is empty),
    confined to the harness directory. The caller holds r's lock.

func WriteSnapshot(dir string, s Snapshot) error
    WriteSnapshot writes s to dir/SnapshotFile.

func WriteState(r Repo, s State) error
    WriteState makes r's notes and harness s: the harness by a complete new
    directory renamed into place, then the notes file replaced atomically
    (removed when s has none), the old harness removed after. A swap that fails,
    or a notes write that fails after it, puts the old harness back, so the
    notes and the harness stay one state; a restore that fails too is joined to
    the error. Once the swap and the notes write are done the write is done:
    an old harness that cannot be removed is a leftover (WriteStateReport names
    it, SweepLeftovers removes it later), not an error. The caller holds r's
    lock (Lock). A harness path that is not clean (cleanName) is refused before
    anything is written.

func WriteSuperseded(s Scratch, proposed State, changes []byte, reason string) error
    WriteSuperseded writes the proposal a curation follows up on into s's
    superseded/ directory, for the curator to read: its notes as notes.md, its
    harness under harness/, its changes.json, with a reason for every section
    and file it kept, merged or removed, and reason, why it was superseded,
    as reason.txt (none when reason is empty). The notes changed since that
    proposal was made, or its reviewer (the operator or the notes critic) sent
    it back, so it was superseded rather than applied; its work is not lost.


TYPES

type Blob struct {
	Path   string // slash-separated, relative to the harness directory
	SHA256 string
	Body   []byte
}
    Blob is one harness file with its content.

type Change struct {
	Name   string `json:"name"`
	Action string `json:"action"`
	Into   string `json:"into,omitempty"` // merged: where it went
	Reason string `json:"reason"`
}
    Change is one item of Changes.

type Changes struct {
	Sections []Change     `json:"sections"`
	Files    []Change     `json:"files"`
	Misses   []MissChange `json:"misses,omitempty"`
}
    Changes is the curator's changes.json: what became of every notes section
    (by its "## " heading) and every harness file, each with a one-line reason,
    and of every miss the curation was given (misses.json).

type Check struct {
	Base State
	// PRNumbers are the repository's pull request numbers; Branches their
	// head branches. A harness file named after a number, or notes naming a
	// branch, carry one pull request's content.
	PRNumbers []int
	Branches  []string
	// Misses are the ids of the misses the curation was given: the proposal
	// accounts for each.
	Misses []int64
}
    Check is what Validate compares a proposal with: the state the curation
    started from and what names one pull request of the repository.

type CriticRun struct{ Dir string }
    CriticRun is one critique's run directory.

func PrepareCritic(dir string, live, proposed State, changes, review, rejections []byte) (CriticRun, error)
    PrepareCritic makes a new run directory dir holding live (the notes as
    current.md, the harness as current/), proposed (proposed.md and proposed/),
    the proposal's changes.json, the review data (review.json) and the earlier
    rejections (rejections.json). The decision file is the critic's to write.

func (c CriticRun) Changes() string
    Changes is changes.json, the curator's account of every section and file.

func (c CriticRun) Current() string
    Current is current.md, a copy of the notes now.

func (c CriticRun) CurrentHarness() string
    CurrentHarness is current/, a copy of the harness now.

func (c CriticRun) Decision() string
    Decision is decision.json, the critic's answer.

func (c CriticRun) Proposed() string
    Proposed is proposed.md, a copy of the proposed notes.

func (c CriticRun) ProposedHarness() string
    ProposedHarness is proposed/, a copy of the proposed harness.

func (c CriticRun) Rejections() string
    Rejections is rejections.json, why the repository's last proposals were
    declined, and by whom.

func (c CriticRun) Review() string
    Review is review.json, the proposal as `magnum notes <repo> --review --json`
    prints it.

type Decision struct {
	Decision string   `json:"decision"`
	Target   string   `json:"target"`
	Reason   string   `json:"reason"`
	Losses   []string `json:"losses"`
	Checked  []string `json:"checked"`
}
    Decision is the critic's decision.json. Target is the fingerprint of the
    state it reviewed (the prompt gives it), which binds an apply to that state.
    Losses lists the removed lines the critic accepts losing and Checked what it
    examined: free text the registry keeps with the decision for the operator,
    which magnum interprets in no other way.

func ReadDecision(run CriticRun) (d Decision, missing bool, problems []string)
    ReadDecision reads the critic's decision.json in run: a regular file of the
    run directory (fsx.ReadRegularIn: what an agent leaves is not trusted),
    one JSON value, no unknown fields. Problems are worded for a nudge (the
    file's name and the parse error, never its content); missing reports that
    the file was not written.

type DecisionCheck struct {
	// Target is the fingerprint the prompt gave: the state the critic
	// reviewed.
	Target string
	// Conflict: the notes changed since the proposal was made and its merge
	// with their changes conflicts. Lossy: what applying it would write loses
	// lines of the notes now (CheckPreserved). Either makes apply invalid and
	// recurate valid.
	Conflict, Lossy bool
	// Leaks names what is wrong with the reason (a pull request, a login, a
	// branch, a probe file, a repository, a secret or a home path): phrases
	// to report, nil = none. Nil checks nothing.
	Leaks func(text string) []string
}
    DecisionCheck is what ValidateDecision compares a decision with.

type File struct {
	Name   string `json:"name"`
	Size   int64  `json:"size"`
	SHA256 string `json:"sha256"`
}
    File is one harness file: its slash-separated path relative to the harness
    directory, its size and the SHA-256 of its content.

func List(dir string) ([]File, error)
    List lists the regular files under dir, recursively, sorted by name;
    symbolic links and other special files are left out (never followed).
    A missing dir lists nothing.

func Scripts(files []File) []File
    Scripts is a listing without the archive: the harness of QA scripts.

type HistoryNotes struct {
	ID     int64
	At     time.Time
	Source string
	Notes  []byte
}
    HistoryNotes is the notes text of one version of a repository's history
    (store.NotesHistory: the judges', the people's, the imports and the applied
    curations', never a proposal's own state).

type Leftover struct {
	Path string
	Err  error
}
    Leftover is a directory next to the harness that a write could not remove:
    the old harness, once the new state was in place.

func WriteStateReport(r Repo, s State) (*Leftover, error)
    WriteStateReport is WriteState that also reports the leftover of a write
    that succeeded (nil when the old harness was removed or none existed);
    a leftover never comes with an error.

type Limits struct {
	MaxBytes        int64 `json:"max_bytes"`
	MaxLine         int   `json:"max_line"` // characters
	MaxHarnessFiles int   `json:"max_harness_files"`
	MaxHarnessBytes int64 `json:"max_harness_bytes"`
}
    Limits are the notes curation triggers: past any of them the repository is
    marked for curation. None of them blocks a review or a proposal.

type MergeConflict struct{ Start, End int }
    MergeConflict is a range of base lines both sides changed differently:
    lines [Start, End) of base, 0-based.

func Merge3(base, ours, theirs string) (merged string, conflicts []MergeConflict)
    Merge3 merges the changes ours and theirs made to base, line by line (diff3,
    as `git merge-file` does it). A region of base that only one side changed
    takes that side's lines, and one both changed the same way takes them once.
    Changes that overlap or touch (an insertion next to the other side's
    change included, as git treats changes on adjacent lines) are one region,
    and when the two sides' lines for it differ the region is a conflict:
    it is listed in conflicts and merged keeps base's lines there, so merged
    means something only when conflicts is empty.

type MissChange struct {
	ID      int64  `json:"id"`
	Action  string `json:"action"`
	Section string `json:"section,omitempty"`
```
