```text
	// included (Config.RolesFor of the PR's watch); nil = Config.RolesFor(nil).
	// RolesToRun picks the ones that run.
	Roles []config.Role
	// Requested names roles (names or aliases) asked for this round
	// (`magnum review --role`, --simplify): a runs = "first" or "manual"
	// role runs when requested.
	Requested []string

	Previous *PreviousReview  // rereview/recovery: the last review by the reviewer login (or a former one)
	History  []PreviousReview // recovery: earlier reviews (Previous is used when empty)
	// FormerLogins are the logins (REST form) the PR's reviews were posted
	// as before its identity migrated to the round's: their reviews and
	// threads are the round's own history (the reply contract's threads, the
	// judge's earlier findings). Verification still accepts only the round's
	// own login, so a former login's review never counts as the round's.
	FormerLogins []string
	Since        time.Time // rereview: read every comment since then
	ForcePushed  bool
	// BaseMerged (rereview): the commits since the previous review have a
	// merge commit (the base branch merged in), so previous..TargetSHA
	// carries the base branch's commits too: the re-review prompts compare
	// the PR's own diff before and after them instead
	// (RoleData/JudgeData.BaseMerged). ForcePushed wins over it.
	BaseMerged bool
	MovedFrom  string // agents.Workspace.MovedFrom
	// DeltaCheck (rereview, or recovery for a judge in a fresh session): the
	// round is a delta check: Roles hold the judge alone, which reviews the
	// small delta since its last review (JudgeData.DeltaCheck) at its
	// rereview effort; nil = an ordinary round.
	DeltaCheck *DeltaCheck
	// SameHead (rereview, or recovery for a judge in a fresh session): the
	// round re-reviews the head the judge's last review covered, with no new
	// commits: Roles hold the judge alone, which re-decides its earlier
	// findings from the replies (JudgeData.SameHead) at its rereview effort.
	SameHead bool
	// Replies (with SameHead, or a continue of such a round): the round is
	// a reply round: that many replies came on the judge's review since it
	// last read the threads (JudgeData.Replies). When its verdict and event
	// stay, the judge answers in its threads (post-review --replies) and
	// posts no review: the round ends OutcomeReplied, verified by the
	// replies carrying its run's reply marker. 0 = an ordinary round.
	Replies int
	// Complete (rereview, recovery; with SameHead): the round completes the
	// clean review of an earlier round whose judge went without some
	// reviewers' reports for a cause that passes (complete.go): Roles hold
	// the round's candidates, of which the judge and the roles Complete
	// names run, with the reviewer prompts of the round it completes; the
	// judge gets the other roles' reports of that round and the late ones,
	// marked late. A continue of a paused completion (KindContinue) carries
	// it too, so its judge's reports are the same. nil = no completion.
	Complete *Completion
	// CIRed (with SameHead): the round is a CI follow-up: a check of the
	// head failed after the judge of its last review was prompted, so that
	// review did not see it. The judge decides each failed check of the
	// head's failing-checks.json (a P1 the PR causes, or an unrelated
	// Checks line) and posts one review (JudgeData.CIRed).
	CIRed bool
	// ColdJudge (recovery): the judge alone started in a fresh session
	// because its conversation's prompt cache had gone cold ([pipeline]
	// judge_fresh_after) or its session served the role's
	// max_session_rounds, while the reviewers kept theirs: the judge gets
	// the recovery prompt, and the reviewers re-review the commits since
	// the last review as in a re-review (their rereview prompts and effort)
	// instead of reviewing the whole PR again. The judge works at its
	// rereview effort too, and its own pass reads the commits since the
	// previous head unless the push rewrote history
	// (agents.JudgeData.ColdJudge); a recovery after a lost session reviews
	// the whole PR at the full effort.
	ColdJudge bool
	// FullPass (recovery): the round is a scheduled full pass ([pipeline]
	// full_pass_every; the engine's fullpass.go): every role started in a
	// fresh session, the reviewers review the whole PR with their
	// first-review prompts and effort (as in any recovery without
	// ColdJudge), and the judge's own pass and recovery prompt ask it to
	// review the full PR diff again as a first review does, then decide
	// every earlier thread (agents.JudgeData.FullPass).
	FullPass bool
	// Audit (recovery, with ColdJudge): the round is an audit pass
	// ([pipeline] audit_every; the engine's audit.go): every session
	// started fresh, the reviewers re-review the delta, and the judge gets
	// these areas of the PR's evidence map in AuditFile, to probe through
	// their real entry points with a control before it re-reviews the
	// delta (audit.go, agents.JudgeData.AuditFile). nil = no audit pass.
	Audit []AuditArea
	// HoldApproval (rereview, recovery, continue): the round cannot approve
	// ([pipeline] approve_after_full_pass; the engine's approval_hold.go):
	// the PR had that many re-reviews since its last full pass, so its
	// no-findings event is COMMENT (JudgeEvents' noApproveEvent) and the
	// judge's prompt says that a clean verdict posts as a comment and a full
	// pass of the whole PR follows before the approval
	// (agents.JudgeData.HoldApproval).
	HoldApproval bool
	// NoApproval: why the round cannot approve although its identity
	// would, by the approval's gates that need no review, decided at
	// dispatch (the engine's approval_gates.go: a draft, a muted PR, one
	// its watch would not review on its own, one that changes its own
	// workflows or actions or the review agents' instructions or hooks, or
	// whose files magnum cannot list), in a few fixed words that never
	// carry PR text ("the PR changes its own workflows or actions"); a
	// continue keeps the paused round's. The judge's no-findings event is
	// then COMMENT whatever the identity, and its prompt says why
	// (agents.JudgeData.NoApproval). "" = none.
	NoApproval string
	// CIGate is the approval's CI gate (the engine's approval_gates.go),
	// asked when the judge's prompt is written, a continue's too, of the
	// PR as the registry has it then (the read failing-checks.json comes
	// from) and the round's target, while the round would approve a clean
	// review: a Refusal (the target's checks fail other than the way the
	// base branch's tip fails them) makes its no-findings event COMMENT and
	// is said as NoApproval is; checks that still run, or pass, let the
	// APPROVE through. nil = no gate.
	CIGate func(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, target string) CIGateResult
	// RestartJudge starts the round's judge once more in its pane, the way
	// the round started it, when its session is gone, or herdr never
	// registered its agent, at the own pass's prompt (ownPassTurn) or at
	// its prompt for the review, the candidates prompt after an own pass
	// (judgeAgain), once for each; nil = such a prompt fails as any other.
	RestartJudge func(ctx context.Context) error

	DryRun bool // the judge posts nothing; GitHub is not consulted
	// Blind (magnum eval, with DryRun): the round replays a pinned head to
	// measure what a review finds, so its roles must not read what was
	// written about the PR later (reviews, comments, later commits) and the
	// judge takes the local diff, not GitHub's (the PR may have moved on or
	// closed). Rendered as `blind: true` in the prompts.
	Blind bool
	// Local (with Blind and DryRun): the round is the factory's local round
	// of a change before its PR exists (engine.RunLocal): no PR on GitHub to
	// read, so the judge takes the title and the body from DescriptionFile
	// and the ticket from TicketFile, as data, and the reviewers the
	// description too (agents.JudgeData.Local, RoleData.DescriptionFile).
	// nil = a round of a PR on GitHub, whose prompts render as they always
	// did.
	Local *Local
	// StoredReports (magnum eval --judge-only, with the Round of the stored
	// runs): the reviewers do not run; their reports are the files in the
	// round's report directory that their runs of Round on TargetSHA
	// verified, read as a continued round reads its paused round's
	// (existingReports), and the judge alone gets the round's prompts, its
	// own pass first when OwnPass asks and a report is there. Roles still
	// hold the reviewers, which name the reports.
	StoredReports bool
	// PostMerge: GitHub merged the PR before magnum reviewed it (the engine
	// dispatched a `magnum review` of a merged PR). The judge reviews the
	// commits magnum missed as usual but posts a COMMENT whatever the
	// identity's or repository's events (JudgeData.PostMerge, rendered as
	// `post_merge: true`), and the round dismisses no earlier review: a
	// verdict after the merge blocks nothing.
	PostMerge bool

	// NotesPath is the repository notes file the roles read and the judge
	// rewrites (RoleData/JudgeData.NotesPath); "" = none.
	NotesPath string

	// Readiness is what the round runs in the checkout before the reviewers
	// (readiness.go); the zero value still runs the built-in Ruby check
	// when the checkout pins a Ruby. A continued turn runs nothing.
	Readiness ReadinessPlan

	// ContinueRunID is the paused judge run whose marker the continued turn
	// may already have posted (KindContinue); "" uses the new run's id.
	ContinueRunID string

	// MaxRestarts bounds how often the round starts its reviewers over on a
	// head the poller recorded while they ran, before the judge is prompted
	// (daemon.max_round_restarts); 0 = never. Switch must be set too.
	MaxRestarts int
	// DispatchedHead is the PR head the poller had recorded when the round
	// was dispatched (the one its checkout asked for): a later PR head other
	// than TargetSHA is a push. "" = PR.HeadSHA.
	DispatchedHead string
	// Switch checks a newer head out in the round's slot (the caller's
	// checkout path) for a restart and reports what is checked out now.
	Switch func(ctx context.Context, sha string) (Switched, error)

	// OwnPass ([pipeline] judge_own_pass = "parallel" for the PR's watch):
	// the judge does its own pass while the reviewers work (ownpass.go) and
	// judges their reports once both ended; false prompts it once, after
	// the reviewers. A judge alone (a delta check, a continued turn, a
	// round without reviewers) gets one prompt either way.
	OwnPass bool
	// Related is the PR's watch's related_lookback and related_ignore
	// (config.Config.RelatedFor): every judge prompt names related.json, the
	// repository's other PRs that change the same paths (related.go), and
	// history.json leaves out the paths related_ignore lists (history.go).
	Related config.Related
}
    RoundInput describes one round. The slot is already checked out at TargetSHA
    (re-read the slot after slots.Checkout: CheckedOutSHA is the round's
    target).

type RoundResult struct {
	Outcome    string
	Round      int
	ReportDir  string
	JudgeRunID string // the run whose id the review's marker carries
	// TargetSHA is the commit the round reviewed: RoundInput.TargetSHA, or
	// the head of its last restart (Restarts > 0).
	TargetSHA string
	Restarts  int // how often the reviewers started over on a newer head

	ReviewID     int64
	ReviewURL    string
	ReviewCommit string
	Event        string         // APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED (dry run: the planned event)
	Findings     map[string]int // P0..P3 from the judge's result file
	// PreviousOpen is the earlier findings the review keeps open, P0..P3
	// (the result file's previous_findings.open); nil when the result gives
	// only their number, or none.
	PreviousOpen map[string]int
	// HarnessUsed are the repository notes' harness files the judge said it
	// ran or read (its result's harness_used), as written: names relative to
	// notes_dir or paths under it.
	HarnessUsed []string
	// Evidence is what the judge said it examined in the round (its
	// evidence file, validated: evidence.go), which the engine merges into
	// the PR's evidence map when the review posted; nil when it wrote none.
	Evidence *Evidence

	Pause *Pause
	// Refusal is who was refused in which run (OutcomeRefused); nil
	// otherwise.
	Refusal *Refusal
	Reports map[agents.Role]RoleReport // by role name: every non-judge role the round ran (or skipped as logged out)
	// OwnPass is how the judge's own pass ended (RoundInput.OwnPass; Path
	// set when it wrote its file); nil when the round prompted none.
	OwnPass *RoleReport
	Nudged  bool

	DismissedReviewID int64 // the stale CHANGES_REQUESTED review dismissed after posting
	Warnings          []string
	Error             string

	// Replies are the thread replies of a replied round (OutcomeReplied),
	// as GitHub shows them; none when the judge found nothing to answer.
	Replies []PostedReply
	// JudgePromptedAt is when the judge's first prompt of the round went
	// out: the replies and comments it re-decided are those it could read
	// then (zero: no judge prompt).
	JudgePromptedAt time.Time
	// NoApproval is why the judge's prompt asked for a COMMENT where its
	// identity would approve a clean review: the approval's gates refused
	// it (RoundInput.NoApproval, or CIGate's refusal when the prompt was
	// written), in their fixed words; "" = they did not. The engine keeps it
	// with the review posted (store.KVPRNoApprovalReview), so the needs-you
	// list takes that review, when clean, for an approval.
	NoApproval string
	// ThreadsRead: the round read the reviewer's threads before the judge's
	// prompt (re-reviews and recoveries), so Stops is what they say now.
	// Stops are the threads marked stop (agents.ReviewThread.Stop): after
	// two of the reviewer's rebuttals someone answered again. A posted or
	// replied round whose judge named the stopped threads it keeps open
	// (the result's stops_open) keeps only those: the others' answers
	// settled their findings.
	ThreadsRead bool
	Stops       []StopThread
	// StopsOpen are, when StopsOpenGiven, the stopped threads whose finding
	// the judge keeps open, from a posted or replied round that read no
	// threads but carries the decision of the judge an earlier round gave
	// them to: a continued turn (KindContinue), or the adoption of an
	// earlier run's review (unverified.go). That earlier round flagged its
	// stops before its judge decided them; the engine keeps only these of
	// the PR's flag. A round that read the threads leaves them unset (its
	// Stops are decided already).
	StopsOpen      []string
	StopsOpenGiven bool
}
    RoundResult is the round's verdict. The engine decides the PR state from
    Outcome (and Pause).

type Runner struct {
	Agents Agents
	GitHub GitHub       // as Identity; unused under RoundInput.DryRun
	Git    Git          // the checkout check after each stage, and restarts (nil = no check; every new head counts as a push)
	Exec   execx.Runner // the readiness step's commands, and the restore of a checkout a stage left modified
	Keys   Keys         // optional: interrupt timed-out roles (nil = leave them running)
	Store  *store.Store
	// Tickets reads the PR's Jira issue for the judge (ticket.go); nil when
	// [jira] is off.
	Tickets Tickets

	Identity identity.Source // who posts: login, kind, GH_CONFIG_DIR
	// SelfLogin is the user's own login (config.OperatorIdentity). A PR
	// authored by it or by the reviewer login is self_authored (the judge
	// posts COMMENT).
	SelfLogin string

	Config *config.Config
	Layout paths.Layout

	// OnPause pauses an agent kind at once when a run proved it logged out
	// or over its usage limit (a reviewer's run failed with the error, see
	// finishReviewerRun), before the round ends: the engine's PauseTool.
	// nil = the round's settle pauses it from the reports.
	OnPause func(ctx context.Context, p Pause)

	Clock        func() time.Time                                 // nil = time.Now
	Sleep        func(ctx context.Context, d time.Duration) error // nil = a timer honouring ctx
	PollInterval time.Duration                                    // 0 = DefaultPollInterval
	Logger       execx.Logger                                     // optional
	// Ended hands out the observe pass's run-ended broadcast
	// (agents.Manager.Ended): a channel closed when the pass next ends a
	// run or loses a session. A turn's wait selects on it beside its poll,
	// so the next stage starts as soon as the run ended. nil = the poll
	// alone.
	Ended func() <-chan struct{}
	// AgentTag is agents.Deps.Tag of the agents this runner prompts ("eval"
	// for magnum eval); it leads the shell roles' pane titles too.
	AgentTag string
	// Mise is the mise executable the readiness step runs the pool's reset_db
	// commands through (slots.MiseExecArgs, as the release does); "" means
	// "mise" on PATH. It is the slots manager's (slots.Deps.Mise).
	Mise string
}
    Runner runs review rounds. One Runner serves one identity; it holds no
    per-round state and is safe for concurrent RunRound calls.

func (r *Runner) AppendToReview(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, reviewID int64, text string) error
    AppendToReview adds text as the last paragraph of review reviewID, which
    the runner's identity posted (editReview), above the footer magnum appended
    (footerMarker), so the footer stays the last paragraph. A body that carries
    text there already is left alone.

func (r *Runner) RunRound(ctx context.Context, in RoundInput) (RoundResult, error)
    RunRound runs one round and blocks until it ends. The error is non-nil
    only when Outcome is error (the round could not run or be evaluated) or
    stopped because ctx was cancelled; every other outcome, including timeouts
    and pauses, returns a nil error. Run rows created but never prompted are
    abandoned; runs already sent stay submitted/working when ctx is cancelled
    (they are observed, never re-sent).

type Sibling struct {
	File    string `json:"file"`
	Sibling string `json:"sibling"`
}
    Sibling is an added file and the closest existing file to it.

type StopThread struct {
	ID        string // GraphQL node id
	URL       string // its first comment's
	LastReply int64  // the answer after the second rebuttal (the thread's last reply)
}
    StopThread is a thread where the reviewer stopped arguing
    (agents.ReviewThread.Stop).

type Switched struct {
	TargetSHA   string // the commit now checked out (a fetch may find a newer one); "" = the one asked for
	BaseSHA     string // its merge base with the base ("" = unknown: the round keeps the old one)
	ForcePushed bool   // the previous review's commit is not an ancestor of TargetSHA
	BaseMerged  bool   // the commits since the previous review have a merge commit (RoundInput.BaseMerged)
}
    Switched is the checkout after RoundInput.Switch.

type ThreadLister interface {
	ReviewThreads(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int) ([]github.Thread, error)
}
    ThreadLister is implemented by a GitHub client that lists a pull request's
    review threads with their comments (github.Client.ReviewThreads). Optional:
    without it a re-review names no threads file and the judge reads the replies
    itself.

type Tickets interface {
	Ticket(ctx context.Context, key string) (jira.Ticket, error)
	// WarnTokenFile reports whether a token file problem is a warning:
	// true once per daemon start, then false (info), as the config's
	// warning already names it.
	WarnTokenFile() bool
}
    Tickets reads Jira issues: *jira.Client, made once per daemon start.

```

## postreview

```text
package postreview // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/postreview"

Package postreview is `magnum post-review`, the judge's posting tool.
The judge writes its review (event, body, inline comments) to a file; Run checks
it (the fields, then every inline anchor against the pull request's diff),
posts it once as the judge's identity (never twice: a review carrying the run's
marker counts as posted) and reads it back. RunReplies is its replies-only mode:
when authors answered the judge's threads and the head is unchanged, the judge
answers in the threads instead, each reply carrying a hidden marker the daemon
verifies and counts rebuttals by. It works from its Options, gh and git in the
checkout alone: it loads no config, opens no registry, never contacts the daemon
and writes no file.

CONSTANTS

const (
	PostConversation  = "conversation"   // a comment on the PR's conversation
	PostReply         = "reply"          // a reply in a review thread
	PostTitle         = "title"          // a new title
	PostReviewRequest = "review_request" // a review request
)
    The kinds of post magnum comment makes (Posted.Kind, CommentPart.Kind).

const (
	ReplyAck      = "ack"      // a reason the judge accepts: one short acknowledgement
	ReplyRebuttal = "rebuttal" // the judge keeps the finding: one sentence with evidence
	ReplyAnswer   = "answer"   // an answer to a question
)
    Reply kinds (Reply.Kind).

const (
	StatusPosted           = "posted"            // posted and read back
	StatusAlreadyPosted    = "already_posted"    // a review carrying the run's marker exists; nothing posted
	StatusDryRun           = "dry_run"           // checked; nothing posted (Outcome.PlannedReview)
	StatusInvalid          = "invalid"           // the review file is wrong (Outcome.Problems)
	StatusInvalidAnchors   = "invalid_anchors"   // inline comments off the diff (Outcome.InvalidAnchors)
	StatusRejected         = "rejected"          // GitHub refused the review and none was created
	StatusError            = "error"             // anything else; Outcome.Message says what
	StatusReadbackMismatch = "readback_mismatch" // posted, but the review reads back differently
)
    Outcome statuses (Outcome.Status).

const (
	EventComment        = "COMMENT"
	EventRequestChanges = "REQUEST_CHANGES"
	EventApprove        = "APPROVE"
)
    Review events the judge may post.

const (
	SideRight = "RIGHT" // the head's lines: added or context
	SideLeft  = "LEFT"  // the base's lines: deleted or context
)
    Sides of an inline comment.

const CommentMarker = "<!-- magnum:comment -->"
    CommentMarker ends every comment `magnum comment` posts: a chat session's
    comment, posted as the watch's fixer App. By it magnum tells these comments
    from the author's replies and from the fixer's (FixReplyMarker): they are
    magnum's own word, never the author's, and never a reply that starts a
    review round or a fix loop. As with the fix marker, it means that only in a
    comment of one of magnum's logins.

const FixReplyMarker = "<!-- magnum:fix -->"
    FixReplyMarker ends every reply the fixer posts (skills/magnum-fix/SKILL.md,
    section 6). The fixer posts as the PR's author, the operator, whose login a
    gh identity shares, so the retro (learn.OwnThreads) tells its answers from
    the author's by this marker alone.

const FooterMarker = "<!-- magnum:footer -->"
    FooterMarker starts the footer magnum appends to a verified review
    (pipeline's footerMarker); a judge never writes it.

const MaxBody = 65536
    MaxBody is GitHub's limit for a review body and for a comment body,
    in characters.

const StatusReplied = "replied"
    StatusReplied: the replies are posted, or were all posted already.


FUNCTIONS

func IsComment(body string) bool
    IsComment reports whether body carries CommentMarker.

func IsFixReply(body string) bool
    IsFixReply reports whether body carries FixReplyMarker.

func IsOwnAnswer(body string) bool
    IsOwnAnswer reports whether body is an answer of magnum's side to someone
    else's comment: a fixer's reply or a magnum comment. A reader asks it only
    of a comment by one of magnum's logins (or, for a fix reply, the author's,
    whom a gh fixer posts as).

func ParseReplyMarker(body string) (runID, kind string, ok bool)
    ParseReplyMarker reads the reply marker in body: its run id and kind;
    ok is false when body has none.

func ReplyMarker(runID, kind string) string
    ReplyMarker is the line every reply of run carries: `<!-- magnum:reply
    run=<run id> kind=<kind> -->`. The daemon finds a round's replies on GitHub
    by it, and counts magnum's rebuttals per thread.

func RunMarker(runID, head string) string
    RunMarker is the line every review of run carries, on head: `<!--
    magnum:run=<run id> head=<first 7 of head> -->`.


TYPES

type BadAnchor struct {
	Index     int    `json:"index"` // in the review file's comments
	Path      string `json:"path"`
	Line      int    `json:"line"`
	StartLine int    `json:"start_line,omitempty"`
	Side      string `json:"side"`
	Why       string `json:"why"`
	// Valid are the line ranges of the file's hunks on that side
	// ("12-20"); empty for a file the pull request does not change.
	Valid []string `json:"valid"`
}
    BadAnchor is an inline comment GitHub would refuse: its line (or its
    start_line) is not a line of the pull request's diff on its side.

type CommentGitHub interface {
	FixReplyGitHub
	RecentReviews(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, stop func(github.Review) bool) ([]github.Review, bool, error)
	Pull(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int) (github.Pull, error)
	RequestReviewers(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, logins []string) error
	UpdatePullTitle(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, title string) (github.Pull, error)
}
    CommentGitHub is what RunComment reads and writes on GitHub (*github.Client,
    as the watch's fixer App).

type CommentOptions struct {
	Owner, Repo    string
	Number         int
	ReplyTo        int64
	RequestReviews []string
	Title          *string
	Login          string
	Identity       string
	MagnumLogins   []string
	DryRun         bool
}
    CommentOptions name what `magnum comment` does on a pull request:
    a comment on the conversation, or with ReplyTo a reply in the review
    thread of that comment (any comment of it); a new Title; review requests of
    RequestReviews (users' logins). Login is the App it posts as (Account form),
    the one GitHub must show as the author, and Identity the name of its
    [[identity]]; MagnumLogins are the logins whose threads magnum's review
    started (config.Config.MagnumThreadLogins, or for a PR in the registry
    PRThreadLogins, and the PR's last reviewer), where it refuses to reply.
    DryRun reads and checks everything and posts nothing.

func (o CommentOptions) Check() (out CommentOutcome, ok bool)
    Check is the outcome RunComment refuses o with (ok false) before it reads
    anything: what the line got wrong (the pull request, the comment id,
    the title, a login) is StatusInvalid, exit 2, the caller's to fix; no App
    login is the caller's own error.

func (o CommentOptions) CheckText(text []byte) (out CommentOutcome, ok bool)
    CheckText is Check with text, the comment read from stdin, checked too:
    one is needed for the conversation and for a reply, and it follows
    fix-reply's rules (not empty, no magnum marker, no local path, not too long
    once marked). The caller asks it before it mints a token.

type CommentOutcome struct {
	Status         string             `json:"status"`
	Message        string             `json:"message,omitempty"`
	Problems       []string           `json:"problems,omitempty"`
	PR             string             `json:"pr"`
	Identity       string             `json:"identity,omitempty"`
	As             string             `json:"as,omitempty"`
	Comment        *CommentPart       `json:"comment,omitempty"`
	Title          *TitlePart         `json:"title,omitempty"`
	ReviewRequests *ReviewRequestPart `json:"review_requests,omitempty"`
	Event          string             `json:"event,omitempty"`
}
    CommentOutcome is what RunComment printed: a status (StatusPosted,
    StatusAlreadyPosted, StatusDryRun, StatusInvalid or StatusError), the
    pull request, the identity and the login it posts as, and each part done,
    found done or planned. Event is the CLI's note of a registry record it could
    not write.

func RunComment(ctx context.Context, gh CommentGitHub, o CommentOptions, text []byte, onPosted func(Posted)) CommentOutcome
    RunComment does what o names on its pull request as the App o.Login (gh
    is its client): text, when it says something, signed with CommentMarker,
    as a reply in the thread of o.ReplyTo (to its first comment) or on the
    conversation; then the title; then the review requests. Everything is
    checked before the first write: the line and text (fix-reply's rules: empty,
    a magnum marker, a local path, too long), the pull request (its author is
    never asked for a review), the comment id (one of this pull request's,
    and in no thread magnum's review started: the daemon's poll reads no
    comment text and would take the App's reply there for the author's).
    A comment the same as one of the App's already there with nobody else's
    after it (postedLast; on the conversation nobody else's review either,
    reviewedSince) is not posted again, a title already so is not sent,
    and a login asked already is skipped, so after an unclear failure the same
    line runs again safely. GitHub must show the App as each comment's author:
    another account there is StatusInvalid (otherAuthor) and nothing more goes
    out, and the newest copy of the same comment found by another account is
    StatusInvalid before the first write (alreadyByOther). onPosted (nil: none)
    hears of each post, with the author GitHub showed when it is not the App,
    and of a comment found already there.

func (o CommentOutcome) ExitCode() int
    ExitCode is 0 when everything is on GitHub (posted, already there) or a dry
    run checked it, 2 when the comment or the line must change, and 1 otherwise:
    something could not be confirmed, so run the same line with the same text
    again.

func (o CommentOutcome) Summary() string
    Summary is the outcome in one line (ids and links, no comment or title
    text).

type CommentPart struct {
	Kind    string `json:"kind"`
	Thread  int64  `json:"thread,omitempty"`
	ID      int64  `json:"id,omitempty"`
	URL     string `json:"url,omitempty"`
	Already bool   `json:"already"`
	Planned bool   `json:"planned,omitempty"`
	// Author is who GitHub shows wrote the comment posted when that is not
	// the App (Posted.Author); "" when it is.
	Author string `json:"author,omitempty"`
}
    CommentPart is the comment of an outcome: on the conversation or a reply
    in the thread of Thread (its first comment), its id and link, posted,
    found already there, or (dry run) planned.

type Deps struct {
	GitHub GitHub
	Git    Git
	Dir    string
}
    Deps are Run's GitHub, as the judge's identity, and git in Dir, the checkout
    ("." = the current directory).

type FixReplyGitHub interface {
	AllReviewThreads(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int) ([]github.Thread, bool, error)
	ReplyToReviewComment(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, commentID int64, body string) (github.ReviewCommentReply, error)
	IssueComments(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, stop func(github.PRComment) bool) ([]github.PRComment, bool, error)
	CreateIssueComment(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, body string) (github.IssueComment, error)
}
    FixReplyGitHub is what RunFixReply reads and writes on GitHub
    (*github.Client, as the fixer's gh login: the PR's author).

type FixReplyOptions struct {
	Owner, Repo string
	Number      int
	CommentID   int64
	Issue       bool
}
    FixReplyOptions name what `magnum fix-reply` answers: the pull request (the
    fixer's pane's MAGNUM_PR_URL) and either a review comment, whose thread
    the reply goes into (CommentID: its first comment or any reply in it),
    or the pull request's conversation (Issue).

func (o FixReplyOptions) Check() (out FixReplyOutcome, ok bool)
    Check is the outcome RunFixReply refuses o with (ok false; `magnum
    fix-reply` asks it before it reads the reply too). A pull request the
    fixer's pane names wrongly (its MAGNUM_PR_URL) is StatusError, exit 1:
    nothing the fixer types mends it. What the fixer's line got wrong, a comment
    id below 1, or both or neither of --comment and --issue, is StatusInvalid,
    exit 2, the fixer's to fix: exit 1 would tell it that the reply could not be
    confirmed and to run the same line once more.

type FixReplyOutcome struct {
	Status   string   `json:"status"`
	Message  string   `json:"message,omitempty"`  // what went wrong (error)
	Problems []string `json:"problems,omitempty"` // why the reply was refused (invalid)
	// Thread is the first comment of the thread the reply went into, 0 for
	// a comment on the conversation; ID and URL are the reply's, posted or
	// found already there.
	Thread int64  `json:"thread,omitempty"`
	ID     int64  `json:"id,omitempty"`
	URL    string `json:"url,omitempty"`
}
    FixReplyOutcome is what RunFixReply printed: a status (StatusReplied,
    StatusAlreadyPosted, StatusInvalid or StatusError) and its details.

func RunFixReply(ctx context.Context, gh FixReplyGitHub, o FixReplyOptions, text []byte) FixReplyOutcome
    RunFixReply posts text, one reply of the fixer, on the pull request o names,
    as gh's login, which is the PR's author: the text, a blank line and
    FixReplyMarker, by which magnum tells the fixer's replies from the author's
    own (learn.OwnThreads, the fix job's external file). It refuses a reply
    that is empty, carries a magnum marker of its own, names a local path or
    is too long before it reads GitHub. With a comment id it reads the review
    threads once, refuses a comment that is in none of them (one of another pull
    request, or of none) and answers its thread's first comment, the only one
    GitHub takes a reply to; with Issue it writes a comment on the conversation.
    A thread, or the conversation, that already holds the same marked reply
    with nobody else's comment after it gets nothing more (StatusAlreadyPosted,
    postedLast), so a retry after an unclear failure posts the reply once,
    while the same answer to new pushback goes out.

func (o FixReplyOutcome) ExitCode() int
    ExitCode is 0 for a reply posted or already there, 2 when the fixer must fix
    its reply or its line (the comment it names, its flags), 1 otherwise.

func (o FixReplyOutcome) Summary() string
    Summary is the outcome in one line (ids and links, no reply text).

type Git interface {
	RevParse(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) (string, error)
	MergeBase(ctx context.Context, dir, a, b string) (string, error)
	FileDiff(ctx context.Context, dir, base, head, path string) (string, error)
}
    Git is what Run reads from the checkout (*gitx.Client).

type GitHub interface {
	PullSHAs(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int) (base, head string, err error)
	PullFiles(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int) ([]github.FileDelta, bool, error)
	CompareFiles(ctx context.Context, owner, repo, base, head string) ([]github.FileDelta, error)
	// AllReviews (and whether the list is complete) is the post-once
	// guard's: a review carrying the run's marker is the review.
	AllReviews(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int) ([]github.Review, bool, error)
	SubmitReview(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, r github.ReviewRequest) (github.RESTReview, error)
	ReviewREST(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, id int64) (github.RESTReview, error)
	ReviewComments(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, reviewID int64) ([]github.ReviewComment, error)
	// ReviewThreads and ReplyToReviewComment are RunReplies's.
	ReviewThreads(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int) ([]github.Thread, error)
	ReplyToReviewComment(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, number int, commentID int64, body string) (github.ReviewCommentReply, error)
}
    GitHub is what Run reads and writes on GitHub (*github.Client, as the
    judge's identity).

type Options struct {
	Owner, Repo string
	Number      int
	HeadSHA     string // the reviewed commit: the review's commit_id
	RunID       string // the round's marker id
	Login       string // reviewer_login, REST form ("talkable[bot]")
	// FormerLogins posted this PR's reviews before its identity migrated: a
	// review of theirs carrying the marker counts as posted too.
	FormerLogins []string
	DryRun       bool // check everything, post nothing
	// LocalBase (a blind replay, with DryRun): check the anchors against
	// `git diff LocalBase HeadSHA` in the checkout and read nothing from
	// GitHub, whose pull request may have moved on since HeadSHA.
	LocalBase string
	// NoFindingsEvent is the round's no-findings event, the judge prompt's
	// no_findings_event (EventApprove or EventComment; "" = not given, any
	// event goes): with EventComment the round cannot approve, so Parse
	// refuses a review whose event is EventApprove, and the judge rewrites
	// its file. REQUEST_CHANGES stays the judge's to post either way.
	NoFindingsEvent string
}
    Options are the run's facts, from the judge's <magnum> block.

func (o Options) Check() error
    Check reports what is wrong with o.

type Outcome struct {
	Status  string `json:"status"`
	Message string `json:"message,omitempty"` // what went wrong (error, rejected), or what was found
	// Problems are the review or replies file's faults (invalid).
	Problems []string `json:"problems,omitempty"`
	// InvalidAnchors are the comments off the diff (invalid_anchors).
	InvalidAnchors []BadAnchor `json:"invalid_anchors,omitempty"`
	// Unchecked are the indexes of comments no diff could check (a binary
	// or too large file without its commits in the checkout): kept, GitHub
	// decides.
	Unchecked []int `json:"unchecked_anchors,omitempty"`
	// MarkerAppended: the body lacked the run marker; it was added as its
	// last line.
	MarkerAppended bool `json:"marker_appended,omitempty"`

	ReviewID  int64  `json:"review_id,omitempty"`
	ReviewURL string `json:"review_url,omitempty"`
	Event     string `json:"event,omitempty"` // the event posted (or, already posted, the review's)
	// EventDowngraded: GitHub refused a self-verdict, so the review went
	// out as COMMENT.
	EventDowngraded bool   `json:"event_downgraded,omitempty"`
	State           string `json:"state,omitempty"` // as read back
	CommitID        string `json:"commit_id,omitempty"`
	Comments        *int   `json:"comments,omitempty"` // inline comments read back (dry run: planned)
	// Mismatches say how the review read back differs (readback_mismatch).
	Mismatches []string `json:"mismatches,omitempty"`
	// PlannedReview is the request a dry run would have sent.
	PlannedReview *github.ReviewRequest `json:"planned_review,omitempty"`
	// Replies are the replies RunReplies posted (so far, after a failure),
	// found already posted, or planned in a dry run, in the file's order.
	Replies []PostedReply `json:"replies,omitempty"`
	// Skipped are the replies RunReplies did not post because another
	// reviewer or the author started their thread, in the file's order.
	Skipped []SkippedReply `json:"skipped,omitempty"`
}
    Outcome is what Run printed: a status and its details. ExitCode maps it to
    the command's exit status.

func Run(ctx context.Context, d Deps, o Options, data []byte) Outcome
    Run posts the judge's review file data for the run o names: check the file,
    check its inline anchors against the pull request's diff, look for a review
    already carrying the run's marker, then post (or, in a dry run, plan) the
    review once and read it back.

func RunReplies(ctx context.Context, d Deps, o Options, data []byte) Outcome
    RunReplies posts the judge's replies file data for the run o names (o's head
    is only checked for form: a reply answers a thread, whatever its commit). It
    checks the file, reads the review threads once, and checks that each reply
    answers the first comment of a thread on the pull request and that magnum
    has not already rebutted twice there; a reply to a thread someone other
    than the reviewer (or a former login) started is skipped (Outcome.Skipped),
    not refused; a thread that already holds a reply carrying the run's marker
    gets nothing more, so the tool is safe to run again after a failure.
    Then it posts the other replies in file order (or, in a dry run, plans them)
    and stops at the first failure: replied even when it posted nothing.

func (o Outcome) ExitCode() int
    ExitCode is 0 for posted, already posted, replied and a dry run, 2 when the
    judge must fix its file, 1 otherwise.

func (o Outcome) Summary() string
    Summary is the outcome in one human line (ids and counts, no PR text).

type Posted struct {
	Kind      string   // PostConversation, PostReply, PostTitle or PostReviewRequest
	CommentID int64    // the comment's (PostConversation, PostReply)
	Thread    int64    // the first comment of the reply's thread (PostReply)
	URL       string   // the comment's link; the pull request's for a title or a review request
	Reviewers []string // the logins asked (PostReviewRequest)
	Already   bool     // the comment was there already: nothing posted now
	// Author is who GitHub shows wrote the comment when that is not the
	// App (Account form; "an account it does not name" when it named
	// none): a wrong login in the config, or a post under a person's
	// login. "" when it is the App.
	Author string
}
    Posted is one post RunComment made, or (Already) a comment it found already
    there from an earlier run: what the caller records.

type PostedReply struct {
	CommentID int64  `json:"comment_id"`
	ID        int64  `json:"id,omitempty"`
	URL       string `json:"url,omitempty"`
	Kind      string `json:"kind"`
	Already   bool   `json:"already,omitempty"` // posted by an earlier run of the tool for this run id: not posted again
}
    PostedReply is a reply RunReplies posted, found already posted by this run,
    or (dry run) planned.

type RepliesFile struct {
	Replies []Reply `json:"replies"`
}
    RepliesFile is the file the judge writes for --replies.

type Reply struct {
	CommentID int64  `json:"comment_id"` // the thread's first comment (threads_file's comment_id)
	Kind      string `json:"kind"`
	Body      string `json:"body"`
}
    Reply is one answer in a review thread.

type Review struct {
	Event    string                `json:"event"`
	Body     string                `json:"body"`
	Comments []github.DraftComment `json:"comments"`
}
    Review is the file the judge writes: the review to post. Comments use
    GitHub's fields (path, line, side, start_line, start_side, body).

func Parse(data []byte, o Options) (r Review, appended bool, problems []string)
    Parse decodes and checks the judge's review file for the run o names.
    It returns the review to post, with each comment's side (RIGHT unless
    given) and a multi-line comment's start side filled in and the run's marker
    appended as the body's last line when the body lacks it (appended reports
    that), or the problems found, each naming its field. An APPROVE in a round
    whose no-findings event is COMMENT (Options.NoFindingsEvent) is one of them.

type ReviewRequestPart struct {
	Requested []string `json:"requested"`
	Already   []string `json:"already"`
	Planned   bool     `json:"planned,omitempty"`
}
    ReviewRequestPart is the review requests of an outcome: the logins asked
    (or, planned, to ask) and the ones asked already, whom it skipped.

type SkippedReply struct {
	CommentID int64  `json:"comment_id"`
	Kind      string `json:"kind"`
	Reason    string `json:"reason"` // who started the thread (no text)
}
    SkippedReply is a reply RunReplies did not post because its thread is not
    the reviewer's: another reviewer or the author started it, so it is theirs
    and never answered inline (DECISIONS "An author's own inline threads are not
    replies").

type TitlePart struct {
	Changed bool `json:"changed"`
	Already bool `json:"already"`
	Planned bool `json:"planned,omitempty"`
}
    TitlePart is the title of an outcome: changed, already so, or planned.
```

## prstatus

```text
package prstatus // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/prstatus"

Package prstatus is the contract of the factory part of a PR's status
comment: one JSON file per PR a factory task published, <factory
dir>/pr-status/<owner>/<repo>/<number>.json (Path, which takes GitHub names
only, in lower case, and a positive number).

  - Who writes: the factory daemon (Write), from the publish on, and only when
    the content changes: no file exists before the PR is published.
  - Who reads: magnum's review daemon, read-only (Read), to render it in the
    status comment it already keeps on the PR. A missing file is no factory
    part; a file Read refuses counts as missing.
  - Fixed words only: counts, enums, times, the task id, the Jira key and the
    staging environment's slug, never free text from a PR, a ticket, a question
    or an agent. Every enum is a string type whose Valid lists its words,
    and Read refuses any other word.
  - Version rule: v is Version, and Read refuses any other. A field that changes
    its meaning or its type, or goes away, bumps it. A new field or a new
    word of an enum keeps it: a reader ignores the fields it does not know,
    and refuses only a file that holds a word it does not know.
  - Digest rule: digest is the hex sha256 of the canonical JSON of every field
    but updated_at and digest, the fields a reader does not know included:
    encoding/json's encoding of the object decoded as a map (keys sorted at
    every level, no spaces, numbers as written). Neither the order of the keys
    nor the update time changes it. Read refuses a file whose digest does not
    match; Write writes nothing when the file already has the digest, so an
    unchanged status costs no write and no edit of the comment.

It imports only the standard library, internal/paths and internal/fsx (the
atomic write and the capped read; a leaf internal/paths already imports),
so either daemon imports it without the other.

CONSTANTS

const MaxSize = 64 << 10
    MaxSize is the most bytes Read reads: a bigger file is refused.

const Version = 1
    Version is the schema version Write writes and Read accepts.


VARIABLES

var (
	ErrTooBig   = errors.New("over 64 KiB")
	ErrCutShort = errors.New("cut short")
	ErrNotJSON  = errors.New("not a JSON object")
	ErrVersion  = errors.New("unknown schema version")
	ErrInvalid  = errors.New("invalid field")
	ErrDigest   = errors.New("digest does not match the content")
)
    Read's refusals, each wrapped with the file's path (and, for ErrInvalid,
    the field's name, never its value).


FUNCTIONS

func Path(l paths.Layout, owner, repo string, number int) (string, error)
    Path is the status file of PR number of owner/repo in l's factory directory:
    paths.Layout.FactoryPRStatus, then owner, repo and <number>.json. owner and
    repo must be GitHub names (no "." or "..", no slash, not empty) and number
    positive, or Path refuses them. The names are lower-cased: GitHub ignores
    their case, so the writer's spelling and the reader's name one file.

func StagingEnv(name string) string
    StagingEnv is the Env of the configured staging environment name: the name
    when it is a slug, else "" (the row then has the state without a name),
    so a name such as "Alpha" or "qa env" never makes Write refuse the status.

func Write(path string, s Status) (bool, error)
    Write writes s to path when its content differs from the file's, and reports
    whether it wrote. It sets V and Digest, keeps the times in UTC to the second
    (a zero UpdatedAt is the time of the write) and refuses a status Read would
    refuse (ErrInvalid), writing nothing. When the file on disk has the same
    digest it writes nothing and returns false, so the file keeps the UpdatedAt
    of the last change. The write is atomic and durable: a temporary file in
    the same folder, synced, renamed over the file, then the folder synced;
    the file is 0600, the folders it makes 0700.


TYPES

type Code struct {
	Commits int   `json:"commits"`
	Proof   Proof `json:"proof"`
	Specs   int   `json:"specs"`
}
    Code is the change: its commits, its proof and its specs.

type FixLoop struct {
	State           FixState `json:"state"`
	Cycle           int      `json:"cycle"`
	Pushes          int      `json:"pushes"`
	ThreadsAnswered int      `json:"threads_answered"`
}
    FixLoop is magnum's fix loop on the PR: its state, its cycle, its pushes and
    the review threads it answered.

type FixState string
    FixState is the fix loop's state: none yet, running, needing you, done,
    or off for the PR.

const (
	FixNone     FixState = "none"
	FixRunning  FixState = "running"
	FixNeedsYou FixState = "needs_you"
	FixDone     FixState = "done"
	FixOff      FixState = "off"
)
    The fix loop's states.

func (s FixState) Valid() bool
    Valid reports whether s is one of the fix loop's states.

type Jira struct {
	Key    string     `json:"key"`
	Status JiraStatus `json:"status"`
}
    Jira is the task's Jira issue: its key (ABC-123) and status. Both are "" for
    a task without an issue.

func JiraOf(key string, status JiraStatus) Jira
    JiraOf is the Jira of a task's issue key with status: the zero Jira (no
    issue) for a key that is not one the file takes (ABC-123), so the writer's
    key never makes Write refuse the status.

type JiraStatus string
    JiraStatus is the issue's status, in the factory's words.

const (
	JiraToDo          JiraStatus = "to_do"
	JiraInDevelopment JiraStatus = "in_development"
	JiraInCodeReview  JiraStatus = "in_code_review"
	JiraDone          JiraStatus = "done"
	JiraOther         JiraStatus = "other"
	JiraUnknown       JiraStatus = "unknown"
)
    The Jira statuses.

func JiraStatusOf(category, name string) JiraStatus
    JiraStatusOf is the file's word for an issue's status, by Jira's category
    of it (its statusCategory key) and its name, case aside: new is to_do and
    done is done; indeterminate is in_code_review when the name holds "review",
    in_development when it holds one of devWords, else other (a QA, a deploy,
    a block: "in development" would tell the reviewer something false);
    any other category, "" included, is other. A task whose issue was never read
    is unknown, which the writer says without this.

func (s JiraStatus) Valid() bool
    Valid reports whether s is one of the Jira statuses.

type LocalReview struct {
	Rounds    int     `json:"rounds"`
	Verdict   Verdict `json:"verdict"`
	NotesOpen int     `json:"notes_open"`
}
    LocalReview is the local review's rounds, its last verdict and the notes it
    left open.

type Now struct {
	Who   Who   `json:"who"`
	Stage Stage `json:"stage"`
}
    Now is who the PR waits on and the task's stage.

type Plan struct {
	QuestionsAsked    int `json:"questions_asked"`
	QuestionsAnswered int `json:"questions_answered"`
}
    Plan counts the questions the task asked you and the ones you answered.

type Proof string
    Proof is what the coding stage proved: nothing yet, the spec red on the
    base, red on the base and green at the head, or (a kind whose proof is
    green) the specs green at the head.

const (
	ProofNone       Proof = "none"
	ProofRed        Proof = "red"
	ProofRedToGreen Proof = "red_to_green"
	ProofGreen      Proof = "green"
)
    The proofs.

func (p Proof) Valid() bool
    Valid reports whether p is one of the proofs.

type Stage string
    Stage is the task's stage, in fixed words: the phase its kind's configured
    stage falls in (a kind names its own stages; these words do not change with
    it), then the task's state once it is published.

const (
	StagePlan      Stage = "plan"      // investigate, judge, critic and the questions and reproduction gates
	StageCode      Stage = "code"      // the writer's stage, up to its proof
	StageReview    Stage = "review"    // the local review loop
	StageReady     Stage = "ready"     // the PR body and the ready card
	StagePublished Stage = "published" // the PR is open
	StageDone      Stage = "done"      // the PR merged
	StageStopped   Stage = "stopped"   // you stopped the task
	StageFailed    Stage = "failed"    // the task failed
)
    The stages.

func (s Stage) Valid() bool
    Valid reports whether s is one of the stages.

type Staging struct {
	Env   string       `json:"env"`
	State StagingState `json:"state"`
}
    Staging is the deploy of the change to one staging environment:
    Env is the configured staging environment's name when it is a short slug
    ([a-z0-9-]{1,32}), else "". The config takes any name that is not blank,
    and Write refuses a whole status whose Env is not a slug, so the writer sets
    Env with StagingEnv.

type StagingState string
    StagingState is the staging deploy's state.

const (
	StagingNone      StagingState = "none"
	StagingDeploying StagingState = "deploying"
	StagingDeployed  StagingState = "deployed"
	StagingFailed    StagingState = "failed"
)
    The staging deploy's states.

func (s StagingState) Valid() bool
    Valid reports whether s is one of the staging deploy's states.

type Status struct {
	// V is the schema version, Version.
	V int `json:"v"`
	// Digest is the hex sha256 of the content (the package doc's digest
	// rule); Write sets it.
	Digest string `json:"digest"`
	// UpdatedAt is when the content last changed, in UTC to the second
	// (Write keeps the file, and its time, while the content stays the same);
	// never zero. It is outside the digest, so Read checks it on its own.
	UpdatedAt time.Time `json:"updated_at"`
	// TaskID is the factory task that published the PR, positive.
	TaskID int64 `json:"task_id"`
	// Jira is the task's issue; the zero Jira says it has none.
	Jira Jira `json:"jira"`
	// Plan counts the task's questions.
	Plan Plan `json:"plan"`
	// Code is the change's commits, proof and specs.
	Code Code `json:"code"`
	// LocalReview is the factory's review of the change before the publish.
	LocalReview LocalReview `json:"local_review"`
	// PublishedAt is when the PR was published, in UTC to the second; never
	// zero, since the file begins at the publish.
	PublishedAt time.Time `json:"published_at"`
	// FixLoop is magnum's fix loop on the PR.
	FixLoop FixLoop `json:"fix_loop"`
	// Staging is the change's deploy to a staging environment: the first of
	// Stagings, for the readers from before them, or {state: none} for a
	// repository without one.
	Staging Staging `json:"staging"`
	// Stagings are the change's deploys to each staging environment of its
	// repository, in the config's order; none (no key) for a repository
	// without one. A field added under v=1: a reader before it ignores it.
	Stagings []Staging `json:"stagings,omitempty"`
	// Now is who the PR waits on, and the task's stage.
	Now Now `json:"now"`
}
    Status is one PR's factory part. Every count is 0 or more, every enum one of
    its words and both times set; Write refuses, and Read refuses, any other.

func Read(path string) (Status, bool, error)
    Read reads the status file at path, a regular file of at most MaxSize bytes
    (a symbolic link is refused, not followed). A missing file is no status:
    (zero, false, nil). A file Read refuses is the zero Status and an error
    that says why (errors.Is ErrTooBig, ErrCutShort, ErrNotJSON, ErrVersion,
    ErrInvalid or ErrDigest), in fixed words and the field's name, never the
    file's content; the caller treats it as missing. Fields Read does not know
    are ignored, and the digest covers them.

type Verdict string
    Verdict is the local review's last verdict.

const (
	VerdictNone     Verdict = "none"
	VerdictClean    Verdict = "clean"
	VerdictFindings Verdict = "findings"
	VerdictFailed   Verdict = "failed"
)
    The verdicts.

func (v Verdict) Valid() bool
    Valid reports whether v is one of the verdicts.

type Who string
    Who is who the PR waits on.

const (
	WhoYou       Who = "you"
	WhoMagnum    Who = "magnum"
	WhoReviewers Who = "reviewers"
	WhoCI        Who = "ci"
	WhoFactory   Who = "factory"
	WhoNone      Who = "none"
)
    Who the PR can wait on.

func (w Who) Valid() bool
    Valid reports whether w is one of who a PR waits on.

```

## prview

```text
package prview // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/prview"

Package prview is a PR of magnum's registry as magnum's screens draw it:
the head's CI (CI) and the findings of magnum's last posted review (Findings,
Held), so the PR board's CI and FINDINGS columns and the factory screen's say
the same of a PR. It reads the registry and writes nothing; the painters are
internal/tui's.

FUNCTIONS

func CI(ci *store.CIStatus, head string, req store.RequiredChecks, m Merge) *tui.CIInfo
    CI is a PR's CIInfo at head, by its repository's required checks req
    (store.Store.RequiredChecks): ci is the head's checks as magnum's readers
    see them (store.SeenCI, the checks ignore_checks names left out); nil when
    magnum has no checks for the PR yet. A required check is matched by name
    across workflows (store.RequiredRuns), one that never ran on the head is
    "missing", and the checks of an older commit than head leave every required
    check that did not fail pending. The failed checks keep their pages (Links),
    and GitHub's merge state of the read says, with m, why it blocks the merge
    (Blocked, mergeBlock); it never makes a check green.

func CheckLabel(pattern string) string
    CheckLabel is a required check's short name on the screens: without the
    "workflow:" prefix, and a glob without its trailing wildcards and the
    separators before them ("ci / *" → "ci", "rspec*" → "rspec"); the pattern
    itself when nothing would be left ("*").

func Findings(s store.ReviewSummary, held bool) *tui.FindingsInfo
    Findings is magnum's posted review s as the FINDINGS columns say it;
    held says the review held its approval (Held).

func Held(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, prID int64, s store.ReviewSummary) bool
    Held reports whether s, PR prID's latest posted review, held its
    approval ([pipeline] approve_after_full_pass): the approval hold record
    (engine.KVPRApprovalHold) names that very review, as the engine's
    heldReviewOf requires; one it left behind for an older review holds nothing.
    Only a clean verdict holds, so no other reads the record; a clean comment
    without one is a comment-only repository's. A registry that cannot say holds
    nothing.


TYPES

type Merge struct {
	Draft    bool
	Decision string
}
    Merge is what CI reads of a PR beside its checks to say why GitHub blocks
    its merge (tui.CIInfo.Blocked): whether it is a draft, and GitHub's
    review decision (store.ReviewGate.Decision: APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED or
    REVIEW_REQUIRED; "" when its base requires no review or magnum has not read
    the gate).

```

## relay

```text
package relay // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/relay"

Package relay is magnum-relay, the small service that receives a GitHub App's
webhook deliveries and keeps them for magnum's daemon, which sleeps behind NAT
and cannot receive them itself.

POST /github/webhook refuses, before it reads the body or takes a turn,
a request whose X-Hub-Signature-256, X-GitHub-Event or X-GitHub-Delivery header
is missing or malformed (401, 400), and closes its connection. Then it waits
for one of a few turns and reads the body whole (at most 26 MiB, 413 above),
both within DefaultBodyTimeout of the headers (408 for a body that stalls, which
frees its turn; 503 when no turn came), checks the signature as the HMAC-SHA256
of those exact bytes with the current or the previous secret (401 when neither
matches, and nothing is stored or parsed), then reads only the routing fields
of the payload (Envelope) and inserts them under the delivery's GUID: 202
when stored, 200 for a delivery already stored, 503 when the journal refuses.
With Options.Installations set, a delivery of another installation, or of none
but the App's ping, answers 202 {"status":"ignored"} and is not stored. A
delivery is answered within WebhookDeadline of its headers, under GitHub's 10 s.
The body itself is never stored or logged.

GET /v1/events lists the journal after a cursor ("<epoch>:<seq>") in journal
order, for a bearer token (CheckToken's bounds) whose SHA-256 is among the
accepted hashes, and waits up to `wait` for a first event when there is none
(a long poll woken by the next insert; at most MaxWaiting wait at once, and one
more answers 429). A cursor of another journal (epoch), or one older than the
journal's oldest cursor (its events were pruned) or ahead of its high water,
answers 410 "gap", and the daemon then resyncs by polling GitHub. GET /healthz
tells anyone whether the journal answers ({"ok":true}, or 503 {"ok":false}),
and adds its epoch, the events kept and when the newest arrived for an accepted
bearer token, from counters the journal keeps and a snapshot read again at most
every 2 s.

Retention deletes the events older than Options.Retention (30 days by default),
as a prefix of the journal, so the oldest cursor only moves forward. Logs carry
delivery ids, event names, sequence numbers and error classes, never a body,
a secret, a token or an error's text. A request refused before it is
authenticated, and a delivery of another installation, logs no line of its own:
RunRefusalLog logs their count by kind once a minute.

CONSTANTS

const (
	// MaxCheckName is the longest check name kept, in runes.
	MaxCheckName = 120
)
const (
	// DefaultMaxBody is the largest delivery read (GitHub caps payloads at 25 MB).
	DefaultMaxBody = 26 << 20
	// DefaultRetention is how long the journal keeps an event.
	DefaultRetention = 30 * 24 * time.Hour
	// MinRetention is the shortest retention Open accepts.
	MinRetention = time.Hour
	// MaxWait is the longest long poll a listing may ask for.
	MaxWait = 30 * time.Second
	// DefaultLimit is the events of a listing that asks for no limit.
	DefaultLimit = 200
	// MaxLimit is the most events one listing returns.
	MaxLimit = 500
	// DefaultMaxWaiting is how many long polls may wait at once; one more answers 429.
	DefaultMaxWaiting = 16

	// DefaultBodyTimeout is how long a delivery has, from its headers, to wait for its turn and send its
	// whole body (BodyTimeout may only shorten it). A body still arriving then is cut (408), which frees
	// its turn.
	DefaultBodyTimeout = 7 * time.Second
	// WebhookDeadline is the longest a delivery takes from its headers to its answer: the body timeout
	// and the journal's write. It stays under GitHub's 10 s.
	WebhookDeadline = DefaultBodyTimeout + insertTimeout

	// MinTokenLength is the shortest bearer token, in `magnum-relay hash-token` and in the listing alike
	// (CheckToken).
	MinTokenLength = 32
	// MaxTokenLength is the longest bearer token, in `magnum-relay hash-token` and in the listing alike.
	MaxTokenLength = 512
)

VARIABLES

var ErrPayload = errors.New("payload is not JSON")
    ErrPayload is a delivery whose payload is not a JSON document.


FUNCTIONS

func CheckToken(token string) error
    CheckToken says whether token can be one of the relay's bearer tokens:
    one word of MinTokenLength to MaxTokenLength printable ASCII characters.
    `magnum-relay hash-token` and the listing apply it alike, so a token setup
    accepts is one the listing accepts. Its errors never quote the token.


TYPES

type Check struct {
	Name       string `json:"name"`
	Conclusion string `json:"conclusion"`
}
    Check is a CI event's name and conclusion: a check run's name and
    conclusion, a check suite's app name and conclusion, a status's context and
    state. Names are data, at most MaxCheckName runes; a conclusion is "" until
    there is one.

type Event struct {
	// Seq is the event's place in the journal (its cursor is "<epoch>:<seq>").
	Seq int64 `json:"seq"`
	// DeliveryID is the delivery's X-GitHub-Delivery GUID, which a redelivery keeps.
	DeliveryID string `json:"delivery_id"`
	// Event is the X-GitHub-Event name and Action the payload's action ("" when it has none).
	Event  string `json:"event"`
	Action string `json:"action"`
	// InstallationID and RepositoryID are 0 when the payload has none.
	InstallationID int64 `json:"installation_id"`
	RepositoryID   int64 `json:"repository_id"`
	// Repository is "owner/name", "" when the payload has none.
	Repository string `json:"repository"`
	// PRNumbers are the pull requests the event names, ascending: the pull request of a pull_request*
	// event, the issue of an issue_comment on a pull request, a check's pull_requests (empty for a fork's,
	// whose HeadSHA is then the key), and none for a status.
	PRNumbers []int `json:"pr_numbers"`
	// HeadSHA is the pull request's head, the check's or the status's commit: 40 hex or "".
	HeadSHA string `json:"head_sha"`
	// BaseRef is a pull_request* event's base branch, else "".
	BaseRef string `json:"base_ref"`
	// Check is set only for check_run, check_suite and status.
	Check *Check `json:"check,omitempty"`
	// ReceivedAt is when the relay stored the event (UTC, whole seconds).
	ReceivedAt time.Time `json:"received_at"`
}
    Event is the routing envelope of one delivery, what the journal keeps and
    the listing answers: ids and routing only, never a title, a body, a comment,
    a patch, a user name or a URL.

func Envelope(event string, body []byte) (Event, error)
    Envelope reads the routing fields of a delivery's payload for its event
    name. A field of an unexpected shape, or a value that is not well formed (an
    id below 0, a SHA that is not 40 hex, a repository that is not owner/name),
    is left empty rather than refusing the delivery; a payload that is not JSON
    is ErrPayload. Seq, DeliveryID and ReceivedAt are the caller's.

type Options struct {
	// DB is the journal's SQLite file; its directory is created 0700 and the file 0600.
	DB string
	// Secrets are the webhook secrets a signature may match: the current one, then the previous one
	// during a rotation.
	Secrets [][]byte
	// TokenHashes are the SHA-256 digests of the bearer tokens the listing accepts.
	TokenHashes [][sha256.Size]byte
	// Retention is how long an event is kept (DefaultRetention when zero, at least MinRetention).
	Retention time.Duration
	// MaxBody is the largest delivery read (DefaultMaxBody when zero).
	MaxBody int64
	// BodyTimeout is how long a delivery has to wait for its turn and send its body (DefaultBodyTimeout
	// when zero, at most DefaultBodyTimeout).
	BodyTimeout time.Duration
	// MaxWaiting is how many long polls may wait at once (DefaultMaxWaiting when zero).
	MaxWaiting int
	// Installations are the ids of the App's installations whose deliveries are kept, each at least 1; a
	// signed delivery of another installation, or of none but the App's own ping, answers 202 and is not
	// stored. Empty keeps every installation's.
	Installations []int64
	// Logger receives the relay's logs (discarded when nil).
	Logger *slog.Logger
	// Now is the relay's clock (time.Now when nil).
	Now func() time.Time
}
    Options configures a Relay.

type Page struct {
	// Epoch is the journal's random id; a journal created again has another, and every cursor of the old
	// one answers 410.
	Epoch string `json:"epoch"`
	// Events are the events after the cursor, in journal order (never null).
	Events []Event `json:"events"`
	// Next is the cursor to pass as `after` next: the last event's, or the request's when none came.
	Next string `json:"next"`
	// HighWater is the cursor of the newest event the journal ever stored.
	HighWater string `json:"high_water"`
	// Oldest is the cursor just before the oldest kept event: `after=<oldest>` lists every kept event, as
	// `after=` does, and a cursor below it answers 410 (its next events were pruned).
	Oldest string `json:"oldest"`
	// ServerTime is the relay's clock (UTC).
	ServerTime time.Time `json:"server_time"`
}
    Page is the answer of GET /v1/events.

type Relay struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Relay is the receiver, the journal and the listing.

func Open(ctx context.Context, opts Options) (*Relay, error)
    Open checks the options and opens (or creates) the journal.

func (r *Relay) Close() error
    Close closes the journal.

func (r *Relay) Epoch() string
    Epoch is the journal's random id, the first part of every cursor.

func (r *Relay) Handler() http.Handler
    Handler serves the webhook, the listing and the health check.

func (r *Relay) Prune(ctx context.Context) (int64, error)
    Prune deletes the events older than the retention and returns how many it
    deleted.

func (r *Relay) RunRefusalLog(ctx context.Context, every time.Duration)
    RunRefusalLog logs the refusals counted since its last lines every interval
    (serve's is a minute), one line a kind with its count, and once more
    when ctx ends. A request the relay refuses before it is authenticated,
    or a delivery of another installation, logs nothing on its own, so a flood
    of them costs a few lines a minute, not one a request.

func (r *Relay) RunRetention(ctx context.Context, every time.Duration)
    RunRetention prunes at once and then every interval, until ctx ends.

func (r *Relay) StopWaiting()
    StopWaiting answers every long poll at once and keeps later ones from
    waiting, before a shutdown.

```

## reveal

```text
package reveal // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/reveal"

Package reveal brings the herdr client to the front of the user's terminal:
focus the existing client when there is one, otherwise open a new tab or window
running `herdr --session <name>`.

It is a Go port of the terminal layer of the Raycast herdr extension
(terminal.ts, terminal-focus.ts, process-lookup.ts, terminal-config.ts).
herdr clients are found through `ps -axo pid=,tty=,args=` (never pgrep,
see docs/spikes.md probe 8) and matched to a terminal tab by tty: iTerm2 and
Terminal.app through AppleScript, Ghostty through a temporary marker title
(`herdr terminal title set`), WezTerm through `wezterm cli`. A custom launcher
template and a generic `open -a <App>` cover everything else.

Every subprocess (ps, osascript, open, wezterm, herdr, the custom launcher)
runs through execx.Runner. Read-only lookups are not marked Mutates; anything
that touches the UI (focus, launch, title set, activate) is, so DryRun prints it
instead of running it. A DryRun therefore yields Unavailable focus results and
an "activated" outcome, never a false "focused".

The package never changes herdr state: it does not start servers, create
workspaces or panes, and only sets (then clears) the outer terminal title for
the Ghostty flow. Focusing a pane inside herdr (`herdr agent focus`) is the
caller's job and happens before Reveal.

TYPES

type Action string
    Action says what Reveal did.

const (
	ActionFocused   Action = "focused"   // focused an existing client
	ActionLaunched  Action = "launched"  // opened a new client tab/window
	ActionActivated Action = "activated" // could only bring the terminal app forward
)
type AutomationError struct {
	App string // the application the script controls: iTerm, Terminal or Ghostty
}
    AutomationError is a focus script macOS refused to run (osascript's error
    -1743, "Not authorized to send Apple events"): the app that runs magnum may
    not control App under Privacy & Security → Automation.

func (e *AutomationError) Error() string

type FocusResult string
    FocusResult is the outcome of looking for an existing herdr client.

const (
	// Focused: an existing client's tab/window was brought to the front.
	Focused FocusResult = "focused"
	// Missing: the terminal is scriptable and confirmed there is no client in it.
	Missing FocusResult = "missing"
	// Unavailable: the answer could not be determined (process list failed,
	// osascript denied or timed out, terminal cannot be scripted).
	Unavailable FocusResult = "unavailable"
)
type Kind string
    Kind is the family of terminal application magnum reveals herdr in.

const (
	KindTerminal Kind = "terminal" // macOS Terminal.app
	KindITerm    Kind = "iterm2"
	KindGhostty  Kind = "ghostty"
	KindWezTerm  Kind = "wezterm"
	KindCustom   Kind = "custom"  // user-supplied launcher template
	KindGeneric  Kind = "generic" // `open -a <App>` only
)
    The supported terminal kinds. Anything DetectKind does not recognise
    (including Muxy) is KindGeneric: the app can be activated but not scripted.

func DetectKind(app string) Kind
    DetectKind maps config.Terminal.App to a Kind. Matching is case-insensitive
    and tolerant of a ".app" suffix or a bundle id. An empty name means the
    built-in Terminal.app, as in the Raycast extension.

type Options struct {
	// NewWindow opens a new window instead of a tab in the current one.
	NewWindow bool
	// Session is the herdr session to reveal (`herdr --session <name>`):
	// the session of magnum's review panes or the factory's. "" means the
	// configured [terminal] session, yours.
	Session string
}
    Options tunes Launch and Reveal.

type Outcome struct {
	Action  Action `json:"action"`
	Kind    Kind   `json:"kind"`
	Session string `json:"session"`
	// Detail carries the reason when the result is a fallback (for example why
	// focusing was unavailable).
	Detail string `json:"detail,omitempty"`
}
    Outcome describes what Reveal did, for `magnum open` output and --json.

func Reveal(ctx context.Context, run execx.Runner, cfg config.Terminal, herdrBin string, opts Options) (Outcome, error)
    Reveal builds a revealer for cfg and herdrBin and runs its Reveal.

func (o Outcome) String() string
    String renders the outcome as one human-readable line.

```

## scrub

```text
package scrub // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/scrub"

Package scrub masks the secrets, emails and host names in text before magnum
keeps or shows it. It is a leaf both daemons import: the factory's runtime.Scrub
keeps what you typed and what it sent through Text (spec section 11.1),
and the review daemon masks the tails of failed CI job logs with Secrets.
The improvement loop's scrub.py (.claude/skills/magnum-improve/scripts) is held
to the patterns below by a test and a fuzz in this package.

FUNCTIONS

func Secrets(text string) string
    Secrets masks the secrets in text and leaves emails and host names:
    execx.Redact (GitHub tokens, JWTs, Authorization values, private keys), then
    AWS keys and other token shapes, then the values of password=, token: and
    the like, also under a quoted key ("password": "x") and an env-style name
    (DB_PASSWORD=x), then (R60) the password of a URL (postgres://app:x@host),
    the user of an http URL (a Sentry DSN's key), the password of curl -u
    and mysql -p, and the value of an all-caps name that ends in a key word
    (PGPASSWORD=x). The key stays. It is for text where a host or an address is
    what the reader needs, such as a failing test's output in a CI log.

func Text(text string) string
    Text masks what Secrets masks, then emails and host names (and the host
    after a masked userinfo, which the email pass cannot read). It is what the
    factory keeps of the words that pass through it (runtime.Scrub).

```

## settings

```text
package settings // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/settings"

Package settings is the core of the settings screen (`magnum settings`):
the typed allowlist of the settings it may change (Fields), what the user
config says for each (Snapshot), the roles a draft resolves to after a
restart (Preview), and the save: the draft becomes in-place edits of
~/.config/magnum/config.toml (internal/confedit), checked as `magnum config`
checks a file, shown as a diff (Plan), then written atomically with the previous
file kept in the config history (Commit), and the daemon asked to restart on it
when idle (RequestRestart). Identities, auto_approve_as, keys, paths, commands,
args, env, hooks, MCP, the sandbox and pools are never in the allowlist:
they are edited by hand.

CONSTANTS

const (
	SectionSpend    = "Spend & models"
	SectionCaps     = "Usage caps"
	SectionWatches  = "Watches"
	SectionRepos    = "Repositories"
	SectionSchedule = "Schedule"
	SectionReviews  = "Reviews & agents"
)
    The sections, in the order the screen lists them (its Runtime section is not
    config and is the screen's own).

const (
	CellModel          = "model"
	CellEffort         = "effort"
	CellRereviewEffort = "rereview_effort"
)
    Grid cells of a role in a [spend.<level>] table or its [[role]] block.

const HistoryKeep = 20
    HistoryKeep is how many earlier versions of the config the history keeps.

const KVDaemonConfigSHA = engine.KVDaemonConfigSum
    KVDaemonConfigSHA is the registry key holding the hex SHA-256 of the user
    config the running daemon loaded ("" when it read none).


VARIABLES

var Efforts = []string{"low", "medium", "high", "xhigh"}
    Efforts are the effort levels magnum's levels use (the agent CLIs take
    these).

var ErrChanged = errors.New("settings: the config file changed on disk since it was loaded; reload it")
    ErrChanged is a save over a config that changed on disk since the screen
    loaded it (an editor, another screen): nothing is written.


FUNCTIONS

func RequestRestart(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, sum [32]byte) error
    RequestRestart asks the daemon to restart on the config whose hash is sum
    once nothing is in flight (engine.KVConfigRestart), and the next start
    clears the mark. It checks nothing itself: the daemon loads the file before
    it exits (engine restartSafe), and drops the mark when the file does not
    load.

func RestartPending(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, s *Snapshot) (bool, error)
    RestartPending reports whether the config on disk differs from the one
    the daemon runs: its content's hash against the one the daemon recorded at
    start. False when no daemon recorded one.

func Sections() []string
    Sections lists the sections in order.


TYPES

type Applies int
    Applies is when a saved value takes effect.

const (
	AppliesAfterRestart Applies = iota // the daemon reads the config at start
	AppliesNow
)
    When a value applies.

type Draft map[Target]DraftValue
    Draft is the edits the screen staged, by target.

type DraftValue struct {
	Text    string
	List    []string
	Default bool
}
    DraftValue is one staged edit: Text for a scalar, List for a list field,
    Default to remove the key (back to the default; its comment stays as a
    comment line).

type Field struct {
	ID      FieldID
	Section string
	Label   string
	// Key is the TOML key path, a template for the scoped ones:
	// "pipeline.spend", "kinds.<kind>.spend", "spend.<level>.<role>.model",
	// "role.<role>.model", "watch.roles", "repo.stakes".
	Key   string
	Scope Scope
	Type  Type
	// Role, Level and Cell place a grid cell (ScopeSpendLevel, ScopeRole):
	// Level "" is the role's base model in its [[role]] block. Kind is the
	// agent kind of a [kinds.<kind>] spend. All four are "" in a template.
	Role, Level, Cell, Kind string
	// Options are an enum's members when they are fixed; Snapshot.Options
	// computes the others (spend levels, roles, models seen in the config).
	Options      []string
	Validate     func(string) error   // a scalar's own check (nil: none)
	ValidateList func([]string) error // a list's own check (nil: none)
	Description  string
	DefaultText  string // the built-in default, as the screen shows it
	Applies      Applies
}
    Field is one setting.

func Fields() []Field
    Fields is the allowlist: every setting of the screen's v1, in screen order,
```
