```text
    the role grid and the kind spends as templates (Role, Level and Kind empty;
    Snapshot.Fields expands them for a configuration).

type FieldID string
    FieldID names a setting: a template's ("pipeline.spend",
    "watch.roles", "spend.model") or a concrete grid or kind field's
    ("spend.high.claude-review.model", "role.claude-review.model",
    "kinds.codex.spend").

type HistoryEntry struct {
	Path  string
	Saved time.Time
	Sum   [32]byte
	Size  int64
}
    HistoryEntry is an earlier version of the config: a file of the history
    directory, when it was replaced, the hash and size of its content.

func History(layout paths.Layout) ([]HistoryEntry, error)
    History lists the earlier versions of layout's user config the saves kept,
    newest first: Snapshot.History without loading the current file, which a
    hand edit may have broken.

type Hunk struct {
	Table          string
	Line           int
	Removed, Added []string
}
    Hunk is one place a save changes: the table it is in ("[pipeline]",
    "[spend.burn]", "[[repo]] talkable/web", "[[watch]] 2 (talkable)"),
    its line in the old file (where the added lines go for an insertion),
    and the lines removed and added.

type Plan struct {
	Path     string
	Old, New []byte
	Sum      [32]byte // of Old: the file the plan was built on
	NewSum   [32]byte
	Diff     string // a unified diff (no context lines), each hunk headed by its table
	Hunks    []Hunk
	Warnings []string
	Count    int
	Keys     []string

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Plan is a save checked and ready to write: the old and new bytes, the hash
    of the file it was built on (Commit refuses another), the diff, the loader's
    warnings about the new file, how many settings it changes and the key paths
    it changes (for logs: never values).

func RestoreFile(layout paths.Layout, base string, e HistoryEntry) (*Plan, error)
    RestoreFile is the save that puts e back over layout's user config as it is
    on disk, whether or not it loads: Snapshot.Restore for a file that no longer
    loads (a hand edit broke it). The version must load over base and render, as
    any save's file must; Commit writes it, refusing a file that changed since,
    and keeps the replaced file in the history.

type RepoInfo struct {
	Name     string // owner/name
	HasBlock bool
	Line     int // the block's header line (HasBlock)
	Watch    int // the user file's [[watch]] that covers it; -1 for none, or a watch of the base file
}
    RepoInfo is a repository the screen offers: a [[repo]] block of the user
    file, or a repository a watch's include names without one (the save creates
    a minimal block for it).

type Result struct {
	History string
	Sum     [32]byte
}
    Result is a written save: the history file holding the previous bytes (""
    when there were none: the file did not exist) and the new file's hash.

func Commit(p *Plan) (Result, error)
    Commit writes a plan under the saves' lock (a flock on a file beside the
    config, lockFile, so two screens or a screen and a script never interleave,
    whatever layout each runs with): the file must be one the write cannot
    break (checkWritable) and still hash as the plan's old bytes (ErrChanged
    otherwise), the previous bytes go to the config history (the last
    HistoryKeep kept), then, both checks made again right before the write,
    the new bytes replace the file atomically, keeping its mode (0600 for a new
    one).

type RoleRow struct {
	Role, Kind, Model, Effort, RereviewEffort, Spend string
}
    RoleRow is a role as it resolves after a restart: its kind, model, first and
    re-review effort, and the spend level it follows.

type Scope int
    Scope is what a setting belongs to.

const (
	ScopeGlobal     Scope = iota // a key of a [section]
	ScopeWatch                   // a key of a [[watch]] (Target.Watch picks it)
	ScopeRepo                    // a key of a [[repo]] (Target.Repo picks it)
	ScopeRole                    // a key of a [[role]] (Field.Role)
	ScopeSpendLevel              // a role's key in a [spend.<level>] table (Field.Level, Field.Role)
	ScopeKind                    // a key of a [kinds.<name>] table (Field.Kind)
)
    The scopes.

type Snapshot struct {
	Path   string // the user config (paths.Layout.UserConfig)
	Bytes  []byte // its content; empty when it does not exist yet
	Sum    [32]byte
	Doc    *confedit.Doc
	Config *config.Config

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Snapshot is the user config as the screen loaded it: its bytes and their
    hash (a save refuses a file that changed since), the scanned file, the
    resolved configuration, and the settings expanded for it.

func Load(layout paths.Layout, base string) (*Snapshot, error)
    Load reads the user config (layout.UserConfig; a missing file is an empty
    one) and resolves it over base as config.Load does (base: the --config file,
    "" for the built-in defaults or $MAGNUM_CONFIG). A file the editor does
    not model fails with confedit.ErrUnsupported, one magnum refuses with the
    loader's error.

func (s *Snapshot) Check(t Target, v DraftValue) error
    Check is t's own validation of a draft value: the field's check, an enum's
    members, the round roles of a roles list. Whether the whole file still loads
    is Plan's check.

func (s *Snapshot) Field(id FieldID) (Field, bool)
    Field is the setting id names.

func (s *Snapshot) Fields() []Field
    Fields are the settings of this configuration, in screen order: the grid for
    every level, role and cell, the base model per role and the spend per kind
    concrete, the watch and repository fields as templates (a Target picks the
    instance).

func (s *Snapshot) History() ([]HistoryEntry, error)
    History lists the earlier versions of the config the saves kept, newest
    first.

func (s *Snapshot) KeyText(t Target) string
    KeyText names t's key as the file spells it: "[pipeline] spend",
    "[spend.high].claude-simplify.model", "[[watch]] 1 (talkable) · roles",
    "[[repo]] talkable/web · stakes", "[[role]] claude-review · model".

func (s *Snapshot) Levels() []string
    Levels are the spend levels: low, medium, high, then the operator's own
    ([spend.<level>] tables) by name.

func (s *Snapshot) Options(t Target) []string
    Options are the values a target offers: an enum's members, the spend levels,
    the round roles, the judges, the models and efforts the configuration names,
    a watch's repositories ("" is a judge_fallback of none).

func (s *Snapshot) Plan(d Draft, notes bool, now time.Time) (*Plan, error)
    Plan builds the save of d: the file re-read and refused when it changed
    since Load (ErrChanged), the edits applied in place (with "was <old>" notes
    when notes is on) and verified, the new file checked as `magnum config`
    checks one (the loader, then every prompt rendered with this build), and the
    diff. Nothing is written.

func (s *Snapshot) Preview(d Draft) ([]RoleRow, error)
    Preview is the roles after a restart on the draft, resolved by magnum's own
    loader from the edited file: a draft that does not load is its error.

func (s *Snapshot) Repos() []RepoInfo
    Repos are the repositories the screen offers, by name: each [[repo]] block
    of the user file, and each repository a watch's include names (without a
    glob) that the watch covers, with or without a block.

func (s *Snapshot) Restore(e HistoryEntry, now time.Time) (*Plan, error)
    Restore is the save that puts an earlier version back: a Plan like any
    save (the file must not have changed since Load, the version must load and
    render, and the version it replaces goes to the history in turn).

func (s *Snapshot) Saved() []RoleRow
    Saved is the roles as the file on disk resolves them.

func (s *Snapshot) Value(t Target) Value
    Value is what the user config says for t and what applies. A role that
    several [[role]] blocks of the file name is not edited here (Check and Plan
    refuse it): its Source says so.

func (s *Snapshot) Watches() []WatchInfo
    Watches are the user file's [[watch]] blocks.

type State int
    State says whether the user config sets a setting.

const (
	StateDefault State = iota // the file does not set it: the default (or what it inherits) applies
	StateSet                  // the file sets it
)
    The states.

type Target struct {
	Field FieldID
	Watch int    // ScopeWatch: the 0-based position among the user file's [[watch]] blocks
	Repo  string // ScopeRepo: owner/name, with or without a [[repo]] block yet
}
    Target is one setting of one scope instance: a global or concrete field
    alone, a watch field with its watch, a repository field with its repository.

type Type int
    Type is a setting's value type: how its text is read, checked and written.

const (
	TypeEnum     Type = iota // one of Options
	TypeBool                 // "true" or "false"
	TypeDuration             // Go syntax with days: "15m", "2h", "1d"
	TypeInt
	TypePercent // 0-100, a fraction allowed
	TypeLogins  // a list of GitHub logins
	TypeRepos   // a list of repository names (no owner)
	TypeRoles   // a list of role names
	TypeText    // one line
	TypeModel   // a model name the agent CLI takes
	TypeEffort  // an effort level the agent CLI takes
	TypeChecks  // a list of required check names (workflow:<glob> for a workflow)
)
    The types.

func (t Type) IsList() bool
    IsList reports whether values of t are lists (DraftValue.List).

type Value struct {
	Text string   // what the file says, in the field's text form; "" when StateDefault
	List []string // a list field's entries as the file has them (StateSet)
	// Effective is what applies: the default (or what is inherited) when
	// StateDefault ("inherit (high)", "2h"), the resolved value when
	// StateSet.
	Effective string
	State     State
	Line      int    // the key's 1-based line in the user file (StateSet)
	Source    string // where Effective comes from: "your file, line 12", "built-in default", "[pipeline] spend", ...
}
    Value is what the user config says for a target and what applies.

type WatchInfo struct {
	Index   int // its position among the user file's [[watch]] blocks
	Owner   string
	Label   string // "talkable · web, api +3"
	Include []string
	Line    int // its header's line
}
    WatchInfo is one [[watch]] of the user file.

```

## slots

```text
package slots // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/slots"

Package slots manages the checkouts magnum reviews in: the Talkable pool slots
(~/Projects/talkable.reviewN, provisioned once with bin/worktree-setup and
reused) and per-PR worktrees for small repositories, next to the repository's
main clone whatever it is named (~/Projects/<owner>-<name>__worktrees/pr-N).

Every operation is a sequence of steps.Step side effects, each idempotent or
prechecked, so a crash in the middle is repaired by calling the same operation
again. Slot state moves through compare-and-set store transitions; the slot row
is written before any side effect so the registry always knows about a directory
or database before it exists.

Heavy commands (setup, dependency installs, schema reloads, teardown) run
through `mise -C <slot> exec -- env <slot env> /bin/sh -c <cmd>` and are
serialized by the Manager, so at most one runs at a time.

CONSTANTS

const (
	HookPostCreate = "post-create"
	HookPostStart  = "post-start"
	HookPreRemove  = "pre-remove"
	// HookSetup and HookTeardown label [[repo]] commands.
	HookSetup    = "setup"
	HookTeardown = "teardown"
)
    Worktrunk hook types magnum runs (other tables in wt.toml are ignored).

const (
	MiseLocal       = "mise.local.toml"
	MiseLocalDotted = ".mise.local.toml"
)
    The two spellings of the per-checkout local mise file, both read by mise.
    magnum renders a checkout's under the name the main clone's file has
    (MiseLocalName), MiseLocal when the main clone has none.

const (
	SetupTimeout    = 45 * time.Minute
	DepsTimeout     = 30 * time.Minute
	ResetDBTimeout  = 30 * time.Minute
	TeardownTimeout = 30 * time.Minute
)
    Timeouts of the heavy commands.

const (
	HoldPinned            = "pinned"
	HoldForeignAgent      = "foreign_agent"
	HoldForegroundProcess = "foreground_process"
	HoldHeadDrift         = "head_drift"
	HoldUnpushed          = "unpushed_commits"
	HoldDirtyWorktree     = "dirty_worktree"
)
    Hold reasons returned in ErrHold. HoldHeadDrift, HoldUnpushed and
    HoldDirtyWorktree are also persisted as slots.hold_reason (the slot stays
    held until Unpin); the others are transient and only refuse the current
    operation.

const AgentPrefix = "mg-"
    AgentPrefix starts the name of every agent magnum starts; the guard treats
    any other agent as a human's.

const BreakAfterResetFailures = 2
    BreakAfterResetFailures is how many rounds in a row whose readiness reset_db
    failed in a pool slot break it at its release (resetSchema): the release
    keeps a LazySchema slot's databases, so nothing else ever tells the operator
    that every round in the slot fails the same reset.

const DefaultCloneRoot = "~/Projects"
    DefaultCloneRoot is used when a watch has no clone_root.

const MarkerFile = "tmp/.worktree-db-slug"
    MarkerFile is written by bin/worktree-setup with the slot's database slug.

const Refused3730 = "MySQL error 3730 (a table the schema does not know refers to one the load drops)"
    Refused3730 names MySQL's refusal in the errors and events of a reset that
    hit it.

const SchemaFile = "db/schema.rb"
    SchemaFile is read for the `define(version: …)` the slot's dev database must
    match after a release.

const SlotLogMax = 2 << 20
    SlotLogMax caps each log transcript writes (slot-<name>.log,
    provision-<name>.log, perpr-<slug>.log): the write that would push one past
    it first moves it to <name>.1, replacing the previous one, as daemon.log
    rotates. A seed that prints its SQL fills several MB on every reset.

const WTConfigFile = ".config/wt.toml"
    WTConfigFile is worktrunk's project config, relative to the main clone.


VARIABLES

var (
	// ErrNoFreeSlot: the pool has no free, unpinned, unheld slot.
	ErrNoFreeSlot = errors.New("slots: no free slot")
	// ErrBroken: the slot was moved to broken (needs Repair).
	ErrBroken = errors.New("slots: slot is broken")
	// ErrLowDisk: provisioning refused below pool.min_free_disk_gb.
	ErrLowDisk = errors.New("slots: not enough free disk space")
	// ErrOriginMismatch: an existing clone's origin is not the expected repository.
	ErrOriginMismatch = errors.New("slots: clone origin does not match the repository")
	// ErrVerify: a post-condition (HEAD, marker file, databases) did not hold.
	ErrVerify = errors.New("slots: verification failed")
)
var (
	// ReleaseStates can be released: claimed and held start a release,
	// releasing and dirty_schema resume one.
	ReleaseStates = []string{store.SlotClaimed, store.SlotHeld, store.SlotReleasing, store.SlotDirtySchema}
	// RemoveStates are the pool slot states Remove starts from without force
	// (removing resumes; removed is a no-op).
	RemoveStates = []string{store.SlotFree, store.SlotBroken, store.SlotLost, store.SlotProvisioning}
	// ForceRemoveStates are the extra pool slot states Remove starts from
	// with force. Busy never is.
	ForceRemoveStates = []string{store.SlotClaimed, store.SlotHeld, store.SlotReleasing, store.SlotDirtySchema}
	// RemovePRStates are the per-PR worktree states RemovePRWorktree starts
	// from (removing resumes; busy never is).
	RemovePRStates = []string{store.SlotProvisioning, store.SlotClaimed, store.SlotHeld, store.SlotReleasing,
		store.SlotFree, store.SlotBroken, store.SlotLost}
)
    Slot states each operation accepts; cleanup plans with the same lists.
    Callers that extend one must slices.Clone it first.

var DefaultStripEnv = []string{"GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN", "GH_TOKEN", "GITHUB_TOKEN"}
    DefaultStripEnv is always dropped from a checkout's rendered local mise
    file, a pool slot's (in addition to [pool] strip_env) as well as a per-PR
    worktree's (in addition to [[repo]] strip_env): a GitHub token there would
    override the reviewing identity's gh selection in the agents' panes, and the
    checkout runs PR-controlled code.

var ErrHook = errors.New("slots: per-PR hooks")
    ErrHook: a per-PR worktree's hook file or template cannot be used.

var ErrMiseLocal = errors.New("slots: cannot render the main clone's mise.local.toml or .mise.local.toml")
    ErrMiseLocal means the main clone's local mise file cannot be rendered
    safely.

var LockFiles = []string{
	"Gemfile.lock", "pnpm-lock.yaml", "yarn.lock", "package-lock.json", "bun.lock",
	"composer.lock", "go.sum", "Cargo.lock", "poetry.lock", "uv.lock",
}
    LockFiles are the lockfiles, at the checkout's root, that lockHash hashes
    with pool.PostCheckout into slots.lock_sha: a change of one the checkout
    holds, or of the commands, reruns them. A name added here moves the hash
    only of a checkout that has the file; reordering the names moves them all.

var WorkspaceNameVars = []string{
	"CONDUCTOR_WORKSPACE_NAME", "EMDASH_TASK_NAME", "SUPERSET_WORKSPACE_NAME",
	"COMMANDER_CONTEXT_NAME", "CLAUDE_CODE_WORKTREE_NAME", "WM_HANDLE",
}
    WorkspaceNameVars are the workspace-name variables bin/worktree-setup and
    bin/worktree-archive read before WT_BRANCH; a per-PR worktree blanks them
    (the pool does the same through [pool.env]) so an orchestrator's value
    inherited from the daemon's environment cannot pick other databases.


FUNCTIONS

func CloneRoot(watch config.Watch) string
    CloneRoot is the watch's expanded clone_root (DefaultCloneRoot when unset).

func CopyIntoCheckout(src, checkout, rel string) error
    CopyIntoCheckout copies src (a file outside the checkout, e.g. in the main
    clone) to rel inside checkout through WriteCheckoutFile, keeping src's
    permission bits; a missing src is skipped (nil).

func DBListPrefixes(pools ...config.Pool) (prefixes, bad []string)
    DBListPrefixes returns the distinct name prefixes ("<base>__") of the pools'
    database templates, sorted: talkable_development__ and talkable_test__
    for talkable_development__{slug} and talkable_test__{slug}. bad lists the
    templates that do not end in "__{slug}" (config validation should refuse
    them); they are left out of prefixes.

func DBPrefix(pool config.Pool) string
    DBPrefix is the common start of the pool's database templates before "{"
    (talkable_), "" when there are none or they share nothing.

func DBSlug(name string) string
    DBSlug sanitizes a workspace name the way talkable's database.yml
    does (WORKTREE_NAME.gsub(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_]/, "_")[0, 30]): magnum-pr-7 →
    magnum_pr_7.

func DropGuard(pool config.Pool) mysqlx.Guard
    DropGuard is the one drop guard for a pool's own databases, shared by slots,
    inventory and cleanup: Prefix is the common start of the pool's database
    templates before "{" (talkable_ for talkable_development__{slug} and
    talkable_test__{slug}; a single template's text before "{"), and AllowRegexp
    is slot_name sanitized as SlotDBSlug sanitizes a slot's name, with {n} as
    [0-9]+ (^review[0-9]+$; example-review{n} gives ^example_review[0-9]+$),
    so only magnum's own slot slugs are ever droppable. A pool without database
    templates, with no common prefix or with a slot_name lacking {n} gets the
    zero Guard, which refuses everything.

func ForeignKeyDropRefused(text string) bool
    ForeignKeyDropRefused reports whether text, a failed reset_db's output
    or error, is MySQL's 3730: a table the schema load does not know (a PR's
    schema added it) refers to one the load drops, so every load fails until the
    databases start empty (RecreateDatabases).

func IsPRWorktree(dir string) bool
    IsPRWorktree reports whether dir is a per-PR worktree as PRWorktreePath
    names one: a pr-<N> directory in the <clone>__worktrees directory of a clone
    (a directory below one is not).

func LazySchema(pool config.Pool) bool
    LazySchema reports whether pool's slots reload their databases only when a
    round's checkout needs another schema (CheckSchema, before the reviewers)
    and keep them through the release: the pool names schema_paths and reset_db,
    and reset_db_on_schema_change is on. Otherwise the release loads the base
    schema again, as before.

func ListPoolDatabases(ctx context.Context, c DBLister, pools ...config.Pool) (dbs []mysqlx.Database, bad []string, err error)
    ListPoolDatabases lists the per-worktree databases of pools: every schema
    named <prefix><slug> for a prefix of DBListPrefixes, ordered by name (the
    client's answer is checked again: a LIKE scan is only a coarse filter).
    Templates without "__{slug}" are skipped and returned in bad for the caller
    to report. No pool template at all lists nothing (and is not an error).

func MiseExecArgs(dir string, env map[string]string, script string) []string
    MiseExecArgs builds `-C dir exec -- env K=V… /bin/sh -c script` (keys
    sorted; blank values blank the variable): the arguments of the mise
    executable that run a pool script as the release, the provisioning and
    `magnum open` do, with the real Ruby first on PATH (no shim that would
    re-apply the checkout's local mise file's [env] over env).

func MiseLocalName(mainClone string) string
    MiseLocalName is the name of the main clone's local mise file:
    the spelling that exists there, MiseLocalDotted when both do (mise loads
    it after MiseLocal, so its values win: "`.mise.local.toml` overrides
    `mise.local.toml`", https://mise.jdx.dev/configuration.html), MiseLocal when
    neither does.

func PRSlotName(repo string, number int) string
    PRSlotName is the slot name of a per-PR worktree: "owner/name#N".

func PRSlug(number int) string
    PRSlug is the workspace name of per-PR worktree number: magnum-pr-<N>.
    It is WT_BRANCH for the worktree's hooks and agents.

func PRWorktreePath(mainClone string, number int) string
    PRWorktreePath is the per-PR worktree of a main clone:
    <clone>__worktrees/pr-<N>, next to the clone whatever it is named
    (~/Projects/<owner>-<name>__worktrees/pr-7).

func PRWorktreePaths(watch config.Watch, repo string, number int) (mainClone, path string)
    PRWorktreePaths returns the default layout for repo "owner/name" when
    no clone exists yet: the main clone <clone_root>/<name> and its per-PR
    worktree. CreatePRWorktree finds an existing clone first (FindClone).

func PerPREnv(rc *config.Repo, number int, path, clone string) map[string]string
    PerPREnv is the environment of per-PR worktree number (path, main clone
    clone) for its hooks and its agents: WorktreeEnv under PRSlug(number).

func ProvisionLog(name string) string
    ProvisionLog is the name of slot name's provisioning log in layout.Logs(),
    its setup and post_checkout scripts' (RunLogged).

func ReadMarker(dir string) (string, error)
    ReadMarker returns dir's MarkerFile, the database slug its setup wrote,
    trimmed. The checkout's code writes it, so it is read with fsx.ReadRegular:
    a symlink or a special file is fsx.ErrNotRegular, one past 4 KiB
    fsx.ErrTooLarge, and a missing marker is fs.ErrNotExist.

func RenderMiseLocal(src []byte, strip []string, set map[string]string) ([]byte, error)
    RenderMiseLocal renders a checkout's local mise file (MiseLocal or
    MiseLocalDotted) from the main clone's file src. src is parsed as TOML:
    its `env` value must be absent or a table, however it is spelled ([env],
    [env.KEY] sub-tables, dotted keys, a root-level `env = { … }` inline table);
    every key in strip and every key in set is deleted from that table whatever
    its value (a string, an inline table, a sub-table such as { value = "…" }),
    then each key of set is set to its string value. The whole tree is encoded
    back after miseMarker with sorted keys, so the output is deterministic and
    rendering it again with the same arguments yields the same bytes. Comments
    of src are dropped, commented-out secrets with them, and so is the order of
    its keys. A src that does not parse, or whose `env` is not a table ([[env]],
    a string), is ErrMiseLocal. An empty src renders the marker and an [env]
    table with set.

func SlotDBSlug(sl store.Slot) string
    SlotDBSlug is the database slug of a slot: slots.db_slug, else the slot
    name, sanitized like a workspace name (DBSlug: review3 stays review3,
    example-review1 becomes example_review1, owner/name#7 owner_name_7),
    the slug the setup's database.yml derives from WT_BRANCH and writes to
    MarkerFile. A row that stored a raw slot name resolves to it too. Slots,
    inventory and cleanup all use it.

func SlotLog(name string) string
    SlotLog is the name of slot name's log of its other pool scripts in
    layout.Logs(): its deps, reset_db and teardown (RunLogged).

func SlotSlugRegexp(slotName string) *regexp.Regexp
    SlotSlugRegexp matches the database slugs of the slots a slot_name
    template renders: each name sanitized as SlotDBSlug sanitizes it,
    {n} as [0-9]+ (^review[0-9]+$ for review{n}, ^example_review[0-9]+$ for
    example-review{n}). DropGuard allows only these; inventory takes the
    factory's copy names' as the factory's databases.

func StripKeys(extra []string) []string
    StripKeys is DefaultStripEnv plus extra (a strip_env), sorted and
    deduplicated: the keys dropped from a checkout's rendered local mise file.

func TemplateRegexp(tmpl string) *regexp.Regexp
    TemplateRegexp matches what a slot template renders to (slot_name review{n},
    an expanded slot_path): the template anchored, its text quoted, every {n} as
    [0-9]+ (^review[0-9]+$).

func WorktreeEnv(rc *config.Repo, slug, path, clone string) map[string]string
    WorktreeEnv is the per-PR environment of a worktree (path, main clone clone)
    under workspace name slug: WT_BRANCH=slug, every WorkspaceNameVars entry
    blank, then the [[repo]] env (rc may be nil) with {slug} as slug on top.

func WriteCheckoutFile(checkout, rel string, data []byte, perm fs.FileMode) (err error)
    WriteCheckoutFile writes data to rel inside checkout atomically (temp file
    in the same directory, then rename), with permission perm, creating parent
    directories, through an os.Root on checkout: a rel that is absolute or
    escapes (.., or a symlink in a parent pointing outside) is an error and
    nothing is written outside checkout. A symlink at rel itself is replaced,
    not followed.

    The checkout holds PR-controlled files (tracked symlinks included), so every
    write magnum makes into one goes through here.


TYPES

type DBLister interface {
	ListPrefixed(ctx context.Context, prefixes []string) ([]mysqlx.Database, error)
}
    DBLister is the listing half of *mysqlx.Client: the schemas whose names
    start with one of prefixes followed by a non-empty slug, ordered by name.

type DBRecreator interface {
	Recreate(ctx context.Context, name string, g mysqlx.Guard) error
}
    DBRecreator is the part of *mysqlx.Client that empties a database: it drops
    it and creates it again (Recreate). A Deps.MySQL without it recreates
    nothing.

type Deps struct {
	Store *store.Store
	Run   execx.Runner
	// Git defaults to gitx.New(Run). Share one client with other packages so
	// fetches into the same clone stay serialized.
	Git   *gitx.Client
	MySQL MySQL // required for pool slots
	// Snapshot feeds the guard (e.g. (*herdr.Client).Snapshot). Nil skips the
	// herdr checks.
	Snapshot func(ctx context.Context) (herdr.Snapshot, error)
	// ProcessInfo (e.g. (*herdr.Client).PaneProcessInfo) lets the guard see a
	// non-shell foreground process in panes without an agent. Optional.
	ProcessInfo func(ctx context.Context, paneID string) (herdr.ProcessInfo, error)
	Layout      paths.Layout
	// Mise is the mise executable; "" means "mise" on PATH.
	Mise string
	// LookPath finds Mise for per-PR worktree hooks (nil: exec.LookPath);
	// without it they run through /bin/sh. Pool scripts always use mise.
	LookPath func(file string) (string, error)
	// Repos are the [[repo]] blocks (config.Config.Repos): setup, teardown,
	// copy_files, strip_env and env of per-PR worktrees.
	Repos []config.Repo
	// SecretEnv names the variables of the daemon's environment that hold a
	// secret of its own, the App identities' private_key_env: heavy commands
	// never inherit them (heavyUnset).
	SecretEnv []string
	// FreeDiskBytes returns the free bytes of the filesystem holding path;
	// nil uses statfs.
	FreeDiskBytes func(path string) (uint64, error)
	// Now defaults to time.Now.
	Now func() time.Time
	// Log receives one line per decision and dry-run plan (optional).
	Log execx.Logger
	// DryRun makes every mutating method log what it would do and return
	// without touching git, MySQL, files or the store. Claim returns the slot
	// it would claim.
	DryRun bool
}
    Deps are the Manager's collaborators.

type ErrHold struct {
	Reason string // one of the Hold* constants, or a manual hold_reason
	Detail string // what was seen (pane, process, shas)
}
    ErrHold is returned when a guard refuses to touch a slot because a human
    is (or may be) using it. Match it with errors.As(err, &slots.ErrHold{}) or
    AsHold. A slot.hold_reason set by hand is reported with that reason.

func AsHold(err error) (ErrHold, bool)
    AsHold reports whether err carries an ErrHold.

func (e ErrHold) Error() string

type Hook struct {
	Type    string // HookPostCreate, HookPostStart, HookPreRemove, HookSetup or HookTeardown
	Name    string // the table key ("setup"); the type for a bare string; "1", "2"… for [[repo]] commands
	Command string
}
    Hook is one command of a hook table.

type Manager struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Manager runs slot operations. Safe for concurrent use; heavy commands are
    serialized.

func New(d Deps) *Manager
    New returns a Manager.

func (m *Manager) Adopt(ctx context.Context, pool config.Pool, path string) (store.Slot, error)
    Adopt registers an existing checkout at path as a free pool slot:
    path must be pool.Path(n) for some n, a worktree of the main clone,
    its tmp/.worktree-db-slug must say DBSlug(pool.Slot(n)), and all its
    databases must exist (ErrVerify otherwise). An already registered live slot
    is ErrConflict; a removed, lost or broken row with that name is revived (its
    PR and open assignment released with reason "adopted").

func (m *Manager) CheckSchema(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pool config.Pool) (SchemaCheck, error)
    CheckSchema compares the schema a pool slot's checkout needs with the one
    its databases carry: a reload is needed when the fingerprints differ or none
    was recorded. A match is checked once more against the development database,
    whose MAX(schema_migrations.version) must be the version the checkout's
    db/schema.rb declares (a migration someone ran by hand, or an agent,
    moves it; a failed read counts as a mismatch). Read-only.

func (m *Manager) Checkout(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pr store.PR, pool config.Pool, targetSHA string) error
    Checkout puts pr's head into a claimed or held slot that belongs to pr.
    Steps (subject "slot:<name>:pr:<N>:<sha7>", a new generation on every call;
    each step is idempotent): fetch (refs/pull/N/head → refs/magnum/pr/N,
    plus origin/<base> for pool slots; when the fetched head differs from
    targetSHA the fetched head is used and a slot.head_moved event is written),
    guard, switch (detached at refs/magnum/pr/N, discarding tracked changes the
    guard took for magnum's residue after a slot.discarded event names them;
    the target commit is written to the kv store first and checked_out_sha
    right after, so a retry after a failure in a later step recognizes HEAD as
    magnum's own switch, not a human's commit), and for pool slots render_mise,
    deps (pool.post_checkout through mise exec, 30m, when the hash of the
    LockFiles and the commands differs from lock_sha) and schema (dirty_schema
    = 1 when the PR changes pool.schema_paths since its merge base with
    origin/<base>), for per-PR slots render_mise alone (PreparePerPR,
    as at the worktree's creation: the main clone's local mise file with the
    [[repo]] strip_env and env as the daemon has them now, its copy_files);
    finally verify (HEAD == fetched head → checked_out_sha, last_used_at).
    The slot state is left as it was: moving claimed → busy after the prompt is
    acked is the engine's job. Read the slot again for the sha actually checked
    out. pool is ignored for per-PR slots.

func (m *Manager) CheckoutFetched(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pr store.PR, pool config.Pool, targetSHA, fetched string) error
    CheckoutFetched is Checkout of the head Fetch brought into the slot's main
    clone (fetched), without fetching again: its fetch step only checks that
    refs/magnum/pr/N still holds that commit, and fails when a fetch since moved
    it (the caller read fetched, not the newer head).

func (m *Manager) Claim(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, pool config.Pool) (store.Slot, error)
    Claim hands a free pool slot to pr: store.FreeSlots (the slot that last
    held the PR first, then least recently used) and store.ClaimSlot for each
    candidate until one succeeds (PR → claiming, slot → claimed, open assignment
    with the pool's database names). A lost race moves on to the next slot;
    a PR that is not claimable is ErrConflict; no slot left is ErrNoFreeSlot.
    The returned row is the claimed slot.

func (m *Manager) ClearPin(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot) error
    ClearPin removes the slot's pin and nothing else: a hold a guard persisted
    (hold_reason: a person's changes, unpushed commits, a moved HEAD) stays
    until Unpin, so the guard keeps refusing the slot. A review request uses
    it on the slot `magnum open` pinned: the person's work stays protected,
    the pin alone no longer holds the review.

func (m *Manager) CreatePRWorktree(ctx context.Context, watch config.Watch, repo string, pr store.PR, targetSHA string) (store.Slot, error)
    CreatePRWorktree checks pr out into its own detached worktree for a
    repo without a pool. The main clone is found with MainClonePath (an
    existing clone under any of the usual names, else the directory to
    clone into) and the worktree goes next to it (<clone>__worktrees/pr-N).
    The slot row (kind per_pr, state provisioning) is written first; then
    steps of subject "slot:owner/name#N": clone (only when no clone was found,
    see ensureClone; an existing directory's origin must be owner/name,
    else ErrOriginMismatch), fetch (refs/pull/N/head → refs/magnum/pr/N;
    a head different from targetSHA is used and reported as slot.head_moved),
    worktree_add (--detach at refs/magnum/pr/N, skipped when listed at the
    fetched head; a listed worktree at another commit, left by an earlier
    attempt, is switched to it after Guard), verify (HEAD == fetched head),
    render_mise (the main clone's local mise file rendered with the per-PR env,
    [[repo]] copy_files), setup (the [[repo]] setup commands or the main clone's
    .config/wt.toml [post-create]/[post-start] hooks as WT_BRANCH=magnum-pr-<N>,
    see hooks.go; a failure moves the slot to broken and returns ErrBroken) and
    claim (slot → claimed with pr_id, checked_out_sha and db_slug when setup
    ran, then its open assignment). The PR's state is not changed: move it to
    claiming before calling. Calling it again for a slot that already holds pr
    returns that slot (at its recorded paths), opening its assignment if a crash
    between the claim's two writes left none; a removed, broken or lost row for
    the same PR is reused (its old assignment closed) and its steps start over.

func (m *Manager) EnsureSchema(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pool config.Pool) (string, error)
    EnsureSchema gives a pool slot handed to a person (magnum open)
    the databases of its checkout, as a round's readiness step does:
    when CheckSchema finds they carry another schema, the pool's reset_db
    runs through mise exec (ResetDBTimeout, the slot's log) and the new
    schema is recorded. It returns what it did for the person. A reload that
    MySQL refused with 3730 recreates the slot's databases and runs once more
    (RecreateDatabases). A failed reload is an error and leaves the schema
    unknown. A pool that is not LazySchema, or a per-PR worktree, runs nothing:
    its released slots carry the base schema.

func (m *Manager) Fetch(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pr store.PR, pool config.Pool) (string, error)
    Fetch is Checkout's fetch alone, for a caller that reads the head before
    it checks it out (the engine compares the project config a running agent
    reloads, before the checkout moves under it) and then checks it out with
    CheckoutFetched: refs/pull/N/head → refs/magnum/pr/N in the slot's main
    clone, plus origin/<base> for a pool slot. It returns the commit fetched,
    which may be newer than the radar's head. The slot must belong to pr; its
    state does not matter, as nothing in its work tree changes. pool is ignored
    for per-PR slots.

func (m *Manager) ForgetSchema(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot) error
    ForgetSchema marks the schema of the slot's databases unknown, before a
    reload that may stop half-way: the next round reloads them again unless
    RecordSchema follows.

func (m *Manager) Guard(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot) error
    Guard refuses to let magnum touch a slot a human may be using. It returns an
    ErrHold when:
      - the slot is pinned (HoldPinned) or has a hold_reason (that reason);
      - herdr shows an agent magnum did not start (name not starting with
        AgentPrefix), idle or not, in a pane whose cwd or foreground cwd
        is the slot or below it or in the herdr workspace of the slot's PR
        (HoldForeignAgent), or a pane in the slot without an agent whose
        foreground process is not its shell (HoldForegroundProcess). Panes of
        magnum's own live sessions are ignored, and so is the process of any
        pane in their workspaces;
      - the slot's HEAD is not the recorded checked_out_sha (HoldHeadDrift) or,
        with no recorded sha, HEAD (or, for a pool slot, its placeholder branch,
        which Release resets wherever HEAD is) carries commits on no remote or
        magnum ref (HoldUnpushed). A HEAD equal to the commit an interrupted
        Checkout (or a release's reset) was switching to is magnum's own and is
        recorded instead, and so is the PR's pushed head on a clean tree with
        nothing unpushed (pushedPRHead);
      - the working tree has changes to tracked files and a human was there
        (HoldDirtyWorktree): a foreign agent or process as above, or the PR's
        human_active_at after the slot's last checkout (last_used_at), which the
        agents package sets when someone types into the PR's magnum panes.

    Without such evidence changes are magnum's own residue (tests rewriting
    db/schema.rb, bundle install touching Gemfile.lock, copy_files the repo
    does not ignore): Guard passes, and the step that discards them records a
    slot.discarded event naming them (noteDiscard).

    Drift, unpushed commits and held changes are persisted as hold_reason,
    so the slot stays held until Unpin; live holds (agent, process) on a clean
    tree are transient. A herdr snapshot failure is returned as a plain error
    (not a hold): the caller retries later. Git checks are skipped when the slot
    directory is missing.

func (m *Manager) GuardLive(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot) error
    GuardLive is the part of Guard that saves nothing: it refuses a pinned or
    held slot (HoldPinned, its hold_reason) and a human's agent or process in
    it or in its PR's workspace (HoldForeignAgent, HoldForegroundProcess),
    and looks at neither HEAD nor the tree. A forced removal runs it instead of
    Guard: Guard would save the moved HEAD, the unpushed commits or the changes
    the force discards as the slot's hold_reason, and a removal that failed
    after it would leave the slot held in removing, where cleanup skips and
    refuses it.

func (m *Manager) HumanEvidence(ctx context.Context, sl store.Slot) (string, error)
    HumanEvidence explains why changes in slot sl's tree would be a human's
    rather than magnum's residue: its PR's human_active_at is after the slot's
    last checkout. "" when nothing says so. Live evidence (a human's agent or
    process in the slot) is Guard's; read-only, for planners that want to show
    what a release or removal would hold on.

func (m *Manager) MainClonePath(ctx context.Context, watch config.Watch, repo string) (mainClone string, found bool, err error)
    MainClonePath is where repo "owner/name" lives under the watch's clone_root:
    the clone gitx FindClone discovers (<name>, <owner>-<name>, <owner>_<name>,
    else any directory whose origin is the repository) or, when there is
    none (gitx.ErrNoClone), the directory a clone goes into: <root>/<name>,
    or <root>/<owner>-<name> when a folder named <name> exists but is not a git
    repository. found reports an existing clone.

func (m *Manager) NextSlotNumber(ctx context.Context, pool config.Pool) (int, error)
    NextSlotNumber returns the lowest slot number whose name is not used by a
    non-removed slot and whose path does not exist (an unregistered directory,
    or a removed slot's path that is back, is a human's, not magnum's to take
    over). It does not check pool.max.

func (m *Manager) Pin(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot) error
    Pin marks the slot pinned: no automatic claim, checkout, release or removal
    until Unpin.

func (m *Manager) PreparePerPR(ctx context.Context, sl store.Slot, p PerPRPlan) error
    PreparePerPR renders the main clone's local mise file into the worktree
    under its name (MiseLocalName; strip list removed, the per-PR env set;
    trusted with mise when it is available) and copies the plan's copy_files
    that exist (p.Copy, the [[repo]]'s), from sl.MainClone into sl.Path,
    at the worktree's creation and at each round's checkout (render_mise),
    every write confined to the worktree (WriteCheckoutFile). Without a local
    mise file in the main clone nothing is rendered.

func (m *Manager) ProvisionPool(ctx context.Context, pool config.Pool, n int) error
    ProvisionPool provisions pool slot number n (name pool.Slot(n),
    path pool.Path(n)). The slot row (state provisioning, kind pool,
    db_slug and placeholder_branch = name) is written first, then the
    steps of subject "slot:<name>" run: worktree_add (fetch origin/<base>,
    `git worktree add --no-track -b <name> <path> origin/<base>`, skipped when
    the path is already a worktree), render_mise, setup (each pool.setup command
    through mise exec, 45m, logged to logs/provision-<name>.log), verify_marker
    (tmp/.worktree-db-slug == name), verify_dbs (every pool database exists),
    post_checkout (each pool.post_checkout command through mise exec, 30m,
    logged there too, then lock_sha, the hash of the lockfiles and of the
    commands it ran: that of a run, not of a setup that may install less) and
    mark_free (provisioning → free, slot_databases).

    A slot that is already provisioned is left alone (nil). A provisioning
    slot resumes at the first step without an ok row; a removed or broken one
    starts over. A new or removed slot whose path already exists is refused
    (ErrConflict): that directory is not magnum's (adopt it instead). Failures
    (a failing post_checkout or its timeout too) leave the slot provisioning
    with last_error, except failed verifications, which move it to broken
    (ErrVerify). Below pool.min_free_disk_gb nothing is added (ErrLowDisk).

func (m *Manager) RecordSchema(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, c SchemaCheck) error
    RecordSchema stores c, CheckSchema's answer, as the schema the slot's
    databases carry, once its reload succeeded, and forgets the slot's failed
    resets (ResetFailed): the count is of rounds in a row.

func (m *Manager) RecreateDatabases(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pool config.Pool) error
    RecreateDatabases empties the slot's databases for a reset_db that MySQL
    refused with 3730 (ForeignKeyDropRefused): each database of the slot's own
    list (the pool's databases for its slug, pool.DBNames), and none other,
    is dropped and created again through the pool's drop guard (DropGuard),
    as the step recreate_dbs of subject slot:<name>:recreate_dbs with its begin,
    ok or fail event; the caller then runs the reset once more. A dry run,
    a pool without databases or a guard, or a MySQL that cannot recreate
    (DBRecreator) drops nothing and says why.

func (m *Manager) Release(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pool config.Pool, reason string) error
    Release hands a claimed or held pool slot back to the pool. Steps (subject
    "slot:<name>:release"): guard (Guard: pins, holds, a human's agent or
    process, HEAD drift, tracked changes a human made), then the slot moves
    to releasing, fetch_base, abort_in_progress (a merge, rebase, cherry-pick
    or revert left in progress, which git would refuse the reset over,
    is aborted after a slot.discarded event for the tracked changes it drops,
    with a slot.aborted event: abortInProgress), reset (placeholder branch
    → origin/<base>, tracked changes discarded after a slot.discarded event,
    checked_out_sha cleared; origin/<base>'s commit is written to the kv store
    first, as Checkout's switch does, so a release interrupted after the reset
    is no head drift), delete_ref (refs/magnum/pr/N, kept for a row of another
    repository: otherRepository), render_mise, deps, schema_check (resetSchema:
    a LazySchema pool keeps the databases unless MAX(schema_migrations.version)
    of the development database differs from the version of the schema recorded
    for them; otherwise when dirty_schema is set or that version differs from
    db/schema.rb at HEAD: the slot moves to dirty_schema and pool.reset_db
    runs through mise exec, 30m; a second failure in a row moves the slot to
    broken, with its PR released unless it is pinned, and returns ErrBroken,
    as does a slot whose readiness reset_db failed in BreakAfterResetFailures
    rounds in a row) and mark_free (store.ReleaseSlot: free, pr_id cleared,
    assignment closed with reason). A releasing or dirty_schema slot resumes
    after its last completed step, after Guard ran again: whatever a human did
    since the last attempt refuses the release before its next destructive step.
    Per-PR slots are removed instead (RemovePRWorktree semantics).

func (m *Manager) Remove(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pool config.Pool, force bool) error
    Remove tears a pool slot down: steps of subject "slot:<name>:remove" are
    guard (skipped with force: Guard, untracked files counted as changes since
    the removal deletes them), teardown (pool.teardown through mise exec,
    skipped when the directory is gone), verify_dbs_gone (leftover pool
    databases dropped with the pool's drop guard, slot_databases marked
    dropped), worktree_remove (--force with force or over magnum's residue,
    see removeWorktree), branch_delete (placeholder, -D), worktree_prune and
    mark_removed. RemoveStates can be removed; with force also ForceRemoveStates
    (never busy). A removing slot resumes after the guard ran again; a removed
    one is a no-op. Per-PR slots are handed to RemovePRWorktree.

func (m *Manager) RemovePRWorktree(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, force bool) error
    RemovePRWorktree removes a per-PR worktree: steps of subject
    "slot:owner/name#N:remove" are guard (skipped with force: Guard, untracked
    files counted as changes), teardown (the [[repo]] teardown commands or the
    main clone's .config/wt.toml [pre-remove] hooks as WT_BRANCH=magnum-pr-<N>;
    skipped when the directory is gone, failures logged and tolerated),
    worktree_remove (--force with force or over magnum's residue,
    see removeWorktree), delete_ref (refs/magnum/pr/N), worktree_prune and
    mark_removed (pr_id cleared, assignment closed). RemovePRStates can be
    removed (a busy slot is ErrConflict); a removing one resumes after the guard
    ran again; a removed one is a no-op.

func (m *Manager) Repair(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, pool config.Pool) error
    Repair re-runs provisioning (render, setup, verification, post_checkout)
    for a free, broken, provisioning or lost slot; a missing worktree is added
    again. The slot ends free, its PR and open assignment released (reason
    "repaired"). A pinned or held slot is refused (ErrHold): Unpin it first.

func (m *Manager) Reserve(ctx context.Context, pr store.PR, pool config.Pool) (store.Slot, error)
    Reserve hands a free pool slot to pr without touching the PR's state,
    for a human who wants the PR's checkout back (magnum open on a parked PR):
    like Claim but through store.AssignSlot (slot → claimed with pr_id,
    open assignment with the pool's database names). A claimed or held slot the
    PR already has is returned as is; no free slot left is ErrNoFreeSlot.

func (m *Manager) ResetFailed(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, cause string) (int, error)
    ResetFailed counts a round whose readiness reset_db failed in slot,
    with cause (the failed command's last line), and returns how many rounds
    in a row failed it. At BreakAfterResetFailures the slot's release breaks
    it (store.BreakSlot, as the release's own reload failing twice does),
    so `magnum slots repair` takes it; the round itself goes on.

func (m *Manager) Resync(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot, sha string) error
    Resync puts a slot back in order after a run that committed in it (the fix
    job's fixer): it switches the slot, detached, to sha and records sha as
    checked_out_sha, so Guard sees no head drift and the next round's checkout
    starts clean. sha is the head the job settled on, a commit id: the one
    the fixer pushed, or the head the review ran on when nothing was pushed,
    in which case the fixer's local commits are left behind (the reflog keeps
    them). It runs the steps guard, fetch, abort_in_progress and switch under
    the subject "slot:<name>:resync:<sha7>", a new generation on every call,
    and ends with a slot.resync event:
      - guard is guardDiscard, not Guard: the slot is refused (ErrHold) when it
        is pinned or held, when a person's agent or process is in it, or when
        someone typed into the PR's magnum panes since its checkout and the tree
        has tracked changes (held as dirty_worktree), because the switch drops
        those changes; Guard's head check would persist the very drift Resync
        repairs as the slot's hold;
      - fetch looks sha up in the slot and fetches the commit by id into the
        main clone only when the slot lacks it (a head pushed from another
        clone);
      - abort_in_progress ends a merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert left in
        progress (the fixer's base merge, fix-sync's replay), which git would
        refuse the switch over (abortInProgress);
      - switch notes the tracked changes it drops (a slot.discarded event) and
        records the resulting HEAD as checked_out_sha through the pending-switch
        key, as a checkout does. A HEAD that already is sha with no tracked
        changes is only recorded, with no switch.

    Resync can run again after any failure, and again for the same sha.

func (m *Manager) RunHeavy(ctx context.Context, dir string, env map[string]string, script, label, logName string, timeout time.Duration) error
    RunHeavy runs one heavy script in dir (a slot) through mise exec with env,
    a pool script's way, under timeout, through RunLogged: serialized with every
    other heavy command, with a redacted transcript in layout.Logs()/<logName>.

func (m *Manager) RunLogged(ctx context.Context, c execx.Cmd, logName string) error
    RunLogged runs a heavy command c, serialized with every other heavy
    command of the Manager and without the daemon's secrets (heavyUnset:
    the git variables, DefaultStripEnv and Deps.SecretEnv), and appends a
    redacted transcript to layout.Logs()/<logName>: the begin line when the
    command starts (`tail -f` shows which step runs), then its output, each
    stream cut to its last logStreamTail bytes, and the end line. The rotation
    is decided before the begin line for the largest block a command can append,
    so a command's lines land in one file and a log stays under SlotLogMax.

func (m *Manager) ShellCmd(dir string, env map[string]string, script, label string, timeout time.Duration) execx.Cmd
    ShellCmd is the command that runs script in dir with env, a per-PR hook's
    way: `mise -C dir exec -- env K=V… /bin/sh -c script` when mise is available
    (as pool scripts do), else /bin/sh -c script with env overlaid (blank values
    exported blank).

func (m *Manager) Unpin(ctx context.Context, slot store.Slot) error
    Unpin hands the slot back to automation: pinned and hold_reason are cleared,
    and so is a last_error that is a hold ("slots: held: …"). A head_drift or
    unpushed_commits hold is acknowledged by taking the current HEAD as the new
    checked_out_sha, so the next guard passes and the next release resets the
    slot. A dirty_worktree hold comes back at the next guard while the changes
    are there and a human still shows (their agent or process in the slot,
    or human_active_at after the checkout): commit, stash or discard them first
    (or remove the slot with force).

type MySQL interface {
	DBLister
	SchemaMigrationsMax(ctx context.Context, dbName string) (string, error)
	DropAll(ctx context.Context, names []string, g mysqlx.Guard) []mysqlx.DropResult
}
    MySQL is the part of *mysqlx.Client the slots package uses.

type PerPRPlan struct {
	Source          string
	Slug            string
	Setup, Teardown []Hook
	Copy, Strip     []string
	Env             map[string]string
}
    PerPRPlan is what magnum runs for one per-PR worktree (PlanPerPR):
    the commands' Source ("[[repo]] owner/name", WTConfigFile or "" for none),
    the workspace name Slug (PRSlug of the number for a PR's own), the Setup
    and Teardown hooks (templates expanded), the [[repo]] copy_files (Copy),
    the keys dropped from the rendered local mise file (Strip: StripKeys of the
    [[repo]] strip_env) and the hooks' and agents' Env (WorktreeEnv).

func PlanPerPR(rc *config.Repo, repo, slug, path, clone, base string) (PerPRPlan, error)
    PlanPerPR resolves the setup/teardown commands, files and environment of a
    per-PR worktree of repo (owner/name, its [[repo]] block rc, nil for none;
    path the worktree, clone its main clone) under workspace name slug
    (PRSlug of the number for a PR's own worktree; the env is WorktreeEnv's,
    and wt.toml's {{ branch }} is slug) for a PR based on base. A wt.toml that
    cannot be read, parsed or templated is ErrHook.

type SchemaCheck struct {
	// Need is true when the slot's databases must be reloaded (the pool's
	// reset_db) to carry the checkout's schema.
	Need bool
	// Why says why a reload is needed, or why not ("schema unchanged since
	// abc1234: no reset").
	Why string
	// FP, SHA and Version are the checkout's schema: the fingerprint of
	// the files schema_paths match at SHA (its HEAD) and the version its
	// db/schema.rb declares ("" = none). RecordSchema stores them once the
	// reload succeeded.
	FP, SHA, Version string
}
    SchemaCheck is CheckSchema's answer for a pool slot.

type WTHooks struct {
	PostCreate []Hook
	PostStart  []Hook
	PreRemove  []Hook
}
    WTHooks are the hook tables of a .config/wt.toml, each in file order.

func ParseWTHooks(data []byte) (WTHooks, error)
    ParseWTHooks reads the [post-create], [post-start] and [pre-remove] tables
    of a worktrunk project config (`post-start = "cmd"` is accepted as a
    one-command table named after the hook). Commands keep their {{ templates
    }}; every other key is ignored. A non-string command is an error.

```

## sqlitetest

```text
package sqlitetest // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/sqlitetest"

Package sqlitetest keeps a test's SQLite database in memory: a private database
on one connection, loaded from the image of a database a test binary migrated
once, so the test writes no database file. storetest and registrytest build
their registries on it, and the store package's own tests use it directly (they
cannot import storetest). It imports only the SQLite driver and the standard
library. Only tests and those helpers import it.

CONSTANTS

const FastFile = "_pragma=journal_mode(MEMORY)&_pragma=synchronous(OFF)"
    FastFile is what a test's own raw writer of a database file (an old schema
    a migration test starts from) adds to its DSN: the rollback journal stays in
    memory and nothing is synced, so the file is written once.

const Params = "_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)&_pragma=foreign_keys(1)&_pragma=temp_store(MEMORY)&_txlock=immediate"
    Params are the connection settings of store.Open and registry.Open
    (busy_timeout 5 s, foreign keys on, temporary tables in memory,
    BEGIN IMMEDIATE) without the two that only a file has: journal_mode(WAL),
    which a memory database refuses (its journal is in memory), and synchronous.


VARIABLES

var ErrLostConnection = errors.New("sqlitetest: the in-memory database lost its only connection")
    ErrLostConnection is what every use of a database from Open returns after
    its only connection was closed: the database lived in that connection,
    so a new one would be empty.


FUNCTIONS

func FileImage(image []byte) []byte
    FileImage returns a copy of image with header bytes 18 and 19 set to 2,
    the bytes of a WAL database checkpointed and closed: what a test writes to a
    file that store.Open or registry.Open then opens.

func Image(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB) ([]byte, error)
    Image returns the bytes of db's main database (sqlite3_serialize): for an
    in-memory database, the file SQLite would write, with a rollback header
    (bytes 18 and 19 = 1), which Open loads.

func Open(image []byte, params string) (*sql.DB, error)
    Open opens a private in-memory database with params (Params, or a test's
    own), loaded from image (nil starts empty). The pool holds one connection,
    which never expires, because the connection is the database: once it is
    closed every use fails with ErrLostConnection rather than going on with
    an empty database. The image is copied, so one image serves every test of
    a binary. It must be a rollback image (header bytes 18 and 19 = 1), which
    Image returns; a WAL file's bytes are refused (FileImage turns one into the
    other).

```

## staging

```text
package staging // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/staging"

Package staging tells, for each open PR and each staging environment of its
repository, whether the PR is live there (latest), pushed but not yet confirmed
by a deployment (pushed), on staging at an older commit (outdated), absent
(none), or unknown.

It reads a treeless bare mirror of the repository (`git clone --bare
--filter=tree:0`), GitHub's deployments of each environment and ci.yml's runs.
A staging deploy is a two-parent merge, [staging tip, PR head], pushed to
staging-<env>; Jenkins deploys a tip once its ci.yml passes and then records a
deployment of the environment whose ref is that tip. So a PR is on staging at
commit X when X is the newest PR commit that is an ancestor of a second parent
of the branch's first-parent chain (within a window), and live when the newest
successful deployment's history holds the merge that brought it in. Ancestry
decides, never sha equality.

Status, Refresh and Effects only read: Status never pushes, and every git
command runs in the package's own mirror directory. Refresh fetches and reads
GitHub at most once a minute per repository across processes (a flock and a
state file beside the mirror); Status is a pure lookup over the last Refresh.

The deploy (deploy.go) is the one writer: on the operator's confirmed word,
Deploy merges a PR into a shared staging-<env> branch as that two-parent merge
and pushes it with a plain push, through a resumable effect whose journal sits
beside the mirror (<mirror_dir>/<owner>/<repo>.deploys). Plan shows the operator
what a deploy would do first; Step advances the effects a tick at a time;
Cancel stops one. A deploy never force-pushes, never pushes after a cancel,
and never reverts a push.

CONSTANTS

const (
	StepClaim   = "claim"
	StepPlan    = "plan"
	StepMerge   = "merge"
	StepVerify  = "verify"
	StepPush    = "push"
	StepWatch   = "watch"
	StepConfirm = "confirm"
)
    The steps of an effect, in order (Effect.Step).

const (
	PhaseBegin = "begin"
	PhaseOK    = "ok"
	PhaseFail  = "fail"
)
    The phases of a step, as Deps.Event gets them.

const (
	// EffectQueued: another effect runs on the env; this one waits.
	EffectQueued = "queued"
	// EffectRunning: it holds the env and advances a step at each Step.
	EffectRunning = "running"
	// EffectNeedsYou: it stopped before anything was pushed, for the
	// operator: the tip moved and the merge now brings migrations or
	// workflow changes the plan did not show. A new plan and Deploy of the
	// same PR and head resumes it.
	EffectNeedsYou = "needs you"
	// EffectFailed: it ended on a failure, Why says which; before the push
	// step nothing was pushed.
	EffectFailed = "failed"
	// EffectCancelled: the operator cancelled it; a push before the cancel
	// stands.
	EffectCancelled = "cancelled"
	// EffectDone: pushed, CI passed, and a deployment holds the merge, or
	// Why starts with NotConfirmed.
	EffectDone = "done"
)
    The states of an effect (Effect.State). Queued and running are live;
    the others end it.

const (
	ByCLI     = "cli"
	ByLiaison = "liaison"
	ByFactory = "factory"
)
    Who asks for a deploy (Deploy's by), recorded in the journal and every
    Event; never inferred.

const (
	ResolveRunning = "running"
	ResolveDone    = "done"
	ResolveFailed  = "failed"
)
    The states of a resolver's job (ResolveResult.State).

const (
	// Window and WindowAge bound the first-parent walk from a branch's tip:
	// the last Window first-parent commits, or WindowAge, whichever ends
	// first. A PR merged before it is none.
	Window    = 400
	WindowAge = 90 * 24 * time.Hour
	// ConfirmWait is Status's: how long after the push (the merge's
	// committer time) a passed ci.yml waits for a deployment before the PR
	// is "not confirmed".
	ConfirmWait = 45 * time.Minute
	// ConfirmAfterCI is a deploy's: how long after ci.yml passed on its
	// merge the confirm step waits for a deployment that holds the merge
	// before the effect ends done, "pushed, not confirmed" (Jenkins waits up
	// to 50 minutes for ci.yml, then migrates and deploys).
	ConfirmAfterCI = 50 * time.Minute
	// RefreshEvery is how often Refresh fetches and reads GitHub for a
	// repository at most, across every process that shares the mirror.
	RefreshEvery = time.Minute
	// StaleAfter is how old the last good Refresh may be before Status says
	// unknown, "stale": Refreshes that keep failing or being cut never leave
	// an old answer standing.
	StaleAfter = 10 * time.Minute
	// Workflow is the workflow file whose run on a merge says its CI.
	Workflow = "ci.yml"
)
    The fixed numbers of the rules.

const NotConfirmed = "pushed, not confirmed"
    NotConfirmed starts the Why of an effect done without a deployment that
    holds its merge: none ConfirmAfterCI after ci.yml passed, or the deployments
    are not readable.

const WhyNotReadable = "deployments not readable (Deployments: read on the poll App)"
    WhyNotReadable is EnvStatus.Why of a pushed PR whose environment's
    deployments GitHub refuses (a 403 or 404): not readable is never "none".

const WhyVolumeNotMounted = "the mirror's volume is not mounted"
    WhyVolumeNotMounted is EnvStatus.Why while the mirror's volume (a
    /Volumes/<name> disk) is not mounted.


VARIABLES

var ErrNoMirror = errors.New("no mirror")
    ErrNoMirror is what Git.Base's error wraps when dir is no mirror: Refresh
    moves such a dir aside and clones the mirror again.

var ErrNotReadable = errors.New("not readable")
    ErrNotReadable is what GitHub.DeploymentsOf's error wraps on a 403 or a 404:
    the token may not read deployments, which never means "none".


FUNCTIONS

func DeployBeforeMerge(paths []string, envs []EnvStatus) (migrations []string, needed bool)
    DeployBeforeMerge reports whether a PR whose changed files are paths must
    go to a staging before its merge: it changes a migration (migrations are
    every such path, in byte order, each once; nil for none, even when needed
    is false), and every environment in envs was read and holds none of the PR's
    head. An environment that is latest or pushed holds the head, and one that
    is unknown may hold it, so either makes needed false: the needs-you line
    says only what the mirror backs. No environments (staging not configured) is
    never needed. The board and the factory's card share this rule and its words
    (DeployBeforeMergeWords).

func DeployBeforeMergeWords(migrations []string) string
    DeployBeforeMergeWords is the needs-you line of a PR that DeployBeforeMerge
    says needs a staging deploy before its merge: the first of its migrations
    (byte order) by name, and how many more there are (MigrationWords). The
    first clause, "deploy to a staging before the merge", is the same for any
    count: the board stores the words as they are, and the factory's short form
    is that clause (it cuts at the first " ("). No migration is no line: "".

func MigrationWords(migrations []string) string
    MigrationWords say which migrations a PR changes: the first of
    migrations (byte order) by name, and how many more there are ("it changes
    db/migrate/a.rb", "it changes db/migrate/a.rb and 2 more migrations");
    "" for none. DeployBeforeMergeWords and any line that names the migrations
    of a PR share them.

func MirrorDir(root string) func(repo string) (dir string, ok bool)
    MirrorDir is Deps.Mirror over staging mirror_dir root: owner/name's mirror
    is <root>/<owner>/<name>.git, in lower case. It reports ok false for no
    root, a root that is /Volumes or a volume's root, a repository name that is
    not owner/name, and a root under /Volumes/<volume> while that volume is not
    mounted (then with the dir, which Refresh reads as WhyVolumeNotMounted).
    It creates nothing.

func MirrorRoot(root string) func() (dir string, ok bool)
    MirrorRoot is Deps.MirrorRoot over staging mirror_dir root, beside
    MirrorDir: root itself, ok false for no root, a root that is /Volumes or a
    volume's root, and a root under /Volumes/<volume> while that volume is not
    mounted (then with root). It creates nothing.


TYPES

type Client struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Client answers staging status from what Refresh read. It is safe for
    concurrent use.

func New(d Deps) *Client
    New returns a Client on d.

func (c *Client) Cancel(ctx context.Context, id EffectID) error
    Cancel stops effect id at once: a queued or running effect ends cancelled,
    its resolver job is cancelled, and it never pushes after (a step in flight
    finishes first, under the effect's flock). A cancel after the push stops
    only the watching: the push stands, a deploy never reverts. An effect
    that already ended stays as it is. It finds the effect under mirror_dir,
    whoever started it.

func (c *Client) Close()
    Close stops the client's background clones and waits for them: their context
    ends, so execx ends each git's process group (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL),
    and the half clone is removed; a clone it cut counts as no failure. A closed
    client starts no clone, whatever Refresh it races. It also lets go of the
    env flocks of the deploys it runs: their journals stand, and the next client
    resumes them. The daemons' wiring is to call it when a daemon stops.

func (c *Client) Deploy(ctx context.Context, plan DeployPlan, by string) ([]EffectID, error)
    Deploy starts, on the operator's confirmed plan, one effect per env,
    or resumes the one of the same PR and head that needs you there;
    by is who asked (ByCLI, ByLiaison, ByFactory). It starts all or none:
    every env is checked first (on the allowlist, with a plan: no Why, a tip,
    at most maxPlanPaths migrations; no live effect of the same PR at the same
    head), and every journal is written, under the deploys dir's flock, before
    any claim; a write that fails takes the others back. Each effect is written
    queued and claims its env when no other effect holds or waits for it;
    it returns at once, after the claim: Step does the rest.

func (c *Client) Effects(repo string) []Effect
    Effects lists repo's effects, the newest first, from their journals:
    those of every process that deploys from the same mirror_dir.

func (c *Client) Plan(ctx context.Context, pr PR, envs []Env) (DeployPlan, error)
    Plan reads, never writes a journal or pushes: for each env, the current tip,
    whether the PR's head merges cleanly into it (merge-tree in the mirror),
    the migrations the merge adds and whether it changes any .github/workflows
    path. It fetches the env branches and the PR's pull ref into the mirror,
    under its flock. Every env must pass the allowlist, and the remote's pull
    ref must be the PR's head; an env whose branch is absent, whose merge cannot
    be read or whose tip holds the head already has Why. The caller shows the
    plan to the operator before Deploy.

func (c *Client) Refresh(ctx context.Context, repo string, open []OpenPR) error
    Refresh fetches the mirror once (the staging-* tips, each distinct base of
    the open PRs and their refs/pull/N/head, and those another client asked for
    in the last minutes), reads each staging environment's deployments (with
    their ETag) and the ci.yml runs of the merges that brought the open PRs'
    heads in, and builds the lookup data Status reads for the repository, each
    PR's commits derived as its Base..refs/pull/N/head. A base that is no plain
    branch name (git check-ref-format --branch, no leading '-') is refused and
    never reaches git; its PRs, and those of a base the fetch cannot read, are
    unknown, Why naming the base. It runs at most once a minute per repository
    across processes (a flock in the mirror dir); a call within the minute
    reuses the data and returns its error again. It never blocks longer than
    ctx: a Refresh that ctx cuts keeps the data it had and returns ctx's error.

    The first Refresh of a repository, or one that finds its mirror dir no bare
    repository of its own (it is moved aside, never repaired in place), starts
    the clone in the background on a context of its own (at most cloneTimeout)
    under the flock, and returns: until it is done every status is unknown,
    "cloning the mirror". A clone that fails is tried again after 1, 5, 15 and
    then 60 minutes.

func (c *Client) Status(pr PR, envs []Env) []EnvStatus
    Status returns where pr stands on each of envs, in their order, from the
    last Refresh of pr.Repo: no git, no network. Without a Refresh (or with one
    that failed), each env is unknown.

func (c *Client) Step(ctx context.Context) error
    Step advances every live effect under mirror_dir one step: per env,
    the effect this client holds the env for, or the next one it can claim
    (an env another process holds is left to it). It finds the effects itself
    (deployRepos), so a deploy one daemon started resumes in the other with no
    wiring. It never blocks on an agent or on CI, only on git in the mirror
    (a fetch, a merge, a push); a Step while another runs on the same client
    returns at once. A daemon calls it each tick.

type Commit struct {
	SHA     string
	Parents []string
	At      time.Time // committer time (FirstParent only)
}
    Commit is a commit as the mirror lists it.

type DeployPlan struct {
	PR   PR
	Envs []EnvPlan
	At   time.Time
}
    DeployPlan is what a deploy of PR would do on each env, for the operator to
    confirm before Deploy.

type Deployment struct {
	ID        int64
	SHA       string // the commit GitHub resolved the deployment's ref to
	Ref       string // the ref as created (the deploy records the tip's sha)
	CreatedAt time.Time
	Success   bool // it has a success status
}
    Deployment is a GitHub deployment of an environment.

type Deployments struct {
	// ETag is the answer's ETag, to send as If-None-Match next time.
	ETag string
	// NotModified: GitHub answered 304 to the etag sent; List is empty and
	// the last list stands.
	NotModified bool
	// List is the deployments, newest first (a page is enough: the newest
	// successful one is what counts).
	List []Deployment
}
    Deployments is one read of an environment's deployments.

type Deps struct {
	Git    Git
	GitHub GitHub
	// Mirror is the repository's mirror dir; ok false = not configured or
	// its volume is absent (dir, when not "", says which: MirrorDir).
	Mirror func(repo string) (dir string, ok bool)
	// GitEnv is the environment of the fetch (the poll identity's git env:
	// its GH_CONFIG_DIR, the credential helper's login); gh is git's only
	// credential helper, so the operator's own credentials never answer
	// implicitly. Nil, or nil for a repository, and nothing is fetched.
	// MirrorRoot is mirror_dir, where a deploy finds every effect (Step and
	// Cancel scan <mirror_dir>/*/*.deploys); ok false = not configured or
	// its volume is not mounted, and nothing is scanned (MirrorRoot).
	MirrorRoot func() (dir string, ok bool)
	GitEnv     func(repo string) map[string]string
	Now        func() time.Time
	Log        *slog.Logger

	// Stagings lists the staging environments a repository may be deployed
	// to: its [[factory.repo.staging]] entries (config.Stagings). Nil, or no
	// entry for an environment, refuses every deploy to it; the structural
	// rules (the branch is staging-<name>, never master, main, the remote's
	// default branch or production*) apply as well.
	Stagings func(repo string) []Env
	// Resolver resolves a deploy's merge conflict; nil = none: a conflict
	// ends the effect failed, "conflict: resolver not configured".
	Resolver Resolver
	// PushEnv is called right before each push: it applies its own rules
	// (a merge that changes .github/workflows) and returns the env of the
	// push (the bot's credentials); nil = push not configured: the effect
	// ends failed at push.
	PushEnv PushEnv
	// CommitIdentity is the bot's name and email, the author and the
	// committer of a deploy's merge commit. Nil, or an error, ends the
	// effect at merge, "commit identity not configured", with no commit.
	CommitIdentity func(ctx context.Context, repo string) (name, email string, err error)
	// Event records each step's begin, ok and fail (phase) of an effect, by
	// whom it was asked (Effect.By); text holds shas, counts, the effect's
	// own words and paths made safe, never PR text. Nil = not recorded. An
	// event is written in the journal with the state it records and handed
	// to Event after that write, and after the deploys dir's and the
	// effect's flocks are let go (the env's, held for the effect's life and
	// only ever tried, may be held), so a crash between the two hands it on
	// when the effect next loads: at least once. A repeat (a crash, or another
	// client loading the same write) has the same key, (e.ID, e.Seq, step,
	// phase), which the registry dedupes on; e is the effect as that write
	// left it. Each flush delivers in Seq order, but two flushes can
	// interleave (two clients, or a Step beside a Cancel or a Deploy of one
	// client): order a deploy's events by Seq, never by arrival. An ended
	// deploy's outbox is delivered by the next Step's scan (settle). A
	// failure the step tries again records none; the end it leads to records
	// one.
	Event func(e Effect, step, phase, text string)
}
    Deps is what a Client runs on.

type Detail string
    Detail is why a pushed PR is not confirmed yet.

const (
	// DetailCIRunning: ci.yml runs on the merge (or has not started yet).
	DetailCIRunning Detail = "ci_running"
	// DetailCIFailedOurs: ci.yml failed, and a failing job names a path the
	// PR changes, or a job failed on the PR's merge's own run that passed on
	// the branch's tip right before it ("new against" it: a flaky job reads
	// the same).
	DetailCIFailedOurs Detail = "ci_failed_ours"
	// DetailCIFailedNotOurs: ci.yml failed, but neither: no failing job names
	// a path the PR changes, and the same jobs failed on the tip before, or
	// the run covers more first-parent commits or is a later merge's, or it
	// cannot be told (Why says so).
	DetailCIFailedNotOurs Detail = "ci_failed_not_ours"
	// DetailWaitingJenkins: ci.yml passed, and the deploy has not recorded a
	// deployment yet, less than ConfirmWait after the push.
	DetailWaitingJenkins Detail = "waiting_jenkins"
	// DetailNotConfirmed: ci.yml passed but no deployment holds the merge
	// ConfirmWait after the push, or the deployments are not readable.
	DetailNotConfirmed Detail = "not_confirmed"
)
    The details of StatePushed.

type Effect struct {
	ID               EffectID
	Repo             string
	Env              Env
	PR               PR
	By               string
	Step, State, Why string
	Merge, RunURL    string
	Try              int
	Started, Updated time.Time
	Seq              int
}
    Effect is a deploy effect as the screens see it: its step and state, why,
    the merge's sha once made, ci.yml's run, and Try, the merge's try (1, and
    one more after each move of the tip). Seq is the journal write it was read
    at: each write counts one more. With an Event it is the write that recorded
    the event, so (ID, Seq, step, phase) keys a delivery: Deps.Event is at least
    once, and a repeat carries the same key.

type EffectID string
    EffectID names a deploy effect: <env>-<pr>-<time>-<random>, lower-case
    letters, digits and dashes.

type Env struct{ Name, Branch string }
    Env is a staging environment: its name, which is also the GitHub deployment
    environment, and its branch, staging-<name>.

type EnvPlan struct {
	Env        Env
	Tip        string
	Clean      bool
	Conflicts  []string
	Migrations []string
	Workflows  bool
	Why        string
}
    EnvPlan is a deploy's plan on one env: the branch's tip, whether the PR's
    head merges into it cleanly (else the conflicted paths), the migrations
    the merge adds (db/migrate files it adds against the tip), and whether it
    changes any .github/workflows path. Why says why the env has no plan (no
    such branch, the merge could not be read, the head is on the branch already:
    "already there"); Deploy refuses such an env. The paths are as git lists
    them, not made safe for a terminal.

type EnvStatus struct {
	Env         Env
	State       State
	Detail      Detail
	Tip         string    // staging-<env>'s tip
	DeployedTip string    // the newest successful deployment's ref, "" if not readable
	DeployedAt  time.Time // when that deployment was created
	InTip       string    // the PR commit found in the tip: the head, or for outdated the older one
	Behind      int       // outdated: the PR's commits after InTip that the tip lacks
	PushedAt    time.Time // the merge commit that brought InTip in: its committer time
```
