var ErrSettingsChanged = errors.New("the config file changed on disk since it was read")
    ErrSettingsChanged is a save over a file that changed on disk since the
    screen read it; a source wraps its own error in it, and the screen offers to
    read the file again and keep the staged edits.


FUNCTIONS

func AskComment(login, key, question, context, example string, options []CardOption) string
    AskComment is the Jira comment the factory drafts when you ask login a
    question of task key instead of answering it: the question, why it is asked,
    its example and the options (the ask and your-own-words options of a card
    left out). The factory writes it for you to post, and the recap shows the
    same text before you send.

func BoardHelpKeys() []string
    BoardHelpKeys are the key labels the PR board's help lists ("g / G", "ctrl+r
    / F5"): the keys the help of `magnum tui` has to name.

func DashboardHelpKeys() []string
    DashboardHelpKeys are the key labels the status dashboard's help lists ("j/k
    ↑/↓", "enter, o"): the keys the help of `magnum status` has to name.

func DeltaCheckPhrase(lines int) string
    DeltaCheckPhrase names a delta check of lines changed code lines: "delta
    check (4 lines)".

func HumanAgo(d time.Duration) string
    HumanAgo renders how long ago something happened: "12s ago". Zero or a
    negative duration means it never happened and renders as "never".

func HumanBytes(n int64) string
    HumanBytes renders a byte count the way the plain-text status does: "0",
    "812K", "34M", "1.3G".

func HumanDuration(d time.Duration) string
    HumanDuration renders a duration compactly: "42s", "7m", "3h12m", "2d4h".
    A negative duration renders as its absolute value.

func IsTerminal(f *os.File) bool
    IsTerminal reports whether f is a terminal (the termios ioctl answers), so
    a caller picks a screen of this package over plain-text output. /dev/null,
    pipes and regular files are not terminals.

func NewSettings(ctx context.Context, src SettingsSource, rt SettingsRuntime, opts SettingsOptions) tea.Model
    NewSettings is the settings screen as a model, for a program of the
    caller's: RunSettings runs it in one of its own. Leaving it quits that
    program (tea.Quit).

func OpenHoldPhrase(hold time.Duration) string
    OpenHoldPhrase is how long a restore by `magnum open` holds the PR, as its
    question says it: "until 30 minutes after your last input" for an open_hold
    of 30m, "until you unpin it" for 0, a lasting pin.

func OpenRestoreQuestion(ref string, hold time.Duration) string
    OpenRestoreQuestion asks before an open restores ref in a slot (the board's
    o, `magnum open` on a terminal): the role it opens has no live pane,
    so the daemon claims a slot, resumes the sessions and holds the PR for hold
    ([daemon] open_hold; 0 pins it until `magnum unpin`, OpenHoldPhrase).

func RatingReasonKeys() []string
    RatingReasonKeys are the keys of the reasons the task card's + and − offer,
    in the order of their digits: the keys the factory takes for a rating
    (factory.RatingReasons), which a test in the cli pins them to.

func RenderPRBoard(rows []PRBoardRow, width int, opts PRBoardOptions) string
    RenderPRBoard renders the board once, for output that is not interactive and
    for tests: the title bar, the state summary, the column headings and every
    row of opts.DefaultView and opts.DefaultOwner (in opts.DefaultSort order,
    largest first), fitted to width (0 = no limit). It uses the dark palette and
    no cursor; ages count from opts.Now.

func RunDashboard(ctx context.Context, src DashboardSource, act DashboardActions, opts DashboardOptions) error
    RunDashboard shows the live status dashboard until the user quits or
    ctx ends. act may be nil (the action keys then say so). It returns
    ErrSwitchToBoard when the user pressed tab (or t) for the PR board.

func RunFactory(ctx context.Context, src FactorySource, act FactoryActions, opts FactoryOptions) error
    RunFactory shows the factory screen until the operator quits or ctx ends.
    act may be nil: the screen then only shows, and its action keys say so.

func RunPRBoard(ctx context.Context, src PRBoardSource, act DashboardActions, opts PRBoardOptions) error
    RunPRBoard shows the live PR board until the user quits or ctx ends. act may
    be nil (the action keys then say so). It returns ErrSwitchToDashboard when
    the user pressed tab for the status dashboard.

func RunSettings(ctx context.Context, src SettingsSource, rt SettingsRuntime, opts SettingsOptions) error
    RunSettings shows the settings screen until the user leaves it or ctx ends.
    src may not be nil; rt may be (the Runtime section then says so).

func RunWatch(ctx context.Context, fetch WatchFetch, opts WatchOptions) error
    RunWatch mirrors fetch's frames full-screen, read-only, until the user
    quits (q, esc or ctrl+c), ctx ends (both return nil) or a fetch returns a
    StopWatch error (RunWatch returns the wrapped error).

func StageDuration(d time.Duration) string
    StageDuration renders a stage's length: "12s", "18m04s", "1h02m".

func StagingDeploySummary(d StagingDeploy, now time.Time) string
    StagingDeploySummary is d in the words of the card's STAGINGS block, without
    its effect: its state ("not confirmed" for a done no deployment confirms),
    the step and phase of its last event, and how long ago that came ("running ·
    push begin · 3m ago").

func StagingDeployWords(d StagingDeploy) []string
    StagingDeployWords are the lines under a deploy on the card and in `magnum
    staging`: its last event's words, then why it ended, once when they are
    the same (an end's event says its why), then what the resolver does for its
    conflict ("resolver try 1: ...", naming the agent's pane).

func StagingDeploysFolded(ds []StagingDeploy) []bool
    StagingDeploysFolded says for each of ds whether it folds into one line
    (StagingFoldedLine) on the card and in `magnum staging`: a deploy that
    ended failed or cancelled, and that a later deploy of the same env and
    head follows, one whose last event came after its own. The later one
    speaks for the env then, whatever it is (running, failed too, done), so the
    earlier one's long words are not said again. A deploy that is not over,
    one that needs you, a done one and a deploy with no known head never fold.
    Only the views fold: the action log, `magnum staging --json` and
    engine.StagingDeploysOf keep every record.

func StagingFoldedLine(d StagingDeploy) string
    StagingFoldedLine is the one line of a deploy that StagingDeploysFolded
    folds: its effect and that an earlier try ended, "deploy <effect>:
    an earlier try failed" (or "was cancelled").

func StagingSummary(s StagingInfo, now time.Time) string
    StagingSummary is s in the words of the card's STAGINGS block, without the
    env's name: its state, CI's or Jenkins' part of it, the head in the tip or
    how far behind, and when it was deployed or pushed, relative to now ("pushed
    · CI running · head aaa1111 · pushed 3m ago").

func StalemateWhat(urls []string) string
    StalemateWhat says that magnum stopped arguing in the threads at urls,
    naming the first: the card's NEEDS YOU (stalemateSentence) and the attention
    line `magnum status` and the dashboard give such a PR.

func StopWatch(err error) error
    StopWatch wraps err so that RunWatch ends and returns err (for "the pane
    closed" or "herdr is gone"). StopWatch(nil) is nil.

func TimingsText(t RoundTimings) string
    TimingsText is t on one line: "fetch/checkout 12s · claude-review 18m04s
    · … · total 34m10s", a running stage marked "(running)", a failed one
    "(failed)".


TYPES

type ActionLog struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    ActionLog is the outcomes of the screens' last actions, newest last,
    with the requests among them the daemon has not answered yet. The board
    and the dashboard share one (tab keeps it), so a request queued on one
    screen flashes on the other when the answer comes. Safe for concurrent use;
    the zero value is ready.

func NewActionLog() *ActionLog
    NewActionLog returns an empty log.

type ActionResult struct {
	// Text is everything the action printed: the footer shows its last line,
	// the action log all of it.
	Text string
	// Requests are the daemon requests it queued, as last read.
	Requests []Request
	// Ask is the question an action that only planned asks before its
	// next step, ending in "?": the daemon's plan of a merge of the parent
	// (MergeParentPlan), which the screen puts as y/N before it merges.
	// "" for none.
	Ask string
	// Staging is what a staging deploy's plan (StagingPlan) binds its
	// deploy to, which y sends (StagingDeploy); nil for none.
	Staging *StagingAsked
	// Parent is what a merge of the parent's plan (MergeParentPlan) binds
	// its merge to, which y sends (MergeParent); nil for none.
	Parent *MergeAsked
	// CIFix is what a CI fix's plan (FixCIPlan) binds its start to, which y
	// sends (FixCI); nil for none.
	CIFix *CIFixAsked

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    ActionResult is what a finished action reports.

type ActivityInfo struct {
	LastPoll, LastTick, LastReconcile time.Duration
	PollsFailing                      []WatchFailing
}
    ActivityInfo is how long ago the daemon last polled GitHub, ticked and
    reconciled; zero (or negative) means never. PollsFailing are the watches
    whose radar calls have failed for engine.PollFailingShown or longer (as of
    StatusData.GeneratedAt), which the poll's part of the line names.

type AgentsInfo struct {
	CodexWorking, CodexMax, ClaudeWorking int
	Other                                 []KindCount // other agent kinds the roles use, shown after claude
	Error                                 string
}
    AgentsInfo counts working agent panes; a non-empty Error ("herdr
    unreachable") replaces the counts.

type ApproveAs struct {
	Identity, Login, Refusal string
}
    ApproveAs is the operator's own account A approves a row that needs them as:
    the identity the approval names, its login (the question names it),
    and why the daemon would refuse the approval now, "" when it would not
    (engine.OperatorApprovalRefusal).

type AttentionRow struct {
	Subject, Kind, Message string
	Fix                    string // optional
}
    AttentionRow is something that needs the user.

type AutoApproval struct {
	ReviewID int64
	Head     string
	URL      string
	At       time.Time
}
    AutoApproval is an approval magnum posted as the operator: GitHub's review,
    the head it approved and when.

type Badge struct {
	Label, Text string
	// Color is one of red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan or gray ("" =
	// the terminal's; an emoji keeps its own colors).
	Color string
}
    Badge marks a PR that carries a GitHub label: Text (e.g. "🚩") shows before
    the title, Label names it on the card.

type CIFixAsked struct {
	Head    string
	Entries []string
	Count   int
	At      time.Time
}
    CIFixAsked is what a CI fix's y/N binds its start to: the PR's head,
    the failed required entries, the CI fixes the PR had, and when the daemon
    planned it.

type CIInfo struct {
	// State is "passed" | "failed" | "pending" | "skipped" (every check
	// skipped: none ran) | "none" (no checks).
	State                                   string
	Total, Passed, Failed, Pending, Skipped int
	// Failing names the failed checks, "workflow / job" when the workflow is known.
	Failing []string
	// Workflows summarises the checks per GitHub Actions workflow ("" = checks outside a workflow).
	Workflows []WorkflowCI
	// Required are the repository's required checks with their state: Name
	// as GitHub or [[repo]] required_checks names it ("Completion",
	// "workflow:CI"), State "passed" | "failed" | "pending" | "skipped" |
	// "missing" (never ran on this head).
	Required []CheckState
	// RequiredSource says who requires them: "github" (the repository's
	// rulesets) or "config" ([[repo]] required_checks overrides them).
	RequiredSource string
	Stale          bool // describes an older commit than the PR's head
	// Links are the failed checks' pages, in Failing's order and named as
	// it names them; a failed check that posted no page has none. Whoever
	// posts a check sets its page: cleanCI keeps only an http or https one.
	Links []CheckLink
	// Blocked is why GitHub blocks the merge, in words ("GitHub blocks
	// the merge: Completion failed"); "" when GitHub does not, has not said
	// or said it of an older commit than the head.
	Blocked string
}
    CIInfo is the head commit's CI as the board shows it.

type CardAgent struct {
	Name, Why, Now, State string
	For                   time.Duration
	Output                time.Time
}
    CardAgent is one agent of a task. State is "working", "done" or any other
    state the agents view names ("waits on you", "stopped"). Why says what it is
    for, Now what it does at the moment (a working agent), For how long it has
    worked and Output when its pane last printed.

type CardFile struct {
	Path           string
	Added, Removed int
	// InPlan is false for a file the plan did not name: checking it is on the
	// operator.
	InPlan bool
	// Flagged marks a file a FLAGS line names (a migration, a sensitive
	// file, an old guard): it is drawn first, with the files not in the plan.
	Flagged bool
}
    CardFile is one changed file of a ready card.

type CardOption struct {
	Label, Means string
	// Send is what the option answers: "" for its Label; "ask:<login>" asks
	// that person instead (the factory drafts the comment).
	Send string
	// Own marks the option that takes your own words ("Type your own
	// answer"): picking it asks for them.
	Own bool
}
    CardOption is one choice and what it means for the question's example.

type CardPR struct {
	State     string
	CI        *CIInfo
	Review    string
	Findings  *FindingsInfo
	Approvals *FactoryApprovals
	Reviewers string
	Threads   string
	FixLoop   string
}
    CardPR is what a PR is, on its card (your PR's, or a published task's),
    as magnum's registry tells it: each line is drawn only when it has its data,
    under its label in WAITING FOR's column. State is the PR line (its state,
    head, branches, last activity); CI is drawn as the board's CI cell;
    Review is magnum's last posted review in words, after its findings' cell
    (Findings); Reviewers are the people's reviews and whom the PR asks,
    after the APPR cell (Approvals); Threads are the replies magnum's judge has
    not read; FixLoop is magnum's fix loop on it.

type CardQuestion struct {
	Text    string
	Context string // one line of why it is asked
	Example string // one example, drawn behind "Example:"
	// Options are drawn in the order given, the recommended one first. The
	// last one is usually "Type your own answer", which has no Means.
	Options []CardOption
	// Recommended is the index of the option the factory picks; -1 means no
	// recommendation, and nothing is marked.
	Recommended int
	// Why is the reason of the recommendation. With no recommendation it is
	// why there is none ("the ticket and the code give no hint").
	Why        string
	Answer     string // the answer as the recap says it; empty: not answered
	AnsweredAt time.Time

	// TookRecommendation is true when the answer is the recommended option.
	TookRecommendation bool
	// Comment is the drafted Jira comment of an answer that asks someone: the
	// recap draws it, and counts the question as an ask, not an answer.
	Comment string
	// Asks is who the Comment asks ("rev-ann").
	Asks string

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    CardQuestion is one question with its options and, once answered, its
    answer.

type CardStage struct {
	Name, State, Proof string
	Took               time.Duration
	Finished           time.Time
}
    CardStage is one stage of a task. State is one of "done", "skipped",
    "waiting", "working", "failed" or "todo". Proof says what makes the stage
    done, in words.

type CheckLink struct{ Name, URL string }
    CheckLink is a check's page: Name as CIInfo.Failing names the check, URL its
    run's page.

type CheckState struct {
	Name, Label, State string
	Done, Total        int
}
    CheckState is one required check and its state: Name as configured ("ci /
    *", "workflow:CI"), Label the short name the board's cell shows ("" = Name),
    Total the checks it matched on the head and Done those that finished (Total
    0: none, or the head's are not known yet).

func (c CheckState) Count() string
    Count is "done/total" for a passed or pending required check that matched
    several checks ("3/3", "1/3"); "" otherwise (one check, none, or a failure
    the card names).

type CleanupAction struct {
	ID      string // stable id the caller maps back to its own action
	Kind    string // release_slot, remove_slot, drop_db, reset_external, ...
	Subject string // owner/name#N, slot:<name>, slug:<slug>, path:<dir>
	Why     string
	Bytes   int64 // disk freed (0 = none or unknown)
	DBBytes int64 // MySQL space freed
	DBNames []string
	// NeedsTypedConfirm, when non-empty, is the exact text (for example a
	// slug) the user must type before the plan is applied.
	NeedsTypedConfirm string
}
    CleanupAction is one thing the plan would do.

type CleanupOutcome struct {
	Apply       bool     // true only after the user confirmed (and typed every required text)
	SelectedIDs []string // in plan order; empty when cancelled
}
    CleanupOutcome is what the user decided.

func RunCleanupPlan(ctx context.Context, plan CleanupPlan) (CleanupOutcome, error)
    RunCleanupPlan shows the plan full-screen so the user can pick actions,
    confirm them and type any required texts. It returns Apply false when the
    user cancelled or ctx ended.

type CleanupPlan struct {
	Actions []CleanupAction
	Skipped []CleanupSkip
	Totals  CleanupTotals // whole-plan estimates, shown for reference
}
    CleanupPlan is what the cleanup screen reviews: the actions the planner
    proposes, the things it left alone, and whole-plan estimates.

type CleanupSkip struct{ Subject, Reason string }
    CleanupSkip is something the planner left alone, with the reason.

type CleanupTotals struct{ Disk, MySQL int64 }
    CleanupTotals are whole-plan estimates, in bytes.

type CodexPace struct {
	Used int // percent
	Cap  float64
	At   time.Time
}
    CodexPace is the Codex budget used now and when, at the pace it has
    been spent since its window began, it reaches Cap ([usage] codex_soft,
    or codex_hard once past it), before the window resets.

type ColumnWidths interface {
	LoadWidths(ctx context.Context, screen string) (map[string]int, error)
	SaveWidths(ctx context.Context, screen string, widths map[string]int) error
}
    ColumnWidths keeps the column widths dragged with the mouse across runs,
    per screen ("board", "dashboard") and column name. LoadWidths returns nil
    when nothing is kept; SaveWidths with an empty map forgets them. The screens
    call both from commands, so a slow store never blocks a key.

type DaemonFacts struct {
	// SkewOld is the build the daemon runs when it is older than the CLI's
	// or the one on disk ("v1.4.0", "dev (8ad5bb2)"), SkewSince when that
	// daemon started and SkewNew what is built, as a phrase ("v1.5.0 built",
	// "new build 18:48"); SkewOld is "" when the daemon runs the newest
	// build.
	SkewOld, SkewNew string
	SkewSince        time.Time
	// Paused: `magnum pause` holds automation since PausedSince (zero when
	// unknown), holding Held review requests people made.
	Paused      bool
	PausedSince time.Time
	Held        int
	// Draining: `magnum daemon-restart --drain` holds new rounds; DrainerPID
	// is the draining command (0 when unknown).
	Draining   bool
	DrainerPID int
	// PollsFailing are the watches whose radar calls have failed for
	// engine.PollFailingShown or longer, the oldest failure first: magnum
	// sees no new PRs or pushes of them.
	PollsFailing []WatchFailing
	// NeedsMe counts the open PRs magnum approved that GitHub still blocks
	// on the operator's approval (PRBoardRow.NeedsMe).
	NeedsMe int
	// AutoApproved counts the open PRs magnum approved as the operator
	// whose approval stands (PRBoardRow.AutoApproved).
	AutoApproved int
	// Codex is the Codex budget's pace when it reaches a cap before the
	// window resets; nil otherwise.
	Codex *CodexPace
	// NotesProposals counts the curation proposals for repository notes
	// that wait for the operator (`magnum notes <repo> --review`).
	NotesProposals int
	// LearnProposals counts the skill proposals the gate held for the
	// operator (`magnum learn --review`).
	LearnProposals int
}
    DaemonFacts are what the titles say of the daemon; the zero value says
    nothing.

type DaemonInfo struct {
	Running bool
	PID     int
	Uptime  string // preformatted ("3h12m"); empty when unknown
	Launchd string // launchd job state ("running", "not loaded")
	// Skew says the daemon runs an older build than the CLI's or the one on
	// disk ("daemon runs v1 since …; v2 is built: `magnum daemon-restart`");
	// "" when it does not.
	Skew string
}
    DaemonInfo is the daemon process and its launchd job.

type DashboardActions interface {
	Open(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	Review(ctx context.Context, ref string, opts ReviewOpts) (ActionResult, error)
	Pin(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	Unpin(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	Release(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	Mute(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	Unmute(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	// Snooze holds the PR's automatic reviews for d and Unsnooze lifts
	// that (magnum snooze [--off]); the board's z.
	Snooze(ctx context.Context, ref string, d time.Duration) (ActionResult, error)
	Unsnooze(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	Abort(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)  // kill the PR's running review
	Ignore(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error) // abort, mute and free the slot
	// Approve and RequestChanges post the reviewer's own verdict on the head
	// magnum reviewed (magnum approve / request-changes); an approval goes
	// as identity as ("" = the PR's posting identity; magnum approve --as).
	Approve(ctx context.Context, ref, as string) (ActionResult, error)
	RequestChanges(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	// Unapprove withdraws the approval magnum posted as the operator and
	// stops it approving the PR as them (magnum unapprove).
	Unapprove(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	// Fix starts a fix loop on the operator's own PR: a fixer agent fixes
	// the findings of magnum's review and pushes as them (magnum fix); the
	// request is followed on the screen, not waited for. FixOff takes the PR
	// out of autofix (off) or puts it back (magnum fix --off / --on); both
	// start no loop.
	Fix(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	FixOff(ctx context.Context, ref string, off bool) (ActionResult, error)
	// MergeParentPlan asks the daemon what a merge of the PR's parent, its
	// base branch, into the operator's own PR as the fixer App's bot would
	// do (magnum merge-parent --dry-run) and returns the plan as the
	// result's Ask, the y/N the screen puts before the merge, and what it
	// asks about as Parent. MergeParent sends the merge bound to that, once
	// the screen's y/N said yes (P): the daemon refuses it when what the
	// question named moved since.
	MergeParentPlan(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	MergeParent(ctx context.Context, ref string, asked MergeAsked) (ActionResult, error)
	// FixCIPlan asks the daemon what a CI fix of the operator's own PR
	// whose required check failed would do (magnum fix --ci --dry-run) and
	// returns the plan as the result's Ask, the y/N the screen puts before
	// it, and what it asks about as CIFix. FixCI starts the CI fix bound to
	// that, once the screen's y/N said yes (c): the daemon refuses it when
	// the head, the failed checks or the count of CI fixes moved since.
	FixCIPlan(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	FixCI(ctx context.Context, ref string, asked CIFixAsked) (ActionResult, error)
	// StagingPlan asks the daemon's plan of a staging deploy of the
	// operator's own PR to envs (magnum staging --deploy --dry-run) and
	// returns its y/N as the result's Ask and its binding as Staging (the
	// envs that take the merge, the head, what the question names); an
	// answer with nothing to deploy is an error. StagingDeploy sends the
	// deploy so bound, once the screen's y/N said yes (E).
	StagingPlan(ctx context.Context, ref string, envs []string) (ActionResult, error)
	StagingDeploy(ctx context.Context, ref string, asked StagingAsked) (ActionResult, error)
	// FixDone says that the operator did what a fix loop left them: the PR
	// goes back from needs attention to reviewed with no review (magnum fix
	// --done); the board's d, which asked first. seen is the digest of the
	// attention the row showed (PRBoardRow.AttentionSum): one that changed
	// since is refused, not lifted.
	FixDone(ctx context.Context, ref, seen string) (ActionResult, error)
	// OpenWhiteboard opens the PR's whiteboard, the Whiteboard session its
	// record names, in Whiteboard Desktop (magnum whiteboard --open); the
	// board's w, which refuses a row without one before asking.
	OpenWhiteboard(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	// Star stars the PR (on) or unstars it (magnum star [--off]): the
	// board's *, which asks nothing. The registry keeps the star and only
	// the board reads it: no daemon request.
	Star(ctx context.Context, ref string, on bool) (ActionResult, error)
	Attention(ctx context.Context) (ActionResult, error)
	OpenBrowser(ctx context.Context, url string) error
	// Requests re-reads the requests ids name; one the registry no longer
	// has is left out.
	Requests(ctx context.Context, ids []int64) ([]Request, error)
}
    DashboardActions run what the dashboard's and the board's keys ask for.
    ref is a row's PR reference (or a slot name, for pin/unpin/release of
    an empty slot). The result's text is shown in the footer (only its last
    non-empty line when it has several) and kept whole in the action log;
    an error is shown instead, until a key is pressed. A request the result
    names as pending marks its row and is re-read (Requests) on every refresh
    until the daemon answers. One action runs at a time; the data refreshes
    right after it returns.

type DashboardOptions struct {
	Refresh    time.Duration    // between Gather calls; default 2s, at least 200ms
	ShowManual bool             // start with the manual worktrees section shown
	Title      string           // default "magnum status"
	Now        func() time.Time // clock for "updated Xs ago"; default time.Now
	Judge      string           // the judge role's name in the help ("open the PR's <Judge> pane"); default "judge"
	Icons      IconMode         // the symbols: unicode (default), nerd (Nerd Font icons and emoji) or ascii
	// Tick schedules the screen's timers (refresh, flash, the wait before
	// closing); default tea.Tick.
	Tick func(time.Duration, func(time.Time) tea.Msg) tea.Cmd
	// NoMouse starts with mouse support off ([terminal] mouse = false);
	// m turns it on and off either way.
	NoMouse bool
	// MouseToggled, when set, hears every m, so the next screen can start
	// the same way.
	MouseToggled func(on bool)
	// Widths keeps the column widths dragged with the mouse across runs;
	// nil keeps them for this run only.
	Widths ColumnWidths
	// Log keeps the actions' outcomes (! shows them) and the requests still
	// pending; the board shares it, so tab keeps both. nil = a log of this
	// screen's own.
	Log *ActionLog
	// Settings, when set, lets `,` open the settings screen over the
	// dashboard; esc there comes back to the dashboard as it was left.
	Settings *SettingsScreen
}
    DashboardOptions tune the dashboard.

type DashboardSource interface {
	Gather(ctx context.Context) (StatusData, error)
}
    DashboardSource supplies the dashboard's data; Gather is called once per
    refresh, never concurrently with itself.

type Digest struct {
	Since time.Time
	Done  []string
	Chip  string
}
    Digest is what happened while the operator was away, shown until the next
    key. Since is when the operator was last seen. Done are the tasks that
    finished since then, one line each ("PR-12302 Remove old sync job · merged
    21:15"), drawn under "DONE SINCE <day time>" in place of the DONE TODAY
    group; Chip is the chip line's segment ("away 14h: 2 done, 2 new for you"),
    in place of the done count.

type DiskInfo struct {
	FreeGB float64
	MinGB  int
}
    DiskInfo is the free space where slots live; FreeGB <= 0 means unknown.

type FactoryActions interface {
	Start(ctx context.Context, text, kind, repo string, wordsOnly bool) (ActionResult, error)
	Preview(ctx context.Context, text, repo string) (NewTaskForm, error)
	Answer(ctx context.Context, taskID int64, rev int, answers map[int]string, needless map[int]string) (ActionResult, error)
	Decide(ctx context.Context, taskID int64, choice, reason, note string, bound ReadyBinding) (ActionResult, error)
	Stop(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) (ActionResult, error)
	Retry(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) (ActionResult, error)
	Rate(ctx context.Context, taskID int64, value int, reason string, diffOpened bool) (ActionResult, error)
	Open(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) (ActionResult, error)
	OpenBrowser(ctx context.Context, url string) error
	Seen(ctx context.Context, at time.Time) error
	Focus(ctx context.Context, focused bool, at time.Time) error
	Diff(taskID int64) *exec.Cmd
	Fix(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	FixOff(ctx context.Context, ref string, off bool) (ActionResult, error)
	// MergeParentPlan and MergeParent are DashboardActions': the factory's
	// P on a PR row, the plan first, then the merge bound to it.
	MergeParentPlan(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	MergeParent(ctx context.Context, ref string, asked MergeAsked) (ActionResult, error)
	// FixCIPlan and FixCI are DashboardActions' too: the factory's c on a PR
	// row or card, a CI fix of the PR's failed required check (magnum fix
	// --ci), the daemon's plan first (a dry run, whose Ask the screen puts
	// as its y/N and whose CIFix binds the start), then the CI fix so bound.
	FixCIPlan(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	FixCI(ctx context.Context, ref string, asked CIFixAsked) (ActionResult, error)
	Abort(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	OpenPR(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	Review(ctx context.Context, ref string, o ReviewOpts) (ActionResult, error)
	Snooze(ctx context.Context, ref string, d time.Duration) (ActionResult, error)
	Unsnooze(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	Mute(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	Unmute(ctx context.Context, ref string) (ActionResult, error)
	StagingPlan(ctx context.Context, ref string, envs []string) (ActionResult, error)
	StagingDeploy(ctx context.Context, ref string, asked StagingAsked) (ActionResult, error)
	// AcceptQA lets a task go on with what QA left you accepted by you, at
	// its head: the defects the writer declined, at its fix loop's stop or
	// whose pages a QA run did not walk again, the writer's fixes a QA run
	// did not walk again, and the states a walk that reached its pages could
	// not reach (the task card's A, as `magnum factory retry --accept-qa`).
	AcceptQA(ctx context.Context, taskID int64) (ActionResult, error)
}
    FactoryActions are the screen's requests to the factory. Each runs from a
    command on the screen's context; the ones that change something return what
    they did (its last line goes to the footer, all of it to the log).

      - Start starts a task from the new task's text, of kind ("" = the factory
        picks it), in repository repo ("" = the one the text tells); Preview is
        what the factory makes of a text in repo, making nothing.
      - Answer sends a batch for the questions of revision rev, by question
        index from 0: an option's label, the operator's words, or "ask:<login>";
        needless flags questions with the key of the reason.
      - Decide decides on the ready card: FactoryPush, FactorySendBack (with the
        reason's key and the note; the reason FactoryReasonKnown takes none) or
        FactoryDrop.
      - Stop drops a task (frees its copy, keeps its branch); Retry lets a task
        that waits on the operator go on at its stage.
      - Rate rates a published or a done task + (value 1) or − (-1), with the
        key of a reason ("" for none); diffOpened says the screen showed the
        operator the task's diff first (the factory adds the diff its newest
        push on the ready card recorded as opened). It asks no y/N: a rating is
        undoable, rating again stores a new one.
      - Open steps into the task's pane (asks nothing).
      - OpenBrowser opens url in the browser: b a task's PR, t its Jira issue
        (asks nothing, as the board's b and t).
      - Seen says the operator saw home at at: the first key after a digest,
        and any key or click at most once a minute (the digest counts the
        absence from the last input); Focus that the screen's terminal gained or
        lost focus at at, the event's time (the factory holds its toasts then).
      - Diff is the pager on the task's diff, run with tea.ExecProcess; nil:
        there is no diff to show. It is called on the screen's own turn,
        so it only builds the command: it reads and waits for nothing.
      - Fix, FixOff and Abort act on your own PR ref ("owner/name#4512", a row's
        FactoryPR) through magnum's request paths, as the board's f, F and K do:
        Fix has magnum's fixer take what is open, FixOff switches the PR out of
        autofix (off) or back in, and Abort stops what magnum runs on it (its
        fix loop, the re-review the loop forced). They never go through the
        factory daemon.
      - OpenPR steps into magnum's pane of PR ref, as the board's o does
        (magnum open): the judge's, or the fixer's while its loop works,
        restoring a parked one in a slot (the screen asked y/N first then,
        FactoryPR.Restores).
      - Review, Snooze, Unsnooze, Mute and Unmute act on PR ref as the board's
        r and R (a review, fresh with o.Fresh), z (a snooze of d, or its lift)
        and M and U do, through the same calls (DashboardActions): magnum's own
        request paths, never the factory daemon. The screen asked y/N first,
        in the board's words.
      - StagingPlan and StagingDeploy are DashboardActions': E's plan of a
        staging deploy of PR ref to envs (a dry run, whose Ask the screen puts
        as its y/N and whose Staging binds the deploy), then the deploy so
        bound, through magnum's daemon, never the factory's.

type FactoryAlert struct {
	At   time.Time
	Text string
}
    FactoryAlert is one alert the factory raised: when, and what it said.

type FactoryApprovals struct {
	Approved, Changes, Stale int
	Decision                 string
}
    FactoryApprovals is what the people's reviews of a PR say, as GitHub's merge
    gate counts them: Approved and Changes count the reviewers whose latest
    opinion is an approval or a changes request, Stale the approvals of an
    older commit than the head; Decision is GitHub's review decision (APPROVED,
    CHANGES_REQUESTED, REVIEW_REQUIRED; "" when the base branch requires no
    review).

type FactoryCards struct {
	Task     TaskCard
	Question *QuestionCard
	Ready    *ReadyCard
	// Bind is the ready card's head and hashes as the factory drew it; the
	// screen fills in its own times and sends it with the decision.
	Bind ReadyBinding
}
    FactoryCards are a task's cards: its task card always, and the decision card
    it waits on, if any: its questions or its ready card.

type FactoryData struct {
	// Repos are the factory's repositories ("owner/name"), in its config's
	// order: the title line names them, or counts them when they do not fit.
	Repos    []string
	Rows     []FactoryRow
	Blocking []string // the machine facts that stop work ("memory full: new tasks wait")
	RuleChip string   // "1 rule to approve (L)"
	Digest   *Digest  // what finished while the operator was away; nil: none
	Cards    map[int64]FactoryCards

	// BlockingLong are Blocking with their detail, for a wide screen.
	BlockingLong []string
	// Decisions counts the single answers owed across all tasks ("5
	// decisions"), apart from the tasks.
	Decisions int
	// Next is what the operator does next when nothing waits on them.
	Next string
	// Flash is the last news for the status rule ("14:02 you said MFA done →
	// bart deploy resumed"), drawn green when the screen has none of its own.
	Flash string
	// Alerts are the alert events, newest first: ! lists every one with its
	// time (spec 9.F: nothing vanishes).
	Alerts []FactoryAlert
	// OwnUnread says this read could not list your own open PRs: their
	// rows are missing (Blocking says why), so an owner scope whose only
	// rows they were is kept, as the board keeps its scope on a load that
	// failed.
	OwnUnread bool
}
    FactoryData is one read of the factory: home's rows and chips and every
    task's cards. Rows are drawn grouped by Group (factory_rows.go); Cards are
    by task id (FactoryRow.ID).

type FactoryGroup int
    FactoryGroup is the band of the home list a task sits in, by who it waits
    on.

const (
	// GroupNeedsYou holds the tasks that are stopped until the operator decides or acts.
	GroupNeedsYou FactoryGroup = iota
	// GroupWaits holds the tasks that wait on someone or something else.
	GroupWaits
	// GroupYours holds the open PRs from magnum's registry that magnum's
	// look leaves alone, or that magnum does not review (LEFT ALONE: a
	// baseline, a mute, a draft), your own and the published tasks' alike:
	// they ask nothing. The other PRs sit in GroupNeedsYou or GroupWaits by
	// what they wait on, fix off included (magnum still reviews them).
	GroupYours
	// GroupDone holds the tasks that finished today.
	GroupDone
)
type FactoryJiraPlan struct {
	Milestone, Mode, Outcome string
	From, To, Transition     string
	Transitions              []string
	Cause                    string
	Begun, At                time.Time
	Moved, MovedTo, MovedBy  string
	MovedAt                  time.Time
}
    FactoryJiraPlan is the factory's plan of a move of a task's Jira issue at a
    milestone ("start", "published"), in its mode ("shadow": planned and never
    made): its outcome ("" while it waits for its read, else planned, already,
    assigned_other, no_transition, needs_fields, target_done or unread),
    the status it read (From) and the target (To), the transition it would take,
    the transitions Jira offers (none to the target), the failure of an unread
    plan (a class, never ticket text), when it began and when its read was; then
    what the factory saw after a planned move: Moved ("target", "elsewhere",
    "none"; "" before anything was seen), the status it moved to, when,
    and who moved it (MovedBy: "you", "other", "" unknown). The names are Jira's
    statuses and transitions, never a person's.

type FactoryJiraStatus struct {
	Name, Category          string
	Since                   time.Time
	Assigned, AssignedToYou bool
	// YouUnknown says the issue is assigned but not known to be you: the
	// read of your account failed after the issue answered, so
	// AssignedToYou is false without saying someone else has it.
	YouUnknown      bool
	ReadAt, TriedAt time.Time
	LastError       string
	// DaemonDown says no factory daemon runs to read the issue again: the
	// facts are as old as ReadAt.
	DaemonDown bool
}
    FactoryJiraStatus is where a task's Jira issue stands, as the factory
    daemon's last read of it that worked says it (its tracking row): the
    status's name ("In Review": one line of at most 64 bytes, without control
    or format characters; "" while no read worked, when LastError says why),
    Jira's category of it ("new", "indeterminate", "done"; "" for another word),
    since when the issue holds it (zero: not known), whether it has an assignee
    and whether that is you, when the read was (zero: none worked), when the
    last try was, and its failure ("" when it worked): a class of failure in
    fixed words, never ticket text. The row and its task card share one value:
    a painter reads it, never changes it. A failed try after the read (TriedAt
    after ReadAt), or DaemonDown, leaves facts that may no longer hold:
    the painters say so.

type FactoryMark int
    FactoryMark is the one-cell mark before a row: what the task is doing now.

const (
	// MarkNeedsYou is drawn in yellow: the task is on the operator.
	MarkNeedsYou FactoryMark = iota
	// MarkWorking is the only moving mark: an agent works on the task.
	MarkWorking
	// MarkWaits marks a task that waits on someone or something else.
	MarkWaits
	// MarkDone marks a task that finished.
	MarkDone
)
type FactoryOptions struct {
	Icons   IconMode // the symbols: unicode (default), nerd or ascii
	NoMouse bool     // start with mouse support off ([terminal] mouse = false); m turns it on and off
	Now     func() time.Time
	// Tick schedules the screen's timers (the refresh, the spinner's frames,
	// the end of a footer note, the wait before a preview); default tea.Tick.
	Tick func(time.Duration, func(time.Time) tea.Msg) tea.Cmd
	// Settings, when set, lets `,` open the settings screen over the factory.
	Settings *SettingsScreen
	// Repo shows only this repository's rows ("name" or "owner/name", as
	// the board's --repo; case aside) and the rows that name none; ""
	// shows every repository.
	Repo string
	// DefaultRepo is daemon.default_repo ("owner/name"): its owner comes
	// first when O cycles the owners, as on the PR board.
	DefaultRepo string
	// DefaultOwner is the owner scope the screen opens in, the board's (O):
	// "" shows every owner, as does an owner with no rows. OwnerChanged,
	// when set, hears every change of it (O, or its owner's last row
	// leaving), so the next screen can open in it.
	DefaultOwner string
	OwnerChanged func(owner string)
}
    FactoryOptions tune the factory screen.

type FactoryPR struct {
	// Ref names it as magnum's commands do ("owner/name#4512").
	Ref string
	// Fixing says magnum's fix loop runs on it.
	Fixing bool
	// FixOff says you switched it out of autofix (`magnum fix --off`).
	FixOff bool
	// Off is why magnum's look leaves it alone (its verdict is off: a
	// baseline, fix off, a watch that leaves your PRs out), in its words;
	// "" when the look covers it. The row is drawn dim: it asks nothing.
	Off string
	// Restores says magnum's open of the PR (o) restores it in a slot,
	// which claims the slot and holds the PR for Hold ([daemon] open_hold):
	// o asks y/N first, as the board's does; false when it focuses a live
	// pane, which asks nothing.
	Restores bool
	Hold     time.Duration
	// Facts are what r, R, z, M and U go by, as magnum's registry tells
	// them; nil when the screen read none: the keys then refuse only what
	// the rest of the row tells, and magnum's daemon decides the rest.
	Facts *FactoryPRFacts
	// StagingDeploys are the PR's staging deploys magnum's daemon runs, or
	// ran in the last day, live ones first, each as its newest event left
	// it (engine.StagingDeployRecord, the records the board reads): the
	// task card draws them under STAGINGS, home's rows none. nil when the
	// screen read none.
	StagingDeploys []StagingDeploy
	// StagingEnvs are the staging envs the config names for the PR's
	// repository ([[factory.repo.staging]], config.Stagings), in its order:
	// on a row without staging cells (none read yet, or your own PR's, whose
	// the factory reads none of) E's chooser lists them, each not read yet,
	// and the review daemon plans them. nil: the repository has none.
	StagingEnvs []string
}
    FactoryPR is a row's open PR on the factory screen (your own PR's, or a
    task's), as magnum's registry tells it: what the row's keys go by.

type FactoryPRFacts struct {
	// State is magnum's state of the PR ("reviewed", "reviewing"), GHState
	// GitHub's (OPEN, CLOSED, MERGED).
	State, GHState string
	// Head is the PR's head commit, Reviewed the head magnum reviewed last
	// ("" when never).
	Head, Reviewed string
	// Muted says the PR is muted (`magnum mute`, M); SnoozedUntil is when its
	// snooze ends (zero: not snoozed; `magnum snooze`, z).
	Muted        bool
	SnoozedUntil time.Time
	// CodexFlag is the PR's Codex flag in one cell ("" when not flagged): the
	// review keys refuse it, as `magnum review` does.
	CodexFlag string
	// MergedUnreviewed says GitHub merged it before magnum reviewed its last
	// push; FlagDismissed that a mute dismissed that flag (M and U act on it).
	MergedUnreviewed, FlagDismissed bool
	// Replies counts the replies on magnum's review its judge has not
	// re-decided yet (store.PR.PendingReplies): r then has the judge alone
	// re-decide them, as the board's r does.
	Replies int
	// Autofix says the PR's watch starts fix loops by itself (autofix "own"
	// or "open"): the questions say what a key does to them.
	Autofix bool
}
    FactoryPRFacts are what the board's row actions (review, fresh review,
    snooze, mute, unmute) know of a PR on the factory screen, read from magnum's
    registry, read only, and from its watch: the facts the board's refusals and
    y/N questions go by, so a key refuses where the board's does.

type FactoryRow struct {
	ID int64
	// Key is what the task is called in the list: its Jira key, or its GitHub
	// number ("#4512") for a PR the operator wrote by hand. GitHub is the
	// PR's number, shown beside the Jira key on a wide screen.
	Key, GitHub, Title string
	// Repo is the repository the row is of ("owner/name"): the task's, or
	// your PR's. The painter draws it in a column of its own, unless the
	// title names one repository and every row is of it.
	Repo     string
	Group    FactoryGroup
	Mark     FactoryMark
	WaitsOn  []WaitsOn
	Move     string // the step the factory recommends; NeedsYou rows only
	Stagings []StagingCell
	Since    time.Time // when the task began to wait on this; zero = not shown
	Help     string    // the line under the rule while the row is selected

	// Jira is the Jira key of a task keyed by its GitHub number, for the wide
	// screen's JIRA cell. Empty: the Key, unless the Key is the GitHub number.
	Jira string
	// JiraStatus is where the task's Jira issue stands, as the factory
	// daemon last read it; nil before the first try of its key, and on a
	// row of your own PR.
	JiraStatus *FactoryJiraStatus
	// MoveShort is Move on a narrow screen.
	MoveShort string
	// DeployFirst says the row's PR waits on your merge, changes a
	// migration and is on no staging (staging.DeployBeforeMerge): its move
	// is E, a staging deploy before the merge, which home's hints and its
	// card's offer first.
	DeployFirst bool
	// HelpShort and HelpLong are Help on a narrow and on a wide screen.
	HelpShort, HelpLong string
	// Frees is what frees a queued task ("frees when PR-12360 is pushed"):
	// the text of its last blocker on a 140-column screen ("copy: frees when
	// PR-12360 is pushed"), after the blocker's own text on a wide one; a
	// narrow one keeps the blocker's Short, or Frees when it has none.
	Frees string

	// CI, Findings and Approvals are the row's PR as magnum's registry tells
	// it, for the CI, FINDINGS and APPR columns: the head's CI and magnum's
	// last posted review as the board's CI and FINDINGS columns say them,
	// and the people's reviews GitHub counts. nil on a row without a PR, or
	// before magnum read the PR.
	CI        *CIInfo
	Findings  *FindingsInfo
	Approvals *FactoryApprovals

	// PR is the row's open PR in magnum's registry, which f, F, K, r, R, z,
	// M and U act on: on a row of your own PR, not a task (in any group but DONE
	// TODAY), whose ID is the negative of magnum's id of the PR, which no
	// task's has (yourPR); and on a task's row whose PR magnum read. nil on
	// a task's row without one.
	PR *FactoryPR
}
    FactoryRow is one task on the home list, one line.

    The fields after Help are optional extra forms of the text before them:
    the painter draws the form that fits the screen and falls back to the plain
    one when a form is empty.

type FactorySource interface {
	Frame(ctx context.Context) (FactoryData, error)
}
    FactorySource reads what the factory screen shows. The screen calls Frame
    from a command, on its refresh and after each action, with a context that
    ends when the screen closes.

type FindingsInfo struct {
	Counts          [4]int // P0..P3 findings posted
	Simplifications int    // optional simplification suggestions posted
	Fixed, Open     int    // earlier findings fixed / still open (a re-review)
	// OpenProblems is how many of Open are problems to fix before merging
	// (store.ReviewSummary.OpenProblems: P0 to P2, or all of Open when their
	// priorities are unknown): f fixes them too.
	OpenProblems int
	// OpenCounts is Open by priority, P0..P3
	// (store.ReviewSummary.OpenCounts); nil when the result gives only
	// their number.
	OpenCounts *[4]int
	Answered   int // earlier findings answered with a reason
	// Verdict is the review's decision whatever its repository lets it
	// post: blocking (request changes), non_blocking (comment) or clean
	// (approve).
	Verdict string
	Posted  string // what it was posted as: APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED or COMMENTED (an event's name, APPROVE, is read alike)
	SHA     string // the reviewed head
	// Held: this review held its approval ([pipeline]
	// approve_after_full_pass): its clean verdict posted as a comment and a
	// full pass of the whole PR decides the approval. Only the review the
	// hold record names (engine.HeldReviewID) is held, never a clean comment
	// by itself (a comment-only repository posts every one so); FINDINGS
	// reads "✔ held" in place of "✔ clean".
	Held bool
}
    FindingsInfo is what magnum's latest posted review of a PR concluded.

type FormLink struct{ Kind, URL, Offer string }
    FormLink is a link in the new task text. Kind is "jira" (a Jira link is its
    key), "pr" (a GitHub PR, which offers adoption) or "run" (a GitHub Actions
    run, which offers a CI task); Offer says what the factory makes of it ("its
    key PR-12345", "adoption comes in milestone 2").

type GitHubInfo struct {
	Remaining, Limit int
	ResetIn          time.Duration
}
    GitHubInfo is the GraphQL rate budget; Limit 0 means unknown (no poll yet).

type IconMode string
    IconMode is the set of symbols the PR board and the status dashboard draw
    ([terminal] icons). A screen cannot tell which font the terminal uses,
    so the configuration decides; nothing is detected.

const (
	// IconsUnicode draws Unicode symbols (✔ ✗ 💬 📌) that any font has: the
	// default, also for an empty or unknown mode.
	IconsUnicode IconMode = "unicode"
	// IconsNerd draws Nerd Font icons and emoji: a colored marker before
	// every state, verdict and finding priority, an icon in every state
	// pill and before the section headings. Needs a Nerd Font.
	IconsNerd IconMode = "nerd"
	// IconsASCII draws plain ASCII ("+", "x", "pin").
	IconsASCII IconMode = "ascii"
)
type JiraPreview struct {
	Key, Type, Status, Priority, Reporter, Summary, Excerpt string
	Read                                                    time.Time
	// More is true when the description has more than the Excerpt.
	More bool
	// Found is the note drawn after the key on its row when the text names
	// it elsewhere than at its start ("found in your text"); empty for a key
	// at the start.
	Found string
}
    JiraPreview is a Jira issue as the daemon read it.

type KindCount struct {
	Kind    string
	Working int
}
    KindCount is the number of working panes of one agent kind.

type ManualRow struct {
	Folder, Branch, PRRef, GitHub, DBs, Agents, Disk string
}
    ManualRow is a manual worktree (read-only, not selectable).

type MergeAsked struct {
	Head, Base, Tip string
	Conflicts       int
	Merge           string
	At              time.Time
}
    MergeAsked is what a merge of the parent's y/N binds its merge to:
    the PR's head, the parent (its base branch) and the tip of it the plan read,
    how many files the merge conflicts in (0: none), the merge magnum holds
    for your y whose push the plan names (Merge; "" for a merge to make,
    held_merge.go) and when the daemon planned it.

type NewTaskForm struct {
	Text string
	// Jira is the issue the text starts with, read by the daemon; nil: the
	// text is a prompt.
	Jira                  *JiraPreview
	Kind, KindWhy, Branch string
	Starts                string // "now, in talkable.factory2 (free)" or why it is queued
	Agents, Rules         []string
	// AgentsByKind are the agents each kind's start launches, by the kind's
	// name: the AGENTS row and the y/N of a kind picked with tab draw that
	// kind's (Agents are the guessed kind's). None for a kind: Agents stay.
	AgentsByKind map[string][]string
	Err          string // a problem with the text, drawn in the JIRA row
	Repo         string // the repository, named in "3 talkable rules go into its prompts"
	Title        string // the title of a task started from words
	Ask          string // the y/N question being asked; empty: the key hints
	// ShowRules lists the rules under their count; false: the count alone.
	ShowRules bool

	// Links are the links the text holds, in its order.
	Links []FormLink
	// Overlap is the advisory line of what else touches the work: commits
	// and PRs that name the key, open PRs that change the same files.
	Overlap string
	// Reading is true while the daemon reads Jira: the JIRA row says so,
	// behind the spinner frame Spinner.
	Reading bool
	Spinner int
	// Guidance is what goes to every agent with the ticket, as the daemon
	// parsed the text: the words after a key or a Jira link at its start, or
	// the whole text for a key found in it. The form draws it as it is and
	// never parses the text; empty: no GUIDANCE row.
	Guidance string
	// Keys are the keys Jira knows that the text names, when it names
	// several: the task is the prompt task it is, whose questions ask which
	// issue it is, and no ticket is drawn as its own.
	Keys []string
	// WordsOnly is true when the key at the start of the text is one Jira
	// does not know (Err says so): enter then asks to start from your words
	// only, the key kept as words and never read as the task's ticket.
	WordsOnly bool
	// RepoWhy says how the factory chose Repo: "from the EX tracker" (a key
	// of the tracker of that repository alone), "from the link" (a GitHub
	// link of it) or "your pick".
	RepoWhy string
	// Repos are the factory's repositories, in the config's order: with two
	// or more the form draws a REPO row, whose key cycles through them, and
	// with none chosen (Repo empty) it draws that row only, and enter starts
	// nothing.
	Repos []string
	// NotJira is the key the text starts with when its tracker is not Jira:
	// the task's key, never read from Jira; the task starts from your words.
	NotJira string
	// Hints are the footer's key hints; none: the form's own (newTaskHints).
	Hints []hint `json:"-"`

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    NewTaskForm is the new task screen: the operator's text and what the factory
    understood of it. A row is drawn only when its field is filled.

type PRBoardOptions struct {
	Refresh time.Duration    // between Rows calls; default 5s, at least 200ms
	Title   string           // default "magnum · pull requests"
	Now     func() time.Time // clock for ages and the refresh time; default time.Now
	// Tick schedules the board's timers (refresh, spinner and shimmer
	// frames, flash, the wait before closing); default tea.Tick.
	Tick func(time.Duration, func(time.Time) tea.Msg) tea.Cmd
	// SelfLogins are the logins that count as "me": the user and magnum's
	// own reviewer (e.g. "zhuravel", "talkable[bot]"). Case, a leading "@"
	// and a "[bot]" suffix do not matter.
	SelfLogins  []string
	DefaultSort PRSort // default SortUpdated
	DefaultView PRView // the view the board opens in; default ViewAll
	// DefaultOwner is the owner scope the board opens in; "" (the default)
	// shows every owner, as does an owner without PRs.
	DefaultOwner string
	// OwnerChanged, when set, hears every change of the owner scope (O, or
	// its owner's last PR leaving), so the next board can open in it.
	OwnerChanged func(owner string)
	// ViewChanged, when set, hears every v, so the next board can open in
	// the same view.
	ViewChanged func(PRView)
	Repo        string // show only this repository ("name" or "owner/name"); empty shows all
	// DefaultRepo is daemon.default_repo ("owner/name"): its owner comes
	// first when O cycles the owners.
	DefaultRepo string
	Icons       IconMode // the symbols: unicode (default), nerd (Nerd Font icons and emoji) or ascii
	Judge       string   // the judge role's name in the help ("open the <Judge> pane"); default "judge"
	// NoMouse starts with mouse support off ([terminal] mouse = false);
	// m turns it on and off either way.
	NoMouse bool
	// NoShimmer keeps the state cells of the PRs that need the operator
	// still ([board] shimmer = false); by default their colors slide.
	NoShimmer bool
	// HideSkipped starts the board with the ignored and skipped PRs hidden
	// (h toggles it); HideToggled, when set, hears every h so the choice
	// can be kept.
	HideSkipped bool
	HideToggled func(hide bool)
	// MouseToggled, when set, hears every m, so the next screen can start
	// the same way.
	MouseToggled func(on bool)
	// Widths keeps the column widths dragged with the mouse across runs;
	// nil keeps them for this run only.
	Widths ColumnWidths
	// RecentClosed is [board] recent_closed, the window the heading of the
	// recently closed section names ("merged or closed in the last 24h");
	// the source marks the rows in it (PRBoardRow.Recent).
	RecentClosed time.Duration
	// Log keeps the actions' outcomes (! shows them) and the requests still
	// pending; the dashboard shares it, so tab keeps both. nil = a log of
	// this screen's own.
	Log *ActionLog
	// Facts, when set, reads what the title says of the daemon (an older
	// build, a pause, a drain, the Codex budget's pace) with every load.
	Facts func(ctx context.Context) DaemonFacts
	// Limit caps the rows the table lists after the view, the filter and the
	// sort (`magnum tui --limit`), as the printed rows are capped: the sort
	// decides which rows show, and a starred PR shows first. 0 lists all.
	Limit int
	// OwnElsewhere, when set, counts your own open PRs the source left out
	// because the factory screen lists them ([board] own_prs = "factory"),
	// as of its last load: the status rule says so while it has nothing
	// else to say.
	OwnElsewhere func() int
	// Settings, when set, lets `,` open the settings screen over the board;
	// esc there comes back to the board as it was left.
	Settings *SettingsScreen
}
    PRBoardOptions tune the PR board.

type PRBoardRow struct {
	Ref, Owner, Repo   string
	Number             int
	Title, Author, URL string
	// Issue is the first issue key in the title a [board] trackers template
	// knows ("PS-38553"), IssueURL its page; "" when the title names none.
	Issue, IssueURL   string
	Draft             bool
	Labels, Assignees []string
	// State is magnum's state: baseline, queued, reviewing, reviewed,
	// rereview_pending, needs_attention, paused, closed, released,
	// ineligible (the configuration skips it; the board says "skipped") or
	// ignored (magnum ignore).
	State string
	// SkipReason says why the configuration skips an ineligible PR ("bot
	// author", `author "x" is in skip_authors`, ...).
	SkipReason string
	// Badges are the PR's labels that [board] badges marks, in its order.
	Badges  []Badge
	GHState string // GitHub's state: OPEN, CLOSED, MERGED
	// ActivityAt is the PR's last activity, which the UPDATED column, the
	// updated sort and the card show: a push, a comment, a review, a label,
	// a review request, a draft change, a rename, a description edit, a base
	// change, a close, reopen or merge; GitHubUpdatedAt until magnum read it.
	ActivityAt time.Time
	// GitHubUpdatedAt is GitHub's updatedAt, which also moves for what a
	// reviewer never sees (a project field, a resolved thread); tui --json
	// only.
	GitHubUpdatedAt time.Time
	HeadSHA         string
	LastReview      *ReviewInfo // the latest review magnum knows of; nil when none
	// Replies counts the replies on magnum's review its judge has not
	// re-decided yet: LAST REVIEW shows "↩N" and r re-decides them now (the
	// judge alone) while the head is the reviewed one.
	Replies int
	// Stalemate are the URLs of the threads where magnum stopped arguing
	// after two rebuttals, which wait for the operator: the title cell
	// carries the attention mark and the card's NEEDS YOU says what to do.
	// Empty when magnum argues in none (or the operator has acted).
	Stalemate []string
	// Findings is what magnum's latest posted review concluded (its findings
	// by priority, simplifications and verdict), also where it could only
	// comment; nil when magnum has not reviewed the PR.
	Findings *FindingsInfo
	// CI is the head commit's checks; nil when unknown.
	CI          *CIInfo
	Reviewers   []ReviewerInfo // everyone who reviewed or was asked to
	SinceReview *ReviewDelta   // what changed since the last review; nil when unknown
	Slot        string         // folder of the review slot holding the PR, if any
	// SlotHold is the hold a slot guard persisted on that slot (slots.hold_reason:
	// head_drift, unpushed_commits, dirty_worktree, ...); "" when the PR holds no
	// slot or the slot holds nothing. u acknowledges a head_drift or
	// unpushed_commits hold, and x says so instead of skipping the slot.
	SlotHold string
	Pinned   bool
	// Starred: the operator starred the PR (`magnum star`, the board's *;
	// store.KVPRStar), so it leads its section, the open PRs or the
	// recently closed ones, whatever the sort; StarredAt is when (zero when
	// the record does not say). The title's first tag marks it.
	Starred        bool
	StarredAt      time.Time
	Muted          bool
	Notes          bool      // the repository has reviewer notes (magnum notes)
	NextEligibleAt time.Time // earliest next automatic review; zero when not scheduled
	// LastError is the one-line explanation of the PR's stored error (for a
	// PR in needs_attention, why it needs you); ErrorFix the next step and
	// ErrorDetail the end of the failing command's output.
	LastError   string
	ErrorFix    string
	ErrorDetail []string
	// AttentionSum is a digest of the PR's stored error as the engine wrote
	// it (its last_error, which LastError explains; "" for none), never
	// drawn: the board's d sends it as the attention you saw, so `magnum fix
	// --done` lifts no attention that changed since the row was read.
	AttentionSum string
	// AttentionKind is why the engine parked a PR in needs_attention, the
	// reason kind it recorded (attention.Kind*: failed, overloaded, blocked,
	// needs_attention, identity_error, identity_leak, fix; inferred from the
	// stored error for older rows); the attention pill names it in a word
	// ("attention · failed"). "" for a PR that does not need attention.
	AttentionKind string
	RoundsToday   int
	LastRound     *RoundTimings // the stages of the last review round; nil when none ran
	// RoundWhy says which roles the last round ran and why; nil when unknown.
	RoundWhy *RoundWhy
	// Progress is the round in flight: its start and its roles, which the
	// state cell turns into the stage and the time ("simplify · 17m") and
	// the card into a timeline; nil when no round runs or it is unknown.
	Progress *RoundProgress
	// Spend is the agent time the PR's runs took over the last 7 days and
	// how many rounds they ran in; nil when none ran.
	Spend *SpendInfo

	// Wait and WaitDetail say why a PR waiting for a round has none yet (the
	// daemon's account): the compact form the state cell shows ("re-review
	// · quiet → 14:09") and the sentence with the command that lifts it,
	// which the card shows. "" when the PR does not wait or no daemon said.
	// WaitNarrow is Wait for a narrow state cell (a retry without its cause:
	// "re-review · retry 2/3 → 22:57"); "" when it has no narrower form.
	Wait, WaitDetail, WaitNarrow string
	// PinWait: the round the PR waits for waits on its pinned slot
	// (engine.WaitPinned), pinned by PinnedBy ("magnum open"; "" when
	// unknown); the card says who pinned it and that u unpins it.
	PinWait  bool
	PinnedBy string
	// HeldUntil is when the hold `magnum open` set on the PR ends
	// (engine.OpenHold.End): its pin is that hold, which ends by itself, so
	// the state cell says "held → 03:21" where nothing else waits there, the
	// card "held by open until 03:21" and the title line counts it held, not
	// pinned. Zero for a lasting pin, or no pin.
	HeldUntil time.Time
	// OpenRestores: o restores the PR in a slot (the role it opens has no
	// live pane and its session is parked, or its session is gone and
	// another role's parked one stands in for it), so o asks first, saying for how
	// long the restore holds the PR: OpenHold, [daemon] open_hold (0: until
	// `magnum unpin`).
	OpenRestores bool
	OpenHold     time.Duration
	// DeltaCheck: the round the PR waits for is a delta check (the judge
	// alone on a small delta); the state cell says so, as it does for a
	// round in flight whose RoundWhy is one.
	DeltaCheck bool
	// SnoozedUntil is when the PR's snooze ends (`magnum snooze`, z): no
	// automatic round starts before; SnoozedAt is when it was set and
	// SnoozedBy who set it ("magnum snooze", "the board"). Zero while the
	// PR is not snoozed. The state cell says "snoozed → 18:00" when nothing
	// else waits there, the card says all three, and z lifts it.
	SnoozedUntil, SnoozedAt time.Time
	SnoozedBy               string
	// CodexFlag is the PR's Codex flag in one cell ("Codex flagged · never
	// reviewed again", engine.CodexFlag.Short): its provider refused a round
	// as a possible cybersecurity risk, so magnum never reviews it again,
	// and the review keys refuse. CodexFlagSentence is the card's account
	// of it, with the command that lifts it. "" while the PR is not flagged.
	CodexFlag, CodexFlagSentence string
	// MuteReason is why the PR was muted (the latest `magnum mute`'s
	// reason), for the card; "" when it was muted without one or is not.
	MuteReason string
	// Fixing is the PR's fix loop while its fixer works, as the state cell
	// shows it ("fixing 1/3 · claude-fix", engine.FixState.Short); "" when
	// no fixer works on it (a loop waiting for its re-review shows the PR's
	// state). FixLoop: the PR has a fix loop in either phase, the fixer at
	// work or the loop waiting for its re-review or next cycle (its
	// engine.KVPRFix row exists): K aborts it, although the PR may be
	// reviewed. FixOff: the PR was switched out of autofix (`magnum fix
	// --off`); its tags and the card say "fix off".
	Fixing  string
	FixLoop bool
	// Fixer is the login the PR's fixer pushes and replies as (its watch's
	// fix role's identity: a fixer App's bot, or yours), which f's
	// question names; "" when the config does not say.
	Fixer  string
	FixOff bool
	// HeldMerge is the held-merge.diff (absolute) of the merge of the
	// parent magnum holds for your y on the PR (the engine's HeldMerge),
	// which e opens in the pager and P's question pushes; "" for none.
	HeldMerge string
	// Whiteboard is the PR's whiteboard, the Whiteboard session that holds
	// it and the head it describes (engine.KVPRWhiteboard, written after a
	// review or by `magnum whiteboard`); nil when the PR has none. The card
	// says "whiteboard <head>" among the PR's flags, and w opens it in
	// Whiteboard Desktop.
	Whiteboard *PRWhiteboard
	// Note is a one-line remark about the last review shown under LAST REVIEW
	// on the card (e.g. "comment-only push skipped (a7b3f8c → 602da9d)").
	Note string
	// ProjectNote says that the agents of the PR's head ran without the
	// PR's changes to the checkout's own agent config (e.g. the PR changes
	// .codex/, so Codex ran with the checkout untrusted) or, for a record of
	// residue (agents.ProjectNote.Residue), without the checkout's files
	// there that the PR's commits do not change; the card shows it under
	// LAST REVIEW. "" = nothing to say.
	ProjectNote string

	// RequestedToMe is the latest review request that asked one of the self
	// logins; LastRequest the latest one whoever it asked; Requests the
	// latest request to each reviewer, newest first. Nil or empty when the
	// registry knows none (only the newest ten requests of a PR are kept).
	RequestedToMe, LastRequest *RequestInfo
	Requests                   []RequestInfo

	// ClosedAt is when GitHub merged the PR, else closed it; zero while it
	// is open. Recent marks a PR GitHub merged or closed within [board]
	// recent_closed: the board lists it in a section after the open PRs.
	ClosedAt time.Time
	Recent   bool
	// ReleaseAfter is when the close grace of a PR GitHub merged or closed
	// ends and the daemon releases its slot; zero when there is none.
	ReleaseAfter time.Time
	// MergedUnreviewed: GitHub merged the PR before magnum reviewed its last
	// push (store.IsMergedUnreviewed); LastReview.CommitSHA is the commit
	// magnum reviewed last, if any.
	MergedUnreviewed bool
	// FlagDismissed: the PR is muted without being flagged though it would
	// be flagged unmuted (store.IsFlagDismissed): a mute dismissed the
	// merged-unreviewed flag, and M restores it.
	FlagDismissed bool
	// NeedsMe: magnum approved the PR's head, but GitHub, which never counts
	// a GitHub App's approval, still blocks it on the operator
	// (store.NeedsMe): NeedsMeApprove while it requires an approval that
	// counts, NeedsMeLift while the operator's own changes request is the
	// only one blocking it; "" otherwise. The state cell says "✔ needs you"
	// or "✔ lift your ✗" and the updated sort lists it first.
	NeedsMe string
	// NeedsMeReason: magnum's clean review of the head is a comment because
	// the approval's gates refused the approval its identity would have
	// posted, in the list's words ("approve by hand: the PR changes its own
	// workflows or actions", store.NeedsMeWords); "" otherwise. The card says
	// it when no line about the approval as the operator does.
	NeedsMeReason string
	// ReviewDecision is GitHub's reviewDecision: APPROVED,
	// CHANGES_REQUESTED or REVIEW_REQUIRED; "" when the base branch requires
	// no review or magnum has not read it yet. tui --json only.
	ReviewDecision string
	// AutoApproved is the approval magnum posted as the operator that
	// stands on the PR ([[watch]] auto_approve); nil when none. The state
	// cell says "✔ auto" and D withdraws it.
	AutoApproved *AutoApproval
	// AutoStopped is why magnum no longer approves the PR as the operator
	// (they dismissed one of its approvals, reviewed the PR by hand or ran
	// magnum unapprove); "" when it may. The card says so.
	AutoStopped string
	// AutoRefused is why magnum does not approve the PR as the operator
	// although its review of the head left nothing to fix
	// (engine.AutoApproveRefused: an author auto_approve_skip_authors
	// lists or auto_approve_authors leaves out, a reviewer's missing report,
	// a PR its watch would not review on its own, a change to the review
	// agents' instructions, the head's checks); "" otherwise. The card says
	// so ("auto-approval: off for this author (auto_approve_skip_authors)"
	// or "(not in auto_approve_authors)" for the first).
	AutoRefused string
	// ApproveAs is whom A approves a NeedsMe row as: the watch's
	// auto_approve_as, the operator's own account, whose approval GitHub
	// counts. nil on a row that does not need the operator, or whose watch
	// names none: A then refuses (only an approval by hand counts) and the
	// card says so.
	ApproveAs *ApproveAs
	// Open is autofix = "open"'s verdict on your own open PR (the engine's
	// pr.<id>.open); nil on another's PR and on one without a verdict. The
	// title's tags mark the row with it ("open: needs you") and the card
	// says it ("verdict: ...").
	Open *PROpen
	// Stagings is where the PR stands on its repository's staging envs, in
	// the config's order, as the daemon last told it (engine.KVPRStaging,
	// unknown once it is stale or of another head): the STAGE column's
	// glyphs and the card's STAGINGS block. nil for a repository without
	// staging envs and for a PR that is not open.
	Stagings []StagingInfo
	// StagingDeploys are the staging deploys of the PR magnum runs, or ran
	// in the last day, live ones first, each as its newest event left it
	// (engine.StagingDeployRecord): the card's lines under each env.
	StagingDeploys []StagingDeploy
	// DeployFirst is staging's line for an open PR whose head changes a
	// migration that no env of Stagings holds or may hold: "deploy to a
	// staging before the merge (it changes db/migrate/...)"
	// (staging.DeployBeforeMergeWords of engine.StagingFirst over the
	// head's file list); "" otherwise, for a PR that can never deploy to a
	// staging (engine.StagingNeverDeploys: a fork's), and while a deploy of
	// the head in StagingDeploys is live (queued or running: E would say it
	// is already deploying; one that needs you keeps the line). The card says
	// it: in yellow where the deploy is your next step (DeployNeedsYou),
	// else dimmed; the ready view leaves the PR out.
	DeployFirst string
}
    PRBoardRow is one pull request on the PR board. Ref is what actions receive;
    Owner, Repo and Number label the row (Ref is parsed when they are empty).

func FilterPRBoard(rows []PRBoardRow, v PRView, selfLogins []string) []PRBoardRow
    FilterPRBoard returns the rows of rows in view v; selfLogins are the logins
    that count as "me" (PRBoardOptions.SelfLogins).

func SortPRBoard(rows []PRBoardRow, by PRSort, desc bool) []PRBoardRow
    SortPRBoard returns a copy of rows in the given order; desc puts the
    largest key first (newest update, latest review, most recent verdict,
    newest request, most lines changed, most urgent state). Rows lacking the key
    (never reviewed, no request, no delta) come last either way; ties put the
    newest update first, then order by ref. An unknown sort means SortUpdated.
    The recently closed rows (Recent) come after all the others, newest closed
    first, whatever the sort: they are the board's own section. In each section
    the starred rows come first, newest update first (then by ref), whatever the
    sort and its direction: the operator starred them to keep them in sight.
    The updated sort, the board's default, lists the unstarred PRs that need the
    operator's approval (NeedsMe) first, either way, each part in its order.

func (r PRBoardRow) DeployNeedsYou() bool
    DeployNeedsYou reports whether r's staging deploy before the merge is the
    operator's next step: their own PR whose fresh verdict is idle with the
    merge theirs (PROpen.Merge: approved, or a base that requires no review)
    while the board's read says the deploy comes first (DeployFirst), as the
    factory screen puts it on its wait on your merge. Its tag and verdict line
    then say it needs you. Never on another's PR, whose merge is its author's:
    a NeedsMe there stays about the approval; nor while anything the verdict
    names comes first (needs_you, waits).

type PRBoardSource interface {
	Rows(ctx context.Context) ([]PRBoardRow, error)
}
    PRBoardSource supplies the board's rows; Rows is called once per refresh,
    never concurrently with itself.

type PRBoardSourceFunc func(ctx context.Context) ([]PRBoardRow, error)
    PRBoardSourceFunc adapts a function to PRBoardSource.

func (f PRBoardSourceFunc) Rows(ctx context.Context) ([]PRBoardRow, error)
    Rows calls f.

type PROpen struct {
	Verdict, Why, Head string
	Stale              bool
	// Merge: the verdict is idle and leaves the merge to you
	// (engine.OpenMergeIsYours over the PR's review gate: approved, or a
	// base that requires no review).
	Merge bool
}
    PROpen is autofix = "open"'s verdict on your own PR as the board shows it:
    fixing, waits, needs_you, idle, unknown or off, why in magnum's plain
    words (never the PR's text), the head magnum decided at, and whether it is
    stale (magnum's last tick long ago, another head, a PR row changed since):
    magnum is then looking at the PR, never idle.

type PRRow struct {
	Ref, Title, Author, State, Next, Age, URL string
	Review                                    *ReviewFacts // for the y/N question before a review; nil when unknown
	GHState                                   string       // GitHub's state: OPEN, CLOSED or MERGED; "" when unknown
	// MergedUnreviewed: GitHub merged the PR before magnum reviewed its last
	// push; FlagDismissed: the PR was muted after that, so it is not flagged
	// (store.IsMergedUnreviewed, store.IsFlagDismissed). M dismisses the one
	// and restores the other.
	MergedUnreviewed, FlagDismissed bool
	// FixLoop: the PR has a fix loop in either phase (its engine.KVPRFix row
	// exists), which K aborts although the PR may be reviewed; FixOff: it
	// was switched out of autofix (`magnum fix --off`), so F reads "fix on".
	FixLoop, FixOff bool
	// Fixer is the login the PR's fixer pushes and replies as (its watch's
	// fix role's identity: a fixer App's bot, or yours), which f's
	// question names; "" when the config does not say.
	Fixer string
	// Stagings is where the open PR stands on its repository's staging
	// envs (PRBoardRow.Stagings), which E's chooser lists; nil without.
	Stagings []StagingInfo
	// HeldMerge is the held-merge.diff of the merge of the parent magnum
	// holds for your y on the PR (PRBoardRow.HeldMerge), which e opens;
	// "" for none.
	HeldMerge string
}
    PRRow is one queued (or closing) PR; Ref is what actions receive.

type PRSort string
    PRSort orders the board.

const (
	SortUpdated          PRSort = "updated"           // newest update first
	SortLastReview       PRSort = "last-review"       // latest review first
	SortReviewerActivity PRSort = "reviewer-activity" // latest verdict by anyone first
	SortRequested        PRSort = "requested"         // latest review request first
	SortChanges          PRSort = "changes"           // most lines changed since the review first
	SortState            PRSort = "state"             // most urgent state first
)
    The board's sorts, in the order s cycles through them.

func PRSorts() []PRSort
    PRSorts lists the sorts in the order the s key cycles through them.

func ParsePRSort(s string) (PRSort, error)
    ParsePRSort reads a sort name such as "updated" or "last-review" (case,
    "_" and spaces do not matter); empty means SortUpdated.

type PRView string
    PRView is a preset subset of the board's rows.

const (
	ViewAll    PRView = "all"    // every row
	ViewMagnum PRView = "magnum" // rows magnum reviewed or is reviewing (state not baseline or ineligible), or whose review is requested from a self login
	ViewMine   PRView = "mine"   // assigned to one of the self logins, or their review is requested
	ViewReady  PRView = "ready"  // open, not a draft, approved on the head, nothing blocking, required checks passed, no staging deploy first
)
    The board's views, in the order v cycles through them.

func PRViews() []PRView
