```text
    PRViews lists the views in the order the v key cycles through them.

func ParsePRView(s string) (PRView, error)
    ParsePRView reads a view name ("all", "magnum", "mine", "ready"; case does
    not matter); empty means ViewAll.

type PRWhiteboard struct {
	Session string
	Head    string
}
    PRWhiteboard is a PR's whiteboard as the board knows it: the Whiteboard
    session that holds it, which w opens, and the head it describes
    (engine.WhiteboardRecord).

type Pause struct {
	Key    string // scope: daemon, codex, claude, watch:<owner>, identity:<name>, github
	Reason string // why, with "until" already folded in when it applies
	Fix    string // command or step that lifts it; optional
}
    Pause is one reason automation (or part of it) is held back.

type PauseSpec struct {
	For    time.Duration
	Until  string
	Reason string
}
    PauseSpec is `magnum pause`'s flags: For or Until (a local 15:30 or an
    RFC3339 time), neither for a pause until resumed.

type PickAction int
    PickAction is what the user chose to do with the picked PR.

const (
	PickActionCancel    PickAction = iota
	PickActionReview               // enter
	PickActionFresh                // ctrl+f: review with new sessions
	PickActionOpen                 // ctrl+g: open the judge pane
	PickActionBrowser              // ctrl+o: open the PR URL
	PickActionTogglePin            // ctrl+p: pin, or unpin when Entry.Pinned
	PickActionRelease              // ctrl+x
)
    The picker's actions; PickActionCancel is the zero value. ctrl+r (and F5)
    refreshes the list, as on every screen.

func (a PickAction) String() string

type PickEntry struct {
	Ref    string // what actions receive: owner/name#N (repo#N labels work too)
	Title  string
	Author string
	State  string // magnum state, with flags ("reviewed,pinned")
	Age    string // since the last activity ("3h")
	URL    string
	Pinned bool         // ctrl+p means unpin when true
	Review *ReviewFacts // for the y/N question before a review; nil when unknown
	// GHState is GitHub's state of the PR: OPEN, CLOSED or MERGED; "" when
	// unknown. A MERGED one is asked about as a post-merge review.
	GHState string
}
    PickEntry is one PR the picker lists.

type PickOutcome struct {
	Action PickAction
	Entry  *PickEntry
	Query  string // the filter text as the user left it
}
    PickOutcome is the picker's result. Entry is nil when the action is Cancel,
    or when the query matched no entry but reads as a PR reference (URL,
    owner/repo#N, repo#N, #N or N): the caller resolves Query then.

func RunPicker(ctx context.Context, entries []PickEntry, opts PickerOptions) (PickOutcome, error)
    RunPicker lets the user filter entries and pick one with an action. It
    returns a Cancel outcome (and nil error) when the user cancels or ctx ends.

type PickerOptions struct {
	Query string           // initial filter; a PR URL or reference narrows to that PR
	Title string           // default "magnum pick"
	Now   func() time.Time // clock for "reviewed 2h ago" in the y/N question; default time.Now
	// Lookup resolves a typed reference the list lacks to a PR magnum knows,
	// e.g. a merged one, so the y/N question can say what it is; nil means none.
	Lookup func(query string) (PickEntry, bool)
	// Reload lists the PRs again for ctrl+r and F5 (the registry may have
	// changed since the picker opened); nil means the keys say so instead.
	Reload func(ctx context.Context) ([]PickEntry, error)
}
    PickerOptions tune the picker.

type QuestionCard struct {
	// TaskKey is the task's Jira key ("PR-12345") or its GitHub number.
	TaskKey, Title, Kind string
	Asked                time.Time // when the batch was asked
	Questions            []CardQuestion
	Current              int // the index of the question on the card

	// AsOf is the revision of the questions the answers are for ("as of
	// 14:12"), drawn on the recap. Zero: the sentence is left out.
	AsOf time.Time

	// Cursor is the option of the current question under the mark, which j k
	// move; out of range (-1) = none. The screen starts it on the
	// recommended option, and on none when there is no recommendation.
	Cursor int
	// Needless offers the − key: flag the current question as needless.
	Needless bool
	// NeedlessReasons are the reasons a needless flag takes, picked by their
	// digit: while they are set (after −) the footer asks for one.
	NeedlessReasons []string
	// Hints are the footer's key hints; none: the card's own (questionHints).
	Hints []hint `json:"-"`

	// Revision is the revision of the questions on the card: the batch of
	// answers binds to it, and the factory refuses a batch for another
	// (ErrQuestionsChanged).
	Revision int
	// Ask is the y/N question being asked; empty: the key hints (or the
	// line you type).
	Ask string

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    QuestionCard is the agents' questions before coding, one at a time,
    and their recap. Questions are drawn in the order given; Current is the one
    on the card.

type QuestionsChangedError struct {
	At  time.Time
	Why string
}
    QuestionsChangedError is ErrQuestionsChanged with when the questions changed
    and, when the factory knows, why ("Question 2 is open again.").

func (e *QuestionsChangedError) Error() string

func (e *QuestionsChangedError) Is(target error) bool
    Is makes every QuestionsChangedError match ErrQuestionsChanged.

type ReadyBinding struct {
	HeadSHA, ReportHash, DiffHash string
	DiffOpened, Shown             time.Time
	DiffDwell                     time.Duration
	Recommended                   string
}
    ReadyBinding binds a decision on the ready card to what the card showed:
    the head and the hashes of the report and the diff (from the source),
    and the screen's own times: when the card was first shown, when the diff
    was first opened and how long the pager was open in all (zero: never).
    Recommended is the choice the card marked recommended as it was drawn when
    you decided (FactoryPush, FactorySendBack or FactoryDrop), "" when it drew
    none (before the diff was read, or push not offered).

type ReadyCard struct {
	// TaskKey is the task's Jira key or its GitHub number.
	TaskKey, Title, Branch string
	Waited                 time.Duration // how long the card has waited
	Cause, Fix, Proof      string
	Files                  []CardFile
	Doubts                 []string // what the agents were unsure of or skipped
	Screenshots            int
	// DiffOpened is when the operator opened the diff; zero: not yet, and
	// neither Recommended nor Why is drawn.
	DiffOpened time.Time
	// Recommended is the option the factory picks: 0 push + PR, 1 send back,
	// 2 drop; -1 for none.
	Recommended int
	Why         string

	// Kind is the task's kind ("bug"), Commits the commits on the branch.
	Kind    string
	Commits int
	// ScreenshotsNote says what the screenshots show ("from the copy's own
	// server: the copied campaign shows 25 points").
	ScreenshotsNote string
	// Ask is the y/N question being asked; empty: the key hints.
	Ask string

	// Flags are the FLAGS line: what needs a second look before the push,
	// one each ("not in the plan: spec/factories/reward_rules.rb").
	Flags []string
	// Leftovers are the KNOWN row, what the local review left open that does
	// not block (the PR body's "Known" list), one each: its leftovers, the
	// findings the writer declined with their risks, the doubts, and the
	// reviewers a round went without.
	Leftovers []string
	// FixedAfter are the FIXED AFTER row, the findings the writer fixed after
	// the local review's last round, at its cap, which no round reviewed
	// (the PR body lists them under Known too), one each; none: no row.
	FixedAfter []string
	// Known is how many of the local review's leftovers are defects that w
	// sends back to the writer, in one key (not the simplifications, the
	// doubts or the declined findings, which the KNOWN row also lists). The
	// key is offered only while it is above zero; the y/N names the count.
	Known int
	// Unread are the changed files the operator has not opened in the diff,
	// drawn as "unread: <file>".
	Unread []string
	// Frees is what the push frees ("talkable.factory3; PR-12395 starts in
	// it"): the push's y/N names it ("It frees ..."). A drop's y/N is the
	// spec's sentence, which names the copy itself.
	Frees string
	// Reasons are the reason keys of a send back, picked by their digit:
	// while they are set the footer asks for one, before the note.
	Reasons []string
	// Cursor is the option under the mark, which j k and 1-3 move; -1 (any
	// value out of range) = no mark. It is -1 until the operator moves it or
	// opens the diff: before the diff nothing is marked (spec 9.C). Its zero
	// value marks push + PR.
	Cursor int
	// Hints are the footer's key hints; none: the card's own (readyHints).
	Hints []hint `json:"-"`

	// Copy is the copy the task holds ("talkable.factory3"), which a drop
	// frees: its y/N names it.
	Copy string
	// NoPush says why push is not offered on this card ("the base conflicts:
	// the writer merges it"); empty: it is. The screen refuses a push then,
	// and the card says so on the option.
	NoPush string
	// Failed are the checks that failed ("rubocop: 2 offenses"), drawn under
	// PROOF behind a red ✗; the recommendation is then send back.
	Failed []string
	// QA is the QA row, after PROOF: what the change's visual QA found
	// ("clean: 3 pages walked at abc1234, 1 note", "not needed: no
	// user-facing file changed"); empty: no row. QAReport is the QA run's
	// report (summary.md, absolute), which e opens in the pager: "" for
	// none, and no e then.
	QA, QAReport string

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    ReadyCard is a finished task waiting for the operator's decision: read the
    diff, then push, send back or drop. The recommendation is hidden until the
    operator opened the diff.

type Request struct {
	ID     int64
	Kind   string // review, pin, release, …
	State  string // RequestPending, RequestDone or RequestFailed
	Result string // the daemon's answer; "" while pending
}
    Request is a daemon request as the screens follow it.

type RequestInfo struct {
	To   string // the reviewer: a login (a bot's keeps "[bot]") or "team:<slug>"
	By   string // who asked; "" when unknown (a deleted account)
	At   time.Time
	Mine bool // To is one of the self logins
}
    RequestInfo is a review request: who was asked, by whom and when.

type ResumeSpec struct {
	Tool  string
	Watch string
}
    ResumeSpec is `magnum resume`'s flags: Tool is an agent kind or "all",
    Watch a watch owner; both empty resume automation.

type ReviewDelta struct {
	Base                                 string
	BaseSHA                              string
	Commits, Files, Additions, Deletions int
	Truncated                            bool // the counts are lower bounds
	// MergedBase is the base branch the commits since merged in (or were
	// rebased onto) when the counts leave its changes out (the PR's own);
	// Raw: they merged it, but the counts include its changes (the PR's
	// own diff could not be compared in full). RawBase names it then.
	MergedBase, RawBase string
}
    ReviewDelta is what changed on a PR since Base: "reviewed" (the last
    reviewed head) or "base branch" (no review yet: the whole PR).

type ReviewFacts struct {
	HeadSHA     string
	ReviewedSHA string    // the last reviewed head; "" when never reviewed
	ReviewedAt  time.Time // zero when unknown
	ReviewedBy  string    // who posted that review; "" when unknown
	// SinceReview is what changed since ReviewedSHA (Base "reviewed");
	// nil when unknown, e.g. not counted yet for the current head.
	SinceReview *ReviewDelta
}
    ReviewFacts is what the y/N question before a review says about a PR on
    the dashboard and in the picker (the board reads its own rows): the head,
    the last reviewed head and the commits since it.

type ReviewInfo struct {
	Login, Event string // Event: APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED, COMMENTED, DISMISSED (any case)
	SubmittedAt  time.Time
	CommitSHA    string
	Stale        bool // the head moved since
	Mine         bool // Login is one of the self logins
}
    ReviewInfo is the latest review on a PR.

type ReviewOpts struct {
	Fresh    bool // new agent sessions instead of resuming
	Simplify bool // run the role aliased simplify this round (magnum review --simplify)
	// Replies has the judge alone re-decide the replies on its review now
	// (magnum review --replies): a reply round on the head magnum reviewed.
	// It excludes the other variants.
	Replies bool
}
    ReviewOpts are the review variants the screens ask for. A forced round
    reviews the head even when it was reviewed already, so there is no "again"
    variant.

type ReviewerInfo struct {
	Login       string
	Verdict     string // approved | changes_requested | commented | dismissed | pending
	SubmittedAt time.Time
	CommitSHA   string
	Stale       bool // the head moved since the verdict
	Requested   bool // a review is requested from them
	Mine        bool
}
    ReviewerInfo is one reviewer's latest verdict on a PR.

type RoleProgress struct {
	Role, Label string
	Judge       bool
	// OwnPass: the judge's own pass, its runs of kind own_pass, listed as an
	// entry of its own before the judge's.
	OwnPass         bool
	Started, Ended  time.Time
	Working, Failed bool
}
    RoleProgress is one role of a round in flight. Started is when its run was
    prompted (zero: not started yet) and Ended when it ended (zero while it
    works); Working: its run is submitted or working; Failed: it failed or was
    abandoned. Label is the short name the state cell gives it while it works
    (the shortest of its name and aliases, see the cli's stageLabel); the judge
    is "judge" whatever its names.

type RoleRerun struct {
	Role  string
	Lines int
}
    RoleRerun is a role that ran again because Lines code lines changed since
    its last run.

type RoleRotation struct {
	Role   string
	Rounds int
}
    RoleRotation is a role whose session served Rounds review rounds, its
    max_session_rounds, so the round started it in a fresh session.

type RoundProgress struct {
	StartedAt time.Time
	Roles     []RoleProgress
}
    RoundProgress is a round in flight: when it started (the PR's
    last_round_started_at) and its roles, the ones with a run in the order
    their runs were created, then the ones the round named that have none yet,
    the judge last and its own pass right before it.

type RoundTimings struct {
	Round   int
	Kind    string        // the round's kind: initial, rereview, continue, recovery
	Stages  []StageTiming // checkout, then each role in the order it started, then verify
	Total   time.Duration // the first stage's start to the last one's end (to now while running)
	Running bool          // the round is still in flight
}
    RoundTimings is how long each stage of a PR's last review round took,
    from the registry's runs and step events.

type RoundWhy struct {
	Kind      string // initial, rereview, continue, recovery, nudge
	PostMerge bool   // a post-merge review
	// DeltaCheck: a re-review of DeltaLines changed code lines by the judge
	// alone (a delta check).
	DeltaCheck bool
	DeltaLines int
	// FullPass: a scheduled full pass ([pipeline] full_pass_every), a
	// recovery of every role in fresh sessions over the whole PR;
	// BeforeApproval: the one that follows a review that held its approval
	// ([pipeline] approve_after_full_pass).
	FullPass       bool
	BeforeApproval bool
	// AuditPass: a scheduled audit pass ([pipeline] audit_every), a
	// recovery in fresh sessions whose judge first probes what no round
	// probed.
	AuditPass bool
	// Replies: a reply round, whose judge re-decides this many replies on
	// the head it reviewed.
	Replies   int
	Roles     []string // the roles it ran, in the order the round named them
	Requested []string // the roles asked for this round
	Reruns    []RoleRerun
	// Triaged: triage decided this round's roles; Skipped are the roles it
	// dropped and Reason its words (the model read the PR: PR content,
	// cleaned like any). EveryRole is why triage kept every role ("the diff
	// could not be read"); all empty when triage did not run.
	Triaged   bool
	Skipped   []string
	Reason    string
	EveryRole string
	// Rotated are the roles the round started in a fresh session because
	// their sessions served their max_session_rounds.
	Rotated []RoleRotation
	// At is when the round started (its engine.round_start event).
	At time.Time
}
    RoundWhy says which roles a PR's last round ran and why: its kind (a
    continue runs the judge alone), the roles asked for it (`magnum review
    --role`, --simplify), the roles that ran again because their code changed
    (rerun_min_lines), and triage's decision.

type RoundsInfo struct {
	Active, Max int
	ActivePRs   []string
	Progress    []*RoundProgress
}
    RoundsInfo is the review rounds in progress. Progress[i] is the round
    of ActivePRs[i], which the rounds line follows with its stage and time
    ("talkable#1 · simplify · 17m"); nil, or missing, when unknown.

type RuntimeEntry struct {
	Name   string // "automation", the kind, the watch owner
	Label  string // what its row says ("watch 1 talkable"); "" = Name
	Paused bool
	// State is the row's text: "running", "no pause", "paused: usage limit
	// until 07:50 · since 02:10".
	State string
	// Detail is the detail strip's line for it: why it is paused and what
	// lifts it by itself.
	Detail string
	// Live counts an agent kind's live sessions `magnum restart-sessions`
	// would restart (a pinned PR's left out).
	Live int
}
    RuntimeEntry is one pausable thing: automation, an agent kind or a watch.

type RuntimeState struct {
	// Daemon is true when a daemon runs; otherwise a change applies when it
	// starts.
	Daemon     bool
	Automation RuntimeEntry
	Kinds      []RuntimeEntry // one per agent kind
	Watches    []RuntimeEntry // one per watch owner
}
    RuntimeState is what the Runtime section shows.

type SettingField struct {
	// Target is the draft's key: the setting and its scope instance, unique.
	Target  string
	Section string // the rail's section it lists under ("Spend & models")
	Scope   string // "" for a global setting, else a SettingsScope.ID
	Label   string
	// Key is the TOML path as the detail strip shows it ("[pipeline] spend",
	// "[spend.high].claude-simplify.model").
	Key         string
	Type        SettingType
	Options     []string          // the choices of an enum, effort, model or roles setting
	Notes       map[string]string // a note on an option ("burn": "starts from medium, then its table (7 roles)"; a role: "judge")
	Description string
	Default     string // what applies without the key ("medium", "inherit (high)")
	AppliesNow  bool   // applies at once; else after a daemon restart
	// Text and List are what the file says ("" and nil when it does not set
	// the key); Value is the value in effect as the row shows it.
	Text  string
	List  []string
	Value string
	Set   bool   // the file sets the key; else the default applies
	Line  int    // the key's line in the file (0 = not in it)
	From  string // where the value comes from ("your file, line 96", "built-in default")
	// Role, Level and Cell place a spend setting in the roles grid: the role,
	// its spend level ("" = the role's base [[role]] block) and the cell
	// ("model", "effort" or "rereview_effort").
	Role, Level, Cell string
	// Path is the setting's key path as magnum's loader names it in its
	// messages ("usage.codex_soft"), so a refusal marks its row.
	Path string
	// Inherits is the Target of the setting this one takes its value from
	// while unset ("inherit (high)" from [pipeline] spend), so the row
	// follows a staged edit of that one; "" for none.
	Inherits string
	// Validate checks a scalar value and ValidateList a list before the edit
	// is staged; nil accepts anything.
	Validate     func(string) error
	ValidateList func([]string) error
}
    SettingField is one editable setting of one scope instance.

type SettingType string
    SettingType is how a setting is edited.

const (
	SettingEnum     SettingType = "enum"     // one of Options (a Select)
	SettingBool     SettingType = "bool"     // true or false (a Select)
	SettingDuration SettingType = "duration" // "15m", "2h" (an Input)
	SettingInt      SettingType = "int"      // a whole number (an Input)
	SettingPercent  SettingType = "percent"  // 0-100 (an Input)
	SettingText     SettingType = "text"     // free text, 300 characters at most (an Input)
	SettingModel    SettingType = "model"    // a model name: one of Options or another (a Select, then an Input)
	SettingEffort   SettingType = "effort"   // a reasoning effort, one of Options (a Select)
	SettingLogins   SettingType = "logins"   // GitHub logins, in order (the list editor)
	SettingRepos    SettingType = "repos"    // repository names, in order (the list editor)
	SettingRoles    SettingType = "roles"    // role names out of Options (a MultiSelect)
	SettingList     SettingType = "list"     // other strings, in order (the list editor)
)
    The setting types; the list types (Logins, Repos, Roles, List) hold
    SettingField.List.

func (t SettingType) IsList() bool
    IsList reports whether t holds a list.

type SettingsData struct {
	// File is the config file as the title names it
	// ("~/.config/magnum/config.toml").
	File string
	// HistoryDir is where a save keeps the previous file
	// ("~/.local/share/magnum/config-history/").
	HistoryDir string
	// RestartPending is true while the daemon runs an older file than this
	// one (the daemon's config hash differs from the file's).
	RestartPending bool
	// Sections are the rail's sections in order; Runtime, the screen's own,
	// comes first whether or not they name it.
	Sections []string
	Fields   []SettingField  // every editable setting, per scope instance
	Scopes   []SettingsScope // the watches, then the repositories
	Roles    []SettingsRole  // the roles as the saved file resolves them
	Warnings []string        // what the loader says of the saved file
}
    SettingsData is one load of the user config.

type SettingsDraft map[string]SettingsEdit
    SettingsDraft is the staged changes by SettingField.Target.

type SettingsEdit struct {
	Text    string
	List    []string
	Default bool
}
    SettingsEdit is one staged change: a value, a list, or back to the default
    (the key goes; its comment stays as a comment line).

type SettingsHunk struct {
	Table          string
	Line           int
	Removed, Added []string
}
    SettingsHunk is one changed place of the file: its table heading, its line
    in the file as saved, and the lines it removes and adds.

type SettingsOptions struct {
	// Scope opens the screen on a watch or a repository ("watch:2",
	// "repo:talkable/web"); "" opens the global settings.
	Scope string
	// Restore opens the save view of the n-th kept version (1 = the newest).
	Restore int
}
    SettingsOptions tune the settings screen.

type SettingsPlan struct {
	Count    int            // the settings it changes
	Hunks    []SettingsHunk // the changed lines, file order
	Warnings []string       // what the loader says of the new file
	Notes    bool           // the changed lines carry dated notes
	Restore  int            // the kept version it puts back (0 = a save of the draft)
	// Opaque is the source's own plan, handed back to Commit.
	Opaque any
}
    SettingsPlan is the save of a draft (or a restore), checked and not yet
    written.

type SettingsRole struct {
	Role, Kind, Model, First, Again, Level string
}
    SettingsRole is one role as a config resolves it: its model and its first
    and re-review efforts under the spend level it follows.

type SettingsRuntime interface {
	// Runtime reads the automation pause, each agent kind's pause and each
	// watch's identity-leak pause.
	Runtime(ctx context.Context) (RuntimeState, error)
	// Pause pauses automation as `magnum pause` does; the text is its answer.
	Pause(ctx context.Context, p PauseSpec) (string, error)
	// Resume lifts a pause as `magnum resume` does: automation (an empty
	// spec), an agent kind or all of them (Tool), or a watch (Watch).
	Resume(ctx context.Context, r ResumeSpec) (string, error)
	// RestartSessions parks the live sessions of an agent kind (or "all")
	// so that they resume in new processes, as `magnum restart-sessions
	// --tool` does; the text is its answer.
	RestartSessions(ctx context.Context, tool string) (string, error)
}
    SettingsRuntime is the runtime side of the settings screen (applies now,
    never saved to the file): the pauses `magnum status` lists and the same
    requests or registry writes `magnum pause` and `magnum resume` make.

type SettingsSaved struct {
	History string // the file that keeps the previous version
	Sum     string // the new file's hash
	// AfterRestart is true when the save changed settings the daemon reads
	// only when it starts.
	AfterRestart bool
	// Opaque is the source's own result, handed back to RequestRestart.
	Opaque any
}
    SettingsSaved is what a commit did.

type SettingsScope struct {
	// ID names it in SettingField.Scope: "watch:1" (by position, from 1),
	// "repo:owner/name".
	ID    string
	Watch bool     // a [[watch]]; else a repository
	Index int      // a watch's position, from 1
	Name  string   // a watch's owner, a repository's owner/name
	Repos []string // a watch's repositories; the title shows the first ones
	// NoBlock is a watched repository the file has no [[repo]] block for: a
	// save of one of its settings creates a minimal block.
	NoBlock bool
}
    SettingsScope is a watch or a repository whose settings a section edits.

type SettingsScreen struct {
	Source  SettingsSource
	Runtime SettingsRuntime
	Options SettingsOptions
}
    SettingsScreen is what the dashboard and the PR board need to open the
    settings screen on `,`.

type SettingsSource interface {
	// Load reads the user config as it is on disk now.
	Load(ctx context.Context) (*SettingsData, error)
	// Preview is the roles the daemon would run after a restart on the file
	// with d applied, computed by magnum's own loader; an error is the
	// loader's refusal of the candidate.
	Preview(ctx context.Context, d SettingsDraft) ([]SettingsRole, error)
	// Plan checks d against the file Load read (refusing a file that changed
	// on disk since) and returns the save it would make: the changed lines,
	// with a dated note on each when notes is true.
	Plan(ctx context.Context, d SettingsDraft, notes bool) (*SettingsPlan, error)
	// Commit writes p, keeping the previous file in the history. The screen
	// calls it only after the operator's y.
	Commit(ctx context.Context, p *SettingsPlan) (SettingsSaved, error)
	// RequestRestart asks the daemon to restart on the saved file at its
	// first idle moment; the text says what happens next.
	RequestRestart(ctx context.Context, s SettingsSaved) (string, error)
	// Restore is the plan that puts the n-th kept version back (1 = the
	// newest), a save like any other.
	Restore(ctx context.Context, n int) (*SettingsPlan, error)
}
    SettingsSource is the config side of the settings screen: what the user
    config file says, the roles it resolves to, and the one path that writes it.
    The cli adapts internal/settings into it. Every value it hands over is
    display text; the screen never parses TOML.

type SlotRow struct {
	Name, Folder, PRRef, PRState, SlotState, DBs, Disk string
	State                                              string // the slot's state: free, busy, held, …
	Pinned                                             bool   // the slot is pinned (magnum pin)
	URL                                                string // PR URL for b; optional (looked up in Queue by PRRef)
	PRGHState                                          string // GitHub's state of the slot's PR: OPEN, CLOSED or MERGED; "" when unknown
	// PRMergedUnreviewed and PRFlagDismissed are PRRow's MergedUnreviewed and
	// FlagDismissed for the slot's PR; read with PRGHState.
	PRMergedUnreviewed, PRFlagDismissed bool
	// PRFixLoop and PRFixOff are PRRow's FixLoop and FixOff for the slot's
	// PR: a PR whose fixer works is reviewed, so it shows on its slot's row
	// and in no queue.
	PRFixLoop, PRFixOff bool
	// PRStagings is PRRow's Stagings for the slot's PR.
	PRStagings []StagingInfo
	// PRHeldMerge is PRRow's HeldMerge for the slot's PR.
	PRHeldMerge string
}
    SlotRow is one review slot. Actions on a slot row target PRRef,
    or the slot Name for pin/unpin/release when it holds no PR. SlotState is
    the slot's state as the table shows it, with its flags ("held [pinned,
    hold:<reason>]"); the actions read State and Pinned, never SlotState,
    whose hold reason is free text.

type SourceFunc func(ctx context.Context) (StatusData, error)
    SourceFunc adapts a function to DashboardSource.

func (f SourceFunc) Gather(ctx context.Context) (StatusData, error)
    Gather calls f.

type SpendInfo struct {
	Window    time.Duration // how far back it counts (7 days)
	AgentTime time.Duration
	Rounds    int
}
    SpendInfo is what a PR's reviews cost over a window: the agent time (the sum
    of its runs' durations, to now for a run still going) and how many rounds
    those runs belong to.

type StageTiming struct {
	Name     string        // "fetch/checkout", a role's name, the judge's own pass ("codex-judge own pass"), "verify"
	Duration time.Duration // to now while Running
	Running  bool
	Failed   bool
}
    StageTiming is one stage of a round.

type StagingAsked struct {
	Envs []string
	Head string
	Seen []StagingSeen
}
    StagingAsked is what a staging deploy's y/N binds its deploy to: the envs
    that take the merge, the head the plan merges, and what the question named
    of each env (a deploy that now adds more is refused).

type StagingCell struct {
	Name, State, Count string
	Seen               time.Time

	// OnYou marks a conflict that is out of fix tries, which is on the
	// operator: the cell turns yellow.
	OnYou bool
}
    StagingCell is one staging server's column on a row. State is one of "none",
    "outdated", "merging", "conflict", "ci", "ci-fail" (the staging branch's
    CI failed on the PR's own change), "deploying", "qa", "qa-pass", "qa-fail",
    "latest" or "unknown". Count is the progress of a "ci" or "qa" cell
    ("12/41", "4/9"). Seen is when the factory's read first saw its state:
    a wide screen and the task card show its age, how long the state has stood
    as the reads tell it.

type StagingDeploy struct {
	Effect, Env, Head, Step, Phase, State, Why, Text, RunURL string
	// Resolver is what the resolver's job does for the live deploy's
	// conflict ("try 1: the agent resolves ... pane w3:p1 ..."); "" when
	// none works on it.
	Resolver          string
	At                time.Time
	Live, Unconfirmed bool
}
    StagingDeploy is a staging deploy of a PR on one env: its effect,
    the step and phase of its last event, its state (queued, running,
    done, failed, cancelled, needs you), why it ended, that event's words,
    ci.yml's run on its merge, when the event came, whether it still runs,
    and whether it is a done that no deployment confirms (pushed, not confirmed:
    engine.StagingDeployRecord.Unconfirmed), and the PR head it deploys (which
    StagingDeploysFolded compares).

type StagingInfo struct {
	Env string
	// State is latest (live: the env's newest deployment holds the PR's
	// head), pushed, outdated (an older commit of the PR is there), none or
	// unknown; Detail says why a pushed one is not live yet: ci_running,
	// ci_failed_ours, ci_failed_not_ours, waiting_jenkins or not_confirmed.
	State, Detail string
	// InTip is the PR's commit the env's branch holds: the head, or an
	// older one Behind commits before it.
	InTip  string
	Behind int
	// PushedAt is when the merge that brought InTip in was made,
	// DeployedAt (live only) when the deployment that holds it was.
	PushedAt, DeployedAt time.Time
	RunURL               string // ci.yml's run on that merge
	Why                  string // why it is unknown, or what could not be told
}
    StagingInfo is where a PR stands on one staging env.

type StagingSeen struct {
	Env        string
	Migrations []string
	Workflows  bool
}
    StagingSeen is what a deploy's question named of one env's plan:
    the migrations Jenkins then runs, and whether the merge changes
    .github/workflows.

type StatusData struct {
	Daemon    DaemonInfo
	Activity  ActivityInfo
	GitHub    GitHubInfo
	Rounds    RoundsInfo
	Agents    AgentsInfo
	Disk      DiskInfo
	Pauses    []Pause
	Slots     []SlotRow
	Queue     []PRRow // open PRs, then closed ones pending release
	Attention []AttentionRow
	Manual    []ManualRow // manual worktrees, shown when toggled on
	Warnings  []string    // sources that could not be read
	// Notes sums the repository notes up ("4 repos · 2 proposals to review
	// (...) · 1 over limit"); "" when no repository has notes.
	Notes string
	// Facts are what the title says of the daemon: an older build, a pause,
	// a drain, the Codex budget's pace.
	Facts       DaemonFacts
	GeneratedAt time.Time
}
    StatusData is one snapshot of what the dashboard shows. Table cells are
    display strings the caller formats (refs, folders, sizes); the header
    numbers are formatted by the dashboard.

type TaskCard struct {
	Key, Kind, Title, Branch string
	// Repo is the task's repository ("owner/name"), the first fact under
	// the header with its PR's number.
	Repo string
	// Copy says which copy the task holds ("copy 2 of 3, server off").
	Copy       string
	Started    time.Time
	WaitingFor string // starts with who it waits on ("rev-ann: review of #4527")
	// WaitingStep is the part of WaitingFor that names a step of the
	// factory's own work ("precheck: jest") and WaitingSince when it began
	// (WaitsOn.Since): the painter adds how long it has run after that part.
	// Zero WaitingSince: no time.
	WaitingStep  string
	WaitingSince time.Time
	// Follow is the file o follows live (less +F) while no agent of the
	// task works and the factory itself runs something for it: its checks'
	// live.log, its copy's setup log, its QA server's log (absolute; "" for
	// none, and o steps into the task's pane). The card names it on a line
	// of its own.
	Follow string
	// Links are what the task waits on you for, as links (the threads and
	// findings its PR's verdict says need you), drawn under WAITING FOR.
	Links []string
	// FixNeeds are what magnum's fixer left you on the PR, one item each in
	// its own words (its report's Needs you, the comment id left out), drawn
	// under WAITING FOR before the links; FixReport is that report (absolute),
	// which e opens in the pager: set for any fix attention whose report
	// magnum keeps, "" for none.
	FixNeeds  []string
	FixReport string
	// Findings are the local review's blocking findings of a task its cap
	// stopped for you ("P2 <title> · <path>"), one each, drawn under WAITING
	// FOR as FixNeeds are; none for any other task.
	Findings []string
	// PRInfo is the PR's own lines (CardPR), drawn first in the card's
	// body: on your PR's card and on a published task's once magnum read
	// its PR; nil before.
	PRInfo *CardPR
	// Stagings are where a published task's PR stands on each staging
	// server, as its row's cells say it, drawn as one STAGINGS line after
	// the PR's lines (each server's state and how long it has stood); none:
	// no line.
	Stagings []StagingCell
	// StagingDeploys are the PR's staging deploys magnum's daemon runs or
	// ran in the last day (its row's FactoryPR.StagingDeploys), drawn under
	// the STAGINGS line in the board card's words; none: no lines.
	StagingDeploys []StagingDeploy
	// JiraStatus is where the task's Jira issue stands, as its row's
	// JiraStatus says it; nil: not read.
	JiraStatus *FactoryJiraStatus
	// JiraPlan is the factory's latest plan of a move of the task's Jira
	// issue (its repository's jira_moves in shadow), drawn as the card's
	// JIRA MOVE line; nil: none.
	JiraPlan *FactoryJiraPlan
	Stages   []CardStage
	Agents   []CardAgent
	// Report lines each start with a label word and a space ("cause the offer
	// email takes ...").
	Report []string
	// Learned is what the task taught the factory, one lesson per entry.
	Learned []string

	// PR is the task's GitHub number once pushed ("#4527"); PRURL its page,
	// which b opens: "" until the factory published the PR or adopted one.
	PR, PRURL string
	// Issue is the task's Jira key ("PR-12330"), "" for a task of your
	// words; IssueURL its page, which t opens: the key's link by the [board]
	// trackers, as the board links a PR's issue, "" when no template names
	// the key.
	Issue, IssueURL string
	// YourTime is how long the operator spent on the task.
	YourTime time.Duration
	// Cursor is the line the mark is on: the stages, then the agents, then
	// the REPORT line, counted in that order; out of range = none.
	Cursor int
	// AgentsNote is the AGENTS line's remark ("the factory merges bastion itself").
	AgentsNote string
	// Spinner is the frame of the working marks, the card's only motion.
	Spinner int
	// Retry is true when a retry can go on: the task needs the operator at
	// a stage that checks again what stopped it (magnum factory retry), not
	// for its questions. The card's hints then offer r.
	Retry bool
	// Rate is true on the card of a task that is published or done: + and −
	// rate it (a rating is undoable and asks no y/N), and the card's hints
	// offer them. A task at work, waiting or stopped is rated by neither.
	Rate bool
	// AcceptQA is what A accepts: the QA defects the writer declined at the
	// task's head, which its QA fix loop stopped on ("1 QA defect the writer
	// declined at abc1234 (flow on /settings/security)", magnum factory
	// retry --accept-qa), the fixes a QA run there did not walk again ("1
	// fix QA did not walk again at abc1234 (...)"), or the states a walk
	// there could not reach ("1 state QA could not reach at abc1234 (...)");
	// "" for none, and no A then.
	AcceptQA string
	// QAReport is the report of the QA run whose stop AcceptQA names
	// (summary.md, absolute), which e opens in the pager there; "" for none.
	QAReport string
	// Hints are the footer's key hints; none: the card's own (taskHints).
	Hints []hint `json:"-"`
	// Ask is the y/N question being asked (a retry, a drop); empty: the key
	// hints.
	Ask string

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    TaskCard is a task's card, cut to what milestone 1a draws: the header,
    what the task waits for, its stages, agents, report and lessons.

type WaitsOn struct {
	Who, What string
	OnYou     bool // the blocker is the operator: drawn in yellow, whatever Who says

	// Short and Long are What on a narrow and on a wide screen.
	Short, Long string

	// Since is when the step What names began, on a wait on the factory's
	// own work (a check's command, a copy's preparation, a QA server's
	// boot): the painter adds how long it has run after the text
	// ("precheck: jest · 3m"), from each frame's clock. Zero: no time.
	Since time.Time
}
    WaitsOn is one thing a task waits on. Who is "you" (WaitsOnYou), "agent",
    "CI", a login, "magnum", "memory", "usage", "copy" or "nothing"; What says
    why.

type WatchFailing struct {
	Watch string
	Since time.Time
	Error string
}
    WatchFailing is a watch whose radar calls fail since Since, the last with
    Error ("HTTP 502"; "" when unknown).

func (w WatchFailing) Text(now time.Time) string
    Text is w as the screens and `magnum status` say it at now: "talkable polls
    failing 47m (HTTP 502)", without the parenthesis when the cause is unknown.

type WatchFetch func(ctx context.Context) (WatchFrame, error)
    WatchFetch reads the current frame. It must honor ctx, which has a deadline
    (five intervals, at least 10s): a hung fetch then shows as an error instead
    of freezing the frame. An error shows in the header and the last good frame
    stays, unless it was wrapped with StopWatch, which ends the screen.

type WatchFrame struct {
	Title  string // e.g. "talkable#11920"
	Role   string // the session's role name (config.Role.Name), e.g. codex-judge
	Pane   string // herdr pane id
	Status string // agent status as the caller reports it ("working", "idle", ...)
	Text   string // pane contents
	ANSI   bool   // Text carries ANSI styling to pass through; false strips escape sequences
}
    WatchFrame is one snapshot of the pane being mirrored.

type WatchOptions struct {
	Interval time.Duration    // between fetches; default 2s, minimum 200ms
	Now      func() time.Time // clock for the header age; default time.Now
	// Tick schedules the next fetch; default tea.Tick.
	Tick func(time.Duration, func(time.Time) tea.Msg) tea.Cmd
}
    WatchOptions tunes RunWatch.

type WorkflowCI struct {
	Name, State                    string
	Passed, Failed, Pending, Total int
}
    WorkflowCI is one workflow's checks on the head commit.

```

## usage

```text
package usage // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/usage"

Package usage reads how much of an agent CLI's subscription budget is used.

Codex writes a token_count event into its session file
($CODEX_HOME/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl) after every turn; the event
carries the account's rate-limit windows as Codex last saw them:

    {"timestamp":"…","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"token_count",
     "rate_limits":{"primary":{"used_percent":7.0,"window_minutes":10080,
     "resets_at":1791710538},"secondary":null,"plan_type":"pro"}}}

Codex reads the newest of those snapshots without starting Codex or calling any
API, CodexAt the newest one at or before a past time. Decide turns a snapshot
into a soft/hard verdict for the scheduler. Everything here is read-only.

CONSTANTS

const (
	// MaxFiles is how many session files, newest modification first, are
	// searched for a snapshot.
	MaxFiles = 8
	// MaxTailBytes is how far from its end a session file is read.
	MaxTailBytes = 4 << 20
	// MaxHeads is how many session files written at or after the time
	// CodexAt asks about have their first line read, to tell whether the
	// session began before that time.
	MaxHeads = 256
)
    Bounds of one Codex read.

const LoginAPIKey = "api-key"
    LoginAPIKey stands for the account of a login in API-key mode (auth.json
    holds OPENAI_API_KEY and no ChatGPT account): the key itself is never read
    past telling it is there.


VARIABLES

var ErrNoData = errors.New("usage: no Codex rate-limit snapshot found")
    ErrNoData means no rate-limit snapshot was found: no session directory,
    no session files, or none of the newest files carries one.

var ErrNoLogin = errors.New("usage: no Codex login in auth.json")
    ErrNoLogin means auth.json is absent, or holds neither an account nor an API
    key.


FUNCTIONS

func DefaultCodexHome() string
    DefaultCodexHome is $CODEX_HOME, or ~/.codex when it is unset.

func PaceSince(cur Window, past Snapshot, from, now time.Time) (float64, bool)
    PaceSince is the pace of window cur from from to now: the share of its
    budget used since past, Codex's reading at or before from (which stands
    for the usage at from), over the share of the window between from and now.
    The window of past as long as cur (primary or secondary) is compared,
    and it is cur's window when its reset is within an hour of cur's. ok is
    false when past has no such window or it is another one (a reset in between:
    the budget before it is not comparable), cur's length or reset is unknown,
    its window began after from or ended by now, the used share went down,
    or now is not after from.


TYPES

type Level int
    Level is a scheduling verdict on a snapshot.

const (
	// OK means below the soft threshold.
	OK Level = iota
	// Soft means at or above the soft threshold: defer optional work (first
	// reviews), keep what is already promised.
	Soft
	// Hard means at or above the hard threshold: start nothing that needs
	// this agent kind.
	Hard
)
func Decide(snap Snapshot, soft, hard float64) Level
    Decide compares snap.Used() with the thresholds (percentages). A threshold
    of zero or less is off.

func (l Level) String() string

type Login struct {
	// Fingerprint is the first 12 hex digits of the sha256 of the login's
	// account: tokens.account_id, or LoginAPIKey in API-key mode.
	Fingerprint string
	// ChangedAt is when auth.json last changed: the newer of its own
	// modification time and, when it is a symlink, its target's.
	ChangedAt time.Time
}
    Login is the Codex login of a CODEX_HOME, as far as magnum tells logins
    apart.

func CodexLogin(home string) (Login, error)
    CodexLogin reads the login of home's auth.json (home is a CODEX_HOME; empty
    means DefaultCodexHome), following a symlink. A ChatGPT login's account
    (tokens.account_id) wins over an API key. It returns ErrNoLogin for no file,
    a dangling link and a file with neither; a file that is not JSON is an error
    that quotes nothing of it.

type Pace struct {
	Used     float64   // percent of the budget used, 0–100
	Start    time.Time // when the window began: ResetsAt minus its length
	ResetsAt time.Time
	Now      time.Time
}
    Pace is how fast a rate-limit window's budget is being spent: the share used
    against the share of the window elapsed.

func PaceOf(used float64, windowMinutes int, resetsAt, now time.Time) (Pace, bool)
    PaceOf is the pace at now of a window windowMinutes long that resets at
    resetsAt, with used percent of it used. ok is false when the length or the
    reset is unknown (<= 0, zero) or now is not inside the window (before its
    start, or at/after the reset).

func (p Pace) Elapsed() float64
    Elapsed is the share of the window elapsed, 0–100.

func (p Pace) Ratio() float64
    Ratio is Used over Elapsed: 1 spends the whole budget exactly at the reset,
    2.7 runs out at 37% of the window. 0 when nothing elapsed.

func (p Pace) Reach(pct float64) (time.Time, bool)
    Reach is when the used share reaches pct at the current pace (the average
    since the window began: Start + (Now-Start)*pct/Used). ok is false when it
    is reached already (Used >= pct), nothing is used yet (Used <= 0), pct <= 0,
    nothing has elapsed to extrapolate from, or the time is not before ResetsAt.

type Snapshot struct {
	Window
	Secondary *Window
	// Plan is the account's plan_type ("pro", "plus", …); empty when absent.
	// Sessions under different logins can report different plans; the
	// newest snapshot wins whatever its plan.
	Plan string
	// At is the timestamp of the event the snapshot came from.
	At time.Time
	// Path is the session file it came from.
	Path string
}
    Snapshot is the newest rate-limit report found. The embedded Window is
    Codex's primary limit; Secondary is the other one when Codex reports two
    (older Codex versions report a 5-hour primary and a weekly secondary).

func Codex(ctx context.Context, home string, now time.Time) (Snapshot, error)
    Codex returns the newest rate-limit snapshot in home's session files (home
    is a CODEX_HOME; empty means DefaultCodexHome). It looks at the MaxFiles
    most recently modified rollout files, reads each from its end (at most
    MaxTailBytes), skips malformed lines and token_count events without rate
    limits, and returns the snapshot with the latest timestamp. Windows whose
    reset time is at or before now read 0% used. It returns ErrNoData when
    nothing is found.

func CodexAt(ctx context.Context, home string, at time.Time) (Snapshot, error)
    CodexAt returns the newest rate-limit snapshot in home's session files
    (empty means DefaultCodexHome) stamped at or before at: the budget as Codex
    last reported it then. Its windows read as reported, one that has reset
    since included; the caller compares ResetsAt. It reads, each from its end
    (at most MaxTailBytes), the files last written before at as Codex reads the
    newest (the newest one usually settles it) and the sessions spanning at,
    written at or after it but started at or before it; at most MaxFiles of
    each. Of a file written at or after at only the first line, the session_meta
    record stamped when the session started, is read to tell (of the MaxHeads
    such files written closest to at). It returns ErrNoData when nothing is
    found.

func (s Snapshot) Used() float64
    Used is the higher used percentage of the primary and secondary windows:
    the budget that runs out first.

type Window struct {
	// UsedPercent is the share of the window's budget used, 0–100. Codex
	// reports it as of At; a window whose ResetsAt has passed reads 0.
	UsedPercent float64
	// WindowMinutes is the window's length (10080 for the weekly limit).
	WindowMinutes int
	// ResetsAt is when the window resets; zero when Codex did not say.
	ResetsAt time.Time
}
    Window is one rate-limit window as Codex reported it.

```

## webhooks

```text
package webhooks // import "github.com/zhuravel/magnum/internal/webhooks"

Package webhooks reads the events magnum-relay keeps of the GitHub App's webhook
deliveries: GET <url>/v1/events, a long poll by cursor, with curl through execx.
The operator's outbound firewall blocks Go's own HTTP client in a rebuilt,
unsigned magnum binary, and gh reaches only GitHub, so curl, which the firewall
lets through, makes the request.

The relay's bearer token is read from a file only its owner can open
(CheckTokenFile) and goes to curl on stdin, in the config curl reads with
--config -, never in argv, a log or an error; --disable, the first argument,
keeps a ~/.curlrc out (one that turns on verbose would print the header).
An event carries ids and routing only: no title, body, comment, patch, user name
or URL.

CONSTANTS

const (
	MinToken = 32
	MaxToken = 512
)
    MinToken and MaxToken bound a token's length, as the relay's
    relay.CheckToken does (MinTokenLength, MaxTokenLength).

const MaxLimit = 500
    MaxLimit is the most events the relay lists in one page.

const MaxWait = 30 * time.Second
    MaxWait is the longest long poll the relay serves (wait=).

const PageSlack = 10 * time.Second
    PageSlack is how much longer than its wait curl gives a page (its
    --max-time): a page answers within wait + PageSlack or fails.


VARIABLES

var ErrBusy = errors.New("the relay is busy (HTTP 429: too many long polls wait)")
    ErrBusy is the relay's HTTP 429: as many long polls wait as it lets wait at
    once; it asks for another try a second later (Retry-After: 1), which says
    nothing of the stream's health.

var ErrUnauthorized = errors.New("the relay refused the token (HTTP 401): check webhooks.token_file against the relay's tokens")
    ErrUnauthorized is the relay refusing the token (HTTP 401).


FUNCTIONS

func CheckTokenFile(path string) error
    CheckTokenFile checks the file holding the relay's token: a regular file,
    symlinks followed, that neither its group nor others may read or write (0600
    or narrower; fsx.CheckPrivate). A missing file is fs.ErrNotExist.

func ReadToken(path string) (string, error)
    ReadToken reads the relay's bearer token from path: a file CheckTokenFile
    accepts, holding one token the relay can accept (relay.CheckToken: one word
    of MinToken to MaxToken printable ASCII characters), trimmed of surrounding
    white space. Its errors never quote the token.

func ValidCursor(s string) bool
    ValidCursor reports whether s can be one of the relay's epochs or cursors:
    1 to 100 bytes of letters, digits and ._:- (what safe keeps of a value a
    message quotes). A page carrying any other is malformed, and the consumer
    never keeps or writes one.


TYPES

type Check struct {
	Name       string `json:"name"`
	Conclusion string `json:"conclusion"`
}
    Check is a CI event's name and conclusion (names are data).

type Client struct {
	Runner execx.Runner
	// URL is the relay's base URL (https; config.Webhooks validates it).
	URL string
	// TokenFile holds the relay's bearer token (CheckTokenFile).
	TokenFile string
}
    Client reads the relay's events.

func (c *Client) Events(ctx context.Context, after string, limit int, wait time.Duration) (Page, error)
    Events reads the page of at most limit events after the cursor after ("" =
    from the oldest kept event; limit 0 = the relay's default), waiting up to
    wait for one when there is none yet. curl gets wait + PageSlack.

type Event struct {
	// Seq is the event's place in the relay's journal.
	Seq int64 `json:"seq"`
	// DeliveryID is the delivery's X-GitHub-Delivery GUID, which a
	// redelivery keeps.
	DeliveryID string `json:"delivery_id"`
	// Event is the X-GitHub-Event name ("pull_request", "check_run") and
	// Action the payload's action ("" when it has none).
	Event  string `json:"event"`
	Action string `json:"action"`
	// InstallationID and RepositoryID are 0 when the payload has none.
	InstallationID int64 `json:"installation_id"`
	RepositoryID   int64 `json:"repository_id"`
	// Repository is "owner/name" ("" when the payload has none).
	Repository string `json:"repository"`
	// PRNumbers are the pull requests the event names: a pull_request*
	// event's, an issue_comment's on a pull request, a check's (none for a
	// fork's, or a status).
	PRNumbers []int `json:"pr_numbers"`
	// HeadSHA is the pull request's head, or the check's or status's commit
	// (40 hex or "").
	HeadSHA string `json:"head_sha"`
	// BaseRef is a pull_request* event's base branch, else "".
	BaseRef string `json:"base_ref"`
	// Check is set only for check_run, check_suite and status.
	Check *Check `json:"check,omitempty"`
	// ReceivedAt is when the relay stored the delivery.
	ReceivedAt time.Time `json:"received_at"`
}
    Event is one delivery as the relay keeps it (relay-api: ids and routing
    only).

func (e Event) Name() string
    Name is the event's name with its action: "pull_request.synchronize",
    "status".

type GapError struct {
	// Epoch and Oldest are the relay's journal and the cursor before its
	// oldest kept event.
	Epoch, Oldest string
}
    GapError is the relay's HTTP 410: the cursor is another journal's, or older
    than the oldest event it keeps, so the events after it are lost.

func (e *GapError) Error() string

type Page struct {
	// Epoch is the journal's id: a journal created again has another, and
	// every cursor of the old one is a gap.
	Epoch  string  `json:"epoch"`
	Events []Event `json:"events"`
	// Next is the cursor to ask after next.
	Next string `json:"next"`
	// HighWater is the cursor of the newest event the journal stored.
	HighWater string `json:"high_water"`
	// Oldest is the cursor before the oldest event the journal keeps.
	Oldest     string    `json:"oldest"`
	ServerTime time.Time `json:"server_time"`
}
    Page is one answer of GET /v1/events: the events after the cursor
    asked for, in journal order, and the cursors to go on from. A cursor is
    "<epoch>:<seq>".

type StatusError struct{ Code int }
    StatusError is an answer of the relay that is neither a page nor a 401 or
    410: a 5xx (Server) or another code.

func (e *StatusError) Error() string

func (e *StatusError) Server() bool
    Server reports whether the relay itself failed (5xx).

```
